entries.name: Blast Cartridge.
entries: A weapon that boasts the Blast Cartridge property is inlaid with a firing mechanism that can be triggered whenever you hit a creature with a melee attack wielding it, spending one appropriate piece of ammunition to do so. ( Usually a bullet. ) Whenever you do, you inflict additional damage equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property. A Blast-Cartridge weapon is considered to have the Reload (1) Property as per loading and managing rounds spent by this Property, unless stated otherwise. These are separate from average Reload Property, if present, as if they were different feeding mechanisms that can be fired at once.

If you are playing on a campaign that does not concern itself with particular tracking of ammunition, you may have your maximum ammunition count be double your proficiency bonus, regaining half that value on a short rest and fully restoring it upon the end of a long rest, as you scrounge around more pieces to refill your spent reserves.

entries.name: Reload.
entries: Weapons with the Reload property have a limited amount of rounds that can be shot before needing to be reloaded. A Reload weapon needs to be reloaded after a certain amount of attacks, with this value being found in parenthesis following the property. To do so, you must spend your Action or Bonus Action to do so - Nevertheless, you cannot take the Attack action using the reloaded weapon until the end of your current turn when you reload it.

entries.name: Expanded Ammunitions List
entries: For the sake of brevity, the Spell Slot Level used for anything will be referred to as SL, any reference to your Proficiency Bonus will also be shortened to PB.

entries.name: Disruptive Bullet
entries: Also called thundershot, this bullet doesn't pack much of a punch but manages to disorient a person long enough to be helpful.

When used, you may choose a target within your Marksman Weapon's range and perform a ranged weapon attack against them, on a hit you deal {@dice SLd4} thunder damage and they suffer a penalty to Concentration checks and to any roll pertaining Interacting with an Object until the end of their next turn, as exceedingly loud ringing in their ears impedes them from doing so. This penalty's value is equal to half your PB times SL.

entries.name: Suppressive Fire
entries: Although not very practical for inflicting great damage, this magazine contains a series of compact bullets useful to effectively pin down a target. When used, you may choose a target within your Marksman Weapon's range, it must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer immense hardship to leave its position, having their movement speed reduced by 5 * SL, to a minimum of 5-feet. In addition, if the target does move during this duration, the next attack aimed against them has your SL as a bonus modifier to hit.

entries.name: Congealed Shot
entries: This bullet features a smooth gelatin congealed within its casing which explodes after hitting a target. When used, you may choose any point within your Marksman Weapon's range to shoot. When the bullet hits a surface, it detonates in the form of a 5-ft large sphere of gelatin.

If this gelatin hits a creature, they must perform a Strength Saving Throw or be pushed in the opposite direction of where they were hit for up to 10 * SL feet, with Large or greater creatures having advantage on this Saving Throw.

After being deployed, any creature within 5-feet of the gelatin may use their bonus action to hop onto the Gelatin, being flung in the air on a long jump for the same distance as if they would be hit in length and half that number, rounded down, of height, or the inverse if they choose to perform a high jump.

entries.name: Shrapnel Shot
entries: Various steel pellets are found within this bullet's shell, having a second ignition trigger after hitting a target and exploding to expand its field of effect. When used, you may choose a point within your Marksman Weapon's range, all creatures within a 5 * SL radius of the point must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer SL die of damage plus your Charisma Modifier, with the type of die and damage matches the Marksman Weapon's. On a success, creatures take half the damage rolled

entries.name: Booster Shot
entries: Instead of the usual shell, this piece of ammunition is a syringe which will inject its contents upon piercing a target. When used, you may choose any creature within your Marksman Weapon's range, firing a healing round at them. They are healed by {@dice SLd6|SL d6} hit points and gain a +2 bonus to Constitution Saving Throws against being poisoned for the next hour, as the medicine strengthens their immune system temporarily.

entries.name: Lead Bullet
entries: Simple, effective. This bullet is made of solid lead, containing only a handful of poisons and acids applied. When used, you make a ranged weapon attack with your Marksman Weapon. On hit, in addition to its normal damage inflicted, the target must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or suffer from the {@condition Poisoned} Condition for the next minute, repeating this Constitution Saving Throw at the end of their turns. On the first failure of this Saving Throw and on subsequent Saving Throws at the end of their turn, regardless of their outcome, the {@condition Poisoned} creature also suffers {@dice SLd8|SL d8} poison damage. Creatures immune to poison damage instead treat this damage as if they only had resistance.

entries.name: Detonation Bullet
entries: Waiting for the second time to press the trigger is often harder than landing the shot. This bullet contains a small incendiary explosive capable of causing a big wreck. When used, you make a ranged weapon attack against a target within your range. On a hit, a Detonation Bullet is lodged inside them.

You may, as a free action taken whenever there is no ongoing roll, pull a trigger to have the explosive perform its role. The creature containing the bullet must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or take SL * d12 fire damage as if they were Vulnerable to fire damage, or half this damage on a success. In the case of a failure, all creatures within a 15-feet radius of the detonation must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take SL * d8 fire damage, or half on a success.

entries.name: Brainburst Bullet
entries: Sometimes the best choice is to fully attempt to break a targets mind before their body. When used, you force a target creature within your range to attempt a Charisma Saving Throw, on a success they take {@dice 3d4} psychic damage. On a failure, they take {@dice 3d4} psychic damage upon failing and suffer an additional {@dice 2d4} psychic damage at the end of each of their subsequent turns, as the bullet pulses with psionic energy that causes massive aching. This lasts for up to one minute and the target may attempt the Charisma Saving Throw again after suffering the psychic damage at the end of their turn. On a success, the effect ends early but they suffer a parting echo of the psionic pain, taking {@dice 4d8} psychic damage.

entries.name: Atelier Logic Caliber
entries: Have you wanted a smart, heat-seeking round? The Atelier Logic Caliber Bullet is laid in silver and expensive, extravagant technology to maximize its hit chance.

When used, you make a ranged weapon attack against a target within your range, you have a +3 to hit with this bullet. This attack's Critical Hit range is changed to a minimum of SL-20. On a Critical Hit, this attack instantly kills a creature with SL * 25 Hit Points or lower.

entries.name: Catalyst
entries: A weapon with the Catalyst Property was specially made for the purpose of channelling spells, often bearing their own engraved forms of spell craft. A weapon with this property does not use Strength for its attack modifier, instead making use of the spellcasting ability of the Class(es) shown in parenthesis next to this property. It also uses that classes Spell Save DC if required. The displayed classes automatically have Proficiency with the weapon, even if they wouldn't usually. These also count as spell foci for them.

entries.name: Path of the Hammer of Faith
Follower of an Order Prescripts
entries: Whenever you draw from this table, re-roll the result if you've drawn this Prescript before. You may choose to add another Prescript Table to this roll, if able, rolling 2d100 and summing the result. On rolling two ones, roll a d4, taking odd numbers as a final result of one and even numbers as a final result of two.
If any of the following Prescripts display a specific time until completion, you may draw your next Prescript as usual while the pecific-timed Prescript remains active.

These are intentionally vague and containing varying levels of interpretation, as such, you may either consider any technical completion of a Prescript as enough, with the DM having final say in the matter.

entries.caption: Follower of an Order Prescripts
rows: "Consume all hair strands of your head until smooth." You may spend your Action to do so. You suffer the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.

"Publicly perform a dance to at least two dozens of people." You may use a Performance check to do so, greatly impressing people on a result of 20 or greater, and greatly humiliating yourself on a 10 or lesser.
"Hunt three squirrels or similarly sized mammals and leave their bodies in the nearest tree-hollow or hole after you are done."
"Drink a litre of milk before performing any major activity." You must drink one litre of milk before any combat.
"Only eat, or write, or fight with your right hand.
"Follow every second command issued by others."
Whenever you first see a sword, slap it off the wielder's person with the back of your hand."
"Find a groom or a bride." You gain a +9 bonus on Charisma Checks against a target with dark brown hair.
"Spill another's insides." You must kill another non-summoned, non-construct creature.
"Act like the first creature you see after waking up for the next 12 hours."
"Stab the nearest person you love most with a knife."
"Paint the insides of a temple, town hall, tavern or shop to be picturesque."
"Bake a cake and gift it to the closest creature sleeping to your right. You must fully insert a needle into said cake before gifting it."
"Find the nearest reflective surface and face it towards another."
"Throw the the object you are currently holding towards the direction you are facing, then pick it up."
"Bite down your nearest friend's arm." Upon a successful bite, you deal 1d6 plus your Strength modifier in piercing damage.
"If you would go to sleep, instead stay up until you encounter the next unknown person of the same race as vou. Challenge them to three-card monty until one of vou has lost five silver."

"Go to a place where alcohol is served and challenge the fourth person you meet to a drinking contest. Should you win, find somewhere to sleep. Should you lose, leave the bar and walk a thousand steps west."
"Find a Wanted Man (Or Woman ), make him wish you brought him Dead instead of Alive."
"Defeat a target with a kick travelling at least 10 feet in the air. Ensure an explosion happens behind you until 10 seconds after you land."
"Ask the person to your left to draw their family members (or loved ones) then burn it in front of them."

"From where you are standing right now light a torch. Then, walk ten paces forwards, however if you cannot do so turn 90 degrees to the right until you can walk forwards towards a torch to light. Then, throw the torch as hard as you can in front of you."
"On your fifth time of rest after receiving this prescript, cut a lock of hair from the shortest member of your party while they sleep and spread it on a river when the witching hour strikes."
"When you meet an object with malnutrition, give it a bird and if it sleeps soundly introduce it to a friend."
"Write a letter to someone you love and do not send it. Burn it at sunset."
"Smile when delivering bad news. Frown when delivering good news."
"Carry a weapon openly but don't use it. Let others decide its purpose."
"Within 12 hours, steal from the 2nd Wizard vou come across."
"Reveal an important secret to a person named _______. This is a name of the DM's choice."
"Eradicate the nearest group of bandits or outlaws."
"Do not utter a single word for the next six hours."
"If the first person you meet outside today answers your greetings by lifting their right hand, sink a blade into their body; if the person ignores your greetings, install a blade into your body."
"Walk 120-ft. to the left, then turn and walk 5-ft. to vour immediate right."
"Discover 3 hidden critters within your vicinity and crush them in front of the eight man you meet today."

"Ask the person to your immediate right to think of a number between one and ten. Guess that number correctly. If the person fails to choose a number within that range or lies, punch them in the stomach."
"Create a moving metallic pendulum that moves with the vibrations of the ground and append a pen to its tip. Leave it near the closest prison or house of law."
"Punch the closest object of the colour red until vour knuckles bleed."
"Draw detailed directions toward your homeland. Bury them near a body of water."
"Mount a horse or other quadruped and ride it for the entire day. Do not dismount until hearing a birdcall in the morning."

"Dice a slice of meat from a monster into five cubes and proceed to salt them until the surface is fully white. Have four other people consume one." Whenever a creature attempts to eat one of these salted cubes, they must pass a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or puke.
"Split the nocturnal lights of the a settlement's district thrice before 6 days pass."
"Deafen the fifth person who smiles at you today."
"Drink a litre of juice in the morning and warm-up before meeting your companions."
"Recite E every time you greet someone."
"Point to anyone who you speak to for the next 12 hours. Speak clearly and loudly."
"Shear 663 strands of hair and enclose them in an envelope, to be deposited at the nearest arcane shop or school."
"Buy groceries for someone you hate."
"Avert your eyes to the world until you go to sleep." You are blinded for this duration. A blindfold is recommended.
"Behead seven beings who resist your blade."
"Face toward the north and walk a mile forward. At the end, leap off the nearest cliff or inclination."
"Write a competent letter of admission toward the nearest institution."
"Kiss more girls than yesterday." At least one more.
"Cut off the tongue of the first person that casts a somatic spell intended to hurt or heal another."
"Make a statue out of the first person that speaks to you today, and gift it as a gravestone for the second person that intends to interact with you today."
"Sing the favourite song of the second person you see, then, make them unable to speak."
"Draw a sheep. Leave the paper inside a clock's glass."
"Etch the bearing of a god into a tomato."
"Sever one's head from their shoulders."

"Give out prescripts to the second, fourth and seventh people you see today. Do not gaze unto their contents." When giving these prescripts, roll on this table to grant them. If their recipients conclude them, they receive a Devotion Point. If they don't, the DM determines their immediate fate.
"Always punish another's mistakes, alternating between a light punishment and a severe punishment each time someone else fails."
"Break open the second lock you see after lunch using a toothpick and the back of a key."
"Inhale smoke and hold it in your mouth for half an hour. Exhale within five seconds."
"Recite the favourite prescript you have carried out to your favourite person."
"Inebriate the third animal or mystical creature you perceive today."

"Use non-weapons as cutlery. Use cutlery as weapons. Switch back after hunting a meal with cutlery and preparing a meal from this hunt using your weaponry. Share this meal with someone else and ask them for their honest opinion, then note it down for future improvement."
"Cut off your pinky finger." Roll a d4, if the result is an even number; cut off your right pinky. If the result is an odd number, cut off your left pinky.
"Get on your knees and pray to the very cool and awesome Index Messenger whom resides in The Undertomes."

"Play a child's game with a kid that wants to play. Let them win without them noticing." You may attempt a Deception, Performance or Sleight of Hand check against their passive Insight score to determine your ability to not let them know.
"Convince the fifth right-handed person you meet that you are their long lost relative."
"Take a personal belonging from the next person you fight. Leave it inside the nearest water fountain."
"Inspect the quality of every second blade you see for the day."
"Compose a song for your own funeral."
"Profess your undying love to every person you can see whenever you hear an animal's call."

"Ask every other person you meet if it is their birthday. .If If it it is, is, give them a gift. If they hair is blonde, red or multi coloured, give them four handfuls of dirt in a satchel instead." The DM may roll a d100 if they haven't decided if the person's birthday is today, with it being their birthday on a roll of 91 or greater. If the result is 1, they were born on a leap year."
"Throw the remains of the first meal you have today in a trash bin. Collect the bin and toss it at who cooked this meal."
"Ask the nearest person to name a profession. Gain employment in that profession within a week and quit on the fifth day of employment."
"Ignore anyone taller than you. Gift one gold piece to any being shorter than you."
"Put on clown make-up and use juggling pins as your weapon until you knock down a living thing."

"Give this prescript to the second person you greet today and tell them to follow this Prescript." If any creature fails to conclude this Prescript, the paper explodes into light and carves a number equal to the number of times this Prescript was concluded into the back of the hand of its last courier's.
"Open your bag, place the nearest object that will fit into it, carry it for three hours. Do not answer why."
"Remove a single item from your possession and give it to the first person you make eye contact with. Then walk backwards 10 feet."

"Pickup the first object that can fit into your hand, name it, carry it, and treat it as if it were a capable of speaking to you for the remainder of the day. Dump it into the nearest body of water at the end of the day."
"Walk in a circle, then stare at the third person you see for 6 seconds. Afterwards, wave at them and proceed to not look at them for at least 3 hours."
"Maintain eye contact with anyone you see until they blink. Do not blink until then."
"Whenever you hear a spell being cast by someone else, stare at its caster's eyes for at least six seconds."
"Wear a bucket on your head for the entire day. Do not answer why. Do not acknowledge the bucket."
"Light any graves or rotting meat you see between this sunrise and the next using a flint and steel."
"Whenever you feel pain, tell a secret less than ten people know."
"Adopt a pet. Name them after someone you hate and buy them at least one piece of jewelry."
"Do not eat, drink or sleep for the next three days. After the 72nd hour comes to pass, write down your current thoughts in a paper, fold it between your fingers and sleep in a public space."

"For three hours you may only speak in a language outside of your common tongue. You may convey meanings through hand gestures, movements, and examples. You may not in any way speak in your common tongue."
"Introduce another person of your choice to the concept of Prescripts and turn them into a neophyte."
"Write an autobiography. Gift the manuscript to the third person you meet."
"Carve a path leading into the heart of the nearest woods or similar ecosystem."
"Swap your left index finger with your right index finger and your right index finger with your left index finger."
"Break the thumbs of anyone you see that is wearing red."
"At some point in the day, capture a small animal, carry it with you, feed it a portion of your meal when you eat. Release it after the first time you feed it."
"Wear a different hairstyle. If anyone comments about it, ask them if they like it."

"Tattoo the name of the first person you've ever felt romantic love toward in the back of your neck. If you have not felt romantic love toward a person, tattoo your favourite word on your left hand's knuckles."
"Jump through every window you see once."
"Do not tell a lie until midnight. Afterward, spend the next hour alone.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: When creating a character who follows the Living Will, it's recommended to sit down and talk to your Dungeon Master about how to best develop a faction of other followers into the setting you wish to play in, as this subclass heavily interacts with fellow followers of the Will. For DMs, consider creating Messenger NPCs that are the usual deliverer's of prescripts towards your player and other followers, also using these Prescripts outside of the pre-written ones from tables to include your own plot-hooks through these orders.

entries.name: Burn
entries: A Burning creature is set ablaze constantly, taking an amount of {@damage d4} fire damage equal to the number of Burn count on itself at the end of their turn, also halving its total count.
When at one Burn count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

entries.name: Charge
entries: A creature that is Charging is amassing an amount of energy - electrical, magical or otherwise, having jolts and arcs surround her body as the quantity intensifies.
Charge and its unique counterparts do not affect a character by itself, instead being a renewable resource to be spent for activating certain abilities and effects.

entries.name: Rupture
entries: A creature suffering from the Rupture Condition takes an amount of extra damage die equal to half their current Rupture count whenever they suffer an attack hit. The additional damage die depend on the attacking creature's Proficiency Bonus, being {@damage d4} at +2 Bonus, {@damage d6} at +3 Bonus, {@damage d8} at +4 Bonus, {@damage d10} at +5 Bonus, a {@damage d12} for +6 Bonus and finally {@damage 2d6} at +7 Bonus and greater.
Once an attack successfully hits and the condition is triggered, they lose all of their remaining Rupture count.
Ex: If a creature suffering from 5 Rupture would suffer a hit from a creature with a +4 Proficiency Bonus, they would take an additional {@damage 3d8} damage.

entries.name: Tremor
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor is one suffering from immeasurable shaking and vibrations inside their body.

When a Tremoring creature suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage d4} thunder damage equal to their current Tremor count, then losing all remaining count.
The Condition is also lost after combat is over or at the end of the next short or long rest, if it was gained outside of combat.

entries.name: Tremor Burst
entries: Tremor Burst is not a Condition, but instead a trigger for the {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Condition which is caused by some feats, spells or other abilities.

entries.name: Bleed
entries: A Bleeding creature is well, bleeding! They take {@damage 1d4} damage when they perform any action ( Each attack is considered a different action, this also includes Bonus Actions, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ), and then Bleed is reduced by a count. They may have all Bleed count removed if any creature passes a successful {@skill Medicine} check on them as an Action. Otherwise, half their current Bleed count is removed upon receiving healing through an item or through a 4th level or lower spell. It is also fully removed upon the use of an item such as a {@item potion of greater healing|DMG|potion of Greater Healing} or a 5th level or greater spell.

On the case of casting a spell, they suffer an amount of {@damage d4} damage and lose an amount count equal to the spell's level plus one. ( Cantrips only deal {@damage 1d4} damage, 1st Level Spells deal {@damage 2d4} and so on. ) If a creature is suffering from lesser count than the spell slot level spent, they still suffer the maximum damage and remain at a single count.
The DC for this is 10 + their current Bleed count. If they have only one Bleed count, it may only be reduced through a {@skill Medicine} check.

entries.name: Poise
entries: A creature benefitting from being Poised has their stance slowly being perfected to enter "the zone" while fighting, being able to perform a Posture Critical hit whenever they roll at least a 19 on attack, before adding any modifiers. This threshold is reduced by each additional count of Poise they have after the first, up to 4 ( Triggering a Posture Critical Hit on a roll of 16 or higher) and removing all Poise count from them when they land a Posture Critical hit.
When this effect is triggered, this creature deals an additional {@damage 2d6} damage on a hit of type equal to your attacks damage type.

If they have 6 or more stacks of Poise, they deal an extra {@damage d6} of damage for each two count above 6, to a maximum of {@damage 6d6} total. A Posture Critical Hit is not a regular Critical Hit.

entries.name: Sinking
entries: A creature that is Sinking has trouble focusing on anything as a deep unease washes over them, making way for pure leg-shaking terror or difficulty performing what they must. While suffering Sinking the afflicted creature has a negative modifier to Attack Rolls for each 3 Sinking afflicted to them, to a maximum of -5. Additionally, they have their Wisdom Saving Throws reduced by a negative modifier for each 10 Sinking, to a maximum of -3.
Sinking count is halved at the end of a creatures turn, rounded up. Upon having one count remaining it is removed entirely instead.

Ex: A creature with 12 stacks of Sinking suffers a -4 penalty to Hit. Additionally, that creature has their Wisdom Saving Throws reduced by a negative modifier for each 10 Sinking, to a maximum of -3.

entries.name: Haste
entries: A creature that is going through Haste has a spring to their step, pushing themselves to move faster or are being carried through magical effects to become nimble as the breeze.

This creature gains 5-ft. of additional walking speed and, if already available, flying speed for each Haste count they are benefitting from, to a maximum value of 5 times their proficiency bonus plus 5. All count of the Condition is lost at the start of the creature's next turn.

entries.name: Immobilized
entries: A creature suffering from Immobilized is one who's suffering to move their stiffening limbs and joints. While enduring Immobilized, they take a penalty equal to the count of Immobilized they are currently afflicted with to all of their attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws. All Immobilized stacks are removed at the end of the creature's turn or after a minute has passed outside of combat.

entries.name: Heavy Blood
entries: Heavily Bleeding creatures are bleeding intensely, instead causing the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Condition and 2 count are removed every time it is triggered. The {@skill Medicine} Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

entries.name: Tremor - Hemorrhage
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor - Hemorrhage is one that is currently bleeding out from countless cuts that move and worsen inside their being.

A creature with Tremor - Hemorrhage counts suffers {@damage 1d4} damage whenever they perform any action ( Each Attack counts as a different Action, also including Bonus Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ) and then the Condition's count is reduced by one count. Creatures that have no blood are immune to this effect.

When a creature with Tremor - Hemorrhage suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage d6} damage equal to the total count of the Condition they are currently suffering from, then losing all remaining counts of the Condition. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious}, If they are healed to their Maximum Hit Points they instantly lose all counts of the Condition, also losing 2 counts whenever they are healed by any amount of Hit Points.

entries.name: Tremor - Scorch
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor - Scorch is one currently suffering from a blazing inferno that is eating them from inside out, with each flicker of flame reverberating across their entire being.

A creature with Tremor - Scorch counts suffers an amount of {@damage d4} fire damage equal to their current Tremor - Scorch count divided by 3, to a maximum of {@damage 8d4} per turn. After suffering this damage, the Condition's total count is halved.

When a creature with Tremor - Scorch suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage d6} fire damage equal to the total count of Tremor - Scorch they currently have, then losing all counts of Tremor - Scorch. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious}, if they are fully submerged in non-flammable liquid or combat is over or on the next short rest, if it was gained outside of combat.

entries.name: Immolation
entries: A creature beset by Immolation is suffering from the holiest of flames, taking an amount of {@damage d4} radiant damage equal to their current Immolation count at the end of their turns, also halving its total count. When at one Immolation count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

entries.name: Nails
entries: A creature suffering from Nails has a number of them embedded in their flesh, drawing out blood and the faith of certain individuals in equal measure. At the end of their turns, a Nailed creature halves their Nail count and gains the same value halved as {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.
Fanatical creatures gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls against Nailed creatures for each 15 Nails* they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of +3.

entries.name: Assist
entries: A weapon with the Assist property is one that was designed to aid in defending the wielder, yet it's usage makes it cumbersome to wield anything too big at the same time. While wielding an Assist weapon you gain a +1 bonus modifier to your Armor Class, but you cannot benefit from wielding Heavy weapons or a {@item Shield|PHB}.

entries.name: Burst
entries: Weapons with the Burst property are ones that can be fired or used in a quick burst of attacks that compromise accuracy for the chance of more damage. You may benefit from Burst weapons whenever you take the {@action Attack} action, choosing to replace a singular attack you would be able to make with a number of attacks displayed in parenthesis next to this property. You may choose only one target for each burst of attacks, being able to switch between targets with each differing attack replaced to do so.

You may do so for each attack you would usually be able to make, but suffer a negative modifier starting at a value equal to your Dexterity modifier minus the first number in parenthesis (Minimum of 1), further subtracting one for each individual attack made after the first. This negative modifier is reduced by 2 if you are wielding your weapon with two hands and fully reset at the end of your turns.

You do not add your ability modifier to damage dealt by this Property's feature, and the damage dealt by a burst shot may differ from the original damage that would be dealt by the weapon. If so, this value is displayed after the number of attacks made in a burst.

Ex: As a level 5 Fighter you have two attacks as per the {@action Attack} Action. You may perform one normal attack and then choose to use the feature from a Burst (3) weapon, performing three attacks against the same target. You have a Dexterity modifier of 3, thus having no negative modifier for the first roll in your burst, then a -1 for the second and a -2 for the third.

entries.name: Chain-Through
entries: A weapon with the Chain-through property has an easy way of cutting into targets after initially being lodged onto them. These are saws, barbed axes and even barbed spears which can be wedged, pushed and pulled for a nasty amount of damage even if the target tries to dodge away. While dealing damage with a Chain-Through weapon, provided you haven't missed your previous attack, you deal at least half the value of damage die you'd roll if you had rolled lower than that.

Ex: If you, a Paladin, deal {@damage 2d8} slashing damage + {@damage 2d8} radiant damage with a Chainsword, if you roll a total of 2 slashing and 2 radiant damage, you instead deal 8 slashing and 8 radiant damage on that hit.

entries.name: Concealed
entries: A weapon with the Concealed property is perfect for hiding in-between clothes or other belongings, seeming like a harmless trinket until it is drawn. While not being held, you may use your Bonus Action to suddenly draw it with a free hand and perform a weapon attack roll against a creature within reach. If you had no free hands, you instantly swap one of your held items with the Concealed weapon. You also gain a +5 bonus modifier on {@skill Stealth} checks to hide a Concealed weapon.

entries.name: Draw
entries: A weapon with the Draw property is one meant to deliver its full force when unsheathed instead of over various strikes. While sheathed, your next unsheathed attack made with a Draw weapon gains a bonus modifier to hit equal to half it's wielder's proficiency bonus, rounded down, and deals an additional damage die on a hit. After being unsheathed, it's wielder may spend one of their attacks as part of the {@action Attack} action to sheathe it.

entries.name: Ennervate
entries: A weapon with the {@i Ennervate} property is usually a living, breathing thing - Feeding on that very same life to fuel a diverse spectrum of effects. These are found under their own section of the {@i Ennervating} weapon and may be activated by sacrificing an amount of Hit Points equal to the number listed within parenthesis beside this property.

entries.name: Entrench
entries: A weapon with the Entrench property carries an enormous punch but also a considerable amount of blowback whenever it is fired or swung. Whenever you perform an attack with it, your remaining movement speed is reduced by the value in parenthesis beside this property. If two numbers are shown, these are in order the amount of movement speed reduced by one handed attacks and two handed attacks.

entries.name: Blazing
entries: With the right angle, a weapon with the {@i Blazing} property ignites the air in a furious blaze., Whenever your base dice roll is equal to or greater than the first value displayed in parenthesis besides this property, you apply an amount of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the second value presented.

entries.name: Blast Cartridge
entries: A weapon that boasts the {@i Blast Cartridge} property is inlaid with a firing mechanism that can be triggered whenever you hit a creature with it, spending one appropriate piece of ammunition to do so. ( Usually a bullet. ) Whenever you do, you inflict additional damage equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property.

entries.name: Hemorrhaging
entries: Meant to cause deep gashes and cuts, a {@i Hemorrhaging} weapon excels at drawing out blood. Whenever your base dice roll to hit a creature is equal or greater to than the first number presented in parenthesis beside this property, you inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the second value presented.

entries.name: Mesmerizing
entries: ( Also known as Funny ) Mesmerizing weapons aren't made just to be used with the usual strength of technique that a swordmaster or a great archer would have, no. They instead rely on another technique: that of the spectacle! You may use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength while using these weapons.

entries.name: Lobbing
entries: A lobbing weapon isn't just thrown straight ahead, instead aiming up to strike down from afar. Lobbing weapons ignore cover if that cover isn't at least as tall as their short range, as per the Range or thrown properties.

entries.name: Reload
entries: Weapons with the Reload property have a limited amount of rounds that can be shot before needing to be reloaded. A Reload weapon needs to be reloaded after a certain amount of attacks, with this value being found in parenthesis following the property. To do so, you must spend your Action or Bonus Action to do so - Nevertheless, you cannot take the {@action Attack} action using the reloaded weapon on the same turn you reload it.

entries.name: Set
entries: A weapon with the Set property is instead multiple weapons that can be used together or a stock that is easily replenished in the heat of battle, whether they are thrown and lost or easily breakable upon impact. The maximum amount of uses these weapons have is shown in parenthesis after the weapon property, with you having the ability to easily produce or procure more at the end of a short or long rest. A lack of a number instead indicates that the weapons may be used infinitely.

entries.name: Splash
entries: A weapon with the splash property has a tendency to cover an area of effect in its strikes or have a small splash zone where hits go off to. While you wield a Splash weapon to hit a target, all other hostile creatures within 5-ft. of the target take damage equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property. By default the damage type is the same as the weapon's first presented damage type, or denoted if otherwise.

entries.name: SteelHack
entries: A weapon with the SteelHack property is designed to have sliding or otherwise transmutative mechanisms to allow it to exist in multiple forms at once. The base weapon is described in the initial weapon text, with a secondary one being presented below it for each alternative form, which may change its properties, damage and so on. Ammunition stashed in a SteelHack weapon remains inside it even if its current form wouldn't use it, requiring a form-change to rip it out. Additionally, changing a weapon's form this way usually takes a Bonus Action, with any deviations of that rule being specified in parenthesis beside the property as A for Action and FA for a Free Action that may be taken at any time.

entries.name: Imposing
entries: An {@i Imposing} armor set is the kind of clothing that demands some level of respect, no matter from whom. You benefit from having your {@skill Intimidation} skill modifier be at least the value displayed in Parenthesis, if it was any lower.

entries.name: Impenetrable
entries: An armor seat with the {@i Impenetrable} property has remarkably good stopping power against piercing forces and other kinds of missiles. Your AC against attacks that would deal piercing damage or that are otherwise missiles ( such as arrows, bullets or certain ranged spells ) is considered to be higher by a value presented in parenthesis near this property. Additionally, whenever you would suffer damage through one such attack it is reduced by an amount equal to double the value presented in parenthesis.

data.name: Wondrous Pets & Friends
entries: A “Wondrous Pet“ is the mechanical term this document uses to refer to, well, pets! A Pet in this way is a magical being that while attuned, will always remain within a 60-feet radius of its perceived owner. They do not require food nor sleep, but will gladly partake in either joy.
A Pet does not partake in combat initiative, instead it is treated like any other magic item when called upon for an active or passive ability it grants.

Additionally, it has no stat block of its own, instead only providing static benefits to its master. Much like the {@spell Find Familiar} spell, a pet may be commanded with a free action to move and to enter or exit an extradimensional space where it is kept safe. It automatically enters that space if it would be immediately be put in harms way, instead remaining safe.
If the {@spell Dispel Magic} spell is cast on the Pet, it vanishes for one minute, and then rematerializes after this time. During its vanishing, you cannot benefit from its abilities.

In the case that the “Pet” is instead a Friend or otherwise similarly sentient and possibly humanoid creature with their own will and volitions, they still try to stick close to you and keep out of harms way, but cannot ( if they aren't inherently magical ) enter the aforementioned extradimensional space.

Otherwise, in the case that the setting calls for the destructability or otherwise harm of a Wondrous Pet or Friend, they have a pool of Hit Points that matches their attuned master's level and their rarity, as per the following table:

entries.caption: Hit Points
rows: {@dice 1d4} per Player Level + Level
Common
{@dice 1d6} per Player Level + Level
Uncommon
{@dice 1d8} per Player Level + Level
Rare
{@dice 1d10} per Player Level + Level
Very Rare
{@dice 1d12} per Player Level + Level
Legendary

entries: You may roll on this table when first attuning to them.

entries.name: Reaching 0 Hit Points
entries: Upon reaching 0 Hit Points, various things may happen depending on the Setting's intended tone and should be discussed between the Players and Dungeon Master when including Wondrous Pets & Friends into their setting. These are as follows:

items: The Pet is knocked {@condition Unconscious} until the end of battle and loses its effects until the next short rest.
The Pet initiates Death Saving Throws like a Player Character would, dying upon three failures. While {@condition Unconscious}, it does not provide any benefits.

If a Pet or Friend dies, you may choose to either have them be able to be brought back through a {@spell Revivify} or similar spell, through a ritual similar in cost to the {@spell Find Familiar} spell that any Spellcaster may perform or have them permanently die.

data.name: Deployable Tools
entries: Deployable tools are traps or other mechanisms that a character may employ in dire times. They are placed down within an unnocupied 5-ft reach by spending your Bonus Action during your turn and have a trigger according to its properties, as shown below their name, much like weapon properties. If a Tool requires a Saving Throw to be passed, it will be displayed before it's properties, with the DC's associated Ability Score being placed in parentheses, and below that it's effect(s) when trigger. Tools usually occupy a 5-ft by 5-ft square. You may also spend your Bonus Action to retrieve a Tool.
Unless specified, all Deployable Tools only trigger against creatures hostile to who deployed it.

All Tools have a Durability Property, which denominates how many times they may be activated until they break down and require repairs. A broken down Tool may be repaired by a blacksmith for half of it's buying price or during a Long Rest spending one use of a Repair Kit during a Long Rest, where at least one Character must spend their time repairing or re-stocking the Tool. Otherwise, a Player Character with a number of levels in the Artificer Class may fix up to their Proficiency Modifier's worth of Tools during a Long Rest. To do so, they must meet a minimum level requirement according to the Tool's rarity, as follows:

entries.caption: Repairing Tools
rows: Common
Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary

entries: Furthermore, Artificers may choose to use their Spell Save DC instead of the Deployable Tool's when it is triggered, instead of the Tool's original Saving Throw required. This also applies to the Artificer's Spell Attack Modifier in the case the Deployable Tool performs attacks.

entries.name: Active
entries: An Active {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} requires active usage from a creature who must spend their Action while within 5-ft of the Tool to trigger it.

entries.name: Adherent
entries: An Adherent {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one that can easily cling to any even surface, being able to be placed on unoccupied ceilings or walls.

entries.name: Arcane
entries: An Arcane {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one commonly used by scholars and people attuned to the arcane, such as Wizards and Sorcerers. Characters with levels in these classes may repair up to their Proficiency Bonus' worth of Relicary Tools during a Long Rest as if they were an Artificer, also being able to choose using their own Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Modifier for these Tools.

entries.name: Bulky
entries: A Bulky {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} requires more space than usual for its operation. This space is listed in parentheses after this property is listed.

entries.name: Contact
entries: A Contact {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} triggers whenever a creature moves into the area it occupies.

entries.name: Concealed
entries: A Concealed Tool is made hard to perceive. All Creatures have Disadvantage on {@skill Perception} Checks to find it, with the tool having a Passive {@skill Stealth} Score displayed in parenthesis following this property.

entries.name: Construct
entries: A Construct {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} has the same Resistances as most of its kind, being a mechanical mess of machinery in its operation. It has Resistance to acid damage, Immunity to poison and psychic damage and the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Poisoned}, {@condition Prone} and {@condition Incapacitated} Conditions.

entries.name: Cumbersome
entries: A Cumbersome {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is particularly harder to deploy. You must instead spend an Action to deploy this {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}.

entries.name: Durability
entries: A {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}'s Durability measures how many activations a Tool can handle before needing repairs or re-stocking. This value displayed in parenthesis after this property.

entries.name: Far-Mount
entries: A Far-Mount {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} can be easily tossed and assemble itself. You may deploy a Far-Mountable Tool on any unoccupied space within a radius of yourself as shown by the number of feet within parentheses following this property's listing.

entries.name: Instant
entries: An Instant {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one that does not keep functioning in the field as long as it still has Durability, instead having it's Durability consumed whenever it is placed down, usually because this {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} comes in sets or may be used repeatedly. After a placed Instant Tool is triggered, it is destroyed, with only it's pieces remaining for posterior repairs or resupply.

entries.name: Mount
entries: A Mount {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} may be mounted by a creature standing in the same space as it by them spending their Action or Bonus Action to do so. While mounted their movement speed is 0 and the Bonus Modifier gained from their Dexterity Modifier on Dexterity saving throws can only be a maximum of 2. A creature may spend a Free Action to dismount. Mount {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}s usually require a mounted creature's Action to be used.

entries.name: Multiple
entries: A Multiple {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is actually a set of Tools that may be placed down multiple times while it still has Durability, such as {@item Caltrops|PHB} being thrown from a bag.

entries.name: Primal
entries: A Primal {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one commonly used by those who are surrounded with nature, such as Druids and Rangers. Characters with levels in these classes may repair up to their Proficiency Bonus' worth of Reliquary Tools during a Long Rest as if they were an Artificer, also being able to choose using their own Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Modifier for these Tools.

entries.name: Reliquary
entries: A Relicary {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one commonly used by churches, such as Clerics and Paladins. Characters with levels in these classes may repair up to their Proficiency Bonus' worth of Reliquary Tools during a Long Rest as if they were an Artificer, also being able to choose using their own Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Modifier for these Tools.

entries.name: Sensor
entries: A Sensor {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} triggers whenever a creature of your choice moves in or outside of the range that follows this property in parenthesis.

entries.name: Sturdy
entries: A Sturdy {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is unlike others, having no Durability and instead possessing it's own AC and Maximum Hit Points, displayed respectively in parenthesis following this property. They are usually Immune to psychic and poison damage, Vulnerable to Acid damage and are Immune to the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Grappled}, {@condition Poisoned} and {@condition Prone} Conditions, unless stated otherwise.

entries.name: Timed
entries: A Timed Deployable Tool triggers on a timer, usually at Initiative Count 1 or at whatever count that is lower than yours when it has been set. If you have none, you may choose from 15 below. The Trap only triggers after any other creature with the same Initiative Count has acted.

data.name: Core Bursts
entries: "…In order to use Shin, one must clear their mind of all emotions and then tap into their most intense memories…"

Upon reaching a certain level of awareness and strength, certain people may come to develop a manifestation of their inner self, coming not only to understand what they are but to push that understanding outwards like an expanding force unique to them alone. This is a force composed of a mastery and understanding of your emotions and how you wish to impose that will on the world.

Upon reaching 10th level, you may choose to gain a Core Burst as per what best fits your person, activating it with a Bonus Action during your turn. This effect may come to manifest as a small effect surrounding you like an aura, such as crackling lightning forming whenever you move or smoke raising from your feet. This lasts for up to one minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

This process is exhausting to the mind, being able to be used once per long rest. You may instead use your Core Burst twice per long rest upon reaching 20th level. You may choose to push yourself particularly hard and activate your Core Burst after all uses have been expended, but you gain a point of {@condition Exhaustion} when it ends.

entries.name: Reloading and Ammunition Swapping
entries: A creature may Reload their weapon as usual even if they still have bullets left to spend, recuperating any ammunition they haven't shot. They may also use different Ammunition Types, such as {@i Arcana Shot} or {@i Propulsion Rounds} when Reloading their weapon, consuming an amount of the chosen ammunition equal to the weapon's Reload value. If unloaded, any un-shot ammunition is recovered.

entries.name: Installing and Uninstalling Prosthetics
entries: In a Setting or table where downtime should matter more, you may have the process of acquiring any given Prosthesis for part replacement and upkeep be only the first step in benefitting from such. There are two means of installing Prosthesis, either with the aid of a professional in a specialized clinic/workshop or trying to do so by yourself.

When relying on a Professional such as a surgeon, ripperdoc or meister to do so, you have the limb successfully installed or removed after 8 hours spent in surgery. These are the usual costs for such operations:

entries.caption: Professional Installation and Removal Costs
rows: Common
45 GP.
Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary
Artifact

entries: When relying on yourself or attempting to install a Prosthetic on another creature, you must spend 8 hours of uninterrupted work to do so, also requiring to pass a {@skill Sleight of Hand} check of which you may choose to use either your Dexterity or Intelligence modifier to do so. The base DC for this check is 10, with the following modifiers:

entries.caption: Prosthesis Installation DC Modifiers
rows: Common Rarity
Uncommon Rarity
Rare Rarity
Very Rare Rarity
Legendary Rarity
Artifact Rarity
Unstable Work Environment
Specialized Work Environment
Artificer Levels
Negative modifier equal to Artificer level.
Proficiency in Tinker's Tools

entries: For further clarification, an {@i Unstable Work Environment} might consist as a specially dirty or unsanitary place or an active war zone where the surgeon simply cannot focus properly. On the other hand, an {@i Specialized Work Environment} is a clinic, workshop or anything of the sort. This is ultimately up to the DM's clarification of the current environment. On a failed check, the item is not spent but you must roll on the {@i Surgery Accidents} table:

entries.caption: Surgery Accidents
rows: Nothing too egregious happens and any damage caused to the patient is negligible.

There are some mild wounds that will last for a while, causing the patient's Maximum Hit Points to be reduced by an amount equal to double the Rarity Modifier of the Prosthetic as per the above table. ( To a minimum of 2. ) These Maximum Hit Points are recovered at a rate of 1 per short rest and 5 per long rest.
What have you done. The patient must roll on the {@table Lingering Injuries|DMG} table and suffer its consequences.

entries: If you are attempting to remove a limb, the DC is increased by twice the patient's proficiency bonus instead.

entries.name: Fairy Feast
entries: Wondrous item, rare [ Price: 2.500 GP ]
A bundle of green-ish meat from an unsuspecting fairy. It smells of a mixture of herbs, with more pronounced hints of mint and ginger. It tastes heavenly and pops on your tongue.

A creature may spend a Bonus Action to consume the meat, being healed by {@dice 8d8+8} hit points and gaining {@dice 4d8+4} temporary hit points, then being forced to pass a DC 18 Wisdom Saving Throw or become addicted to {@item Fairy Feast|TheUndertomesASV} on a failure.

An addicted creature must pass a DC 14 Constitution Saving Throw at the start of all Long Rests, with this DC increasing by 2 on a success or the creature failing to benefit from the Long Rest on a failure.
A creature loses this addiction after succeeding three of these Constitution Saving Throws.

data.name: Additional Material
entries: This is a Compendium of mismatched content created daily during the course of October 2024, with evey single day being based around one abnormality from the Project Moon Universe.

entries.name: Deployable Tools
entries: Deployable tools are traps or other mechanisms that a character may employ in dire times. They are placed down within an unoccupied 5-ft reach by spending your Bonus Action during your turn and have a trigger according to its properties, as shown below their name, much like weapon properties. If a Tool requires a Saving Throw to be passed, it will be displayed before its properties, with the DC's associated Ability Score being placed in parentheses, and below that its effect(s) when triggered. Tools usually occupy a 5-ft by 5-ft square. You may also spend your Bonus Action to retrieve a Tool.

Unless specified, all Deployable Tools only trigger against creatures hostile to who deployed it. All Tools have a Durability Property, which denominates how many times they may be activated until they break down and require repairs. A broken down Tool may be repaired by a blacksmith for half of its buying price or during a Long Rest spending one use of a Repair Kit during a Long Rest, where at least one Character must spend their time repairing or re-stocking the Tool.

Otherwise, a Player Character with a number of levels in the Artificer Class may fix up to their Proficiency Modifier's worth of Tools during a Long Rest. To do so, they must meet a minimum level requirement according to the Tool's rarity, as follows:

entries.caption: Deployable Tool Repairs
rows: Common
Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary

entries: Furthermore, Artificers may choose to use their Spell Save DC instead of the Deployable Tool's when it is triggered, instead of the Tool's original Saving Throw required. This also applies to the Artificer's Spell Attack Modifier in the case the Deployable Tool performs attacks.
Deployable Tools use the following properties:

entries.name: Contact
entries: A Contact Deployable Tool triggers whenever a creature moves into the area it occupies.

entries.name: Far-Mount
entries: A Far-Mount Deployable Tool can be thrown and assembles itself. You can deploy it in an unoccupied space within the radius given in parentheses after the property.

entries.name: Multiple
entries: A Multiple Deployable Tool is a set of tools that can be placed multiple times while it has Durability, such as caltrops thrown from a bag.

entries.name: Incorporating Bloodfiends
entries: {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} are, in essence, vampires with "Big monster forms", which your world may already have. As such, you could flavor that {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} are some offshoot or even act as a replacement for these original vampires, or just use them mechanically in place of another option offered. Otherwise, if you would like to append {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} in an equal manner as to how they are presented into the Project Moon universe, here are some key primers that you should think about when including them:

Hunger for Life. Naturally, like any vampire, the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} hunger for blood and it actually does make them stronger, as with the more blood a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} has consumed, the more powerful they become. The Masquerade. Most {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|bloodfiends} tend to want to keep the fact that they exist on the down low, as such, in their own culture it's seen as a horrid act to break away from that facade in any way, with kindred culling each other over such actions. Noblesse & Bloodbags. The culture of {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} is a deeply hierarchical one, with a nearly familial tone about it all, despite them not being blood related, as such a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} who turns another into Kindred, that is to say another {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend}, is considered the Parent of the two, and the newly formed fiend their kindred. It's also considered how many degrees of separation they have from the original parent of all {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends}, such as a particularly off the ladder fiend being considered a sixteenth generation {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|bloodfiend}, or one that came right after the first being from second generation and so on. Additionally {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} may turn other creatures into Bloodbags, having the same wondrous abilities as a Kindred, with the key difference that their intellect plummets so that they're only driven by instinct and bloodlust. Both of these have control exerced over them by their Parent, the latter much more so than the first. Because of this, higher rank {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} tend to keep Bloodbags as blood collectors under them.

Additional Note 1. As an additional, for the sake of balance and letting DMs feel around for what they feel is best, there are also optional rules for drawbacks when playing a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|bloodfiend} that may be discussed with any interested players, do be free to change them even during the campaign as you test waters.

Additional Note 2. A {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} may gain Blood Charges by essentially killing and draining a creature, which may be easily abused by just eating from one of those endless rat-bags and the sort. So, for ease, a DM may rule that only non-magically constructed creatures (ex. summoned from a magical item) have suitable blood for the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend}'s finer tastes, or that are simply not good enough. As a general rule as well, any and all humanoids should be considered good enough for a sip. Additional Note 3. For the purposes of other game mechanics, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} may be considered Monstrosities in addition to having the Humanoid creature type.

entries.name: Bloodfeast
entries: Sanguine desire, red fuel to the veins. Bloodfeast is the coalesced blood of which {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} draw power from, this is a general counter that starts at 0 and is reset to 0 after combat. Bloodfeast is increased by one for each stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} inflicted by a friendly creature during combat, being a resource for the party as a whole. As an alternative rule to distribute Bloodfeast, the highest player in Initiative gains their Proficiency Bonus' worth of maximum Bloodfeast to consume during their turn, with any remaining player doing the same until the last player consumes whatever remains with the same limitations.

entries.name: Bleed & Bloodfeast Optional Rules
entries: Bloody Upcasting Optional Rule. A {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} or any other creature may convert their Bloodfeast count for upcasting their spells. When you would cast a spell, you may consume an amount of Bloodfeast count to cast it at a higher level of your choice, as follows:

entries.caption: Bloody Upcasting
rows: 2nd level
3rd level
4th level
5th level
6th level
7th level
8th level
9th level

entries: To do this, you must know how to cast at least one spell of that level.

Bloodrage Optional Rule. A {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} or any other creature that may benefit from using Bloodfeast might be susceptible to fueling that into a mighty trance to empower what they must do. Once per turn, they may spend Bloodfeast to gain a Bonus Modifier to their next Attack or Skill Check, as shown in the following table:

Special Bleeding Properties Optional Rule. As in any fantasy setting, creatures may have a different reaction to having their blood drawn out - or, to put it more clearly, their blood might have. A DM may give creatures a special property that becomes apparent while they are suffering from the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} condition. Use the following table to add these properties to your game.

entries.caption: Special Bleeding Properties
rows: Bleeding Magic

The creature has an incredibly unstable amount of mana running through its veins, causing it to roll on the Wild Magic Surge table from the Player's Handbook for each 5 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count it was suffering from at the time.
Bloodletter

The creature bleeds particularly quickly, removing all its {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count at the end of its turn but instantly taking a number of d4 damage equal to half that count, rounded up.
Celestial Blood

The creature bleeds a holy ichor that holds life itself, causing any creature that damages it while it is bleeding to regain {@dice 1d4} hit points, or suffer {@damage 2d8} radiant damage if it is Undead.
Gaseous Blood

The creature secretes a gaseous substance instead of blood, filling a radius that expands by 5 feet at the end of its turns, up to 30 feet. The DM decides whether that area is Heavily Obscured or Poisonous. If it is Poisonous, a creature that starts or ends its turn inside the area must pass a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Poisoned} until the end of its next turn. The DC equals the bleeding creature's Constitution modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + 8.
Hyperreactive Veins

The creature has very volatile properties running through its veins or is made of a volatile element, causing it to roll a Constitution saving throw whenever its turn ends. If the roll is lower than a DC of 8 + its current {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count (maximum 10), it causes an explosion. All creatures within 15 feet must pass a Dexterity saving throw against the same DC, taking {@damage 3d8} damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The damage type is whichever makes the most sense for the bleeding creature, as chosen by the DM.
Quickly Regenerating

The creature can regenerate its skin quickly, shutting the gashes that would cause it to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}. Healing cannot fully remove its {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} condition. Instead, healing also reduces its {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count by an amount equal to its Proficiency Bonus, including reducing the count to 0.
Way Too Big

The creature is too massive or has skin too thick to be properly affected by {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}. Whenever it would receive {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count, it receives half that amount instead, rounded down to a minimum of 1.
Rustblood

The creature's blood is highly corrosive to metal. Each time a metallic weapon hits it while it is bleeding, the weapon receives a cumulative -1 modifier, to a maximum of -3. If a nonmagical weapon would become rustier while already at -3, it breaks. Otherwise, the weapon must be repaired by a blacksmith for one-fourth of its original price, rounded down, or by a character proficient with Smith's Tools over a Long Rest at no material cost.

Armor Properties.
entries: Just as Weapons have their many properties, so can certain pieces of armor be designed to fit certain specializations, such as the way they are presented or be enchanted for various minor benefits. Armor properties are displayed to the upper right side of their item descriptions.

entries.name: Regulating Ammunition & Ranged Attacks in the City.
entries: The following is for DM's who'd wish to limit firearm usage in D&D to better fit Project Moon's setting while keeping ranged play viable and strategic.

entries.name: Ammunition Usage & Recovery.
entries: Instead of purchasing or managing ammunition as usual, characters have a limited number of magazines of any ranged weapons they are wielding that is equal to half their proficiency bonus, regaining these Magazines by scrounging around for more ammo, looting it from other people after a fight or any other means after a long rest.
Characters with levels in Artificer benefit further from this by being able to create or at least cobble together their own ammunition, having an amount of Magazines equal to their proficiency bonus.
These Magazines' bullet count is equal to their wielded weapon's Reload property.
Characters may also recover one spent Magazine over the course of a short rest, but must wait until their next long rest to benefit from such again.

entries.name: Weight of a Bullet.
entries: To compensate for the more limited usage, guns are made much more powerful by having their damage die and Condition infliction on ranged attacks doubled, such as a Heavy Revolver now dealing 2d12 piercing damage.

It is also the case that characters may still buy their own backup ammo, and for this it is recommended to double the prices for Common and Uncommon ammunition, triple that of Rare and Very Rare ammunition and quadruple the value of Legendary ammunition.

Another option to better regulate the acquisition of surplus ammunition is by having most Workshops adhere to a code of sale that limits the amount of ammunition an individual may buy in the goal of either complying to City procedure or even as a means of forcing clientele to come back later so they can maximize profits. This limit should be equal to double the character's level. ( Starting and remaining at 6 until 4th level, where that limit increases to 8 and so on. )
This limit of surplus ammunition counts for any kind of ammo acquired as a total, instead of individually.

entries.name: Installing & Uninstalling Prosthetics.
entries: In a Setting or table where downtime should matter more, you may have the process of acquiring any given Prosthesis for part replacement and upkeep be only the first step in benefitting from such. There are two means of installing Prosthesis, either with the aid of a professional in a specialized clinic/workshop or trying to do so by yourself.

When relying on a Professional such as a surgeon, ripperdoc or meister to do so, you have the limb successfully installed or removed after 8 hours spent in surgery. These are the usual costs for such operations:

entries.caption: Professional Installation
rows: Common
45 GP
Uncommon
500 GP
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary
Artifact

entries: When relying on yourself or attempting to install a Prosthetic on another creature, you must spend 8 hours of uninterrupted work to do so, also requiring to pass a Sleight of Hand check of which you may choose to use either your Dexterity or Intelligence modifier to do so. The base DC for this check is 10, with the following modifiers:

entries.caption: Installation Modifiers
rows: Common Rarity
Uncommon Rarity
Rare Rarity
Very Rare Rarity
Legendary Rarity
Artifact Rarity
Unstable Work Environment
Specialized Work Environment
Artificer Levels
Negative mod. equal to Artificer level.
Proficiency in Tinker's Tools

entries: For further clarification, an Unstable Work Environment might consist as a specially dirty or unsanitary place or an active war zone where the surgeon simply cannot focus properly. On the other hand, an Specialized Work Environment is a clinic, workshop or anything of the sort. This is ultimately up to the DM's clarification of the current environment.
On a failed check, the item is not spent but you must roll on the Surgery Accidents table:

entries.caption: Surgery Accidents
rows: Nothing too egregious happens and any damage caused to the patient is negligible.

There are some mild wounds that will last for a while, causing the patient's Maximum Hit Points to be reduced by an amount equal to double the Rarity Modifier of the Prosthetic as per the above table. ( To a minimum of 2. ) These Maximum Hit Points are recovered at a rate of 1 per short rest and 5 per long rest.
What have you done. The patient must roll on the Lingering Injuries table and suffer its consequences.

entries: If you are attempting to remove a limb, the DC is increased by twice the patient's proficiency bonus instead.

entries.name: Reloading and Ammunition Swapping.
entries: A creature may Reload their weapon as usual even if they still have bullets left to spend, recuperating any ammunition they haven't shot. They may also use different Ammunition Types, such as Arcana Shot or Propulsion Rounds when Reloading their weapon, consuming an amount of the chosen ammunition equal to the weapon's Reload value. If unloaded, any un-shot ammunition is recovered.

entries.name: Blast Cartridge.
entries: A weapon that boasts the Blast Cartridge property is inlaid with a firing mechanism that can be triggered whenever you hit a creature with a melee attack wielding it, spending one appropriate piece of ammunition to do so. ( Usually a bullet. ) Whenever you do, you inflict additional damage equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property. A Blast-Cartridge weapon is considered to have the Reload (1) Property as per loading and managing rounds spent by this Property, unless stated otherwise. These are separate from average Reload Property, if present, as if they were different feeding mechanisms that can be fired at once.

If you are playing on a campaign that does not concern itself with particular tracking of ammunition, you may have your maximum ammunition count be double your proficiency bonus, regaining half that value on a short rest and fully restoring it upon the end of a long rest, as you scrounge around more pieces to refill your spent reserves.

entries.name: Reload.
entries: Weapons with the Reload property have a limited amount of rounds that can be shot before needing to be reloaded. A Reload weapon needs to be reloaded after a certain amount of attacks, with this value being found in parenthesis following the property. To do so, you must spend your Action or Bonus Action to do so - Nevertheless, you cannot take the Attack action using the reloaded weapon until the end of your current turn when you reload it.

entries.name: Orlando Furioso

entries: "Le donne, i cavallier, l'arme, gli amori, le cortesie, l'audaci imprese io canto..."
Something inside you has fundamentally broken, like a realization that was meant to be wasn't ever truly concluded. While Furious, you also gain the following:

items: You gain one Extra Attack.
You gain Advantage on Saving Throws.

Choose one of the weapons in your Arsenal to become your Signature weapon. This weapon becomes bound to you and cannot be used by any other creature. Furthermore, you have a +1 bonus modifier to hit with it and it scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20. This bonus does not benefit your 15th Level feature.
Additionally, when you use your Action Surge while Furious, whenever you hit with a weapon your next weapon attack is done at Advantage.
If you are Two-Weapon Fighting, you may immediately perform an additional attack with the weapon on your off-hand without it counting toward your total attacks.

entries.name: Orlando Innamorato

entries: "Amor mi strinse con sì dolce nodo, che mai da poi non fui di me signore."
Your heart has become a fulfilled thing, your mind enlightened by a confidence in all your work, and your steps silent as you bring others into the black with ease. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your experience has shaped you to be versatile not only with your weaponry, but also with your other abilities.
You gain Expertise in one Skill of your choice that you are Proficient with.
Whenever you hit a Surprised creature or while Hidden you may choose to forgo one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action, instead delivering the full brunt of your force in one decisive attack.

This attack benefits from double the effects of your Poesie per il Silenzio feature (Doubling the value of any range, die or other value.) and deals an additional 3 damage die that match your weapon's damage type.
Whenever you kill another creature or knock them {@condition Unconscious} for the first time you may spend your Reaction to {@action Hide}, as per the Hide Action.

subclassFeature.name: 7th-level Notice
entries: Upon reaching 7th-Level in the Blackened Hands Martial Archetype, choose one of the following class features: Scintille un di Pazzo or Muto Errante.
Upon reaching 18th-Level, you gain the feature corresponding to the one you have picked: Orlando Furioso for Scintille un di Pazzo, and Orlando Innamorato for Muto Errante.

entries.name: Scintille un di Pazzo

entries: "Gridando va, senza dir cosa che s'intenda."

The seed of a growing madness and fury has been planted in your heart, having your personhood and the way you portray yourself be tinted in a darker shade than most. Whenever you suffer damage you may use your Reaction to enter a Fury state. While Furious, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain a bonus modifier to hit and to damage rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
After first knocking another creature below one hit point or killing them, you deal one additional damage die on melee weapon attacks until the end of your next turn.
You suffer a negative modifier to Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

entries: You may enter this state once per long rest and remain in it for one minute. This state ends early if you are knocked {@condition Unconscious} or are the target of the {@spell calm emotions} spell.
You may enter a Fury state twice per long rest after reaching 14th level.

entries.name: Muto Errante

entries: "Rimase Orlando, e non parlò parola."

You are a professional in your line of work, rising to be the brightest star you can be in the only way to know how: obfuscating that shine and only revealing yourself after the job is done. Your Arsenal has developed further, allowing you to coat your hands in a fine black substance that dampens all sound around it, save for your weapons cutting through the air.

You may don and doff this coating as a free action, and while having them on any noise within a 15-ft. radius of you is silenced unless you choose it not to be, except for the sounds of your weapons being fired or swung. While donning the coating you also gain advantage on Stealth Skill Checks that involve sound.
When first gaining this feature, you may choose to gain Proficiency in the Stealth or Sleight of Hand skills, or Expertise if you were already Proficient with the chosen skill.

subclassFeature.name: [Anonymous Roguish Archetype]
entries: You came and you will do your gruesome job, and you won't be remembered for it, but instead by only the terror of your work. Anonymous Rogues are a force to be reckoned with, known both for how unknown their whereabouts and personal details are and for how horrendous their assassinations can become, holding a flourish unlike anything the public could ever imagine before.

entries.name: Anonimity
entries: Your identity is a closely guarded secret, and you with to keep it like that for as long as you can. At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in {@skill Deception}, or expertise if you were already proficient in the skill. In addition to that, you can don or doff costumes in an incredibly fast time, also knowing how to make the most of it.

You gain a bonus to Charisma and Dexterity checks to blend in while wearing a disguise equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. Aditionally, when a feature from this subclass calls for a Saving Throw, you use your Anonymous DC, which is equal to: 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: To Make // Irrecognizable
entries: Upon reaching 3rd level, you're already used to turning a slab of meat into a surgeon's worst nightmare. When you reduce a creature below one hit point, you may use your reaction to mangle their corpse beyond recognition or salvation. If they somehow survive, they maximum hit points are reduced by one roll of your Sneak Attack die, only being restored by a Restoration spell or greater means. Upon reaching 13th level and using this feature, the damage instead is only recoverable through the means of a Greater Restoration spell or similarly higher level spells.

Additionally, upon doing this, a sense of despair washes over any creature that was able to see the horrible act. Any creature that can see the scene must pass your a Wisdom Saving throw against your Anonymous DC. On a failure, they must either roll a d4 or have the DM choose the most appropriate reaction of theirs to the scene:
