entries.caption: Irrecognizable
rows: {@b Blind Rage.} Some are still thinking about a fallen friend, and are overtaken by the need of revenge for such atrocities. The creature gains advantage on their next attack, yet all attacks against it have disadvantage until the end of your next turn.

{@b Silent Sorrow.} To become shaken is a natural reaction, a failure for the brain to respond. The creature has a penalty to their {@skill Perception} and to their Wisdom Saving Throws until the end of your next turn that equals half of your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
{@b Bodily Reaction.} They just can't breathe in the scene, puke billowing out their mouth. The creature takes a number of d8 poison damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Paralyzing Fear.} No movement, like a deer caught in headlights. The creatures movement speec is reduced by 5 times your Proficiency Bonus until the end of your next turn.

entries: A creature can only be affected by this feature once per turn, and creatures with immunity against being {@condition Frightened} have advantage on this saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: A Chi Piange Questa Spada

entries: "A chi la impugna, questa spada è morte;"
The manifestations from your inner self have rooted deeply in your heart, blossoming out into an even stronger Arsenal that flows as easily as you breathe. You gain the following benefits:

items: Weapons linked to your Arsenal cannot be destroyed by any means other than the {@spell wish} spell, even if you die.

When attacking with a weapon linked to your Arsenal, you always use the bonus modifier of the highest magical weapon stored in your Arsenal, such as if you attack with a +1 dagger but have linked a +3 sword, you may instead consider the dagger as if it had a +3 modifier instead.
You have advantage against being {@condition Grappled} and skill checks regarding being disarmed in any way.

subclassFeature.name: A Just Vengeance
entries: Your family has only empowered you further, and the more enemies you strike down, the more benefits you reap for your loyalty. Once you reach 6th level, your Unarmed Strike damage dice changes to {@dice 1d8}. Additionally, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, choose one of the two options below:

entries.name: Brush it Off.
entries: Gain temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Unarmed Strike damage dice plus your rage bonus.

entries.name: Ready to Write.
entries: Gain a +1 bonus for your attack and damage rolls for the duration of the combat against enemies with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}.
Your Unarmed Strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

subclassFeature.name: A Lone Firefly's Path
entries: The fire in your heart has not dimmed and will keep on fighting as long as you can have more lights around you, having burned enough to turn your Firefist Engine into a near perfect creation. When you spend any Fuel, the fire damage you deal ignores a target creature's Resistance to fire damage and considers Immune creatures to only be Resistant instead.

Additionally, you may spend your bonus action or a reaction when you would become {@condition Charmed||Charmed}, {@condition Frightened||Frightened} or suffer any Enchantment spell effects that you are aware of you may spend 5 Igniter Fuel to set yourself ablaze, suffering 6 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} Count and immediately ending the condition or effect. While burning this way, all your Fuel is considered Overheated Fuel. You may do this an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, regaining spent uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: A Most Beautiful Touch
entries: When you reach 3rd level, you know your way on how to let prey feel the encroaching force of your Whip. You gain the two following abilities:

entries.name: Thrill of the Hunt.
entries: As an action, you may spend a Bardic Inspiration dice to use your Rosé Whip to force a creature within 30-feet of you to roll a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer one roll of your Bardic Inspiration's worth of piercing damage and then the same number of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks. You cannot use this action while grappling a creature through Embrace of Thorns. You may also use this skill outside of combat to make a short 5-ft. wide suspended bridge that connects where you stand to one point within range. This is considered Difficult Terrain and breaks under the weight of a Large or greater creature.

entries.name: Embrace of Thorns.
entries: As an action, you may spend a Bardic Inspiration dice to use your Rosé Whip to force a creature within 30-feet of you to roll a Dexterity Saving Throw or be grappled by your Whip, which can be destroyed by hitting it. Your Whip has 10 times your Bard level HP and an AC of 8, with vulnerability to fire and necrotic damage. Only one creature may be grappled at once, and while grappled they gain half the result of one roll of your Bardic Inspiration dice in {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks on the start of their turn, rounded up. A creature that is of size Large or greater has advantage on this Saving Throw. The grappled creature is freed upon breaking the Whip.

subclassFeature.name: A Thorn of Intense Will

entries: "The power to cleanse filth with fire... Indeed, it was certainly a good idea to listen to her."

Doubting your faith has become a far-away thought of times long gone, it has seeped through your bones and granted you the willpower to trudge through anything. Whenever you kill a creature during Rage, your desire to purge screams with pride. You gain an additional attack as part of your Attack Action until the end of your next turn and instantly gain {@dice 1d12} Temporary Hit Points which last until the end of your next turn.

Additionally, whenever you fail an ability check, you may choose to suffer {@damage 1d12} psychic damage to grant yourself an {@dice 1d6} bonus modifier to your next ability check within one hour. If this ability check would affect, is targeted at or against a Target of your Ire, gain a {@dice 2d4} bonus modifier instead.

subclassFeature.name: A Tool That Punctures a Hole in the Heart

entries: "Survival matters the most... I'll do anything for it."

The rough path that your lifestyle brought you has shaped you into someone who can make the most of themselves and keep living another night no matter which horde comes knocking down your door, no matter the reason why. You gain the following:

items: When you inflict {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesNA} for the first time, inflict an additional count.
Whenever you deal piercing damage, deal an additional {@damage 2d6} piercing damage.
While below half your maximum hit points you gain an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and add half your proficiency bonus as a bonus modifier to Dexterity and Wisdom saving throws.
While below half your maximum hit points you cannot be targeted by Opportunity Attacks.
You inflict double the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you would when you trigger a Critical Hit.

subclassFeature.name: Abraxas Chariot Martial Archetype

entries: "Every now and then, I find myself thinking back... to the days I spent aboard that bus. Those memories... might be the only things that keep me going in the days to come.."

There are many children who walk upon the world, no matter which. Yet there is a differential present within those that one day will grow to embody the Archetype of the Abraxas Chariot, those that rush through the fine line between the world of light and the world of darkness - Having come to accept the necessity of others and the orders that uphold the world while not denying or shying away from the fear that lingers through every shadow one may see, welcoming the wholeness of oneself.

Despite that, they are often born in wartorn lands, where conflict has forced them to suffer through vile events that have scarred not only their bodies but their minds, often forcing them to pick up a weapon at first for defense against having their innocence broken, yet soon after raising it toward protecting and nourishing their own world between.

At their best, they are brilliant leaders who descend like angels wherever their feet touches the ground, while at their worst they may be cruel as a devil and even be considered flippant about the most horrible things. In either way, their good and bad goes hand in hand, as is the true mark of those who look upon Abraxas for guidance.

entries.name: Historian's Note: Making an Abraxas Chariot...
entries: Many of these subclasses themes involve war and a violent conflict, yet you need not concern yourself to being forced upon that niche to create a character who still fits its mold - Consider instead other types of conflict that may have shaped your character, such as that of having the paradigms of their life crack open and leave them in search of a new balance to order their own being around, or a conflict of ideals that can be either a form of inner turmoil or with an outsider. The possibilities are vast as to where to take the flavour of this subclass, and we do hope you enjoy that process as much as we did creating it!

entries.name: Abate the Smoke

entries: "I, too, once sought the answer from knowledge."

So much has come and gone, yet you still remember your roots - spread deep through Wartorn land and fed by the blood left in your wake. Your place in the world is self-driven, blowing past the obstacles in front of you with a force that only one raised in conflict could boast. When you reach this level, you gain the following:

items: You have felt the weight of your blade in your hands many times, memorized it truly was no more than an extension. Whenever hit with a creature with a weapon attack you also inflict {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. Whenever you deal a Critical Hit or a Posture Critical Hit, you inflict the same {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count an additional time.

Whenever you kill a creature, you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus. Additionally, you gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you first hit a creature during your turn.

Your attacks are dispelling forces in their own might, cutting through 30-ft. lines of gale whenever you perform an attack roll. This manifests either as a general wind or a specific cut, that being slicing through and rendering clear any smoke within 15-ft. long cone in a direction of your choice whenever you perform an attack roll.

entries.name: Rough-hewn Path

entries: "It invaded the mind and clouded the judgement of the victim."

Your upbringing wasn't the best, but it made you become something near that regarding your skills to keep living another day. You gain Proficiency in the {@skill Survival} skill, or Expertise if you were already Proficient in it.

subclassFeature.name: Absolute Path of Paved Ambitions
entries: You have become the splitting image of a powerful Lord, leading on your fellows in battle with unparalleled might and shaping the world to your vision. You gain the following benefits:

items: The reach of your Aura of a Lord increases by 5-ft at the end of your turn if you have not moved from the space you started your turn in. Furthermore, you gain Advantage on Strength Saving Throws and Skill Checks against being moved while your Aura has increased reach. Your Aura of a Lord may increase in this way for a maximum reach of 60-ft and resets when you move or are moved.
Whenever a creature you can see is killed or knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} within 60-ft of you, you gain an additional use of your Reaction until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Accelerating Future

entries: "Feelin' confident? Then parry this, asshole."

As a battle drives on, you have learned how to mark your favored enemies, focusing all of your wrath on a specific being instead of lashing out wildly like a volcano. You may choose to make the last creature you attacked on your turn become your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesPP}. When you hit your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesPP} with an attack roll, once per turn, you may choose to convert all of their counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremor Scorch}. Furthermore, whenever you apply counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesPP}, they suffer 1 additional count of each applied.

Additionally, you have learned how to devote extra energy to your {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP} to calculate the most likely outcome of the near future. As an action, you can expend 5 counts of your {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP} to see 1 minute into the future and discover what the most possible outcomes are. Alternatively, by suffering 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion}, you can see 10 minutes into the future instead.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This ability is left more vague on purpose for DMs and players to have more fun with it, however, I think it's important to give an example of how it can and can't be used to make it clearer.

Let's say you're trying to find out what to bet on in a cassino, or what an NPC will say before they say it - those things are fully under the DM's control and he should be able to disclose the most likely future according to the perception of your eye.

However, things outside of the DM's control, such as what a player character would do/say or the outcome of a combat decided by the dice, are much less likely to be predicted, so your eyes can provide an incorrect assessment of the furure, or no assessment at all.

subclassFeature.name: Active Reload
entries: When you reach 10th level, you come to a point where you can compromise on spending a little more of your precious Ammunition. Once per short rest, you may perform an Active Reload as a bonus action.

When you do so, you recover {@dice 1d8}+(PB/2) Ammunition. Additionally, when you do so, you may say one number from 1-8 out loud. If the die's result equals the value spoken, you perform a perfectly timed reload, gaining a six stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and gaining a +1 bonus to hit on your next attack.
You may use this feature again after spending its free use by spending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Adept's Cloud-Spitting Ascent

entries: "I have endured it all."

You have become used to being in your {@i Stormrider Form}, allowing your stance to become perfected. You may perform an additional attack whenever you take the {@action Attack} Action within your {@i Stormrider Form} and your base movement speed is increased by 5-ft.
Additionally, upon reaching this level you may perform the following as an Action by spending a Druid spell slot:

entries.name: Obsidian Stormrider's Crescent Decapitator [黑風馬脚月斬]
entries: You swing your weapon wildly as you go on a thundering stampede that covers a 10-ft. wide line that has a length equal to 10-ft. per Spell slot level spent and that you may change the direction of at each 20-ft. travelled. All creatures within that area must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Druid Spell Save DC or be trampled, suffering an amount of {@damage d10} bludgeoning damage equal to double the Spell slot level spent and being knocked {@condition prone}, then suffering an amount of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the Spell slot level spent.

subclassFeature.name: Advanced Decompression
entries: You have furthered your means of using the time you compress, putting it through advanced uses as needed. You gain access to the options in the Time Decompression table.

entries.caption: Time Decompression
rows: Physiological Rewind
5 per Turn Rewound (maximum 15)

As an action, you unwind your body, restoring your hit points to what they were one turn before for every 5 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} spent, to a maximum of rewinding three turns for 15 counts. Once you use this option, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Re:Cast
Twice the Spell Slot's Level

You can spend {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} to cast a spell you have cast previously during this combat without expending a spell slot. The cost equals twice the spell slot level you use. For example, casting {@spell magic missile|PHB|Magic Missile} at 2nd level costs 4 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC}.
Hasten

As a bonus action, you decompress an abundance of time onto a friendly creature within 60 feet of you, granting it the positive effects of the {@spell haste|PHB|Haste} spell until the end of its next turn.
Quick Wind

As a bonus action, you quicken the next spell you cast. A casting time of 1 minute becomes 1 action, a casting time of 10 minutes becomes 1 minute, and a casting time of 1 hour becomes 10 minutes. You cannot use ritual spellcasting with this option.

entries: Furthermore, the first time during a combat that you knock a creature {@condition Unconscious|PHB} or kill it, you can use your reaction to absorb and compact its time, gaining a number of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} counts equal to its proficiency bonus. This does not work on summoned creatures, such as those spawned from a Bag of Teeth.

subclassFeature.name: All-Beholding Gaze
entries: Your eyes leave nothing untraced, even the dust beneath your feet should be graced with your acknowledgement - The realization of how low they are compared to you. As such, you cannot be Surprised and you always have a +5 modifier to your Passive {@skill Perception} score.
Additionally, magical darkness and illusions do not obscure your perception unless the source is of 3rd level or higher.

subclassFeature.name: Allez
entries: When your initiative count is higher than that of your target, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with a rapier. This bonus increases to +2 when you reach 10th level.

Additionally, when you hit a creature with a rapier, you gain 2 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and the target gains 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and you may choose to apply one stack of {@condition Focused Attack|TheUndertomesMS}.
You add a +1 to your attack and damage rolls against a creature for each attack it has made with advantage or disadvantage on its last turn.
This ability applies only when wielding a rapier.

subclassFeature.name: Ammunition Tributary

entries: "Let's get ready... Before our superiors with even higher authority have to intervene..."

You've been taught - No, you've had the rules etched to your very brainstem lest it is removed. You are to distinguish between bullet types, know how to produce them when asked to and when to spend them yourself. You are proficient in Firearms and may, once per turn after triggering a {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1}, draw from your Reserves by rolling on the following table:

entries.caption: Ammunition Types
rows: Armor Piercing Rounds
Attack rolls made with this ammunition consider the target's AC as if it were one number lower.
Flame Rounds
Damage rolls made with this ammunition deal fire damage and inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half of the user's proficiency bonus.
Frost Rounds
Damage rolls made with this ammunition deal cold damage and cause the target to suffer a stacking -1 modifier to their attack rolls until the start of the user's next turn.
Shock Rounds

Damage rolls made with this ammunition force the target to make a Strength check against a DC equal to 8 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your proficiency bonus, suffering {@damage 2d8} an additional thunder damage and being pushed back 10-ft. on a hit.

entries: After doing so, you immediately Reload your currently wielded firearm with the resulting ammunition type. It counts as an amount of bullets appropriate to your currently wielded weapon's Reload property.

These ammunition types have their effects take place whenever you hit a creature on an attack made with them, for an amount of attacks equal to the remaining bullets before you need to reload as per the Reload property.

Additionally, you have been imparted with the knowledge of how to make the most of any ammunitions gunpowder, causing your ranged weapon attacks to inflict an amount {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half the damage die they would deal, to a minimum of one.
Upon reaching 5th level you may toss that Ammunition toward another creature within 30-ft. of you, instantly Reloading their weapon with the rolled ammunition instead.

subclassFeature.name: An Old Trade

entries: It knows every children s story and will not stop recounting until the listener finally leaves.

Tales aren’t the only thing one must learn to truly orate, as there are a few things one must know to truly be able to understand them - The weight of a weapon used, how the subject of a tale spun around craftsmanship was painstakingly created, it all needs practical experience. You gain proficiency in your choice of Firearms or one Martial Weapon of your choice and one Artisan’s Kit.

Furthermore, whenever you would deal damage to a creature suffering from Solitude using a weapon whose proficiency you’ve gained from this ability or a cantrip, you deal an additional {@dice 1d6} psychic damage per Solitude stage afflicting it, such as {@dice 1d6} at first and {@dice 3d6} at third

subclassFeature.name: Anatomize

entries: "Let us explore together-the pulsations of your remaining life."

Taking parts of others for your creations, your art, is something you have learned to do with great pride. You acquire one {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} after such.

Additionally, you gain Proficiency with the {@skill Nature} skill. If you already have Proficiency with it, you gain Expertise instead. Your anatomical knowledge knows no bounds, and you always have advantage on anatomy-related checks.

entries.name: My, How We Love the Flesh and the Blood.
entries: If a {@subclass Iron Maiden|Druid|PHB|TheUndertomesIM|Circle of the Iron Maiden} Druid is within 30 feet of you and makes an attack roll, you can use your Reaction to give that attack advantage. If it hits, it deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage and the creature suffers 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This number increases to 2 at level 5, 3 at level 11 and 4 at level 17. After using this ability, if the {@subclass Iron Maiden|Druid|PHB|TheUndertomesIM|Circle of the Iron Maiden} Druid gains {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} due to this attack, you gain the same amount.

subclassFeature.name: Announcer of Grandiosity
entries: As you reach 6th level, you not only put on a show with your gracious moves, but also with words of true inspiration! If you are not surprised, you may spend one Bardic Inspiration dice and your reaction when combat would start, before rolling initiative, to unleash from your sharp as thorns tongue a short monologue to inspire your allies to do their best.
When you do so, all creatures of your choice within 30-feet of yourself may add a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die to their Initiative Bonus, rolled once for each.

subclassFeature.name: Arcana Pierce

entries: "Tears fall like ash, embroidered as if they were constellations."

You have reached the culmination of your suffering and guilt, and as your swords pierce you, they bring forth all manner of emotions that flood and mold the battlefield with their crushing weight. As an action, you gain {@condition Sharpened by Tears|TheUndertomesDD|Tear-Sharpened}. Then, if you are in Blessing Mode, as part of the same action, choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature). If a chosen creature made an attack roll on its previous turn, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, your swords pierce it, and it becomes {@condition Restrained||restrained} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it is not restrained, but it gains 2 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Arcana: Tear and Pierce
entries: If you are in Despair Mode, you instead immediately cast {@spell spiritual weapon|PHB|Spiritual Weapon} without expending a spell slot. If you expend a spell slot, the spell is cast at 5th level regardless of the slot's actual level. While you are concentrating on this {@spell spiritual weapon|PHB|Spiritual Weapon}, all your spell attacks apply 2 additional counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Electrical Discharge Discipline Arcane Tradition
entries: Knowledge is a hard-woven line threaded within the history of those who perceive it, used both in further referencing works or building upon the future with exact precision. Wizards who have chosen to study the A.E.D.D. Arcane Tradition are some who have decided to be meticulous about the very base energies who comprise the world, and to learn how to interface and use said energies - Wether purely arcane or electrical.

They are, at their bests, blossoming masters of their field with theoretical knowledge that could engage with that of an archmage with only little difficulty, yet this dedication to their craft often leads them to be seen as reckless or even destructive in search of results, even more-so considering the risks they may come to accept for the furthering of a thesis instead of the prolonguing of their own lives.

In worlds such as Eberron, these are the ones responsible from tearing all that could be learnt from the war down and inscribe it in new ways to be used by all civilizations, or in others such as Keygen these are the diamonds in the rough spread inbetween the mega-corporations that littler the world - Those destined to burn down everything if it means producing a trickle of light that all else can follow.

subclassFeature.name: Artful Extra Attack

entries: "Please, do share your impressions!"

Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Additionally, whenever you land a Critical Hit, you get to add your Charisma modifier to the damage.

subclassFeature.name: Artist's Zone

entries: "Against the beautiful liberation of the repressed flesh upon shedding the encasement."

Freeing your body is a spectacle in of itself, the act of repressing your flesh being like marinating a great meal only to reveal its glory sporadically to ensure that this exhibition will be as close to perfection as can be. Whenever you enter your Flowing Form, you gain the following:

items: Your movement speed increases by 5-ft. and whenever you take the {@action Dash} Action, your AC increases by 2 until the end of your turn.
Any armor you were wearing is cast off with your Iron Maiden, instead granting you an AC equal to 12 + your Wisdom Modifier.
You are considered proficient with Martial Weapons and you always deal half your proficiency bonus in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you hit a creature.

You may choose, whenever you suffer damage, to become Vulnerable to its damage type for the attack. When you do so, you gain one count of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} for each 8 damage suffered this way.
You may use your spell attack modifier for melee weapon attacks.

entries: Additionally, whenever you hit a creature you may spend up to half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} to enrichen your weapons thirst for even more material, dealing an additional {@damage 1d4} damage of the weapon's type on that attack. This increases to {@damage 1d6} damage when you reach 8th level in Druid, and finally {@damage 1d8} at 14th level.
Furthermore, choose one Charisma skill you are proficient in when first gaining this feature. Whenever you enter your Flowing Form, you are considered to have Expertise with it instead.

subclassFeature.name: As Written
entries: The Mao Branch knows that speed equals strength and has vowed to become the fastest. Immediately after you use Blinkstep, choose one creature you can see within your reach. If its speed is lower than yours, it suffers 1 stack of {@condition Deathrite Haste|TheUndertomesMW}.

Additionally, your instincts draw closer to those of a rabbit, allowing you to carve a path through the earth. You gain a burrowing speed of 30 feet, but can burrow only through nonmagical, nonsolid materials such as dirt, sand, clay, or soft earth. You leave behind a 5-foot-wide tunnel through which other creatures can crawl or use as three-quarters cover.

subclassFeature.name: Assassination Techniques
entries: Through your career, you've picked up a handful of necessary techniques to best perform an assassination, from the best breathing styles in certain scenarios to how to endure for hours at an end in a single combat. You gain the following Assassination Techniques:

items: Deflect Assault. When you would take damage from an attack or a spell that targets only you and before its damage die are rolled, you may use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the AC of the attacker or spellcaster, unleashing your weapon in a vicious attempt to diminish the pain you're about to receive. On a hit, you reduce the damage you take from the triggering effect by an amount equal to your weapon's damage roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down), regaining all expended uses on a short rest.

Endless Battle. At the start of your second turn in combat, and at the start of every turn thereafter, you gain 2 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} as your practiced breathing rhythm keeps your focus steady when most would only exhaust to their limits quickly.

Avoiding the End. Each time you move and feel the pain flare from your fresh wounds a surge of adrenaline shoots down your body, desperate to avoid your own assassination. While you are not wearing medium or heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC for each missing Chunk of hit points.

subclassFeature.name: Astral Mapper
entries: You gain proficiency in Cartographer’s Tools and may use them to easily find your way towards any landmark you know, preventing you from becoming lost as long as you can see the starry sky.

subclassFeature.name: Aura de Sangre
entries: "Blood must continue to flow, to sate more of my family..." You exude an intense sanguine aura that makes your allies' blood boil. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you gain +1 to their AC and +1 to their attack rolls if they're below half their hit points or have counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever they kill a hostile creature, they gain a number of d4s in temporary hit points equal to half your proficiency bonus modifier.

Additionally, whenever a creature within 10 feet of you that is friendly to you falls to 0 hit points or dies, you gain {@condition Responsibility|TheUndertomesDE}. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of a Lord
entries: Your pure, unadulterated presence forms into a magical aura that expands around you as you breathe, bolstering your allies' resolve in unique ways. A friendly creature within 10-ft of you gains one of the following benefits according to their class:

entries.caption: Aura of a Lord
rows: Artificer
The Artificer adds half of your Charisma Modifier to their Flash of Genius bonus.
Barbarian
The Barbarian has an {@dice 1d4} reduction to any damage they take while within the Aura.
Bard
Whenever a creature would benefit from the Bard's Bardic Inspiration die, they also gain an additional {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier.
Cleric

As long as the Cleric or a creature they are targeting are within your Aura, the Clerics spells either deal an additional {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage on a hit or failed Saving Throw or heal for an additional {@dice 1d6} hit points when healing another creature.
Druid
The Druid gains two rolls of your Divine Smite die as Temporary Hit Points when they enter Wildshape. Those last until they are reduced to 0 or the Druid leaves Wildshape.
Fighter
The Fighter is healed by an additional amount equal to two rolls of your Divine Smite die when they use Second Wind.
Monk
The Monk may use an additional Unarmed Attack during their Flurry of Blows.
Paladin
Other friendly Paladins gain an additional Divine Smite damage die.
Ranger
The Ranger deals an additional d8 radiant damage against their Favored Foe.
Rogue
The Rogue gains one additional Sneak Attack damage die.
Sorcerer
The Sorcerer gains a 1 point Metamagic cost reduction while within your Aura. The cost for using a Metamagic Option cannot go below 1 Metamagic Point spent.
Wizard
The Wizard's spells are upcast to be one level higher (If able) if you spend one of your spell slots to empower theirs, doing so when they would cast a spell but you don't spend a Reaction to do so.
Warlock: Blade
The Warlock has a bonus modifier to hit creatures as long as either are within your Aura while wielding their Pact Weapon. This bonus equals half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
Warlock: Chain
The Pact Familiar may perform an attack without the Warlock needing to sacrifice one of their own attacks to do so, provided that either the Warlock or Familiar are within your Aura.
Warlock: Talisman
The Warlock gains an additional bonus to their Talisman re-rolls equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
Warlock: Tome
The Warlock gains a bonus to hit creatures with Cantrips while they or the target are within your Aura. This bonus equals half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.

entries: If a creature within your aura doesn't have a class, it benefits to the closest fitting effect as per your DM's choice, and unless the DM decides so, summoned creatures do not gain any benefit from this. If a player is Multiclassing, they choose which of their classes to benefit from this at the combat's start.
Furthermore, you may spend your Reaction in the following situations to directly order and advise friendly creatures within the aura:

items: {@b Lordsguard.} As long as a creature has another friendly creature within 5-ft of them and either is targeted by an attack, you may spend your Reaction to give one of them an Assist Order. When you do so, the creature defends the other as best they can, imposing Disadvantage on the attacking creature's attacks until the end of their turn. When your Aura is upgraded, you also grant the target a bonus modifier to their AC that equals half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. This lasts until the start of the defended creature's turn.

{@b Exalted Command.} As long as a creature is able to hear you, you may spend your reaction when they would perform an attack, but before rolling, to order them to perform an Exalted Attack instead. When they do so, they add half your Charisma Modifier to hit and on a hit, deal half your Divine Smite's damage die of Divine Damage, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Instability

entries: "Potentially dangerous individual identified. Moving in to suppress."

Wherever you walk, the weight of your armor and arsenal are felt - for your allies, the quaking in your wake brings the image of a bastion, and for your foes a stark declaration of being ubreakable. You emanate an aura of vibrating quakes while you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|PHB}, making it so that whenever a creature of your choice within 10-ft. of you is hit by an attack roll or fails a saving throw they suffer an amount of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Lamentation
entries: You emanate an aura that fills all nearby creatures with endless grief, which overflows and consumes their very core at each strike of your weapons. Starting on 7th level, as long as you're not incapacitated, you and all allied creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you may choose to deal psychic damage to creatures instead of any other damage type they would commonly deal. Additionally, when you hit a creature with psychic damage, they gain a stack of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Magnificence
entries: Starting at 7th level, your radiant charisma inspires awe in those near you. You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you gain a bonus to Charisma saving throws and Charisma-based skill checks equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1).

In addition, whenever you hit with a weapon attack, you deal an extra {@dice 1d4} radiant damage if at least one other friendly creature is within your aura. This extra damage increases to {@dice 1d6} at 14th level and to {@dice 1d8} at 18th level.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Onus

entries: "Seest thou? Verily, the Prescript is absolute!"
Starting at 7th level, your sheer feeling of duty spreads and covers those around you like an invisible membrane. This aura covers 10-ft. around you while you are not {@condition Incapacitated}.

At the start of any creature's turns provided that they are within the area, they may partake into one Prescript that manifests in front of them, gaining one count of Grace of the Prescript upon its completion, or suffering two counts of Karmic Consequence when failing to complete them until the start of their next turn.

To define a Prescript, it is recommended to roll on the Magicked Prescripts Table found at the end of this document When you take a Prescript in this way, you have two turns to complete it (Ending at the start of the turn after your next one.) and you gain an additional count of Grace of the Prescript upon a Prescript's completion.
Additionally, upon reaching 7th level in this subclass you may use your /UNLOCK./ Channel Divinity without spending a use of the feature, but instead suffering 2 counts of Karmic Consequence.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Ordainment
entries: The dirty infidels who go against your word will be left no qualm, each turn your incessant will buffets their spirits like blows to the very soul. At the start of your turn, roll your Order Die, any creature of your choice within your Aura's reach suffer the value rolled as a negative modifier on attack rolls and saving throws.
In addition, you gain the two following effects:

items: Your Order Die increase to d6s.

You may use the Defend me! reaction when you would be targetted for an attack, before any roll is made. When you do so, you may choose for a friendly creature within your Aura's reach to become the new target for this attack, also granting them a bonus to their AC equal to one roll of your Order Die, to a maximum value equal to your Proficiency Modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Preservation

entries: "There can be no hesitation nor failure, for the Obsidian God watcheth over us."

Beginning at 7th level, each step you take becomes a hallmark of hallowed land. You and friendly creatures within 5-ft. of you gain an additional {@dice d10} Temporary Hit Points whenever they would gain those, with creatures other than you that are within reach also gaining 3 {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} count whenever you grant them Temporary Hit Points, to a maximum amount equal to your proficiency bonus plus two if they cannot generate the Condition on their own. ( Such as with Subclass Features. ) Additionally, all Noir-aligned creatures within the area gain an additional count of {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} whenever they would gain it.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of the Big Brother

entries: "... The one that's gonna exterminate the whole bloody lot o' you bastards!"
You emit a powerful and intimidating aura out to a range of 10 feet. If all friendly creatures within the aura have more than half of their hit points, they gain a +2 to their Charisma-based rolls.

When a friendly creature within the aura has less than half of their Hit Points, other creatures can choose to become Vengeful at the start of their turn. A Vengeful creature takes a penalty of -3 to their AC and whenever they're hit they suffer 1 count of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} but always doubles their bludgeoning, slashing and piercing damage dice against a creature that attacked them or a friendly creature they know within the last turn. Additionally, if these creatures would suffer counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they suffer double that amount on the first time they gain one of these Conditions before the start of their next turn.
When you reach 18th level in this class, the range of the aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Turbulence
entries: Starting at 7th level, you start imposing your feelings on the world around you much like a tulpa. Your Paladin's Aura gains the following effects according to your current look:

rows: Sorrow

{@b Dreadful Aura.} All creatures of your choice must make a Charisma Saving Throw when they enter your aura or become {@condition Frightened} of you until they leave, as a crawling paranoia washes over their thoughts.
Elation

{@b Ecstatic Aura.} All creatures of your choice inside your aura feel more energetic to go through life, gaining the benefits from the {@spell guidance|PHB|Guidance} spell. They may only use this benefit every other roll.
Wrath
{@b Murderous Aura.} All hostile creatures inside your aura take an additional amount of radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus, as your rage makes open tears open even more fiercely.
Apathy
{@b Unimpressed.} All friendly creatures inside your aura take less damage equal to your proficiency bonus, as every blow seems to strike more lazily.

subclassFeature.name: Avatar of the Obsidian God

entries: "And thus saith the Lord: 'Unto Le Noir be contentment, and unto the Brand Manager be tribulation and hammer.'"
With this sacred duty in mine hand, I call thee to answer: art thou an adherent of the rules, or… a fomenter of anarchy?"

HIS eyes have fallen onto your back, filling your heart with the utmost radiance and the everlasting presence of le Noir, and it is through your hands that HIS will shall be done - Unquestionable and unerring. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing and Radiant damage, also gaining Immunity against Necrotic damage and any kind of Bite attacks.

Whenever you deal damage to a creature using your Divine Smite you gain half the damage dealt in Temporary Hit Points, which can stack with already existing Temporary Hit Points. These vanish after the duration ends.

You may harken to the grand Voice of the Obsidian God for its blessing as a Reaction whenever you would fall below 1 Hit Point for them to impose the will unto your body, weaving back together torn tissue, gluing bones to their righteous place and letting your heart be the one to bring forth your will to fight. When you do so, you restore all your missing Hit Points, spell slots and any other Paladin and magic item-based resources to the amount they were in at the beginning of combat.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, and its use isn't restored as part of the Reaction granted by this Feature. You may use this Reaction only once per transformation.

subclassFeature.name: Bathed in Love and Justice!
entries: You're even better at manifesting your love now! Starting from 10th level, you may use a bonus action or as a free action when entering rage to magically change into your Magical Girl Outfit, which grants half your proficiency modifier as a bonus to your AC. While in this form, you can treat any Charisma-based skill check as if you were proficient in any of its respective skills, or expertise if you were already proficient with them. You also suffer disadvantage on {@skill Insight} checks while transformed, as the world seems oh so much colorful to you, and you just need to focus on protecting that beautiful color. On that same note, you become vulnerable to psychic damage, yet you gain double the amount of {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG} stacks you normally would when suffering that type of damage as the disembodied whispers of your own hatred sink in.

In addition, this form lasts for up to an hour and you may end it early as a free action. You may use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency modifier, regaining its uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Beast of the Black Forest
entries: {@i In iustitia confidimus, ad nostram protectionem et poenam eorum qui nobis audent laedere.}

The Beast alone remains after darkness fell unto the Black Forest, a far-away place in any world that some regard as a demiplane where a child may become lost in when trying to travel through the woods at night, while others see it as the place seen deep within a bloody puddle left where no other person is.

Nevertheless, it seeks for a grim "protection" of all things living, offering to take a handful of the lost fools who wander into its woods under its sky-covering wings, turning them intoWarlocks of the Beast of the Black Forest, who become afflicted with the same agony over all the existing evil that surrounds the world.
A Warlock of such an Otherworldly Patron must take the following Oath in recognition of their service to a greater ordeal:

items: {@i "None shall lose their way under my witness."} Whenever a creature would cause another to become {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened} or otherwise under the effects of an enchantment spell.
{@i "No evil deed shall go unpunished for as far as my wings reach."} Whenever a creature would cause another to become {@condition Unconscious}, be killed or suffer a Critical Hit.
{@i "No failure to uphold the greater good will be missed by my justice."} Whenever a creature fails a saving throw.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List

entries: "Then, in the middle of all the chaotic cries, someone shouted:'It's the beast! A big, scary monster lives in the black, dusky forest!'"
The Beast of the Black Forest lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell.The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Black Forest Pact Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell detect evil and good|PHB|Detect Evil and Good}, {@spell dissonant whispers|PHB|Dissonant Whispers}
2nd
{@spell phantasmal force|PHB|Phantasmal Force}, {@spell Tasha's mind whip|TCE|Tasha's Mind Whip}
3rd
{@spell bestow curse|PHB|Bestow Curse}, {@spell blinding smite|PHB|Blinding Smite}
4th
{@spell dominate beast|PHB|Dominate Beast}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
5th
{@spell commune|PHB|Commune}, {@spell geas|PHB|Geas}

entries.name: Relicary of the Lost Guardians

entries: "Why do they commit sins, knowing it's wrong?"

You have been granted the blessings of the Beast, being able to call upon them at a time of need. \As an action during your turn you may summon the following three Relics of the Black Forest, symbols of the Beast of which you can, as part of this action, touch and become attuned to for the next minute.They are as follows:

entries.caption: Relics of the Black Forest
rows: Weight of Justice

A blunt greatsword wrapped in black feathers and bandages alike. It is a {@item Greatsword|PHB} of which you have proficiency using, yet it counts as if it were dealing slashing, bludgeoning and piercing damage instead of slashing por the purposes of eploiting Vulnerabilities and ignoring Immunities of its targets. While attuned to this weapon you gain an additional 10-ft. of movement and an extra attack as part of the {@action Attack} action. Upon reaching 10th level in Warlock this weapon also counts as if it dealt force damage.
Lamp-Lit Eyes

A billowing overcoat of black feathers covered in swirling yellow eyes. You gain a +1 bonus modifier to your AC and {@skill Perception} checks while attuned as described below, also being able to spend your reaction when you are hit with an attack or when you are targetted by a spell to force the creature who incurred this reaction to pass a Charisma saving throw or become Enchanted by you. An enchanted creature is {@condition Charmed} by you and must spend all their movement speed during your turn to move closer to you, no matter what harm might be in the way.
All-Devouring Stomach

You gain an internal organ that devours violence and ill-intent, but it is not a thing for an unbeastly body to bear, causing you to have a -2 negative modifier to hit and to damage rolls while attuned. However, you ignore these negative modifiers when targeting a creature that has dealt damage to you during their last turn until the end of your next turn, instead dealing an additional damage die of the same type as your attack's on a Critical Hit. Furthermore, you deal a Critical Hit against such targets on a dice roll of 19-20.

entries: Each relic grows in power in tandem with you, becoming greater when you reach certain levels in Warlock:

items: Weight of Justice becomes a +1 magical weapon when you reach 6th level, +2 when you reach 10th level and +3 when you reach 16th level.
Lamp-Lit Eyes grants a further +1 bonus when you reach 6th level, another at 10th level and a further one at 16th level.

All-Devouring Stomach deals an additional damage die and your Critical Hit dice roll becomes a 18-20 at 6th level, another damage die and a Critical dice roll of 17-20 at 12th and a last damage die at 16th level, alongside a Critical on a roll of 16-20.

entries: You can do this once per long rest, needing to spend a Warlock spell slot any other time you wish to do this.You may only become attuned to one of the Relics at any given time, and they vanish after becoming attuned to one or after one minute, if attuned.

entries.name: Sacrifice to a Beast

entries: "If I kill the creatures first, then no one would be killed by the beast!"

Much as your master has given part of itself to become what it is today, so have you to do its bidding, be that done in a manner of solidarity or as the steep cost of becoming a Warlock of the Beast.When you first choose this Otherwordly Patron you must choose from the following three sacrifices, also gaining boons from the Beast:

entries.caption: Sacrifices to the Beast
rows: Instinctus

{@b Sharpened Beak;} You gave away your innocence, having a permanent -2 modifier to your Charisma score. You, however, have had this dreary break shape you into something closer to beast than human as well, being able to manifest a Natural Weapon you are proficient in whenever you take the {@action Attack} action. This weapon can be a Talon or a Wing, both being wreathed in black feathers. Your Talons deal {@damage 2d4} slashing damage and have the finesse property while your Wings deal {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage and have the Reach property. Furthermore, as a reaction to when a creature would hit you with a melee attack you may perform a melee weapon attack against them using a Beak weapon. This Beak is also a natural weapon you are proficient in, except it uses your choice of Constitution or Charisma as an attack modifier and deals half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@damage 1d12|d12} piercing damage.
Inspectio

{@b Illuminate the Dark.} You gave away your eyes, becoming permanently {@condition Blinded}. You, however, gain a Dark Lantern that is bound to your soul, being indestructible and capable of illuminating a 60-ft. area centered on itself. It must be carried with one free hand yet also functions while set down, provided you are bathed by its light. All other creatures of your choice gain Darksight within the light's radius and you ignore the effects of the {@condition Blinded} Condition whenever being targeted by another creature's attack or when you are attacking another creature within the light. You also gain Blindsight of 30-ft. centered on the Lantern.
Repressio

{@b Broken Balance.} You gave away part of your inherent humanity and capability to see things as they are. A silvered scale has either been lodged as if wing addornments to your shoulders or you bear the tattoo of one covering the area from the back of your neck to your upper back. Whenever a creature you can see or hear breaks one of the tenets described in this subclass' flavour text, it suffers from an invisible weight bearing down their backs, gaining a negative {@dice 1d6|d6} modifier on their next roll. A creature does not need to know your tenets for this to trigger. You are also subject to this effect, except it lasts until the end of your turn if in combat.

entries: Your sacrifice cannot be undone unless you participate in the killing of the Beast of the Black Forest.

subclassFeature.name: Beauty of the Little Things

entries: "...Does it sometimes occur to you when you see a remarkable thing that you want to share the wonderment with others?"

Your soul is one that isn't concerned only with the ever-marching stride of progress, instead you have come to respect and grant love to the small moments of life. You learn the {@spell druidcraft} Cantrip and it counts as a Sorcerer spell for you, but doesn't count toward your total spells known.

Whenever you use this Cantrip you may choose to gain a count of Lingering Blossoms as well, for up to 2 count of the Effect gained this way. Additionally, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient.

subclassFeature.name: Bespoke Stitching

entries: "Right, I'll give you your bloody handmade! HANDMADE! BESPOKE! HAND-SEWN!!"

Despite the ringing of previous clients whinging still not disgracing your thoughts at night, you still have an innate desire to create! To make! To SEW! You can capitalize on that drive as an Action, provided you have any Artisan's tools you are proficient with in one of your hands, putting yourself to work in one of the following:

items: You spend 2 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count to make a {@item Bum-Pick-Stitcher's Blade|TheUndertomesNW}.
You spend 3 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count to make a {@item Double-Needled Needlekin Robe|TheUndertomesNW}.
You spend 5 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count to make a set of {@item Bespoke Garments|TheUndertomesNW}.

entries: The chosen item is ready to be used at the start of your next turn, with you being able to stow your Artisan's Tools away as a Free Action after being done. You are automatically Attuned to the item after its creation, without it counting toward your total. They can all be found after this feature is presented.

All items created this way last until your next long rest, with one of your Needlekin taking it back to the Demiplane for further revisions afterward. Or maybe you just got bored of staring at it and decided to pick it apart for materials. Or you got frustrated by a tiny imperceptible detail you noticed, because of course you noticed, you're an artist, aren't you?
Whenever you or your Needlekin Servants attempt to attack a hostile creature you gain one {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count. Additionally you gain proficiency in Weaver's Tools.

subclassFeature.name: Between God and the Devil

entries: "Some called him the Green Damnation, while others called him the Green Deliverance."

You have become something which threads the centerpath between extremes - a liminal space between what once was and what will be - of good and evil - of so much yet so little. Your prowess is shown right upon arrival - An Ordeal that floods any area of battle in a single feeling, chosen whenever you roll first Initiative during combat:

items: {@b Dawn of Damnation.} Whenever you inflict {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a critical you inflict 2 additional count as well and whenever you achieve a Posture Critical, you gain one {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count. On a Critical Hit, this attack considers a targets damage Immunity as if they were only Resistant to the damage dealt, and Resistance as if they weren't Resistant as well.

{@b Dawn of Deliverance.} You gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns and whenever you get a sum of 8 count, you gain one {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count. On a Critical Hit, all friendly creatures within 30-ft. of you gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. The same happens whenever you Stabilize a friendly creature or protect another creature with any effect such as the {@spell sanctuary|PHB|Sanctuary} spell or with using the Protector Fighting Style.

entries: As you perform better and better in combat, your prowess coalesces into a plume of your own shade - {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} that swirls, and surrounds your body, matching that of your inner world.

While you have {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} during the Dawn of Damnation, you deal an additional 2 damage on weapon hits per count instead of suffering it. While you have {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} during the Dawn of Deliverance, you suffer 2 less damage whenever you would suffer damage instead of suffering it, to a maximum reduction equal to half the total value of damage being taken.
You only lose {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count at the end of combat, but may only hold a maximum of 5 at any given time.

subclassFeature.name: Biomimeticism: Art Imitates Life

entries: "Aesthetics concerns itself entirely with the visible, yet this self-evident familiarity often invites neglect that overlooks the inherent significance of what is seen..."

You are a very unique type of druid, the one who wishes to transcend the binds of their flesh by imitating nature the best they can: constructing and shaping a body sculpted in the image of what once was. You, unlike the vast majority of other circles, embrace the touch of metal while extracting and re-shaping the natural form to become a better meld of your view of reality.

As a form of repression to better understand the limits of your body, you've stowed away the fruits of your slow labour into a metallic armor that paradoxically hides and defines your form. You are always in this Iron Maiden Form until you spend one of your Wildshape uses as a Bonus Action to enter your Flowing State Form, as per described in the Features below.

You, however, do not limit yourself to using your own body as material, also acquiring one {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} after such. You may spend count for the following:

items: You may spend up to your proficiency bonus' amount of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} before performing an attack to deal an additional 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit per {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} spent.

You may spend up to half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} before performing an attack to gain a bonus modifier to hit equal to half your proficiency bonus.

entries: Additionally, your obsession with the humanoid form doesn't stop only at your art, no, your imitation of life extends to what you see from other beings. Whenever you use the Wildshape feature you may transform into Humanoids instead of Beasts, following the usual rules for the Feature. If the Humanoid would be carrying any items in its monster sheet, you create exact copies of them as long as they aren't unique to that creature, and if you copy something akin to a wizard's grimoire, you have the practical content of their spells in Druidic, but not any personal notes and such. Your appearance is always metallic and can be discerned easily to be an imitation by other creatures.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This subclass is intended to be played while locking you out of the usual Wildshape rules to turn into Beasts. If for any reason you'd rather maintain this for your druid, consider that you alter your Form as if the metallic plates that compose your body shifted and melded together to become whatever animal you wish to become, instead of being the usual magical transformation.

subclassFeature.name: Blackened Hands

entries: "That's that, and this is this."

A Fighter with Blackened Hands is someone who has the risk of having all that matters escape their grasp like sand. The only thing keeping them together is their own will to survive as a great warrior, yet the path they thread is forked and oftentimes in solitude or with very few important people.

Some walk a path that cannot be heard, gracefully embracing the shade and coming out only to leave the remains of their targets to be displayed-a magnificent, silent spectacle. Those are masters of stealth and sometimes embodying a chivalric essence with prowess and dignity that is hard to mimic.

Others have lost everything, being resigned to the path marked not only by shade but becoming one with that darkness themselves, wielding a righteous fury that drives men and women mad like a weapon to scorch the earth they thread upon. That path is one of sorrow and where one cannot stop to mourn the angels that are gone.

What binds both, where all roads meet is that it's from their heart and experience that all their power comes from. Every little skirmish, every little scar left on them and by them forms a story that causes the one with Blackened Hands to be a unique being in the way that they paint whichever world they reside in black.

entries.name: Canti ai Grandi Paladini

entries: "L'arme e gli amori, e i cavallier, l'audaci imprese io canto."

Through a rigid mastery over many weapons and experience, you have developed your own technique to employ your own symphony of varied weapons, turning your very fingers into an instrument to tap into your entire arsenal.

You have managed to create a small storage within your own heart, a demiplane connected to your core known as a Lasting Arsenal, formed by a combination of magical items or an innate, magical manifestation of your own inner being.

You may store up to your proficiency bonus' worth of weapons in your Lasting Arsenal, being able to store any weapon not held by another creature as a Free Action you may take while grasping them, and have a stored weapon appear on your hand as another Free Action.

If you would attempt to add another weapon while your Lasting Arsenal has no space left, you must replace any of your already stored weapons with the new one, with the replaced one being manifested in your empty hand.
While a weapon is a part of your Lasting Arsenal, you are considered Attuned to it. This Attunement does not count toward your maximum Attuned items.

entries.name: Cavalier in Nero

entries: "Orlando, il più prode de' paladini, armato di Durindana e di coraggio senza pari, non temeva alcun nemico."

Your mastery in arms is unparalleled, being able to wring out the best of any one weapon that graces your hands. While a weapon is part of your Lasting Arsenal, you gain special benefits listed at the end of this subclass.

These have both passive effects that are active as long as you are wielding the weapon or they are stored inside your Arsenal, and active Flourishes which can be used every other turn per weapon as an Action.
If you use a Dagger's Flourish in one turn, on the next turn you may still use another weapon's Flourish but not your Dagger's.

entries.name: Cavalier in Nero Flourishes
entries: The following Flourishes have passive effects that are granted while within your Lasting Arsenal and active effects that may be used in place of an Attack as part of your Attack action. For any weapon not directly named, you may refer to the Weapon Groups table, such as a Rapier counting as a Shortsword for its Flourish bonuses. If a Saving Throw is requested, your DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Dagger's Agility
entries: Daggers grant unparalleled agility and mobility, granting you an additional 5-ft. of movement.

entries.name: Flourish: Rock Bottom Bounceback
entries: You may throw the dagger in a way that it'll ricochet right back to your hand after being thrown. When you do so, perform a ranged attack roll on a target within its Thrown range, ignoring Partial Cover. Regardless of if you hit or miss, the weapon is flung back to you after hitting any surface.

entries.name: Greatsword's Destruction
entries: A greatsword in your hands is a weapon that neglects the need for any shield, cutting through any attack with ease, reducing any damage you take by one plus any Bonus Modifier to hit the weapon has.

entries.name: Flourish: District Cleaver
entries: You may swing the Greatsword to cover great arcs, perform a melee attack roll against a target within reach. The result also counts as if it were targeting any other creatures 5-ft. beside the original target, when you roll damage you do so once for all targets hit.

entries.name: Handaxe's Versatility
entries: The Handaxe is the perfect weapon to cover for any other arm's weakness. You still add half your relevant Modifiers when dealing damage with your Bonus Action attack, as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules.

entries.name: Flourish: Sinking Reverb
entries: You throw your Handaxe at any target creature within its minimum thrown reach. On a hit, you may instantly rush toward them, moving to be within 5-ft. of the target.

entries.name: Heavy Gauntlet's Dukes
entries: A good pair of Gauntlets easily help with maintaining an overall defensive stance, granting you a +1 bonus modifier to Constitution and Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Flourish: Clawing Out the Wind
entries: You deliver a particularly powerful punch to the target's lungs, beating the very air out of them. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they must pass a Constitution saving throw or have their movement speed halved and Attack Modifier reduced by half your proficiency bonus until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Katana's Airwall
entries: The dexterity needed to wield a Katana properly is nothing to scoff at, and it's bursts of action teach a special means of defense against projectiles. Ranged attacks against you suffer a -2 negative modifier to hit.

entries.name: Flourish: Gone in a Blink
entries: You ready your Katana and slash without giving your target a moment to perceive it. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach. If your Katana is sheathed, you have Advantage on this attack and deal additional damage equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) on a hit. Furthermore, if able you may move to be 5-ft. behind the target.

entries.name: Lance's March
entries: The Lance is a movement in of itself, a constant that cannot be broken, granting you the ability to move through up to 15-ft. of Difficult Terrain each turn without needing to spend any additional movement speed.

entries.name: Flourish: Slaughterline
entries: You prepare for a mad dash with your Lance at the forefront. Choose an empty space within 20-ft. to move to, all creatures in the line required for you to move to there must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be impaled, taking your Lance's damage die and being both knocked {@condition Prone} and forcibly moved into the space in front of where you end, or the closest unoccupied space instead.

entries.name: Light Hammer's Wedge
entries: A Light Hammer's head can easily be used to wedge out even the nastiest attack from being a hit. You gain the ability to use your Reaction to increase your AC by one when you would be targeted by an attack, before or after its rolled, potentially turning a hit into a miss.

entries.name: Flourish: Arsenal Breaker
entries: You may use the Hammer's head to hook and tear away your opponents weapon with ease. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or have one weapon of your choice that they are holding be flung toward any space within 15-ft. of them.

entries.name: Longsword's Lockstep
entries: The Longsword's elegant maneuvers ease into a dance of attacks in your hands, granting you a +1 bonus modifier to hit whenever you move before attacking

entries.name: Flourish: Inescapable Void
entries: Though simple in nature, a well-used Longsword is a weapon to put fear into your foe's hearts. You perform a weapon attack roll against a target within reach. On a hit, the target must pass a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened} of you. While {@condition Frightened}, the target cannot willingly move away from you, as they are paralyzed by your presence.

entries.name: Mace's Siege
entries: The strength needed to wield a Mace is one to tear down anything in your path, granting you the ability to deal double any bludgeoning damage to objects and buildings.

entries.name: Flourish: Sundermind
entries: You bring down your Mace in a particularly nasty blow to the head. Perform a melee weapon attack against a creature within reach, on a hit they must pass a Constitution saving throw or receive a negative modifier to their Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Revolver's Deadzone
entries: The Revolver is a versatile weapon, but that versatility is brought out fully only when you have a perfect vision to acknowledge multiple targets at once, granting you the ability to deal an additional 2 damage whenever you first hit a different creature than your last target during your turn.

entries.name: Flourish: Grand Slaughter
entries: Instead of performing a single attack against a single target, you'd rather empty your Revolver and the remaining hostile roster all at once. You perform one ranged weapon attack per each remaining bullet in your chamber, as per the {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} property. Each of these attacks must target a different target creature and you don't add your Dexterity modifier to your damage rolls.

entries.name: Rifle's Positioning
entries: To wield a Rifle perfectly you must learn how to keep the distance between you and any other threat, granting you the ability to spend your Reaction whenever a hostile creature moves into 5-ft. of you to quickly dash away into a 10-ft. line in any direction of your choice. Any Opportunity Attacks that are triggered from this are done at disadvantage.

entries.name: Flourish: Shooting Stars
entries: You take aim to pierce only through soft tissue. Instead of performing an attack roll, all creatures within a line whose range is equal to the minimum Range of your Rifle must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be hit, taking the damage you would do with a regular weapon attack using your Rifle, or half on a success.

entries.name: Shortsword's Denial
entries: The Shortsword's elegant maneuvers ease into a dance of attacks in your hands, having you deal +2 bonus damage on a hit whenever you move before attacking.

entries.name: Flourish: Retake Control
entries: You maintain dominance through any battlefield. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit the target is moved back 5-ft. each time you hit it until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Poesie per il Silencio Weapon Groups
entries: The following weapon groups are meant to simplify the use of certain abilities of both of your 3rd and 10th level subclass features while wielding specific weapons that are not directly mentioned, listing the Main Weapons and the weapons within their groups.

items: {@b Dagger:} Dart, Javelin.
{@b Greatsword:} Battleaxe.
{@b Handaxe:} Trident.
{@b Heavy Gauntlet:} Unarmed Strike, Greatclub, Maul, Quarterstaff.
{@item Single-Stroke Katana|TheUndertomesBH|Single-Stroke Katana}.
{@b Lance:} Glaive, Spear, Pike.
{@b Light Hammer:} Halberd, Net, Whip.
{@b Longsword:} Flail, Morningstar.
{@b Mace:} Club, Greataxe, War Pick, Warhammer.
{@b Revolver:} Hand Crossbow, Light Crossbow, Shortbow, Sling.
{@b Rifle:} Heavy Crossbow, Longbow, Wooden Staff.
{@b Shortsword:} Double-Bladed Scimitar, Scimitar, Sickle.

entries: Any weapons without required properties such as {@itemProperty DRW|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Draw} or {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} may be considered as if they had them. Ranged weapons within the Revolver group are considered to have Reload (5).

entries.name: Graziosa Pazienzia

entries: "Muovea il cavaliere con passo misurato e gesto gentile, ché ogni azione traduceva onore."

The marks and scars of your training and expertise fit your fingers like a glove, yet they are worn not only as a symbol of brutality but of grace and restraint. You gain proficiency in your choice of Sleight of Hand or Stealth, or Expertise instead if you were already proficient with the chosen skill.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: If you wish to employ Two-Handed Fighting with this subclass is subclass, you may count both weapons as single one for the sake of storing them into your Arsenal while consuming only one "Equipment Slot", but to summon them you need both hands free, instead of being able to summon each individually.

subclassFeature.name: Blade Wreathed in Heavenly Authority
entries: During a long rest, you can apply a series of talismans to a weapon with which you are proficient, transforming it into a Weapon of Heavenly Authority. The weapon deals only half the damage rolled with it after adding all modifiers, but inflicts 1 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on every hit. While you wield it, it gains the Light property and loses the Two-Handed and Heavy properties.

Whenever you deal damage with the weapon, you gain 1 stack of {@b Tianjiu Star's Blade}, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. When using the weapon for two-weapon fighting, you can spend your bonus action during your Attack action to make one additional attack with it, then resume any attacks you could still make.
The {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} inflicted on a hit increases to 3 at 8th level and 4 at 14th level.

subclassFeature.name: Bleeding Extra Attack

entries: "Here folks play by ma rules, or else!"

You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with an Attack Roll, they suffer 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Blinding White Dawn

entries: "Thou mayest know me as Don Quixote, Fixer of the third Section of Cinq Association East!"

Your Pyrojades are fully energized and can create concentrated fire strong enough to melt anything it touches. As an action, choose a point you can see within 80 feet. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d10} fire damage, suffers 8 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and becomes {@condition Frightened||Frightened} of you until the end of its next turn. While frightened this way, it must immediately use its reaction, if available, to move as far from you as possible, provided it can see you. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers half as many {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, with no additional effect.
Any nonmagical item, equipment, tool, or structure in the sphere is burned or melted and destroyed. The area becomes difficult terrain as the structures liquefy.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Blink, Gone

entries: "It would have been nice to have those who would lament my passing, yet the remembrance of the dead has no place in the hearts of those who live here."

The butterflies of the afterlife have come to rest their weary wings upon your shoulders, much as you have been trained and ordained as a grave keeper of sorts - caring and nurturing for the dead and passing on of the world. These butterflies, spirits of transience, have chosen to aid you in your goals just as you aid them - Whenever you make a hit a creature you inflict {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesFL} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. Whenever you hit multiple hostile creatures with a spell or they fail a saving throw from your spells you instead cause each creature to suffer an amount of {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesFL} equal to half your proficiency bonus plus the spell slot level consumed, split equally amongst every target of the spell. ( To a minimum of one. )

Additionally, these butterflies that surround you have a tendency to perch upon the bodies of those that linger to pass on, giving you Advantage on {@skill Insight} and {@skill Perception} checks to perceive a creature as being of the Undead type. Furthermore, if you cast the {@spell Find Familiar} spell you may choose to summon your familiar as a kaleidoscope of these butterflies, a group that remains with you for prolonged periods of time. These use the {@creature Owl} stat sheet except they are a Medium swarm of Tiny Undead and have the {@i Tranquillity} trait appended to their sheet, as per what is presented below.

entries.name: Tranquillity
entries: The Kaleidoscope of Dead Butterflies uses your Spellcasting modifier, including any bonuses from magical divine foci, to their {@skill Insight} checks to detect the presence of Undead creatures within 15-ft. of themselves and to discern another creatures Alignment. They may report back to you any information gleamed this way through ethereal whispers of a gentle nature.

subclassFeature.name: Blinkstep
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} action as your action, your feet temporarily morph into rabbit paws, granting you 3 stacks of {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesMW}. As part of the same action, you can use your remaining movement and make a melee weapon attack against a target you can reach. On a hit, the target suffers 1 stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. After the attack, you can jump up to 5 feet away from the target without provoking opportunity attacks.
