You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Blood-Tinted Scissorblades
entries: Also at 3rd level, you've found a way to enhance your Weaver's Tools for devastating effect. You may create Blood-Tinted Scissorblades with your Bloodfeast, which gradually becomes stronger with the amount of blood you spend. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Blood-Tinted Scissorblades Ranks
rows: 3rd

Your Weaver's Tools count as a martial melee weapon you are proficient with. They deal {@dice 2d4} slashing damage, can use Intelligence for attack and damage rolls, and have the Hemorrhaging (18-20) and Heavy properties.
I
3rd
Your scissorblades deal {@dice 2d4} slashing damage and have Hemorrhaging (17-20).
II
6th

Your scissorblades deal {@dice 2d6} slashing damage plus {@dice 1d6} slashing damage against targets afflicted with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. They count as a +1 weapon and a +1 spellcasting focus for artificer spells, and have Hemorrhaging (16-20).
III
12th

Your scissorblades deal {@dice 3d8} slashing damage plus {@dice 2d8} slashing damage against targets afflicted with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. They count as a +2 weapon and a +2 spellcasting focus for artificer spells. On a critical hit, the target suffers additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to your proficiency bonus. They have Hemorrhaging (16-20).

subclassFeature.name: Bloodflame Massacre [血炎亂舞]

entries: "Hah, what's that? You lot haven't had your fill just yet, either...? Fine! Come and get me!"

The oil you use to ignite your sword is now coursing through your veins, and every single part of you is itching to start a conflagration. While you're raging, you can use a Reaction when you take Fire damage to immediately make an attack against a creature within reach. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.
Whenever you bring a creature to 0 hit points after an attack, you can immediately walk up to 15 feet and make another attack roll against a creature within reach.

entries.name: Rooster's Rampaging Blades Under the Ensanguined Heaven.
entries: Once per long rest, as an Action you can take when you have half of your hit points or less, you open your wings and coat your weapons and yourself in flammable oil, gaining 4 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. You can reach each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere around you without spending movement speed. You can make a number of attack rolls against them equal to half the count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself. Your weapon damage dice for all of these attacks is {@dice 1d4} fire damage, but you can still apply your Rage bonus to them. If you reduce a creature to 0 hit points this way, your damage dice becomes {@dice 1d6} for the duration.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodied Hands
entries: Also when entering this Divine Domain, the weight of sin that you must carry pools around your fingers and hardens into devastating tools of purification. You gain Bloodied Hands with your Bloodfeast, which gradually becomes fiercer the more blood you spend. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Bloodied Hands Ranks
rows: 1st

You have a metallic holy symbol that acts as stake, if lost or destroyed you may recreate it during a long rest without spending materials. It is a martial weapon you are proficient in and it deals {@dice 1d6} piercing damage.
1st

Your Bloodied Hands seep into the symbol, forming a bloody whip to inflict salvation unto others. This weapon gains Reach and deals an additional {@dice 1d4} piercing damage to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creatures.
6th

The blood weeps further from between your fingers. Your weapon now deals {@dice 2d6} piercing damage plus {@dice 2d4} piercing damage to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creatures. When you hit a target with a melee attack while using this, you regain two hit points. Additionally, this weapon counts as a +1 Holy Symbol and a +1 Weapon.
12th

Your sinful hands will never be fully washed away from the red that coats them. Your weapon now deals an additional {@dice 3d4} piercing on {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creatures, and has a reach of 10 feet, also healing 3 hit points on a melee hit. It counts as a +2 Holy Symbol and a +2 Weapon. On a Critical Hit with this weapon, you may heal yourself or a creature within the weapon's reach for up to two times the stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on target.

entries: This table's effects do not stack, any changes to the weapon are as described.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodsteeped Scent of the World

entries: "Now... Behold. These flowers are in full glory. Once all these flowers have been stained red... that shall be when 'I' bloom as well."

Blood, sweat and tears stain the garden that is the world as fertilizer for its growth, and you have acted as its gardener and centrepiece for long, absorbing all you need to have your soul bloom like no other. Once per long rest you may spend 10 Lingering Blossoms as a Bonus Action to bloom yourself, and have the world around you follow suit.

When you do so, a 320-ft. radius around you visibly changes to be overgrown with vibrant plants that match your fragrance and view, with your essence being unmistakeable to those therein. When first creating this area, all creatures of your choice within reach instantly lose all their Sinking count and you gain the sum of all count lost this way.

The pains of others serve as no pain of your own, instead washing away all impurities and capturing in time all the chances they have had to bloom, taken or missed. While suffering from Sinking this way, its effects change as you do, causing that whenever you would suffer a negative modifier from the Condition, you gain a positive one instead.

Additionally, you inflict 4 Sinking count whenever you damage another creature and 6 when they fail a saving throw from your spells. Whenever you kill or first knock a creature {@condition Unconscious}, they lose all their Sinking count and you gain it instead. While within this area, you do not create clouds as per your Culminating Fragrance feature. Instead, the entire area is considered a Fragrant cloud.
Whenever you would lose Sinking count, you gain one Lingering Blossoms count for each 3 Sinking lost this way. This area of bloom decays and vanishes when you aren't suffering from Sinking anymore.

subclassFeature.name: Bloody Barber Specialization
entries: The work of the Bloody Barber is one that most people, the fools, struggle to grasp. Those who use of stitches and scissors to masterfully imbue life itself to the very concept of beauty are rare and few between, boasting knowledge of the arcane and sharp fashion senses, these are usually eccentric people who don't tend to band together with one another, instead wanting to have their craft flourish through their own merit.

In settings such as the Forgotten Realms, the art of the Bloody Barber has become one passed down through generation after generation, with renowned artificers taking a handful of pupils under their wing as they teach this necromantic art form. Most people might find the production method of the finest silk in the Sword Coast a reviling thing, but none can deny the quality of such fabulous clothing.

In others, such as Ravenloft, the Bloody Barber has become a nightmare inducing children's tale, one that was spread from Barovia and far into the mists, of the shady person that would abduct children of their homes and madly snap at them using their blood-red scissors, turning them into pretty little bows spread around the trees.

subclassFeature.name: Blubbering Toad

entries: If only I could gather all the sorrow, all the tears together, and cry in their stead...

You have learned to channel your tears into powerful protective magic for you and your allies. As an action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to grow a toady, porous armor rather than transforming into a beast form, and you gain 4 temporary hit points for each level you have in this class. While this feature is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: As a reaction to when you’re hit, you can increase your AC by 2 until the end of the turn. If the attack still hits you, you can force all creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you to roll a Charisma saving throw against your spell save dc. If they fail, they gain counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to your proficiency bonus.

As a bonus action, you can target any creature within 30 feet of you other than yourself and grant them 1 count of {@condition Blubberbubble|TheUndertomesASV} and {@dice 1d8} temporary Hit Points. You can grant up to 2 counts and {@dice 2d8} at level 6, 3 counts and {@dice 3d8} at level 10 and 4 counts and {@dice 4d8} at level 14.
When you hit an enemy with Sinking, you deal an extra {@dice 1d4} cold damage at level 2, {@dice 1d6} at level 6, {@dice 1d8} at level 10 and {@dice 1d10} at level 14.

entries: These benefits last for 10 minutes, until you lose all these temporary hit points, or until you use your Wild Shape again.

subclassFeature.name: Body Fixation Studies (Fist)

entries: "The hand is mightier than the key. I am certain that I have smote that understanding into them. And... Hm. I do not recall what I had planned to say hereafter."

The fists that you use to tightly grip your knowhow have become something else, a tool to protect it - To impede anything else from smoothing your brain more than you already do. As long as you are unarmed and have Temporary Hit Points you gain Resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage.

Additionally, whenever you first gain Temporary Hit Points while having none you may choose to become Resistant to one of the following damage types for the same duration: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic or radiant.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

subclassFeature.name: Boundary of Death
entries: Upon reaching 17th level, your mastery of straddling the line between life and death becomes a weapon you turn on others. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, roll a d4. On a result of 4, you deal additional damage die equal to half your total Sneak Attack amount (rounded down). These are added as extra Sneak Attack dice to this attack. Additionally, your violence intensifies as you near the end. On a Sneak Attack hit, you deal an extra {@dice 1d6} damage per missing Chunk of hit points. When you are down to your last Chunk of hit points, you gain one additional reaction each round. While in this state, your Deflect Assault technique becomes more refined: for each damage die rolled during Deflect Assault that lands on its maximum value, you reduce an additional amount of damage equal to that maximum result.

subclassFeature.name: Brandishes to Quell the Innermost Self

entries: "By day as by night, this City... shows itself only as a pale blur, as though the rain has washed its silhouette white"

To become a better tool yourself, you have mastered many a weapon for its best use, being able to bring out their full potential while they're in your hands. Once every other turn you may replace one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action with a Weapon Brandish according to your current Wilful beeper form, as presented below:

entries.name: Hatchet Brandish: Filo del Ragno
entries: You extend your Hatchet's liquid hilt toward any target creature within 30-ft. of you, performing an weapon attack roll against them. On a hit, you may instantly rush toward them, moving to be within 5-ft. of the target. They have Disadvantage on attacks against you until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Stiletto Brandish: Guida Falsa
entries: You maintain dominance through any battlefield. Perform an amount of melee weapon attacks against a target within reach equal to half your proficiency bonus ( rounded down ), on a hit the target is moved back 5-ft. each time you hit it until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Bastard Brandish: Vuoto Ardente
entries: Though bland, one with a practiced Bastard Sword can put fear into their enemies' core. You perform a weapon attack roll against a target within reach. On a hit, the target must pass a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened} of you. While {@condition Frightened}, the target cannot willingly move away from you, as they are paralyzed by your presence. Whenever you finish your turn within 5-ft. of the {@condition Frightened} creature, you gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Rapier Brandish: Intecciare
entries: Fencing is all about positioning, and you know how to make your opponent's the worse possible. You instantly gain 3 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and may instantly move to any empty space within 5-ft. of your target to Flank with another friendly creature, if able, then perform a weapon attack roll against them. On a hit target must spend their Action and Bonus Action if they attempt to Disengage from you until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hammer Brandish: Scindermentes
entries: You bring down your Hammer in a potentially horrid blow to the cranium. Perform a melee weapon attack against a creature within reach, on a hit they must pass a Constitution saving throw or receive a negative modifier to their Intelligence, Wisdom and Constitution saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus until the end of their next turn, rounded down.

entries.name: Great Brandish: Mannaia Distrettuale
entries: You may swing the Great Sword to paint broad strokes, perform a melee attack roll against a target within reach. The result also counts as if it were targeting any other creatures 5-ft. beside the original target, when you roll damage you do so once for all targets hit, with an additional d6 slashing damage for each hit target.

entries.name: Lance Brandish: Linea di Macellazione
entries: You brace for a reckless dash forward using your lance to raze all in your path. Choose a point within 20-ft. of you to move to. All creatures in a line between you and your end goal must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC or be impaled, taking 1d12 + half your proficiency bonus' worth of d12 piercing damage ( rounded down ) and both being knocked {@condition Prone} and forcibly moved to 5-ft. in front of you or the closest available space on a failure.

entries.name: Whip Brandish: .Spezzaarmatura
entries: You may use the Whip's everchanging point to hook and tear away your opponents weapon with ease. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or have one weapon of your choice that they are holding be flung toward any space within 35-ft. of them.

entries.name: Spork Brandish: Coraggio a Metà
entries: You have to make the best out of the worst with this weapon. Perform a weapon attack roll with this weapon, on a hit you inflict double the {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you normally would.

entries.name: Scythe Brandish: Riverbero Splendente
entries: Pursuit is the only way to make a weapon sing, and you will pursue until your Scythe runs hoarse. You perform three weapon attacks against a target within reach. If the first two attacks hit, your third attack is considered a Critical Hit if it hits as well.
Furthermore, at the start of your turns you roll a d4, with the following effects occurring:

rows: You deal an additional die of bludgeoning damage whenever you deal bludgeoning damage. You ignore Resistance to bludgeoning damage and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.
You deal an additional die of slashing damage whenever you deal slashing damage. You ignore Resistance to slashing damage and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.
You deal an additional die of piercing damage whenever you deal piercing damage. You ignore Resistance to piercing damage and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.

You deal an additional die of matching damage type whenever you deal bludgeoning, slashing or piercing damage. You ignore Resistance to these damage types and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.

entries: Additionally, once per long rest you may consume one count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD} to always choose your Wilful Beeper's form at the start of your turns. You cannot choose the same form twice in a row this way.

subclassFeature.name: Breach Reaction Training
entries: One of your jobs greatest requirements is efficient and quick action during cleaning hours, as such, starting at 7th level, you may add your proficiency bonus to your Initiative modifier, in addition, you gain advantage on your first attack against creatures below you on the Initiative Order.

subclassFeature.name: Breaking your Oath
entries: When first creating a Paladin of Procurement, its best to consider which path your character might go down. As it stands, this subclass is centered around giving up your free will to be guided by a greater force that altough might be beneficent in certain settings, is mostly serving its own purpose at best or is actively detrimental to most and stiffling to you at worse. As such, this subclass features a modicum of support toward the end of an Oathbreaker.

Through the levels in this subclass you have many features that depend on being in tune with the Will, so it is highly recommended to talk to your DM about planning out if your character will start having doubts and possibly even having their powers fail them suddenly at hours of need for the drama and development.

We also would like to make it clear that the best way to do this (in our perspective) is to have this be a slow-burn development, with your character slowly coming to realize the error in surrendering their self to a greater Will or even through other party members pushing them toward thinking for themselves.

There is a matter as of how to keep mechanics and the flavours of an Oathbreaker in tune during this, and although a Capstone feature is provided for them, their other features aren't provided in such alternatives. In their stead, we recommend having the character coming to learn that all the power driven from their Oath is instead a manifestation of their own Faith that becomes easier to wield as they accept themselves and start believing in their own unfettered potential.
Another thing to keep in mind is how other characters may react to their breach of Oath, since the Living Will and their associated Factions usually employ heavy witch hunts to take out Oathbreakers.
In the future there may have supplemental content to this concept, yet as of now we wish the best of luck for those who can't wait to have their character's develop past the need of another's Will.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: As you might come around reading this s subclass subclass as a whole, you will see that it employs many unique Conditions and Effects. As such, we cannot recommend it for beginners with the 5e System, as it might be too complex to follow for that.

For those intending to use it, we recommend that the Player who plays this subclass keeps track of their own Prescript list, current Poise, Grace, Karma and Unlock counts. Do so either using a simple notepad in your computer or at the corner of your sheet/piece of paper.
As for Sinking application or Grace/Karma on other creatures, we recommend noting such down beside their turn in Initiative so their effects are easier to keep track of when triggered.

subclassFeature.name: Bursting Elation

entries: Just a little taste of heaven won’t hurt, right?.
Your mastery of the art of granting joy has become more proeminent, causing your Thorns to inflict the following two ranks upon sufficient infliction:
You also inflict one more Thorn count whenever you hit a creature with a spell attack.
Furthermore you gain Expertise in the {@skill Persuasion} skill and you may now create up to four Nettleburst Joints per long rest.

rows: IV
The target is violently shaking, unable to stop as they are as if compelled to dance.
The target suffers disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws. Furthermore they cannot speak coherently enough to cast Verbal spells.
V
The target’s mind is clouded to a point where it can’t think straight, only looking for even more pleasure.

All your attacks have advantage against the target and they have disadvantage attacking you or on saving throws against you. Furthermore they suffer half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, as a negative modifier to Wisdom and Intelligence saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Bygone Days

entries: Allow me to introduce you to this manor.

The influence of the old master of the manor courses through your mind, slowly shaping your thoughts to be closely attuned to that of his servants. As a bonus action, you can place a curse on a creature, marking it as an Interloper. To maintain this curse, you concentrate on it as if concentrating on a spell. You can use this ability once, twice upon reaching level 10, and you regain all expended uses on a short or long rest.

A creature cursed as an Interloper takes an additional {@dice 1d6} cold damage when you hit it with an attack, and suffers 2 counts of Sinking when you hit it with a spell attack. Additionally, choose a saving throw when a creature is cursed as an Interloper.
While cursed this way, the creature has disadvantage on that saving throw.
Furthermore, by spending a spell slot, you can summon a Portrait of the Old Days.

This portrait can look however you wish, yet it is always an old wooden frame holding a picture or painting of the humanoid form of the old master, a luxurious person wearing dark brown clothes of your choice. The Portrait hit points is 10 x your proficiency bonus, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage. Your Portraits hover, and as a free action on your turn, you can move them up to 30 feet in any direction. As a bonus action, you can force all creatures of your choice within 10 feet of it to roll a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or gain 3 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, on a successful save, they gain only 1 count instead. When a creature reduces a Portrait to 0 Hit Points, you may use a reaction to make a spell attack against it. Your Portraits last until they’re reduced to 0 Hit Points or until you finish a short or long rest, upon which the remaining portraits turn to dust.

Designer's Note: How the Old Master used to look is completely up to you, and it can be anything that would fit the vibes of your campaign. Nowadays, however, the Old Master is a rotting wooden carcass fused with a giant insect, wriggling around the mansion as a giant skull with wings and legs.

subclassFeature.name: Cacciatore del Traguardo

entries: "Witness a demonstration of the Palermitan dismantling technique."
"Sezionatura di Cervo!"

The Palermitan style is flashy, often being considered one without restraint or even an oblique facsimile of swordsmanship as an art form to ill-tongues. You've grown to show them wrong, perfecting a series of movements and blocks to make them swallow such words of disrespect toward your tradition. You may perform a Finisher Move that replace the last attack you could make in your turn, requiring you to have hit the same target twice before attempting to your choice of one of the following Finishers:

items: {@b Broken Spear.} Much like a butcher will find a means to use bone and marrow alike, you treat your weapons as tool shards to drive in the sides of your target. You instantly make two melee weapon attacks against a target within reach, then dealing an additional damage die and inflicting one more Condition count on a hit.

{@b Death Mask.} You prepare a series of feints and deceptive strikes to hide your aim for the true goal, a decisive lobotomy through a pierced head. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach at the start of your next turn, reducing your Critical Threshold for each time you were targeted by a hostile creature's attack or spell until then. ( You deal a Critical Hit on a roll of 19-20 if targeted once, 18-20 if twice and so on. )

{@b House as a Fortress.} You ready your blades, not for the sake of attacking the target themselves but instead debilitating their every blow so they may truly feel helpless. You gain a bonus modifier to your Armor Class equal to your proficiency bonus until the start of your next turn.

{@b Sea Urchine.} You deliver deft strikes to the opponents feet, binding them to this duel and of course, their early demise. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach. On a hit their movement speed and Dexterity Saving Throw modifier are halved until the end of your next turn.

entries: You may use your Bonus Action Attack for this finishing blow, and may make use of them for an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest. Whenever you kill a creature using one such Finisher move you regain its use.

You may instantly trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target of your Finisher when you deal damage to them, or instead choose to convert all their {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. count into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead.

subclassFeature.name: Can't Let You Through

entries: "Ahem, ahem. I'd say our performance might just warrant a bonus for going above and beyond."
Making sure those around you are around you are safe has become second nature to, allowing you to take the Knight's Advance Bonus Action and Knight's Denial Reaction:

entries.name: Knight's Advance
entries: You throw your body weight forward to quickly reposition yourself, spending your Bonus Action to move up to 10-ft. in a line toward any direction. Whenever you would enter another creature's space by doing this, you may attempt to shoulder-bash them, forcing that creature to pass a Strength saving throw against your Paladin Spell Save DC or be knocked {@condition Prone|PHB} and suffer 2 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. On a success, you are moved back to the nearest unnocupied space within 5-ft. of the target and where you came from.

entries.name: Knight's Denial
entries: Whenever you would be targeted by a ranged attack or the line of reach for such an attack would pass through within 5-ft. of you, you may spend your Reaction to attempt intercepting that projectile. You reduce the amount of damage that attack would deal by a d10 + your proficiency bonus, rolling an additional d10 for each {@condition Defensive Stance|TheUndertomesPRT} count you currently have.

Furthermore, You now have an additional amount of Reactions you may take equal to half your proficiency bonus, but you may only use them for Opportunity Attacks, Knight's Denial, Shock-Nullification and the Reactions granted by the Shield Master feat or Protection fighting style. You also gain an additional use of your Bonus Action that you may only spend for Knight's Advance.

subclassFeature.name: Celebration for the Departed

entries: "The barrel of the gun does not fire bullets of butterflies; it is merely that butterflies, both living and dead, bloom from where the gun points."

The memory of fireworks is one that warms the hearts of many people, calling to attention a blast of heat that warms the heart as much as it does the body. You might have come to harbour something near such memories, yet the principle of a spectacle to remark on the importance of life isn't ever lost on you, and that manifests in your weapons of choice. You gain proficiency in Firearms and due to a gathering of knowledge pertaining to celebrations and ceremonies, you are uniquely qualified to preside over funerals and to safely guide souls to a peaceful afterlife.

You may perform funeral rites over a period of at least an hour, granting a lifted weight for the living, yet guaranteeing the restfulness of the dead. The dead subject of this ceremony cannot be revived through any means other than {@spell True Resurrection} under the condition of the spirit being willing as well and may not be contacted through means such as the {@spell Speak with Dead} spell.

To properly complete this ritual you need at least the body of a deceased creature or an item of great importance of the dead. They may be of undead type, but must be Unconscious and willing for the whole duration to become departed.

subclassFeature.name: Celestial Abjugator
entries: Upon reaching 20th level, your words are infused with an overwhelming power when used right, moving and molding the hearts of others with ease. You gain 1d4+4 Order Die after a short rest or 8 after a long rest. Additionally, they are now considered d10s.

You also may cast the {@spell Command} spell at will without spending a spell slot, when you do so, you may spend one Order Die to increase the word limit of the spell to five words, also granting a roll of the Order Die as a bonus to any rolls the creature may go through during the spells order.

subclassFeature.name: Celestial Burst
entries: You may choose to overload your Astral Marbles as an action during your turn, making them not grant any effects on until the end of your next turn, but also causing an active effect to happen, as following:

rows: Anguilla

rows.name: Slithering Pathway
entries: You open a 5-ft. by 5-ft. portal on an empty space within 5-ft. and another one within another unoccupied space you can see in a 60-ft. radius. A creature may spend 5-ft. of their movement speed to cross from a portal to another. You may close these portals as a free action on your turn, otherwise they collapse at the end of your next turn. You can also spend your reaction when a creature would cross to collapse it ontop of them, pushing them back to the space they attempted to travel from and forcing them to pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer your Astral Current’s worth of d8 psychic damage and the same value in {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

rows: Gallus

rows.name: Starburst
entries: You huff your chest and bellow out a mighty scream, causing the air where your voice has carried to tense up and burn in a bright light, forcing all hostile creatures within a 30-ft. radius of you to pass a Constitution saving throw or suffer double your Astral Current’s worth of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, also pushing them your choice of up to your Astral Current times 5-ft. away from you, rendering them {@condition Prone}. On a success that creature only suffers half the {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, rounded down.

rows: Hirudo

rows.name: Blood Collection
entries: You may cast a spell that performs an attack against a Bleeding creature, making a great volume of their blood burst out and having them suffer an additional d8 damage ( Which matches the spell’s damage type ) equal to half the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count the target is suffering from, to a maximum of double your Arcane Current’s worth of extra damage. That same amount of additional damage becomes a pool of hit die you may distribute to creatures within 30-ft of you as part of this action. Creatures who don’t have blood or that have toxic blood are immune to this damage.

rows: Noctua

rows.name: Truth-Pulse
entries: You send out an arcane pulse from your Star Luminary, instantly dispelling all Illusions and making {@condition Invisible} beings visible again within a 60-ft. radius of yourself, also granting an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to yourself or a creature of your choice within 15-ft. This pulse does not reveal Illusions or {@condition Invisible} creatures who have come to be through a spell whose level is greater than your Arcane Current.

rows: Sextans

rows.name: Astral Flare
entries: You may consume 6 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as a bonus action to grant a +1 bonus modifier to your next spell attack or add +1 to your Spell Save DC for your next spell cast. You may spend up to 24 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at once, for up to a +3 bonus modifier.

rows: Rangifer

rows.name: Tectonic Stomp
entries: You place your Star Luminary against a surface, causing a devastating earthquake that covers a 30-ft. long cone, turning it into Difficult Terrain and then forcing all creatures within reach to pass a Strength saving throw or suffer double your Arcane Current’s worth of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and then triggering {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} against them.

rows: Vespa

rows.name: Rapid Striking
entries: You tap into this Marbles powers as an action, suddenly having a burst of speed, being able to perform an amount of melee or ranged weapon attacks equal to your Astral Current as part of this action, but dealing one less damage die on a hit, to a minimum of one damage die. You inflict {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your Astral Current whenever you deal damage from these attacks.
Furthermore, your Star Luminary becomes a +1 Spellcasting Focus.
Stars glow blue in the dark.
Looking at them up close, those weren’t actually stars.
These are stars.
The person claims what they’re holding are stars.
As if they read my mind and knew what I was thinking.

subclassFeature.name: Chainstrike [連擊]

entries: "Until such a time arrives that I might inherit the title, I shall continue to be of service to my master and home myself without end."

You gain proficiency with {@item longsword|PHB|Longswords} and {@item Single-Stroke Katana|TheUndertomesBH|Single-Stroke Katanas}, and all swords you hold gain the {@itemProperty DRW|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Draw} ({@damage 1d8}) property. Once per turn, whenever you perform an attack roll, you may choose to unsheathe your blade, attack, then sheathe it again as a part of the same action, gaining 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} before the attack.

When you do this, as long as you still have 10 feet of movement remaining, you are able to dash through the attacked creature in a 10-foot line to an unoccupied space, dealing additional damage equal to your Martial Arts dice. Until the end of your turn after dashing this way, you no longer provoke opportunity attacks.
Upon reaching level 6, you can perform this twice per turn, and thrice upon reaching level 17.

Additionally, you may attack with your sword while it is still sheathed, dealing Bludgeoning damage instead of Slashing damage. For each sheathed attack that you hit, you may spend 1 Ki point to gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If you kill a creature while your weapon is sheathed, you gain 4 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: Also on 3rd level you gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

entries.name: Dullahan.
entries: As a part of this channel divinity action, you cast the {@spell Find Steed} spell, except it has the casting time of 1 action and its duration is 1 minute, although you don't need to maintain concentration on it, your mount will disappear by the end of the spell.

The form your steed takes when casting the spell this way is always of Dullahan, a headless black horse wreathed in darker shadows. If you already have bonded with a mount through casting Find steed or any other steed spell, you maintain your mount's original stat block, except for the following changes. If you don't have a mount, then Dullahan will use the statblock of Dullahan as described in the end of this document. Additionally, when mounting Dullahan, you may choose whether to take a defensive or offensive stance. If you take the defensive stance, your AC increases by 3, but you take a -2 penalty to attack rolls. If you take the offensive stance, your AC decreases by 3, but you add a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. Whenever you kill a creature you gain 1 point of {@condition Coffin|TheUndertomesOA}, however while mounting Dullahan, you gain 2 points of {@condition Coffin|TheUndertomesOA} instead.

entries.name: O, Dullahan...!
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 ({@dice 1d12+4|1d12 + 4}) psychic damage. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, If the target has {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they take an additional {@dice 1d6} psychic damage for each stack of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Otherwise, they gain 2 stacks of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Call of the Erlking.
entries: As a reaction you take when an allied creature falls unconscious, you may bring them back for the Wild Hunt to continue aiding you. If the creature is not a player, you gain control of it and get to dictate its next actions as a free action on your turn. If the revived creature is a player, you may suggest courses of action, but they ultimately decide what their character will do.

The creatures regain 1 hit point if they're at 0, plus temporary hit points equal to 5 times your Paladin level. After a minute, this effect ends, all of their hit points are lost, and they fall unconscious once more.
For the duration, you also gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever you successfully hit a target with an attack roll, add a +1 to your damage dice for each stack of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} the target has to a maximum amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus. (Rounded Down)
Once per turn, you may choose an ally brought back by the Wild Hunt. They may add an additional +2 to their attack and damage rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity

entries: "Well, then why'd you go narkin' us if you knew what was comin', eh?"

You gain the following two Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works. If there is at least 1 member of the Middle within 10 feet of you, you may spend an additional use of Channel Divinity before needing a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Sibling Retaliation.
entries: As a Bonus Action, until the start of your next turn, you can take 1 additional Reaction per Round, even if you have already spent your usual Reaction. When a friendly creature within 10 feet of you is attacked, you can use a Reaction to punch or kick the attacker as long as they are within reach or you have enough movement speed to reach them. You make an Unnarmed Attack against them, and the enemy suffers either 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, your choice. If the friendly creature that was attacked was from the Middle, you deal an additional dice of unnarmed attack damage and inflict 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Vengeance Tattoo Resonance.
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can use your tattoos to improve your physical capabilities. For 1 minute, your AC increases by 2, and you gain Temporary Hit Points in a number of d8 equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Additionally, you gain advantage on all Strength rolls, and you can jump twice the height and distance you would normally be able to without taking fall damage.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity

entries: "Disruption in the territory protection zone confirmed."
You gain the following two Channel Divinity options once you reach level 3. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

entries.name: Warden's Shock-Negation
entries: For the next minute, while you are wielding a Heavy or Two-Handed weapon you may use the Shock-Nullification. Reaction.

entries.name: Shock-Nullification
entries: As a Reaction, whenever you or a creature within 30 feet of you is hit by an attack, you position yourself to be catch the attack, spending any remaining movement speed you to be within 5-ft. of the target creature and the attacker if you choose to defend someone else. You become the new target for that attack instead, taking half the damage the attack would have dealt and gaining one {@condition Defensive Stance|TheUndertomesPRT} count.

entries.name: Emergency Protection
entries: As a bonus action, choose a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see to be enveloped by the golden aura of your aegis. They gain a bonus to their AC equal to half your proficiency bonus the next minute or until you next fall {@condition Unconscious|PHB}.

Additionally, when you first reach 3rd level in this subclass any weapon you wield that has the Heavy or Two-Handed properties is considered a Shield for the purposes of the Protection fighting style or similar requirements.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity

entries: "Behold, I proclaim this land a hallowed sanctum. Radiant shall it shine."
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Sanctum of Conservation
entries: As a Bonus Action you summon a holy field that covers an area of 30-ft. around you, weaving from light and faith various lines to spread the influence of your god. While you are within this area, the following effects are active:

items: Whenever you cast a Paladin spell, you instantly may grant yourself or a creature within the area an amount of {@dice d10} Temporary Hit Points equal to the Paladin spell slot level spent. This becomes a {@dice d12} for other Noir-Aligned characters.

Whenever you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, they suffer half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} and you gain the same value of {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS}.

Starting at 7th level, you may use your Reaction to spend 8 {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} count whenever a creature within the area would have their Hit Points reduced below 1 to have their Hit Points become unable to be lowered or raised until the start of your next turn.

entries: This area increases by 30-ft. when you reach 8th level, (60-ft.) and by a further 60-ft. upon reaching 14th level. (120-ft.)

entries.name: Sanctuary of Preservation
entries: As a Bonus Action you create a magical resting ground to lay upon, covering an area of 120-ft. around you. While inside, you and other creatures of your choice are washed over by calming sounds that whisper of prosperous and safe futures, granting Advantage to the chosen creatures to resist or end the {@condition Frightened|PHB} Condition. Additionally, this space becomes a prime zone for the creation and advent of thought, granting each creature inside a bonus to History, Religion and any type of Artisan's Tools checks equal to your Charisma modifier.

You may spend 12 {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} count to use either of these Channel Divinity without spending their use. Both your Channel Divinity areas do not move from the space they were first summoned around, and must be re-used to do so. They also last for up to one minute. Additionally, there may be multiple areas at once but their effects do not stack.
"Where order falls, only barbarism will remain."

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Gaze of Contempt.
entries: As a bonus action, you focus your excruciating gaze, forcing all creatures of your choice within 60 feet who can see you to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is {@condition Frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. While {@condition Frightened} in this way, it cannot take reactions or ready actions. Additionally, you have advantage on ability checks to Grapple or Restrain creatures {@condition Frightened} by this feature, and your weapon attacks deal extra damage to them equal to half your Paladin level (rounded down).

Creatures immune to being {@condition Frightened} automatically succeed on this saving throw. Starting at 13th level, such creatures instead have advantage on the saving throw rather than automatically succeeding.

entries.name: Lato Inspire Awe.
entries: The way you walk, the flourishes you take when you swing your weapon - You are simply awe-inspiring, daybreaking and resplendent to the core. As a reaction to when you would reduce a creature to 0 hit points, prevent another creature from taking damage or land a Critical Hit you may perform an awe-inspiring flourish such as a special finishing move, a striking declaration or simply sweeping your hair back.

When you do so, all friendly creatures within 30-ft of you that can see or hear you feel reinvigorated, gaining a number of d6 in temporary hit points equal to half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down. For each creature who gains this bonus you gain an Awesome Die. You may use these as a free action at the start of your turn to restore a number of d6 hit points equal to the amount of die spent or when you would deal damage to another creature, adding an additional d6 of the same damage type as the attack's damage for each Awesome Die spent. The temporary hit points gained last until your next Short or Long Rest, where any remaining Awesome Die also vanishes.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Divine Ordainment
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to ready the holy words to write into history as you speak. When you use this Channel Divinity, you gain 4 Order Die, which are d4s, which you can spend for the following uses:

entries.name: See This Through!
entries: As a reaction to when a creature would attempt an ability check, before it is rolled, you can spend a number of Order Die for up to your Proficiency modifier and spout orders on how to perform the action properly. They add your the Order Die spent to the value rolled. On a failure, you suffer the Die's value in psychic damage as your orders haven't worked.

entries.name: To Me!
entries: As a bonus action, you may spend one Order Die to have one friendly creature move up to half their total movement speed in your direction, as you give them the correct actions to take so they will do so swiftly and harmlessly, also having any opportunity attacks that came from this movement be performed at disadvantage.

entries.name: Hunt Your Quarry!
entries: By spending a number of Order Die for up to your Proficiency Modifier as a reaction to when a friendly creature hits with an attack, you may grant them the same number of spent die as a bonus to their damage. These bonus die are the same as the die size of the attack, such as a daggers d4 or a fire bolts d10, and deal the same damage type, as you hurriedly impose your might onto your allies, bolstering their force in turn.
You lose any Order Die that you haven't used after a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Overwhelming Control
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to augment your already strong presence with divine authority. As a bonus action, you grant yourself a +5 bonus to Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks for the next 10 minutes.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Punish the Impure

entries: To lay down judgement is not a secretary’s role.
You are an executor of your god’s will, allowing them to find and reach the unfaithful no matter where they stand. You lift your Holy Symbol towards a creature within 30 feet of you.

They must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, enormous green hands emerge from the skies to punch down at the creature, making they take {@dice 4d10} radiant damage and suffer 4 counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, your choice. On a success, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Sacrifice for the Family
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to raise your Holy Symbol high above your head and call upon the necessary sacrifices of your fellows for a grander good. As an action, you may send a wave of blood crashing down a 30 foot radius around you. All creatures within reach must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or have the blood leave gashes down their bodies, causing them to suffer half your Proficiency Modifier (Rounded Down) of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and the same value of slashing damage. If a creature fails this Saving Throw while having less than half their hit points, they suffer an additional stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} as their already present wounds are made much worse. On a Success, the creature only takes half damage. All the Bloodfeast gathered by this feature is raised into a bloody sphere flying above your head, which grants you and any other Bloodfeast consuming creatures within 15-ft of you a +1 bonus modifier to hit equal to each 5 Bloodfeast gathered, as the current yield of your sacrifice only makes your thirst more pronounced. This bonus can only reach up to a +3 and is reduced by one at the end of the round in initiative, the ball of blood dissolving when this bonus modifier becomes 0.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Solemn Lament for the Living
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to summon and unseal a great coffin that leads into where the dead go to rest, then retrieving the tools for your grave keeping amongst the living.
As an action, you raise your holy symbol and cause a coffin to raise from ethereal mists, then grab one of the following weapons of your choice:

entries.name: Condolences and Eternal Rest
entries: You retrieve a pair of twin revolvers that remain in inverse colours to one another, a set of tools to reap life from those that should remain dead. These have the {@itemProperty Light}, Range (30/60-ft.) and {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} (6) weapon properties and deal {@damage 1d8} of your choice of radiant or necrotic damage.

entries.name: Quiet Coffin. ( Requires at least 8th Level. )
entries: You forgo simply retrieving a weapon from the inside of the coffin, instead grabbing the coffin itself and shifting its material form to be that of a heavy machine gun. It has the {@itemProperty BST|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burst Fire} (PB), {@itemProperty Heavy}, {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} (PB) and {@itemProperty Two-Handed|PHB|Two-handed} weapon properties, yet whenever you take the {@action Attack} Action using this weapon you have a reach of a 45-ft. cone starting from you instead of having to select a single target. You roll a single attack roll whose result is considered against the AC of all hostile creatures within that reach, dealing your choice of {@damage 1d4} radiant or necrotic damage. If you make use of this weapon's {@itemProperty BST|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burst Fire} feature you may only select one target for all your attacks.

All these weapons count as divine foci for you, Whenever the {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesFL} Condition would be inflicted through your spells and you are using weapons from this Channel Divinity as your divine focus, you use your full proficiency bonus instead of half that value. ( Whenever aiming at a single or multiple targets. ) And provided you are wielding these weapons only, you inflict an additional {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesFL} count whenever you deal damage to a target
To reload these weapons you use no form of bullet, instead relying on the dead butterflies that kindly offer themselves as a source of ammunition.
These weapons also grow in power in tandem with you, becoming +1 magic weapons when you reach 5th level, +2 at 10th level and a +3 at 17th level.

Lastly, these weapons remain corporeal for one minute until they dissipate in thin air. For the duration you may summon a kaleidoscope of butterflies to aid you in locating the dead and undead within a range of 300-ft times the magic weapon bonus you gain from this feature, instantly allowing you to find the general direction of the aforementioned beings provided they are not actively entombed through walls of stone or metal that are at least 5-ft.
{@i He's carrying a coffin. A large coffin to pay tribute to the employees who have nowhere else to go. It is still too small to comfort those innocent sacrifices.}

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Summon Stew Cauldron
entries: With a chattering incantation you summon forth a huge soup cauldron that occupies a 5-ft an space thats within touch range of yourself, blessed to fulfil your duty of cooking. Once per combat, any friendly creature may spend their bonus action to drink from its glorious soup while within 5-ft of it, recovering an amount of {@dice d8} hit points equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, and gaining the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} condition, if they didn't have it already. Whenever a hostile creature or one you deem unworthy attempts to drink from the cauldron, they take the same amount they would be healed for as fire damage.
While within 5-ft of the cauldron you may spend your bonus action to add a Magical Ingredient to the brew, as described on the list below:

items: {@b Grilled Ginger.} A specially spicy pepper that teems with flickering flames. A creature who ingests this peppery brew deals an additional stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when they hit an attack, for up to 2 times per turn. This lasts as long as they are {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS}.

{@b Life Lettuce.} Crunchy and makes you feel fresh as a newborn leaf. A creature who ingests this alleviating brew is instead healed by an amount of {@dice d8} hit points equal to the Lifestew Cleric's proficiency bonus.

{@b Guiding Guarana.} This ingredient is famous for how its refreshing, calming the mind to focus on what it needs to. While {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} a creature who ingests this brew may add a {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to their skill checks. After doing so, they can only add this bonus again after failing another skill check.

{@b Brutal Beef.} Hard to chew and extremely juicy, this ingredient packs a punch by itself. A creature who ingests this thick brew has advantage on Strength Saving Throws and ability checks. This lasts as long as they are {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS}.

{@b Monster Mash.} This is undescribable but a great remedy to poison. A(n unlucky) creature who ingests this (???) brew instantly vomits. this clears their body of any poisons or non-magical diseases currently affecting them. If the ingesting creature was suffering from the poisoned condition, they may choose to instead hold the vomit in, performing an melee ranged attack they are proficient in choosing a target creature within 5-ft of them as a free action during the end of their turn. On a hit the target takes {@dice 3d4} poison damage and gains the poisoned condition instead.

entries: You may add a Magical Ingredient an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per long rest, rounded down. The cauldron has an amout of hit points equal to 10 * your level in Cleric and an AC of 13 + your proficiency bonus. When it would be reduced to 0 hit points, the iron cauldron crumbles to dust while the soup explodes violently, forcing any creature within a 15-ft radius to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw equal to your cleric Spell Saving Throw or suffer {@dice 4d8} fire damage and 4 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
This cauldron may be drawn from an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, becoming inert and empty after all uses are consumed.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: The Great Magicked Beeper

entries: "'Those whose eyes you have met, and those whose eyes you have not. 72 minutes. Kill.' Tis thou. Flee thee not, for the P-Prescript pointeth to thee."
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: /UNLOCK./
entries: Your heart and soul are entwined with the Living Will, and it's bidding is your own desire. Although bound in chain and key, you may spend your Action to temporarily be removed from such bounds. When you do so, you enter an /UNLOCKED/ state (More may be found below.) for the next minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

While in an /UNLOCKED./ /state, state, a shadowy flame-like emanation covers your arms and sprouts from your forehead like horns, (or covers your horns, if able.) completely synchronizing you with the Will. These count as natural weapons you are proficient with, they deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage and have the Finesse property, but the formation of claws around your fingers impedes wielding any weapons or shields. Additionally, at the start of your turns, if no hostile creature is The Prescript's Target, a creature becomes the Target as per the effect's description found at the end of this document.

Furthermore, while in this state your Unlocking slowly intensifies to greater outputs of power as you carry out the Will, starting with an Unlock count of 1. You inflict {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts on your weapon and spell attacks equal to your current Unlock count. You have Advantage on your first Attack Roll during your turn against the Target.

You gain one further count of Unlock for each cumulative 3 counts of Grace of the Prescript you have, and lose all counts when you exit your /UNLOCKED./ state. You gain one Grace whenever a creature with The Prescript's Target is first knocked {@condition Unconscious} or is killed.

entries.name: /PREORDAIN./
entries: You convene with your magicked device for guidance and clearance on what to do in a difficult path. You may ask any question to your DM, to which they may answer with a simple "Yes." or "No.", or if unable to produce such a clear answer, instead uttering a single word as a tip toward your objective, such as for example:

If you and your fellows are hunting a mad vampire, your DM may answer a vague but usable answer, such as "Spire." Nevertheless, if your objective is one that mav be blessed by the Device (A list can be found below. ), you gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Skill Checks pertaining to concluding that objective as your intuition grows stronger and more attuned to the Will.
Your /PREORDAIN./ Channel Divinity may come to grant you its bonus modifier in the following situations:

items: Finding a place or locale that you have asked about as part of this Channel Divinity.
For any Checks toward reaching the answer of a piece of research, such as finding a cure for a great plague.
To Charisma checks pertaining to interacting with other creatures to reach a desired outcome as per what you asked in this Channel Divinity.
To survive an immediate threat and escape from it, such as when asking the question of how to run away from a Dragon.
To tame or calm an animal or other similarly bestial creature.
Anything else that your DM agrees is fair to your question and that will lead you to the Will's objective.

entries.name: Designer's Note 1
entries: Usually, a Paladin of this subclass has a special Device that conveys them orders from their deity. It's a good idea to have this be a magic item that is permanently bound to them for as long as their Oath endures, re-appearing on their person if lost or that they may recall with a special ritual. It is also a recommended idea to have this function as a magic focus for the Paladin.

entries.name: Designer's Note 2
entries: Some may find the/PREORDAIN./ Channel Divinity too messy or too difficult to use, and for that we recommend instead using the alternative Channel Divinity that can be found at the end of this feature.

entries.name: /PREORDAIN./ [ALT].
entries: You convene with your magicked device for guidance and clearance on what to do in a difficult path. You instantly cast any Divination spell from the Paladin spell list without spending a spell slot. You may only cast these spells as long as you may cast spells of that appropriate level, such as needing to reach at least 5th-level in Paladin to cast the {@spell locate object} spell.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: The Road Back From Oblivion

entries: I want you to feel it all the same… The misery of forgetting it all… losing it all…

You can use your Channel Divinity to ask your god for temporary sanctuary, being able to take one creature of your choice within 5-ft. of you to a demiplane that is overlaid atop of the material plane, rendering you and that creature {@condition invisible} and intangible to all other creatures until the end of your next turn, but you both can see and hear what is happening as if you were in the same space of the material plane.

During this you cannot attack or otherwise interact with any creature that isn’t in this demiplane, which usually takes an appearence ontop of the terrain around you, such as an old brick road appearing under your feet above whatever was once there and ruined pillars all around. At the end of your next turn you are both warped back as a strong gale sweeps through you and the other creature, healing you both for half your maximum hit points, rounded down. If you brought an {@condition Unconscious} creature to this demiplane you may forgo your healing and instead have the other creature be healed for their full amount of hit die. Whenever you do this, you gain half your maximum Lifepowder count.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: The Sin Was of Your Bearing

entries: "The wooden doll begins - to tremble ever so slightly."

You raise your Holy Symbol and peel off all Talismans on your body, having all your pains cling to the paper to then pass along. Choose one creature within 30-ft. of you to throw these at, you lose all your {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} count and any counts of negative Conditions affecting you and inflict all of them to the target. If the target's level or CR is greater than a value equal to your level plus your proficiency bonus, they must pass a Wisdom saving throw or then have the counts passed to them. On a success, half of the count is inflicted while the other half remains on you.

Upon reaching 8th level, your Channel Divinity improves in the way you can divide this, being able to choose when using this Channel Divinity to target up to a number of creatures within 60-ft. to have your Condition counts equally divided amongst themselves. This number is equal to your current Talisman count and you may not target creatures that would benefit from a Wisdom Saving throw against this ability.

entries.name: Designer's Note.
entries: For the sake of clarification, it is good to denote that "Negative Conditions" are in specific {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and so on, including their permutations such as Heavily Bleeding or {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: To Paint the Rough Waves

entries: "I shall replicate a passionate heart."

Starting at 2nd level, you may use your Channel Divinity to unleash a wave of powerful attacks using your Beeper, changing it's fluid shape after every attack and drawing out every ounce of pain so that your goal may be reached. As an action you dash toward up to your movement speed toward a target within reach and perform an amount of weapon attacks using your Wilful Beeper equal to half your proficiency bonus, changing its form as per the Multitudes in a Crashing Wave before each attack.

On a hit, you inflict 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target and deal additional psychic damage equal to half their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, rounded down. Upon killing a creature this way, you may instantly move up to another creature within a reach equal to your movement speed and perform the same number of attacks with the same effects, repeating this process until you fail to kill a creature.

If a creature killed this way was {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD|Marked by the Prescript}, your next target becomes {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD|Marked by the Prescript} instead and you gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. If you fail to kill your target, you perform an final additional attack using the Scythe form of your Wilful Beeper at Advantage. This attack is a Critical Hit on a dice roll of 17-20.

After using this Channel Divinity, its use is not restored after finishing a short or long rest, instead requiring that you consume one count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD} to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: With the Power of Justice

entries: "As mandated by chivalry, foul play is strictly forbidden in combat; however, mercy should also not be expected."
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to summon forth the constellations from your tears, turning them into physical swords that surround you and protect your allies.

As a bonus action, if you are in Blessing Mode, you can lift your holy symbol and become surrounded by starry swords. For 1 minute, when a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force one of your swords to pierce you. The creature takes only half the damage from the attack, and you take the other half. This damage ignores your resistance and immunity.

entries.name: With the Tear-Sharpened Sword
entries: As an action, if you are in Despair Mode, you can lift your holy symbol and choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature). Sharp swords surround the chosen creatures, pointing toward hostile creatures. For 1 minute, when one of the chosen creatures hits an enemy with an attack roll, it can use its reaction to be pierced by one of the swords, taking {@damage 2d8} cold damage that ignores resistance and immunity and causing the creature it hit to take the same amount of damage.

subclassFeature.name: Checking the Book
entries: Every barbarian in the path of grievance carries magical tattoos that empower them in fights and allow them to deal devastating blows to their enemies and the enemies of their family. Also on level 3, you engrave two tattoos of your choice on your body, from among the tattoos described below, and each time you gain a level in this class, you can replace one tattoo you know with a different one from this feature, as they need a constant flow of magical ink, not permitting all of them to be active at once. When you reach certain levels in this class, you learn additional tattoos, as shown in the Tattoos Known table.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can engrave one of your known tattoos onto a willing creature or reactivate one with magical ink. Your tattoo remains active on that creature until you finish a long rest, after this, the magical ink ceases to have effect unless you activate it again. Any Tattoo can be engraved and activated, as long as it is known to you. Allied creatures can count levels from any class for the sake of using your level-restricted Tattoos.

entries.caption: Barbarian Tattoos Known
rows: 3rd
6th
10th
14th

entries: The tattoos shown at the bottom of this document are available to you when you learn a tattoo. If a tattoo has a level requirement, you must be at least that level in this class to learn the tattoo. If a tattoo requires a saving throw, your Tattoo Magic save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.

items: {@optfeature Tattoo of Family|TheUndertomesPG}
{@optfeature Tattoo of Remembrance|TheUndertomesPG}
{@optfeature Tattoo of Loyalty|TheUndertomesPG}
