subclassFeature.name: Cheerful Spirits

entries: "T'was but another jolly holiday night. That the Cheerful Spirits came out to bring fear and delight. Through gifts, plentiful and wondrous. Their dear patrons would find their lives quite disastrous."

Warlocks of the Cheerful Spirits follow the harrowing whims of a multitude of different souls, being granted a single gift-bag with a myriad possibilities for chaotic delight. Of course, they are also provided with a handful of co-worker gnomes that will do their best to fulfil whatever is needed to bring out the cheer in people!

The lifes of these Warlocks is beset by an undecisive magic that always keep them on their toes, usually either forcing badness unto them directly or having them become closed off in a last ditch attempt to endure their supernatural holiday calling.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Cheerful Spirits lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Cheerful Spirits Pact Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell chaos bolt|XGE|Chaos Bolt}, {@spell grease|PHB|Grease}
2nd
{@spell Nathair's mischief|FTD|Nathair's Mischief}, {@spell pyrotechnics|XGE|Pyrotechnics}
3rd
{@spell create food and water|PHB|Create Food and Water}, {@spell sleet storm|PHB|Sleet Storm}
4th
{@spell confusion|PHB|Confusion}, {@spell fabricate|PHB|Fabricate}
5th
{@spell animate objects|PHB|Animate Objects}, {@spell awaken|PHB|Awaken}

entries.name: Fine Gifts For All!
entries: You have made a pact with a number of discordant, dissonant and dishevelled spirits who only care for whimsy and merriment, being granted an artifact from them all. This artifact is a Cheerful Giftbag made from patchwork and conflicting feelings alike, usually taking the appearance of a large burlap sack covered in ribbons and chimes, or any other appearance of your choice. This Giftbag has the same properties as a {@item Bag of Holding}, except you can also pull Giftboxes out of it which contain mysterious presents for your use.

As an action during your turn you may draw a Giftbox from the bag and either open it as part of that same action, gift it to a creature within 5-ft. of you or toss it anywhere within 60-ft. of you. If you gift it to an unwilling creature, it must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock Spell DC or be compelled to accept the gift, dropping whatever it is holding if it doesn't have a free hand. After you decide to keep, give or throw a Giftbox like this, roll a {@dice 1d8|d8} to determine its effects when opened as per the following table:

entries.caption: Mystery Gift Box of Heck Effects
colLabels: Mystery Gift Box of Heck Effects
rows: Gnomic Helpers

A gaggle of four Gnomes jumps out of the Giftbox and each one rushes toward a creature of your choice within 30-ft. of the Giftbox. That creature gains an additional {@dice 1d4|d4} bonus modifier to their rolls until the end of your next turn, where they pop into confetti.
Gift Within a Gift

There is a box within the box, roll {@dice 1d4}. On a 1, there is a {@item Potion of Healing}. 2 has a {@item Potion of Growth}. 3 has a {@item Potion of Flying} and a roll of 4 has a {@item Potion of Mind Reading}.
Modern Classic

Its a round, dark and very volatile bomb. All creatures within 15-ft. of the GIftbox must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@damage 1d6} + your proficiency bonus' worth of {@damage 1d8|d8} piercing damage. On a success, they only suffer half that damage. Structures and objects not being held or worn suffer double this damage.
Gnomic Raiders

A gaggle of four Gnomes with weapons emerge from the Giftbox, attacking the nearest creature within 60-ft.. You perform a number of spell attack rolls against that creature equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. On a hit, they deal {@damage 2d4} + your Charisma modifier slashing damage. This damage cannot be non-lethal and on killing a creature, the Gnomes overtake the corpse until the end of the next Round. Upon that time passing, roll a {@dice 1d4|d4}. On a roll of 1, the body is made into a surprisingly cute trinket ( as per the Player's Handbook Trinket Table ) . On a roll of 2, it becomes a +1 weapon of the DM's choice. On a roll of 3, it becomes a +1 armor of the DM's choice. On a roll of 4, it becomes a +1 magic focus. Any magic items created like this rot away after one day.
Yuletide Howls

The box is actually a music box, playing a loud cacophony of holiday tunes that covers a 30-ft. area around itself. All creatures within reach must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC or become frightened of it until the end of their next turn. Creatures {@condition Frightened} this way may re-attempt this Wisdom saving throw at the end of their next turns.
You

The gift grows a toothy candy-cane maw and attempts to eat the nearest creature within 10-ft. of it. That target must pass a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition Grappled} and {@condition Restrained} inside the box until the end of your next turn. While suffering these Conditions, the target creature gains Resistance against all damage types.
Buddy-Ship
Its pure holiday cheery magic! You and up to your proficiency bonus' worth of creatures within 30-ft. of you gains a +1 bonus modifier to their Saving Throws for the next minute.
Santata's Big Surprisese!

A gigantic, muscular and dry arm bursts out to sucker punch the nearest target within 15-ft. That target must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of {@damage 1d12|d12} bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half on a success. Also on a failure the target is pushed up to 15-ft. in a direction of your choice.

entries: You may also forgo rolling by spending a Warlock spell slot, being able to choose the exact effect instead. You may pull a gift from the bag this way an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring spent uses after a short or long rest.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This ability and subclass as a whole is incredibly chaotic, and a way to mitigate it if the player and GM concur on doing so is by allowing the player to roll the {@dice 1d8|d8} for effect and then being able to decide if they wish to keep, give or throw their gift. Another option is treating the low-level character as someone who doesn't know much about the gifts yet and is getting familiar with them, being able to roll before deciding how to act after seeing each effect happen or reaching 4th level first.

entries.name: Infinite Gifts
entries: Happiness can come in many ways, and the Cheerful Spirits have blessed your very touch to contain and spread holiday cheer. You gain proficiency in land Vehicles and through the course of a long rest you may enchant one to gain a fly speed equal to its movement speed for the next 24 hours, as it is infused with sheer holiday cheer. Furthermore, you also gain proficiency in the Performance skill.

subclassFeature.name: Chink in One's Armor

entries: "You're full of openings."

Your ability to exploit weaknesses has grown in precision, being able to drive your blade right through even the scales of a dragon to ensure that you'll carve your way out of any bad situation. When your attack roll would trigger a Sneak Attack against a creature that is benefitting from armor or natural armor you may focus to pierce straight through the smallest openings available, considering the target's AC is against this attack to be only 10 + their Dexterity Modifier. On a hit using this ability you also inflict an additional 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring spent uses on a long rest.
Additionally while your {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesSR} count is 2 or greater creatures have Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

subclassFeature.name: Chronocrush Arcane Tradition
entries: Wizards of the Crushbound Arcane Tradition are oddballs among oddballs, obsessed with compressing the very concept of time into the palm of their hand to use much like a battery, unleashing its potential to hasten themselves or the world around them just as they slow it by extracting this precious metaphysical concept.

They are most often a subsect of the Chronurgy school of magic, specializing in a practical and direct reapplication of time as a resource and procuring as much knowledge as they can within this niche of the arcane sciences.

Crushbound wizards are few and far between in any realm, usually hermits in search of higher knowledge about the concept of time. They are often drawn to adventure either to search for it or to apply their widely insane theories in field practice, with little regard for the consequences of compressing time, as they see it as simply another source of energy.

subclassFeature.name: Chrysalide de la Chair

entries: "Cette campagne ne prendra jamais fin, pas tant que nous n'aurons pas arraché le moindre lambeau de la Peau d'Or des Noirs pour nous l'approprier..."

The red of your Changing Room calls to you once more, and your heart skips a beat from having found its calling. The next time you have a long rest, you spend all of it inside the Changing Room as you feed and grow into something else, then choosing either the Chef-d'Œuvre Vorace or Foi Inébranlable feats to gain.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Hexbind
entries: Druids of the Hexbind are ones that at first sight might not seem to fit the usual thoughts of such a nature-keeper, yet their druidism lies in their deep connection to life and the concept of animation itself, giving movement to beings whose bodies would be inert otherwise. Usually these folk are coated in a mask of dramatic flair and a desire to broaden their craft, turning the very world to their stage. Of course, another important part of these is that their penchant for dabbling in life also comes with the ability to alterate its nature, usually with magic that binds the very soul with powerful curses.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, Hexbinders were originally wizards who researched the homes of horrid Hags, learning through observation and various attempts to recreate the animations these witches, eventually leading to the creations Hex Dolls and this sub-type of the arcane itself.

On others such as Eberron, the liveliness of a Hexbinder is lost in favor of those reanimating the hulks of forgotten machines for their own means, being seen less as some sort of odd bard-witch, and much more like a necromancer reanimating dead warriors for their own pursuits.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Tears
entries: {@i A Druid Subclass by the Undertomes}

Druids of this circle are completely in-tune with their emotions and the feelings of those around them - they carry the burden of people, animals and plants that come to them for aid. They know tears are a necessary, cleansing part of life, and they are not afraid to cry when they need to, as well as teach whoever needs it to cry as well.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Iron Maiden
entries: Druidism is regarded as an ancient tradition relating to the natural world and sometimes even abhoring that of technological advancement that stiffles that natural growth of all things. Despite that, or even because of that there is a small, peculiar circle of druids which choose to embrace that technology - that so called tainted metal to replicate nature itself, a controversial medium for a pure passion of this so called "artwork".

Those which follow the circle of the Iron Maiden have stripped themselves of their supple flesh and instead addorn it as material for their creations, embellishing the natural world with their very self for the sake of spreading their unbridled joy and vision of the world around them. They also do such in a way that encapsulates the moment of lightning striking the ground or a volcano erupting - a slow, deliberate sudden moment where they may spend months and years under their iron shell only to enrichen a glimpse of the presence of their body underneath.
They may not be well seen in druid communities, but one thing is certain: the passion these folk have for their art is unrivaled, going toe to toe with even that of a bards love for the arts.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Obsidian Stormrider

entries: "His Majesty's Hongyuan converges with your vision for Hongyuan at its culmination, young Miss."

Loyal as can be, the druids who form the Circle of the Obsidian Stormrider are hardly connected amongst themselves, instead claiming to hold the force of a hundred men on their own - Often choosing to leash their life to a master to whom they serve diligently.

At their best, they are houndlike in their loyalty and steadfast in assuring the growth and protection of those who surround them - However, this is two-fold, with some being easily perceived as sticklers for the rules or extremely demanding of their master for their own sake.

In certain worlds such as in the Forgotten Realms, these can be found as servants of the myriad rich families that litter the lands, often acting as their wardens and caretakers. In others such as Thespis they are roving travellers in search of true guidance toward their future glory, living only to become something grander than they could by their lone selves.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Wounds
entries: {@i A Druid Subclass by the Undertomes}

Moving on from death is a hard passage for most, yet an unavoidable piece of happenstance to all. You are one who has taken the calling of aiding the very world and those who live in it to move onto the other side, be that in freeing those who remain after their time from their ethereal permanence, removing the remains of the dead to where they may wither away in piece or guiding those in life to become focused in living instead of mourning the everpresent dead.

subclassFeature.name: Class and Respect

entries: "I'm a Soldato Secondo, you know...? It's about time I moved away from ammo cleaning duty to something more important, like ammo carrying duty for the esteemed Capos."

You've managed to be recognized as a decent enough soldier to reach a higher rank within your organization, benefitting from all the little amenities that can come with - But also being granted the great deal of importance to deliver orders to others in a clean and concise manner.

You may spend your Bonus Action to give an Order to a friendly creature within 30-ft. that can hear and understand you, granting them an {@dice 1d6} bonus modifier to their next skill check. You may also do so as a Reaction whenever they are about to make a skill check. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

This has also been ingrained through the very act of teaching, allowing you to spend a long rest teaching another creature that can understand you on tactics regarding a Skill you are Proficient in. They gain Proficiency in that skill until your next long rest. If you grant them Proficiency in the same skill six times in a row, they become permanently Proficient with that skill. (A creature may only gain proficiency in a only a single skill like this.)

subclassFeature.name: Cleaner's Supplies
entries: For your heavy workload you do own a set of tools and know many techniques to facilitate it all. Starting from 3rd level, you may select two of the following abilities. You may select an additional one every time you gain another Cleanup Expert feature. In addition, you may switch one single chosen Supply when you level up.

rows: Overcharge
None.
You forgo spending your action for this turn, but gain {@dice 1d6+2|1d6 + 2} {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks.
Endurance Matrix
None.

Your clothes have a thin sheet made out of energy that converts impacts done unto you into proper {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. You gain one {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when you take damage, up to an amount of times per turn equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Leap
None.

Tear a rift in space in front of you by spending 2 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, jumping in and moving up to 15-feet forward in a line, you reappear at any unoccupied space within that reach. If the area is fully occupied, the rift closes immediately after being opened and you do not spend {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Quick Recharge
None.

You've got a few small generators running at all times. You gain one {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stack at the beginning of your turns. You also gain an additional {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when generating it outside combat.
Rewind
None.

You spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to restore grievous wounds or destroyed objects. You do this as an action, when targeting another creature it is healed for {@dice 3d4+3|3d4 + 3}, and when targeting an object it falls under the effects of the {@spell Mending} cantrip, with the change that its area is 10-ft. by 10-ft.
Radio Comms
None.
You may spend 1 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to cast the {@spell Message} cantrip without its somatic component.
Charged Evasion
None.
You may spend 5 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to take a Dodge action as a bonus action.
Cleanup Mastery
None.

You gain an additional 5 feet of movement speed during your turn per 5 stacks of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} you currently possess. If you'd spend {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, this bonus movement remains until the end of your turn.
Instability Detonation
None.

You're outfitted to fully destroy unstable rifts, and whatever is touching them. When your attacks would cause {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to trigger, deal additional force damage equal to the amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks on target.
Energy Cycle
None.

Once per turn, before an attack you may declare to be using Energy Cycle. When you do, you spend one {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, but gain an additional stack of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit.
Ripple
None.

As part of your attack action, you may spend 3 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to briefly empower your weapon, granting it a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls until the end of your turn.
D. Demon Edge
None.

When you knock a creature below 0 hit points and it hasn't been rendered {@condition Unconscious} before in this combat, you gain 3 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, as your weapon absorbs their remaining energy.
Overcharge Order
None.

Your weapon has been fitted with blowout capacitors that boosts its performance the longer its been in combat. You gain a cumulative +1 to hit equal to each 10 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} spent during combat, resetting at any combat's end.
Show Off Instability
Dagger.

You may, as a free action at the start of your turn, spend 2 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} so that your attacks do not cause {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to be removed after striking a creature suffering from {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Disruption Generator
Longsword.

As an action, you may spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to briefly tinker with the tuning on your Longsword's energy projection. Perform a melee weapon attack against a creature within reach, on a hit, after inflicting Bind, all the stacks of Bind the creature are suffering become stacks of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesCL} instead.
Cleanup Support
Spear.

When a friendly creature within your reach attacks another creature, you may use your reaction to spend 2 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and perform a melee weapon attack against it. You have a +1 to hit if you currently have 4 or more {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Ceasement Order
Axe.

As a free action, you may spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to have your blade crackling from its electricity current, on your next hit against a creature, it takes an additional {@dice 1d4} lightning damage and has its movement speed reduced by half its maximum amount, as its too shocked to move.
Charged Leap
Gauntlets.

By spending 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and your action, you may Leap as in the Leap Cleaning Supply, with the addition that you may forcefully hit a target creature within the range of whatever space you reappear in, perform a melee weapon attack against them. On a hit, you deal two additional weapon damage die.
entries.caption: Cleaner's Supplies

subclassFeature.name: Cleanup Expert
entries: A Cleanup Expert is essentially a well-trained mercenary for many means, employing a variety of tools that they either made or learned how to use to their best ability. They are known for taking care of wiping out small raiding squads or even clearing out an area from invaders swiftly and efficiently, also restoring whatever space was left tattered and broken.

In the Forgotten Realms, Cleanup Experts run in the Express Clearance Guild that spreads through Waterdeep to Neverwinter, yet its reaches when it comes to work spread far and wide, dealing with relatively small goblin and kobold invasions at settlements or as the afterparty for when buildings are ransacked and need a quick restoration.

In Eberron, these Experts began their work in a much humbler approach, as a relatively small group wanting precisely to rebuild after the war, to turn weapons of destruction into restoration for such a torn world.

In the misty fogs of Ravenloft, Cleanup Experts walk with much less advanced tools, instead opting for the mystical and arcane, finding the ruins of places long destroyed and rebuilding them for their own use, a wanted sight for any roaming caravan lost in such lands.

subclassFeature.name: Close Quarters Combat
entries: Sometimes preserving a bullet might be the right shot, and you have learned that your Magic Bullets are not truly spent when not fired from your Marksman's Weapon, only unleashing a fraction of their power otherwise. You have developed your own form of close-quarters combat using your Marksman's Weapon in melee. It counts as a martial melee weapon with which you are proficient, you can use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls, and it deals {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage and 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

As a bonus action, you can prepare to empower your next hit with the Magic Bullet currently in the chamber. When you next hit, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 2d4} force damage and suffers the corresponding effect from the Close Quarters Magic Bullets table. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect unless the table says otherwise.

entries.caption: Close Quarters Magic Bullets
rows: The 1st Magic Bullet
You deal extra force damage equal to half your warlock level, rounded down, or half that amount on a successful save.
The 2nd Magic Bullet
On a failed saving throw, the target can take only one of a bonus action or a reaction on its next turn.
The 3rd Magic Bullet

On a failed saving throw, the target suffers 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and a penalty to its attack rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it suffers only 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
The 4th Magic Bullet
All hostile creatures within 5 feet of the target must make the same saving throw or suffer the same base effect.
The 5th Magic Bullet
On a failed saving throw, the target has its AC reduced by 2 until the end of your next turn.
The 6th Magic Bullet
This attack is repeated up to three times, once for every 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target.
The 7th Magic Bullet
This attack deals {@damage 4d8} force damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much on a successful one, but you take the same damage dealt.

entries: The effect is determined by the bullet currently in your Marksman's Weapon's chamber. You cannot benefit from the effect of a bullet that has already been fired until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: College of Lifeblood
entries: Members of the College of Lifeblood decided to add a spice to their shows and parades that no other Bard would morally consider - which makes their craft more special than any other. They fearlessly draw from cruelty, violence and fear to paint the crowds in unforgettable shades of crimson. White blood and guts, they lead a march of masks, parasols and colorful dresses that change the lives of any towns and villages they visit forever.

Their parasols have a special mechanism which allows them to both draw and expel blood quickly through its end tip, which they use to sign their works and paint vibrant pictures of carnage. They always carry masks with themselves to add to the mystery of whoever is behind it, as well as to avoid the ones focused on maintaining the law.

Bards of this College want to spread joy, in their own twisted sense, throughout the realms, but they also want to be the lead as they do so - the one that vaunts always in front of the bloody promenade. The centerpiece, and the brightest jewel. Let your jealousy and the envy of others burn as you rise as the main character of life's spectacle.

subclassFeature.name: College of Screaming Harmony

entries: "I know it hurts, but please, stop struggling...!"
"I promise, nothing could make as fascinating music as a human can... Nothing!"

Rockin' is all that a bard of the magnanimous and great COLLEGE OF THE SCREAMING MELODY needs to be alive, to be able to shred flesh with metal and have music be performed by each dying noise and beating gargle of another - Ah! Pure ecstasy.

Of course, people - MOST people don't understand the artistry at work upon taking apart the human body to find the music inside, so these bards either take to being secretive in their work, only forming the occasional band perofrmance with their fellows or they swing the complete other way in an obsessive opulence that rivals even that of paladins!

subclassFeature.name: College of the Heartthrob
entries: {@i A Bard Subclass by the Undertomes}

Bards who follow the College of the Heartthrob are often neither bards nor followers, instead being such beautiful visages to behold and to hear that their exotic existence captivates the mortal heart, turning it into a maleable tool under their whims.

Most recognize their talent and use it to fulfil a duty inspiring others and becoming grand leaders and advisors, but others might choose to use such a gift to gain everything their ever wanted while leaving a trail of heartbreak behind their wake.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Rosehunters
entries: To trim the world into perfection, to let the roseate bloom of all things radiate - That is the creed of the Rosehunter bards.

Bards of the Rosehunter College are usually not only versed in how to hunt prey, but live for the sweet attention it brings, seeing being gifted a rose thrown into their way as a sign that what they are doing is what they are always meant to be doing. Overall, they are great acrobats who wield both whip and magic to masterfully put on a show no matter where.

In the Forgotten Realms, Rosehunters are found as a troupe of circus performers by day, using ropes and great monuments to show off their abilities in dazzling displays, while at night they stalk streets still with a shine in their eyes, using their thorns to destroy anything that might harm their circus goers.

In the dense mists of Ravenloft, Rosehunters embrace much more the glory of a well done hunt, making use of tight, coiling vines to choke out the life of their prey and then rip them to bits, directing any colleagues into the most perfect roles for such work.

subclassFeature.name: College of Weathered Tales
entries: {@i A Bard Subclass by the Undertomes}

The College of Weathered Tales is a particular craft passed down from generation to generation, sometimes through a hereditary tradition in certain families, sometimes by an old master to a completely unrelated student. In either case, a bard of such College is oftentime a minstrel by trade who spins stories of times forlorn to time, using their magic and knowledge to make one feel like they were stuck back into the past, using of nostalgia as a powerful tool to enable and disable all alike.

Inside this College tales are often the same told time after time, with one’s grandest objective as a bard being not only to tell them far and wide, but to add to them - To create or learn of such a story that will withstand time with pride, never leaving the shared repertoire of their peers.

subclassFeature.name: Colpi di Taglio

entries: "... I've already waited way past what anyone oughta put up with. And right when I thought I was finally getting my ass outta this goddamn cold, what happens? My Ticket turns into blank scrap paper, all because of that mongrel brat! Ha... Haha... Gimme a fucking break."
This is done through dual weapons, allowing you to make perfected use of Two-Weapon Fighting:

items: You may wield two weapons without the prerequisite of one of them being Light, instead only requiring that neither weapon is Heavy.

Whenever you make an {@action Attack} as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules you still add half your ability modifier to the damage dealt. Whenever you do so, you choose whether you inflict 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on your target, or triggering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Upon reaching level 10, this count increases to 4.
When you Attune to a pair of magical weapons, they both count as a singular Attunement, taking only one slot and becoming Unattuned if either Attunement is broken.

entries: Additionally, whenever a creature misses you with an attack you may spend your Reaction to use {@i Sezionatura di Coniglio} as an attack against that creature. You may do so an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.
When entering your Rage, you may use {@i Sezionatura di Coniglio} as an attack against a creature within range without expending a use of the feature.

entries.name: Sezionatura di Coniglio
entries: On a hit, you deal damage as usual and the creature suffers 1 count of both {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you are raging, you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Creatures that are Small or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Commanding Cry

entries: "Leap upon the first. - And the second. - Break and surmount them."

There is an order to things that you have long understood, and you have better found a way to convey that to others so that they may find their place in any setting that demands it. You may spend your Bonus Action to shout a Commanding Cry to a creature that can hear you within 60-ft. When you do so, choose one of the following type of order to bark out:

entries.name: Charge Forward! [冲锋!]
entries: The target creature gains an +1 bonus modifier to hit and deal double the damage they would to structures and unworn un-carried objects until the end of their next turn. This bonus is increased to a +2 upon you reaching 12th level.

entries.name: Hold the Line! [坚守阵地!]
entries: The target creature gains a +1 bonus modifier to their AC until the start of your next turn. This bonus is increased to a +2 upon you reaching 12th level.

entries.name: Center Yourself! [静心!]
entries: The target creature gains a {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to all rolls pertaining to one Skill of your choice for the next minute. This bonus is increased to a {@dice 1d6} upon you reaching 12th level.
You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Complete and Total Extermination!!

entries: "Scurry off and lick your wounds, 'cuz by the time I return, there'll be enough pain to go around for the whole gang."
For a while, you are able to show your siblings the true apex of an elder brother. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: At the start of your turn, you choose a creature within 30 feet of you to gain a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}.
A creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} has Vulnerability to Bludgeoning damage for the first attack they receive each Round.

Once per turn when you hit a creature, you can force them to roll a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take an additional dice of damage equal to your unarmed attack and are sent flying back in a 30-foot line and fall {@condition Prone}. Any creature within that line takes {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition Prone}. If there is a non-magical structure in their way, the structure is destroyed and they take an additional {@damage 1d8} dice of bludgeoning damage.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

entries.name: MY HAIR COUPOOOOOOOOOOONS!!!!
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can use an Action to Jump up to 50 feet in the air, then fall in a space within range. You do not take fall famage, and all terrain within 30 feet of your landing becomes Difficult Terrain, except for you and other Middle-aligned creatures. If the space is occupied, the creature must perform a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you slam their head against the ground, dealing {@damage 8d12} bludgeoning damage and Paralyzing them. On a successful save, they take only half that damage and suffer no additional effects. A creature Paralyzed this way rerolls this saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. If the creature had 50 hit points or fewer, regardless of if they failed or succeeded in the saving throw, they immediately explode from the impact and die.

subclassFeature.name: Corporist Specialization
entries: You have decided to lead your very own artistic movement inspired by the hidden beauty inside every living creature. Artificers with the Corporist Specialization aren't afraid to get their hands bloody in search of materials for their craft. To them, the anatomy of every living being is a canvas waiting to be turned into art, and you always research the best methods to heed their call.

subclassFeature.name: Corporist Spells
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Corporist Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don't count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.caption: Corporist Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell charm person}, {@spell inflict wounds}
5th
{@spell hold person}, {@spell spike growth}
9th
{@spell animate dead}, {@spell fear}
13th
{@spell dimension door}, {@spell grasping vine}
17th
{@spell dominate person}, {@spell raise dead}

subclassFeature.name: Corpus Ribcage Arrangements

entries: "These blood vessels are sufficiently thick. Not bad at all."

Your armored state has been perfected like the bark of a tree, splintering off when hurt and stabbing back at its attackers. Whenever you roll Initiative, you may also roll an amount of Hit Die up to half your proficiency bonus, then gaining that value plus your Wisdom Modifier's worth of Temporary Hit Points. You instantly lose these when entering Flowing Form. While these Temporary Hit Points remain, whenever another creature deals damage to you through a weapon attack they suffer 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

While in Iron Maiden Form you've developed a new ways to move, throwing your weight in one direction at the risk of becoming rattled. Once per turn you may spend 5-ft. of movement as a Free Action to instantly move up to a 15-ft. line. If you would collide with a creature or object that is at least small, that target must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Druid Spell DC or suffer half your proficiency bonus' worth of d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure. On a success or if you don't hit anything, you trip and must attempt that saving throw yourself instead, suffering the same consequences on a failure.

Additionally you have learnt how to distort your voice well in the chambers of your second skin, granting you Advantage on {@skill Deception} checks and other creatures Disadvantage on attempting {@skill Insight} checks targeting you, provided you are in Iron Maiden Form.

subclassFeature.name: Corteous Dress Making
entries: Upon reaching 15th level, you've created and recreated many pieces of wear, but now you've outdone yourself in a way that would leave even the dullest fashion sense in awe. Over the course of a long rest, you may create a Fashion Masterpiece, which counts as light armor that you are proficient with. When you create your Fashion Masterpiece, you may choose to give it up to three of the following traits:

items: {@b Blooming Rose Adornment.} You may spend 5 Bloodfeast to cause floral and thorn-like adornments of your clothing to magically lash out at creatures within 5-ft of you as a reaction to when you take damage. All creatures around must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@dice 4d10} slashing damage and be pushed back 5-ft, or take half the damage on a success.

{@b Reinforced Fabrics.} You may spend 3 Bloodfeast and a bonus action during your turn to soak your clothing in blood, making it more resilient. You gain +1 AC until the end of combat or when you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}. You may benefit from this up to three times per combat.

{@b Light Weaving.} You may spend up to 5 Bloodfeast at the start of your turn to make your clothes much lighter, gaining an additional 5-ft of movement per 1 Bloodfeast spent. You retain that bonus until the end of your turn.
{@b Fit for a Parade.} You may spend 4 Bloodfeast to restore your own blood, you may instantly spend two of your Hit Die and be healed for that amount.

{@b Jagged Shoulderblades.} You may spend 1 Bloodfeast before an attack to inflict an additional stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit as blood seeps into your gloves and aids your movements.

{@b Protective Padding.} You may spend 5 Bloodfeast as a reaction after you take damage to gain resistance against that damage type for the next three turns. If you use this feature while still benefiting from it, you lose the old benefits and gain the new, as your clothing can only reactively change its design to protect you when using its full focus. You cannot gain resistance against fire damage.

entries: You may only have one Fashion Masterpiece at any given time, if you attempt to create a new one while another already exists, you start seeing the failures in your old work, tearing it to pieces before being able to create again. You may choose to swap one of the Masterpiece's traits during a long rest, and it counts as a magical item which you must be attuned to, and you are automatically attuned to it when you create.

subclassFeature.name: Crimson Phoenix

entries: "What a... short-lived spring this is..."

Further mysteries of martial arts have been imparted onto you by your master. If the target has 3 or more Conditions affecting it, you score a Critical Hit on rolls of 19 or 20. Additionally, you have studied more Forms to improve your attacks. You gain access to the following abilities once per turn:

items: {@b Second Form - Destruction (壊).} By spending 2 Ki points, you score a Critical Hit whenever you hit an object or a structure until the end of your turn.

{@b Third Form - Blaze (炎).} By spending 5 Ki points, your next attack that hits does not remove any counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after triggering them, and applies half that amount of counts on the creature.

{@b Fourth Form - Qi (氣).} By spending 3 Ki points, if you would trigger a Posture Critical Hit this turn, you deal an additional d6 of damage and do not lose counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
{@b Fifth Form - Wings (翼).} By spending 4 Ki points, you gain a Flying speed equal to your movement speed for 1 minute.

subclassFeature.name: Crimson Spring

entries: "Hey, this is what money's for. To celebrate good tidings."

You have reached a point where your moves inspire both awe and fear into your enemies. If the target has 3 or more Conditions affecting it, you gain advantage on all Saving throws related to it and gain advantage on your first attack against them every turn. Additionally, you have studied the final Forms to turn your attacks into decisive blows. You gain access to the following abilities once per turn:

items: {@b Second Form - Passion (熱).} By spending 5 Ki points, whenever you hit a creature with an attack this turn, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Form Save DC or become {@condition Charmed} by you for 1 minute. A creature {@condition Charmed} this way continues {@condition Charmed} even if they are hit by an attack, and may reroll the saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success.

{@b Third Form - Decapitation (斬).} By spending 5 Ki points, the next time you score a Critical Hit until the end of your turn, you decapitate the attacker, and it dies if it can't survive without its head. If it would not die without a head, deal {@damage 6d8} bludgeoning damage instead. If you do not score a Critical Hit, you also deal an additional {@damage 6d8} Bludgeoning damage on your last attack that hit this turn.

{@b Fourth Form - Flow (巡).} By spending 5 Ki points, you can move this turn without provoking opportunity attacks. If you manage to hit the same creature at least 3 times from different positions, it must make a Constitution saving throw against your Form Save DC. On a failed save, they become {@condition Paralyzed}. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} Bludgeoning damage. Additionally, until the end of your turn, you get to perform a melee opportunity attack when entering the reach of a creature.

{@b Fifth Form - Blossom (花).} By spending 5 Ki points, you immediately gain 5 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. During this turn, if you score a Posture Critical hit, the creature suffers 4 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and you do not lose your counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At the end of your turn, if you didn't score a Posture Critical hit, the last creature you attacked suffers 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

{@b Plastered Sleep, Unrestrained Ripples [酔睡浪浪].} After you have used all of your Crimson Spring Forms at least once, you gain access to this ability. Once you use it, you must activate all of your Crimson Spring Forms at least once to use it again. the next time you hit a creature with an attack, they take a number of d12 Bludgeoning damage equal to the number of Conditions affecting them + 2 rolls of your Martial Arts die in damage (minimum of 1d12 + 2 Martial Arts dice). If that kills them, you can move up to your movement speed and roll a melee attack against a creature within reach, producing the same effect and increasing the number of the martial arts die by one. If the first creature you hit isn't killed, you instead gain resistance to all damage types until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Crimson Strike

entries: "Hongyuan's certainly not changed one bit. Except for its roads, I suppose."

Whenever you hit a creature, the attack deals extra damage equal to one additional role of your Martial Arts die as long as it has 3 or more Conditions affecting it. Additionally, you have studied many Forms to improve your attacks.

If any Form requires you to roll a Saving Throw, your Form Save DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier. You cannot activate the same Form more than once if it hasn't yet ended. You gain access to the following abilities once per turn:

items: {@b Second Form - Rupture (破).} By spending 1 Ki point, until the end of your turn, you inflict 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you hit a creature.

{@b Third Form - Might (强).} By spending 2 Ki points, until the end of your next turn, whenever you make an attack roll or spend points of Ki you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to a maximum of 4.

{@b Fourth Form - Binding (束).} By spending 2 Ki points, until the end of your turn, whenever you hit a creature with an attack roll, they lose 5 feet of movement. If you hit the same creature more than two times, they lose 10 feet instead.

{@b Fifth Form - March (進).} By spending 3 Ki points, whenever you roll your Martial Arts die for damage, you may choose to roll double that amount of Martial Arts die instead, immediately ending this Form afterwards.

{@b Crimson Cleave.} After you have used all of your Crimson Strike Forms at least once, you gain access to this ability. Once you use it, you must activate all of your Crimson Strike Forms at least once to use it again. After you hit a creature, you may choose to transform one of each of their Conditions into counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: They gain 1 count of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each Condition that they are currently suffering and 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each non-stackable Conditions (such as {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Stunned}). For this attack, they will take additional damage equal to all of their counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead of half of them.

subclassFeature.name: Crossing Dervish

entries: "Leaping across rooftops of the City~ To protect its peace and safety~"

You have reached a point in your life where your knowledge has branched out to cover famous criminals and adventurers, and your battle skills are unrivaled. Once per Long Rest, you can cast {@spell legend lore} without expending a spell slot, however, it will also work for adventurers even if they are not yet of legendary importance.

If you have cast {@spell legend lore} this way to obtain information on a creature, you may choose to have this creature gain {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until your next Long Rest. Finally, you gain the following benefits. The DC for them is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier:

items: When you take the {@action Dash} action, you leave a fire trail behind you until the start of your next turn. Any creature that moves into or ends their turn inside the area must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your save DC. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d6} fire damage. On a successful save, they only take half that damage.

When you take the {@action Disengage} action, choose a creature within 5 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be forced to drop one of the items they're holding at random as you kick at them to fain momentum to escape.
When you take the {@action Hide} action, your next attack that hits deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the weapon's type.

subclassFeature.name: Crushbound Metronome
entries: Chronurgy's lineage of arcane traditions can be very specific at times, and you have studied the ways of compressing and compounding a series of moments into a smaller form fit for your hand, to use in any way you wish. Coupling that with a metronome-like technique to conduct your spells, you have begun mastering the ways of the Chronocrusher, gaining the following benefits:

entries.name: Accumulating Time
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you gain 1 count of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC}, a magically contained string of compacted time you can use to empower yourself. You can also use your action to gain 4 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC}, or your bonus action to gain 2 counts. When you successfully cast {@spell counterspell|PHB|Counterspell} against a creature, you gain 2 counts as well.

entries.name: Metronomic Quality
entries: Beginning on the first turn in combat, you switch between tempos of attack and defense in the way you weave spells. Odd-numbered turns are Tick turns, while even-numbered turns are Tock turns.

entries.name: Tick (Odd Turns)
entries: The flow of your spells focuses on the everlasting destruction in the passage of time. As a bonus action, you can spend up to twice your proficiency bonus in {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} to gain a bonus to either your next spell attack roll or your spell save DC equal to half the number of counts spent, rounded down. This effect lasts until the end of your turn. Furthermore, whenever you deal damage with a wizard spell, you inflict 1 additional point of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Tock (Even Turns)
entries: The flow of your spells dictates a mechanical, rigid defense that cannot be easily meddled with, just as time itself. As a bonus action, you can spend up to twice your proficiency bonus in {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} to gain a bonus to your AC equal to half the number of counts spent, rounded down. This bonus is reduced by 1 each time a creature hits you with an attack. Furthermore, you gain a bonus to Dexterity saving throws equal to half your Intelligence modifier, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Culminating Fragrance

entries: "It makes a pungent smell, does it not? It strikes your senses so intensely, you might almost fall to the ground... Such a deep and fragrant scent, it is."

Whenever you cast a spell, it leaves behind a lingering cloud of spice that nourishes your fellows and harms your foes. This cloud expands from the point it has hit to cover a radius of 5-ft. times the Spell Slot Level used, to a minimum of 5-ft. In the case of spells with multiple targets, this creates multiple clouds whose area is divided by the number of creatures targeted, rounded down.
Friendly creatures gain while starting or ending their turns within the cloud:

items: Recover 2 Hit Points at the start of their turns inside the cloud, unless they are {@condition Unconscious}.
Gain a +1 to Wisdom and Dexterity saving throws, or a +2 when you reach 18th level.
Are considered Lightly Obscured by hostile creatures.

entries: And hostile creatures suffer the following at the start or end of their turns inside the cloud:

items: 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
A -1 to Constitution and Charisma saving throws, or a -2 when you reach 18th Level.

entries: When ending their turn inside the cloud they must pass a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Blinded} until the start of their next turn. Any cloud created this way lasts for up to the start of your next turn if you haven't passed through it or ended your turn inside it. Furthermore, any magical gusts may cause the clouds to disperse and mundane ones only have it move 5-ft. in the wind's direction due to their high density.

subclassFeature.name: Culmination of a Fluttering Ego
entries: Your journey has reached a turning point. You will either be consumed by your own flame in self-destructive rage or embrace it as a controlled part of yourself. Choose Melting Pinion or Searing Wings, as you and your DM agree best fits your character development.

subclassFeature.name: Curse-Engraved Sword
entries: You gain proficiency with greatswords if you do not already have it, and greatswords have the Finesse property for you. Whenever you hit with a melee attack using a greatsword, you can use one of the following reactions:

entries.name: Strider Unleashed
entries: Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot line directly in front of you must make a Dexterity saving throw against a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and suffers 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, it takes the damage but suffers no additional effect.

entries.name: Runic Explosion
entries: The creature you hit must make a Constitution saving throw against a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 1d6} damage for each stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it currently has. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Curse-Wrought Bullets

entries: "There is neither; no fragments of memories, no need to look into them... fire, only fire!"

Whatever you touch eventually becomes tainted by the weight of memories you will never be able to run from, yet you have learnt how to focus the smog on your soul into a single point. At the start of your turns you may choose to have a creature become {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM}, the centre of your everlasting hatred. You may only do so provided there is no creature already {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM}, or you can use your Bonus Action to switch the victim of your Stigma.

Whenever you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack you gain 1 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, whenever you hit a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} creature, gain two additional counts as well.

Whenever you kill a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} creature you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus and one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} count, as the already dissolving mental image of that which you have shattered lingers on in your aim. If you kill or knock a friendly creature {@condition unconscious} you gain one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM}, yet you may only gain one count per creature per combat.
During your turn you may spend {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} as a Free Action you may take once per turn for the following:

items: {@b Reload, Then Fire.} By spending one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} you may perform an additional attack as part of your Attack action during your next turn. This extra attack does not stack. Additionally, any ranged weapons you are wielding are instantly reloaded at the start of your next turn provided you have enough ammunition on your person.

{@b Designated Target Fire.} By spending at least three {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} count you may spend your Action to perform a special attack, coating an 15-ft. radius within your weapon's range in a red haze that reeks of lingering sweat and charred hair. All creatures of your choice within that radius must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of d10 piercing damage and a sum of 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} spent. Creatures who succeed take half that damage and count instead. Afterward you gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each creature damaged through this, with an additional 8 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count if you have killed your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} creature through this attack. These 8 count do not count toward your turn limit. You cannot gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} in a single turn greater than double your proficiency bonus through this way.

entries: You gain an additional {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and deal an additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count from ranged weapon attacks after reaching 8th level in Ranger, and then an additional of each count upon reaching 14th level.

Whenever asked for a saving throw by a subclass feature, you use your Ranger Spell Save DC. Additionally, any attacks or effects that consume {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} count as magical attacks for the purposes of bypassing Resistances.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Cloud Blade
entries: Upon reaching 10th level your bladework is enough to entice fear into the hearts of your opponents, slicing cleanly through armor and those that would dare hide away their bodies in defense. As a bonus action during your turn you may give yourself a bonus to hit targets who are wearing Heavy Armor or have their Armor Class increased by external effects, such as the Shield spell. This bonus is equal to your Proficiency Modifier and you deal an additional damage die on a hit, with the dice being the same as your weapons damage dice. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Modifier, restoring its uses on a long rest.
Upon reaching 15th level, you deal an additional die of damage against targets within the criteria mentioned.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Cloud Martial Archetype
entries: "I would like to ask you to save business until later. I'd like to clean my blade in peace."

The life of a Dark Cloud fighter is one who acknowledges that their body will tell a tale just as well as any of their actions, forever preserving their great acts and tragedies in their flesh. Usually found as people who hold deep-rooted beliefs about life and grown to uphold their traditions, fighters of this archetype take special care of their weapons and when fighting to be decisive and lethal, a force to be reckoned with that will not be ignored, flowing with grace and holding mighty power such as the clouds above.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, the Dark Clouds are actually a proper group spread across Faerûn, assassin gangs that wield their blades for either whoever pays more or whomever holds the most power, usually collaborating with the Zentharim as they grew in power. Living as this type of mercenary is a life of stable and bloody work, as most of those trained in the bladework grow used to.

Meanwhile, in other places such as the mists of Ravenloft, Barovia itself holds a select group of such warriors, groomed and grown to serve under the eye of Count Strahd Von Zarovich as both money and blood-collectors, taken in not by any allegiance or contract, but bound by the whims of the vampire, living in fear that their swords will not be enough in case their master decides they are not needed anymore.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Clouds Gathering
entries: As you grow closer to your party and form tales with them. At 15th level you may offer to ink your entwined tales for the past and the future. You may do so during a Long Rest with a willing friendly creature, and may create up to your Proficiency Modifier's worth of Cumulus Tattoos at any given time, switching them when you gain a level in this class. A creature who is tattooed by you is considered linked and you gain advantage on {@skill Insight} checks against each other. Linked creatures may only benefit from one of your tattoos at any given time.

rows: Sun-Eater Cumulus

An ostentatious tattoo which resembles the overwhelming force of cutting through a horde together. You and the linked creature gain +1 AC when standing within 5 feet of each other and cannot be Surprised if the other isn't. Additionally, you do not suffer the negative effects of being {@condition Prone} if within the aforementioned range of your linked creature, as you can protect one another.
Cosmonaut Cumulus

This ink represents landscapes that warmed both of your hearts, forming an ever-living wanderlust of what once came to pass and what may then become. You and the linked creature can use a bonus action to see and hear through each other's senses while becoming {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} to your own surroundings. Only one of you can use this feature actively. Additionally, if any of you use the Help action on one another you may add the helping creature's modifier to your own, provided they are proficient in the required skill check.
Gathering Cumulus

Union formed in life and immortalized in ink. You and the linked creature may use your reaction when another attempts a roll to give the roll an additional {@dice 1d6} bonus modifier. You cannot re-use this feat to give your linked creature a bonus until they give you said bonus, or vice versa. Additionally, you are always aware of the general direction of each other and gain advantage on skill checks for tracking each other.
entries.caption: Dark Clouds Gathering

subclassFeature.name: Deathwalker Roguish Archetype
entries: A Rogue who walks so close to death is one who has for a long time worked as an assassin or dealt in the life trade. The hands of the dead still cling to their backs, yet that weight is a discomforting reminder of the job that has been done and that will keep being done, a flame to keep burning no matter what. Deathwalkers tend to have no qualms displaying their exhaustion, yet only fools believe that fatigue will stop one such assassin. In realms such as Faerûn, Deathwalkers are commonly found as those who forgo dark hoods when sitting at taverns, much more concerned with actually getting a moment of rest before they are sent to their next job issued by any who pay, be it Harper, Zentharim or else. In others, such as the forsaken mists of Ravenloft, the Deathwalkers are no more than those who have embraced the lingering death everywhere, letting it fester in their hearts like a rot, using that very poison to keep themselves alive until they can become a force of nature.

subclassFeature.name: Deduction Start!
entries: Someone of your standing must always be ready for action when it comes knocking at your door, as it often does for anyone who wishes to bring change about. As such, you are always prepared - After rolling Initiative but before the first creature in the Initiative Order you may take the Ready action.

Upon reaching 12th level in Artificer, your preparations have come to another level, allowing for a quick witted movement before any others. Once per Long Rest, you may choose to have one extra turn at Initiative count 20, once per combat. During this turn you are only preparing the battlefield, being unable to take the Attack action or the Cast a Spell action if it is targeting a hostile creature or area containing hostile creatures.

subclassFeature.name: Defibrillator Tactics

entries: "It would seem there is a bit of questionable irregularity in the test results. That's fine. Failure is expected of ordinary minds; making the effort to overcome it is what defines the ideal researcher."

Simply managing the ebb and flow of an electrical current is not enough for you, as you've interspliced the knowledge you have on the arcane, of lightning and of life itself to form a means of keeping your body in perpetual motion and give others the jolt they need to keep moving as well. Whenever your would be knocked {@condition Unconscious}, you may spend your Reaction to enter an emergency mode of sorts, transforming all your {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count into {@condition Self-Charge|TheUndertomesAED} instead.

{@condition Self-Charge|TheUndertomesAED} is a Condition that represents a mixture of sheer willpower and overwhelming energy keeping you from bursting at the seams. While you have count of the Condition, you are Immune to being knocked {@condition Unconscious} through any means. It counts as {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for the purposes of fuelling your skills and decays at a rate of 3 count at the end of your turns and 1 whenever you would suffer damage.

Additionally you may cast the {@spell Revivify} spell without spending a spell slot or material components by spending 5 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. If you do so targetting a creature that already has been affected by this spell before their next long rest, you must roll a d20, requiring a result of 6 or greater for the spell not to fail. This DC increases by 6 each time the creature is revived before said next long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Despair Domain

entries: "I look down? Nah, it's gotta be the E.G.O gear... Or, maybe it's just the night getting me all sentimental. Yeah... you know how it is."

Not all clerics of the Despair Domain chose this calling. While there is a congregation of cultists that worship gods of trickery, disaster, and tragedy, some, if not most, of the ones chained by their domain are people that have lost it all and have had their mind and soul consumed by despair. If at every waking moment your only thoughts are related to a tragedy you suffered, you are a devotee of the Despair Domain.

Clerics and chosen ones of the Despair Domain have their lives filled with grief and a sense that their future will not be long. However, they are possibly some of the largest sources of hope in the universe, both for themselves and for others. As dark and thick as despair may be, there always remains a meager thought that it might one day be cleansed by the light of the coming day. The larger the tragedy befallen one of the Despair Domain, the grander their revival could be.

Essentially, clerics and chosen ones of the Despair Domain are constantly switching from sinking down and being mired in thoughts of defeat to standing proud and rising to conquer their demons with a radiant glow of hope flowing from them.

entries.name: Despair Domain Spells

entries: "E.G.O Corrosion rate... acceptable... Probably."
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Despair Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell arms of Hadar|PHB|Arms of Hadar}, {@spell sanctuary|PHB|Sanctuary}
3rd
{@spell spiritual weapon|PHB|Spiritual Weapon}, {@spell warding bond|PHB|Warding Bond}
5th
{@spell beacon of hope|PHB|Beacon of Hope}, {@spell conjure barrage|PHB|Conjure Barrage}
7th
{@spell death ward|PHB|Death Ward}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
9th
{@spell conjure volley|PHB|Conjure Volley}, {@spell hallow|PHB|Hallow}

entries.name: The Sword Sharpened with Tears

entries: "All I had left was a hollow, weathered pride..."

Uncertain of your place in the world, whether a warrior of hope or a knight of despair, you still try to radiate what you believe in to your allies. You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor, and you always have a Blessing/Despair counter, which can have a maximum value equal to your proficiency bonus and a minimum equal to the negative value of your proficiency bonus. If your Blessing/Despair counter does not change for 1 minute, it shifts 1 point toward 0: a positive value decreases by 1, and a negative value increases by 1.

While the value of your Blessing/Despair counter is greater than 0, you are in Blessing Mode. Any creature that attacks you while you are in this mode gains 1 count of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per attack. Additionally, when a creature within 15 feet of you other than yourself is targeted by an attack, you can use your reaction to give that creature a bonus to its AC equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. This bonus lasts until the end of the round.

While the value of your Blessing/Despair counter is lower than 0, you are in Despair Mode. Any creature you hit with a weapon or a spell gains 3 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you miss an attack roll against a creature with {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, you can use your reaction to roll again.
As a bonus action, you can perform a Hollow Wail to raise or lower your Blessing/Despair counter by 2. It also changes under the following circumstances:

entries.caption: Blessing/Despair Counter
rows: When you heal another creature.
When a friendly creature becomes {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}.
When you deal a critical hit.
When you suffer a critical hit.
When you succeed on a saving throw.
When you fail a saving throw.
When a creature fails a saving throw you forced it to make.
When a creature succeeds on a saving throw you forced it to make.

entries: Your Blessing/Despair counter resets to 0 when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: The Knight's Sanctuary

entries: "The Knight of Despair still dwells in her past glories, just like her sisters."

As you cry on the battlefield, your teardrops transform into stars that float around you, forming constellations of weapons that remind you there is still a battle to be fought. At the start of your turn in combat, or once per turn by using a bonus action, if you are in Blessing Mode, you gain 1 count of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesDD}. When a creature within 30 feet of you is attacked, you can use your reaction to spend all your counts of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesDD}, reducing the damage by {@dice 1d8} for each count spent. If you spend 6 counts of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesDD} this way, the damage is reduced to 0.

entries.name: Faded Faith.
entries: At the start of your turn in combat, or once per turn by using a bonus action, if you are in Despair Mode, you gain 1 count of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesDD}. When a creature within 30 feet of you deals damage to another creature, you can use your reaction to spend all your counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesDD}, adding {@damage 1d6} cold damage to its damage roll for each count spent. If you spend 6 counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesDD} this way, the damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclassFeature.name: Detective Extraordinaire Artificer Specialty
entries: A Detective Extraordinaire isn't exactly an inventor at heart but one who uses of technology and ingenious aplication to further their goals, looking either to push themselves or a cause, usually in advantage of the very people, for wits are the one thing that cannot be bought by money.

Equipped with tremendous intelligence, they travel the worlds solving both cases and societal problems with equally dashing as revolting solutions, stopping at nothing to become their own Master Detective.

They may be found as Harpers disguised as Private Detectives around the shallow streets of Waterdeep, in Fâerun, or might even spread out as info collectors and brokers amongst many other operations around the realms.

subclassFeature.name: Dimension Shredder Roguish Archetype

entries.name: Distance and closeness can be deciding factors in many fights.
entries: Most combatants have to choose between fighting close to their enemies or from far away, and then specialize in that specific style. Dimension Shredders have no need for that, proficient in striking from any distance, they utilize their abilities to carve small gashes in space to give themselves an unmatched advantage in the battlefield.

In the Forgotten Realms, Dimension Shredders usually belong to a clan of Rogues called the "Bleeding Eye", comprised of people that were touched by Aberrations powerful enough to warp reality and survived, able to utilize a drop of their power still within them to alter space in the Material Plane to their advantage. In Eberron, usually those who spent too much time around dimensional seals, especially those that install them, may acquire the ability to warp through space a few feet in distance. In Ravenloft, some who get lost in the Mist are changed irreversibly, becoming lunatic wanderers similar to monsters themselves, carving their way through Domains of Dread in a desperate attempt to escape.
What was the event that rendered you capable of manipulating and warping space? How proficient are you with your new aberrant energy? Do you perhaps seek the creature that did this to you?

Are there any deformities or changes to your body because of this alien ability? Consider how space-warping shapes not only the path ahead, but yourself and the things and people around you, as well as the road you plan to tread on.

subclassFeature.name: Disgrace Finds a Way
entries: There has always been something clinging to you-a curse, an illness, a nightmare you can't wake from. Whatever it is, you've never overcome it, but you've learned to endure. That pain is now your fuel. Choose one of the following marks of disgrace. You gain both its benefits and drawbacks:

items: The Diseased. An illness has assailed you since you can remember, one of which you couldn't ever get rid off, no matter which potion or magic you tried. In your weak health you suffer disadvantage on Constitution Saving Throws, yet your vast knowledge on {@skill Medicine} nets you proficiency in the skill. You also gain the ability to cure a creature you touch of the {@condition Poisoned} condition once per rest, using part of your collection of cures to do so.

The Disarmed. You have somehow had one of your arms completely detached from your body, lost or destroyed, and no matter which prosthetics you might have attempted they never feel quite right. You can only wield or use items that require one hand. You cannot use weapons or objects that require two hands, with one exception: paired magical items (e.g., magical gauntlets) still function when worn on just one arm.

entries: This peculiarity has also made your remaining arm one that packs quite a punch. Once per short rest you may perform a Noble Slash, granting you advantage on your next melee weapon attack. You also deal additional damage equal to half your Proficiency Bonus ( Rounded Down ) on your melee weapons attacks. This bonus damage type matches your weapon's.

items: The Disturbed. Horrible nightmares assail you relentlessly, and the years dealing with those have caused you to develop your own ways of coping with either a fearlessness being developed or your constant fright making you much less shocked when you see the horrible, you were expecting, after all.

entries: This constant haunting has caused you to never be able to properly rest, when you take a Short Rest you may only recover up to half your Hit Die, and when you take a Long Rest you may only recover up to half your Maximum Hit Points. Both of these are rounded down. However, this state of alertness is one that never quite leaves you: You gain Expertise in the {@skill Perception} skill, you are immune to the {@condition Frightened} and {@condition Charmed} conditions.

subclassFeature.name: Disgust of the Faithful

entries: "That filth... I'll purge it off you!"

There are horrific things in this world that you just can't brush aside, beings whose sheer existence fills your mouth with the bitter taste of sin. They must be purged. When you first gain this subclass, choose one of the following creature types aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead to become the Target of your Ire. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid as Targets.
You inflict 2 additional {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count against Targets of your Ire and you may make an additional attack as part of the Attack Action against them during your turns.
You may change the creature type only when going through substantial character development or at levels where you would gain Ability Score Improvements, with you DM's permission.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike

entries: "There are times in life when one may shed tears over the littlest things."

You gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

entries: "I fear letting even the lightest wisp of frivolity upon this lament... Thus, it's only right that I wreath solemnness upon my heart as I pull their triggers."

The domain which presides upon the transient state of life unto death concerns itself on the matters regarding both the living and the departed equally, seeing to guide any lingering spirits to the great beyond and make sure any funeral procession goes accomplished without issue.

{@i withered and feeding on the poor dew that respiration makes.}
{@i I fade with my palm over the mouthpiece the butterfly}
{@i too shall spring away.}
