subclassFeature.name: Don't Let Something Like This Break You!

entries: "I don't need some stupid crutch like that "Core Burst (心)" crap. I just gotta pull as much power as I can from these tattoos and grit my teeth, and I'll overpower your fancy little tricks no problem."

You live in a dangerous world, so your solution was to become the most dangerous thing within it and not just survive, but rule it. Whenever you use your {@classFeature Second Wind|Fighter|PHB|1} ability when you have half of your hit points or less, for 1 minute you gain Resistance to all damage types except Psychic or Force, and the first time you hit an attack every turn, you heal hit points equal to {@dice 1d10} + your constitution modifier.
When you use this ability, you can only use it again after a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Downcast Gaze

entries: "I have to... try my best to uphold the perfect manners and etiquette."

Those above you are the only ones allowed to look up to the sky, you've taken that to mean that you also must keep sure of the presence of all that dwell on the ground beside you, granting you Proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill. Additionally, that exceptional precision has made it so that whenever you trigger a {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1} you can also trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Duel Livestream
entries: You know speed is key for winning a duel, and you have practiced your entire life to be the fastest there is. You have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, when you defeat a creature that had been the target of your {@condition Focused Attack|TheUndertomesMS}, you gain advantage on the first ability check, saving throw, and attack roll you make before the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Dèfensive
entries: A musketeer of smiles must always stand guard and be prepared to show all spectators that there is nothing to fear while they're on the battlefield. Starting on level 15, you may use a bonus action instead of an action to take the Dodge action. While Dodging, when a creature misses an attack against you, you can spend your reaction to make an attack roll against it using your Allez ability as a reaction, gaining an additional two stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and applying two additional stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} if you hit. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

If you choose to Dodge while within combat and no hostile creature attacks you for an entire round, you and all allies within 30 feet of you will gain 4 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and, until the end of their next turn. Their next attack that hits will inflict 4 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, as they're emboldened by the clear fear in the enemy's eyes.

subclassFeature.name: Efflorescence of Will

entries: "Preordained! Absolute."

Your own will has been attuned to match a near perfect synchrony with the Will, and that glorious revelation has been set in stone in a way that an overwhelming feeling of pride and relief washes over you whenever you conclude a Prescript. As such, you gain the following:

items: Once per short rest you may choose which Prescription you or another creature gains at the start of their turn instead of rolling on the Magicked Prescripts Table. (Or other suitable Table.)
Whenever you conclude a Prescript you may choose to end one negative Condition that is afflicting you.
Whenever you conclude a Prescript you gain one count of Fulfilled Onus. This counter can be spent to use the following abilities as an Action:

items.name: The Proxy of the Will.
items.entry: You spend one Fulfilled Onus to have your heart beat in tune with the Will, giving up your body momentarily as a conduit of it. You instantly move up to 15-ft. toward any other creature and perform a melee weapon attack against them. On a hit you gain 4 Poise and the target suffers from Mark of the e Prescript until the end of combat or until they are killed.

items.name: Engrave.
items.entry: You spend one Fulfilled Onus to unleash the Will's mark upon the world. You perform two melee weapon attacks against a target within reach. These attacks inflict 4 Sinking count on a hit, or deal half the damage they would on a miss.

items.name: Annihilate.
items.entry: You dutifully follow your orders. You spend three Fulfilled Onus and perform up to five melee weapon attacks against a target within reach. If a creature dies to Annihilate, you may instantly move up to 15-ft. toward another creature and perform any remaining attacks plus one against them, repeating the process up to 3 times. Whenever a creature is killed in this way, you gain one Grace of the Prescript.

subclassFeature.name: Efflorescing Magnificence

entries: "The bud has risen. Effort has borne fruit."
Your presence as a person is tantamount to magic, enchanting and bedazzling those in your surroundings in various ways. When you first reach 6th level in this Class, choose from one of the following:

items: {@b Flourishing.} Your fragrance is bountiful and invigorating, nourishing others to be at their best behaviour. At the start of your turns, you may spend a count of Lingering Blossoms to grant yourself and friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you {@dice 2d8} Temporary Hit Points. While these Temporary Hit Points remain, the affected creatures gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws.

{@b Liberating.} Your fragrance is that of a free spirit, easing the notion of being unbound and free to go wherever. You and all friendly creatures who start their turn within 45-ft. of you gain an extra 5-ft. of movement speed. Additionally, whenever you use your Bonus Action to grant a creature a bonus modifier to roll as per your Beauty of the Little Things feature, your bonus is instead {@dice 1d6} and you may choose to give another creature within the aura the same bonus by spending an additional Lingering Blossoms.

{@b Withering.} Your fragrance is that of rot, an agent to make way for a fresher world. Creatures suffering from Sinking count suffer an amount of d6 necrotic damage at the end of their turns equal to half their Sinking count, for a maximum of {@damage 4d4}. Furthermore, they suffer the same negative modifier from the Condition to their Constitution and Strength modifiers.

entries: You may choose to change this feature upon great moments of character development as this should be determined by your current outlook on life and yourself, which directly correlates to how their presence and power manifests. You and your DM must agree with the choice.

subclassFeature.name: Embodied Cumulus
entries: There have been happenings during your lifetime that you've deemed worthy to tell through a simple glance at your body. Starting at 3rd level you gain proficiency in Tattoo Kits. Additionally you may, when you gain this subclass, tattoo your body with one of the choices below. You may only have one tattoo at a time and may change them when you level up.

rows: Crimson Clouds

You etch onto your body a dark red pattern that resembles bloody strife. You gain a {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier when you attempt to Intimidate another creature, additionally, you may once per day give advantage to other friendly creatures performing {@skill Stealth} checks, drawing the attention to yourself by passing an {@skill Intimidation} check contested against your target's {@skill Insight}.
Inked Clouds

You etch black clouds onto your body, your way of life permeating even your appearance, signifying your devotion not only to your bladework but also how you attempt to convey yourself. You may use your Strength or Dexterity modifiers instead of Charisma on {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Deception} and {@skill Performance}.
Pale Clouds

You etch a visage of kind memories and good times on your body, so they never may be forgotten. You gain a {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier when you attempt Charisma checks on a hostile creature to attempt to pacify them. Additionally, others that would find you grotesque or threatening tend to be more patient with giving you a chance, giving you advantage on your first Charisma skill check against someone that you've met for the first time.
Colorful Clouds

Your body has celebrations of many events etched onto it, giving you advantage on {@skill Performance} checks and an additional {@dice 1d4} bonus in doing so. Once per long rest, you may tell the tale of your tattoos for up to double your proficiency bonus' worth of creatures around you that can hear you. These creatures may use an {@dice 1d6} bonus once in any of their rolls until their next short rest. You can only use this feature once per long rest.
Black Clouds

Dark clouds are a tapestry that covers most of your body, their meaning nebulous to anyone but yourself and a select few. You gain a {@dice 1d4} bonus to {@skill Stealth} rolls when you are Lightly Obscured, as you easily blend with the shadows. If you are Heavily Obscured you also gain advantage.
entries.caption: Embodied Cumulus

subclassFeature.name: Embrace Emotional Flow
entries: During the day, your emotions shifting have become a force to be reckoned with by themselves. When you reach 15th level, when your Look changes, you may spend your reaction to let the energy of the shifting emotions out, with the following effects:

rows: Sorrow

{@b Tearful Wails.} You let out all the pent up sadness in your soul with a single scream. All hostile creatures around a 15-feet radius around you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or have disadvantage on attacks against you until the end of your turn, as they are staggered from the sudden outburst.
Elation

{@b Inspiring Confidence.} Your sudden jollyness is infectious. Choose one friendly creature within 30-ft of yourself you'd like to inspire. That creature gains the effects of the {@spell bless|PHB|Bless} spell, they hold Concentration for its normal duration yet this concentration doesn't count against other concentrated spells.
Wrath

{@b Biting Anger.} The rage inside you bursts out in a powerful blow, you perform an attack with advantage against a creature within reach. On a hit, it has the benefits of a 2nd-level Divine Smite, without spending any spell slots.
Apathy

{@b Snap of Stability.} For a moment, you reclaim your calm in a moment of no bursting feelings, the focus giving you an opening to quickly cast one of the spells gained from your Oath Spells table at 3rd level without spending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Emergency Batteries
entries: You've fought many battles, enough to know that retreat to clean another day is a valid tactic. As such, you've acquired a device to safely extract yourself and your teammates out of a horrid situation, at the cost of heavy battery consumption. At 18th level, as an action, you may spend 10 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to activate your escape device, opening up a 10-foot by 10-foot portal on an empty space behind yourself, it is connected to another one in any unoccupied, presumedly safe space within a 1-mile radius. Only creatures you've allowed may pass through the portal by spending a bonus action to jump inside, coming off the other side at the closest unoccupied space. This portal lasts for one minute, or until you close it. It cannot be dispelled with the {@spell Dispel Magic} spell, but may be destroyed by the {@spell Disintegrate} spell.

You may also choose to forgo spending {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for this, but instead you take two points of Exhaustion per 3 missing {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to a minimum of one, as even your body's energy is consumed to fuel the jump. Additionally, any other creature who goes through the portal also suffers the Exhaustion points.

subclassFeature.name: Emergency Measures
entries: Sometimes a quick decision is needed to keep on burning, and you've made sure that your Firefist Engine is adaptable for that. As a bonus action during your turn you may choose to have your Engine tap onto a magic item you're attuned to's magic power to convert it into fuel. The item becomes inert and loses its magical properties until the next short rest and you regain Igniter Fuel based on its rarity:

entries.caption: Emergency Measures
rows: Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary

subclassFeature.name: Endless Elation Arcane Tradition
entries: {@i A Wizard Subclass by the Undertomes}

Those who study the Endless Elation Arcane Tradition are often hedonists who seek joy in its purest form, how it’s born and how it’s best injected. Alchemical study and plentiful of psychodelic ground reasearch has allowed them to reach one of the answers for true, unending and unbearable elation to be spread to all.

Wizards of this Tradition can usually be seen alongside bardic troupes or even in more cloistered groups which all seek the answers to their research in unison, fully dedicated to happiness at all costs.

subclassFeature.name: Enduring Lacrima
entries: Your tears are for the protection of the meek, and they will not be easily wiped. You may use a reaction when a creatures loses all their counts of {@condition Blubberbubble|TheUndertomesASV} to make it burst. All creatures of their choice within 15 feet of them must roll a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take {@dice 3d8} cold damage and 6 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If a creature is killed as a result of this, you may grant 2 counts of {@condition Blubberbubble|TheUndertomesASV} and {@dice 2d8} temporary Hit Points to a creature within 30 feet of you. On a success, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expendef uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Enlightened Saint
entries: You've achieved a higher state of being through your mastery of your very own emotions. Starting at 20th level, your turbulence has died down, letting your mind become unshackled for true serenity. You can now change your current Look with a bonus action and you now have two Looks' effects actives at the same time, as your mind can easily adapt to a place between the both of them. When you would use Coagulate Feelings, you may choose two of its effects to enact during a single action. Evolving also as a spiritual guide, you can better aid creatures through their own emotions, granting you Expertise in the {@skill Persuasion} skill and allowing you to choose which of your Auras of Turbulence are active on each creature that is affected, such as choosing for one to benefit from the Sorrow Aura while another benefits from Elation. Your Aura is no longer locked to follow your Look of the day, yet other creatures may still only benefit from one of them. You may only change your Look every other turn.

entries.name: Designer's Note on Today's Look!
entries: It is suggested for the sake of truly embracing turbulence to allow yourself to be taken by the whims of the dice when you can, instead of always choosing which emotion is more convenient at any given time. The option to choose instead of trusting the dice is mainly given with the intention of better allowing a character to not become dissonant mechanically from how they are in roleplay, and should be used with that in mind.

subclassFeature.name: Entangled Phenomena Restoration
entries: You have traversed enough elemental planes to know how fearsome they can be to those unaccustomed to them. Starting on 13th level, you may cast the {@spell Banishment} spell on 5th level once per long rest without expending material components. Additionally, you may choose to which elemental plane you send the creature or creatures to. For the duration of the spell, on the end of their turn, they must make a Constitution saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier) or take {@dice 1d6} damage of the appropriate elemental type on a failure.

subclassFeature.name: Erlking
entries: Upon reaching 20th level, you manifest your desire for oblivion in a single instant of pure, unadulterated destruction. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: As a part of your attack action on your turn, you can force the creature you attacked to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, gaining vulnerability to psychic damage until your next turn on a failure.
Your mount has its speed doubled. While mounted, you have advantage to attack creatures, and creatures have disadvantage to attack you.
Whenever a creature dies within 30 feet of you, you may spend a reaction to make an additional attack against a target creature within your range.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Everyday Exhaustion
entries: Due to the constant pressure in your mind, you've grown used to pushing through it in specific moments of need. Starting at 3rd level, while you are suffering the effects of Exhaustion, you don't suffer Disadvantage on Skill Checks you are proficient with. Additionally, you may choose to gain Expertise instead of Proficiency with those Skills before you roll, concentrating on them alone and taking advantage of the fact that your attention to the world at large is already diluted.
You may grant yourself Expertise as per this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining spent uses on a short or long rest.

Additionally, your experience has given you a better way to deal with this state of mind when given the opportunity. You remove one additional point of Exhaustion from yourself during a Long Rest. Once per short rest, you may choose to take a breath as an action. When you do so, you perform a Constitution Saving Throw whose DC is 10 + Half your Level, rounded up. On a success, you take deep, restorative breaths that alleviate you of 2 Exhaustion points. On a failure, you only manage to catch your breath briefly, removing only one point of Exhaustion as your body remains strained.

entries.name: Designer's Note to DMs.
entries: If the movement speed reduction from Extreme Fatigue is proving cumbersome to the party as a whole, consider ruling it so this reduction only affects movement in combat, flavouring it as the character being able to focus more on their movement outside of it.

subclassFeature.name: Exceptional Voltage Distribution Discipline

entries: "Hm... Very well. I'll forward this report directly to the higher-ups. The figures look promising. Ah, you there, are you well-rested now? Then deliver this report for me... and take this, too. It's a report on your experiment."

The thesis born from your body of work has become a new backbone in the Arcane Electrical Discharge Discipline, and you have learnt how to control said discharges especially well - managing to cut costs of extreme exertion with predictable results and gaining a keen sense for what can result from your experimentation.
You gain an additional Reaction during your turn that you may use exclusively to perform Alternating Discharge Support.

entries.name: Alternating Discharge Support
entries: Whenever a creature that you can see within 60-ft. of you would spend Sorcery Points, Ki Points or a generic countable Condition such as {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you may spend your Reaction to boost their energy projection, causing the cost of the spenditure to be halved. You may do this an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Additionally, the value to re-roll skill checks as per your Undying Persistence feature becomes 2, while you can now still spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to re-roll your own attack rolls and saving throws as per the same stipulations.
Finally, if you didn't already have it, you gain Expertise in the Arcana skill due to a perfected understanding in the flow of arcane energy.

To make use of Expanded Ammunition, you must spend a Spell Slot and use your action. A detailed description of each Expanded Ammunition type is presented at the end of this document.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be a conjuration or a necromancy spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spells List

entries: "Thus I felled the rogue rebel as His Majesty has commanded-then, Hongyuan, march on... without fear."

Your mutations and application of theory into practice grants you access to certain spells. At 2nd level, you learn the {@spell blade ward} cantrip. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of the Stormrider Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

subclassFeature.name: Exploit the Strong
entries: Your investigative genius is unmatched and has been allowed to grow into a menace that won't be easily dealt with. You know just the right strategy to have your comrades bring those who oppress you to their knees, as such you may spend a Bonus Action during your turn to designate a target hostile creature that you can see within 120-ft of you as a {@condition Culprit!|TheUndertomesDX}.

While being a {@condition Culprit!|TheUndertomesDX}, a creature suffers an additional 2 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever it is hit and suffers a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20, before any modifiers. The Condition ends after one minute, after the {@condition Culprit!|TheUndertomesDX} suffers a Critical Hit or after the {@condition Culprit!|TheUndertomesDX} is knocked {@condition Unconscious}. When a {@condition Culprit!|TheUndertomesDX} suffers a Critical Hit, they also suffer from {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
You may assign a creature as a {@condition Culprit!|TheUndertomesDX} up to three times per Long Rest, but may only do so once per creature.
Furthermore, your deductive capability to profile someone has truly flourished, as such while outside of combat you may spend a minute to analyze a creature or 120-ft location for your advantage:

items: {@i If you analyze a creature.} You must pass an {@skill Investigation} Check against a DC that is equal to the targets CR ( Maximum of 14 ) + Their {@skill Insight} Modifier. On a success, you may choose to deduce their Maximum Hit Points, Damage Vulnerabilities, Damage Resistances and Immunities or what Magic Items they are currently attuned to. On a failure, you cannot attempt to analyze them until the next day.

{@i If you analyze a location.} You gain a +1 bonus to hit and to damage while within this area, also adding a bonus modifier equal to half your Intelligence Modifier, rounded down, to any Dexterity Saving Throws and {@skill Perception} checks while inside the area, as you know exactly how and where everything is.

subclassFeature.name: Express Area of Impact Delivery
entries: You've only now realized how volatile a shaken up can of WellCheers can be. As such, you may expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and your action to shake up and toss a can on any space within 60-feet of you. When reaching a surface, it explodes, the soda engulfing a 15-foot radius of that point, with its effect depending on its flavour, which you select when you use this action.

Minty Breeze. An upgrade on the Cherry flavour, it refreshes anything and everything! All creatures within radius are healed by {@damage 3d8} hit points and gain a +1 to Saving Throws until the end of your next turn.
Oceanic Rage. What do you do when someone is a mean Shrimp? Exactly, you blow them up to high heaven.

All creatures within the Delivery's radius must pass a Dexterity Saving throw or take {@damage 4d8} acid damage, or half on a success. Marshmellow Cushions. All creatures around the radius must make a Constitution Saving throw, creatures who fail this saving throw suffer as if the {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} spell was cast at 2nd level on them, falling asleep if the treshold beats their current hit points, or becoming {@condition Drowsy|TheUndertomesASF} if it is higher than half their current hit points.
Despite the flavour used, the area covered by the Delivery is covered in sticky soda, being considered hard terrain.

subclassFeature.name: Extreme Fatigue
entries: You've lived a life filled with death, and it takes its toll on you, weighing down your shoulders akin to a forlorn spirit clinging to its last sparks of life. Nevertheless, you keep onward, wading through the exhaustion. Upon reaching 3rd level, the way Exhaustion affects you is different from most others, as you are used to its weight and know how to wield it to your advantage. The following table details the effects of Exhaustion on you:

rows: You're assaulted by a general drowsiness, causing you to retreat slightly into your own thoughts. You suffer disadvantage on ability checks.

Your body feels heavy and sluggish, but you know how to throw that weight around. Your speed is reduced by 15-ft. As a bonus action during your turns, you may quickly sidestep, moving in any direction for up to 15 ft. When you do so, Opportunity Attacks against you are made with disadvantage.

Your mind's protection starts to lull into haziness; however, your instincts are honed to protect you. You suffer disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma Saving Throws, but gain advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution ones.
You feel that adrenaline is the only thing keeping your heart beating so fast in its weakening state. Your Hit Point maximum is halved, but you gain a +2 bonus to your AC and Saving Throws.

The flesh cage that binds you has become unmovable. Your speed is reduced to 5 ft., yet you gain advantage on attack rolls, as all your remaining energy is diverted into protecting yourself from any who come near.

Flickers of your spirit and will to survive through hardship are all that keep you alive. At the start of your turn in Initiative, you must pass a Constitution Saving Throw without advantage or fall {@condition Unconscious} with two failed Death Saving Throws. The DC for this Saving Throw is 13 and increases by 2 at the start of your subsequent turns. You cannot die during this state.
entries.caption: Extreme Fatigue

entries: Additionally, when you start your first turn in combat, you may choose to allow some of your past works to wash over your thoughts, bearing their weight for your own success. When you do so, you can choose to either lose 25% of your maximum hit points, rounded down (From now on, this value will be referred to as a "Chunk" of your hit points), or suffer up to half your proficiency modifier in Exhaustion points.

subclassFeature.name: Fa Jin

entries: "The virescent pyrojade burneth."

Once per turn after you hit a creature with an attack, you can either inflict 1 point of {@condition Nerve Strike|TheUndertomesBJ} on the target or gain 2 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At 11th level, you can use this ability twice per turn.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Facsimile of Perfected Life

entries: "At long last, Faust has completed the masterpiece that even the Maestro will have no choice but to approve."

The stride toward becoming an artist - the brutal steps taken in reflecting your artwork itself - it has all culminated into who you are now. What you are now. You have transcended the repressed flesh and became a living embodiment of your love of nature and of humanity itself, represented in each threaded tendon and re-shaped muscle. You gain the following:

items: While in your Iron Maiden Form, your base AC is now 13 + your Constitution modifier + your Wisdom modifier and you are considered resistant to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing attacks.
While in your Flowing Form you gain an additional 5-ft. of movement and deal an additional 2 damage on a hit against Bleeding creatures.
You have Expertise in any skill checks revolving around Artisan's Tools you are proficient in. You also gain Expertise in the {@skill Performance} skill for producing and enacting your art.
You may spend a Bonus Action to successfully discern the intent behind any creation of another creature, such as a forged weapon or artwork.

entries: Additionally, you may now spend your Bonus Action while within 5-ft. of a non-summoned corpse that has been dead for less than a day to do the following artworks:

entries.name: Minimalist Manifesto.
entries: A small prompt to keep yourself sharp with the removal of corpus. When creating this sculpture you instantly gain your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO}.

entries.name: Cascading Columnal Crevice.
entries: A bundle of nerves and bones ready to explode out at the most minimal movement. Whenever a creature moves into or out of 5-ft. of this sculpture you may spend your Reaction to whistle in the right frequency to set it off. It lashes out in an explosion of vine-like blood vessels and spike-ish bone, forcing all creatures within a 15-ft. radius to pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Druid Spell Save DC or suffer {@damage 5d10} slashing damage and 4 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

entries.name: Horrifyingly Beautiful Creation.
entries: You produce your standard artwork. Hostile creatures and creatures not familiar with your work must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Druid Spell Save DC when first seeing it or suffer {@damage 3d8} psychic damage and become Frightened of you and your sculpture for one minute, being able to re-attempt this saving throw at the end of their subsequent turns. Whenever they do so, they instantly suffer an additional {@damage 2d8} psychic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Fallstar Slayer [落星一殺]

entries: "Should I return bearing the heads of these fallen foes... Then perhaps, this time, my master might speak of the name Dihui Star... and how I am growing to deserve it."

The end of your quest is within reach, especially now that you have learned the technique necessary to render universes hostage within your hold. As an Action, you may spend 5 Ki points to create a 10-foot line rift to the Astral Plane in any area within 15 feet of you.

Any creature within 10 feet of the gate must perform a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier). On a failure, they are sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane.
On a success, they take {@damage 10d10} slashing damage but manage to escape the rift's hold. The rift then closes. The rift is one-way only and can't be reopened.

subclassFeature.name: Fangripper Ranger Archetype
entries: "{@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} are not only vile, they're also very persistent. So~ we should make sure we have everything ready to take them on, right?" It is true that one trait shared between many rangers is their specialization towards a specific type of quarry, but this truth is the boldest and most dogmatic when it comes to the Fangrippers, who dedicate their lives to destroying the scourge that are bloodsuckers.

Wielding impressive arsenals of their own design, the Fangrippers prowl about in search of all the uglies that go bump in the night, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|bloodfiends}, vampires or any other type of shapechanger, all with the objective of ending them.

Wherever they may be found, they are usually seen in groups, armed to the teeth and knocking on doors with the friendliest demeanor for the living, saving all their pent up hatred for those that have abandoned life itself.

entries.name: Additional Favored Enemy
entries: You've collected enough about the leeches of your world, as such you gain the benefits of Favored Enemy towards a new type of favored enemy: Shapechangers. These include Vampires, Changelings, Werewolves and other Werebeasts. In general, monstrous beings who keep their true nature hidden are considered Shapechangers, except for Fey. When in doubt, the DM holds final ruling about what is and isn't considered a Shapechanger.

entries.name: Cheerful Hunt's Focus
entries: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn it into a deliberate wound. The damage is halved, and you suffer twice the number of the attack's damage dice in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} counts.
While suffering from Bleed, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being {@condition Grappled||grappled}.
You have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist having a weapon removed from your grip.
You have advantage on Wisdom saving throws made to resist being {@condition Frightened||frightened} or {@condition Charmed||charmed}.
Whenever you deal damage, the target suffers {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} counts equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

entries: You can use this reaction once per short or long rest, twice beginning at 8th level, and three times beginning at 14th level.

entries.name: Arms of the Hunt
entries: At the end of the day, you can't deal with abominations with the common weaponry you see everyday, Instead you gather a variety of resources to employ in your crusade against the dark, gaining a pool of Preparation Die that you may spend during a Long Rest to prepare any of the following items:

entries.caption: Arms of the Hunt
rows: Antitoxin
Any Horror Trinket from Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft or similar useless bauble
Caltrops (20)
{@item Grappling Dart|TheUndertomesTO}
{@item Stake|TheUndertomesTO} (6)
{@item Bonecrusher Hammer|TheUndertomesTO}
Net
{@item Styptics Bag|TheUndertomesTO}
{@item Sanctified Canister|TheUndertomesTO}
{@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesTO}
{@item Vial of Silver Water|TheUndertomesTO}
{@item Aromatized Incense Burner|TheUndertomesTO}

entries: At the start of a long rest, if you had any unused item you break them down for scraps, as you've got to make the most of each piece you have. Additionally, these items are usually scrapped together or have already seen their fair share of use and have to be rebuilt, causing merchants to be wary of buying them.

subclassFeature.name: Farrier of the Mind

entries: "I ruminate and ruminate upon the fragments of the incident to learn of what I could have done that the young Miss might have lived."

Like any other steed that has their heart set on accompanying a master, you have learned a trade or two in pursuance of both increasing your usefulness and to remain of sound mind, taking care of yourself even out of battle. You gain proficiency in one {@skill skill} and one {@item Artisan's Tools|PHB|Artisan's Kit} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Fashionista's Supplies
entries: At third level, your ability with scissors isn't limited only to combat. You gain proficiency in Weaver's Tools or Expertise if you were already proficient with such. You also create Hardblood Accessories, small trinkets formed from blood and skill. You may do so once per turn by using your bonus action and spending three points of Bloodfeast, creating one of the following:

items: {@b Flourish of Bloodletting.} You deftly create a pendant you may attach to a weapon. When attached, it magically causes blood to coat its surface or ammunition and form jagged points that cause even more blood to pour out, the weapon gains the Hemorrhaging (18-20) property for one minute.

{@b Mistmaker Shoes.} You fabricate a pair of shoes that seem to stir with life. When equipped by a creature, it gains {@dice 2d4} temporary Hit Points. While those remain they also gain a 5-ft bonus to their movement speed.

{@b Roseate Shawl.} You weave a neck adornment with an intricate design that grants {@dice 4d8} temporary Hit Points to an equipped creature. While those remain this creature suffers a -1 penalty to their AC.

entries: When you create one of these items, you may grant them to an ally within 5-ft of you and have them equip the item instantly, additionally each ally may benefit only once per Accessory per combat, and if you attempt to give an ally two Accessories at the same time, the one created first becomes inert, providing no bonuses.

When a creature takes damage while they have Temporary Hit Points gained from this feature remaining, they are considered to have vulnerability against fire damage as it burns away the clothing, but any damage remaining after the clothing is destroyed is negated.

subclassFeature.name: Fatalism Domain
entries: Fatalism. "The belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable." Those who follow its domain believe as if the concept itself was God, a force of nature with no parallel or counterweight - And one that if they go against, it'd be as going against their own heartbeat.

These have become empty husks that embraced a prescribed fate to their name, old or new, and molded themselves accordingly. They are often imitations of someone that once was, is or will be and pursue barely any personal goal past what was ascribed to them. Despite that, there are still those that try to look for cracks in "Fate's" mask, to have little actions and pursuits that might change things ever so slightly, all to satisfy imprinting their own will into the world, like a wave trying to form in the sea.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms those who follow the Fatalism Domain are the highest members of those under the Living Will, acting as their indirect proxies and undercover agents that are used to shape other settlements in certain ways to go according to plan. In others such as Thespis, there was but one true believer of the Fatalist Domain - Their name lost to time and story far, far ago, and their remains being distorted tales that many a new cleric tried to imitate and reach, attempting to forge their own unbreakable fatalism.

subclassFeature.name: Favoritism

entries: "A Critique Salon! Exhilarating Prospect."

Your ability to interact with the body - the corpus of living creatures has evolved beautifully through criticism and hard work, rendering you a better artist than ever before. Whenever you would gain {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} in this Form, gain an additional count.
Upon reaching 10th level you may perform a second additional attack as part of your Attack Action while in Flowing Form.

Additionally, this improvement also expanded your horizons on how to work your materials, granting you the ability to spend 4 {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} when entering your Flowing Form to instantly re-roll your Initiative, taking the higher value for the rest of the combat. You may also spend 6 count when you must attempt a Dexterity saving throw to instead use your Wisdom modifier instead of Dexterity.

Furthermore, criticism and sudden bursts of shared inspiration have become a true driving force for you. Whenever you would benefit from a Bardic Inspiration, Flash of Genius or a similar beneficial class ability, you may add an additional bonus modifier equal to half your Wisdom modifier to the affected roll.

subclassFeature.name: Favoritism
entries: You are finally starting to ascend in the family, growing from a common runt to a person of some respect. Once you reach level 10, your Unarmed Strike damage dice changes to {@dice 1d10}. Additionally, whenever a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} is killed, the creature that last attacked you or an ally this combat gains a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}.

Whenever an allied creature within 30 feet of you is hit by a hostile creature, the allied creature with least HP gains a +1 bonus to their ability checks, attack rolls and saving throws until the end of their next turn, to a maximum of +3.

subclassFeature.name: Featherstride Technique

entries: "'Tis an emergency, hm? Do know that it shall cost thee a tad more!"

Your training through serious and casual environments has helped you hone a diverse arsenal of skills that aid you in surviving both official tournaments and tavern brawls. You gain the following abilities:

items: If you are within 5 feet of a stationary object at least 10 feet tall, such as a lamp post or tree trunk, you can use a bonus action to swing around it and launch yourself in a 30-foot line. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, it is pushed to the end of the line and takes a number of Martial Arts dice in damage equal to one for every 10 feet traveled, with a minimum of one die. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and is not moved.

If you are holding a weapon or object, you can use an action to slam it into a creature within your reach. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, it suffers 3 stacks of {@condition Nerve Strike|TheUndertomesBJ} and takes damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect. The damage increases to four rolls at 11th level and five rolls at 17th level.

When a creature attacks you while you are adjacent to a wall or vertical surface at least 5 feet tall, you can use your reaction to evade by running along the wall. You gain a bonus to your AC against that attack equal to 1 for every 10 feet of the wall's height, to a maximum of +3. If the attack misses and the attacker is within your melee reach, you can make one melee weapon attack against it as part of the same reaction. You then land in an unoccupied space behind the target, if one is available.

When you successfully deflect a ranged attack using Deflect Missiles, you burn the missile before throwing it back as part of the same reaction. If it hits, it inflicts 2 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: You can use these abilities a total number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can spend 2 ki points to activate one of them.

subclassFeature.name: Feign Folly, Face All, Reign Tall

entries: "here come moments wherein I find myself longing to be tagged unfrozen; alas, my darling daughter appears to have mislaid the memory to do so. Hah... how draining this is."

A husk is all that remains of you when it comes to obeying the Will, to resonate with it so profoundly that your entire being is made by it. That devotion, however, has not gone unheard, allowing you some reprieve at the hardest of times just to reach your ultimate goal.
You gain the following effects:

items: You have learnt how to fill the empty husk that you are with anything demanded by the greater Will, granting you the ability to use your Wisdom modifier instead of Charisma on any Skill Checks that would use the Attribute.

Every time you would be afflicted with a negative Condition or Effect such as the {@condition Frightened} Condition, roll a d100. On a roll of 75 or greater, you instead suffer nothing as fate seems to miraculously intervene.
Whenever a creature would damage you with a Critical Hit, they must confirm it by rolling a d20, with any result below 15 having the hit instead be a regular attack only.

You may guide others toward the Will's bidding with expertise, become Immune to being {@condition Frightened} and {@condition Charmed}. Additionally whenever you Charm a creature, they benefit from your current {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD} count as a bonus modifier to their attack and damage rolls while friendly to you.

The grace of your God reaches even those who indirectly contribute to it's whims, granting you a 15-ft. aura of where any friendly creature within reach benefits from the d4 effects of your Brandishes to Quell the Innermost Self feature.

subclassFeature.name: Fell Memoir Ranger Archetype

entries: "It promised to give me a gun that can blow up anything, but the catch was that its last shell would land on the head of my beloved."

Times of war have long since painted history in their glory and gore, tinting red the lives of various people. Yet there are those who are overtaken by a smoke-like feeling that clings to their skin like a plume of flame just near going off. Those are Fell Memoir Rangers.

Usually characterized by a worn-out exterior and carrying an equally well-used gun, they roam the lands in search of more and more targets to blow up, living for the perpetual feeling of being in a conflict - of reliving their own memories and destroying that of others they find in their wake. Now, rarely they may be still clinging to some sort of feeling, an unresolved lack in their own recollection that pushes them onward, yet in most cases they are a blaze waiting to grow large enough to overtake everything one may think of.

entries.subclassFeature: Memoir of a Fallen Stigma|Ranger|PHB|Fell Memoir|TheUndertomesFM|3

subclassFeature.name: Fente
entries: A musketeer of smiles must always keep their enemies on their toes, striking true and fast without letting them ever get too close. Starting on level 10 when you hit a creature with your Allez ability, you gain 4 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead of 2. Additionally, you gain a +1 bonus to your initiative rolls.

As part of a melee weapon attack, you can attempt to push a creature back with a well-placed jab. If the attack hits, the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier) or be pushed 10 feet away from you. On a failure, the creature will also gain 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, if its initiative count is lower than yours. It gains two more stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} if it has or had at least one stack of {@condition Focused Attack|TheUndertomesMS} during the last round. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ferrous Discipline

entries: "Not even the Thumb, one of the Five Fingers sitting at the apex of the Backstreets, can just waste bullets willy-nilly... Some just stick to raw strength, though"

Most of your subordinates still rely solely on their allotted rounds to finish their work, but you've become more self reliant despite the fact that you're allowed an even greater amount of ammo. Your bayonet fighting rips through the battlefield better than most bullets, and you have come a long way into being a threat to your underlings - for its hard for them to keep their eyes away. You gain the following:

items: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

Your nasty bladework has become an urban legend amongst your subordinates. You consider any melee weapon you are wielding to deal magical damage for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and they are also considered to be at least a +2 Weapon, if it was any lower than that.
Whenever you would make a melee weapon attack you may choose to instantly move up to 10-ft. in any direction of your choice without spending additional movement, provided you will reach a target.
You have an additional 4 Scorch Propellant Rounds.

In the case you are ever without a weapon, your fists have become quite the reliable tool, calloused enough to hit like pure iron and counting as natural melee weapons that you are proficient with. These have the Finesse and Light properties and deal {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a hit, and although they cannot benefit from your Round they deal an 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

subclassFeature.name: Festering Hearts

entries: Unbeknownst to all, Melting Love’s army grows day by day.

There are some hearts that you were born to keep, or rather that you have learnt how to keep. You may now also transfer an amount of Heart Robbed to a creature {@condition Charmed} by you up to your Charisma modifier when they are {@condition Charmed} by you.

Upon triggering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} against a creature {@condition Charmed} by you, the creature suffers from the effects of {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} an additional time for each count of Heart Robbed it currently has, halving the {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count they are suffering from each time a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is triggered instead of fully removing the condition, rounded up.

Furthermore, when a creature {@condition Charmed} by you dies, you may spend your reaction to draw out everything that was left in their heart, transforming their remains into a Valentine’s Ooze that is friendly to you and your allies. Medium or smaller creatures only create one such Ooze, with Large creatures creating two, Huge creatures creating four and Gargantuan creatures creating six.

These Oozes act in a single turn taken after yours, following your orders as they are best able to, putting themselves in direct danger if needed. They melt into a puddle when combat ends or they die, also granting you a count of Heart Robbed that does not vanish until your next long rest.

If you have created a Valentine’s Ooze in this way before, you may spend your action to summon one ontop of an unnocupied space within 30-ft. of you, materializing it from the lingering adoration of those who once loved you. When you do this, you may spend a number of Heart Robbed to strengthen it, granting it 20 temporary hit points per count spent and a +1 bonus modifier to its attack rolls and damage for each 2 count spent, to a maximum bonus of +4.

subclassFeature.name: Fire Tempered in Moonlight
entries: You gain resistance to psychic damage and proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Flame Rooster's Death Defiance [炎鳥不死戦]

entries: "Roosters crow only when the lord holding our leash commands us to."

Roosters never die, they're simply out of breath, ready to recover and burst back into the fight like a living inferno. If your hit points drop to 0 or you become {@condition Unconscious}, you can use a reaction to immediately deplete all of your counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or half the counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature within 15 feet of you and lose the {@condition Unconscious} condition, recover 1 hit point and gain {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points for each count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} depleted this way. After this, you can immediately start Raging and move up to your movement speed towards a creature to perform an attack roll. If you score a critical hit or reduce the creature to 0 hit points with this attack, you gain an additional {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points.
You can use this feature once, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest. Upon reaching level 14, you can use it twice.

subclassFeature.name: Flamespout Artificer Specialist
entries: "What'd I say, big sis? I said I'd return to burn it all down."

The life of an artificer isn't an easy one, much less the one of a person who has had their life burn down around them. Those who specialize in the Flamespout have grown to believe one theory above all the rest: That flame will be the only salvation for their soul, not for an afterlife or grander reward, much less greater good; All they wish for is their peace again.

A Flamespout artificer specializes in producing copious amounts of combustion to lay waste unto anything within their path, setting out in a burning crusade of their own making. They save no fuel until their job is done. Flamespout artificers are often misfits and people abandoned by their world no matter the setting, usually having lost all they ever had in one way or another, and with no way to revert that loss they turn into making sure that the price of their suffering is paid by all of those that have wrongfully crossed their path.

entries.name: Convictions in Flame
entries: Hope is akin to a candle's fire, despite its ephemerality it still grants safety amidst the dark. This is something that you've learnt well, and as such your obsession with flame has led you to better implement it in your weapons.

You gain proficiency with Gauntlets and during a long rest you may choose to perform maintenance on weapons you are proficient with to have them be able to deal fire damage instead of their initial damage type, provided they dealt Slashing, Piercing or Bludgeoning damage before. You choose which damage type to deal when you would deal it, as you coat your weapon in burning fuel or shove it off.

Additionally, this constant burning has you deal one stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} whenever you would cause fire damage with a weapon attack. This increases to two {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} when you reach 8th level and three upon reaching 16th level. You may only benefit from this up to an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per round, rounded down.

entries.name: Flamespout Spells
entries: You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the table below. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don't count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.caption: Flamespout Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell burning hands|PHB|Burning Hands}, {@spell hellish rebuke|PHB|Hellish Rebuke}
5th
{@spell aganazzar's scorcher|XGE|Aganazzar's Scorcher}, {@spell flaming sphere|PHB|Flaming Sphere}
9th
{@spell erupting earth|XGE|Erupting Earth}, {@spell fireball|PHB|Fireball}
13th
{@spell fire shield|PHB|Fire Shield}, {@spell wall of fire|PHB|Wall of Fire}
17th
{@spell dawn|XGE|Dawn}, {@spell flame strike|PHB|Flame Strike}

entries.name: Drink in Flame
entries: The beauty of darkness being lit is one that your heart finds confidence in, a source of fuel to move forward. As such, you gain a bonus modifier to Wisdom Saving Throws for each {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} creature within 20-ft of you, up to a maximum equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

If there are four or more creatures {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} within that range, you also gain half your proficiency modifier's value (rounded down) as a bonus to attack rolls.

entries.name: Workshop Bathed in Fuel
entries: Your Firefist Engine holds Igniter Fuel equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus. You can use that fuel for the following features:

entries.name: Pre-Heated Gasoline
entries: As a bonus action, spend Igniter Fuel to heat the engine. The next time this turn you deal fire damage, apply 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count per 4 Igniter Fuel spent. A creature that succeeds on a saving throw against the initial fire damage suffers half as many Burn counts, rounded down.

entries.name: Fuel Detonation
entries: As an action, spend 2 Igniter Fuel per {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count on a Burning creature and make a melee weapon attack against it. On a hit, the attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} fire damage per Burn count on the target.

entries.name: Burning Grounds
entries: As an action, spend Igniter Fuel in multiples of 4 to coat a radius of 5 feet per 4 fuel spent. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. The area is difficult terrain for other creatures. Whenever one creature in the area suffers Burn, every other creature in it suffers half as many Burn counts, rounded down. The zone lasts until a creature uses its action to extinguish a 10-foot radius or running water washes the fuel away.
You regain all Igniter Fuel when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Flesh Yielding Style
entries: Upon reaching 11th level, the scars you've gained are a testament to your fearlessness, and the wounds to fuel your outward aggression. When you suffer a critical hit or when you take damage that is equal to or greater than a third of your maximum hit points in one attack, rounded down, you may spend 3 Ki Points to perform the To Claim Their Bones action, as described in the following:

entries.name: To Claim Their Bones.
entries: There is no anguish you can't stand, and there is no pain you won't let out through your blade. By spending your reaction when you would be able to use To Claim Their Bones, you perform three devastating swipes of your blade, rolling to hit every creature within a 15-ft wide, 5-ft long rectangle of you, with each attack roll being treated as if attempting to hit each individual creature within the area. The damage dealt by this attack is equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts Die plus one additional Martial Arts Die per hit after the first attack of this reaction and its damage type is slashing. For each 4 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on you, the area of effect of To Claim Their Bone Their Bones increases by an additional 5-ft to the sides and an additional 5-ft in front of you, to a maximum of becoming a 25-ft wide, 15-ft long rectangle.

Additionally, as long as you have two Ki Points or more remaining, you may choose to keep on fighting even when your body would fail you. When you would be reduced below one hit point, you may choose to spend two Ki Points you may choose to remain at one hit point until the start of your next turn instead. At the end of combat, you gain one point of Exhaustion for each time you avoided falling below one hit point like this.

subclassFeature.name: Flourish of Panic
entries: Sometimes all you want to do is not just to kill a creature, but to maim them to your hearts content, drawing in attention from your barbarisms like a maestro conducting an orchestra. Upon reaching 13th level, you may perform the Flourish of Panic action instead of a Sneak Attack. The same restrictions of Sneak Attack apply and you may use this action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining expended uses on a long rest.

Flourish of Panic. Instead of delivering only one swift strike to destroy a foe, you instead draw the pain out by swiftly hitting them where it hurts the most, joints, the face, shallow cuts on the fingers - anywhere. When you do so, you perform an attack for each dice of your Sneak Attack, dealing your normal weapon damage plus {@dice 1d8} of the same damage type on a hit.

Every other hostile creature must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or have their next roll reduced by a negative modifier equal to the number of times you've hit your original targets. After rolling any dice except for damage dice, this negative modifier is reduced by one, until it becomes zero, as they are slowly recovering from the shock of such a scene. Creatures who are imune to being {@condition Frightened||frightened} have advantage on this Saving Throw.

subclassFeature.name: Fluttering Life Domain

entries: "Where do humans go upon the final egress from life? You ask a rather stimulating question. I have once written my reflections on the end of life; perhaps we may have a chance to discuss it later."

A buttefly soars freely through the world, needing not the wind to propel its sails nor a great will to guide its whims. Those who have chosen to dutifully follow the domain of a Fluttering Life srive to be much like that, to find, enact and nurture this freedom to live life through all the sorrows that death brings, acting often not as evangelists but instead as travelling undertakers and funeral orators.

They, at their worst, may come off as stark or even have a downlifting aura about their dour workings, yet when allowed to practice freely they usually become stalwart pillars of comfort and calm enforcers of welcoming acceptance of passing on.

In worlds such as Eberron, these first rose from the cracked ground as manifestation of the battlefields - Undead beings of solidified sorrows that roamed the earth and passed down their teachings not to end undeath of itself, but to finally allow those that couldn't to finally find peace. In others, such as that of the grim lands of Balefire beat their boots through the entire world as a rare, unseen sight - Preventing the malaise of souls from spreading by exhuming the bodies of the fallen and being one of the few, few people who fight back flame not with more flame, but instead with extinguishing the pain that yet assails the world.

subclassFeature.name: Foi Affamée

entries: "Convoitez-la...! Dévorez-la...! La Toison d'Or est gaspillée entre les mains avides des Noirs: arrachez-la de leurs murs! Jusqu'au moindre lambeau!"

There is a hunger that you've grown familiar with, that of the desire to feel passion slip from your lips and form into burning consumption of all that your heart may come to wish. Your soul has seeped into your organism, and the nourishment of the flesh has come to nourish the spirit as well: You may consume magic items during a long rest to absorb their effects, for an amount of items equal to half your proficiency bonus, with you requiring to lose one of your eaten magic item's benefits after exceeding the limit.

You have one collective amount of charges if an item has any charges that is a sum of all separate items, with them fully recharging at dawn. If you eaten magical weapons, all your weapon attacks gain the greatest bonus modifier to hit and damage between all the eaten weapons. If any had passive effects, you may choose to turn them on or off as a Free Action you may take once per turn.

After being consumed, the magic item is destroyed and you feel a brief, passing moment of satisfaction. If you benefit from the effects of consumed armor, you count as using armor for the effects of your Unarmored Defense.

subclassFeature.name: Force Blades
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can manifest ripples between space as purple energy blades that can cut through reality. You can manifest a force blade from your free hand, and whenever you take the Attack action, you can make the attack with that blade. This magic blade is a simple melee weapon with the finesse and thrown properties. It has a normal range of 60 feet and no long range, and on a hit, it deals force damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus the ability modifier you used for the attack roll. The blade leaves a purple scar on the target if the attack hits. The blades vanish immediately after it hits or misses its target after being thrown or after leaving your grasp.

After you attack with the blade, you can make a melee or ranged weapon attack with a second psychic blade as a bonus action on the same turn, provided your other hand is free to create it. The damage die of this bonus attack is {@dice 1d4}, instead of {@dice 1d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Fragrant Soul

entries: "Keep the door ajar. The sunbeam... is warm for once."

Those blessed by a Fragrant Soul are a rare sight to be seen, marking the world with their sorcerous powers like a painter would to a canvas and sowing seeds of growth for others whenever they come by.

They usually become well-trusted leaders of revolutionary movements or groups seeking some sort of improvement on the world, all driven by their desire to experience the small blossoms of ingenuity and beauty that may come along their lifetime, performed by themselves or others.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, Fragrant Soul Sorcerers are found with ease to those seeking them, as they have left their trails through the jungles of Chult in a great cult to bring full unity to the unruly land. In realms such as Thespis, they are the rare spawn of the Nushae who are blessed with a connection to the forests of the Wyrd, brandishing their magic as great magicians of their tribes, usually being cherished and highly-expected by their fellows.

entries.name: Fragrant Soul Origins
entries: Sorcerers who exhibit a Fragrant Soul are obvious to the naked eye, with leaves and branches growing from their bodies like a natural expansion-not to mention the eponymous smell from their eternal partial bloom.
These sorcerers may come from various origins, with only a few presented below, but most of the times they have deep ties to the nature of the world itself or its evolution, man-made or otherwise.

rows: You were born under the solstice of Autumn, blessed by nature itself and your heart is an enchanted organ.
You always had latent power that never seemed to sprout until a certain event changed everything in your life.
The powers granted to you were implanted by a third party without your knowledge, either at birth or later in life. You would only learn of it when first noticing the fragrance others couldn't.
Despair has marked your heart to the point that it became a seed of magic, granting you a power to sweep through the world and raze it to the ground, allowing it all to grow anew,
An archdruid has given you their blessing and infused your soul with druidic magic.
You were raised in a flower-pot and are actually a magician's homunculus.

entries.subclassFeature: Beauty of the Little Things|Sorcerer|PHB|Fragrant Soul|TheUndertomesFS|1

subclassFeature.name: Fragrant Soul Spells
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Fragrant Soul Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.
Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be from the sorcerer or druid spell list.

entries.caption: Fragrant Soul Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell compelled duel}, {@spell entangle}
3rd
{@spell barkskin}, {@spell locate animals or plants}
5th
{@spell plant growth}, {@spell speak with plants}
7th
{@spell freedom of movement}, {@spell grasping vine}
9th
{@spell commune with nature}, {@spell wrath of nature|XGE}

subclassFeature.name: From a Paper Note to the Starry Sky

entries: "As if drawn by a magnet, the talismans flew toward the doll."
"So that no one will cry..."

This is it. No matter the pain, no matter the sorrow, your heart keeps pounding. It has become something akin to an old oak - carved out from various little cuts and finished in your blood, making sure that every little corner of you remains alive to keep the wish glowing on.

You gain a Wishmaker token whenever a creature suffering from {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} is killed, you pass your negative Conditions to hostile creatures or absorb them from a friendly creature. You may spend them in the following ways:

items: As a Reaction to whenever you or a creature within 5-ft. of you fails a skill check or a saving throw, you may spend one token to grant them a little bit more willpower to see their task through. That creature adds a {@dice d6} bonus modifier to the roll, potentially turning that failure into a success.
At the end of your turns you may spend a token to cause all damage you'd take because of a countable Condition until the end of your next turn.

As an Action you may spend a hundred Wishmaker tokens to cast the {@spell Wish} spell and make a reality closer to what you've always wanted, no matter what short-reach it would have. You may do so once in your life. Be proud of what you paint unto the world.

entries: Additionally, you gain the following:

items: Once per long rest, you may use your Reaction whenever you would fall below one Hit Point or be killed to spend one of your Channel Divinity uses and cast away your pains, snapping every Talisman off of your body and immediately purifying them. When you do so, you cannot suffer damage until the start of your next turn and you instantly recover half of your Maximum Hit Points. Any negative Condition afflicting you also ends instantly.

Whenever you would throw a Talisman on a creature as per your So That No One Will Cry feature, you may spend another Twisted Curse Talisman count to target an additional creature for a ranged spell attack. You roll an additional one for such.

subclassFeature.name: Fuel My Rampage
entries: You have become a fearsome, opportunistic beast. Whenever you knock a hostile creature {@condition Unconscious} or kill them, you may spend your Reaction to move up to your base movement speed towards a creature within reach and perform a melee weapon attack against them if able. In addition you are healed by half a roll of your Second Wind ability when you land a Critical Hit against a hostile creature, knock them {@condition Unconscious} or kill them.

subclassFeature.name: Full Temporal Release
entries: There is a point where the pure, distilled disruption of time itself becomes like a bomb, and you have mastered how to weaponize it. Once per long rest, you can use your action to perform Crushbound Past.

entries.name: Crushbound Past
entries: You unleash a stream of temporal disruption from your hand like a gigantic laser in a 90-foot-long, 30-foot-wide cone in a direction of your choice. Each hostile creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d8} force damage, suffers 4 points of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and then suffers a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers half as much {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, rounded down.

Before unleashing this attack, you can spend up to 40 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} to empower it. You inflict 1 additional {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for every 2 counts spent. For every 10 counts spent, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}'s damage die increases by one step, such as from a d4 to a d6 and then to a d8, and your spell save DC increases by 1 for this attack. After the attack, you suffer one level of exhaustion, plus one additional level for every 10 counts spent.

subclassFeature.name: Full-Stop to Life
entries: When you reach 14th level, you've faced your fair share of near-death experiences, of times where you had to make risky judgements that you couldn't before. Nowadays, you trust that judgement, and you will trust it to the grave, be that grave yours or your enemy's.

As a bonus action before performing a Marksman Weapon Attack, you may spend an amount of Ammunition to empower this attack's damage. The damage is increased by one of the weapon's damage die per point of Ammunition spent. Additionally, you gain one point of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per Ammunition spent.

If you spend the max possible amount of your Ammunition in this shot, a Posture Critical hit also counts as a Critical Hit, having its effects. This effect does not stack in the case of a natural 20 roll.
You may use this ability once per short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Futile Lamentation

entries: I thought I might go crazy if I had to hear its cry any longer. I would rather just…

Your tear ducts overflow with the desire to protect those around you, but the display of emotion can be somewhat shocking. As a bonus action, you start crying loudly, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can hear you crying is enveloped by a magical aura of both comfort and sadness, recovering {@dice 1d10} Hit Points, gaining {@dice 1d6} temporary Hit Points and 3 counts of Sinking.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Additionally, you gain advantage on {@skill Persuasion} ability checks due to your tear-stained appearance and likeness to burst into tears.

subclassFeature.name: Gallery Ingredient - A Bloodied Ring

entries: "Allow me to play the curator for our guests-from kitsch to avant-garde, delving deep into each trend of art movement."

You have developed an extradimensional key that leads you to your very own Gallery of the Ring within its many Corridors. You now have a small key that can be recreated on a Short or Long Rest if lost or destroyed, destroying the old one upon recreation. You can use an Action to insert it into a door or into a space that could be considered a gate between two rooms or spaces, creating a portal to your personal gallery which you immediately enter. Your gallery is 60 feet long and 35 feet wide, with 20-foot high ceilings. Only creatures you allow inside the gallery can enter it with an Action. The interior is completely white, and furnished with pedestals that you can store your various creations inside. Only you can store, remove or give permission to store or remove items in the pedestals.

Creatures can remain inside the gallery up to a number of hours equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus. Creatures exit the gallery early if they use a Bonus Action to leave, if you die, or if the key is destroyed. Creatures can only leave if you allow them to or if you're unconscious. When any creature exits the gallery, they appear in the unoccupied space closest to it. Any objects left in the gallery remain there until carried out, but every creature is expelled in a similar manner to you. If the key is destroyed, every object stored there harmlessly appears in the unoccupied spaces closest to the key's former space. Once you enter the gallery, you can't enter again until you finish a Long Rest.
The key's AC equals your spell save DC. Its hit points equal your Artificer level plus your Proficiency Bonus, and it is Immune to Poison and Psychic damage.
Additionally, when you score a Critical Hit, you regain one use of your Flash of Genius ability.

entries.name: Installation Art no. 3: Improvised Ribcage.
entries: While inside your gallery, you can use an Action to summon rib cages around a creature that you can see within the gallery in attempts to imprison it. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition restrained} for a minute. They may reroll this saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending this effect on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Gamefowl Martial Archetype
entries: Most Fighters live for fighting, simple as it may be, but none embody the vital need for pure, unadulterated violence as the Gamefowl Martial Archetype, defined by being an opportunistic and usually battle-crazed bundle of blades who craves nothing more than a good fight.

By using a special technique to ignite their blades in oil and then spark that with their victim's blood, they turn the battlefield into a searing inferno as they rush around, seeking not the greatest fight possible like a grandious warrior wanting glory, but like a mad rooster needing to feed on the greatest amount of battles possible, being proficient at finalizing creatures and heading onto the next as soon as possible.

In realms such as Fâerun, they are found as a Mercenary Group with the same namesake as the Archetype, a bunch of warriors with barely any hierarchy, only waiting to be leased by whatever lord of the land they aimlessly wander into so they can incur the wrath of their flock onto some poor target.

entries.name: {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} Sword
entries: Through a rare technique you've managed to procure an efficient way to enchant your blade to ignite when soaked in blood, turning it into oil to fuel your violence. While you have a free hand you gain one count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} whenever you deal damage to a creature that has below half its Maximum Hit Points. You also gain one count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} whenever a creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or is killed within 15-ft of you.

While you have {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR}, you may easily coat your swings into a pure blaze, causing you to deal an additional {@dice 1d6} fire damage per count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} and also inflict two times your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on melee weapon attacks, You may have up to three counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} at any given time, losing one whenever you deal damage to a creature and at the end of combat.

entries.name: Battle Roosting
entries: In the high tide of battle you may wish to fan the flames so a fight is brought straight to you, disregarding your safety just for more violence. As a Bonus Action during your turn you may let out a battle-crazed screech, causing all creatures around 30-ft of you to have Advantage on attacks against you. Furthermore, when you do this you deal additional damage on melee weapon attacks equal to the target's {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, for a maximum amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The type of this additional damage is the same as your weapon's.
These effects last until the start of your next turn and you may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus (Rounded Down) per Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Rooster's Flight
entries: Through magical mutations that have pinions grow upon your arms to aid with your movement or special training that have you feel as if you could fly, you have achieved a point where your movement is leagues above the usual person. You gain Proficiency in Athletics, or Expertise if you were already Proficient in this skill. Furthermore, as a Reaction to when you would take fall damage you may attempt to catch yourself on any footholds on walls nearby or to soften your fall as you can by attempting an Athletics Skill Check with a DC that equals 13 + 1 for each 10-ft you fell. On a Success, you take no damage from falling.

subclassFeature.name: Games of Trust

entries: Your head will soon be filled with happiness.
To find the true source of quantifiable joy you have been studying how to be social and how to thrive in such settings.
You may use your Intelligence modifier instead of Charisma on skill checks and gain proficiency in Alchemist’s Supplies.
During a long rest you can produce two Nettleburst Joints during a long rest, a magical drug that becomes impotent at the start of your next long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Gap Attack

entries: "Stay sharp and focus on the fight if you don't want to snuff it."

Opening a gap for you and your fellows to strike through is a tough opportunity to pass by, so you create it yourself when no one else will. When you deal damage through your Sneak Attack, you may choose to engage in a swift withdrawal of your blade to have the target suffer a count of {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesNA} and an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus.
Whenever you perform a Sneak Attack you may choose to inflict {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after the Sneak Attack.
