Additionally, keeping your step clean and your options open cash in your shot is tantamount to you, granting you half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesSR} count on a successful Sneak Attack.

subclassFeature.name: Gathering Electricity

entries: "... So the pebbles rolled and rolled, eventually amassing into this mountainous pile—the terminus of dregs that could not even become Distortions. Their potentialities must have manifested as an unstoppable, downhill inertia, and... *exhale*"

The Arcane Electrical Discharge Discipline Tradition is one that you've come to be apart with deliberate understanding and appliance of its teachings, of creating and maintaining an ever-lasting current for you to tap upon despite any circumstances. Whenever you cast a spell you gain {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus plus that spell's level, to a minimum of 1 for cantrips. While you have this electricity gathering around you, the following happens:

items: For each 6 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you have, you gain a +1 to your Spell Save DC.

For each 3 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you have, your AC increases by a +1 bonus modifier. This bonus becomes half your {@condition High-Voltage Exoskeleton|TheUndertomesAED} count when under the Condition.

At the end of your turns , you lose all your {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and gain half that value in {@condition High-Voltage Exoskeleton|TheUndertomesAED}, to a maximum count equal to your proficiency bonus, retaining any surplus {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} that would be consumed above that.

Whenever you hit a creature with a spell attack, you may spend multiples of 6 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you currently have to inflict a count of {@condition Charged Sting|TheUndertomesAED|Charge Sting} against the target for each 6 count spent. If you would cause a saving throw effect, you instead divide each {@condition Charged Sting|TheUndertomesAED} count you would inflict between creatures who failed this save.

If you'd gain {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count through a spell that deals lightning damage, you gain additional count of the Condition equal to half your proficiency bonus.around them.

subclassFeature.name: Gathering of Knowledge as Kindling

entries: "Remember not only to refill what you have burned but also to add new knowledge into your repositories."

Your free time is often spent in the dwellings of books, absorbing knowledge as if it were oxygen. Whenever you take a long rest you may choose to become Proficient in two skills you weren't Proficient with, then having these Proficiencies lost at the next long rest as the knowledge fades from your mind as you make space for more.

Yet the wisdom imparted to you is left not only in theory, but also used to glimpse Insights of the world and its ways in a practical manner. You may do the following to gain counts of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE}, which is used to fuel certain abilities or to passively bolden yourself:

items: You may spend a Bonus Action to instantly forget one of your skill Proficiencies, gaining 2 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} count.
You may spend a Bonus Action to instantly forget one of your Artisan's Tools, Instrument or Gaming Kit Proficiencies, gaining 1 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} count.

entries: Whenever you forget a proficiency you effectively juxtapose that piece of knowledge to re-frame the world in front of you, aiding in the connection and conceptualization of ideas you may not have seen before, yet you also forget the original purpose of this piece of intelligence, having its base set to crumble within the annals of your mind. You lose the ability to use your proficiency bonus in rolls regarding the lost proficiency until the end of your next long rest.

While you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} you gain a bonus modifier to unarmed attacks and Intelligence skill checks equal to half of your current count of the Condition. Additionally, you gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence saving throws and skill checks equal to your current count. You may have a maximum count of the Condition equal to your proficiency bonus.

If you spend Ki to perform an ability that requires you to have a minimum amount of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE}, you lose one count at the end of your turns. Otherwise, your count is reduced by one per minute spent outside of combat.

subclassFeature.name: Giving Form to Shape

entries: "It is because of this that Faust forged this panoply. Not merely to provide a veil behind which the bashful Fascia might reside, but also to stage a dual aesthetic: the weighted inertia of the armored body..."

You have constructed or even grown a metallic armor that encases your entire body most of the time, only being doffed when you need to put on a magnificent display of power and artistry - a show of the humanoid form at its peak. While not in your Flowing Form, you are in Iron Maiden Form, which affects you in the following ways:

items: Your movement speed is reduced by 10-ft. and any effects that would give you additional movement speed is halved. ( Rounded up. )
While not donning any armor your AC is equal to 11 + your Constitution modifier + your Wisdom modifier.
You are considered proficient with Martial Weapons, but may only add half your proficiency bonus to attacks made with them.

You are considered proficient with Heavy Armor and suffer no penalties to {@skill Stealth} skill checks while donning it. When wearing this armor, you usually implement it as an outer layer of your Iron Maiden shell.

entries: Additionally, whenever an attack misses you and the difference between the attack and your AC is equal to or greater than a value of 10 - your proficiency bonus, you may spend your Reaction to perform a melee weapon attack against the attacker. You may otherwise cast a cantrip that has a spell attack against the same target.

Furthermore, while in this Form you may use your Bonus Action to revest your body with {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO}, spending 3 count to grant yourself Resistance to your choice of bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage until the start of your next turn. Upon reaching 8th level, you may spend 6 count instead to grant yourself Resistance to any damage type for the same duration.

subclassFeature.name: Gnome's Help-ome!
entries: The Cheerful Spirits are always watching! And they are always happy to help you and your fellows. Whenever you would become {@condition Unconscious} or afflicted with a condition that would cause you to be have your movement speed reduced to 0-ft., a gaggle of gnomes emerges from the Giftbag and rushes to aid you move, having you always maintain at least half your walking speed. If you would be {@condition Grappled}, they do not help you move, instead coming out to attack the creature Grappling you repeatedly. At the end of your turns, you may perform one melee spell attack against that creature, dealing {@damage 2d4} + your Charisma modifier damage on a hit and granting you advantage on your next skill check against being {@condition Grappled}.

subclassFeature.name: Golden Grasp
entries: At 15th level, your contempt manifests as golden spectral hands that erupt from the earth to seize your foes. When you successfully cause a creature to be {@condition Grappled} or {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesCL}, you can choose to summon this manifestation of your grandiosity. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become {@condition Grasped|TheUndertomesRES} until the end of your next turn, instead of being {@condition Grappled} or {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesCL}.
A {@condition Grasped|TheUndertomesRES} creature suffers the following effects:

items: A grasped creature's speed becomes 0, and they can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
The creature has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
The creature cannot restore hit points while grasped and suffers two of its hit die in bludgeoning damage at the start of their turns.

If the grasped creature is reduced to 0 hit points during the condition, their body is instantly crushed into paste by the hands holding it, rendering it impossible to revive through any means lesser than the {@spell Resurrection} spell or greater. Furthermore, you are magically healed by four of the creatures hit die's worth of hit points as their blood cascades down.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Designer's Note.

The Inspire Awe Channel Divinity option does not count summoned creatures or otherwise "companion" creatures such as the Battle Master's Steel construct or Wild Companions towards granting you additional Awesome Die.

subclassFeature.name: Goodbye Now, A Sorrow in You

entries: "At the heart of a broken mirror, I see the fading butterfly. A wandering butterfly I cannot bloom, yet the duty of lamentation is mine, thus, it is also mine, this melancholy."

You come to reach a point where you lead a calm life despite all that assails your life, embracing the transience of life as a simple fact, much like day slips into night and night to day. To that end, your lectures toward the dead have come to be an aura that follows you to the ends of the earth. You gain the following:

items: Whenever a creature that you can see dies within 60-ft. of you a small collection of butterflies crowd toward you, granting you two {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesFL} count. This Condition has no effect on you and does not change or diminish at the end of your turns, instead you gain a +1 bonus modifier to Wisdom saving throws for each 4 count you currently have, to a maximum of +3. Whenever you would inflict {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesFL} on a creature, you may choose to spend from your count to add the same amount to theirs.
You always have the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell prepared and may cast it at will without spending a spell slot.

Creatures that you lay to rest ( through killing or through use of any of your features ) may choose to linger on as a butterfly, using the {@creature Owl} stat sheet except they may speak telepathically through any language they knew in life and they instantly die when wandering further than 360-ft. of you. They become neutral toward you if they were hostile but are otherwise friendly and calm toward you. You may use their butterfly body to revive them through a {@spell Resurrection} or greater spell without requiring their original body.

subclassFeature.name: Grasped Life

entries: The coffin bursts open, letting them out..

Feasting on the dead and liberating them from their mortal coils is the calling of your swarm. You can command your Clerid Swarm to take the Consume Body Action while you are performing your Woundhealing ritual.

You are also able to spend your Reaction whenever a creature within 30-ft of you or your swarm is reduced to half or below their maximum hitpoints to perform a Revenous Bites attack with your swarm against them, generating 1 Lifeblood Count when you do so.
Furthermore, you may spend Lifeblood in the following ways:

items.name: Entice the Swarm.
entries: You may spend your Action and consume up to 9 Lifeblood to draw out your Swarm’s unending appetite, granting it a +1 to attack and damage rolls per each 3 Lifeblood spent this way. Furthermore, their Ravenous Bites attack deals an additional damage die for each 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on it’s target, to a maximum amount of {@dice 5d8} additional damage. This effect lasts up to three turns, or until you fall {@condition Unconscious}.

items.name: Death Postponed.
entries: Before you cast the {@spell Shrouded Hand|TheUndertomesASV} cantrip you may spend 2 Lifeblood count to make it so the cantrip instead heals a creature it grasps instead of dealing damage, chanelling life from your Coffin.

items: You may have a maximum 10 Lifeblood count at any given time, losing half (Rounded Up) your total counts upon taking a short or long rest.
Furthermore, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill or expertise if you were already proficient.

subclassFeature.name: Greta's Melody - Anatomization of the Unanatomized by the Anatomized

entries: "What a beautiful hue it has. A piece worthy of its own pedestal."

You've become a true master of anatomy, able to bend any bone and tendon to your will. If you kill a non-Construct creature of CR 10 or lower, you may choose to store its body with you until your next Long Rest, during which you may transform it into an Automanikin and revive it under your command. This creature has the same stat block as the original creature, except its creature type is Construct. It listens to your commands as a Bonus Action, but will take the Dodge action if not commanded to do anything else during that turn. Alternatively, you can use an Action to transform Humanoids you have killed into Automanikins. Immediately after creating them, you may order them as part of the same Action to do something, and they will attempt to complete that order to the best of their abilities until they die or the order changes. You can have a maximum number of Automanikins equal to your Proficiency Bonus if they're CR 2 or lower Humanoids, or only one if they are non-humanoid or higher than CR 2.

entries.name: Closing Time - Installation Art no. 1: Your Flesh and Bones as the Gallery's Seats.
entries: As an Action inside your gallery, you may have any of your art pieces expand their bones and puncture creatures nearby. Choose any number of creatures that you can see up to your Proficiency Bonus. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or be pierced, taking {@damage 8d6} Piercing damage and having to roll on the Lingering Injuries Table. If this kills a creature, they are immediately added to your gallery as one of its sculptures. Once you use this feature, you can only use it again after a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Grief of the Deprived

entries: Come back to me, so I won’t be lonely…

The world has seen it’s fair share of abandonment, of being constantly robbed for lavish ends and by treacherous means, much like you and your god. Due to this, you’ve formed a kinship to the things of the land, being able to ask a number of questions to an animal ( Beast-typed creatures ) or plants, granting them a shared blessing that allows you to understand them as if they could speak a language you understand.

The subject of this blessing may have their own personality and only knows what it could know by itself, such as what an animal has seen while wandering around or a plant has heard in its vicinity, but most tend to answer truthfully. You may use this ability for a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest, rounded down.
Furthermore you gain proficiency in your choice of the {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Animal Handling} or {@skill Nature} skills.

subclassFeature.name: Grudgekeeper Otherworldly Patron

entries: "...I don't care that we failed. It's my failure, not the Middle's. And the Middle always pays its debts."
The Grievance is a living concept represented by groups united as a family, not necessarily through blood, but through kindred ideals and care for one another.

Warlocks who follow the Grudgekeeper personally rectify everyone who has wronged their kin or ideals, granted power by their betters or a great deity to act in their stead. Such a warlock will stop at nothing to aid their siblings, carrying a heavy bound tome that empowers their every movement, granting them magic instead of ink and the force to do what they must.

The Grudgekeeper takes many forms across different worlds, from a far-reaching cult acting as brigands and gangsters to the servants of a grand war-profiteer whose chains spread across the land. Either way, a Grudgekeeper pays their dues and lives to cross names from their list.

subclassFeature.name: Guerrilla Tactics

entries: "Though now, I've come to realize that knowledge holds no real answers."
You have come to wield the stress of duelling against something much greater than you with prowess, developing a handful of techniques to ensure your success no matter where your halberd falls upon:

items: {@b True Decapitation Deathblow.} While having at least 6 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, you may use your Action to perform a melee weapon attack roll against a target within reach, dealing an additional damage die and inflicting one additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each extra attack you would be able to perform during your turn. You deal a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20, before any modifiers. This does not trigger effects such as that of a {@item vorpal sword|DMG|Vorpal Sword}. If you kill a hostile non-summoned creature this way you gain double the {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you would gain as per your Abate the Smoke feature.

{@b Excision of Sacrifice.} As a Reaction to when you would successfully pass any Saving Throw or similar effect that would cause you to suffer half damage, you may deliver a staggering counter-blow that cuts through any onslaught. You and a number of other creatures of your choice suffering this Saving Throw suffer no damage, or half the damage that would be dealt if they failed this Saving Throw themselves. This number starts at 0 and you may spend 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to increase it by one, to a maximum number of chosen creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

{@b Lend My Inner Ear to Myself.} As a Bonus Action, you may consume 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to quell your inner turmoil, calling upon everything you went through to live another day - After all, what is a better comrade than you? You instantly end any negative Conditions afflicting you. If you could not use a Bonus Action during your turn because of an external effect, you can still use this specific Bonus Action.

entries: You may use these skills an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus per short or long rest. Alternatively, upon reaching 9th level you may spend an use of your {@classFeature Indomitable|Fighter|PHB|9} feature to utilize one of these techniques without counting toward your limit per short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hallowed Strikes

entries: "It is a heavy gift that I shoulder a twain of wayward souls in each of my palms, fingers held ever-closer."

At 8th level, the cleric gains the ability to infuse their weapon strikes with a mixture of balancing energy. Once on each of the cleric's turns when they hit a creature with a weapon attack, the cleric can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage to the target whenever they deal radiant damage, and the inverse when dealing necrotic damage. When the cleric reaches 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d4}.

subclassFeature.name: Hardblood Thorn
entries: You can use a parasol as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells. This parasol is the perfect tool to easily channel blood from your enemies to you, and vice versa. You gain Blooming Thorns with your Bloodfeast, which gradually grows in power the more blood you spend. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Blooming Thorn Ranks
rows: 3rd

If your parasol is lost or destroyed, you may recreate it during a long rest without spending materials. It is a martial weapon you are proficient with, deals {@dice 1d8} piercing damage, and can use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls.
I
3rd

Whenever you apply stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to a creature, you add twice that amount of Bloodfeast to your party's pool. Once per day, you can cast {@spell Melf's acid arrow|PHB|Melf's Acid Arrow} with your parasol without material components. Instead of dealing its additional {@dice 2d4} acid damage, it applies 2 stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. You can also spend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to cast this version as though it were prepared.
II
6th

Your parasol deals {@dice 2d8} piercing damage. As a bonus action, you can open it to grant yourself and a creature directly behind you half cover. Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker gains 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. The parasol counts as a +1 arcane focus and a +1 weapon.
III
14th

Your parasol deals {@dice 2d10} piercing damage plus {@dice 1d8} piercing damage against enemies with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever you apply stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you add three times that amount of Bloodfeast to your party's pool and regain hit points equal to the Bloodfeast acquired. It counts as a +2 arcane focus and a +2 weapon. On a critical hit, you can heal yourself or a creature within the weapon's reach for up to twice the target's {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks.

subclassFeature.name: Haunted Noble Martial Archetype
entries: The Haunted Noble's burden is not only that of paranormal curses, but of constant mental torment. Those who fit into this cast are the ones who despite their advantaged upbringing have been scarred, be it from the diseases of the body or the ones who assail the soul - It doesn't matter in the end, for that has become part of their life, a life marred in pursuit for a cure or any sort of relief that so far has eluded them.

This martial Archetype can be found in many shapes and in many worlds, not having any pre-ordained calling to a realm. They, however, might be born and exiled from a royal family, cast unto a dishevelled reality where their tutoring with a blade became not only for show anymore, instead being thrusted knee-deep into the steep flooring of mercenary work, or a sickly child who desperately is clinging to the hope of finding a cure that could empty their lungs of their decay.

subclassFeature.name: Haunted Toymaker
entries: A Haunted Toymaker does not simply make playthings for children and adults alike, but tense and dangerous objects that could prove lethal to any inexperienced handler. They implement a mixture of sharpness and dark magic in their inventions for a myriad of reasons, such as revenge, a twisted sense of pride or personal entertainment.

If you're going to play as a Haunted Toymaker, be sure to let your party know. You will likely follow the trope of a mad scientist or someone equally unhinged, and not all groups mesh well with a strong personality like that. Haunted Toymakers are always looking for new cursed items to turn into child's play and victims to be the target of their inventions. You will want to create things normal people would naturally shun and you want to not only give them the chance to shine but to take revenge on those that would leak down on their nature.

In the Forgotten Realms, every toy store has at least one of these-no Artificer is completely rid of sparks of madness; Haunted Toymakers simply own it. In Ravenloft, these specialists take a more sinister turn, usually leaving their constructs in unassuming houses to terrorize their inhabitants. In the high fantasy world of Aster, those haunted by the corrupting influence of Salem, The Great Witch, might dedicate themselves to the craft of the abominable.

subclassFeature.name: Haunted Toymaker Spells
entries: Starting at 3rd-level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Haunted Toymaker spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don't count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.caption: Haunted Toymaker Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell dissonant whispers|PHB|Dissonant Whispers}, {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiars}
5th
{@spell cloud of daggers|PHB|Cloud of Daggers}, {@spell darkness|PHB|Darkness}
9th
{@spell bestow curse|PHB|Bestow Curse}, {@spell fear|PHB|Fear}
13th
{@spell blight|PHB|Blight}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
17th
{@spell dream|PHB|Dream}, {@spell mislead|PHB|Mislead}

subclassFeature.name: Haute Couture: Le Rouge

entries: "De ma propre main, j'abattrai quiconque osera se dresser sur le chemin de l'Être Chéri."

Thread spinning through your fingers and needling through is muscle memory for you, the simplest notions for one who wishes to become a luxurious fashionista. You gain proficiency in Weaver's Tools, or Expertise if you were already proficient. Additionally, you may use your Weaver's Tools modifier on skill checks made to attempt figuring out what creature type a creature you can see it, attempting to recognize the material their body would provide.

subclassFeature.name: Headless Fowl
entries: Death's door has now been a far thought in your head, barely considered even as you stand by it - Your desire for more always fueling your will to move foward to the next fight, no matter what. When you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious}, once per Long Rest, you instead suffer the {@condition Headless Fowl [无头鸡]|TheUndertomesGF} condition.

While in this state you have Disadvantage on any Saving Throws and Skill Checks, but may still move as your body acts upon its instincts looking for more fights. Whenever you inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on another creature, you deal one more count of the condition and you deal an additional damage die on every melee weapon attack, with its damage type being the same as your weapon's. You must roll a Death Saving Throws at the end of your turn and automatically regain half your Maximum Hit Points if you pass three Death Saving Throws, however instead of taking damage when a creature would deal any to you, you instead fail one Death Saving Throw per creature, per turn. You may benefit from Fuel My Rampage while like this.

subclassFeature.name: Heartburn Martial Archetype
entries: Fighters who understand that a wildfire is not composed of one flame have forged their bodies into weapons of all-out war. Their fists bring the heat into battle as they sweep into the fray and extinguish enemies in their path.

subclassFeature.name: Heishou Mutation [Si]

entries: "Once I took the Si Bolus, I lost most of my sense of taste... But hey, I can still enjoy the texture."

Your limbs were modified by a special medicine to stretch farther than is usual for humanoids. You can stretch your arms up to 5 feet beyond their normal length, allowing you to interact with objects and creatures at a distance, and your melee weapon attacks have the Reach property. This distance increases to 10 feet at 6th level, 30 feet at 14th level, and 60 feet at 18th level. Additionally, you have resistance to poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Manual - Practical Uses 101
entries: There are a number of tricks that any good hunter must learn to employ to further their goals, afterall, you're only a regular person when compared to a beast of blood. As such, you've learnt how to make the most of your limited resources, gaining the following uses for your Arms of The Hunt through spending an action:

entries.caption: Practical Uses 101
rows: Antitoxin

rows.name: Inject
entries: You may use your Bonus Action to administer Antitoxin to yourself or to a creature within your melee reach, instantly ending the {@condition Poisoned||Poisoned} condition on them and causing the target to be Resistant to poison damage until the end of their next turn.

rows: Horror Trinket

rows.name: Spook
entries: As a Bonus Action you may immolate the Horror Trinket as an Effigy, forcing up to your Proficiency Bonus' worth of creatures within 60-ft that can see you to pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or become {@condition Frightened||Frightened} of you for up to one minute. You gain a bonus modifier to {@skill Intimidation} Skill Checks against creatures {@condition Frightened||Frightened} like this equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature {@condition Frightened||Frightened} this way may re-attempt this Saving Throw at the end of their turns, ending the condition on a success.

rows: Caltrops

rows.name: Wedge
entries: Whenever a creature would take damage because of your Caltrops, they also suffer an additional {@damage 2d6} piercing damage and two {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} Count.

rows: {@item Grappling Dart|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Pull-Through
entries: When the {@item Grappling Dart|TheUndertomesTO|Grappling Dart} is lodged into a creature you've hit that is of your size or Larger, or is an Object that weighs more than you, you may spend your Bonus ACtion to pull yourself to be within the closest unoccupied 5-ft space from the target.

rows: {@item Stake|TheUndertomesTO} (6)

rows.name: Twisting
entries: As a Reaction taken after you deal damage using a Stake, you may choose to twist the piece of wood and cause the target to trigger {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} up to half your Proficiency Bonus' worth of times, rounded down, removing {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count in accord.

rows: {@item Bonecrusher Hammer|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Veincrush
entries: Makes it so the target can't recover Hit Points for the amount of turns equal to your Proficiency Modifier.

rows: Net

rows.name: Laminate
entries: Your net is laced with a special coating that makes it easily cut when put under strain, causing any creature that tries to break free from the net to suffer 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} on a Failure.

rows: {@item Styptics Bag|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Imbibe
entries: When used, the {@item Styptics Bag|TheUndertomesTO|Styptics Bag} also heals the target for {@dice 2d4 + 2} hit points.

rows: {@item Sanctified Canister|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Aimed Throw
entries: You know how to use the explosion to direct creatures away on the right angle. When you throw the grenade and it explodes, you may choose to have the detonation forcefully push any creature who fails the Saving Throw in a 15-ft line of your choice.

rows: {@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Gouge
entries: When you would trigger Hemorrhaging while using this weapon, you may spend your Reaction to quickly draw out the pain inflicted to either scratch at a creature's eye or sink into their ear, causing them to be respectively {@condition Blinded||Blinded} or {@condition Deafened||Deafened} until they are cured of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}.

rows: {@item Vial of Silver Water|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Accessorise
entries: You may don this item not as a charm but as the weight at the end of a whip or another melee weapon's pommel as a Bonus Action, causing any damage you deal with the adorned weapon to also deal an additional {@damage 2d4} radiant damage against Shapechangers and Undead creatures, yet the Vial breaks if you receive or deal a Critical Hit. You may spend an Action to retrieve the Vial out of the weapon.

rows: {@item Aromatized Incense Burner|TheUndertomesTO}

rows.name: Combust
entries: Your Incense is particularly strong, making it so that the 30-feet area around the Incense Burner also becomes Heavily Obscured to any Undead or Shapechanger creature. This area increases by 5-ft at the start of your turns and lasts for up to one minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}. Furthermore, any Undead or Shapechanger creature who starts or ends their turn inside this area instantly suffers {@damage 1d4} radiant damage.

You may use this feature for an amount of times equal to your Proficiency Modifier, regaining half the spent uses at a Short Rest or all spent uses on a Long Rest. Despite the nature of the original item, such as a weapon being used, it is always consumed or destroyed after use, as you wring out all its usefulness at once. The DC for any Saving Throws mentioned in this table is equal to your Ranger Spell Save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Manual - The Secret Trades
entries: You have become quite the Hunter, learned in their ways and nimble with their thoughts on how to take down the befanged threat. So much so, that you've learnt how to become a threat yourself. Upon reaching 15h level you may choose one of the following weapons to have as your Signature Weapon, a weapon of which you have trained painstakingly to become a monster with:

entries.caption: Signature Weapons
rows: {@item Serrated Hand-axe|TheUndertomesTO|Serrated Hand-axe}

While wielding a Serrated Edge, you are an unstoppable menace, gaining the following effects: Once per turn you may choose to suffer only half the damage you would take from an attack, shrugging it off as one of your many lacerations. Furthermore, you deal an additional {@damage 2d8} slashing damage with {@item Serrated Hand-axe|TheUndertomesTO|Serrated Hand-Axe} attacks and always inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}, inflicting two additional counts instead of one when triggering Hemorrhage. You also deal double any damage rolled against structures and objects that are not being worn or wielded.
Steel-Tipped Whip

You have made some modifications to your whip, using a specific alchemical formula to make any Steel-Tipped Whip you wield to be considered as a Silvered Weapon that deals an additional {@damage 3d4} radiant damage against Undead and Shapechanger creatures, of which cannot recover hit points after being dealt damage this way until they bask into complete darkness for 12 hours. Furthermore, you may use your Whip to cause other creatures to fall {@condition Prone||Prone} by forgoing dealing damage when you would hit them, also inflicting 6 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} Count on the target.
{@item Stake|TheUndertomesTO}

You're a monster when it comes to pinning the monsters of night down and bleeding them dry. You may treat {@item Stake Crossbow|TheUndertomesTO|Stake Crossbows} as if they had the Light property in place of Heavy and Two-Handed. Furthermore, when you spend your Bonus Action to attack with them, you fire three stakes without any additional ammo cost, being able to perform a ranged weapon attack to the same or another target. At the end of your turn, if you have hit one target with Stakes at least thrice, they must pass a Constitution Saving Throw against your Ranger Spell Save DC (Or 8 + your Dexterity Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or become {@condition Restrained||Restrained} until the end of your next turn on a failure. A creature who fails this Saving Throw automatically succeeds it on the next time it is forced to attempt it. You also inflict 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} whenever you hit an attack while using Stakes. When you do so, you do not trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture}'s effects or reduce its Count.
{@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesTO}

You have dabbled into the arts of potioncrafting, or more specifically: poisoncraft. As a Bonus Action during your turns you may douse a {@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesTO|Vein Splitter} with this poison, which forces a creature that takes damage from it to pass a Constitution Saving Throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or be {@condition Charmed||Charmed} by you until they stop {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} or is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}. While {@condition Charmed||Charmed} in this way, the creature is under effect of your choice of illusion from the {@spell major image|PHB|Major Image} or {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer} spells as if you had cast them and only the {@condition Poisoned||poisoned} creature can perceive it. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, restoring spent uses on a Long Rest. You may use your Signature Weapon for your Practical Uses 101 ability an amount of times before it breaks equal to your Proficiency Bonus, also fixing and recreating it during a Long Rest without the need to spend extra resources.

subclassFeature.name: Hype up the Masses!

entries: "If everyone threw their bodies into me, it'll certainly create an even sweeter melody"

A lively life is one that is marched with an entire band and not a single sad little player, after all, how are you going to play without plentiful instruments?! That thought has crawled in the back of your mind enough times for you to consider the occasional welcoming of others into your melody and actually learning how they tick from the outside in. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient. Charisma is your Ability Modifier for this skill.

Additionally, whenever a creature attempts a Strength, Dexterity, Constitution or Charisma ability check you may spent your Reaction to play a backing track to hype them - and yourself - up, granting them half your Charisma modifier as a bonus modifier to their roll. If they still fail, the sounds of their broken body fill you with joy, with that creature suffering an amount of {@damage d8} bludgeoning damage equal to half their proficiency bonus and you instantly recovering one use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1}. This must be done before they roll. You may only use this feature an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: I Can Take Care of The Baddies!
entries: Starting at 6th level, just like the magic that clings under your skin seems to develop more and more, so does your elation when thwarting Villains! In tandem, though, so grows your despair when things don't go your way, as they often may not. While raging, every time you miss an attack or take damage from a creature who is a {@condition Villain|TheUndertomesMG}, you gain one stack of {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG}, gaining double on any critical failures. You lose a stack whenever you land a hit against the {@condition Villain|TheUndertomesMG} and lose them all when the {@condition Villain|TheUndertomesMG} is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or dies or your rage ends.

While under the effects of {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG}, you progressively get more deranged in your pursuit of justice, your lofty goals propelling you forward like a hurricane of pain. As such, you may spend {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG} stacks to perform the following:

entries.name: Arcana Beats!
entries: As part of your attack action, you may spend a {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG} stack per attack to literally beat your righteousness into the air using your Magic Wand! You gain an additional 15-feet radius to your attack and it deals an additional {@dice 1d4} force damage on a hit, as beams of arcane energy shoot out to complement it.

In the Name of Love and Hate! By spending an action and three {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG} stacks you may prepare a series of magical circles to soak your Magic Wand into as you deliver a single powerful blow enchanted by each circle, you roll a weapon attack as usual, on a hit you instead deal {@dice 2d12} plus your Strength Modifier in force damage, and the target must pass a Constitution Saving Throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or suffer a stack of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesMG}.

subclassFeature.name: I Shall Impale
entries: "So drink, drink with abandon, for that is the only dream this existence has permitted us." You ascend to the position you were always meant to hold, manipulating the blood around you to create an unbreakable lance to guide your kin. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute: As a reaction, if a creature within 30 feet of you would be reduced to 0 hit points due to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage, instead you take a number of d4s in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage equal to half their {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, and they recover Hit Points equal to that damage, afterwards losing all stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, You gain a +5 bonus to {@skill Perception} checks made to notice creatures that are missing Hit Points. Additionally, if you have inflicted {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a target, you always know where it is as long as it is within 1 mile of you and still has counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

Whenever you apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature, they immediately take the damage after the attack but do not lose any counts that round. Ascendant Hardblood Arts - La Sangre. Once you become the only one capable of leading the Vampires or {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} forward, once you are certain of your position and will in this world and are chosen as their guide by at least three other relevant {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends}, you gain these additional benefits: As a reaction when a hostile creature within 30 feet of you takes {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage, you can heal another creature within 30 feet of you by double that amount.

Whenever you hit with an attack, you apply 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. When you kill a creature that was Bleeding, you generate 10 Bloodfeast. As an action, you can empower your lance and immediately use all of your movement speed to move in a straight line and force every creature of your choice within that line to roll a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.

If they fail, they take {@damage 5d12} piercing damage and {@damage 5d12} necrotic damage, they gain 4 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and are pushed back towards the end of your lance, becoming {@condition Restrained||restrained}. On a success, they only take half the damage and half the count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, As a reaction to when a creature {@condition Restrained||restrained} this way is hit by an attack, you can spend 30 Bloodfeast to make them vulnerable to all damage types until the end of that round. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.
Designer's Note

subclassFeature.name: I'll Gut You Like a Fish

entries: "Hahahahaha! Having a good time, Kiddo? Mama's the best, huh?"

You've heard the destructive desire of the sword would eventually corrupt your spirit - bullshit, you're as sane as the day you killed for this thing. As long as you're holding {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM}, you gain the following abilities:

entries.name: Gut Stab [Lævateinn]
entries: If you are Grappling a creature, you gain advantage on attack rolls against it. Additionally, if you hit 3 or more attacks against the Grappled creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they gain an Internal Injury from the Lingering Injuries table. On a successful save, they instead receive a Festering Wound.

entries.name: Complete and Total Extermination [Lævateinn]
entries: As an Action, you can make an attack roll against a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If it hits, you throw your sword at them, piercing their gut and dealing {@damage 3d8} Piercing damage and {@damage 3d8} Fire damage, as well as 8 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. They must then make a Constitution saving throw as you attempt to cleave the sword out of them. On a failed save, they take an additional {@damage 5d8} Slashing damage and you sever one of their limbs off in a non-lethal way. If this would reduce them to 0 hit points, you bissect them instead, melting their insides. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

subclassFeature.name: If I Could Go Back…

entries: Sad, sad things happened here. Many sad things.

You gain the ability to reduce the suffering of those around you and use those feelings to empower yourself and your allies. As an action, choose a creature you can see within 120 feet of you. They must roll a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, and they can choose to fail, as one of your arms becomes woody and stumpy, and insectile roots charge at the creature. On a failed save, you remove {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts from them (minimum of 3 and maximum of 15). For each 3 counts you remove this way, you may target an additional creature within 120 feet of you and grant them {@dice 2d6} temporary Hit Points. On a successful save, they aren’t affected by this effect, however, instead of halving their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the end of the turn, they lose 3 counts instead.

subclassFeature.name: Il Cacciatore

entries: "I'll show you an infinitely close approximation of your angle an' speed."

A hunters discipline comes into effect not just with creating the perfect situation but with live studies of their prey, taking in their movements, their mistakes and their weaknesses as the hunt rages on - and you've made yourself adept at doing just that. While there is no more than one hostile creature within 5-ft. of you and no friendly creatures within the same range, you gain a count of {@condition Escalating Duel|TheUndertomesSP} whenever you first hit a creature during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Image of a Heart

entries: "Verily, I say unto you, the days spoken of in the Apocalypse are nigh!"

Your heartbeat is faint, linked to a mystic machine that aids in keeping you living. You always have a {@item Machine Coil|TheUndertomesPH} in your person, which re-appears to be within 5-ft. of you if lost. You are always Attuned to this item, although it does not count toward your limit. It also grows in strength according to your levels in Sorcerer:

entries.caption: Machine Coil Growth
rows: 1st
Uncommon
5th
Rare
11th
Very Rare
17th
Legendary

entries: Whenever you reach the levels presented above, you gain the respective modifier to attack and damage rolls using the {@item Machine Coil|TheUndertomesPH}, which also increases your Spell Save DC by the same value.

After becoming a Rare item you may make use of the Coil's Float trait to have it follow another creature of your choice as a Bonus Action, also calling it back as a Free Action. While it is following and hovering around a creature ( including yourself ), that creature gains an amount of {@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH} equal to half your proficiency bonus at the end of your turns. ( Up to a maximum count equal to your proficiency bonus. )

After becoming a Very Rare item you may make use of the Coil to release emergency discharges of energy , spending 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as a Reaction whenever a creature within the weapon's reach would be hit to increase their AC by a value equal to your proficiency bonus, possibly turning a hit into a miss.

subclassFeature.name: Immemorial Domain
entries: {@i A Cleric Subclass by the Undertomes}

Those who come to inherit the Immemorial Domain serve the Gods that have been wounded, forgotten by time and left out ot bleed. These Gods might want to incur their mighty wrath in vengeance for whatever has befallen them, or only wish to heal and live on, nevertheless their clerics are devoted to their own God’s healing, having grown to see the wounds in the very world they live in, the wear and tear of roads and each cut delivered upon a tree, so recklessly taken from just as the deity they follow.
Clerics of a God Immemorial are dutiful souls who wish only to grant their deity their due reprise, acting upon their will in a way that is often much more personal than most others in clergy.
Ozma

subclassFeature.name: Improved Embodied Cumulus
entries: At 10th level the tales your ink tells have grown and spread around your body. You gain an additional tattoo that you may pick from the original Embodied Cumulus list or the one below. These tattoos draw magical power from the same source as a bard's magic, and are treated as such for the sake of magic debilitation effects, such as an anti-magic field.

rows: Warring Skies

Red isn't enough to signify your power, so you wear the very concepts of battle on your arms. Whenever you would knock a creature {@condition Unconscious} or below one hit point, you gain one stack of {@condition Battle Ready|TheUndertomesDC}, to a maximum of 3. Additionally, you only lose a stack of {@condition Battle Ready|TheUndertomesDC} after inflicting {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} through Hemorrhaging, which also inflicts one additional stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Stormbearing Skies

The ink on your skin is a danger warning to any who would dare scratch it. As a reaction to when you would be targeted for an attack while the attacker is within your melee weapon reach, you may perform a melee weapon attack against them beforehand. If this attack hits, you gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn. This becomes a +3 to AC at 15th level. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Modifier.
Twilit Skies

Magic is a part of life like any other, and by engraving your skin with its language you learn how to make use of it. When you choose this tattoo, you may choose to learn any spell of 3rd level or lower from the Wizard Spell List. You may cast this spell once per long rest and either Strength or Dexterity are your spellcasting modifier for this, as your body fuels the necessary magic.
entries.caption: Improved Embodied Cumulus

subclassFeature.name: In Finely Ground Mistfall
entries: As an action, you get to raise your parasol in front of you and spin it, releasing a sharp storm of blood crystals in a 15 foot Cone. Every creature in this Cone must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they take {@dice 2d10} piercing damage and gains 2 stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, they take only half the damage and suffer no additional effects. If a creature that failed the saving throw was also the successful target of your Lead of the Parade ability, creatures attempting to hit them gains a +1 bonus to their attack and damage rolls on their first attack against them until the start of your next turn.

After a creature uses Bardic Inspiration, as a reaction, you may walk up to 15 feet and use this ability. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: In the Culprits Shoes
entries: People might call you a fool for your idealism and the rare methods you employ to learn about your fellow man, yet you know better than them that for the well-being of all this is all nescessary. Either through your own deductive skills and detailed explanation or through a device you've invented, you manage to reconstruct a course of action that happened inside a 60-ft cube around you, which molds to fit the room you are in. By using a very descriptive process or that machine, you and other creatures can see an illusion of what has happened inside that area for the past hour, using clues and details around the area to deduce so. To do this, you must spend at least ten minutes inside the area. If you've spent an hour inside that area or with each Glaring Clue (That is, a clue that DM determines already counts towards this) that you've collected you gain additional insight into the case, being able to deduce what happened within the space of an additional day per hour or Glaring Clue spent. You might get facts wrong as per the DM's discretion in cases such as another creature purposefuly planting evidence, to which you may pass an {@skill Investigation} DC to recognize as a fake or not. In such cases, the DC to be rolled is decided by the DM, who does not have to reveal if you have succeeded or failed this roll, instead only needing to describe what you perceive through your deduction.

subclassFeature.name: In the Name of Hatred!
entries: There are those moments where anyone simply cracks. Not all can withstand the weight of the worlds in their shoulders, and you have for so long! When you reach level 14th in this class, your arcana sometimes peeks past to reveal your true rage. While raging, when you have more than five {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG} stacks you may spend a free action to sink even deeper in your hatred, your body magically transforming to that of a decrepit-looking humanoid snake, your eyes bloodshot and obsessed, and your mouth sparking with the fires of your unrequited love. This form lasts until your rage is over, and during it your AC is only 10 + your Strength modifier, as you don't care about the hurt anymore. In addition, any of your attacks are much more devastating, dealing an additional {@dice 2d4} force damage on a hit, alongside the ability to change the damage type of your Brutal Criticals to force damage. While in this form, you may spend 4 stacks of {@condition Hysteria|TheUndertomesMG} to use {@skill Arcana} Slave.

entries.name: Arcana Slave.
entries: You may spend your action to let out a colossal, waste-laying beam of unrequited love and pure arcana at any meanies in your way. This line originates from you and is fifteen-feet wide, sixty-feet long, with any creature caught in its wake needing to pass a Charisma Saving Throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or suffer {@dice 8d10} force damage, or half on a success.

subclassFeature.name: In the Name of Love!
entries: When you choose this path at 3rd level, your latent quasi-bardic magic is beginning to manifest better, encompassing your weapons in the name of Love! When you enter rage, you may choose one weapon that you are wielding and transform it into a Magic Wand, the weapon morphing in a flash of light into the style you'd prefer, but maintaining any sharp edges and its general shape. While you are wielding your Magic Wand, as long as no other creature is suffering from the {@condition Villain|TheUndertomesMG} condition, the next creature you deal damage to suffers from being considered the {@condition Villain|TheUndertomesMG}.

While you can see or hear the {@condition Villain|TheUndertomesMG}, your near-sacred mission of protecting love takes hold of you. You gain a bonus to attack rolls equal to half your Proficiency Modifier against the creature and you deal your Strength modifier's worth of force damage instead of the usual damage type following your weapon on a hit.
Your Magic Wand morphs back into its original form when you finish raging.

subclassFeature.name: Indefinite Compression
entries: The act of compressing time could end catastrophically if mishandled, yet you have conquered that fear and learned the perfect means of handling such a fragile energy source indefinitely. Your {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesCC} count does not degrade below your proficiency bonus while you are out of combat.

Furthermore, during a long rest you can compress one spell into a small lightbulb, which can be crushed to cast the stored spell. The spell must be of 3rd level or lower, and any creature holding the lightbulb can use a bonus action to crush it and cast the spell. You can prepare a second lightbulb at 14th level and a third at 18th level. When you finish a long rest, the stored time in any previously prepared lightbulbs dissipates, causing them to lose their magical properties.

subclassFeature.name: Indomitable Pursuit
entries: There is nothing that will stop you from reaching your goals-not the pain, not the blood, not even the looming threat of death. You push forward, no matter how fractured you become. When you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you may use your Indomitable feature as a reaction to instead remain at 1 hit point until the start of your next turn, as you cling desperately to life.

After the rush fades, a deep fatigue takes hold. At the end of combat, you gain 1 level of exhaustion for every two times you took damage while remaining at 1 hit point through this feature (rounded down).

subclassFeature.name: Infinity Warp
entries: At 17th level, your control over the fabric of space has become unparalleled. You no longer have a distance limit between your rifts.

subclassFeature.name: Ink Over
entries: Upon reaching 7th level, you've perfected your slashes to a fine degree. You deal a +1 additional slashing damage on a melee weapon hit for each remaining attack you can perform during your turn. Additionally, if your last hit per inflicted {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you gain advantage on your next attack.

subclassFeature.name: Inner Ardor

entries.name: Precise Ignition.
entries: When you make a melee weapon attack, you inflict 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count, plus 1 additional count if the unmodified attack roll is 15 or higher.

entries.name: Ardent Techniques.
entries: You learn three Ardent Techniques from the Novice Ardent Techniques table. You learn one additional technique at 7th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level. Whenever you gain a fighter level, you can replace one technique you know with another technique available to you.

You gain 1 Ardor Point whenever you hit a creature or succeed on an ability check. Your Ardent Technique save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (chosen when you gain this subclass). You lose 1 Ardor Point for every minute in which you do not spend any Ardor Points.

entries.caption: Novice Ardent Techniques
rows: Red Kick
Attack

Make an unarmed melee attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage plus fire damage equal to its {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count, and it suffers additional Burn counts equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
Single Point Stab
Attack

Make an unarmed melee attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, it takes {@damage 2d4} piercing damage and has disadvantage on concentration checks until the end of your next turn. The next time before then that it makes a Constitution, Intelligence, or Wisdom saving throw, its current {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} damage triggers. This can trigger once per turn.
Stalwart Stance
Bonus Action
Varies

Spend Ardor Points equal to your proficiency bonus. Until the start of your next turn, whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack, it suffers {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts equal to the points spent. You also gain a bonus to Constitution saving throws equal to half the points spent, rounded down, until the start of your next turn (or for 1 minute outside combat).
Passionate Cheer
Bonus Action
Choose up to a number of creatures within 120 feet equal to your proficiency bonus. Until the end of your next turn, each gains a {@dice 1d4} bonus to attack rolls and ability checks.
Burning Knifehand
Free Action

Your next attack has advantage if its target has 6 or more {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts and deals additional slashing damage equal to a number of d8s equal to half the target's Burn count. An unattended object or structure instead takes {@damage 6d8} fire damage and suffers 6 Burn counts.
Flaming Fists
Free Action
Until the end of your turn, your melee attacks inflict additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
Warm Up
Reaction
When you make a saving throw or would suffer the charmed, frightened, or poisoned condition, gain a bonus to the saving throw equal to your proficiency bonus.
Flame Counter
Reaction

When you or a friendly creature within 5 feet is hit by a melee weapon attack, after damage is rolled, make a melee weapon attack against the attacker. On a hit, it suffers 1 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count. This attack cannot be a critical hit.

entries: You are proficient with attacks made as part of Ardent Techniques. You gain access to the Advanced list at 7th level and the Master list at 15th level. A technique with an activation time of Attack can replace one attack made as part of your Attack action or an opportunity attack.

subclassFeature.name: Inner Disharmony

entries: "Verily, I say unto you, the days spoken of in the Apocalypse are nigh!"

Ever since the first time you've opened your eyes you've awakened to the same thing, a world where touch warrants pain and your voice could be used to send that hurt far, far away from you, to build an invisible wall to hold back all of the fright that may come. Whenever you spend a Sorcerer spell slot you may channel that inner power to harmonize or disharmonize the air around you and the target, as per the following:

items: If you are targetting a hostile creature, on a success ( You hit or they fail a saving throw. ) you vibrate the arcane energies connecting you two to generate sparking vibrations in the air, granting yourself {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the spell slot level spent.

If you are targetting a friendly creature you may also spend up to your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to harmonize their thoughts with your own, inducing them to subconsciously fear the hands that will harm their bodies. That creature gains {@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH} count equal to half the {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} spent.

entries: Furthermore there is a host of knowledge that is simply engrained in your head that arises whenever necessary. You are considered to have Expertise on History checks pertaining to gaining knowledge, recalling information or practicing the laws that govern whatever region you are currently in or one that you have visited. This knowledge comes from you magically if you have never directly interacted with it, like small blurbs of text are flashing toward your eyes in-between moments of real life.
You also gain {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of Sorcery Points you spend whenever these are consumed.

subclassFeature.name: Inner Harmony

entries: "BABEL. BABEL. BABEL. BABEL. One man's hymns of praise became other men's curses. People spoke the same language, but could not understand each other..."

Upon reaching 18th level in this subclass, you must face a choice. Is this the world of your dreams? Is the order that you have craved for so, so long truly worth it? Does pain truly justify closing your heart in bricks and stone, so it may never be reached? Is a Heart's purpose insignificant in the greater view? If you have answered yes to all questions, gain the Citizenship Unto the Masses feature. If you have answered no to any questions, gain the Repudiation of the Tower feature.

subclassFeature.name: Iron Lotus
entries: Once per long rest, when you or a friendly creature is knocked unconscious, you can use your reaction to enter Iron Lotus. The state lasts until you are knocked unconscious and grants the following effects:

items: If you have 0 hit points, you regain 1 hit point. You then gain temporary hit points equal to your current hit points.
You suffer 10 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. These counts are removed only when you are knocked unconscious or when a friendly creature you can see dies.
Your attacks inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts and deal an additional {@damage 1d10} fire damage against creatures suffering from Burn.
Your Ardent Techniques cost half as many Ardor Points, rounded up.
A hostile creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of you suffers 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count.

Whenever a friendly creature within 30 feet is knocked unconscious, you gain a cumulative +1 bonus to attack rolls and saving throws and temporary hit points equal to half that creature's hit point maximum.
You have advantage on rolls against effects that would make you charmed, frightened, paralyzed, restrained, or stunned.

subclassFeature.name: Iron Stage Touches the Heart
entries: Anathema is what one would call you, yet you've grown unbothered by such words, for iron is only nature refined. Starting at 14th level, you may make full use of a Silkbound creatures multiattack feature, or if there are multiple Silkbound creatures you may make both attacks twice with that feature, or have both perform an action while only consuming your one action. When you summon a sole Hex Doll, you may choose to spend 2 Hex Points to inflict a ravaging curse unto them as a bonus action. When you do so, they suffer two stacks of {@condition Hexbind Curse|TheUndertomesCH|Curse} and gain a +2 modifier to hit and to their damage rolls, you also may choose for their attacks to deal necrotic damage instead.

In addition to that, you may spend 4 Hex Points and an action to make your Hex Doll happily dance around a creature within its melee attack reach, letting the putrid energy gather in its movements, forming a giant rusted iron nail above its heart. When you do this, you sever your connection to the Hex Doll, which now acts after its original target creature, taking the Dodge action and using their movement to chase the target in their prances, attempting to stay within 5-feet of them.

While your Hex Doll is severed like this, you may then spend another action to drive the iron nail through its heart in a grand finale, causing all the pent-up energy to explode in a Cursed miasma. All creatures within a 10-feet radius of the Doll must pass a Charisma Saving Throw or suffer the Hex Doll's original amount of Hit Die in necrotic damage and 4 Stacks of {@condition Hexbind Curse|TheUndertomesCH|Curse}, or take half the damage and Stacks on a success. If there were no attempts to reduce or otherwise limit the Doll's moving speed before it explodes, the creature it was following gains disadvantage and suffers the effects of the {@spell Bestow Curse} spell, chosen by you.

subclassFeature.name: Issued Weaponry
entries: You have a special kind of weapon for your duties, or most often than not, you can modify a previously existing one for your uses. Starting from 3rd level, when you choose this subclass, choose one of the weapon types below. On a long rest, you may spend your time to install special components onto a weapon, non-magical or otherwise, to shape it into a proper tool for your cleaning.

Weapons enhanced like this retain their damage die and usual properties, in addition to gaining other effects in accord to the table below and the weapons type. You may attune to this weapon during a long rest, including the one you create it. While attuned, you gain one stack of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you deal damage to another creature, to a maximum of 10 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and with all charges vanishing after combat. Outside combat, you may spend one minute tinkering with your tools to generate 4 stacks of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, which last for one more minute.

rows: Daggers

Everytime you deal damage to a creature, it also suffers one stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, as the daggers leave a trail of unstable space. A creature suffering from {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} take extra dice of damage whenever they're attacked equal to half their stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. The damage die are always the same as the highest damage dice in the attack that hit. The afflicted loses all stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when they are hit.
Axe

Once per turn, when you hit a creature you also tear its defenses asunder temporarily. It has a cumulative -1 penalty to its AC until the end of your next turn. The maximum penalty that can be suffered by this is equal to your Proficiency Modifier.
Spear

As a bonus action you may spend any number of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to grant one creature within your spears reach a {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Barrier, which is to say a number of d4 Temporary Hit Points equal to the amount spent, with the maximum {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} spendable at once being equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Longsword

When you hit a creature, they suffer one stack of {@condition Charge-Bind|TheUndertomesCL}, the torn space around where you swiped continuously forcing the creature to repeat its actions, slowing it down before space unwarps. {@condition Charge-Bind|TheUndertomesCL} deducts an amount to the afflicted's initiative score equal to each stack of {@condition Charge-Bind|TheUndertomesCL} on a given creature, it also deducts 5-feet from their movement speed times the {@condition Charge-Bind|TheUndertomesCL} value. All stacks are destroyed on the end of the afflicted's turn.
Gauntlets

When you would gain {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, gain one additional stack of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you're at max {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when you score a Critical Hit, deal an additional weapon die equal to your weapons damage.
entries.caption: Issued Weaponry

subclassFeature.name: Jolly Old Hunter
entries: With time and experience so comes the strengthening of bones broken numerous times. You gain Advantage on Constitution, Wisdom and Intelligence Saving Throws. Furthermore, you may push your body beyond its limits to change a failed Saving Throw into a Successful one, also taking no damage if you still would. Whenever you do this you suffer one Point of Exhaustion and may do so up to an amount of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Judgement Domain
entries: {@i A Cleric Subclass by the Undertomes}

Clerics from the Judgment Domain are guided by a simple command: exact the judgment of their god in their stead. They do not discern themselves what is right and what is wrong, they simply follow the teachings of their faith and pass on the decisions of their divine onto others. Carrying an emerald tablet of commands and principles, they read from it for guidance and record the doings of the creatures they see so that their god may be aware of the actions that transpire on the mortal realm. They are executors of law, first and foremost.

subclassFeature.name: Kindling for the Mind
entries: A steady mind is as important as a strong body. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Athletics, Acrobatics, History, Investigation, or Survival.

subclassFeature.name: Kindred Domain
entries: The weight of a pious soul is a heavy one to bear, yet Clerics who follow their Kindred will do so without complaint, weaving their own blood drawn from self-flaggelation to wash away the sins of their fellows, no matter what terrible pain they may have to endure. Kindred Domain clerics can come in a grand amount of variety, some using literal blood, sweat and tears to fuel their holy rituals, others channeling their own soil to aid others, and some even taking the pain of their fellows literally; Yet one thing connects them all, the need to bear a cross in the name of those they love. In the Forgotten Realms, most Gods who value companionship may hold the Kindred Domain, yet in particular some scant few followers of Lathander take the mantle of Kindred Clerics, attempting to hold onto their own virtue while lifting their fellow worshippers, no matter how much this vision of perfection may cost them. In other worlds such as Eberron, the Kindred Domain sometimes isn't held by those who have faith in a God, but those who have faith in themselves and who beckon the faith of others, roving warlords and those who wish for more power to their own, willing to endure such suffering to reach it.

subclassFeature.name: Kindred Domain: Ravenous Strikes
entries: You are starved with an obsessive might in battle. Starting at 8th level, when a creature takes Radiant or Piercing damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can change its damage type to become Necrotic. Once you deal this damage you recover hit points equal to half its value, rounded down. You can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn and you may use this feature an amount of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining spent uses during a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Knight's Greatsword Form

entries: "No casualties, minimum collateral damage… that was perfect. Hey, if this story gets out, who knows? Maybe some important folks of the City might be hiring us for those dominion protection jobs.."
You become an avatar of protection and comfort, empowered by the desperate pleads of those in need. As a Bonus Action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: Your AC increases by 2.

You have Advantage on attack rolls against creatures that tried to attack you last turn, and whenever you would hit a creature that has attacked a creature other than you during their last turn you may spend one count of {@condition Defensive Stance|TheUndertomesPRT} to have that attack become a Critical Hit against them. This Critical Hit only affects damage, and does not trigger additional effects such as that of a Vorpal Sword.
If a creature of your choice within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can use your reaction for them to reroll it. They must use the new roll.
Your movement speed cannot be reduced under 20-ft.
If you are wielding a weapon that has the Heavy or Two-Handed properties, it gains the Reach property if it didn't have it already.
Whenever you would deal damage to a creature, you inflict an additional 3 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: L'ascesa del Vice-capitano

entries: "Hierarchy is absolute for the Thumb. To us, it's as natural as the fact of nature that spilt blood only flows downwards, not up."

Hardly just some soldier anymore, you've managed to reach a position of some importance within your organization - A trusted steward to actual captains, a high-achiever between your ilk or even simply a dreadfully good shot. Upon reaching this level, you gain a Feature equivalent to the Feature chosen at 3rd level and may do the following during your turn:

entries.name: Custode della Regola.
entries: You are both beholder and beholdent of the Rules of your organization, and also the acting executor of every single line. Once per long rest you may spend your Action to rally your comrades, granting all creatures of your choice within 60-ft. that can understand you a +2 bonus modifier to hit and double that value to damage rolls until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: La Spada di Palermo

entries: "... But she took me in and put a roof over my head. Fed me. Taught me this... bloody incredible swordfighting style-the sort a lowly vagrant like me would never have had the chance to learn."

The Palermitan Style of Swordplay is an art form that you've got etched deep in your bones, your muscles swerving in pendulum arcs as naturally as you draw out your opponent's breath. This is done through dual weapons, allowing you to make perfected use of Two-Weapon Fighting:

items: You may wield two weapons without the prerequisite of one of them being Light, instead only requiring that neither weapon is Heavy.

Whenever you make an {@action Attack} as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules you still add half your ability modifier to the damage dealt. Whenever you do so, you inflict one count of {@condition Severed Tendons|TheUndertomesSP|Severed Tendon} on your target.
When you Attune to a pair of magical weapons, they both count as a singular Attunement, taking only one slot and becoming Unattuned if either Attunement is broken.

entries: Additionally you may use once per turn the Force Into an Adequate Question attack in place of one of your Attacks as part of the Attack Action or Bonus Action. You may do so an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

entries.name: Force Into an Adequate Question
entries: You perform a swirling flurry of blows that aim not to hit the target, but instead funnel them toward a better positioning for you to benefit from. You perform an attack roll against the target, dealing damage as usual on a hit and having them instantly move up to 15-ft. in a line of your choice, or only 5-ft. on a missed attack roll. You instantly move to follow them. You both must move into unoccupied spaces and will not directly move into a space that would directly harm them, such as blazing ground or off a cliff.

subclassFeature.name: Launching Maneuver [始動]

entries: "No flower ever endures the fall... or so they say."

You can use a bonus action to leap up to a distance equal to your remaining movement speed. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. After you use this bonus action, your speed is reduced by the distance you travelled until the end of the turn.

If you land within 5 feet of a creature, or pass within 5 feet of a creature during this leap, you can make one unarmed strike against that creature as part of the same bonus action. On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to one additional roll of your Martial Arts die.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest. Additionally, vou you always try to separate some time for your studies. Once per Long Rest, you can choose a Language, a Tool or a Skill to become proficient with until your next Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Lead of the Parade
entries: As the centerpiece, you must know how to draw attention and awe from your peers, allowing the envy and jealousy to fester in their hearts and turn that into aggressive power. You gain expertise in the {@skill Performance} skill if you didn't already have it.

As a bonus action, you can choose a creature that you can see in front of you and roll a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check against their presence DC (CR + 10). If you pass, whenever {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is applied to them until the start of your next turn, that number +1 is applied instead. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with a damaging spell or it fails a saving throw, they gain 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and 1 stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Legerdemain

entries: Listen, you sure you can stand after this?

A decayed bark grows above your skin in different areas of your body, which gives you a withered appearance, if not for the gleaming fruits that also sprout from them at will.
