You gain advantage on {@skill Stealth} ability checks performed on the outside or anywhere where the presence of {@skill nature} would not be questioned.

Additionally, you can use a bonus action to feed one of your fruits to a creature within 5 feet of you. If they’re unwilling, they must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC to push you off. If they eat the fruit, until your next long rest you always instinctively know where they are, as long as they are within the same plane of existence as you.

You can use a bonus action to burst the fruit within them, and choose whether it recovers {@dice 1d4} hit points or if the creature suffers 1 count of {@condition Maggots|TheUndertomesASV} as it ruptures. This number becomes {@dice 2d4} and 2 at level 5, {@dice 3d4} and 3 at level 11 and {@dice 4d4} and 4 at level 17. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Let All Blossom Free

entries: "Let us see if humans can continue to insist on such 'righteousness' were they plagued by the same yearning that ails us."

Your blood empowers your kin to be freed from all shackles of this world. You can spend Bloodfeast equal to the amount in the Conditions table below to immediately cure that condition from a creature within 30 feet of you:

entries.caption: Conditions
rows: {@condition Blinded} (Must not be missing this body part)
{@condition Charmed}
{@condition Deafened} (Must not be missing this body part)
5 (for each point of Exhaustion)
Exhaustion
{@condition Frightened}
{@condition Grappled}
{@condition Paralyzed}
{@condition Poisoned}
{@condition Prone}
{@condition Restrained}
{@condition Stunned}

entries: Additionally, there is a desire on your blood to continue the family and protect those you have sired. As an action, you can bite into a willing creature, transforming them into a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} after a minute. The creature's race becomes {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} (Tome of Oblivion), and they become your immediate Kindred. Your Kindred are naturally inclined to listen and obey your demands, as if under the {@condition Charmed} condition, however, you cannot utter commands that would directly harm them, as you wish for their safety and protection as their sire. Instead of two, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} you sire this way can choose up to 3 Blood Arts, but they must consume blood from a living creature at least once per day or take {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage that cannot be resisted or healed in any way.

entries.name: Variant Hardblood Arts 8 - Split Apart.
entries: Once you witness vampires or {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} having completely lost their minds due to the hunger and the repression of their base instincts, turning into murderous, psychopathic beasts; or if you have a Bloody Barber Artificer in your party, this ability becomes available. As a bonus action for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as another bonus action, your Lance transforms into a giant pair of scissors. These scissors retain all Hardblood properties your Lance would have, except their damage changes to {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and increases to {@damage 2d4} at Rank I, {@damage 2d6} at Rank II, and {@damage 3d8} at Rank III. Additionally, after hitting a creature with your pair of scissors, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition Restrained} by bloody threads until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Lifestew Domain

entries: "Salutations!!!!!! I implore thee to try this soup!!!!"

None are more warm-hearted and kind than the ones who follow the Lifestew Domain, focused on hailing the ancient {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesLS|Basillisoups}'s word of keeping anyone and everyone well fed through cold winters and harsh famines alike. A member of the Lifestew Domain usually starts out working to aid in their soup-kitchen bases, yet adventures call to them like a second nature, looking both for new ingredients they can bolster their order with or hungry mouthes to taste the delights of Dragonstew!

In some realms such as Faerun, the clerics of this domain ride along the sword coast in their mighty chariot-train pulled by the very divine beasts that they consider so beloved, aiding any settlement they come across and bringing a happiness unlike no other to the festivals of the world, being sought after to calm down and pacify even the most starve-crazed monsters and bandit groups, one of their main tenets being that all creatures deserve to be well-fed in the end.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Lifestew Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell animal friendship}, {@spell catapult|XGE}
3rd
{@spell Aganazzar's scorcher|XGE}, {@spell flaming sphere}
5th
{@spell elemental weapon}, {@spell Leomund's tiny hut}
7th
{@spell dominate beast}, {@spell polymorph}
9th
{@spell awaken}, {@spell conjure elemental}

entries.name: Dragonstew Kitchen
entries: Among the countless cookbooks you've memorized and holy precepts that were gotten to an art, you've also attained the skill to unite both in the divine objective of keeping a belly fed. As such, you know a ritual to summon a {@item Basillisoup Ladle|TheUndertomesLS} that you're proficient in during a long rest, which remains with you until its destroyed, lost or you summon another one, where the old one vanishes. You may use this Ladle as a holy symbol.

Furthermore, you've also mastered the art onto preparing enchanted food to give poor souls their deserved nourishment no matter what; Whenever you deal fire damage to a friendly creature who has the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} condition, they instead ignore fire Resistance or Immunity and heal the target by half the damage dealt, as they have a chance to consume the food flying at them.

A creature may benefit from this only once per turn. When you apply {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} through a Ladle ( By attacking with it or using it to cast your Cleric Spells ), they are instead healed by half the hit points they would suffer as per the Condition's fire damage.

entries.name: Sanctified Cook
entries: In a kitchen you are a ruler, the kitchen utensils being your noble knights to serve as you will. You gain proficiency in Cook's Utensils and during a short rest you may prepare a feast for your allies, be it a good old Dragonstew or even varying with a Dracopie, either ways your delicious food grants them the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} condition until the next short or long rest, alongside a number of {@dice d4} temporary hit-points equal equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. These temporary hit-points last until {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} wears off.
Upon reaching 6th level your cooking improves, causing a {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} creature to gain Resistance against the Fire and at 12th level, Cold damage as well.

subclassFeature.name: Locked Potential

entries: "As the Prescript commands-my blade strikes."

The Living Will has graced you with presence beyond direct communication, permeating your arms and weapons to fully envelop you as an instrument of your whims. After you have spent all your Warlock spell slots and if you've spent them without casting any given spell more than once since your last short rest, you enter a Blade Unlocked state until your next short rest. While in this state, gain the following:

items: Whenever you would deal damage through melee attacks, you may choose to have its type be force damage instead of its original type.
Any Cantrips you use deal additional damage to hostile targets equal to half your Warlock level, rounded down. While in this state, they count toward ascending from the Will's Paper Slip III.

At the start of your turns, roll a d4 as of the Will's Paper Slip I effect. You gain a +2 bonus modifier to hit until the end of your turn, as long as the attack would deal the resulting type of damage.

subclassFeature.name: Lone Stand on the Crimson Garden
entries: The struggles of battle and scars of many past events have shaped your road, yet through it all you remain with your head held high and proud. As such, it is much harder for you to fall than most, only becoming a tougher opponent as a fight goes on: You deal an additional d8 divine damage on your melee attack and spell attack hits for each 20 Maximum Hit Points you have missing from your total to a maximum of {@dice 5d8}.

Furthermore, once per month you may instantly revive yourself when you would die, healing half your Maximum Hit Points and ending any Conditions on yourself. If you do so outside of combat or after it ends you instantly suffer 5 points of Exhaustion after reviving, as crystallized blood sprouts around your limbs like the scales of a dragon from the sudden manifestation of your power.

subclassFeature.name: Lonely Nullification

entries: Her stories are poisonous things. They infiltrate all those who surround and listen, leading them into an unbearable world.

Time has indeed taken it’s toll, yet it will take no more in respect of you and your tales. This is how your life was meant to be, and you will keep living as long as you have a tale to tell, gaining the following effects:

items: You do not age past your elderly years, becoming unable to die by natural causes.
Your form cannot change without your will to do so, as the body that has carried you so far will never be allowed to be forgotten.

Your memory cannot be truly altered. If another effect would cause it to be, you remember any altered memories as if a tale removed from you while safekeeping your old ones, being aware of which is which.
Whenever :solitude: Solitude ends on a target, you are healed by {@dice 1d8} hit points as the satisfaction of someone else having went through your tale washes over you.

You can briefly summon the visage of creatures you have seen, met and talked to inside an unoccupied space of your Mist as an Action. You have the Summoned Visage perform an Action or Bonus Action of their creature sheet before vanishing into thin air. The creature’s CR must be of equal value to or lower than your Bard Level - 3. You may also do this to summon one of your party members whose Visage performs a weapon attack or cantrip against a target of your choice. If you have used this ability, you cannot use it on your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Lord of Needleworks Otherworldly Patron
entries: Many people turn toward the dark arts for some ancient, unknowable piece of information that can take them above the rest - Becoming Warlocks to fearsome beings all in pursuit of that power! Those who have forged a pact bearing a name of the Lord of Needleworks have chosen a different path, one of bearing that name for themselves, of becoming the very Lord to rule over their kin!

These are borderline maniacal, driven people whose endeavours toward creation can bring them and their entourage to the ends of the world, at their best being eccentric geniuses of their craft that work with such passion that it'd make a grown Artificer cry. At their worst, though, these Warlocks become tyrants capable of amassing armies for their single-minded purpose in life.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms these are the very few people who have learnt the magic of fey contracts and conscripted their own servants toward an otherworldly craft, while in others akin to the ever blazing world of Balefire have taken up their needles to strip down gods of their flesh in pursuit of making the perfect fabric.

subclassFeature.name: Loser's Penalty

entries: "I don't play with folks who don't trust me."

Playing games is a part of your essence, it's who you are, and sharing the fun you have in those moments is what you seek to do as a toymaker. As a Bonus Action, you can challenge a willing creature to a game, or force an unwilling creature to play if they fail a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC as long as they aren't Immune to the {@condition Charmed} condition.

A game consists of a challenge explicitly defined by you. It can range from avoiding to take a certain amount of damage in combat, rock paper scissors, not being the last player hunting in tag, a best of three on a game of dice, a simple endurance test etc.

A game cannot last more than a day and usually ends once you tale a Short or Long Rest, unless agreed otherwise by you and your DM. The challenge must not be impossible to be beaten by any of the parties, as that is the fair spirit of haunted games.
The creature that wins the game can choose one of the following benefits until their next Long Rest:

items: You gain advantage on any ability checks and saving throws against the losing creature.
You gain {@dice 1d10} Temporary Hit Points whenever you hit the losing creature with an attack.
The losing creature drops one piece of weapon or armor of your choice.
The losing creature has to give you {@dice 3d10*50} gold coins (as long as it has that amount, or as much as possible).
The losing creature gains disadvantage on all ability checks and saving throws related to you.
The losing creature takes 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever it is hit by an attack.
The losing creature cannot willingly lie to you, and has to answer one of your questions truthfully to the best of its abilities as long as it is with a "yes" or "no".
The losing creature is hit by your pins and needles, suffering 4 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesHT}.

entries: Additionally, whenever you personally kill a creature, you gain 2 Souls instead of 1.

subclassFeature.name: Loyalty
entries: Starting on level 3, you can roll {@dice 1d6} in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strike, which now also count as Heavy Weapons. When you hit a creature, you can choose to make them roll a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or be pushed back 5 feet.

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition Unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until the end of the first round of combat. Whenever you hit an enemy with a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, they gain 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency on Painter's Supplies for the sake of carving magic tattoos on yourself and others.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Bullets

entries: "The vows of your contract are clear - pull the trigger and shoot to kill, for your bullet shall never miss its mark."

As the main benefit of your pact with the Marksman, you receive a magical ranged weapon called a Marksman's Weapon that serves as the instrument of your will. You can summon or dismiss this weapon as a free action, and it takes the shape of a two-handed ranged weapon of your choice, such as a bow or rifle. It uses the statistics of a {@item longbow|PHB|Longbow}, with which you are proficient. While wielding it, you can cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK} by expending one of your warlock spell slots.

This weapon comes loaded with a revolving chamber of seven Magic Bullets, each engraved with a number and increasingly potent magic. At the start of combat, the First Magic Bullet is always slotted. Once per turn, you can rotate the chamber to select a higher-numbered bullet, such as moving from the First to the Fourth, but you cannot move from a higher-numbered bullet to a lower-numbered one. When you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK|Magic Bullet Fire} while a Magic Bullet is slotted, the spell gains the corresponding effect:

entries.caption: Seven Magic Bullets
rows: The 1st Magic Bullet
A creature within range takes force damage equal to your warlock level, or half as much on a successful saving throw.
The 2nd Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw is {@condition Incapacitated|PHB} until the end of its next turn.
The 3rd Magic Bullet

The width of the spell's line increases by 10 feet, and the line becomes 30 feet longer. A creature that fails this saving throw suffers 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and has the damage it deals reduced by half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, until the end of your next turn.
The 4th Magic Bullet
Whenever a creature that fails this saving throw takes damage before the end of its next turn, it suffers 1 count of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesMK}.
The 5th Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw has its AC reduced by half your proficiency bonus until the end of your next turn.
The 6th Magic Bullet

All creatures within range must repeat this saving throw once for every combined 7 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count among all targets before the spell was cast. A creature that fails one of these saving throws takes {@damage 2d10} force damage and suffers 3 counts of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesMK} instead.
The 7th Magic Bullet

A creature that fails this saving throw takes a number of {@damage 1d10 + 1} force damage rolls and suffers a number of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesMK} counts equal to your warlock level. It is vulnerable to force damage for this attack and until the end of your turn. A creature automatically fails this spell's saving throw unless it expends a Legendary Resistance. You take the same damage and {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesMK} count, which cannot be reduced by any means.

entries: When you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK|Magic Bullet Fire}, the chamber automatically rotates to the next bullet, if able. At 6th level, you can cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK|Magic Bullet Fire} at 1st level without expending a spell slot. At 14th level, you can instead cast it at 2nd level without expending a spell slot.

If you die because of the Seventh Magic Bullet and are returned to life by any means other than {@spell true resurrection|PHB|True Resurrection}, you return with 5 levels of exhaustion, which can be reduced only one level at a time by finishing a long rest.
Any expended Magic Bullets are recreated when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Magical Tailoring
entries: By now, you've learned more than one great trick for your needlework, and you know how to put that to practice along other tiny inventions.
Upon reaching 9th level, you may, with your {@item weaver's tools|PHB|Weaver's Tools} in hand, imbue any piece of clothin with the following traits:

items: The piece of clothing may be touched by its wearer through a bonus action to start or stop emitting a bright light for 15-feet and a dim light for an additional 15-feet.
The piece of clothing may play a song without lyrics when tapped, which can be heard for up to 30-feet away. This song may be up to three minutes long.
At its wearer's will, this piece of clothing may start billowing as if put against a light breeze, become moist as if it entered a body of water or dry up instantly.

You may choose static effects to appear within the piece of clothing, this effect can be picture, up to 40 words of text, lines and shapes, or a mixture of these elements, as you like. You may also choose to make small effects appear around the piece of clothing, such as sparks of lightning or a constant dripping of an illusory liquid.

entries: Additionally, when you do this during a short or long rest, you may further enchant this piece of clothing, with the limit that you can only enchant clothingin this way for a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. You may choose one enchantment presented below for each piece of clothing:

items: You may grant the wearer five of their hit dice as temporary Hit Points that last until reduced or until your next short or long rest. When taking damage while there are Temporary Hit Points remaining, the wearer is considered to have vulnerability against fire damage as it burns away the clothingm, but any damage remaining after the clothing is destroyed is negated.
You may grant the wearer the traits of one of your Hardblood Accesories

entries: When a piece of clothing you've created or enchanted through Magical Tailoring or {@subclassFeature Fashionista's Supplies|artificer|TCE|Bloody Barber|TheUndertomesBB|3|TheUndertomesBB} is destroyed, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit and to damage against the creature who caused its destruction until the end of your next turn, as rage fills you for such diselegance.

subclassFeature.name: Magnum Opus: Tibia

entries: "What do you see... in this piece? I am curious to hear your impressions."

Your very own body gave birth to the skeletal artifact resting in your hands. It is a Martial Melee weapon that you are considered Attuned with at all times. It counts as a magic item for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and it usually takes the shape of a large sword made out of bones, a complete extension of your old body. It deals {@damage 1d8} slashing damage, has the Reach property, inflicts 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and you may choose to use your Intelligence modifier for its attack and damage rolls.

This weapon is considered an Artifact and can only be destroyed upon a century passing after your death. If it is lost - no, it must never be. Your sole mission must be to keep your Magnum Opus on your person the entire time. You will gain an anxious obsession to recover it otherwise, and will not be able to focus on anything else, gaining disadvantage on any ability checks unrelated to finding it, but advantage on all ability checks related to finding it.
Over the course of a Long Rest, you may spend an amount of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} equal to your Proficiency Modifier to permanently upgrade it, as per the following:

items: Your attack and damage rolls with your Magnum Opus increase by +1. When you take it again, it increases by +1 again, to a maximum of +3.
You inflict an additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on enemies that you hit. Whenever you take this again, you inflict an additional count.
Your Magnum Opus's damage becomes {@damage 1d10}. When you take it again, it becomes {@damage 1d12}.
Your Reach extends by 5 feet and the range of all of your abilities extends by 10 feet. When you take it again, both increase by 5 and 10 feet more respectively.
Rolls of 19 or 20 are considered Critical hits for the purpose of your skills that require Critical Hits. When you take this upgrade again, that number becomes 18.

You can strip a magical weapon bare and feed its scraps to your Magnum Opus over the course of a long rest. The magical item used is permanently destroyed and your Magnum Opus gains its properties, such as a Vorpal Sword's Vorpal enchantment, but not any increases to attack and damage rolls. You may only benefit from a single magical weapon consumed like this at any given time, needing to strip your work to fit another weapon if you wish to do so.

You can use a Bonus Action to point your Magnum Opus at a creature and give them advantage on their next ability check, attack roll or saving throw. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

After you hit a creature with an attack you can use a Reaction to tear away some of the creature's flesh. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. Creatures {@condition frightened} this way always suffer an additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever it is inflicted and may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turn, ending the effect on a success. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

You can use a Bonus Action to pose with your Magnum Opus. Choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute. Creatures that are fighting you have advantage on this saving throw. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

You can use an Action to extend your weapon and ensnare someone. Choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become Grappled by you and your weapon for 1 minute, and your movement speed is not halved due to the Grapple. Creatures Grappled this way may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

As an Action, you may cleave your Magnum Opus across a 15-foot cone in front of you. Every creature in this cone must make a Dexterity saving throw. For any creature that fails the save, choose an order. The first one to fail the save takes {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage, the second takes {@damage 2d6}, and this continues to a maximum of {@damage 4d6} Slashing damage. Every creature that failed the save also suffers 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, they only take half damage and suffer no additional effects.

You may use an Action to thrust your Magnum Opus forward in a 30 foot line. Any creature within that line must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding}. {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead causes the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the previous Condition and 2 stacks are removed every time it is triggered. The {@skill Medicine} Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

As part of your attack action, you may attempt a vertical attack roll against a creature within Reach. On a hit, they take the damage they normally would and fall {@condition Prone}. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

As an Action, you may spend 3 {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} to attempt to immobilize a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition restrained} for 1 minute. Creatures {@condition restrained} this way may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. (lvl 9)

As an Action, you enlarge your sword, making it pierce everything in a 30-foot line. Creatures within that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take {@damage 5d8} Piercing damage and gain disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws for 1 minute unless they're healed. This cannot be removed while the creature suffering from it is {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}. On a successful save, a creature only takes half the amount of damage and suffers no additional effects. (lvl 9)

As an Action, you shoot a tendon from your sword to wrap around another creature. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become puppeteered by you. Immediately after failing this saving throw and on your subsequent turns, you may spend a Bonus Action to force the creature to perform any Action it is able to for you on any target within reach. They may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. You can only use this ability once per Short or Long Rest. (lvl 9)

As part of your attack action with your Magnum Opus, you may attempt to hit a creature in a vital spot. They must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition paralyzed} until the end of your next turn. You can only use this feature once per creature per combat. (lvl 9)

As part of your attack action with your Magnum Opus, you gut the creature in front of you. They must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or suffer 1 point of {@condition exhaustion}. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest. (lvl 9)

You pierce your Magnum Opus on the floor, extending its bones underground to hit every creature of your choice within 20 feet of you. The area becomes Difficult Terrain for creatures that are not a part of the Ring and the targets must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d6} Piercing damage and suffer 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and you may spend 3 {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} so that the next attack against each of the affected creatures is done with advantage. On a successful save, they take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. You can only use this ability once per Short or Long Rest. (lvl 9)

Immediately after you kill a creature, you may add parts of its corpse to your Magnum Opus, gaining access to one of their Actions. You can only have 2 different creature actions at a time with this ability. (lvl 15)

As an Action, you can target a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you and extend your Magnum Opus to reach for it. If they have 50 hit points or fewer, they instantly die. Otherwise, they must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 10d8} Piercing damage, suffer 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and are immediately pulled towards you. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. You can only use this ability once per Short or Long Rest. (lvl 15)

entries: You may take each upgrade only once, with the exception of being able to take upgrades marked by your Magnum Opus an additional time upon reaching 5th and 15th levels in Artificer. You are aware that a crowded piece that attempts to convey everything at once is heard by none, so your maximum amount of upgrades is equal to your Known Infusions count and you may exchange an existing one with the same process of creating one. Whenever this feature asks for a saving throw, the Save DC is equal to your Artificer Spell Save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Make a Scene // Elsewhere
entries: A good killer is one that knows when to aid a friend in need, or to have an useful tool help you later. Upon reaching 9th level, you've acquired a knack to making a scene while not being directly involved with it. You may do so as an action, the way you do this differs from scenario from scenario, such as swiftly unscrewing a pork from a merchants cart and causing a ruckus on the market, or throwing a spider onto a guards armor with them noticing way too late. You make a {@skill Deception} skill check with advantage against a DC your DM checks to cause this chaos, which may be decided following the Dungeon Master's Guide's example of levels of difficulty in a check.

On a success, you and any friendly creatures of your choice within a 15-feet radius of you gain advantage to their next rolls as if you had granted them the Help action. On a failure, roll a d4 for a Disaster to happen:

entries.caption: Distraction Disaster Table
rows: {@b Accidents Happen.} Oh no, something exploded or fell right on your face. You and all creatures within a 10-feet radius of yourself must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer a number of d10 bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half on a success.

{@b Suddenly, Fire.} Something has caught fire, and of course it is quickly spreading. An area of 15 times your Proficiency Bonus becomes difficult terrain as its engulfed by an inferno. Any creature who enters this area or ends their turn in it suffers {@damage 1d8} fire damage.

{@b Too Much-Too much!} All the chaos around you all doesn't help, instead having the contrary effect. All the creatures that would be chosen to benefit from this instead have disadvantage on their next roll.
{@b Nothing..?} Nothing happens. Except that one person of the DM's choice notices it was you who did this act.

subclassFeature.name: Manuale in Maturazione

entries: "{@i exhale} What'd I tell you? Other styles ain't keepin' up with how fast the Palermitan style accelerates in a duel."

As a fight rages on your body becomes a better and better blade to cut down your quarry, tempered in bloodshed and moved by sheer willpower. You gain additional effects per each passing round in combat:

items: {@b 2nd Round.} You gain an additional 5-ft. of movement speed.

{@b 3rd Round.} Your Armor Class increases by a bonus modifier of 1 and you may now spend your Bonus Action to perform two melee weapon attacks instead, but you inflict one less count of any Condition you would inflict and do not add your ability modifier to their damage rolls. ( If you would deal greater than 2 counts of any Condition, you deal only half instead. )
{@b 4th Round.} You gain an additional 5-ft. of movement speed.
{@b 5th Round.} Your attacks deal an additional Condition count whenever you would inflict them through melee weapon attacks.

entries: These effects are cumulative and end alongside a combat. Additionally, your knowledge-gathering ability has extended beyond simply going through the motions in a short-term manner, instead also focusing on amassing the needed knowledge to support your general repertoire. You gain proficiency in one Skill of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Marksman
entries: Starting from when you take this pact, your knowledge about guns has been vast enough that you feel comfortable with nearly any type of firearm. You gain proficiency in Marksman Weapons, which are detailed at the end of this document.

Additionally, you gain a pool of Ammunition that equals your Proficiency Bonus * 2, ( Proficiency Bonus will be shortened and referred to as PB going forward in this document ) which serves to fuel your firing using Marksman Weapons and other skills in this subclass. When you would deal damage using a Marksman Weapon by spending Ammunition, it deals one additional damage die equal to the first die size presented, such as dealing {@dice 2d8} piercing damage plus {@dice 1d4} fire damage having an increase of {@dice 1d8} piercing damage.
You regain spent Ammunition on a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Marksman Otherworldly Patron
entries: A warlock who makes a pact with the Marksman is ready to put their life on the line for one simple thing: power, even if they must ultimately pay the final cost.

The Marksman is a deity focused on hunting its targets with ever-perfected precision, infusing a fraction of its ability into magic bullets given to its warlocks, usually in exchange for their lives after a certain number of bullets have been used. The Marksman is usually found in a setting as a serious and cold patron, murmured about through the back alleys of large cities where a person goes missing every other day.

subclassFeature.name: Marksman's Smoking Pipe
entries: Your patron has granted you a replica of one of its prized possessions, a smoking pipe from which you can inhale to sharpen your senses greatly. If this magical item ceases to be in contact with you, it teleports to your hand or the nearest available space, such as inside a backpack you are wearing. As a bonus action, you can take a drag from the pipe, gaining {@dice 1d4} + half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, in {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

While out of combat, the smoke aids you in sharpening your senses, granting a bonus to {@skill Perception}, {@skill Investigation}, and one skill of your choice with which you are proficient, chosen when you gain this feature. The bonus equals half your current {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, rounded down, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. You choose when to add this bonus, and all {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on you is removed after a successful roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, and regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Meal of a Lifetime
entries: You've learnt how to become the best chef possible, a true believer and follower of the Lifestew. As such, you gain the following:

items: You may throw up to two ingredients from your Spice of Life feat into your Stew Cauldron per long rest instead of one.

When you consume your True Dragonlife Stew, you may dedicate a portion of it to the great {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesLS|Basillisoups}. Because of the greatness you've achieved with the pieces of food you make, a mighty {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesLS} appears on the same square as you, having you ride it valiantly into battle. It takes it's turn alongside yours in Initiative, where you may have it move as a free action and spend your action or bonus action to command it to take one of its own. You may spend your reaction for it to take a reaction of its own when triggered.

subclassFeature.name: Means of Cultivation

entries: "Grow your knowledge. Use exams to motivate and push yourselves further. Only then shall you one day be permitted an audience with the Saints."

Upon reaching 3rd level in Monk, choose which way you will proceed to acquire your knowledge with - a perception-bending key to your knowledge or to hold and tear it off with your bare hands. You gain the chosen 3rd level feat and a corresponding one upon reaching 11th level.

entries.subclassFeature: To Grasp Erudition With One's Own Hands (Fist)|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesCE|3
To Behold Light Through a Gilded Keyhole (Key)|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesCE|3

subclassFeature.name: Melting Love

entries: It could barely speak a word or two. It was also mentally unstable. It became extremely nervous whenever Marie was not present.

You’ve learnt how to weave the feelings of one’s heart and harness that sentimental energy like a catalyst for your powers, letting it seep out of the poor bastards infatuated by you as if sweat covering their nervous brows as you make them do your bidding. A creature {@condition Charmed} by you through any means suffers from a pink slime starting to seep from their pores, unable to even notice this congealed feeling sprouting from them. While they are {@condition Charmed}, you may spend your action to order them to perform a weapon attack they are able to against another creature within reach, such as a Soldier swinging their longsword or a Worg bite down another being. You may also order them to move up to half their movement speed in a direction of your choice, with the creature rationalizing this course of action as a necessary one for the sake of your love.
Furthermore, when you trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} against a {@condition Charmed} creature, you gain a count of Heart Robbed.

Heart Robbed is a Condition that bolsters your heart with a superhuman confidence and mental resilience, granting you a +1 bonus modifier on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws, alongside granting {@dice 1d6} temporary hit points when you receive a count of the Condition.

You may grant up to three Heart Robbed count to another creature as part of your bonus action to grant them your Bardic Inspiration. Furthermore, if a creature has benefited from it’s Immunity against being {@condition Charmed} against you before your next attempt to Charm them bypasses their Immunity, as your love melts into their heart like an acid.
Any Heart Robbed count remaining at the end of combat is lost.

subclassFeature.name: Melting Pinion
entries: Your turbulent emotions eat at you whenever you use your power, but you keep clinging to your life and desires. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Passive Effect
entries: While you are in Volatile State, when you take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to scream. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, taking thunder damage equal to the psychic damage rolled on a failure, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Wound of Sorrow.
entries: You can expend a spell slot of 7th level or higher to fire a blazing beam in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide line. Each hostile creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 10d8} fire damage and suffering 10 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts on a failure, or half as much damage and half as many counts on a success. You can expend up to 3 Volatile Passion counts to deal an additional {@damage 2d10} fire damage per count. Before firing, you can gain up to 5 Volatile Passion counts, taking {@damage 2d6} psychic damage per count gained. Before a creature that failed its save takes the damage, it loses fire resistance for 1 minute, or fire immunity becomes fire resistance for 1 minute.

entries.name: Defensive Stance
Supraheat.
entries: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to make the attack a critical hit against you. This damage cannot reduce you below 1 hit point. You then gain a pool equal to the damage taken, which you can spend until the end of combat to regain spell slots according to the Supraheat Spell Conversion table.

entries.caption: Supraheat Spell Conversion
rows: 1st-level spell slot
2nd-level spell slot
3rd-level spell slot
4th-level spell slot
5th-level spell slot
6th-level spell slot
7th-level spell slot
8th-level spell slot
9th-level spell slot

entries: You can use Supraheat a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Memoir of a Fallen Stigma

entries: "A single bullet ain't enough..."

You and the concept of the hunt have been lost in smoke for years, granting you the capability to make manifest fallen memories as if they were still lingering spirits on the world. Once per long rest you may summon two ghoulish apparitions of conflicts past to occupy any unoccupied space you can see within 60-ft. of you.

These beings use the {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} Memory sheet and are unable to speak and are subjugated by your own will, being considered friendly to you regardless of their disposition, they are forced to follow your orders regardless of if it would endanger them.

The appearance of these creatures are usually that of a hazy selection of faces that you have met and taken down in the past - be they friend or foe. You may Bellow Orders as a Free Action during your turn or between other creature's turns, before or after they act.

subclassFeature.name: Memoir of a War-torn Veteran

entries: "Until echoes of gunshots and plumes of smoke bury all that I've ever remembered...!"

Are you in pursuit of a memory of the past or have you become nothing but a blurred memory yourself? Maybe it is your party that grounds you in reality for the brief moments where you remain wholly yourself, or maybe its just the pursuit of the next target that keeps you going. Nevertheless, you have become a veteran in the war that is your life, wringing out every trick you have needed.

items: While you have at least one {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} Memory summoned, you may spend your Reaction whenever you take damage to only take half that damage and have all {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} Memories within 120-ft. reach of you suffer the other half. If a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} Memory is killed in this way, you do not receive its benefits.
Upon rolling Initiative you gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} count.
You inflict an additional 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count against creatures within your Sweet Spot.

Whenever you Critically Hit a creature, you may choose to spend one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} to deal an additional {@damage 2d8} piercing damage and also double any Conditions you would inflict.

For each {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} count you have you gain a +2 on {@skill Deception} checks to conceal your identity, as wreathes of red flame gradually consume your face like a mask that actively muddies the perception and memories of those that try to recall you, remaining to them as only a weaponized fire in their minds eye.

subclassFeature.name: Memorial Procession
entries: You become able to manifest a symbol of death and despair grand enough to make your enemies realize you are everything's end. Once you reach 15th level, you can summon your Coffin as a weapon described at the bottom of the page. Additionally, as long as you are mounting Dullahan, you may force the target of your attacks to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or gain 2 stacks of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and become affected by the {@condition Impending Ruin|TheUndertomesOA} condition whenever they are hit by one of your attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Middle's Blade

entries: "C'mon, Mama! I thought I asked you to knock before barging into my room."

Those that walk the path of the Middle's Blade are excited up and comers ready to serve the faction however they can. They might not have the muscles and the brawn, but they more than make up for it with speed, precise attacks and the right tools for the job. The Middle is a criminal group that values loyalty above all else, treating members as siblings, and your dream is to be taken into their fold like one of their brothers and sisters, no matter the strength behind one of your punches.

In the Forgotten Realms, the Half is a criminal faction in Waterdeep that is recruiting people to join their familial gang, claiming that they're all the half missing on each other. In Ravenloft, the Half unites in small villages on the edges of the Mists, trying to use the fear and paranoia to create a sense of unity to survive the horrors of the world. In the dark fantasy world of Alacritas, the gods have long abandoned humanity, so humanity decided to unite among the remnants and thrive. If the gods no longer care, the Half believes they need to care for each other to get through this endless tribulation. All that are accepted into the Half's fold are family, all that reject it and condemn it will suffer the same human ire the gods faced and deemed too dangerous to love.

There are plenty of ways to play a Middle's Blade. You can be someone excited that recently joined the Middle or relevant criminal gang and want to show your worth to your brothers and sisters. Usually a Middle's Blade is young and unafraid, ready to show their potential and grow within the gang. There's also the possibility that you are not a part of the Middle but would love to be, and have been cosplaying and working hard to become one of their members. Either way, you are someone dedicated to the Middle that would stop at nothing to be recognized by them.

entries.name: The Middle Never Forgets, Y'Know?

entries: "Wanna come read with me and see who our next kill's gonna be, if you're not busy?"

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall unconscious. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature.

If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until your next short rest.

If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until the end of the first round of combat. Whenever you hit an enemy with a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, they gain 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This number increases to 2 at level 5.

If you or a friendly creature within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack from a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, your attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage to them until the end of your next turn. This number increases to {@damage 1d6} at level 5, {@damage 1d8} at level 11 and {@damage 1d10} at level 17.

entries.name: Thermal Weapon

entries: "Duking it out with a badass Fixer, beating the crap outta each other 'till I pop their head off-nothing tops that, right?"

Whenever you start your turn within 30 feet of a creature with counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, gain 1 count of {@condition Thermal Blades|TheUndertomesMBG}. Gain 1 more count of {@condition Thermal Blades|TheUndertomesMBG} if a creature within the area is also suffering from counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

Additionally, you can do cool poses to strike fear into your enemy's heart. You gain advantage on Intimidation ability checks, and, as a Bonus Action, you can make a Charisma (Intimidation) check contested by a creature's Wisdom (Insight) check. If your result is higher, they become {@condition Frightened} of you for 1 minute. They can repeat this ability check at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest. Any creature {@condition Frightened} by you this way takes an additional {@damage 1d4} dice of damage whenever taking ( {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or) {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. damage. Additionally, they become more willing to provide you information, usually not requiring a Charisma (Persuasion) ability check or decreasing its DC by 5.

subclassFeature.name: Midnight Storm
entries: Once per long rest, you can use your action to perform Midnight Storm. Make every attack you could make with the Attack action against one creature, then make one additional weapon attack against it for each {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stack it has. These attacks do not trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}; each hit instead removes 1 stack, pushes the target 5 feet directly away from you, and moves you the same distance to remain within 5 feet of it. If one of these attacks hits, you have advantage on your next attack roll during the turn.
You can also use Midnight Storm in place of the attack made as part of Over the Moon. Once you use Midnight Storm, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mind of the Sacristan

entries: "Records say that the Holy Relic, which we must protect with our lives, was discovered in the abyssal depths of the Ruins."

Through rigorous training, learning and unlearning your mind has become a sacred temple to recycling knowledge - and as any polished reliquary it must find its relic to hold, as all the Saints of your Way have once come to do before you, to the purpose of acquiring all the knowledge that relic holds and to pave the way to those to come after you. You gain the following:

items: The determination to grasp more knowledge has become ingrained not only in your brain but your heart, granting you an additional count of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} whenever you gain it.

Your constant forgetting of all the things of which you must know to answer your calling have led you to develop an instinctual knowledge toward performing them. While you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} you may add an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Skill Checks you aren't proficient in.

entries: Additionally, upon reaching this level you may spend a long rest to denominate a magic item of Very Rare or greater rarity to become your very own Relic, an object that you will do your utmost to keep protected from the world and all that would want it. You instantly gain all knowledge about its creation as if per the effects of the {@spell Legend Lore} spell and know perfectly how it works, as per the effects of the {@spell Identify} Spell.

Furthermore your Relic is considered to be an Artifact in rarity and your Attunement to it cannot be broken unless you die. If it provides a bonus modifier to attack or damage rolls, AC or DCs, that modifier increases by one. If it consumes Charges you only consume half the Charge cost the Relic would consume, rounded down and to a limit of one. If it already only costs one Charge to be activated, you may use the item's effects without spending Charges once per short or long rest.

You can instantly transport this item to your empty hand as a Free Action during your turn and always instinctively know its exact location provided it is within a mile of you. If your Relic is a weapon, you may add all its benefits to your unarmed attack provided it being carried by your person.
If your Relic is a Key of Knowledge, its Truesight range increases to become a 60-ft. cone and it instantly becomes a +4 weapon when chosen as your Relic.

subclassFeature.name: Moment's Floral Breeze

entries: "Welcome. Now what does your heart say... about what you see of my heart?"

There is life within your heart, one that sets its roots in, grows and flourishes beautifully. With every wave of the hand and every single spell cast, you project more of your nature into the world and help shape its path to blossoming.

Whenever you cast a spell, you gain Lingering Blossoms count equal to the Spell Slot Level spent. Whenever you hit a creature with spell attacks or saving throws, you may choose to spend a value of Lingering Blossoms to inflict equal {@condition Blooming|TheUndertomesFS} and double that value of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts.

You may also spend 2 Lingering Blossoms as a Bonus Action to condense it into a small orb of spice that you can toss to a willing creature within 30-ft. of you as part of the same Bonus Action. That creature gains an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to one skill check, attack roll or saving throw of their choice for the next minute, consuming the orb as a Free Action.
You may have a maximum amount of Lingering Blossoms equal to double your proficiency bonus, and that value is halved on a short rest and reduced to zero during a long rest.

Whenever a creature becomes {@condition Blooming|TheUndertomesFS|Fully Bloomed} within 60-ft. of you, you may spend your Reaction to reap the blooming flower you have created, liberating the creature from their suffering and potentially having them see the world with fresher eyes.

They must pass a Constitution saving throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer {@damage 2d6} piercing damage plus a number of d8 psychic damage for each 5 Sinking count they are suffering from, to a maximum of {@damage 8d8}, losing an equal count of the Condition afterward.

subclassFeature.name: Moonshadow Warden Martial Archetype
entries: Moonshadow Wardens are mercenaries who use both blade and talisman to perform swift and deadly acts in the name of a lord, ruler, or boss. They roam the land with antique teachings of bladework and old rituals, taking work as protectors and hunters while forgoing cumbersome defenses in favor of overwhelming agility and force.
In worlds such as Faerun, they are higher disciples of the Heishou Pack, Mao Branch, using their knowledge to protect their brethren and carry out their lord's orders.

entries.subclassFeature: Blade Wreathed in Heavenly Authority|Fighter|PHB|Moonshadow Warden|TheUndertomesMW|3

subclassFeature.name: Multifold Retribution
entries: The family has finally recognized your skills, and given you a position worthy of your power, which demands respect from all people. Once you reach 14th level, your Unarmed Strike damage dice changes to {@dice 1d12}. Additionally, as a reaction when a creature within 30 feet of you attempts to cast a spell, take a bonus action, a reaction, a legendary action or a mythic action, you may use your speed to run up to them without provoking opportunity attacks and perform an attack roll. If you hit, the creature's action and spell slot is spent and lost. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

Whenever you enter your Rage, a burst of purple energy flames explode from your Tattoos, covering your entire body in a menacing aura, signaling you have entered Rageful Vengeance. During Rageful Vengeance, you have all benefits from a normal Rage, with the addition of:

entries.name: Right In the Solar Plexus.
entries: As an action, which can be taken as part of your attack action when you hit a creature or an object, you get to end all magical effects currently affecting that object or creature, and if the creature is shape-shifted, it reverts to its true form. If the magical effect is of 7th-level or higher, you must roll {@dice d20} + your Con modifier against the caster's save DC, dispelling the effect on a success. If the magical effect doesn't need to be activated, and is instead constantly active, like a Monk's Timeless Body, the suppression only lasts for a minute. You can use this ability once per Rageful Vengeance.

entries.name: Watch Your Back!
entries: As part of your attack action, you can force the enemy to roll a Charisma saving throw against your Tattoo save DC. If they fail, they become surprised by your might, recognizing their inferiority, and your second attack immediately grapples the creature on a hit. You have advantage attacking a creature surprised this way. Immediately after grappling them, you may throw them on a 30 feet line in any direction. They take {@dice 1d10} bludgeoning damage for each 10 feet traveled. If they hit another creature or an object this way, they instead take double the dice in damage and what they hit takes half that damage, being pushed along with it to the end of the line if possible. All creatures that took damage this way fall {@condition Prone}. You can use this ability once per Rageful Vengeance.

entries.name: Swear Vengeance.
entries: Whenever you successfully hit a creature with all available Unarmed Attack actions in your turn, they become {@condition Panicked|TheUndertomesASF} until the end of their next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Multitudes in a Crashing Wave

entries: "Be cheerful in your final moments. For you have been chosen."

To become a true follower of the Will you have come to understand that you are into the wielder of a weapon as as an extension of yourself, no. You are no more than a weapon that extends from the whims made manifest.

You gain a Wilful Device, a small golden box which displays your Prescripts and contains a black ferrofluid substance that mimics and adapts as much like your soul. If lost or removed from your person, you may recall it to your hand as a Free Action. It is indestructible and may be wielded as a weapon with the Finesse property. At the start of your turns in combat, roll two d8 to determine the shape it takes as per the following table, disregarding the second roll unless both are the same number.
