Whenever you deal damage with this weapon, also inflict {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries: At the beginning of your turns, if there is no creature suffering the Effect, one random hostile creature within 120-ft. of you becomes {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD|Marked by the Prescript}. You inflict {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus when attacking a {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD|Marked by the Prescript} creature.

Whenever you or a friendly creature within 15-ft. of you knocks a {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD|Marked by the Prescript} creature {@condition Unconscious} for the first time in combat or kills them, you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus.

Upon reaching 4th Level in Cleric, you gain a +1 to hit and to damage rolls while using your Wilful Device to attack. This increases to a +2 at 10th Level and a +3 at 16th Level. It also counts as a Holy Symbol for you.

entries.name: Designer's Note.
entries: This subclass is not meant to be taken as a multi-class with other Dexterity-based classes, since it may provide too-strong a weapon with the Finesse property, which was chosen to be given to all weapons for the sake of greater freedom when designing your player character. We recommend removing the Finesse property and only adding it to Hatchet, Stiletto, Rapier, Lance, Whip and Scythe if multi-classing into a Dexterity-based class to avoid abuse of this feature.

entries.name: Designer's Note.
entries: To define a "random hostile creature" we recommend using the Random Targeting Rule within the Optional Rules & Prescripts section of this document.

subclassFeature.name: Musketeer of Smiles
entries: Focus on speed and weaponizing it against your enemies.

entries.name: Musketeers strive to be the fastest warriors on the battlefield.
entries: They know better than anyone that speed is equal to strength, and the faster they are, the harder enemies fall.

Empower your rapiers with unmatched velocity and strike true at your opponent's hearts, but not without making a show! As a Musketeer of Smiles, you strive to make your battles as fun for an audience as they are for you.

entries.subclassFeature: Student of the Wind|Fighter|PHB|Musketeer of Smiles|TheUndertomesMS|3

subclassFeature.name: Mutation [Mao]
entries: Your mutations become more lasting. You retain {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesMW} points for up to 1 minute while in combat or 1 hour outside combat, after which all remaining points are lost. While you have at least 1 point of {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesMW}, you have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Mutilating Talons

entries: "Listen... I did this for you instead of indulgin' my fighting urges. Remember, that, yeah?"

Your feathers have grown more fierce, are burning hotter, and you can't wait to dispense all of that fury on your enemies. While you have counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR}, you now deal 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to the target and 4 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to yourself. While you have 4 or more counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself, your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} applies thrice its amount as {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on enemies. If you have {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} or counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you get to do an extra attack once per turn. For each consecutive attack that you hit on the same creature this turn, you deal an additional {@dice 1d6} fire damage to them as long as you have counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR}.

subclassFeature.name: My Precious Artwork

entries: "Have you woken up, Fascia? Faust has been waiting-there is a new friend Faust wants to introduce to Fascia."

An artists creation must be seeded and grown carefully, and you have planted your own - cultivating it with the flesh of your own corpus and that of which you gather in your daily exhibitions of violence and/or bodily harm. You have begun created a masterwork, it is a Martial Melee weapon that you are considered Attuned with at all times. It counts as a magic item for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and it usually takes the shape of a greatsword you can wield with but a single hand, an extension of your own body. It deals {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and has the Finesse property.
Over the course of a long rest you may spend an amount of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} equal to your proficiency modifier to permanently upgrade it, as per the following:

items: {@b Enhance Corporal Handling.} You focus on bettering the handling of your masterwork, granting it a +1 bonus modifier to attack and damage rolls. When taken again, this upgrade increases by +1, to a maximum of +3.

{@b Addition of Spinal Spikes.} You sharpen the puncturing edges of your masterwork to better cut an exhibition, increasing its damage die to {@damage 1d8}. Upon taking this upgrade again, it becomes an {@damage 1d10}, and if taken once more, an {@damage 1d12}.

{@b Versatile Vertebrae.} You improve how grasp-able your work is to the public, granting your masterwork the Versatile property. If your weapon deals {@damage 1d12} damage, it has Versatile ({@damage 2d6}).
{@b Ripper Ribcages.} You inlay the blade with smaller, cracked ribs for a lasting impression. You deal an additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit with your masterwork.
{@b Elongated Chords.} You extrapolate your work with femurs woven into the spinal chord of your masterwork to grant it the Reach weapon property.

{@b Condensation of Ideas.} You trepidatiously realize the need to lay it on thick at times. You may stick your masterwork in the ground as a Bonus Action during your turn, and then spend a Free Action before or after any creature acts to pull a small cord connecting it to you as long as you are within 60-ft. of it. When you do so, a cluster of constricted veins erupts violently from the blade - coating a 15-ft. radius around the weapon in powerful lashes. All creatures within that reach must pass a Dexterity Saving throw or suffer {@damage 2d12} slashing damage and become Grappled, being able to attempt to break free against the same DC as a Bonus Action during their subsequent turns. You may do this an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest. You may pick your blade up as a Bonus Action.

{@b Action Painting.} You experiment with your art to make it pop more, like an artery bursting. Whenever you hit a creature and the difference between your roll and their AC is 3 or greater, or if you forego receiving {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesCO} from this hit, you may deliver a gashing puncture that splatters their blood toward a 15-ft. line in any angle behind them, rending the liquid a cutting surface upon itself. All creatures within that range must pass a Dexterity Saving throw or suffer an amount of d4 slashing damage and Bleed count equal to half your proficiency bonus.
{@b Cutaneous Arrangement.} You grant your weapon thicker skin when suffering criticism. While wielded with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to your AC while in Flowing Form.

{@b Additional Handiwork.} You stitch a few extra grippers so you can more easily handle certain other business as necessary. You may cast Druid spells' somatic components while wielding this weapon in either or both hands.
{@b Wing Tendons.} You construct a pile of muscles into pseudo-wings to aid your artwork in soaring high and far. This weapon gains the Thrown (30/60-ft.) property.

{@b Devoration of Inspiration.} You break down a magical weapon to feed it to your masterwork. It inherits any traits of the consumed weapon, such as the Vorpal enchantment, but cannot gain any bonuses to hit or damage from doing so. It however can gain additional damage die and you may only benefit from a single magic item being devoured at any given time, replacing the oldest enchantment when consuming another.

{@b Shifting Presentation.} You change how your weapon presents itself in a regulated setting. When you take this upgrade, you may change your masterworks damage type to your choice of acidic, bludgeoning, piercing or necrotic damage.

entries: You may take each upgrade only once, with the exception of being able to take upgrades marked by your Masterwork's Symbol an additional time upon reaching 8th and 14th levels in Druid. Due to the limits of your own developing flash, your maximum amount of upgrades is equal to your proficiency bonus and you may exchange an existing one with the same process of creating one. Whenever this feature asks for a saving throw, the Save DC is equal to your Druid Spell Save DC.
Additionally upon reaching 6th level, you may perform an additional attack as part of your Attack Action while in Flowing Form.

subclassFeature.name: Nail Down Purification of Filth

entries: "I skewered sixteen today. Tomorrow, I will nail and cremate twice as many. Huhu... It gets fun as you keep at it, doesn't it?"

Your faith drives you not only to simply nail the unworthy, you are driven instead to purge their souls and provide space for a new world where all the faithful can be whole under your grace. You gain the following means of purification:

entries.name: Crucifixion.
entries: You may spend your Action to build up the grave to a new world free of filth. You may consume 8 {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count on a target within melee reach to perform a melee weapon attack against them. On a hit, they have their binds pierce through their limbs and bind them to a single place to suffer divine retribution. That creature suffers {@damage 2d12} piercing damage and becomes Immobilized until the start of your next turn. After recovering from this Condition, they suffer 8 count of {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesHF}. A creature crucified this way becomes overtaken by the adrenaline due to the extreme pain inflicted onto them, gaining a +5 to their AC against being crucified for one minute.

entries.name: Immolating Pyre.
entries: Whenever you hit a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} creature, you may consume 6 {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count to flare the flames of your faith that have eaten at their soul. Any {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target instantly becomes {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesHF} and any {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count becomes {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead. {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead causes the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the previous Condition and 2 stacks are removed every time it is triggered. The {@skill Medicine} Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

entries.name: Wedge the Unruly.
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack while Raging, you may forgo inflicting {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF|Nails} and instead 2 {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} Count against them. You instead inflict an additional d6 radiant damage on that attack equal to half your proficiency bonus.
You may only use one of these abilities per turn, but may use them multiple times if able.

Additionally, you always deal an additional d6 radiant damage against the Target of your Ire, yet your growing obsession grows worse with each passing day, causing you to suffer {@damage 1d12} psychic damage that cannot be reduced through any means if you end your turn without killing a Target of your Ire, provided there is one you can see within 60-ft. of you.

subclassFeature.name: Nameless Slash [無名斬]

entries: "A single straight stroke to fell them all...!"

You are now able to connect your sword with the universe, surprising reality itself as you unsheathe your blade and slice it from afar. Once per turn, when you unsheathe your sword to attack, you gain an extra 10-foot reach to that attack. If you attack objects this way, you deal double damage to them. If you destroy structures this way, they are sliced clean.

While performing an attack like this, you may spend 4 Ki points, 5 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or 2 counts of {@condition Moonlit Azure Blade|TheUndertomesBS} to target an object or item someone is carrying or wearing instead. If it is a magical item, you can still destroy it as long as it is of Rare rarity or lower. Upon reaching level 11 you may destroy Very Rare items, and Legendary items upon reaching level 17.

subclassFeature.name: Neverending Holiday Madness
entries: The mischief and love placed into selecting the gifts of your Giftbag has been multiplied manifold by your devotion. When you roll in the Fine Gifts For All! table, you may choose to roll another {@dice 1d8|d8} in accord to the result, causing an effect from the corresponding table to trigger. ( Ex: Rolling a 1 on the first {@dice 1d8|d8} would cause you to roll another {@dice 1d8|d8} on the Gnomic Helpers table. )
All these tables may be found at the end of this document.

entries.caption: Gnomic Helpers Effects
rows: A gnome waddles out wearing an aerodynamic armor set beset with spikes. It walks up to one creature of your choice within 30-ft., of whom may spend their reaction to kick the gnome towards another creature within 60-ft, dealing {@damage 2d4} + your proficiency bonus' worth of piercing damage on a hit.

Four stylish gnomes waddle out of the bag toward you and up to 3 other creatures of your choice, addorning you in resistant clothes that grant temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus times 3.

A gaggle of bearded gnomes jump out and use their holiday magic to bolden a creature of your choice within 30-ft. of you. The next spell that creature casts until the end of your next turn is done so at one higher level, such as a 1st-level spell being cast at 2nd while still spending a 1st-level spell slot.

A gaggle of gnomes come out with stretchers to move one willing creature of your choice within 60-ft. toward another unnocupied space within the same range of you. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

A gaggle of gnomes rushes toward a creature of your choice within 60-ft., acting menacing to extort them for whatever they have. The target must pass an {@skill Insight} check against your Spell Save DC of be forced to give the gnomes whatever it is holding in their hands. The gnomes then may move it to any other stop within 60-ft. or give the items to you.

A gaggle of gnomes comes out carrying cookies and milk, eating them and returning to your Giftbag at the end of your next turn. Any creature within 5-ft. of them may attempt a Grapple check against the gnomes ( they use your modifier ) to steal their snacks, eating them as part of the same action and having {@dice 3d4+3} of their hit points restored. A creature may also attempt an {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation} against the gnomes for the same effect. ( Against your Spell Save DC. )

A sick gnome waddles out toward the nearest creature within 15-ft. of the giftbox and vomits rainbows on them before being knocked {@condition Unconscious} for the next {@dice 2d8} hours. The target must pass a Constitution saving throw against your Spell Save DC or become {@condition Poisoned} for the next minute. When the gnome wakes up, it walks back to you and enters your giftsack no matter how far you are, as long as you are within the same plane of reality. Otherwise, it becomes sad and sits in place until able to return home.

A thermonuclear gnome waddles out toward the nearest creature within 15-ft of the giftbox. It explodes. Any creature within 15-ft. of the gnome must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer an amount of {@damage 1d8|d8} poison damage equal to double your proficiency bonus.

entries.caption: Gift Within a Gift Effects
rows: {@item Wings of Flying} are within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A bottle of {@item Sovereign Glue} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
{@item Pipes of Haunting} are within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A {@item Periapt of Health} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A Pipe of Bubbles is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A {@item Necklace of Fireballs} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A pair of {@item Gloves of Missile Snaring} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A {@item Robe of Stars} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.

entries: All these items still become snow after one minute.

entries.caption: Modern Classic Effects
rows: The bomb deals fire damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are lit on fire until the end of the next round. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this fire suffers {@damage 2d4} fire damage.

The bomb deals cold damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are frozen over until the end of the next round. Any creature who moves into or within a frozen space must pass an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} check or fall {@condition Prone}. The DC for this check is 14.

The bomb deals acid damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are soaked in an acidic puddle until the end of the next round. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this fire suffers {@damage 2d4} acid damage.

The bomb deals necrotic damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are coated in graveyard grime until the end of the next round. Any creature who moves into or within this area must pass a Dexterity saving throw or have their feet grabbed by a spectral hand, which causes them to lose 15-ft. of movement until the end of their turn. The DC for this saving throw is 14.

The bomb deals poison damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are lit on fire until the end of the next round. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this fire suffers from the {@condition Poisoned} condition until they end their turn outside of this area.

All spaces within the bombs explosion radius are covered by caltrops until the end of the next round. Any creature who moves within that area suffers 2 piercing damage per 5-ft. of movement spend within the area.
The bomb deals thunder damage instead of piercing and its radius is extended by 10-ft..
The bomb deals radiant damage and all creatures who fail its saving throw must pass a Constitution saving throw ( {@dc 14} ) or be {@condition Blinded} until the end of your next turn.

entries.caption: Yuletide Howls Effects
rows: Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, it is assailed by visions of dreadful direwolves which cause them an inability to focus. While {@condition Frightened} this way they cannot take the Aid action and have a negative modifier to any rolls made as a Reaction. This modifier is equal to your proficiency bonus.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they feel as if a biting cold wind swept through them, having them shiver and treat all terrain as difficult terrain for as long as they are {@condition Frightened}.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they feel their extremities freezing to the point of frostbite, instantly suffering 4 times your proficiency bonus' worth of psychic damage.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, an illusory gnome jumps off of the box with a spooky mask, forcing them to spend all their movement speed moving away from the box at the start of their next turn.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they start having illusions of being a giant turkey drumstick. While {@condition Frightened} in this way, whenever they recover hit points they must pass a Wisdom saving throw or perform a melee weapon attack against themselves as a reaction, as they desperately feel the need to take a bite of a nice-looking meal.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they see an illusory gnome jumping over their face and scurrying over their body, having them become {@condition Prone} at the start of their next turn.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, a deep paranoia settles into the creature's mind, as if they forgot to buy presents at the last second. They automatically fail any {@skill Perception} or Investigation checks while {@condition Frightened}.

Instead of playing a cacophony of songs, the music box instead only plays one jolly tune of your choice. All friendly creatures within 60-ft. that can hear gain advantage on their next Wisodm saving throw for the next minute.

entries.caption: Gnomic Raiders Effects
rows: The raiders have extra-sharp weapon, dealing {@damage 1d6|d6s} instead of {@damage 1d4|d4s}.

The raiders have laced their weapons with something foul, dealing acid damage instead of slashing and causing the target to suffer a -1 negative modifier to their Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws per each hit suffered. This modifier recedes by 1 at the end of each of their next turns.

The raiders come out but instantly enter their holiday-mandated break time, remaining on the space of the giftbox for the next minute. They are not agressive but instantly become incensed if any creature moves within 5-ft of them or performs an attack within the same range. Upon becoming incensed, the gnomes perform three melee weapon attacks as per the original Gnomic Raiders effect against the triggering creature, except they deal {@damage 3d8} slashing damage per hit attack. After attacking or if the time passes, they leave back into your Giftsack.

Before attacking the raiders attempt to jump their target, forcing them to attempt a Strength saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failure, they are knocked {@condition Prone}. On a success, the gnomes are shaken off and have disadvantage on their attack rolls against the target.

The more civilized gnomes hop out this time, carrying crossbows to attack instead of their usual junk. You may choose for them to target any creature of your choice within 60-ft. of the Giftbox. They deal piercing damage instead of slashing.

This gaggle of gnomes decided to not be hurtful today, instead waddling in search of being annoying as can be. Their target must pass a number of Wisdom saving throws against your Spell Save DC equal to the amount of attacks they would originally perform. For each failure the target suffers a -1 negative modifier to their attack rolls, with this negative modifier diminishing by one at the end of each of the target's subsequent turns.

The gnomes come all carrying one big weapon together, performing a single attack as per the original effect's rules against their target. On a hit, the target creature takes {@damage 8d8} plus your Charisma modifier's worth of bludgeoning damage and is knocked {@condition Prone}.
The gnomes are incredibly focused today. If they kill a creature as part of the Gnomic Raider's original effect, they make it so the item produced never melts.

entries.caption: You Effects
rows: The box's fangs are horridly jagged, also dealing {@damage 4d8} piercing damage on a failed saving throw or half that damage on a success.

The box instead hopes only to protect until the next winter, making it so the creature inside becomes immune to all damage types except force. Furthemore, they remain {@condition Grappled} for up to the next minute and may spend a free action to break free.

This gift drank bad milk during the holidays and suffers horrible indigestion, spitting the creature out towards any other of your choice within 60-ft. You roll a ranged spell attack against the target and on a hit, the target and the originally {@condition Grappled} creature suffer {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage if the {@condition Grappled} was of small size, {@damage 4d10} if they were normal sized and {@damage 6d10} if they were large. Furthermore, the {@condition Grappled} creature also becomes {@condition Prone}.

This gift is filled with a horrible toxic liquid. A creature {@condition Grappled} by the box suffers {@damage 3d4} acid damage when initially {@condition Grappled} and at the end of their next turn. It does not benefit from the box's Resistance to damage for this acid damage.

The box doesn't want to be the gift at all, running 30-ft. away with the {@condition Grappled} creature towards a random direction. To determine that direction, roll a {@dice 1d8|d8} where 1 is North, 2 is Northeast, 3 is East and so on.

The box is disgusted by whatever it eats, quickly spitting it out after Grappling the creature with a bundle of vomit and spit. The creature has their movement speed halved for the next minute or until they can submerge themselves in a liquid to wash off.

The box is confused as to the logistics of interplanar travel, being teleported upwards by {@dice 1d8} times 20-ft. and then vanishing, leaving the {@condition Grappled} creature to fall. If this would cause the box to be teleported into a solid surface, it instead teleports to the nearest unnocupied space below the surface.

The box is a portal to a demiplane which houses the Cheerful Spirits whom love scaring people, causing them to also be {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, being able to attempt a Wisdom saving throw against the same DC at the end of their subsequent turns.

entries.caption: Buddy-Ship Effects
rows: This magic is dictated by a freaky battle-loving Spirit, also granting this bonus to attack rolls.
This magic is dictated by a nurturing family Spirit, also granting this bonus to it's targets Armor Class.
This magic is dictated by a feisty and hurried Spirit, also granting an additional 10-ft. of walking speed to it's targets.
This magic is dictated by a particularly battle-liking Spirit, also granting this bonus to attack rolls!

This magic is dictated by an old, ancient and long-lived Spirit, making it so the bonus gained by the original effect lasts for the next minute. If any other effects are gained by another Spirit, they also last for the same duration.
This magic is dictated by an experienced and tale-weaving Spirit, granting a +2 bonus modifier instead of +1.

This magic is dictated by you and your friends true friendship. Each creature blessed by this gains a {@dice 1d4|d4} bonus modifier they may grant to another creature as a reaction to when they perform any roll. This {@dice 1d4|d4} lasts for up to the next minute, whereafter the feeling just settles down in their hearts.

This magic is dictated by pure disgust and hatred towards whatever you are facing, making it so it's target creatures deal an additional {@damage 1d4|d4} damage when attacking. The damage's type is equal to the attack's original damage type.

entries.caption: Santata's Big Surprisese! Effects
rows: INSTEAD: A giant leg kicks at the nearest target! On a failed save the target is flung back an additional 15-ft. and if they come in contact with another creature or wall, they suffer an additional {@damage 3d8} bludgeoning damage.
INSTEAD: A giant hand smacks down at the nearest target! On a failed save, the target isn't flung back, instead being knocked {@condition Prone}.

INSTEAD: An ovesized ( and beardy ) face appears and screams at the target! This effect deals thunder damage instead of bludgeoning. On a failed save the target also becomes {@condition Deafened} for the next minute.
INSTEAD: A giant sack is flung at the nearest target! On a failed save the target takes an additional {@damage 2d12} bludgeoning damage.

INSTEAD: A giant pair of fingers jab at the nearest target! On a failed save they suffer piercing damage instead of bludgeoning and become {@condition Blinded} for the next minute if they rely on their eyesight alone.
INSTEAD: A pair of giant hands clap at the nearest target's head! On a failed save the target also becomes {@condition Deafened} for the next minute.

INSTEAD: A torrent of gifts pour out of the giftbag. Instead of Santata's Big Surprisese!'s original effect, you roll a number of ranged attack rolls equal to your proficiency bonus against targets you can see within 60-ft. of you. On a hit, roll on the Fine Gifts For All! table and that gift opens targeting the hit creature. On a miss, nothing happens.

INSTEAD: An oversized ( and particularly hairy ) face bites at the nearest target! On a failed save the target is also {@condition Poisoned} for the next minute, being able to attempt a Constitution saving throw at the end of their subsequent turns against the same DC. While {@condition Poisoned}, the creature feels as if they were drunk ( if able ), like a great deal of alcohol was transfered into their bloodstream.

subclassFeature.name: Night Awl Roguish Archetype

entries: "Be quick in your step, thread the night carefully and get the hell out of dodge before you get snuffed out."
That is the thing that most Rogues who fit in the Archetype of the Night Awl might find themselves hearing from a captain of their gang or even tell themselves.

They are usually people who bear through the brunt of a hard life, away from the flashiness of grandiose magic cast by archmages or the jewel-embezzling tales of bards, instead relying only on themselves and maybe a greater criminal organization where they can punch out a place in, carrying with them only a dirk in hand and a clear goal to be reached with finesse and clarity.

In the Forgotten Realms the Night Awls are a subsidiary of the Zentharim that have earnt themselves some renown, yet through no fault, of their own they are facing adverse times because of poor management. In other worlds such as Keybreak they are small-time info brokers running through the underground webs that connect city to city.

subclassFeature.name: Night-Light Wreath
entries: When you deal damage with a spell, you also incur a Condition in accord to your current active Astral Marbles, as follows:

rows: Anguilla
You deal an amount of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count.
Gallus
You deal an amount of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count.
Hirudo
You deal an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count.
Noctua
You gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count.
Sextans
You gain an amount of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count.
Rangifer

You deal an amount of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count. Whenever you deal spell damage with a 1st-Level spell or greater you may spend your Reaction to trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Vespa
You deal an amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when dealing damage through a spell attack equal to the spell slot’s level, to a minimum of 1 count.

entries: You may refer to the Undertomes Website for a reference of every single condition mentioned.

subclassFeature.name: Nightmarish Restlessness
entries: Your eternal unease sharpens your perception and keeps your mind just out of reach-always teetering on the edge of wakefulness. You are never fully at rest, and always a few steps ahead of fate. When combat begins, you immediately regain one use of both Indomitable and Second Wind and you cannot be surprised while in combat.

Additionally, your mind, twisted by long-suffered nightmares, becomes hostile terrain for any who try to enter it. When a creature targets you with a {@spell Divination} spell that involves direct mental manipulation-such as {@spell Dream} or {@spell Detect Thoughts}-you have advantage on any saving throw the spell requires. If you succeed, the caste must immediately make the same saving throw against their own Spell Save DC.

On a failure, they are affected by the same spell they attempted to cast on you, as though you had cast it on them. You seize the connection and stare back through it, dragging them to be in the spotlight of your mind's eye.

subclassFeature.name: Noble Etiquette
entries: You've learned the manners befitting someone of noble standing. Whether it's knowing the difference between a rice spoon and a soup spoon or wielding language with impeccable grace, you use your refinement to manipulate, inspire, or intimidate. Choose one of the following skills: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Performance}, or {@skill Persuasion}. You gain proficiency in the chosen skill.
You also learn to twist your words like blades. You learn the {@spell Vicious Mockery} cantrip and can cast it without material components. When cast this way, the cantrip has the following changes:

items: You may cast it once per turn as part of one of your attacks during your turn (this does not require a separate action), when cast this way you instead perform a spell attack instead of a Saving Throw.
A creature hit by this cantrip gains advantage on their next attack roll, but the next attack made against them also has advantage.
Additionally, the target of your {@spell Vicious Mockery} suffers a number of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip.
entries: You benefit from magical bonuses (e.g. from a +1 weapon) as if they were bonuses to a spellcasting focus when casting {@spell Vicious Mockery} in this way.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Annihilation
entries: Paladins who swore the Oath of Annihilation have decided to utter a single word to the universe: enough. Whatever is the target of their hunt and ire, be that a person, a creature, a location or even a concept, these Paladins will rest at nothing to see it purged from all realities and planes.
What kindled this flame of wrath that burns within me...? ...No, it doesn't matter why it burns- What matters is that I am the ripping and tearing tempest that will bring about their ruin.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Lordship
entries: The Oath of Lordship is one rarely taken, and those who dare to do it lightly simply do not make it out alive. To be a lord one must know how to answer the fundamental questions of what a World needs, and how to deliver results in that pursuit, commanding their fellows with a strong conviction for all, no matter the cost, also following these principles:

entries.name: Lead With Justice.
entries: Be fair towards those you judge, weighing all they may have done and what they still have to contribute.

entries.name: Show Your Power.
entries: Reject no duel, never be happy in the backseat of a fight; Instead be headstrong in your pursuits, no matter how violent they might be.

entries.name: Be Brazen and Undaunted.
entries: No matter what tactics you may employ, know that to truly be a Lord you must not fear exposing yourself and your truths.

entries.name: Share Knowledge.
entries: Others must understand the grandiosity of your pursuits, so they as well may one day reach enlightenment.

entries.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

entries.name: I Carve The Path of a Lord
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity as an Action to prepare a grand attack while being assisted by a friendly creature within 60-ft of yourself, you perform a melee weapon attack against a target creature within reach and deal your weapon's damage die plus a number of d8 radiant damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Immediately after, one friendly creature of your choice within range performs a Melee or Ranged attack against the same creature with Advantage, regardless if you miss or hit. The friendly creature you chose may also choose to cast a spell against the same target, for a Spell Level equalling half their highest Spell Slot Level known, rounded down. (Ex: A Wizard with access to 5th Level Spell Slots may only cast up to a 2nd Level Spell, or only Cantrips if they only know up to 1st Level Spell Slots.)

entries.name: The Lord of All Beasts
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity as an Action to augment your and your fellows' resolve toward a shared goal, granting you and a number of willing creatures within 30-ft of you equalling your Proficiency Bonus an additional modifier to their Skill Checks for the next minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}. This bonus is equal to half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Loyalty

entries: "Damn, passed out already, huh. Now that grudge is going into the Book of Vengeance... I'll avenge you soon."

Paladins that follow the Oath of Loyalty have a duty to their companions, their family. They will raise them to become the best versions of themselves and protect them from all harm. In return, their bonds will become unbreakable, and there will be no battle great enough to bring them down.

The faction of the Middle, an organization that preaches that all who are a part of it are siblings and must be there for each other, while avenging every misdeed done to its members, is where these Paladins usually hail from. This organization can be flavored however you want in your world, if it even exists, but it must maintain the familial ties that its members follow.

While a Paladin that follows the Oath of Loyalty will never forgive a mistake committed against them by those who are not family, it is generally considered right to look the other way and forgive your siblings for their errors. After all, family is family, and blood is thicker than water.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Procuration
entries: Those who have taken the Oath of Procuration are those who have given up their own desires and judgement in search of executing the Living Will's whims and no more, taking satisfaction in their actions without a second thought-become akin to a guardian devil to whatever it is that such a force comes to desire.

Their personalities might vary, yet a significant characteristic shared among the majority is a seeming lack of a core emotion or understanding of their own actions that can be perceived from how they act. Another characteristic is usually how they are bound in chains, waiting for their unbinding per the Will's whim, and with those chains also always carrying around a device that gives them orders, which is treated much akin to a holy symbol in how fervently they believe in it and cherish it.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, the Will might be a byproduct of the fallen city Netheryl, now using their paladins and shaping them to become great weapons of war and destruction so that the return of such a civilization will then become inevitable. In others, such as Thespis, the tribes of the Lizardmen Nushae have one such Paladin that transforms and shifts without the use of a Wyrdstone-instead channeling the Wyrd directly to enact its lord's will upon the material plane.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Protection
entries: Be the shield that stands between the forces of evil and the weak! Paladins that take the Oath of Protection use their weapons as shields that shelter all of those behind them. Your combat style can be summarized simply as "the best offense is the greatest defense." You might have been plagued by the inability to defend those you loved a long time ago. You might have experienced firsthand the cruelty of those with power over those without. You might have humble beginnings, or have been born in the highest luxury. It does not matter. You have taken a definite stance to protect all of those that need you.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Dream Ender
entries:
{@i "The Family will be well-cared for... after all, the onus always fell on me to provide for what you abandoned."}
Too long have the dreams of foolish idealists ensnared the hearts of your Family and tricked your brethren into serving for the promise of a unified tomorrow. Those dreamers preached and traveled thoughout the lands to share a gospel that was lauded in gold by humans, yet drenched in sweat and tears from your tortured kindred. You have decided to take responsibility and declare a clear and defined end to this perverse goal. Your brothers and sisters are not to toil endlessly for the comfort of humankind. Vampires, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends}, they were birthed with desires and necessities much like humans, however, their numbers falter and plunge them down the food chain. Your very presence aims to tip that scale by shattering the pointless dreams of those selfish utopians and awake the masses to their true purpose in life.

entries.name: Tenets of the Dream Ender

entries: "... Hold your tongue; I will no longer tolerate any more ingenious ideas. I've wasted enough time entertaining those cloud-chasing ruminations."
A Paladin who upholds the Oath of the Dream Ender has promised to end foolish ideals before they take root, and cut down those that are already poisoning the minds of their fellows.

items: {@b Take What Is Yours.} Do not let different systems of morality dictate the well-being of yourself and your brethren. Drink, for the world is your share.

{@b Free Your Kindred.} All Vampires and {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} bound to the yoke of hunger and subservience must be liberated. Unchain them, for the streets are yours to rule.
{@b Protect the Family.} You must never let harm come to those your mantle of blood covers, those you deem family. Shield, for they depend on you.
{@b End Foolish Dreams.} Never allow thoughtless ideals to grow and fester. Crush any notion of unity with those that wish you harm beneath your heels. Slay, for this pain begets truth.

entries.name: Oath Spells

entries: "I shall bear the responsibility for everything."
You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of the Dream Ender Spells table. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work.

entries.name: Guide's Bloodfeast
entries: "For the Family..." Long have you suffered for their joy, but now, their blood is a living fountain of power for you and your allies. Whenever you inflict a creature with counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, including your own.
The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 during a long rest.

entries.name: Hardblood

entries: "From this impalement..."

You have learned to fasten your enemies' demise into a resistant coat and a lance of hardened blood for battle. You gain Hardblood whenever you spend Bloodfeast equal to the same amount spent. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Hardblood
rows: 3rd

You have a long Lance made of hardened blood which you can wield with a single hand even if not mounted, and if lost or destroyed you may recreate it during a long rest without spending materials. It acts as your spellcasting focus and applies 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to any creature that you damage while wielding it.
I
3rd
Your Lance now applies 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead of just one. Additionally, your speed increases by 10 feet.
II
7th

Your Lance now deals {@damage 2d6} piercing damage and an additional {@damage 1d8} slashing damage to bleeding enemies, and it applies 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead, as well as counting as a +1 arcane focus and weapon. Additionally, your AC increases by 1.
III
15th

Your Lance now deals an additional {@damage 1d12} slashing damage to Bleeding enemies, and it applies 4 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead, as well as counting as a +2 arcane focus and weapon. Additionally, your speed increases by 20 feet instead. Whenever you score a critical hit, you gain temporary hit points equal to the amount of Bloodfeast your party holds plus the amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts on the target (maximum 30).

entries.name: Channel Divinity

entries: "... shall it cascade."
You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.
"... shall it cascade." You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works. Enough Is Enough.

As an action, you immediately make a melee attack against a creature within range. You can spend up to 10 Bloodfeast, gaining an additional +1 for the attack roll for each 5 Bloodfeast spent. If your current Bloodfeast count was 0, you can choose to apply 6 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself instead.

If the attack hits, you apply 4 additional counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target, and heal Hit Points equal to half the amount of damage this attack dealt. Variant Hardblood Arts 6 - Whip. This Channel Divinity option substitutes Enough Is Enough once you witness the suffering other {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} or Vampires go through when suppressing their needs in an attempt to live among humans; or if there's a Kindred Domain Cleric in your party.

As an action, you immediately make a melee attack against a creature within range. You can spend up to 15 Bloodfeast, gaining an additional +1 for the attack roll for each 5 Bloodfeast spent. If your current Bloodfeast count was 0, you can choose to apply 6 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself instead.

If the attack hits, you apply 4 additional counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target, and heal Hit Points equal to half the amount of damage this attack dealt. Additionally, for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action, your Lance transforms into a Whip. This Whip retains all Hardblood properties your Lance would have, except its damage dice increases from {@dice 1d4} to {@dice 1d6} at Rank I, {@dice 1d8} at Rank II and {@dice 1d10} at Rank III, and can attack up to 3 creatures as long as they're standing 5 feet next to each other, or 2 creatures as long as they're standing 10 feet next to each other.

Laughters Will Subside. As a bonus action, apply {@condition Shimmering|TheUndertomesDE} to target creature within 30 feet of you. For a minute, they also gain advantage on {@skill Intimidation} ability checks.

Variant Hardblood Arts 15 - Build up to Finale. This Channel Divinity option substitutes Laughters Will Subside once you witness vampires or {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} being objectified or needing to don masks, wear make up or hide who they are in any way to escape the wrath of other creatures; or if there's a College of Lifeblood Bard in your party. As a bonus action, apply {@condition Shimmering|TheUndertomesDE} to up to 2 target creatures within 30 feet of you.

For a minute, they also gain advantage on {@skill Intimidation} ability checks. Additionally, for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action, your Lance transforms into a Parasol. This Parasol retains all Hardblood properties your Lance would have, except its damage changes to {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and increases from {@dice 1d8} to {@dice 1d10} at Rank I, {@dice 1d12} at Rank II and {@dice 2d6} at Rank III, and you can use a reaction when a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack to divert the attack's target to you, and increasing the damage dice by 2.
This damage cannot be diminished in any way, and you generate an amount of Bloodfeast equal to the number of damage dice used plus half your proficiency bonus modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Obsidian Saint

entries: "Though many have fallen to the ground, forsooth... Thou needst not concern thyself, suffering is etched into and remembered by Grand Magasin Sisyphe itself."

One who swears an Oath to the Obsidian God is the soul who has chosen to devote their everything to one day embody a Saint of this deity, vowing piety upon their God so they may wreath themselves in the perseverance needed to keep the world's order forevermore.

At their best, they are often agreeable despite their imposing nature as long as no stranger dares cross their boundaries - lines of which they denote clearly and loudly, yet at worst they are impossibly stubborn in their own way, branding any deviation from that norm as a defilement of the greatest calibre and swiftly taking up arms to correct any seeming mistake in conduct.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms' Faerûn, the Paladins who swore such an oath are barely an established order - Instead being the envoys of a newly arisen god who intend to roll out their perfected view of the world's balance to reach the rest, while in certain worlds such as Balefire such Paladins are some of the few bastions who still retain the will of the being now known as the Charred One, upholding the ash-covered doctrine of a world long overtaken by flame.

entries.subclassFeature: Tenets of the Obsidian Saint|Paladin|PHB|Obsidian Saint|TheUndertomesOBS|3

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Turbulence
entries: Emotions are at the forefront of all life, the happiness of its beginning, the many, many varied feelings thorough its longevity and the sadness or even peace at its end, it all comes and goes, and a Paladin of Turbulence is one to embrace and nourish them all, be it in the name of many gods or for the sake of the simple right to feel. In the forgotten realms, there are no Orders of Turbulence, instead there are quixotic knights roaming around all of Faerun who have adopted the similar tenets of Turbulence, enjoying bringing all who makes them raw around the very realm. In the drowsy lands of Ravenloft, a Paladin of Turbulence might be one more equipped to deal with the droughts of will and bouts of sadness, yet always remain ontop, persevering and aiding to persevere through the many hard times ahead.

entries.name: Tenets of the Turbulence
entries: The vast majority of Paladins of Turbulence hold the following Tenets in their heart:

items: Wear your heart on your sleeve.
Be mindful of others feelings.
Never repress yourself.
Always be genuine with what you do.

entries.name: Today's Look
entries: Starting from when you choose this subclass, every daybreak you may choose between what is appropriate for your character or roll {@dice 1d4} and define what type of feeling is particularly turbulent within you today. These feelings can encompass many others, such as Wrath also accounting for frustration or annoyance, Elation to being particularly inspired or Apathy to being extremely focused. During the day, important events may shift your Look to something else, the DM says when and what it changes into. As an example, a dragon eating your legs would turn you from Elation to probable Sorrow or Wrath.

rows: Sorrow
Elation
Wrath
Apathy

entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Passionate Emotions
entries: You focus on attuning even more with the emotions that currently have their reigns on you, gaining Expertise for one minute with certain skills depending on your current Look, as described below:

rows: Sorrow
{@b Paranoia.} {@skill Insight} and {@skill Investigation}.
Elation
{@b Overjoyed.} {@skill Persuasion} and {@skill Performance}.
Wrath
{@b Enraged.} {@skill Intimidation} and {@skill Athletics}.
Apathy
{@b Focused.} {@skill Perception} and {@skill Stealth}.

entries.name: Coagulate Feelings
entries: You fully embrace the feeling that lays deep in your heart at the moment, letting it out in a flurry of emotions. You gain the following abilities depending on your current emotions:

rows: Sorrow

{@b Whirlpool of Sadness.} As an action you may let out the waterfalls of your tears out, magically becoming greater and greater in size as you wallow. Any creature within 15-feet of you must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or be pulled to the nearest unnocupied space within 5-feet of you, as the torrent of tears draws them closer. You gain advantage on attacks against those creatures until the end of your next turn.
Elation

{@b Joyful Rush.} As a bonus action on your turn, a gale of your elation swirls around you and all friendly creatures within 15-feet of you, gaining an additional 10 feet of movement speed until the end of their next turn, also gaining advantage on the first attack of their turn for that duration.
Wrath

{@b Rapture in Hatred.} As a part of your attack action, you may let out a mighty roar and engulf your weapon in the flames of your rage. Your next hit deals an additional {@damage 4d8} fire damage on a hit, or half if you miss, as the heat is still unbearable. This value increases by an additional D8 on each level you'd gain a feature in this subclass.
Apathy

{@b Icy Focus.} As a bonus action, you steel your resolve and with a deep breath end both the {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Frightened} condition on yourself, gaining immunity to them until the end of your next turn. In addition, for this moment of focus, you land a critical hit on a roll of 19 or higher, before any modifiers.

subclassFeature.name: Oblivion to All Usurpers

entries: I don’t want to live a life of being thieved any longer…

You have become a figure of grace for your god, a stalward pillar they may lean on as much as you lean on them for support on your rising life, and that has you be entrusted with a mighty, milacrous power to wield. When you use your Channel Divinity: {@item The Road Back|TheUndertomesASV} From Oblivion you may instead force another creature to meet your god’s punishment.

When you do this targetting an unwilling creature they must pass a Wisdom saving throw or be momentareousl transported with you to a demiplane where your god resides, with its features and aesthetic directly reflecting that of the deity you have followed for so long. The target may get asked a question from your deity, such as if they are sorry for their past infrictions or a piece of knowledge as to why they have behaved in such a horrid way - On a response that pleases your deity ( As per your GM’s discretion ) the creature is only drained of their energy so they may also experience the regrowth you have, suffering 5 points of {@condition Exhaustion}. On one that displeases your Deity they suffer {@dice 12d10} force damage as celestial might sears through them, a brand being cast upon their back and having them suffer the effects of both the Hex spell targeting one Attribute of your choice and the Locate Creature spell allowing any other Immemorial Domain cleric to sense them freely. Both these effects last until the creature dies.

After this judgement you both are transported back into the material plane. Furthermore, you may rely upon your god for a miracle, allowing you to spend your action to cast one spell you know but haven’t prepared ( still spending the appropriate spell slot ) once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Obsidian Stormrider's Ascent

entries: "Ride, beating of hooves. Rise, grains of sand. Ring, cries of war. Rest, for your flight shall meet a dead end."

As a Bonus Action you may spend a use of your your Wildshape feature to enter a {@i Stormrider Form} having your body morph and change as a violent gale engulfs it. Your lower body becomes that of a trampling beast for the next minute, granting you the following features:

items: Your movement speed increases by 10-ft and your legs are changed or reinforced, allowing you to use your Kicks as a natural melee weapon you are Proficient with. These have the Finesse property and deal {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage on a hit.

You may choose to inflict a value of any combination of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus on a melee weapon hit. Additionally, whenever you hit a creature for the first time during your turn they suffer one count of {@condition Concussion|TheUndertomesOS}.
For the duration the weapon you wield counts as a Druidic Focus for you to be able to cast Druid spells through it even if you have no free hand to do so.

When you spend a use of your Wildshape to enter this form, you gain an amount of Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Maximum Hit Points. You may benefit form this a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries: Additionally you may spend your Bonus Action to stamp your hooves in the ground and let a building storm gather around you as you kick up the dust in your path. Gaining a cumulative +1 bonus modifier to your Armor Class for each 10-ft. travelled until the end of your turn.

When you next perform a melee weapon attack you may choose to turn all this momentum into more force for your attack, consuming up to any amount of additional AC gained this way to fling the target toward anywhere within a radius equal to 5-ft. plus an additional 5-ft. per AC consumed this way.

If this creature falls on a wall or at least medium-sized object, it suffers an amount of d6 bludgeoning damage per 5-ft. travelled. If it falls on another creature, they suffer the same amount of damage and the creature being fallen upon must pass a Dexterity save against your Druid Spell Save DC or suffer the same damage. Creatures who suffer this damage become {@condition prone} afterward and you may choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after dealing this damage.
All bonus Armor Class gained this way is reset to 0 at the start of your next turn and you can't use this ability again until the end of your turn.
Your {@i Stormrider Form} lasts for up to one minute or until you are knocked {@condition unconscious}. Upon leaving this form you lose any remaining Temporary Hit Points gained from it.

subclassFeature.name: Old Master Otherworldly Patron
entries: {@i A Warlock Subclass by The Undertomes}

Somewhere, hidden in the veil that permeates the multiverse, lies a haunted manor that was once the target of a powerful, ancient curse. The master of the manor has long since lost their life, but their soul was bound to its impenetrable walls.

Their servants? Those that did not leave were cursed as well. They roam and safekeep the manor, hoping that one day this curse will be broken and their old master will once more return to his prime and save them all from this accursed existence. You, somehow, wandered through its walls, experienced the memories of the lives imprisoned within, and became another servant of the manor’s master - with the grace of being able to leave its gate unharmed.
Now, you travel the world as the old master commands, in search of a way to unseal the bindings and break the cursed chains that keep them and your fellow servants there.

subclassFeature.name: One Step Ahead
entries: One of the most important qualities of a musketeer of smiles is knowing how to please and excite the crowd with their charismatic fighting style. Once you reach 7th level, after hitting an enemy with an attack, you may use a bonus action to roll a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. The DC for this check is equal to 10+ the Challenge Rating or Level of the creature you hit, whichever applies.

On a success, all allies within 30 feet of you gain advantage on their next attack roll and saving throw until the start of your next turn. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Over the Moon
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} action, you gain 3 stacks of {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesMW}. During that action, you can jump in a straight line up to your speed and make a melee weapon attack against a creature along the distance traveled. Opportunity attacks made against you during this movement have disadvantage. On a hit, the target suffers 3 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and this attack does not reduce its {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} value if it triggers the condition.

If you would hit a wall during the jump, you can use your bonus action to press against it and gain 20 additional feet of movement until you touch the ground, allowing you to wall-jump. You have advantage on any Athletics check required by this feature.
Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Overclocked Cleanse
entries: The selection of tools in your belt is already sizeable, yet you have just devised something that can break past many limits, many roadblocks and it only requires a considerably large battery.
Upon reaching 15th level, you choose one of the following Overclocked Cleaning Supplies. You may only change it at 18th level, if you so desire.

entries.name: Rip Space.
entries: As an action, you may spend 10 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to Overclock your Issued Weapon to its limits, the air around a 30-foot-wide, 15-foot long cone in front of you crackling with plasma. You deliver a vicious wound to space itself, creating a gash that cuts all creatures caught within the cone, these must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take {@dice 6d10} force damage, additionally they suffer from 3 stacks of {@condition Dimensional Rift|TheUndertomesDS}, which has them suffer double that number in {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks at the end of their turn, then destroying the {@condition Dimensional Rift|TheUndertomesDS} stacks.

entries.name: Express Restoration.
entries: You use up 8 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and your action to Overclock restoration mechanisms on your person, a pulse sweeps around a 60-feet area around yourself, rebuilding any objects and structures to be in their pristine state, in addition you may choose up to 6 creatures within reach, these creatures are healed by {@dice 6d8+8|6d8 + 8} hit points.

entries.name: D.D.E.D.R.
entries: You fully enable a direct Overclock to your Issued Weapon, also focusing its nearly unwieldy power to unleash the most amount of pain possible. By spending 10 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and your action, you may declare a target for D.D.E.D.R., you then make a sequence of four attacks against the target. You gain a +1 bonus to hit and to damage for each attack you land, additionally all damage you would deal until the end of your turn is instead considered force damage, you also deal an additional {@dice 1d8} force damage per hit.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Lifestop
entries: There are two very distinct types of people who've signed into the Lifestop, yet they both meld in one thing alone: Desperation.

The Lifestop can be found as many things. For instance, in the Forgotten Realms, the Lifestop is an animated concept given form in an ethereal mist which eludes its chosen as to its whims, instead giving them task after task, aiming for those with no other choice than to take them, for only with the entity's patronage will they be able to survive a hash existence.

In other realms, such as Eberron, this pact isn't such a boon-laden contract with the external, but a promise to the self, with this pact being found amongst the vagabond and down-trotten, trying to eke out their livelihoods through the scarcity of life in a war-torn land.

When creating a Warlock with this Pact, reflect about what made them have the necessity for such a lifestyle, are they a small-time adventurer trying to scrape by tough times in life? Maybe a noble who'd rather only use the best quality munitions available? Or even one who while hunting for their righteous revenge against another, found a possessed revolver with just enough bullets to finish the job, only to have it slowly grind down your brain.

Also take in consideration the possibility of reflavouring this Subclass to best fit your desired character, such as taking any spells learned and spell slots as gadgets to be spent, rather than purely magical effects.

subclassFeature.name: Parade's Bloodfeast
entries: The vital fluid that flows out of the creatures you pierce serves as fuel for your {@skill Performance} and the parade which it conducts. Whenever you inflict a creature with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, and when you use it to fuel your own abilities. The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 during a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Parlor's Bloodfeast
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you've found a way to harden and weave the very blood of other beings. Whenever you inflict a creature with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, and when you use it to fuel your own skills. The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 at the end of combat.

subclassFeature.name: Partial Mutation Training
entries: You can help your allies accompany your speed on a hunt. As an action, you provide a speed talisman to one ally. For 1 hour, its speed increases by 10 feet, after which the talisman burns away. At 13th level, you can provide two talismans to one or two allies. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Additionally, as a bonus action, you can jump a number of feet equal to five times your proficiency bonus without provoking opportunity attacks. You can use this ability once and only while your speed is greater than 0. You regain the expended use when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Party Crashout
entries: Whenever a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} is killed, you recover one warlock spell slot. This can occur a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, per short rest.

Whenever a creature suffers {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} for the first time, rageful duty grants you a surge of power. Whenever you deal damage, you deal an additional {@damage 3d6} psychic damage. This bonus diminishes by {@damage 1d6} at the end of each of your turns.

When a creature bearing {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} or a Vendetta Mark is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} for the first time in combat or killed, you can use your reaction to Boast. Up to three creatures of your choice can add your Charisma modifier to the first attack roll they make before the end of their next turn.
You gain the following additional uses for Offense Points:

items: You can spend 3 Offense Points to inflict {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} on a creature within 60 feet even if it has not Offended you.
Once per combat, you can recharge one use of a Mystic Arcanum spell by spending Offense Points equal to that spell's level + 4.

subclassFeature.name: Party Rapport Style
entries: Choose one of the following styles, which reflects how you support your companions in battle.

items: {@b Walls of Fire.} As a bonus action, choose up to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) hostile creatures within 60 feet. Each must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC. On a failure, it must use all available movement to approach you and focus its attacks on you. A creature engaged with another creature has advantage on the save. While you are more than 20 feet from every friendly creature, you gain +1 AC for each hostile creature within 5 feet of you, to a maximum of +3.

{@b Great Mountain.} When a creature within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 2d8}, plus {@dice 1d8} for every 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts on the attacker, to a maximum of {@dice 3d8} additional reduction. The base reduction increases by {@dice 1d8} at 12th level and again at 18th level.

{@b Level-Headed Emotion.} Once per turn as a free action, choose a friendly creature within 60 feet. It gains a bonus equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to its next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw. You can expend your Second Wind when you grant this bonus to make it last until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Partybringer
entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Offense Points to summon a magical instrument that plays on its own, usually a spectral boombox carried over your shoulder. Each friendly creature that can hear it within 30 feet gains a {@dice 1d4} bonus to attack rolls and saving throws. Whenever one of those creatures deals damage, it deals an additional {@damage 1d4} thunder damage; you instead deal an additional {@damage 2d4} thunder damage.

At the start of each of your turns, you must spend 2 Offense Points as a free action to continue the music, or the instrument vanishes and the effect ends. At 12th level, the bonus to attack rolls and saving throws increases by 1, affected creatures deal {@damage 2d4} additional thunder damage, and you deal {@damage 3d4} additional thunder damage. At 18th level, the radius increases to 60 feet, and all thunder damage dealt through this effect is doubled against wooden, metal, and crystalline structures and objects.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Grievance
entries: Barbarians of the Path of Grievance never forgive and never forget. They remember every slight committed against them and other members of their clan, and will go through all ordeals necessary to see the perpetrators of such crimes be thoroughly punished. They are armed solely with their fists and with magic tattoos given to them after they exact final vengeance, with the purpose of making them stronger. The more tattoos in your skin, the higher your ranking at the clan.

In the Forgotten Realms, the city of Waterdeep has grown restless with fear over a criminal group comprised of people that follow this way of life. Known as the Half, because none of their members are complete without each other, the Barbarians that stem from this family are known for being swift deliverers of vengeance over the smallest injuries and remarks raised against their own.

In the universe of Project Moon, the Middle is one of the Fingers, and, consequently, a Star of the City. They record all injustices made against their members in a book, repaying not in kind, but in cruelty, everything done against them tenfold. Members of the Middle see each other as a family, and would die for the honor of their brothers and sisters.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Precognition

entries: "... I've already waited way past with what anyone oughta put up with. And right when I thought I was finally getting my ass outta this goddamn cold, what happens? My Ticket turns into blank scrap paper, all because of that mongrel brat! Ha... Haha... Gimme a fucking break."

You have found a powerful relic capable of seeing a few seconds into the future, and you have repurposed it into one of your eyes so that your enemies never reach you again. When it overheats, so does your rage, allowing you to hit your enemies with incredible might as a practicioner of La Spada di Palermo, a powerful and fast sword style that confuses most opponents.

You are a washed-up member of the Thumb, a powerful criminal syndicate that values hierarchy above all else. Maybe you were a powerful leader that fell from grace, or you never amounted to much to begin with, but the Thumb has assigned you to be one of the lowest of the low.

Barbarians from the Path of Precognition tend to believe they know everything, and all outcomes were obvious for them. At their best, they are wise leaders that guide their underlings to be their best. At their worst, they're manipulative and vindictive, trying

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Hammer of Faith

entries: "Everything-I'll burn it all... and my whole disgusting life, too."

Those who thread this Primal Path, the ones who take up the Hammer of Faith and embody it are rare prodigies who wield their irate belief like a weapon of mass distruction on those infidel to their preachings. There is no qualm taken in avoiding violence when needed, nor a sacrifice too great for the good of all.

These Barbarians are known for their intense fanaticism toward their belief and legends spread about the few who exist, as they often take to battlefields and single handedly decimate hordes upon their single-minded purge toward a pure world, not to mention the sheer brutality that they wield to carry out their wills.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms... No, there is no god of such a world that would be capable of enticing such faith. It is in the creeping shadows of Ravenloft that the names of forgotten gods are both whispered and screeched openly, a faith born from nothing and elevated into itself. In others, such as the futuristic world of Keybreak, these are the ones who neglect the integration of flesh and machinery, tearing it apart with gusto so that every corrupted being will have their rotten soul expunged before they can trace fingers upon the sheep who remain pure yet.

entries.subclassFeature: Disgust of the Faithful|Barbarian|PHB|Hammer of Faith|TheUndertomesHF|3
Scripture of Truth Within|Barbarian|PHB|Hammer of Faith|TheUndertomesHF|3

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Magical Girl
entries: The Forgotten Realms, the lost cities within... They all need a hero to aid them in their time of need, for justice, for love!.. Oh, NAY, THE ENTIRE MULTIVERSE NEEDS SUCH!

Magical Girls of Love & Hatred are a rare sight to say the least, born from an overabundance of emotion usually, these quasi-bardic people are actually not limited only to females, attaining the name because of unusual chains of events.

As a Magical Girl of Love & Hatred your Rage action is not fueled only by anger, but mayhaps by the indomitable will to bring out justice to the realms, all in the name of love and compassion!... Or to stamp out the hatred stirring deep within you in any villains in your path. These barbarians aren't ever exactly "good", despite what they seem to believe, instead they are single mindedly focused on the desire to do good, to feel needed and will use their near delirious states of mind and strangely specific magic to bring out the "Love" they need.

entries.subclassFeature: In the Name of Love!|Barbarian|PHB|Magical Girl|TheUndertomesMG|3

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Rooster

entries: "Is that it?! Where are the rest? Where?! I ain't stopping 'till- [inhales] ... Fine... Keep it down. I've got to keep this down... or I won't get to fight another day."

Barbarians following the Path of the Rooster have been permanently changed by a powerful magic likening their appearance and instincts to those of the same animal. Usually members of the Heishou Packs, these Barbarians are commanded by the highest payers or strongest authorities, the ones holding the leash of their Packs, to wreak havoc and destruction upon their enemies. In the Forgotten Realms, these Barbarians are usually part of a gang of bandits hired for their lust for battle, unafraid to die in combat as long as they can take out one more enemy. You were born, or transformed, to fight until your last breath.

entries.name: Peck 'Em

entries: "Ya-hah! Now are the rest? Where?! I ain't stopping 'till there's no more of 'em to peck... For to keep this down... or I won't get to fight another day!"

Your body has been altered to sport powerful feathers made to boost your aggression despite damage to yourself. You gain resistance to fire damage, and once per short rest you can use a Reaction when you would take fall damage to negate that damage instead, as long as you didn't fall more than 100 feet.

entries.name: Bloody Storm of Blades

entries: "Ah... and here I thought I'd manage to keep it cool all day today."

You do not simply rage, your fury and lust for battle boil and spill over like an erupting volcano. While you are raging, once per turn when you hit an attack, you gain 1 count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR}. Additionally, you gain 1 count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} when you score a critical hit, when you attack a creature with half or less of its total hit points, or when a creature dies or falls unconscious within 15 feet of you.

While you have counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR}, your attacks also deal 1 count of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to the target and 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to yourself. While you have counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you won't stop raging even if you haven't attacked a hostile creature or taken damage, and you add +1 to your rage damage bonus for every 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} you have on yourself, to a maximum of +3.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Warfare
entries: You gain access to the following Master Ardent Techniques.

entries.caption: Master Ardent Techniques
rows: Perfected Death Fist
Action

Make a melee attack. On a hit, it deals an additional {@damage 2d10} fire damage plus {@damage 1d8} fire damage per {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count on the target. Each other creature within 5 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC, taking the same fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
Pinpoint Blitz
Action

Make four melee attacks against one creature. Each hit inflicts one more {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count than the previous hit. If the target has more than 5 Burn counts, these attacks gain +2 to hit and deal 2 additional fire damage per Burn count. If the first three attacks hit and are not resisted, the fourth gains +3 to hit instead and deals 4 additional fire damage per Burn count; on a hit, the target then loses all Burn counts.
Inner Gate Elbow Strike
Action

Make a melee attack. On a hit, it deals an additional {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage, plus {@damage 2d10} fire damage if the target has more than 5 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. The target must make a Constitution saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC.
