On a failure, it takes a penalty to attack rolls and saving throws equal to its Burn count until the end of its next turn. A creature without a nervous system or unable to feel pain is immune to this effect.
Perfect Palm Strike
Attack

Replace one attack of your Attack action with a melee attack that deals an additional {@damage 2d12} fire damage on a hit. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC. Its AC is reduced by 2, plus 1 for every 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts it has (maximum reduction 6), or by half that amount on a success. Magical armor and natural armor recover after 3 of the creature's turns.
Cerulean Blaze Spread
Bonus Action
Choose a friendly creature within 10 feet. Until the end of your next turn, it gains your resistance to psychic damage and proficiency in Wisdom saving throws from Fire Tempered in Moonlight.

entries: Once per short or long rest, you can use one Ardent Technique without spending its minimum Ardor Point cost.

subclassFeature.name: Perfected Marksmanship
entries: Your eyes have been engraved with your patron's magic, evolving to become unerring in their coordination with your hands. When you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK}, a creature automatically fails its saving throw unless it expends a Legendary Resistance. Furthermore, when you reach 18th level, you can always choose which Magic Bullet to fire, regardless of which one is currently in your Marksman's Weapon's chamber.

subclassFeature.name: Pierce Heaven

entries: "The pelting raindrops shroud the falling arrows, and they will die in the downpour without knowing what killed them."

Mastering control over the elements is what classifies you as a sniper that stands out among the rest, showcasing your incredible skill and unparalleled ability. While you are focusing your aim with the Snipe arrows, you can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty, able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. Additionally, even if you are {@condition Incapacitated}, {@condition Paralyzed}, {@condition Petrified}, {@condition Stunned} or {@condition Unconscious}, you can still make an attack roll as long as you were focusing an attack with your Glimmering Bow [弓閃] feature.

Once per long rest, you can cast the {@spell control weather|PHB|Control Weather} spell without spending a spell slot or material components by shooting a magical arrow into the skies. However, if you cast it this way the casting time is an action, it is a concentration spell that lasts for 1 minute and the change to the weather is instantaneous.
If it's raining or snowing, you may use a bonus action to gain the {@condition Invisible} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Poesie per il Silenzio

entries: "La vittoria ama chi più osa."

Much like a poet weaving hymn and rhyme together, your varied weaponry is swung not with wild abandon, but with a rhythm that unites all you can give. Whenever you perform a weapon attack, if your next attack is made with a different weapon you gain special effects as per the last weapon used. These are as follows:

items: {@b Dagger:} Your next attack gains the Dagger's Thrown property and range.
{@b Greatsword:} Your next attack inflicts additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
{@b Handaxe:} Your next attack is done with advantage.
{@b Heavy Gauntlet:} You may choose to move yourself and the target 5-ft. forward after this attack and on your next attack's hit.
{@b Katana:} Your next attack gains the Katana's {@itemProperty DRW|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Draw} property and is treated as if the weapon is sheathed.
{@b Lance:} Your next attack gains the Lance's Reach property.
{@b Light Hammer:} Your next attack considers its target as if it had 1 less AC.
{@b Longsword:} Your next attack deals damage even if missed. Roll your damage die without any modifiers, the target takes half the value rolled.
{@b Mace:} Your next attack deals an additional damage die.
{@b Revolver:} Before your next attack you may move up to half your movement speed toward any target creature within your attack range without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Rifle:} Before your next attack you may move up to half your movement speed away from any target creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Shortsword:} our next attack has a +1 bonus modifier to hit.

entries: More weapons can be found at the end of this subclass, separated into weapon groups according to the effects above.

subclassFeature.name: Polar Harmony Sorcerous Origin
entries: It is a terrifying life, that of all beings. The presence of the uncertain is the only possibility of which one may have certainty of, and that is one fear that resonates particularly with the Sorcerers who awaken a bloodline of Polar Harmony, those who are so entwined with some concept that they call Order that the unshapely future that takes hold of all feels wrong to them.

They are creatures who can be as cold as can they be expressive, executives of tight restraints that demonstrate the most well controlled points of sorcerous magic, yet that can paradoxically come crashing down upon the realization that deep down all their fear comes from their own inner disharmony. That crash, however, can also come to be what can set them apart, what renders them capable to finally harmonize a world that is so often out of sync.

In worlds such as Eberron, they are one of the rare products of attempting to restore some order to the world, created at the rare blessing of Daanvi to help those who yet remain. In others, such as Keybreak, they are the rare few who manifest a blessing from the Machine Gods which connect all things, being forced to bear enormous capabilities as well as the frights that keep the world never sleeping.

entries.name: Polar Harmony Origins
entries: Those in the Polar Harmony bloodline tend to be born with their powers and the afflictions brought unto them, which take form not only in the magical prowess they hold but in the prejudices that they apply to the world. How has this shaped you? Is your body warped and your flesh replaced with the simple efficiency of metal? Or was it your mind that was straightened to a greater will? The following table has a number of manifestations which are commonplace for such a Sorcerer, and you may roll on it for inspiration regarding your character's appearance:

entries.caption: Polar Harmony Manifestations
rows: Your eyes have different pigmentations. Whenever in the presence of powerful magic or whenever you are casting spells, they glow.
A halo of metal that resembles that of an aasimar hangs behind your head, floating in tandem with your movement.
Those who sleep near you have the static of your thoughts creep into their dreams sometimes, as if you were always emitting a radio that cannot be turned off.
Your hands are akin to porcelain, impossible to be blemished and soft to the touch, yet are always condemned to feel brittle whenever you grasp something tightly.
Your face is locked in a perpetual neutral face, having your head be one that can hardly ever show emotions.
Your voice is melodic and harmoniously flowing, as if forever tuned to a machinesque quality. However, your heart's wants are hard to keep down in your chest, and often slip through your words.

subclassFeature.name: Polar Harmony Spells

entries: "She is the most perfect and most obedient tool which mankind ever possessed! Tonight you will see her succeed before the upper ten thousand."

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Polar Harmony Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be a abjuration or an enchantment spell from the artificer, sorcerer, or wizard spell list.

entries.caption: Polar Harmony Spells
rows: {@spell Alarm|PHB}, {@spell Bane|PHB}
{@spell Earthbind|XGE}, {@spell Sound of Repudiation|TheUndertomesPH}
{@spell Land of Smiles|TheUndertomesASF}, {@spell Tongues|PHB}
{@spell Arcane Eye|PHB}, {@spell Orb of Balance|TheUndertomesASF}
{@spell Geas|PHB}, {@spell Wall of Force|PHB}

subclassFeature.name: Poppin’ Pleasures

entries: It’s scary at first, but the next step won’t be difficult at all.

As an Action on your turn you may cause the elation on Thorn-afflicted creatures to manifest physically in a mist of bubbles that quickly pop around them, instantly dealing {@dice 1d6} psychic damage per Thorns Rank and forcing all creatures within 5-ft of the afflicted to attempt a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer the same damage. This feels like a deep surge of joy that is soon taken away to nothingness.
When the powder that falls from the thorns becomes known to the world, people may forever sink into the swamp of intoxication.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Flame
entries: You gain access to the following Advanced Ardent Techniques.

entries.caption: Advanced Ardent Techniques
rows: Flowing Flame
Free Action
When your next attack hits, it inflicts 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count. Your following attack has advantage and inflicts twice its normal Burn counts.
Flame Cleave
Attack

Choose up to three targets in your reach, each within 5 feet of another target. Make one melee attack and damage roll and compare the attack with each target's AC. The attack gains +1 to hit and damage for every 3 total {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts among the targets.
Rush Down
Bonus Action
Move up to 15 feet toward a creature, then make two unarmed strikes against it without adding your ability modifier to the damage.
Gale Kick
Reaction

When a creature within 60 feet misses you with an attack, make a melee attack against it regardless of distance. On a hit, it suffers 4 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Spellcasting

entries: No… Don’t take away what is mine, not again…
You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Spellcasting

entries: It stood still, giving no response.
You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Spellcasting

entries: "The talismans in hand have turned into sticky blood, slipping between your fingers."
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Powder of Life

entries: Here, child… I’ll give you new life.

You are a cleric who wishes to have the world itself heal in the image of your deity, and that has carried over with a fair share of blessings to enact such an old, tired and kind will. Whenever you heal a creature with a spell or are the cause for another creature to recover hit points, you gain one Lifepowder count. You also gain one Lifepowder count after a short rest or 3 counts during a long rest, being able to hold a maximum amount equal to double your proficiency bonus.
You may spend up to 2 times your proficiency bonus’ worth of Lifepowder to share blessings with the world, having the following effects:

items: As part of healing a creature you may, as part of the same action or bonus action used to do so, grant them a blessing of vigour. That creature also gains an amount of d6 temporary health equal to the sum of each 2 Lifepowder spent.

As an action during your turn you may spend 3 and sprinkle Lifepowder atop a weapon, fruit or vegetable within 5-ft of you that is not being carried or worn. The object of your sprinkling becomes animate for the next minute, growing small arms and legs of metal or twine and roots, acting after you in initiative. This object has an AC of 12 and an amount of hit points equal to ( 8 + the object’s rarity, such as a common object being 1, uncommon being 2 and so on. ) times your proficiency bonus. You may spend a free action on your turn to order the object to walk up to 25-ft. and perform a melee weapon attack using your spellcasting modifier. It’s damage and properties are determined by whatever object it is, with a weapon using it’s own properties while a piece of food instead using whatever weapon you and the GM would find most appropriate, such as a carrot being a dagger or a pumpkin being a warhammer. The object loses all magical properties after a minute passes, but if you use this more than 7 times on the same object it is then permanently under these effects until reduced to 0 hit points or you use this 7 times or another object, as to where the oldest loses it’s properties.

As an action during your turn you may blow out an amount of Lifepowder onto an object or structure to mend it as per the Mending cantrip’s effects, except it covers a 5-ft. by 5-ft. cube per count of Lifepowder spent, to a minimum of 5- ft. by 5-ft. cube and a maximum of a 60-ft.by 60-ft. cube.

subclassFeature.name: Power of the Past

entries: All I have left now… are these children.

Your connection to the world has deepened, with every weather-beaten tree and paved road lighting up to you as you have embraced its simple existance, having engrained the knowledge that the road to recovery is one built from the smallest things. You gain access to the Druid spell list, being able to prepare their spells as if they were Cleric spells.
Furthermore, whenever you heal a creature for a value that surpasses their maximum amount of hit points, any surplus hit points become temporary hit points for them.

subclassFeature.name: Pre-Ordained Strikes

entries: "...Yet my visage, seared and scorched, permits me not a day of reprieve from pain-oh, how it aches even under the gentlest sun."

You gain the ability to channel the Will through your fingertips so your swings may always find their mark, even if that puts you in harm's way. When you miss an attack roll, you may choose to still roll damage and deal half the result still, but suffer the same damage dealt. This does not count as a hit for other effects purposes and inflicts only half any Condition/Effect count that would be inflicted.

You may do this an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short or long rest. Additionally, once per long rest you may consume one count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD} to always deal full damage on a missed attack, but you still suffer half of that damage.

subclassFeature.name: Preparations of the Suffering
entries: To endure what lies ahead, you've developed rituals-strange habits that sharpen your mind, soothe your soul, or fuel your grief. During a long rest, you may perform one of the following in addition to other restful activities:

items: Commiserate. You immerse yourself in a private, brooding sorrow to prepare for the misfortunes yet to come. When you do, you gain advantage on Wisdom saving throws until your next long rest. You may invite up to a number of willing creatures equal to your proficiency bonus to share in this melancholic state; they gain the same benefit.

Bask in Needs. You indulge in your cravings; whether it's listening to calming music, sharpening your favorite blades, or engaging in other eccentric habits. This indulgence sharpens your focus. Until your next long rest, you gain a bonus to hit on the first attack you make on each of your turns turns equal to your proficiency bonus.

Endure the Nightmare. You sit with your visions-the horrors that claw at your mind-and use this moment of reprieve to master them. Until your next long rest, your melee weapon attacks inflict 2 stacks of a {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the first hit of your turn, as your pain seeps into your blade and manifests in each strike.

subclassFeature.name: Prepared Fool
entries: Nothing is built in one day, much less a grand archive of knowledge. You, however, have been taking notes - Building up your own cookbook to remedy any unforeseen situation you and your comrades may find yourselves in. As such, during a Long Rest you may create up to half your Proficiency Bonus' worth of the following selection of Artificer Infusions, rounded down:

items: {@optfeature Vibroweld Morph-Combat Cane|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Faker's Grenade|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Junk Surprise|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Collective's Pocket Watch|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Friendly Warning|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Monocle of Breaking Down|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Wind-up Spanner|TheUndertomesDX}
{@optfeature Replicate Magic Item|TCE}

entries: These gadgets are usually made of rackety materials and are highly volatile, so they tend to break down by your next Long Rest, causing them to be lost if not used but providing scrap so that you don't have to waste any gold in their creation. Furthermore, you've learnt how to keep the knowledge of materials like these on the down low, having any creature who attempts an {@skill Insight} skill check against you be forced to do so at Disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Path du Corset Rouge
entries: Those who chose to don le Corset Rouge are drawn by their own cravings to act upon life with little restraint, being a Primal Path that is throdden not with rage in the heart but pure ambition and desire at the root of one's being, shamelessly tearing through everything as if the person had an unfillable void at their stomach - One that is rarely diminished by simply consuming fleash, but in donning and working it to utmost perfection.

At their best, they are incredibly high-achieving and dedicated people who will stop at nothing to reach their goals and incentivize others to do so as well as if this glamorous existance was a form of attempting apotheosis amongst the living. At their worst, they are zealots of pleasure and unhinged creatures bereft of anything that can come to resemble common sense, if it is applicable in the same way the generic person may apply it.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, these have began to sprout around in various cultist cells trying to birth their own good of Feasting and act with a religious hierarchy in mind, preparing for the Grand Buffet. In others such as that of Balefire, they are ever-present amongst the ranks of the Gilded Saint's, eating away at their god's hoard as much as they consume its flesh, turning their horrendous desert into a landscape painted red with each passing day.

entries.subclassFeature: Tirer du Sens de l'Émotion Brute|Barbarian|PHB|Corset Rouge|TheUndertomesCR|3

subclassFeature.name: Priory's Bloodfeast
entries: Starting at first level, your misericordious hands have dipped into the blood of the sinful, and with them you may flagellate evil as you see necessary.

Whenever you may inflict a creature with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, and when you use it to fuel your own abilities. The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 during a long rest.
Additionally, your relationship to the purifying nature of pain has left you tougher than most. Whenever you gain a level in this class and at first level you gain an additional maximum hit point

subclassFeature.name: Profigy of Divine Purity

entries: "It's only natural. Because I... am the chosen one... Isn't that right?"

You have risen way past the ranks of your fellows to be that which grips divinity itself and holds it high as the guiding star to your people, enabling you to reach a state that can be considered nothing short of sanctified. Your abilities are improved in the following ways:

items: Whenever you enter Rage and become {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF} the very air around you changes. Every creature within a 60-ft. radius may also choose to become a {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF}. Every hostile creature within reach must pass a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened}. If they choose to become {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF}, they are also {@condition charmed} by you while you are Raging. This save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of your Strength or Constitution modifier.

You and any other {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF} creatures within 30-ft. of you while you are a {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF} yourself gain a +2 bonus to Wisdom saving throws, Advantage against being {@condition frightened} and Immunity to being {@condition charmed}.

Creatures who became {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF} through you inflict one {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count on a hit and suffer one roll of their Hit Die of psychic damage at the end of their turns. This damage cannot be reduced in any way.
Creatures Immobilized by your Crucifixion ability are instead {@condition paralyzed} until the end of your next turn.
You also gain a +1 modifier to damage for every +1 modifier attack rolls granted by creatures suffering from {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF|Nails}.
You cannot have your Hit Points reduced below 1 by psychic damage.

If you would be a target to an effect that would cause you to become or {@condition frightened} you may once per long rest spend your Reaction to instantly become a {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF} until the source of the Condition is dead or has been out of your sight for at least an hour. If you become or {@condition frightened}, your faith crumbles and pierces through your mind though. Any positive modifiers you would have to rolls instead become negative modifiers, such as your Strength modifier to attack and you suffer {@damage 2d12} psychic damage at the end of your turns while suffering from the Condition.

entries: Additionally, you may indoctrinate other creatures to partake in your faith during long rests. After doing so once, indoctrinated creatures gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to {@skill Religion} checks until their next long rest. Upon doing so twice, they gain {@dice 1d6} instead. Upon the third time, they become permanently Proficient in the skill instead. If you have Expertise in Religion, any creature who has spent fourteen long rests being indoctrinated by you gains Expertise in Religion permanently.

subclassFeature.name: Pure Adoration

entries: Melting Love makes those who look at it feel affection without realizing it.

Others tend to look up to you in adoration, granting you proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill, or Expertise if you already were proficient in this skill. Furthermore, this adoration extends chiefly to your allies, giving them a subtle yet persistent boost to morale while you are around them.
Creatures within 30-ft. of you gain a further additional modifier to their rolls equal to half your Charisma modifier when they spend your Bardic Inspiration dice, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Pursuance

entries: I will pray for you, so that you shall surely break.

You always carry the teachings of your god close to you, looking for ways to correct other beings into becoming better, purer creatures of faith. You carry with yourself an emerald tablet. If lost or destroyed, it can be magically reconstructed during a long rest. You can control this emerald tablet as a free action and make it float around you to an area of up to 30 feet. This tablet holds tenets which you can see in the Emerald Tablet Tenets table. If a creature within 30 feet of the emerald tablet breaks one of its tenets, you may use a reaction to activate a Lesser Punishment or a Higher Punishment from the table.

entries.caption: Emerald Tablet Tenets
rows: No vile creature shall strike the weak (when a creature hits another creature missing at least half of their Hit Points)
They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or gain -2 to their attack rolls until the end of the turn.
They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or lose all of their extra attacks until the end of their next turn.
No vile creature shall strike the backs of those that retreat (a creature uses an opportunity attack reaction against another creature)

They must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer 2 counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At the end of their next turn, they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

They must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be struck by a giant heavenly fist, suffering 2 counts of Tremor and immediately suffering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. You can heal a number of creatures within 30 feet of the tablet equal to your Wisdom modifier by half the amount of damage dealt.
No righteous creature shall go without enacting justice (when a creature misses an attack roll)
You allow them to use their reaction to perform another attack roll.
Until the end of their next turn, they gain a +2 to all attack rolls and +1 to their AC.

subclassFeature.name: Purvey The Marvelous Christmas Tree!
entries: Your devotion to the spirits of holidays long past and to come have bore fruit in the greatest gift of all, granting you your choice of the following benefits which must be chosen when reaching 14th level in Warlock:

items: When you take the {@action Help|Aid Action} you may spend one of your Warlock Spell Slots to grant the target your choice of a temporary Spell Slot ( Up to 5th Level ) or grant them an Additional Attack as part of the {@action Attack} action or Reaction. These last until the start of your next turn.

Items created by the Gnomic Raiders Giftbox also have special chemicals applied to them. They never rot. You may also have the Gnomes make Uncommon items of your choice, as long as you have been Attuned to the item before. These items can only be gifted to other creatures willingly and without a transaction, they can't be sold or traded for other items or they will instantly become a pile of snow, as the Spirits frown upon such greedy endeavours over the holiday spirit.

The Cheerful Spirits grant you an allowance of gold, to which you can instantly spend to take out a non-magical item out of your Giftbox. It is of pristine condition and always wrapped in colorful ribbons. This item fades into snow after a week and the allowance you are granted is of 100 GP on a short rest and 500 GP on a long rest. Any surplus value left over is instantly spent on eggnog during a short or long rest, which grants you and all friendly creatures who spent the long rest with you advantage on their first Charisma check until the next long rest.

entries: Furthermore, you can ask them for help in a pinch. Once per long rest you may spend your Action to pour out gifts from your Giftbag, rolling your proficiency bonus' worth of {@dice 1d8|d8} on the Fine Gifts For All! table. You may do so targeting yourself or a willing creature within 5-ft. When you do so, the target may choose to activate any of the Giftboxes effects as part of your Action to pour them out or on a subsequent turn by spending their bonus action. These gifts automatically activate if combat ends.

subclassFeature.name: Put Pain Into Writing

entries: "Hooh... hopes, desires, all of these afflictions shall be broken...! And I shall liberate thee from their yoke!"

There's so many pains that afflict the world, and so many wishes to be fulfilled. You've come to the conclusion that these are entwined and should be connected with ink, and that any number of people can be connected with ink, so you will do just that. You can use Bonus Action to absorb the sins of other creatures. All target creatures suffering from {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} within 60-ft. reach have their Talismans detached as you draw them in to bear yourself. Their count of any negative Condition is removed and you suffer them instead. When this happens, they may instantly spend up to an amount of Hit Die equal to their Talisman count, for a maximum value equal to half your proficiency bonus' worth of their Hit Die and recover that amount of Hit Points. You suffer Necrotic damage equal to that value.

subclassFeature.name: Quick Witted
entries: Although a reactonary movement may not be the right call always, its important for any self-respecting detective to be aware enough to always be on the hair trigger to catch the right moment to put a plan into action. As such, you may add your Intelligence Modifier as a bonus to your Initiative Rolls and use it instead of Dexterity for Saving Throws. Fruthermore you gain an additional Reaction during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Rambling Man
entries: By walking amidst the rifts for so long, your body has gotten used to their destructive and warping type of energy. Starting on 9th level, at the start of your turn, if you took no damage on the previous turn, you gain 4 stacks of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to a total of 20. You gain no {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} outside of combat and it dissipates upon its end.
Stacks of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} may be spent individually, all at once, or some at a time to trigger one of the abilities in the table below.

rows: As a bonus action after you perform an attack roll but before it is decided whether the attack hit or not, you may turn the damage type into force damage if it isn't already, or add an additional die of damage instead.

As a reaction to a creature entering one of your rifts, you may immediately close it. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). If they fail, they take {@dice 3d6} Force damage and gain 1 stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. (When a creature is {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they take an additional dice of damage equal to half their stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the next damage roll, then the stack is destroyed.
As a bonus action after you've dealt force damage, heal an amount equal to half the damage dealt.

As an action, you may carve a 10 feet by 10 feet rift, immediately closing all other open ones. Once entering this rift, you may choose any space within 90 feet of it and instantly teleport to it, carving a smaller rift as you exit. Immediately after doing so, you may perform an attack against a target within range. You roll your attack roll thrice, but your damage dice remains unchanged. For each attack you hit other than the first one add an additional die of damage and a stack of {@condition Dimensional Rift|TheUndertomesDS} to the creature. (A stack of {@condition Dimensional Rift|TheUndertomesDS} is immediately converted at the end of the creature's turn and transforms into double that amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks.)

As an action, you may tear a 15 feet by 15 feet rift in your area and call forth an Aberration from the Outer Planes. You may choose any Aberration CR 5 or lower and bring it forth on an unoccupied area within a 10-foot radius of the Rift. The Aberration will be friendly to you and your allies, and obey your commands as best as possible. It will act after you on the initiative. You may use a free action to issue commands to it, but if no commands are issued, it takes its turns either hiding or dodging from enemies. After a minute passes, the rift will attempt to suck the Aberration back to it and close itself. If the creature is not within a 20-foot radius of the rift, it is unaffected. If the creature is near the rift, it must roll a Dexterity saving throw against your DC to escape it, and it rolls with advantage if you and your allies are helping it.
entries.caption: Rambling Man

subclassFeature.name: Rampant Melody

entries: "This way, just a little closer... Hahah! Perfect! That scream, weaving into a ninth chord!"
"Such wondrous... harmony."

Ah, the sweet, sweet and tender dance of notes fluttering down your instrument is ecstasy for your brain! However, you have come to learn that the true bliss comes from creating a twinned harmony by pulling the cords of other's bodies, mangling them to make truly divine music! Whenever you make a melodious attack for the first time during your turn, you may perform an additional melodious attack as part of the same action for each time you've rolled a 20 or greater on the dice roll, including modifiers. This value is diminished by one per melodious attack hit as part of this Action, with it being reset at the end of your turn. You may make one additional attack at 6th level and a second upon reaching 12th level in Bard. You may select the same creature as the target of these additional attacks.

You have a +1 bonus modifier to this roll for each sum of 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count the target is suffering from, to a maximum value of +5. This is considered a direct increase to your roll's base result for the sakes of triggering additional attacks.
When you perform your first melodious attack during your turn you may spend a Bard spell slot to empower your music. You gain the following as part of this Action:

items: Your range increases by 5-ft. and you may choose an additional target per spell slot level spent.
You perform an additional melodious attack for every two spell slot levels spent greater than 0, such as performing two additional melodious attacks when spending a 4th level spell slot.

Instead of delivering more notes and performing additional melodious attacks whenever you've rolled the aforementioned value on a dice roll, you instead inflict 2 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you trigger that roll. This value increases by one for each time you have triggered this additional infliction.

If cast using a 4th level spell slot or higher, you also convert all {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target to be {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead. Additionally, you add your Charisma modifier to damage rolls of melodious attacks.

If cast using an 8th level spell slot or higher, you perform an additional melodious attack for each creature killed as part of this Action. Summoned or otherwise easily-reproducible creatures do not count toward this, as a fake being just does not provide anything but repetitive music to your ears.

If cast using a 9th level spell slot, you deal additional damage on hits equal to your choice of the targets {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Additionally, you recover a spent {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} for each creature killed through this attack, to a maximum amount recovered equal to half your maximum Bardic Inspiration die. Summoned creatures also do not count toward this.

entries: Additionally, you have learnt how to create such electrifying symphonies that they touch the hearts of legions at once. Whenever you grant a creature a use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} dice, you may choose to fill another creature within 30-ft. of that target with inspiration. When you do so, though, your attempt at catering to multiple tastes slightly diminishes the quality of the music, granting each only a {@dice d4}. This increases to a {@dice d6} upon reaching 15th level in Bard.

subclassFeature.name: Rattling Mind

entries: "A spark of inspiration."

Art permeates your breathing like oxygen invades the lung. You gain Proficiency in one Charisma skill of your choice and one Artisan's Tools of your choice. You may use Wisdom in place of Charisma when attempting Skill Checks.

subclassFeature.name: Ravenous Cycle of Bloodletting

entries: The red arms wave in the air, as if pleading not to be left behind.

The festering cycle of life is without an end and without reprieve, and you’ve learnt to weave that flow in your life seamlessly, aiding you as naturally as breathing. Whenever you or your Clerid Swarm would inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to a creature that is already Bleeding, you inflict Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead.

Furthermore, while there are creatures suffering from Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or below half their maximum hit points within 60-ft of you, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to Constitution, Intelligence and Wisdom Saving Throws, or a +2 if there are 4 or more creatures within that area.
Whenever you inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature, you heal one hit point and your Clerid Swarm may take two Actions per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Reliquary of the Mind

entries: "Mm. Indeed, I noticed on my stroll here that the sun had sunk beyond the horizon. Yet, it is said that erudition comes more naturally under the pale moonlight. I suppose I shall read now, then."

The repertoire you have amassed over time regarding all manner of things has truly led you to become able to perform certain things that those that lack your knowledge would consider simply miraculous. You may spend your Ki points in the following ways:

items: You may spend 1 Ki point to cast the {@spell Detect Magic} spell. When you do so, instead of seeing auras around areas you instead manage to filter out every little detail that might be off about environment's natural order, such as realizing when wood has a mismatched texture of once being transmuted from stone or the lingering burn marks of a {@spell fireball} that was once evoked.

You may spend 3 Ki points to cast the {@spell Identify} spell without requiring its material cost. When you do so you also learn if the target has been cursed, yet you must pass an {@skill Arcana} check to determine its nature. ( As per the DM's discretion. ) Additionally you may recall what material was used for this items creation and its general region of origin, such as city or continent.

You may spend 6 Ki points to cast the {@spell Legend Lore} spell without requiring its material cost, instead only requiring a handful of books for research. You spend these Ki points after the casting time has been concluded.

entries: Instead of spending Ki points you may instead choose to spend {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} count, which each spent count accounting for 3 Ki.

Additionally you gain Proficiency in one Intelligence skill of your choice. You may choose a skill you have gained Proficiency in because of this feature as a choice for your Gathering Knowledge as Kindling feat, granting you Expertise with the skill until the next long rest instead.

subclassFeature.name: Request Work
entries: The connection between a warlock and their patron is ultimately one of exchange, including a constant exchange of information. You can request aid from your patron for one of the following effects, using each effect once per short rest:

items: As an action, you cast {@spell locate object|PHB|Locate Object} or {@spell locate creature|PHB|Locate Creature} without expending a spell slot.

As a bonus action, you ask your patron to fire a bullet in your stead. Choose a space within 120 feet of you. A magical circle forms there and casts {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK} at 4th level without expending a spell slot. A creature whose challenge rating is lower than twice your warlock level automatically fails the spell's saving throw. This counts as you casting the spell.

You ask your patron one question, which it answers to the best of its ability, provided you are in good standing with one another. Its knowledge may be limited, and it might refuse to respond truthfully or at all, at the DM's discretion. This question may naturally lead into a conversation if your patron desires.

entries: When communicating with your patron, it may willingly materialize as a figure of smoke from your Marksman's Smoking Pipe. It can hear and be heard by creatures within 60 feet of the pipe.

subclassFeature.name: Retaliating Maneuver

entries: "The rest is silence."

Even after being detected, you have learned to quickly take advantage of the situation and return to the shadows. When a creature successfully detects you while you are hidden, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against that creature if it is within your weapon's range. After the attack, you can move up to 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, and you may immediately attempt a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to hide again if you have cover or concealment.
If it's raining or snowing, you apply the Snipe - Archery damage and {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} bonus to that reaction attack even if the creature can see you.

subclassFeature.name: Revelation from Above

entries: Judgement… Retribution… Punishment.

Your god continues to illuminate you with further teachings to keep you grounded in the righteous path. You gain two additional tenets. You also gain resistance to radiant damage, and you can now use up to two Higher Punishments per Long rest.

entries.caption: Emerald Tablet Tenets
rows: No vile creature shall control the minds of the righteous (when a creature within 30 feet of the tablet becomes {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened})

hey must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer an additional count of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever they’re hit by an attack, suffering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of their next turn.
You cure their current {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened} condition.
No vile creature shall corrupt the bodies of the righteous (when a creature within 30 feet of the tablet becomes {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Deafened} or {@condition Poisoned})
For a turn, they gain advantage on saving throws and ability checks, and any damage they take can be reduced by {@dice 1d6}.
You cure their current {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Deafened} or {@condition Poisoned} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Rhythmaniac

entries: "Make me move... Light my path with the songs!"

No one should, could or would stop you now, they can't stop either when the rhythm that pervades their soul! Your jam sessions have evolved, short strums to melodies to whole shows played over the battle stage and others finally have a shot of truly, lastingly connecting to the song that rips at your heart's strings! At the end of your turns, all creatures who have spent a use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} die during this combat may choose to gain one count of {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM}. While creatures have this Condition you are considered to be Concentrating on it, with all creatures' count being lost if you lose Concentration. This counts an additional Concentration for the purpose of still being able to concentrate on other spells.

A creature with this Condition has been enraptured by the god-rending melody of your carnage, and can't help but want to partake in it as musician and instrument, dealing and suffering an additional amount of damage equal to your Charisma modifier whenever they deal or suffer damage ( respectively ) equal to your 3 times your {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} count that they currently have. Whenever a creature declines receiving {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM}, they halve the counts of the Condition they currently have, rounded up. Additionally, if a creature with this Condition benefits from your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} rolls the minimum value rolled is always equal to their current {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} count, being increased if it was lower.

A creature with {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} gain an additional count whenever they first kill a creature during a round, except for summoned creatures. Additionally, a creature with 3 or more count may spend one count to perform an additional weapon attack or cast an additional spell of 3rd level or lower during their turn.

While out of combat you may grant a creature up to 4 {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} count whenever they receive one of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1}s. When used like this, they gain a +1 to skill checks for each count they currently have, although they can't help but feel the loathsome break in their cadence whenever they fail those, suffering {@damage 1d6} psychic damage for each count they currently have and then instantly losing the Condition.

Additionally, you may spend your Action while within 5-ft. of a medium or greater corpse to perform a haunting melody using it. When you do so, you instantly lose any negative Conditions currently afflicting you and gain 3 {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} count. Any hostile creatures within 30-ft. of you that can see or hear you must also pass a Wisdom saving throw or suffer {@damage 4d8} psychic damage from the horrible sight. While you have {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} count you recover an amount of Hit Points equal to the Condition's count at the end of your turns. If you lose Concentration you suffer an amount of {@damage d6} psychic damage equal to all {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesSM} count lost.

subclassFeature.name: Rip Space
entries: You have an innate ability to warp space around you. Starting at 3rd level, you may spend 15 feet of movement or a free action after a melee or ranged attack with your force blades to carve a purple rift in the air itself in front of you. This rift may stay in the space of another creature, and can be walked through without issue. Once two simultaneous rifts exist, they will become connected, and anything that enters its space will exit through the other linked rift.

A rift can be apart from another rift up to 60 feet. You may also throw your dagger from afar and create a rift up to 60 feet away from your position. You can only have two rifts open at a time, once you open a third one, you'll have to choose which of the other two you'd like to keep.
Your Saving Throw DC for any abilities related to this subclass is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier.
A rift lasts open for one minute, until you dispel them with a bonus action, until you fall unconscious or die.

Creatures from the Material Plane or any other creatures unaccustomed with planar travel (your DM has the final say rather a creature is or isn't accustomed to planar travel) must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier) if subject to travel between your dimensional rifts. On a fail save, they are affected by a random effect on the Rift Sickness table.

rows: The creature becomes frightened for a minute and may reroll their saving throw at the end of their turns. Starting on level 17, the creature becomes paralyzed with fear instead.
The creature takes {@dice 1d6} force damage. This damage increases to {@dice 2d6} on gth level, {@dice 3d6} on 13th level and {@dice 4d6} on 17th level.

The creature becomes charmed. It repeats the saving throw at the end of their turns, having advantage if they are hostile against you and your allies. On 13th level, they do not roll with advantage anymore.
They do not return for the following round, taking time to catch up and finally exit the rift. On 14th level, you can choose to have this effect not affect creatures of your choice.
The creature returns overcharged. All damage they deal until the end of their next turn is force damage instead of any other damage type.

The creature deals {@dice 1d6} additional force damage on their next attack. This damage increases to {@dice 2d6} on 9th level, {@dice 3d6} on 13th level and {@dice 4d6} on 17th level. You can choose to have this not affect hostile creatures.
entries.caption: Rip Space

subclassFeature.name: Rituals of an Ailing Heart
entries: Through your clergy you've learned how to practice certain rites to absolve your fellow sinners of the corrosion that plagues their souls, even if you suffer for it. Starting at 6th level, as a bonus action on your turn you may spend 4 Bloodfeast to perform any of the following Ailing Rites:

items: {@b It's Going to be Okay.} You offer enchanted words of encouragement and kindness while ignoring how hollow they ring inside your own ears. When you do so, you instantly end the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Poisoned}, {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Panicked|TheUndertomesASF} conditions that another creature within 30-ft of you may be suffering, yet their haunting thoughts become your own during this unassuming ritual. After you do so, you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw against your own Spell Save DC or suffer {@dice 2d4} Psychic damage and be afflicted with the Conditions removed until the end of your next turn. You may also use this feature to change the targets of psychic-damage inducing spells such as {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer} to be yourself, ending their effect from the initial target and attempting to pass the same Wisdom Saving Throw or becoming the new target of the spell's effect. If a spell is transferred this way, its duration is not reset.

{@b Endure Further.} With a piercing touch to a willing creature within 5-ft, you sink your own blood into their body along a string of words to have them keep enduring the pains of battle. For up to one minute you maintain Concentration on the following effect: Your ailing mind slowly erodes from an overwhelming anxiety seeping in their blood, causing you to suffer your Proficiency Modifier as an amount of {@dice d6} die of psychic damage at the start of their turns, but granting them a bonus to AC for the duration equal to the amount of damage die taken, as your protection has them move involuntarily away from outside troubles.

{@b Light Concessionary.} You may listen to your kindred's sins and absolve them of such impure thoughts. During combat, you choose one willing creature within 30-ft. of yourself to start a rite of cleansing where they confess their sins to you by spending their reaction to do so. Upon spending their reaction, this creature gains half your Wisdom Modifier (Rounded Up) as a bonus to Wisdom Saving Throws for the next minute. You may use this feature once per day during a Long Rest without spending Bloodfeast as long as you perform no other heavy activity, if this feature is used in this manner you may have it target up to your Proficiency Bonus' worth of creatures and this feature's effects last until the next short rest. You may choose to hear more creatures confess than your limit, but you suffer a cumulative amount of Exhaustion for each creature above your maximum. Eg: One point of Exhaustion for the first, Two for the second, Three for the third and so on. A creature may benefit from this bonus only once per Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Rooster's Battle Techniques
entries: You've developed and mastered techniques using your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} Sword that would make a normal person easily burn themselves from mishandling. These techniques can be used by spending two {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} during your turn, and you can only benefit from one at any given turn. They are as follows:

items: {@b Pecking Storm.} You spend a Bonus Action to perform half your total attacks you may perform during your turn (Rounded Down) as extra melee weapon attacks against a target within reach.

{@b Overwhelm.} You spend your Action to deliver a particularly powerful strike with your blade, sinking it into the target and burning them from the inside out. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they suffer 6 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and suffer {@dice 1d6} burn damage per count they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of {@dice 12d6}. This attack ignores Resistance to fire damage and treats Immune creatures as if they were only Resistant instead.

{@b Rooster's Flight.} You spend your Action to perform up to your maximum amount of attacks' worth of melee weapon attacks against creatures within your reach, moving up to 15-ft in a direction of your choice every time you do so. When you move this way, creatures have Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

subclassFeature.name: Rosé Flourish
entries: Upon reaching 3rd level and choosing the Rosehunter college, you've learnt how to fashion yourself impressive tools out of simple vines or to create them through your magic. You create a Rosé Whip made out of vines and undergrowth which extends up to a certain reach.

You may use your Whip as a grappling hook, using any vantage points you might find to better travel harsh environments, granting yourself advantage on {@skill Acrobatics} checks to do so, in addition, you gain proficiency in the skill.
Also when you reach 3rd level, you may choose one of the following Rosé Arts to learn:

entries.name: Scattering Petals.
entries: As a bonus action, you may create two Rosé Whips targeting two perpendicular walls to grapple and use to slightshot yourself across the battlefield, instantly flinging yourself by 20-ft in a line. You may angle yourself to reach higher, at the expense of gaining 5-ft of height per 5-feet travelled horizontally.

entries.name: Becoming a Garden.
entries: As a bonus action, you may create up to half your Proficiency Bonus' worth of Rosé Whips to lasso around one friendly creature within 45-feet of you, pulling them to be standing in an unoccupied space within 5-feet of you, or pulling yourself to be standing in an unoccupied space within 5-feet of one of them.

subclassFeature.name: Rotten Soul Sorcerous Origin
entries: {@i A Sorcerer Subclass by the Undertomes}

Something has taken hold of your spirit and does not plan to let go. You can feel writhing under your skin, beneath that still, as your very veins seem to be filled something more than blood. Your essence is slowly defiling, and there are only two options:
fight back against this filth that plans to consume you, or become one with the gluttonous energy that’s sapping away at you to use it against your enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Ruler of Needlekind

entries: "Looms... heh. Loopwheels. Sewing machines... heh, heheh... 43200G... No, no, bugger that! Shift the lot! It's "handmade" they're after, innit? "HANDMADE"... Khh..."

You are Warlock and Patron, servant and the served - all at the same time! You have subjects known as Needlekin, barely intelligible creatures that follow your every command provided it doesn't entail not pricking some bastard around.

They are numerous, usually lounging around a demiplane of your making as they avoid being in the Material Plane for long, since it's usually too cumbersome to work in or tiring to be around. You can have an amount Needlekin Servants out in the Material Plane at any given time equal to half your proficiency bonus. These use their eponymous monster block that can be found at the 4th page of this document and obey your orders willingly for the most part, as they can be hard to deal with at times. During those times you may roll your choice of a DC 13 Intimidation or Persuasion check to set them in line.
Instead of dying upon reaching 0 Hit Points, the Needlekin Servants Buzz Off, vanishing to their Demiplane until being summoned again over the course of a long rest.

Needlekin Servants are summoned and anchored to you over the course of a long rest, and can then be shortly dismissed to the Demiplane or called back to a space within 15-ft. of you as a Bonus Action. They may go however far from you that you want, and can always hear your commands through a psychical link at any distance.
When first summoning an individual {@creature Needlekin Servant|TheUndertomesNW} you may choose one of the following traits to grant them:

items.name: Oddly Verbose Needlekin.
entries: This one is actually rather proper when conjecturing to others, being able to speak languages you know clearly and granting you an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma skill checks while it is within 5-ft. of you.

items.name: Neurotic Needlekin.
entries: The bloke just won't sit still, no matter what you do. This Needlekin has an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and gains proficiency in the Acrobatics skill. It also grants you a {@dice d4} bonus modifier to Perception skill checks.

items.name: Bastard Needlekin.
entries: What a cock. This Needlekin is exceptionally rabid, dealing an {@dice 1d4} piercing damage instead of a single point as part of its Tacking Stitch attack. It also grants a {@dice d4} bonus modifier to Strength skill checks.

The additional dice granted by your Needlekin are increased at certain levels, as to become the following: {@dice 1d6} at 5th level, {@dice 1d8} at 9th level and finally to {@dice 1d10} at 13th level. You or other creatures may benefit from these die for an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring spent uses over the course of a short or long rest. ( This is counted across all of the Needlekin Servants you have. )

Your Needlekin Servants may take their Action during your turn by you spending a Bonus Action to order them around. You may order them to spend their movement speed or Cling to another willing creature as a Free Action during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Rules of the Backstreets
entries: In the alleyways of life, you are the one who people fear you are the one who people fear lurks within the darkness. Upon reaching 18th level, your bladework has been honed to near perfection, you've come to understand every rule that is applied to your craft and you can properly enact such. As an action, you sheathe your weapon and forgo dealing any damage for this turn. At the start of your next turn you may perform the Rules of The Backstreets action.

entries.name: Rules of the Backstreets.
entries: As an action you may perform a melee weapon attack targeting any creature of your choice within your weapon's reach. If all targets are suffering from {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you gain advantage for this attack. On a hit, you inflict one stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on each target and deal an additional damage die equal to that of your weapon's for each stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on your targets, summed up.
You may perform this action a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down. You regain its uses on a long rest.

entries.name: Designer's Note:
entries: For Rules of the Backstreets, you only roll your attack once and take that result as if attacking each target individually, hitting individual targets if your roll beats their Armor Class. Ex: You roll a 22 to your attack, you hit all creatures whose AC is 22 or under.

subclassFeature.name: Rupture-breathing Resolve [破吸自桓]

entries: "Let's take them all out. No need to waste our time here."

You have been studying the art of proper breathing to unleash powerful techniques. Whenever you or an ally within 5 feet of you kills a creature that had counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you immediately transform all of those into counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for you.

Additionally, once per Long Rest, you may spend up to your proficiency bonus in counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after an attack to regain 1 Ki point for each 2 counts spent this way.
Furthermore, your studies continue to bear fruit. Once per Long Rest, you can choose a Skill to gain Expertise with until the next Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Salut
entries: You've reached the pinnacle of speed and entertainment, guiding the masses to observe with bated breath as you conclude your battle with an explosive finale. Starting on level 18 you may choose to swap one of your attacks with a Salut attack. You gain 5 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when using this attack. and 5 more if the target has or had at least one stack of {@condition Focused Attack|TheUndertomesMS} during the last round.

For every stack of {@condition Focused Attack|TheUndertomesMS} that the attacked creature has or had during the last round, increase your Rapier's damage dice by one. If the creature hit with this attack was reduced to 0 hit points, you may immediately use your movement speed to walk up to a nearby creature within range and perform another Salutas part of the same action.
This attack doesn't consume stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit, and can only be used once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Scissors and Everything Sharp

entries: "...So you didn't trust me. I told you I'd play scissors!"

You gain proficiency with {@item battleaxe|PHB|Battleaxes} and you forge a Battleaxe called Scrap Scissors. Scrap Scissors are giant, purple scissors made out of scrap metal with their blades tainted with dried blood, and if it is ever lost or destroyed you can forge a new one during a Long Rest.

Furthermore, you can use your Intelligence modifier for attack and damage rolls with the scissors. Whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you kills a hostile creature with the Scrap Scissor, you gain 1 Soul. You can carry a maximum amount of Souls equal to your proficiency bonus.
You can spend Souls to construct the items below with an Action. Any item made with a Soul will erode and destroy itself after 24 hours have passed:

items: {@b Strange Doll (1 Soul).} This item is a smiling porcelain doll that seems to follow you with its painted gaze. As an Action, you can see through the doll's eyes, hear what it hears, use your movement speed to make it walk and cast spells through it until the start of your next turn. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses. The doll has Darkvision.

{@b Toy Carriage of Doom (1 Soul).} This item is a small, dark carriage that appears to function on its own. One creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can use a Bonus Action to force them to use up to half of their movement speed during your turn to walk in a direction you command. On a successful save, they only take {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage instead.

{@b Colorful Pain Brick (1 Soul).} This item is a small, colorful brick covered with nails on its top. Any creature that walks into the area of this item must perform a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage and suffer 3 counts of {@condition Curse|TheUndertomesHT}. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

{@b Jack In the Box (2 Souls).} This item is a box with a nasty, clown-ish surprise inside. When placed on the ground, any creature can interact with it as a Free Action. If a creature interacts with it or it is hit by an Attack, each creature within 15 feet of it must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d10} piercing damage and 3 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesHT}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

{@b Pale Marbles (2 Souls).} This item is a collection of pale white marble spheres. When left on the floor, any creature that walks into the area of this item must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they fall {@condition Prone} and become {@condition Stunned} until the start of their next turn. On a successful save, they take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage from the fall.

{@b Bladed Kite (2 Souls).} This item appears to be a kite covered in blades that floats around you. It protects you from incoming attacks, increasing your AC by 2. If you are hit by a melee attack while holding this toy, the attacker takes {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage once per turn.

entries: Finally, you are able to choose an additional Infusion as long as it is a Haunted Toymaker Infusion. At level 5, you are able to choose two additional Haunted Toymaker Infusions, and at level 9 you are able to choose three additional Haunted Toymaker Infusions instead.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: Your Scrap Scissor doesn't need to particularly look like a scissor, it can be any slashing weapon you can think of that fits your character! Furthermore, DMs, the Souls are meant to be acquired through actual fights and not through magical bags of animals and other similar exploits!

subclassFeature.name: Scripture of Truth Within

entries: "To purge the grounds with fire, and build anew a clean world."

You have read the sacred texts again and again, seared them into your retinae and punched them through your heart. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Religion} skill, or Expertise if you were already Proficient.

subclassFeature.name: Sealed Sword [Lævateinn]

entries: "Hah. What's a couple of pointed fingers when this sword of legends... is resting all snug and sweet in my hands?"

You have discovered a legendary relic, but its power is currently sealed. The mythical Greatsword {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM} requires a specific type of user to attune with it. You are no such user, but you will still attempt to draw out as much power from it as you can. You have the {@item Sealed Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM} Greatsword, you are always attuned to it and it cannot be destroyed. If it is lost, you can magically teleport it to your location during a Long Rest.
When you attack a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} with your {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM}, you may choose one of the following options once per turn:

items: They suffer 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per turn the first time you or another Middle member would inflict them with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the start of your next turn;

They suffer 1 additional count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per turn the first time you or another Middle member would inflict them with {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the start of your next turn;
If there is a Rogue that follows the Middle's Blade Roguish Archetype that you can see within 30 feet of you, you may give them 1 count of Thermal Blades;

If there is a Rogue that follows the Middle's Blade Roguish Archetype that you can see within 30 feet of you, you may show off to them, adding {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage to your attacks until the end of your turn.

entries: You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Searing Wings
entries: When you enter Volatile State, you instead enter Balanced State. Both Offensive Stance and Defensive Stance are active at the same time, and you do not suffer the harmful effects of Volatile State.
Your fire damage ignores resistance and immunity to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Seasoned Veteran's Stride

entries: "Thus, the flame of war burns in Hongyuan.To let slip the lessons of the rotten and the festering, to forget the kindness of his ideality, is what has started the fire."

The way you carry yourself has changed drastically form where you were once but a beast finding your footing, now boasting a confidence and importance with each step taken, be that transformed or not. You gain the following benefits while on your {@i Stormrider Form}:

items: Whenever you would trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} against a creature, it suffers 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever you would trigger the effects of the latter Condition, you inflict 1 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count afterward.
While you have Temporary Hit Points you gain a +2 bonus modifier to your AC. This is reduced to a +1 when none remain.

While you have no Temporary Hit Points you also gain an additional 5-ft. of movement and may spend your Bonus Action to perform an attack using your Kicks. You do not add your Ability Modifier to this attack's damage roll. When you do so, you may choose to force the target to pass a Strength saving throw against your Druid Spell Save DC or be flung 10-ft. backward in a line of your choice.

entries: Additionally, while out of combat you may grant yourself and your allies a moment of collective preparation toward whatever dangers you will face ahead by spending 10 minutes doing so. Upon the completion of these talks and small rituals all creatures involved may end one Condition or Curse to immediately end, or have the first time either would be applied in the next Combat be nullified if they were suffering from neither.
You may have this moment of preparation once per long rest. Only Curses that could be ended by the {@spell remove curse} spell are affected by this use.

subclassFeature.name: Secret Formula: Tropical Takeaway
entries: Upon reaching 6th level, you've devised one of your best creations yet, a flavor of Canned Wellcheers that can put even Shrimp to sleep just from how calming it is, being the first drink ever to boast negative levels of caffeine. As an action, you may force-feed this drink to another creature within 60-feet of you through a well timed Can-Toss, effectively casting the {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} spell at 3rd level at them, with the addition of if they don't fall asleep and the {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} roll was above half their current hit points, they are {@condition Drowsy|TheUndertomesASF}. A {@condition Drowsy|TheUndertomesASF} creature is more succeptible to sleep, with any following rolls of the spell being considered double the result.

In addition they suffer a -5 to their perception checks, as they are just too sleepy. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring its uses on a long rest. The {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} spell cast through this ability is instead upcast at 4th level when you reach 10th level in this class, then at 5th level when you reach 14th level in this class and finally at 6th level when you reach 18th level.

subclassFeature.name: Seize Ya Chance

entries: "Is this your weak spot?"

You are a masterful being in the art of quickly finishing the broken and the battered with extreme mercy. Whenever you trigger a Sneak Attack against a creature suffering from {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesNA}, you may choose to plunge your blade deeper for a vicious maiming of that poor soul. They suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and a {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesNA} instead. You may use this feature twice per long rest, and an additional third time upon reaching 20th level.

Additionally, if two other friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you have failed a saving throw or ability check that you passed you may offer them a stop of help through a hasty tip or a quick shove, granting them a bonus modifier to their roll equal to your proficiency bonus, potentially turning a failure into a success. You may do so once per short or long rest. Increases to two times upon reaching 18th level.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Destructive Dedication
entries: Finally, upon choosing this Divine Domain, you may use the righteousness behind your brutish actions to fuel you onward in flagellation. When you deal melee damage to another creature, you may choose to remove {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks from yourself and transfer them to the target. The number of stacks you may transfer is up to half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down. In addition, you may strike your whip against your own flesh as a bonus action to steel your resolve. You suffer an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to your Proficiency Modifier, and gain the same value as a bonus modifier to Wisdom Saving Throws for as long as you are {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier.
In your dedication, you may also spend the blood spilt by your hands to fuel Bloodarts, horrifying works of hemomancy. They are as follow:

items: Once at the start of your turn you may spend 2 Bloodfeast as a free action to heal yourself by {@dice 1d8} hit points. You may spend additional 2 Bloodfeast to heal additional {@dice 1d8} hit points, to a maximum amount of die healed equal to your Proficiency Modifier.

As a bonus action you may ready an attack empowered by your hunger, by doing so and spending 2 Bloodfeast you may give yourself advantage on your next attack against a creature suffering {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This creature suffers an additional amount of your weapon's damage type equal to the amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks they are currently suffering.

You may spend 3 Bloodfeast and an action to channel a vicious rage, causing you to scream and attempt to goad others into committing sins you can punish. When you do so, all creatures within 15-ft of you must pass a Charisma Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC or be goaded. A goaded creature has a bloody rage also overtakes their senses, be more inclined to target you as the source of their rage until the end of their next turn. Goaded creatures gain advantage to hit you and disadvantage to hit other creatures. Creatures immune to being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened} succeed in this Saving Throw instantly.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Destructive Purge

entries: "She is right-I must carry out more purification... That will then purify my mind with certainty."

{@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF|Nails} are cold, hard reminders of what must be brought down to the ground, so that they may never raise from their filth again. You employ their rusty points with great pride, even if you feel your mind is rusting itself at times, yet that is of no matter. After all, true faith demands effort and sacrifice.

Whenever you deal damage with melee weapon attacks to a creature, you also inflict an amount of {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. These {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF|Nails} stick out of their flesh and body like a flare guiding your fervent belief to hammer them down once dutifully prepared.

Additionally, whenever you enter your Rage you may choose to instead enter a state of sheer {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF|Fanaticism}. While in that stage you have all the features you'd gain by being Raging, alongside the following:

items: Your faith burns brighter than anything, drawing holy wrath down the wounds poked into your foes. You deal an additional {@damage 1d6} radiant damage on and inflict {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesHF} count equal to the target's {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count on a melee weapon attack hit.

Your blind fanaticism may propel you to do grand things, but it also has you convinced of certain tribulations you simply must suffer entirely. Whenever you would be forced to make a saving throw or ability check, you may roll a {@dice d4}. On an odd result, you gain a bonus modifier equal to your proficiency bonus. On an even result, you get the same value as a negative modifier to the roll. If you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, you must always roll this {@dice d4}.

At the end of your turns you suffer {@damage 1d10} psychic damage that cannot be reduced or increased through any means, as the toll of your position is taken. Additionally you have Vulnerability against psychic damage while below half your Maximum Hit Points.

subclassFeature.name: Senzionatura di Inefficienza

entries: "As the propriety of honorable combat dictates... One daft prick at a time."

Slicing at enemies isn't enough. Your blade has turned inward to chop off any little mistakes you would once commit in your swordplay, disregarding any weight that may come to be unbearable on you. You gain the following:

items: You make sure your opening strikes are as dazzling and damaging as your finishing blows. Whenever you deal damage to a creature, they suffer 2 {@condition Severed Tendons|TheUndertomesSP|Severed Tendon} count if they were not suffering from the Condition.

Although a cadence must still be built, you always draw your first move with the upper hand in mind. You add your proficiency bonus to your Initiative modifier and you may perform replace any one of your attacks with a Finishing Move during your first turn, despite how many times you have hit a target.

Constant exhaustion from your relentless training in the style has led you to be more resistant than most, granting you the ability to reduce your current Exhaustion Points by one at the end of combat, for a maximum of twice per short or long rest.

There is an undeniable rush to being in constant combat, moving from duel to duel in the battlefield - Whenever you kill a creature, you may use your Reaction to instantly recover {@dice 1d8} plus your proficiency bonus' worth of Hit Points.into unoccupied spaces and will not directly move into a space that would directly harm them, such as blazing ground or off a cliff.

subclassFeature.name: Serpent Glint

entries: "It's disgusting and ugly, isn't it? It gets worse with time. I'm going to be like the other snakes, like the other beasts of the Heishou Pack... becoming numb to everything."
As your mutations improve, your animal characteristics become more prevalent with each spell conjured. Whenever you use Metamagic, you gain 2 stacks of {@condition Serpent Arm|TheUndertomesSO}.

Additionally, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you have advantage on the roll, as you use your arms to grab onto something and pull yourself out of harm's way.

subclassFeature.name: Serpent's Mortal Flurry

entries: "You won't find a better snake for this job~"

Your transformation into a serpent is almost complete, as you feel your veins slither and tremble beneath your skin. As an action, you transform both arms into myriads of purple serpents, then stretch them toward a point you choose within 60 feet. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d8} poison damage and is {@condition Restrained|PHB} until the start of its next turn. If it had neither resistance nor immunity to poison damage, it is {@condition Paralyzed|PHB} instead. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, but is neither paralyzed nor restrained.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 4 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Sewing Marcation
entries: Upon reaching 5th level, you've learned not only how to sew a magnificent piece of wear, but also how to implement devastating needlework to your attacks. Either when you are outside combat or at the beginning of your turns in combat, you may choose a creature within 60-ft of you to become a Sewing Target.
