The chosen creature loses this property at the beginning of your next turn, and Sewing Target's effects are as follows, depending if the target is hostile or friendly:
If the Sewing Target is a hostile creature:

items: When {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is inflicted on this creature, they take damage equal to your half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down.
Any {@skill Medicine} checks against this creature to remove {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} are made with disadvantage.

You may spend a use of your Flash of Genius as a Flash of Indignance instead, giving your next attack roll against the target advantage and dealing {@dice 1d4} additional damage of your weapon's damage type per each stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the Sewing Target. (To a maximum amount of {@dice d4} equal to your Intelligence modifier.)

entries: If the Sewing Target is a friendly creature:

items: You may spend an action and a use of your Flash of a use Genius as a Flash of Fabulosity instead, granting this friendly creature within 15-ft. of you an additional amount of hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus worth of {@dice d4}, which count towards the durability of a gifted Hardblood Accessory.

Your magnificent craftsmanship and overview not only gives the creature a stunning look, but also a confidence to exude an air of elegance. This creature has a bonus to their Charisma checks and Saving Throws equal to your Proficiency Bonus as long as they are within 120-ft of you and are wearing one of your Hardblood Accessories or another article of clothing produced by you.

entries: Designer's Note. You gain the ability to use the abilities which refer to Flash of Genius beginning at 7th level, where you would gain it. Before that, you can use this ability once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Sezionatura di Elefante

entries: "... Tsk. Great. Not a single damn idiot left to call over for a drink... Bunch of weak-ass pushovers. Got chewed up by those disgusting bugs and died like trash."

You swing your blade with enough strength and speed to leave even the wisest of men unable to comprehend your movements without slowing them down. While raging, you may perform an additional bonus action attack as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules, however, this attack only inflicts 1 count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Furthermore, you gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and creatures that are Large or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll. If you managed to hit the same creature with all four of your attacks, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or suffer the effects of the {@spell Confusion} spell until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Disposal
entries: If you managed to hit the same creature with all four of your attacks and that creature is your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesPP}, you may trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on that creature twice, only expending all counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after the second burst. If that kills it, you may perform this ability one more time. Otherwise, you may only perform this ability once per Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Rabbit Roguish Archetype
entries: The Heishou Pack are a group of mutant assassins and combatants, each assigned to a different branch themed after the Chinese zodiac. Those of the Mao Branch follow the way of the Rabbit, using short hops and agility to secure victory on the battlefield.

Heishou warriors carry magically infused talismans that help them perform superhuman feats while slowly changing each branch member to gain the physical powers of its animal. Members of the Mao Branch commonly grow rabbit tails and eventually lose their feet to black rabbit paws.

The Heishou are mercenaries who owe loyalty only to their lord, the latest person to hire their branch. As a member of the Mao Branch, you might be an assassin on a mission, a beast of black fur trying to escape its leash, or a combatant waiting for a new lord to lead you into battle.

subclassFeature.name: Shared Fortunes
entries: Your constant stargazing has made it so the stars actually gazed back in appreciation, imbuing your Astral Marbles with a sliver of life. As a bonus action you may grant one of your Marbles to a willing creature within 30-ft. of you, having it hover within close proximity of them for up to the next minute, until you recall them as a free action during your turn or when until the creature falls {@condition Unconscious}.
A creature who has been gifted a Marble gains its Night-Light Wreath effects ( also triggering them on weapon attacks )

and you may use your Celestial Bursts and cast spells as if you were in that creature’s position, as if the Astral Marble was a relay. You may only give one Marble to a creature at any given time and it doesn’t count to your active total.
Furthermore your Star Luminary becomes a +2 Spellcasting Focus.

subclassFeature.name: Sharpened Blade
entries: You've come to learn how to take special care of your bladework, wielding them in a way that's perfect for drawing blood. Starting at third level, any weapon you wield is considered to have the Hemorrhaging weapon property. Hemorrhaging causes a stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you land a hit using this weapon, provided the roll equals or surpasses the value presented alongside the property before any modifiers. As for this feature that value is equal to 18 - your Proficiency Bonus, up to 20.

Additionally, you may gain the {@condition Battle Ready|TheUndertomesDC} condition at the start of combat and whenever a friendly creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious}. Summoned creatures and animal companions do not count towards gaining {@condition Battle Ready|TheUndertomesDC}. You lose one stack of this condition at the end of your turn and may have a maximum of 2.

subclassFeature.name: Show's Encore
entries: Starting at 10th level, your control of your strings has become simply masterful. You gain the ability to Silkbind two creatures at once with one use of the Wildshape feature, or when you summon a Hex Doll, you may choose between summoning your Hex Doll with its original maximum hit points as temporary hit points or summoning two Hex Dolls at once, but you the maximum CR of the creature you can summon is that of three levels below in the Druid Class.

Additionally, when you would spend your action to give an order for your Silkbound creature or your Hex Doll to attack, they may attack up to two times if they have the Multiattack feature. You may also choose to divide it so if you're controlling multiple creatures each of them performs one attack.

You may control one Silkbound creature while puppeteering a Hex Doll, yet your number of total controlled creatures cannot exceed two, with the first creature to be controlled being set free in place of a new one, in the case you Silkbind or Summon another creature.

subclassFeature.name: Shredding Melodies

entries: "I promise, nothing could make as fascinating music as a human can... Nothing!"

Music isn't just an art form limited to the conveniently well-accepted instruments that all other bards partake in playing, no, hardly! You have come to understand that there is no greater song machine other than the meticulous inner-workings of living beings when they are subject to glorious torment, and you have done your utmost to become proficient in playing them!

You may perform melodic attacks as an Action during your turn provided you are wielding an Instrument you are proficient in. A melodic attack is an advanced artform comprised of absolutely shredding with your instruments, blowing your targets minds or even setting them ablaze with sheer, overwhelming fervour for the melody. You are proficient with these attacks and use your Charisma modifier for their rolls, dealing {@damage 2d4} plus your Charisma modifier's worth of thunder damage on a hit, also inflicting 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
You may choose which of the Conditions to inflict and how to partition them. The amount inflicted increases to 3 count upon reaching 8th level in Bard.
You start being able to perform a single melodic attack during your turn and upon reaching 6th level your melodious attacks count as magical for the purposes of bypassing Resistance,

Whenever a creature benefits from your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} you may instantly perform a melodic attack as a Reaction against a target within 30-ft. of them, provided they can hear you.

subclassFeature.name: Shrimply Delicious Bard College
entries: Bards of the way of Shrimply Delicious Soda are the very model of a happy go-lucky sort of guy/guyette, breathing in the cold sea breeze and cracking open a delicious can of soda to share with their allies. Those who were privy to the secrets of Canned Wellcheers or even in some worlds invented the drink themselves can easily reproduce it, spreading its unique value to the realms as their rightful duty. In the Forgotten Realms, the College of Canned Wellcheers is a known estabilishment in the Sword Coast, gracing Neverwinter, Luskan and particularly Waterdeep with its nectarine substance, their bards working both on marketing and production of the soft beverage. In Eberron, there are still tales of the magical drink that was divised to end the great war, and all wars on the planet. Those were hoaxes, yet the drink is still pretty good.

entries.name: Canned Caroller
entries: You've essentially mastered the art of producing a good old can of Canned Wellcheers, as such you gain proficiency in Brewer's Supplies. In addition you cannot get the jingle out of your head. Ever.

entries.name: Cheery Sips
entries: You've always got a can or two laying on you just to be the most reliable. When you you grant a creature Bardic Inspiration, the creature who benefits from it also restores hit points equal to the amount rolled, as they sip down on the Soda.

entries.name: Can Toss
entries: In addition to all else, you may expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration die to, as a bonus action, toss another creature a can of your soda, which, if willing, they drink immediatedly. You may choose which flavor of soda to toss, with each having a different effect: Cherry. The vibrant cherry flavour of Wellcheers heals the soul and brings out the best in people.

When consumed, the creature who has done so heals for {@damage 2d8} hit points, healing an additional d8 at 5th level, and another one at 10th level, and an last additional d8 at 15th level. Regular. Canned Wellcheers regular flavor bolsters its irregularized and often rampant dosage of caffeine.

Upon consumption, the creature who has done so gains a bonus equal to half their proficiency modifier to their next Saving Throw. This bonus is increased to their proficiency modifier at 5th level and double that amount on 10th level. Grape.

The most popular and rarest flavor of Wellcheers is popular for a reason, when imbibed, the imbibee gains {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points and benefits from a +1 to their next Saving Throw. Upon reaching 5th level, the drink grants an additional d8 in temporary hit points and a +2 for Saving throws, a third d8 and a +3 to Saving Throws upon reaching 10th level and a total of {@dice 4d8} temporary hit points and a +4 to their next Saving Throw when reaching 15th level. Any cans produced this way lose their effects after one minute, as the drink goes flat.

subclassFeature.name: Sibling Encouragement

entries: "Oh? Well, look at that. Not bad. Here, you earned a 'good-job' kitty sticker for your Book."

You carry with you several gifts and stickers to celebrate when one of your loyal siblings and companions perform a feat you deem worthy enough. As a Bonus Action, you gift them with a kitty sticker or a small trinket, inspiring joy in their heart and a willingness to make you even prouder, gaining a bonus of +1 to their AC, to a maximum of 2, and {@dice 2d6} Temporary Hit Points, as well as advantage on their first attack roll each turn for the duration. The happiness from these stickers and trinkets last for 1 minute once received.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Silent Sniper Ranger Archetype
entries: You have trained since a young age how people think, where they expect an attack from, and how to hide from the most perceptive of targets. The weather is your constant ally to conceal your advances, and your performance as an archer excels beneath the rain and the snow. You are from a group of assassins that always completes their contracts, lest your own life be taken prematurely from you.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Silent Sniper Spells table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

entries.caption: Silent Sniper Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell create or destroy water|PHB|Create or Destroy Water}
5th
{@spell alter self|PHB|Alter Self}
9th
{@spell call lightning|PHB|Call Lightning}
13th
{@spell ice storm|PHB|Ice Storm}
17th
{@spell scrying|PHB|Scrying}

entries.name: Snipe - Archery

entries: "Rain pelts awake hearts."

You know how to operate in any kind of weather, and even pebbles on the street can be efficient weapons to someone with your experience. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill, and if you already have proficiency in it, you gain expertise instead. Additionally, you gain proficiency with improvised weapons.

As a bonus action until the start of your next turn, you can double the range of all ranged weapons you are holding. Additionally, all weapons you are holding gain the thrown property if they don't already have it, with a range of 30/90 feet. When you hit an attack with a weapon while in this state, it deals an additional {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to creatures that can't see you.
If it's raining or snowing, you gain advantage on {@skill Stealth} checks while outside or while experiencing the weather.

entries.name: Glimmering Bow [弓閃]

entries: "Alleyways puddle with steps."

Learning to focus on your target and aim for hours on end is the first thing any competent sniper learns - your bow must be treated not as a tool, but as an extension of your own body. You have 4 Snipe arrows. If one of them is lost or destroyed, you can reconstruct them during a long rest. You can choose to use one of your Snipe arrows instead of the usual ammunition when shooting with a bow. If you use a Snipe arrows instead of another arrow, you gain the following effects:

items: If you would have disadvantage on the attack roll due to distance, you instead do not have disadvantage as long as you haven't moved for 1 minute or longer.
For each 100 feet of distance from the target that you are, you add {@damage 1d10} piercing damage to the arrow, to a maximum of {@damage 4d10}.

Instead of immediately attacking, you may focus on your target, aiming your arrow at them but not moving from your position. You gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per turn you spend aiming without moving, to a maximum of 8.
If it's raining or snowing, the arrow becomes untraceable back to where you shot it.

subclassFeature.name: Silkbound Puppetry
entries: When you choose this subclass at 3rd level, your Wildshape functions differently. You cannot make use of the Wildshape feature to transform yourself, instead gaining the Silkbind and Summon Hexdoll features, both of which cost an action and a Wildshape use to be performed:

entries.name: Silkbind.
entries: When you take the Silkbind action, you choose one creature of Large size or smaller and attempt to entrap them in your strings, forcing them to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or be Silkbound. On a success, the creature gains advantage on future Saving Throws against being Silkbound until the end of your next turn, but you do not spend your use of Wildshape.

A Silkbound creature may be controlled by you by spending your action, bonus action or reaction during your turn to command them to use one of theirs. If the Silkbound creature has the multiattack feature, you may still only attack once when you use your action to do so. Additionally, you may spend your bonus action to move them up to their movement speed in any direction around you. You may also spend your reaction to when a Silkbound creature attempts to hit another creature or perform a Strength or Dexterity Skill Check or Saving Throw, imposing a negative or positive modifier to their roll equal to your Wisdom score.

If you attempt to force a Silkbound creature to cast a spell, they may spend their reaction to fight against your puppetry, making a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC, not casting the spell on a success. Silkbind ends when you dismiss the strings, Silkbind another creature or if the Silkbound creature leaves a 60-feet radius around you, as the strings snap. You may, as a reaction to when a creature would leave that area, force them to make a Strength Saving Throw, having their movement halted at the last moment on a failure.

entries.name: Summon Hexdoll.
entries: You spend your action to create a Hex Doll in any unoccupied space within 10-feet of you, which inherits the stat block of a creature you would be able to Wildshape into, with the following changes:

items: They cannot move outside a radius centered around you equal to their movement speed, as it determines the length of their strings.
You may cast your spells through your Hex Doll as if they were a familiar from the {@spell Find Familiar} spell.
Their maximum hit points are halved.
They gain vulnerability to fire damage.

They are considered a Construct in addition to any other creature types, also becoming immune to Psychic and Poison damage, also becoming immune to the {@condition Poisoned}, {@condition Frightened} and {@condition Charmed} conditions.

entries: Your Hex Doll has no place in Initiative, instead acting during your turn, where you may spend your action to command them to use any of their own action, bonus action or reaction. You may command them to move as a free action, and you may dismiss your Hex Doll at any time.
You may only have one Silkbound creature or one Hex Doll summoned at any given time, if you'd gain control of a new target your control over the last one ends immediately.

subclassFeature.name: Singular Focus of Mind

entries: "This lowly self of mine is yet to deserve the name of a Star."

Focus your breathing - let the world around you go still as you become able to perceive the sound of a falling leaf hitting the ground. During combat, as a Bonus Action, you may spend 1 Ki point to gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Starting at level 5, you may also spend 3 Ki points to gain 5 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Additionally, you may use a Bonus Action to spend 1 Ki point and gain a bonus to your {@skill Perception} and {@skill Insight} ability checks equal to a roll of your Martial Arts dice for 1 minute.

Whenever you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when you already have 4 or more counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you may choose to convert half of that amount into counts of {@condition Moonlit Azure Blade|TheUndertomesBS} instead.

subclassFeature.name: Skewed Justice

entries: "Its scale would never neglect the weight of even the smallest sin."

You may spend your bonus action and a spell slot to channel the Beast's overwhelming desire for all's "Safety" through your body, instantly gaining double your proficiency bonus' worth of Mark of Sin. Mark of Sin is a counter that is transferred once to other creatures whenever a certain trigger is met, allowing you to have special effects against them, as follows:

entries.caption: Marks of Sin
rows: Whenever you are hit my a weapon attack.

The triggering creature suffers a Mark of Punishment. A creature with counts of this effect suffers an additional {@damage 1d10|d10} force damage whenever you hit them per Mark of Revenge they are suffering from, then removing all Mark of Punishment count.
Whenever you witness a creature within 60-ft. of you killing another

The triggering creature suffers a Mark of Justice. You gain a bonus modifier to attack and damage rolls against a creature suffering from Mark of Justice equal to its count, to a maximum of +3. This count is reset to zero when the creature dies or combat ends.
Whenever you witness a creature within 60-ft. of you cast a spell

The triggering creature suffers a Mark of Darkness. Creatures suffering from this effect cannot target you for spell attacks or force you to make a saving throw against their spells, losing one count whenever they cast a spell targeting at least one other creature.

subclassFeature.name: Sleeping Beasts Rise
entries: During a short or long rest, you can grant yourself and a number of friendly creatures equal to your proficiency bonus a Talisman of Haste, which becomes inert when you next finish a short or long rest. A wearer adds 10 feet to the length of its jumps and adds your proficiency bonus to its Athletics and Acrobatics checks. When a wearer rolls initiative, the talisman activates and grants a bonus to the roll equal to your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Slithering Magic

entries: "Sun's up, gotta keep m'lord updated. Fuhu, he's gonna love me for it."

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Slithering Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it does not count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an evocation or transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

entries.caption: Slithering Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell longstrider|PHB|Longstrider}, {@spell ray of sickness|PHB|Ray Of Sickness}
3rd
{@spell pass without trace|PHB|Pass Without Trace}, {@spell spider climb|PHB|Spider Climb}
5th
{@spell hypnotic pattern|PHB|Hypnotic Pattern}, {@spell vampiric touch|PHB|Vampiric Touch}
7th
{@spell evard's black tentacles|PHB|Evard's Black Tentacles}, {@spell grasping vine|PHB|Grasping Vine}
9th
{@spell contagion|PHB|Contagion}, {@spell mislead|PHB|Mislead}

subclassFeature.name: Slithering One Sorcerous Origin

entries: "I did everything as I was told... I was fiercely loyal... so why wasn't it me?"

The Heishou Pack are a group of mutant assassins and combatants, each assigned to a different branch themed after the Chinese zodiac. Those of the Si Branch follow the way of the Serpent, making use of elastic arms and poison to quickly steal from and assassinate their targets.

You are blessed with serpentine features, which could be due to a yuan-ti ritual, a certain poison your mother was afflicted by, a snake-like ancestor, or even a special transformative medicine applied to you. Either way, your body has undergone changes, becoming long and thin. Additionally, you have an affinity for poisons and the natural magic present in the world, able to attune to it similarly to how a druid would.

The Heishou are a mercenary group, owing loyalty to no one except their lord, who is the latest person to have hired a specific branch. As a member of the Si Branch, you might be a hired assassin on a mission, a beast of violet scales trying to escape your leash, or simply an assassin waiting for a new lord to hire you and take you to battle.

subclassFeature.name: Snake Fang

entries: "Didya see that? Doubt ya did... A crooked snake whips faster than the speed of sound, you know."

You can hasten your serpentine transformation and reap the benefits of your monstrous future. As a bonus action, you can spend one or more sorcery points to magically transform your body for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point you spend, you gain one of the following benefits of your choice, which lasts until the transformation ends:

items: You gain blindsight out to 30 feet, as you activate the heat vision of a serpent.
You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Whenever you hit an enemy with a spell that deals poison damage, it suffers 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Your spells ignore resistance to poison damage, and when you reach 18th level, they also ignore immunity to poison damage.

Your head morphs into that of a large, poisonous purple snake. As an action, you can make a melee spell attack against a creature within 30 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 5d8} poison damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer 3 stacks of {@condition Deathrite Venom|TheUndertomesSO}.

subclassFeature.name: Soldato Tuttofare Roguish Archetype

entries: "... I failed to complete my duties. This is but a punishment I deserve."

Stern, rigid and hierarchical. That is the life of any Rogue who has become a Soldato Tuttofare - A foot soldier meant to do anything and everything asked by their superiors in whatever great organization they have found themselves in, be that carrying ammunition to dishing out horrible gashes in cost-effective close-quarters combat.

These are obedient people, for better or worse - Unrelenting in their rulekeeping to a fault, but they often tend to hold themselves to the same standards as they do others, being second to none in reliableness to those who have managed to stand at their side literally and figuratively.

In worlds such as that of Faerun, a Soldato Tuttofare Rogue might find themselves serving in the Zentharim as one of its many agents, or in others such as that of Keybreak they are one of the many, many people vying for a higher position in one of the Ringed Cities' megacorporations' military forces.

entries.subclassFeature: Under the Thumb of Greater People|Rogue|PHB|Soldato Tuttofare|TheUndertomesST|3

subclassFeature.name: Spada Palermitana

entries: "It don't matter even if I'm just a pale imitation. Gettin' stronger ain't what I'm trainin' my Palermitan Style for, anyway."

The Palermitan Sword style is an art that few have learnt, and fewer have mastered - Being famous for its ability to draw oponents on one-on-one fights and through a series of escalating strikes bring the fight to a swift, victorious end. Those who embody the Spada Palermitana are just that - Pupils coming to not only become masters in such a style, but also becoming objects of power in their own right.

They usually are devout and perfectionists in their practice, being fast learners and unusually dedicated at their best but also easily creating bad tendencies to overwork or even reach the depths of their own self-worth, seeing any miniscule failure as a shame without equal.

subclassFeature.name: Speaker for the Mourning

entries: You feel sympathy for the trapped being.

The connection you and your Swarm have is instinctual, like one is an extension of the other. You can speak to and understand your Clerids as if they were a familiar from the {@spell Find Familiar} Spell, except that they cost no GP to be revived. They use the Clerid Swarm [Familiar] sheet.
You also gain proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling}, or expertise if you were already proficient in the skill.

subclassFeature.name: Spice of Life
entries: The noses of cooks long past have been reached by your delightful cooking and they have chosen to give you the blessing of special ingredients to create a True Dragonlife Stew, a magnificent meal meant for the servants of the Lifestew that has a chef transcend their mundane existance and become akin to the mighty {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesLS}. As an action you may take once per long rest, you produce a True Dragonlife Stew and consume it, gaining the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesLS} Condition and the effects of the following ingredients while you have it:

items: {@b Jesty Jallapeños.} You gain a breath weapon as a great fire starts swirling in your gut! You may spend your action to spew fire in a 30-ft cone in any direction, having any creature within this range have to perform a Dexterity Saving Throw, suffering {@dice 5d8} fire damage and 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a failure or half the damage and half the stacks on a success. After using this feature you must roll a {@dice d6} at the start of your next turns only, regaining the ability to use it upon rolling a 5 or a 6. If you were poisoned and consumed a stew with Monster Mash, this Saving Throw becomes a Constitution Saving Throw and in addition to other effects any creature who fails also becomes poisoned for one minute, being able to re-attempt this Saving Throw at the end of their turns.

{@b Clawing Crawfish.} Great draconic claws morph from your fingers and a tail sprouts from your lower back! You gain natural weapons in the form of claws and a tail, the former dealing {@dice 2d4} slashing damage on a hit and having the finesse traits while the latter deals {@dice 1d12} bludgeoning damage and has the reach trait.

{@b Thick Tomatoes.} Your legs transform to be durable and powerful, springing with each step. You gain an additional 10-ft of walking speed and proficiency with the Athletics skill, or expertise if you were already proficient.

{@b Careful Carrots.} Your eyes gain a yellowish tone and slit pupils, becoming fully draconic. You gain advantage on Perception skill checks, can't be surprised and can see Invisible creatures as if they were colorless sillouettes over the world.

entries: Furthermore, you may throw one of these ingredients into your Stew Cauldron as a bonus action on your turn, granting any friendly creature who drinks this it's associated effect. This counts to the amount of times you may throw an ingredient in, and you may add a Spice of Life ingredient once per long rest. If you are knocked {@condition Unconscious} you lose the effects of your True Dragonlife Stew as your stomach becomes upset from not being to enjoy its grace fully.

subclassFeature.name: Sprawling Garden Blooms at Last
entries: Upon reaching 16th level, your abilities with the Rosé Whip are second to none. Your Most Beautiful Touch skills are upgraded:

entries.name: Thrill of the Hunt.
entries: Now has a reach of 45-feet and deals three Bardic Inspiration die in piercing damage that is considered magical, yet the inflicted {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is equal to the highest roll of the three. Additionally when you would trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks to be removed with an attack using Thrill of the Hunt, only half are removed. If you would create a bridge for you and your allies, it is now considered 15-feet wide and Large or smaller creatures can pass without any difficulty.

entries.name: Embrace of Thorns.
entries: You may now target up to three creatures when using this action, additionally, your Whips become much tougher, with an AC of 15 and you may target Large creatures with it without them having advantage. Furthermore, you may spend your action on subsequent turns while you have creatures grappled onto your Whip to make its vines lash out against all creatures of your choice around 10-feet of the grappled, including the grappled creature itself. They must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take {@dice 3d10} piercing damage plus your Charisma modifier and suffer {@dice 1d8} {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks.

subclassFeature.name: Stagefrights
entries: As you develop your knowledge in the arcane arts, you can now not only infuse your magic into your Hex Dolls, but to use it to conjure fear inducing hexes! Starting at 6th level, you gain a pool of Hex Points equal to your Druid level, you may expend a number of them to cast a Hex from the table below. All these Hexes count as spells.

entries.name: Encore, Encore!
entries: By spending 1 Hex Point and a bonus action, you conjure thin nails to sew and heal your Hexdoll for half its maximum hit points, rounded up. You may only do it once per combat targeting the same Hexdoll.

entries.name: Solid Posing.
entries: Summoning many rusty nails, you may spend 2 Hex Points to, as an action, skewer one target creature within 60-feet of yourself, causing a horrible curse to spread and shred through their veins. The target must pass a Charisma saving throw or suffer 3 stacks of {@condition Hexbind Curse|TheUndertomesCH|Curse}. A creature inflicted with the {@condition Hexbind Curse|TheUndertomesCH|Curse} condition feels their very veins constantly being pulled, twisted and nearly torn, making movement exceedingly painful. They suffer one Stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per time one of the following happens: The first time they are forcefully moved by another creature or use their movement speed during a round in initiative, every time they attempt to hit a creature and when they make Dexterity Saving Throws. The accursed creature loses one Stack of {@condition Hexbind Curse|TheUndertomesCH|Curse} at the end of their turn, or all stacks if the {@spell Remove Curse} spell is cast on them.

entries.name: Waning Control.
entries: You let yourself go for a moment, tasting from your own Hexes to remind yourself on how to work them the best. By spending 3 Hex Points and both your action and bonus action, you fully let your magic take control of your movements until the end of your turn. Red string wraps itself around your wrists and ankles as the ghastly visage of your Hex Doll lurks above you, pulling on your strings. For the remainder of your turn, you are considered to have the Flyby trait and you may perform up to three of the attack shown next, suffering one stack of {@condition Hexbind Curse|TheUndertomesCH|Curse} per attack performed in this way. Hex Nail. The spectral hands of your Hex Doll materialize over yours or your nails extend to become claws that you may use to rake others with. This unarmed attack has a reach of 5-feet, you may use your Wisdom to hit and for damage rolls. When you use this attack, the rampant Hexes wrack your body with traces of a lacerating curse, yet the pain only fuels your power. You deal {@dice 2d8} slashing damage on a hit with this unarmed attack, and an additional {@dice 1d8} necrotic damage per Stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on you.

subclassFeature.name: Stamp of Vengeance

entries: "Heh. Why work with your brains when you've got the brawn?"

You don't take shit from anyone, or anything, and you make that very clear with every step you take. Your speed increases by 10 feet. After you use your {@classFeature Indomitable|Fighter|PHB|9} ability, regardless of if you failed or succeeded, you may immediately use your remaining movement speed to move towards the source that forced you to make a saving throw. You can make an unarmed attack against it, as if you had your Tattoo of Stomping active, except it deals double the damage dice. If the source is an object or a structure, it takes double damage from this attack.

Additionally, if you have taken the {@optfeature Fighting Style: Sacrifice|TheUndertomesVM}, you may choose to double the damage dice of your attack once per Long Rest, but both creatures will take the doubled damage, and it cannot be diminished or prevented in any way by the friendly creature. If the friendly creature is a Middle's Blade Rogue, then both them and the creature become Vulnerable to the damage types of your attack as well.

subclassFeature.name: Star Luminary
entries: You have found a way to harness the power of entire constellations through arcane foci carved with an intricate, circuit-board like patterns, powering them up using another contraption called a Star Luminary, which can be either an engine-like device worn around the waist and holding spherical inlays for the Marbles or a stattuete that you carry, accepting power when a Marble is placed within its myriad hands.

You can keep a number of Astral Marbles on hand equal to your proficiency bonus, changing any of your on-hand ones to another by retrofitting their materials and so on and so forth, as long as your total maximum remains the same. You may choose to spend one of your Attunement slots to attune to the Star Luminary. While attuned, you may swap an Astral Marble slotted into your Luminary with another on your inventory through a bonus action. Your Luminary is able to hold a maximum amount of Astral Marbles at once equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded up.

Your Astral Marble effects use your Artificer Spell Save DC whenever a save is mentioned, and its power is linked to your Astral Current, a marker of how well astral energy is converted by the Star Luminary, being a value equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
Astral Marble effects are only active when inlaid into your Star Luminary, starting to glow and whirr in tune with the astral energy being catalyzed. Their effects are as follows:
A “Boosted” attribute score means that attribute score is increased by a value equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

rows: Anguilla

Boosts your Wisdom. While you are {@condition Frightened} you gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to your Astral Current, also being able to move towards the source of your fear as if you were moving through Difficult Terrain. While {@condition charmed}, yours stars in the dark outshine any other creature, making you inclined to want to share them. You can use spell attacks and have advantage on spell attack rolls against the source of your {@condition Charmed} condition, dealing an additional damage die equal to the spell’s damage die, and inflicting {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your Astral Current. When you deal damage to the source of either Condition you may spend your reaction to end the Condition early.
Gallus

Boosts your Charisma. You may have any spell damage you deal become thunder damage instead of it’s original type, as your stars resonate into your craft with a boisterous whirring. As a reaction to whenever a friendly creature within 30-ft. of you would be {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}, you may flare this Marble, causing it to outshine the effect and preventing the condition from being inflicted.
Hirudo

Boosts your Constitution. Whenever you would deal damage to a creature you are healed by one hit point. Furthermore you Resist poison damage and if you become {@condition Poisoned} you may transfer that Condition to another creature you hit with a melee attack, forcing the target to pass a Constitution saving throw or suffer the {@condition Poisoned} condition instead for its remaining duration.
Noctua

Boosts your Intelligence. You may use your Intelligence modifier in place of Wisdom for {@skill Perception} checks and gain a bonus to these and {@skill Investigation} skill checks equal to your Astral Current. You gain 120-ft. of Darksight if you didn’t have it.
Sextans

You gain {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your Astral Current at the start of your turns. You may spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as a bonus action to turn it into a {@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH}, gaining {@dice 3d8} temporary hit points. Furthermore, while having this temporary hit points you resist non-magical slashing, bludgeoning and piercing damage. You may also spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as a bonus action to grant yourself an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to your next skill check.
Rangifer

Boosts your Strength. You are constantly filled with vigour, being able to ignore the first two points of {@condition Exhaustion} you might suffer form and may use Intelligence modifier instead of Strength for Athletics and Acrobatics. Your jump height is tripled while this Marble is active.
Vespa

Boosts your Dexterity. You gain your Astral Current times 5 feet of additional movement speed during your turn, and when an attack misses you, you may spend your Reaction to move 5-ft. in any direction. You may repeat this whenever the same creature attacks you without requiring your reaction until the end of their turn.

subclassFeature.name: Starry Skies Specialization
entries: {@i An Artificer Subclass by the Undertomes}

The gift of harnessing power from the stars themselves is one rare and highly sought of after by Wizards and Artificers alike, but most lose track in their devout studies as they lack reverence for the very subject of their study.

Artificers who Specialize in the Starry Skies are those who have managed to sculpt a reflection of the night sky weaving not only the fruits of devoted intellectual prowess but also a genuine reverence towards each connected star and constelaltion which paints that which all can see through the dark canvas of space, bearing down faces and symbols that these Artificers manage to draw pure power from using specialized tools to do so.

subclassFeature.name: Stillness of Past

entries: She’s filled with loneliness, and tells her tales to fill that void.

Painting a picture from oration alone is a pride, but you go beyond - Forming a living memory in words and smoke. While more than one creature within 120-ft of yourself are suffering from Solitude you may spend your Action to expand that feeling into a scenery that covers a 15-ft wide and 15-ft tall cube around them, being expanded to follow their movement as if forming a trail. This scenery overlays the world in monochrome and may change aspects and aesthetics around to fit the vision of your tale, such as if you are orating about a western-type tale doors might become saloon styled and thumbleweeds may roll around. As part of this same Action and as an Action in your future turns you may spin happenstances into the tale, causing one of the following effects:

entries.name: A Thing Went Bump In the Night
entries: A creature of your choice within the Mist must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Bard Spell Save DC or be {@condition Frightened} of the space they are currently occupying, being forced to spend any remaining movement speed they would have to move away from it in a direction of your choice. The target creature may retry this Saving Throw at the end of their subsequent turns.

entries.name: Thus a Gleaming Weapon Was Spotted
entries: You create a simple or martial weapon of your choice that you have seen before atop an unoccupied space within the Mist. It counts as a +1 weapon with no other magical properties, it becomes attuned to the first creature that picks it up and is proficient in it, with that attunement not counting towards a creature’s maximum number of attunements. The weapon vanishes into smoke when the Mist disperses or as a free action you may take during your turn.

entries.name: Quick, Hide!
entries: You create an object that is 5-ft. wide and tall that may be used as cover atop any unoccupied space within the Mist. This object takes the appearance of your choice and is either wooden or made out of iron, such as a barrel or solid iron bars.

entries.name: Yet Suddenly, They Fell
entries: A creature of your choice within the Mist must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Bard Spell Save DC or fall {@condition Prone} as they trip over an object, slip onto the floor or any other choice of having someone fall over.

entries.name: Yet Suddenly, They Fell Ill
entries: A creature of your choice within the Mist must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Bard Spell Save DC or suffer the {@condition Poisoned} condition, also taking {@dice 2d4} psychic damage at the end of their turns as they believe they are struck with terrible disease. They may retry this Saving Throw at the end of their subsequent turns, after suffering this psychic damage.

You must concentrate on the Mist as if it were a spell and whenever a creature gains or suffers the Solitude Condition within existing Mist, they suffer half your proficiency bonus’ worth of psychic damage, rounded down. All the Mist disperses after a round passes by without any creature suffering from Solitude or if you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

While outside of combat, you may spend your Action to start orating and form the Mist around yourself, but is dispersed at the beginning of combat or after 30 minutes being idle. While surrounded by Mist in this way, you may use it to improve your storytelling and grant yourself an {@dice 1d6} bonus modifier to Charisma skill checks related to spinning a tale.

subclassFeature.name: Stitch per Inch

entries: "In the name... of the King...!"

You've managed to create a little thing to help you when needed - a star-tipped wand of unfathomable power! As long as your Needlekin believe in you, that is. It's light enough that you can pull it out and stash it quickly without worrying about it taking a free hand, and it has a very special use.

entries.name: Reject That Place!
entries: As a Bonus Action during your turn you may choose a Needlekin within 30-ft. of you to levitate using your wand and violently toss it around the air toward another unoccupied space or a friendly creature within 45-ft. of you, with the following effects depending on the target:

items: If thrown on an unoccupied space, they land there safely.
If thrown toward a friendly creature the Needlekin Clings to them as a Free Action.

entries: Alternatively, you may spend your Action to toss one of your Needlekin toward a hostile creature within reach, forcing all hostile creatures within 15-ft. of the initial target to attempt a Dexterity save against your Warlock Spell Save DC or have the rabid little Needlekin do a flurry of pins against them. On a failure, the Needlekin attacks them for an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, automatically succeeding the attack roll and going straight for the damage rolls instead. On a success, they only attack for half your proficiency bonus, also hitting automatically. ( As to trigger {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} various times. ) After being tossed as an Action and attacking, the {@creature Needlekin Servant|TheUndertomesNW} Buzzes Off.

subclassFeature.name: Stomping

entries: "Welcome to the kill zone!"

As a member of the Middle, you do not lack the powerful magical tattoos they are known to boast. You may attune to an additional number of tattoos equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. Additionally, whenever you finish a Short or a Long Rest, you may choose 3 tattoos from the list below to have active (if any of them requires a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Tattoo of Manipulation
entries: Upon getting this Tattoo, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion or the {@skill Deception} skill, your choice. If you already have Proficiency in the chosen skill, you gain Expertise instead.

entries.name: Tattoo of Deep Wounds
entries: When you hit a creature, you may choose to inflict the {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} condition on them as long as they have {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts. Once they are cured of the {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} condition, they become Immune to it for 10 minutes. {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead causes the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the previous Condition and 2 stacks are removed every time it is triggered. The {@skill Medicine} Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

entries.name: Tattoo of Dread
entries: As a Bonus Action, each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you and aware of you must succeed on Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, they become Immune to this effect for the next 24 hours. Creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} have disadvantage on this saving throw.

entries.name: Tattoo of Stomping
entries: You may replace one of your attack actions with an unarmed attack, which you are proficient with, against a creature within reach. On a hit, they take {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and are pushed 10 feet back towards a direction of your choice. This forced movement provokes opportunity attacks, and the damage increases to {@damage 1d10} at level 10 and {@damage 1d12} at level 15.

entries.name: Tattoo of Alliance
entries: For each Middle-aligned friendly creature within 30 feet of you, you gain a +1 bonus to your ability checks, for a maximum of +3.

entries.name: Tattoo of Shielding
entries: You gain +1 to your AC.

entries.name: Tattoo of Chains
entries: As a Reaction when you see a creature move within 30 feet of you, you may attempt to Grapple them from where you are with your {@item Chains of Loyalty|TheUndertomesOL|chains of loyalty}. Creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} have disadvantage on this ability check.

entries.name: Tattoo of Rule Violation
entries: At the start of combat, before any turns take place, you may establish a rule. If that rule is broken by a creature, you can use your Reaction to glare at them, lowering your sunglasses if you are wearing any. They must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition Paralyzed} until the end of your next turn due to your overwhelming presence. Creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} have disadvantage on this saving throw. After a creature is affected by this Paralysis, they become Immune to it for 24 hours.

entries.name: Tattoo of Resentment
entries: You have advantage on your first attack every turn against creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}.

entries.name: Designer's Notes
entries: Your rules for the Tattoo of Rule Violation can be anything you find fitting, but your DM has the final say if something is or isn't allowed. Breathing would not be a fun rule violation most of the time, but it COULD be interesting if used once for a cool roleplaying situation. Basically, make cool rules that everyone at the table can agree with, don't take the fun out of the ability!

subclassFeature.name: Straight-Line Wind

entries: "Nock the arrow, pull, loose-it punches through the target, felling it."

You have honed your arrows to pierce and not be easily removed, becoming a powerful dent in any enemy's armor. When you successfully hit an enemy using a Snipe Arrow as ammunition, it suffers 1 count of the {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesSS} condition. Additionally, whenever you use a Snipe Arrow, you immediately gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} before the attack and you deal {@damage 2d8} additional piercing damage if the creature can't see you instead of the {@damage 1d8} additional damage from Snipe - Archery if the attack hits.

If it's raining or snowing, when you hit a creature that has one or more {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesSS} stacks, your attack scores a critical hit on a lower {@dice d20} roll equal to the number of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesSS|Lodged Arrows} the creature has (For example, a creature with 3 {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesSS} is critically hit on a roll of 17 - 20). When you score a critical hit this way, all {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesSS|Lodged Arrows} are destroyed.

subclassFeature.name: Student of the Wind
entries: At heart, you are a nimble and charismatic individual, ready to take on anything and anyone.
At 3rd-level, you gain proficiency in your choice of either the {@skill Acrobatics} or {@skill Performance} skill.

subclassFeature.name: Summary Judgement

entries: "Obey the orders issued by your superior unconditionally, and do not question the intentions of your superior. Kill if you're told to kill, and die if you're told to die."

The trust put upon you is something that would crush the stature of those which are lower than you, the implicit recognition of the Bosses that you are the one whose judgement will be performed upon the bodies of all that illicit quick punishment. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your experience and discipline has made any gun in your hands seem like it were a higher grade than it really is. You consider any ranged weapon you are wielding to deal magical damage for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and they are also considered to be at least a +2 Weapon, if it was any lower than that.
Whenever you take the Take Aim Bonus Action, your next ranged weapon attack gains a +2 bonus modifier to hit and is considered a Critical Hit on a dice result of 19-20.

Any time you would roll on the Ammunition Tributary table, before you roll you may choose to instead choose to draw the Round of your choice. You may do so an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Supportive Current Leading

entries: "Triggering transfer sequence."

Electricity isn't just a means to an end for you, it is a tool to be wielded in a variety of ways: mainly those that are simply too complex for most others to have the patience in understanding the inner workings of, such as turning the often destructive energy into something much more defensive.

Whenever you would deal damage to another creature or affect them with a spell of yours, you may inflict them with an amount of {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} equal to the spell's level, to a minimum of one. If the spell has multiple target, it inflicts count equal to the spell's level minus the amount of targets. If this would be inflicted because of a target passing your Spell Save DC, they only suffer half that amount of {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} instead, or none if they would only suffer one. You can inflict the Condition this way an for an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Additionally, you may use a Free Action immediately after gaining {@condition High-Voltage Exoskeleton|TheUndertomesAED} at the end of your turns to redirect the electrical currents that protect your body to instead guard your fellows, choosing an amount of friendly creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus when you do so and then losing any amount of available {@condition High-Voltage Exoskeleton|TheUndertomesAED} count on yourself to grant each target the same amount.

subclassFeature.name: Swiftfeet Protection
entries: When a friendly creature is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to spend any number of {@b Tianjiu Star's Blade} stacks and move up to 10 feet toward it for each stack spent. If you arrive within 5 feet of the creature, the attack targets you instead, potentially becoming a miss if its attack roll does not hit your AC. You then make a melee weapon attack against the original attacker, inflicting 2 additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit.

You gain a bonus to your AC equal to the number of {@b Tianjiu Star's Blade} stacks spent until the end of the attacking creature's turn. If you spend at least 2 stacks, your counterattack also inflicts {@condition Deathrite Haste|TheUndertomesMW} on a hit. If you spend at least 3 stacks, it also inflicts {@condition Deathrite Fissure|TheUndertomesMW}.

subclassFeature.name: Tactical Sewing?! Team Threading!!

entries: Even? Neat as a pin! Stitched your traps right shut! Heh, heheheh...! Still reckon that's a machine job, you cheeky sods?!

Coordination is shockingly one of the attributes you can claim to boast of, and after so long you've really reached a new level of synchronization with your servants, with everyone acting as a marching kingdom coming onto your foes! ( With you as the Kingpin, of course. ) After you roll Initiative or as a Bonus Action during your turns you may designate a formation for you and your Needlekin to coordinate around, as per the following:

items.name: Back to Work, Lads!
entries: You call your Needlekin back to a neutral stance with no special modifiers.

items.name: Beat the @*#! Outta Them!
entries: You set your little guys to go on a full out attack, becoming boastful and aggressive toward other creatures. Each Needlekin grants a +1 bonus modifier to attack and damage rolls for creatures they are Clinging to, yet their extremely annoying presence makes it easier for the creature they're Clinging to to be hit, reducing their AC by the same amount.

items.name: Defend the Buggers!
entries: You order your Needlekin to form a pinwall against attacks, granting creatures they are Clinging to a +1 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws, but their overbearing presence makes it harder to attack, granting them an equal negative modifier toward attack and damage rolls.

items.name: Retreat! Buzz off! Get away!
entries: You quickly tell your Servants to pull back from a harsh situation, making all of them disappear into their Demiplane temporarily. You may re-summon them by changing your formation or as a Free Action at the start of your next turn, making them appear in unoccupied spaces within 15-ft. of you. ( Or already Clinging to your back as if they had climbed on top of you. )

These bonuses stack with the amount of Needlekin Clinging to any given creature. Additionally while out of combat you may have the Needlekin give the Aid Action to other creatures on their skill checks, although they only grant a +1 to any roll each whenever they do so. After granting this bonus the Needlekin gets tired and needs a one minute break before being called to help again.

subclassFeature.name: Take Cover
entries: Upon taking this pact, you've known how to make the most out of any available cover, no matter the situation. As a free action that you may take on your turn, you can duck and take cover behind either a friendly creature within 5-feet of you or a dead corpse of a creature of medium size or larger. As long as you're within 5-feet of this creature, your movement speed is reduced to 10-feet, but with quick footwork and reliance on the cover you have, you gain the effects of half cover with the addition of a bonus +1 to your AC and Dexterity Saving Throws.
Upon reaching 8th level, this bonus becomes a +2 to your AC and Dexterity Saving Throws, in addition, you gain a +1 to hit if you haven't moved from your current space in the last Initiative round.

entries.name: Full Focus
entries: Alternate Feature, Mutually Exclusive with Take Cover
When you take this pact, you've already known for long that being attentive only during combat isn't enough, and that focus should be had even outside of it, at least when you have a job to do.

When you would attempt a skill check outside of combat, you may try to focus in and concentrate on the task at hand, gaining a {@dice 1d4} bonus to the roll. You may add this bonus before or after the roll, but not after the result is announced.
You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and this dice becomes {@dice 1d6} at 8th level, and {@dice 1d8} at 16th level.

subclassFeature.name: Tales of a Bygone Time

entries: Dearie, dearie, would you like to hear a story?

Time has taken it’s toll on many things, yet despite any wear and tear your stories carry on to be told in earnest. You know how to spin an engaging tale while working your way through a crowd or a fight, causing a feeling of Solitude and nostalgia unlike any other. As part of when you give another creature your Bardic Inspiration you may choose another target within it’s reach to inflict with Solitude, which usually manifests as a black smog that leaves your lips and disperses before starting to form around the targets head, becoming thicker as time passes.

A creature afflicted by Solitude feels a growing nostalgia gnaw at their heart, a desperate wish to be in a time that will never come back around. This Solitude has three stages, starting at it’s first and evolving to the next at the end of the afflicted creature’s turn. At the first stage, the creature has an anxiety wash over them, inflicting a -1 negative modifier to their Attack and Damage rolls. At the second stage, a dread starts settling into their heart, halving their movement speed and having them suffer Disadvantage on Wisdom Saving Throws, on top of previous effects. At the third stage, the creature is overcome by a grief that might have never even existed before, having their movement speed reduced to 0, suffering Disadvantage on Dexterity Saving Throws and having any attacks made against them being done so with Advantage. After reaching third stage, the condition ends at the end of the afflicted creature’s next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Target Marked
entries: Once per turn when you reach 6th level, you can delegate to your allies an enemy you can see within your Marksman Weapon's range, marking them for a targeted assault.

While marked, you may choose to direct a friendly creature of your choice that is within melee attack reach of the marked creature to perform a melee attack against the target, but they are unable to score a critical hit while doing so.
You may do this a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier, restoring uses after a short rest. You may also instead spend one Ammunition to direct a friendly creature to attack.

subclassFeature.name: Target Watch

entries: "Thus, you sink into a bottomless slumber."

In any field of battle there is a certain distance you must have in consideration to better deal with trampling down a target with your weapon, but you have learnt how to incarnate a devil from wherever you stand. You may spend your Bonus Action during your turn to shift your stance, changing into one of the following Targeting Settings until the end of your next turn:

items: {@b Close-Quarters.} You shift back your weapon and prepare to take only pot-shots or use its body to bash at your foes, suffering no Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks while within 5-ft. of your target. Additionally, you may perform melee weapon attacks using ranged weapons, still counting as a ranged weapon attack and dealing the ranged weapon's original damage die in bludgeoning damage. Your ranged weapons long and short Ranges are halved. (Any distance ending in 5-ft. is rounded down.) Your Sweet-Spot is 10-ft. While on Close-Quarters you gain advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that are within your short range.

{@b Medium-Range.} Your stance becomes firm and flexible, ready to change at any moment. Your ranged weapon's short range value is decreased by 10-ft., and your long range increases by 10-ft. While on Medium-Range you gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to {@skill Perception} checks.

{@b Far-Watch.} Your stance becomes more reserved and rooted, halving your movement speed. Attempting to target a creature within short range applies Disadvantage on your attack roll, but targets within your long range do not. Your long range increases by 20-ft. Your Sweet-Spot is any range greater than your short range plus 15-ft. While on Far-Watch you gain advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that are outside your short range.

entries: Each of these Targeting Settings has a Sweet Spot. When you attempt to hit a target within your current Sweet Spot, you gain a +1 to hit against that target and deal an additional damage die matching your wielded weapon's on a hit. Upon targeting a Huge or greater creature, only the spaces in the middle intersections of where they occupy count as a Sweet Spot.
If you kill your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} creature while it is within your current Targeting Setting you gain an additional 8 {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM} count.

subclassFeature.name: Tear Film
entries: You have learned to master the coating of your tears so that they become more resistant, making enemies that tear through them quiver. As part of your Blubbering Toad Wild Shape transformation, whenever you grant a creature {@condition Blubberbubble|TheUndertomesASV}, they also gain 1 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count per {@condition Blubberbubble|TheUndertomesASV} count plus 1. If an attack reduces their temporary Hit Points to 0, the attacking creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or immediately gain the same amount of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count the attacked creature has and suffer the effects of a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, then both of their {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts are removed.

subclassFeature.name: Tempered Passion
entries: You can now gain 1 Volatile Passion count once per turn when you hit a target or successfully block an attack. You can expend Volatile Passion together with a spell slot of 5th level or higher to use the following abilities.

entries.name: Combusting Courage.
entries: You cast {@spell Fleeting Emberblade|TheUndertomesWW} and can expend up to 5 Volatile Passion counts to transform it into a hellish slash. The slash fills a 30-foot cone, increasing by 5 feet for every 2 counts expended. Make one spell attack roll and compare it with the AC of every target in the cone. On a hit, a target takes {@damage 8d8} fire damage plus {@damage 2d8} fire damage per count expended. Until the end of your next turn, targets with fire resistance lose it and targets with fire immunity instead have resistance.

entries.name: Waned Eventide.
entries: When a creature attacks you, after the attack misses or rolls damage, you can use your reaction and expend 1 Volatile Passion count to move 5 feet backward. The attacker is forced to move with you and suffers 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. Until the start of your next turn, you can repeat this movement whenever another creature attacks you by expending another count.

entries.name: Cooling Heart.
entries: You regain {@dice 4d8} + your Charisma modifier hit points, plus {@dice 1d8} per Volatile Passion count expended. You can expend a number of counts up to your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Annihilation
entries: A paladin who assumes the Oath of Annihilation swears to hunt every version of someone or something from all planes, obliterating everything that stands in their way.
Have no Mercy. No matter how much it begs and screams. It either deserves this, or this is a necessity. Be not dissuaded by momentary pain.

entries.name: Hunt Endlessly.
entries: There is never time to rest. Sleep with one eye open, and always keep your target in the forefront of your mind.

entries.name: Decapitate.
entries: There is only one way to completely destroy something - remove its head or its ability to retain consciousness.

entries.name: Never forget.
entries: Why it is you hunt. Why it must be purged. Let the hatred burn and the ire fester whenever you clash with your sword.

items: {@b Leave no Action Unpunished.} When one wrongs you, your creed or your fellow, you shall act swift punishment so they may never offend again.
{@b Scour The Eart if Need Be.} Nothing should ever stand in the way of your needs, when you speak your truths, they shall be followed to the end.
{@b Obedience of the Powerful.} You shall obey those above you, yet all those under shall listen to your voice, lest they be led astray.
{@b Speak Clearly and Loudly.} Your pride is only another tool for which your commandments grow stronger, speak loud and clear for all to hear.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Loyalty

entries: "The Middle remembers. It doesn't matter what I did here; the Middle will remember everyone and everything that dared to turn their back on it."
The tenets of a Paladin that assumes the Oath of Loyalty require an unshakable bond between them and their family.

entries.name: Never Forget.
entries: If slights were committed against your family, write them down in the book of vengeance. Never allow whoever dared to stand against one of your siblings to see the light of day.

entries.name: Love Your Siblings.
entries: Your brothers and sisters are your loyal family and must be treated with respect. Their slights can be forgiven, and they deserve compliments and rewards when successfully achieving their goals and your own.

entries.name: Recover What Was Stolen!
entries: This is an optional Tenet. You might have lost something extremely precious to you, like hair coupons to an incredible salon of complete and total lusciousness. You and your family will hunt this thief to the ends of the earth, and you will make sure they pays for their crimes.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Procuration
entries: A paladin who takes this oath has the tenets of Procuration has their tenets inscribed at the back of a device they carry around known as a Magicked Beeper or a Procuration Relay. That is a magic item that is Attuned to the paladin, yet doesn't count toward maximum attunement slots.

It cannot be affected by anti-magic effects and if removed from your person, it reappears instantly to be bound to your neck through a collar. You cannot remove the collar by any means short of the Will demanding it, the {@spell wish} spell or through special means.

items.name: Aid the Will With Heart.
items.entry: Nothing matters more than the Will's whims, and you are no exception, follow orders even if they might put you at risk, for that is the Will.

items.name: Follow the Prescripts.
items.entry: Never betray that which binds you to purpose, for procuring their goals is what matter most, for that is the Will.

items.name: Hunt Down Oathbreakers.
items.entry: Those who fail to follow these holy tenets must be struck down by your blade, for that is the Will.

items.name: Recognize That Which is Absolute.
items.entry: Nobody, nothing and no being is above the Will. Bring down any in its path if necessary, for that is the Will.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Protection
entries: The tenets of the Oath of Protection drive a Paladin to perform selfless actions for the wellbeing of others.

entries.name: Be Their Shield.
entries: The weak cannot protect themselves. Those as strong or stronger than you can handle difficulties thrown at them, but you must stand between the defenseless and the incoming danger, feeling the heat of any inferno in their stead.

entries.name: Strike Valiantly.
entries: Your weapons are of a larger size not only to act as a shield, but to strike into an enemy's heart with powerful certainty, making sure they do not get back up after the battle.

entries.name: Drive Back Evil.
entries: Move ahead with your greatsword to push back the forces of darkness that threaten the common people. Do not allow them to pass through your aegis of safety!

entries.name: Dominate the Greatsword.
entries: You do not need to carry both a weapon and a shield. Let your greatsword alone act as both fortress and executioner.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Resplendence
entries: Be above all.

A Paladin who follows the Oath of The Resplendent pleads to no god nor ruler other than themself, carrying divinity not in scripture but in pure presence and grace. They have a tendency to look down on others, but overall what sets them apart from others is how they always put themselves and their thoughts above anyone else.

items: Recognize Yourself. Be true to yourself no matter what, as your being shall be supreme along others.
Always Be Above. Never look up to other things, for your road shall be beaten and paved by yourself.
See Through All. Recognize the flaws of all who are graced with your presence and always act according to your best judgement.
Inspire {@spell Fear}. Let your presence be unforgettable, dig the vision of you deep into anyone's hearts.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of the Obsidian Saint

entries: "A hammer once gripped must be brought down—that is simply the natural law."
A Paladin who takes this oath has the tenets of the Obsidian Saint,

entries.name: Stand Thy Ground.
entries: Impede all of those whom hold ill-wishes toward you, your fellows and the sacred land of which your feet are graced by, lest it be ravaged by the evils that roam abound.

entries.name: Collect Thy Luxury.
entries: The greatest luxuries of the world await ye, however stand fast against that of which mocks grandness in decadence. Differentiate the holiness that is in arduous work upon the structures laid afore creativity.

entries.name: Relay Thy Voice.
entries: Act as the speaking mouthpiece of the Obsidian God, enlighten those whose lack of colouring upsets their soul and offer them the righteous way. Remind them of their mistakes when necessary, and smite those who don themselves in the red of rotting flesh.

subclassFeature.name: The Book of Vengeance

entries: "Kiddo, remember what Mama told you? You ever find anything you don't like, you can talk to me about it!"

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until the end of the first round of combat.

Whenever you hit an enemy with counts of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: The City

entries: "As - deep - as lay - the workers' - city below the - earth, so high above - it towered the complex - known as the "Club of the - Sons," with its lecture halls and - libraries, its theaters and stadiums."

The City your mind envisions can hardly stay within your head nowadays, with your innate magic becoming engrained in the air wherever you pass by. You can make use a fraction of your power to bring that vision to life, using your Bonus Action to reach out to a creature that can hear you within 120-ft. to make them fit into one of the Molds presented below. If the creature is hostile to you, they automatically gain the negative passive effect of the Mold, alternatively if they are friendly they gain the positive one instead.

entries.caption: Molds
rows: Heads

rows.name: The Ascended
entries: The Head has the most magnificent ideas come to them in a spark of inspiration, granting them a +1 bonus modifier to Intelligence and Wisdom checks or saving throws.

rows.name: The Obstinate
entries: The Head cannot accept failure or the disgraces of those below them. Whenever they or a creature friendly to them fails an attack roll, skill check or saving throw they must use their Reaction to attack them if they are within reach. ( Once per creature. )

rows: Hands

rows.name: The Resilient
entries: The Hand is used to heavy workloads and can last in the worst situations, granting them a +1 bonus modifier to Strength and Constitution checks or saving throws.

rows.name: The Worn Out
entries: The Hand is overworked, tired and pacified. Their tender meat causes their AC to be reduced by 2, to a minimum of 10.

rows: Hearts

rows.name: The Diamantine
entries: The Heart often refuses to stop beating, being the lynchpin that keeps the whole body functioning. They are Immune to being {@condition Frightened|PHB} and may spend their Reaction to retain one Hit Point when they would fall below that value. This lasts until the end of the current creature's turn.

rows.name: The Ascended
entries: The Heart feels double whatever others would, being extremely prone to mood swings and to strong emotional responses. They suffer Disadvantage on Intelligence and Wisdom saving throws.
As part of the same Action you may spend a number Metamagic Points for additional effects, as per the following:

entries.caption: Heads Table
rows: The Astute.
The Head may grant themselves a {@dice d6} bonus modifier on any skill check of their choice. They may do this up to thrice per long rest.
The Attentive.
The Head gains an additional Reaction per turn for each 2 Metamagic Points spent.
The Architect.
Whenever the Head grants another creature a bonus modifier, that bonus modifier increases by 1 if it is numeric or increases by one step if it is dice- based. ( D4s become D6s and so on. )

entries.caption: Hands Table
rows: The Resolute/ The Ruined.
The Hand's bonus modifier granted is increased by 1 per each 2 Metamagic spent. Alternatively, the Hand's AC is reduced by a further 1 per each 2 Metamagic spent.
The Winded.
The Hand's body is heavy with the burdens that they must carry without pause, reducing their movement speed by 5-ft. per Metamagic Point spent. ( To a minimum of 10-ft. remaining. )
The Yielding.
The Hand is capable of great change despite all its strengths. They lose all damage Resistances and Immunities, but also lose all Vulnerabilities. They cannot suffer the effects of a Critical Hit.

entries.caption: Hearts Table
rows: The Guiding.

The Heart's teaching proliferate with ease, infest the rigidities of life and transform the world around them. Creatures within 15-ft. of Hearts cannot be {@condition Frightened|PHB} or {@condition Charmed|PHB}. They also add your Charisma modifier to resist the effects of Illusion spells.
The Lethargic.

The Heart's beating becomes weaker and weaker the more life drowns them out in a world of noise which cares not for their well-being. Whenever they fail a saving throw by a difference of 5 or further they suffer one point of Exhaustion.
The Light-headed.

The world shall not destroy that which has been embraced by the light. The Heart gain Resistance to all damage types it isn't Vulnerable to. When you grant this effect to a creature, the DM chooses another creature within reach that is hostile to them. ( Without telling you. ) Any damage that creature deals to the Heart is poisonous and vile, having the Heart be considered Vulnerable to all damage types from that source.

entries: These may be applied to hostile or friendly creatures as long as they are under the effects of your harmonization, yet a creature may only be made fit one Mold at any given time. While under these effects, they are considered Bricks of the Tower.This lasts for up to one minute, until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious|PHB} or you sever the effects on a creature as a Free Action during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: The Eye of Precognition

entries: "What, having a hard time landing a hit?"
