You have 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}. While you have counts of this, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet
Your Armor Class increases by 3

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature misses an attack against you due to your AC bonus, and 5 counts whenever you take no damage after succeeding on a Dexterity saving throw.

Once you lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesPP}. While you have counts of this, you gain the following characteristics:

items: You always roll an additional damage die of the weapon you are attacking with
Your Armor Class decreases by 3
Whenever taking Fire damage, take an additional damage die of the same value as your eye socket burns.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesPP}. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature hits an attack against you due to your AC decrease, and 3 counts whenever you take additional Fire damage from a hostile source. Once you lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesPP}, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesPP} and gain up to 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

subclassFeature.name: The Finale
entries: You have finally become the master of the parade, rivaled by none and adored by all. Once you use your Lead of the Parade ability, you can choose up to three creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you to gain a stack of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesLL}. If you choose three creatures, they will each gain a stack of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesLL}; if you choose two creatures, you can choose which one of them gains two stacks while the other gains one; if you choose one creature, they will get all three stacks.

Additionally, when a creature uses your Bardic Inspiration on their attack roll and successfully hits because of it, they inflict 2 stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: The Living Will

entries: "You may brood over curiosities regarding the Will of the Prescript, yet inquiry bears no weight in its execution. What is absolute can only be obeyed."

A Warlock who serves a patron known only as the "Living WIll" is one who is either purely devoted or forced into submission by forces way past any sense of recognition except acceptance. They are usually highly organized and may even follow a hierarchical structure, unlike many other of those who have made pacts - to the point they may be confused even for clergy with their regimented arts.

When playing with this subclass, consider your character's relation to the Living Will itself and its ordinance, such as if the character is one to follow whatever orders they are given blindly or have questions about them and their vagueness. A good theme to go in line with this choice of subclass is nearly always having your character question their sense of freedom and how much their own will affects themselves and the world around them.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, the Will manifests itself as a by-product of the fall of the great Netheril - a series of magical constructs that melded together into a collective conscience that outlived the fallen empire. In others, such as Thespis, it is instead a creed nurtured by the Nushae, grand lizardkin who worship the Wyrd, taking the Will as the Wyrd's very own and using such force to shape the material plane in its image.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Living Will lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you. You also gain the {@spell First Lightlock|TheUndertomesLW} cantrip as one of your Warlock spells.

entries.caption: Living Will Expanded Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell command}
2nd
{@spell Sense Quarry|TheUndertomesLW}, {@spell spiritual weapon}
3rd
{@spell sending}, {@spell tongues}
4th
{@spell Binding Chains|TheUndertomesLW}, {@spell locate creature}
5th
{@spell geas}, {@spell scrying}

entries.name: Will of the Prescript

entries: "The Index finger points; as does the Prescript that indicates the path we must tread."

The Living Will is a patron who always unavoidably contacts you, immersing you in orders to be fulfilled for your continued existence and grace. The form of contact may differ, from simply appearing as a paper slip in your pocket to having another such follower of the Will approaching you to deliver a message.

At the start of a combat or at the start of your next turn whenever there isn't a target of a Will's Paper Slip, a random hostile creature who has rolled Initiative becomes the target of the effect. To do so, roll an appropriate sided die to the amount of creatures around you, using the dice that matches double the value of creatures if it is only two or an odd number of creatures, then halving the result ( adding one on an odd result ), such as if there are only three creatures you roll a d6 and on a result of 3, you attack the second hostile creature in Initiative.

The Will's Paper Slip effect has four ranks which increase whenever certain conditions are met, starting at 1 and being reset after you or its current target are killed or knocked Unconscious. Whenever advancing the ranks of this Effect, your attacks surge with the Living Will's power, granting bonus effects when triggered. For these effects and how to advance ranks, see the following table:

entries.caption: Will's Paper Slip
rows: I

Roll a d4 when the Paper Slip is first drawn, with 1 being Bludgeoning, 2 being Slashing and 3 being Piercing. 4 is any other damage type. Ascend this Slip whenever you deal damage to the target according to the result.
You inflict double your proficiency bonus in additional damage and double your Sinking count on a hit.
II
Ascend this Slip whenever you deal damage to the target three times after first reaching Rank II.
You gain one Grace of the Prescript until the end of combat and two Poise count.
III
Ascend this Slip whenever you hit the target with a Warlock spell or have them fail one of your Spell Saving Throws. Cantrips do not count toward this ascension.
On ascending past this rank, the target suffers triple the amount of Sinking that would usually be dealt on a hit. You gain the same value in Poise count.
IV

This Slip cannot be ascended. Kill the target or knock them Unconscious to trigger the following effect. If you are fighting against a single stronger target ( Such as a boss, as per the DM's choice ) you trigger this effect whenever it loses more than a fourth of its maximum hit points, rounded down. If this effect is triggered in this way, this Slip reverts to rank I.
You gain two counts of Grace of the Prescript until your next short or long rest.

entries: In addition to that, you always deal an additional amount of damage equal to your proficiency bonus and half that value (rounded down) in Sinking count to targets afflicted by the Will's Paper Slip. The effects of the above table are only triggered upon an ascension (except of fourth rank) and do not stack.

If you are knocked Unconscious while another creature is the target of the Will's Paper Slip effect, you suffer one count of Karmic Consequences. You also suffer one count of the effect if combat ends while a creature is suffering from the Will's Paper Slip or if they are killed by another non-friendly creature.
"The index finger points; as does the Prescript that indicates the path we must tread. That is what gives the Index its name."

entries.name: Follower of an Order

entries: "It is said that the Will of the Prescript and the Will of the City are one and the same."

Regardless of the presence of combat or not, the Will always communicates something for you to perform every single day, so that its whims are set in motion even if you cannot understand. Once per long rest you roll a d100, receiving a Prescript in accordance to the result, a small slip of paper containing a set of orders to follow. These Prescripts may be found at the end of this document.

When complete, you gain one Devotion point, which may be spent to re-roll any roll performed by you or a friendly creature. You may have up to half your proficiency bonus' worth of Devotion points at any given time. You may spend Devotion after any die are rolled, but before its consequences.

You may also spend a Devotion point to have an item of common rarity appear within an unoccupied space in a 30-ft. radius of yourself. This is a result of another follower's dedication to the Will that has set up this item for your use.
If not complete until your next long rest, you suffer a count ofKarmic Consequences.

subclassFeature.name: The Neverseen
entries: Upon reaching 17th level, your prowess to hide yourself is so heightened that you have learnt how to wear another's skin with ease. Not literally, not in most parts, at least. After killing a humanoid ( Or human-like, such as an Angel celestial ) you may spend a long rest studying their body and make prosthetics to don a costume of the dead person.

You also impeccably are able to imitate their mannerisms and habits, as you can infer them from seeing them at their rawest before death. You have advantage on any Charisma checks to pass yourself as the dead creature, in addition you gain half your Proficiency Bonus as a bonus modifier to any skill checks that the dead person was proficient and you are not, as you push yourself to achieve a perfect disguise, so no one may gaze upon your true skin.

subclassFeature.name: The Orthodox Blade [整劍]

entries: "Another step closer to that singular Way of the Blade."

Your dimensional cuts have been getting stronger, and now you can sever the life of more than one enemy at once. At the start of your turn, if you have hit a creature with an unsheathed sword attack last turn, you gain 3 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever you use a feature that would require you to spend Ki points, you may choose to spend thrice that amount in {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.

As part of your unsheathed attack action, you may spend a number of Ki points equal to 2 per additional creature and attempt to hit a number of additional creatures with your attack equal to your proficiency bonus, as long as they are within 5 feet of the creature that was originally attacked.

subclassFeature.name: The Sewing Commences

entries: "I sewed it by hand, just like you bloody asked!! What?! The stitches are too even, so a machine must've done it?! Get back here, you c$#%! I'll show you 18 premium stitches! Shit-ten and bugger-eight, straight into your skin! WITH THIS NEEDLE!!!"

It is only by seeing through the onslaught of insufferable people that you've come to fully understand how to use your broken hands to create anything your mind has been set to, turning thought to idea to action to flesh to shape to weave.

As an Action during your turn you may attempt to Taxidermize a creature, spending a warlock spell slot and rolling your choice of a melee weapon attack roll or a melee spell attack roll against them. On a hit, you manage to turn them into a living pincushion, having them suffer an amount of {@dice d12+2} piercing damage, {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} and {@condition Bind|TheUndertomesNW} count equal to the spell slot level spent.

If you miss your attempt to Taxidermize a creature you may spend your Reaction to unleash the unbearable frustration that has been eating at you, becoming irate and nearly irrational until the end of your next turn. You regain your Action and have two Extra Attacks for the duration, but automatically fail Wisdom saving throws and cannot benefit from your Needlekin's abilities, as they are scared of you. Whenever you deal damage through this state you deal an additional damage die and {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} count.

In the case that you attempt to Taxidermize a creature who has their movement speed reduced to 0 through effects that aren't the {@condition Prone|PHB} Condition you deal {@dice d4+1} piercing damage instead of d12s. This damage is also multiplied by your current amount of Needlekin around, as they join in to prey on the weak.

If you kill a non-summoned creature you've Taxidermize that hasn't recovered ( Lost all their {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} and count. ), you may start working on their dead body as a Bonus Action, creating an item as per your Bespoke Stitching feature without the need to spend {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count. When you do so, this item is not destroyed at your next long rest and counts as a +X magic item, where X is half that creature's proficiency modifier.

Your knowledge of regulation has also granted you a better leadership quality toward your Servants, making it so you suffer no negative modifiers from being Clinged to by them. Additionally, you are considered to Resist any damage you'd suffer in their place.

subclassFeature.name: The Shame of My Famiglia

entries: "... Tsk. Great. Not a single damn idiot left to call over for a drink... Bunch of weak-ass pushovers. Got chewed up by those disgusting bugs and died like trash."

You have lost a position of power important to you, or perhaps something similar, and it has been difficult for you to recover ever since. You have advantage on saving throws against becoming drunk. You refuse to drink {@item ale (gallon)|PHB|Ale}, but after consuming an entire {@item Fine Wine (bottle)|PHB|bottle of Fine Wine}, you may choose to immediately become affected by the {@condition Drunk|TheUndertomesPP} condition for 1 minute. You gain the following characteristics when affected by the {@condition Drunk|TheUndertomesPP} condition:

items: You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks, Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws and ranged attacks.
As a bonus action, you can yell at one of your allies to do better, granting them advantage on their next ability check, saving throw or attack roll, your choice

When you hit a creature that is {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremoring}, or Both, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} die of damage of equal damage to your weapon's damage type
You can substitute one of your attacks for a {@i Sezionatura di Cervo}.

entries.name: Sezionatura di Cervo
entries: On a hit, you deal damage as usual and the creature suffers 1 count of both {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you are raging, you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Creatures that are Medium or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: The Unforgivable Sin
entries: For so long you have held onto the scraps of sanity left from trying to keep everyone around you so pure, yet your disgusting desires can be pushed back no longer. When you reach 17th level you gain the following:

items: {@b All-Engulfing Hunger.} As an action you may unleash your pent up desires in a physical manner that destroys and degrades all around you, you spread an aura around 20-ft of you, taking the image of an unholy whirlpool of blood or any other gruesome description of your choice. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this aura has their blood shift and turn inside them, lashing out and lacerating them from the inside, having them suffer {@dice 2d4} necrotic damage and 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks. Other creatures who consume Bloodfeast are immune to this. This lasts for one minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

{@b Weight of the Kin.} When you would hit with any attack, you may add a number of {@dice d10} necrotic damage die for each cumulative 7 hit points you have missing, fuelled by the wish of finally having other filthy beings feel the same pain you've had to endure for so long. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your Wisdom Modifier, recovering uses on a long rest.

{@b A Holy Man's Breaking Point.} When you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious} or have your hit points reduced below 1, you may spend your reaction to instead cling onto your conscience by throwing away your raving concerns and inhibitions. You cannot regain hit points while in this state and it lasts for up to one minute or until another creature lands a Critical Hit on you or you are killed. Once per each creature's turn you suffer one point of Exhaustion if you take more than 20 damage during their turn. While in this state, All-Engulfing Hunger is always active and deals {@dice 3d6} necrotic damage per turn instead. Additionally, you gain one extra Action that you can use to Attack or Cast a Spell for this duration.

subclassFeature.name: The Will of the Manor

entries: Butlers... Where are the stewards of this house? You must know... Lead me to them, now!

The vengeful wraith that is the Old Master has taken such a profound hold of your soul that it has made your heart its manor, your body its image. As an action, you transform into a Large, vengeful Aberration from the Old Master’s resting place, made out of wood and insectile parts.You gain the following abilities:

items: Any creature of your choice that starts their turn within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer 3 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
When you use your Bygone Days feature, you can mark two creatures as an Interloper instead of one.

As an action, you can make a spell attack against a creature within 30 feet of you to restrain them inside your insectile, wooden mouth. If the attack hits, that creature takes {@dice 2d6} piercing + {@dice 2d6} cold damage and suffers 6 counts of Sinking.

entries: Afterwards, they must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition Restrained} until the start of your next turn. If a creature fails this saving throw twice in a row, they become afflicted with Madness. Roll on the Short-Term Madness table to determine how the creature will react.
You can use this ability once per short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: There Is No Pardon

entries: Before anyone else, you… shan’t pardon me.

No longer grounded, your god has given you wings to fly and exact their punishment with precise judgment. You gain two additional tenets. You also gain the ability to summon two spectral, golden wings for a minute with a bonus action, giving you a flying movement speed of 30 feet. While flying this way, you can use two Reactions per turn, instead of just one. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

entries.caption: Emerald Tablet Tenets
rows: No creature shall harm an envoy of the heavens (when a creature hits you with an attack roll)
You gain a maximum of +2 AC until the start of your next turn, and {@dice 1d10} temporary Hit Points.

The creature must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they are imprisoned and crushed by your deity’s hands, taking {@dice 5d10} radiant damage + {@dice 5d10} bludgeoning damage and being {@condition Restrained} until the start of your next turn. If they succeed, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.
No creature shall force the hand of a divine guardian (when a creature forces you to make a saving throw)
Until the start of your next turn, you gain advantage on saving throws.

They must perform a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they suffer {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the difference between their resulting dice and your save DC. This {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count is not lost after a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At the start of your turn, if you are still afflicted by what the saving throw caused, they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a success, they only suffer half the {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts equal to the difference (rounded down) and they expire normally.

subclassFeature.name: Thorns Granting Happiness

entries: Come under me. I’ll liberate you from all kinds of pain.

Through various feats of alchemy and theories being put to practice, you managed to imbue your very spells with a cloud of elation, having nettles form around your mana to infect others with joy. Your spells inflict Pleasure Thorns on a hit or failed saving throw equal to the spell’s level. These Thorns have an additive effect according to the table below, causing an overflow of joy and euphoria in steps:

rows: I
The target is joyfully distractible.
The target has difficulty paying attention on anything and everything, suffering Disadvantage on Investigation and Perception rolls.
II
Overwhelming positivity afflicts the target.
The target can see the best in all, having Disadvantage against being {@condition Charmed} but advantage against being {@condition Frightened}. They suffer a -1 penalty to their AC.
III
The target cannot perceive pain anymore.
The target always takes at least two of the maximum value of damage from any saving throw that would deal damage.

entries: Effects stack and they lose one Pleasure Thorn per turn they haven’t gained it. Creatures that are Immune to being {@condition Charmed} or being {@condition Poisoned} gain only half the Thorns that would be inflicted. Cantrips inflict one Thorn.

subclassFeature.name: Thruster Compression Bullets

entries: "Daring to breathe when you haven't even followed the underboss's command? Now that's quite discourteous."

There is a special kind of ammunition that runs through your organization, Scorch Propellant Round, a kind of which you have just been trust to carry around and use at your own discretion - Of course, with the possibility of upper sight regarding it as unnecessary, so think well when spending these bullets. You have an amount of Scorch Propellant Round equal to your proficiency bonus, being able to resupply half of them at a short rest and all over a long rest. You may use them according to the 3rd level feature you have chosen, as per the following:

entries.name: Ammunition Tributary
entries: You have learned how to use these Scorch Propellant Round on your ranged fire, being able to instantly replace a regular bullet and spend one such Round before rolling a ranged weapon attack on your turn.

When you do so, the bullet's propellant systems supercharge the shot, causing it to easily pierce through any targets in a line equal to the short Range of your wielded weapon. You make one ranged weapon attack roll once, counting the result against all targets within reach and dealing damage to any whose AC you'd beat, also inflicting {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus. You may then choose to convert the targets current count into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

Additionally, you may roll an additional ranged weapon attack and take the lower result to target any additional creatures that would be within a line equal to your long range. On a hit you deal half that {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead. If you would deal {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1} damage this way to multiple creatures, you only deal half that damage instead.

entries.name: Warden of Respect
entries: You have learned how to use these Scorch Propellant Round on to further the impact and speed of your melee swings, being able to instantly chamber and spend one such Round before rolling a melee weapon attack on your turn.

Whenever you do so, your weapon flares in flame as it swings through the air, dealing an additional amount of d8 fire damage and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. You may also choose to convert the targets {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} as well.

Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with this attack you may immediately spend another Round to make an additional melee weapon attack against the same target benefitting from the same bonuses. You may do so until you perform a total amount of attacks equal to half your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Time for Our Heads to Burst

entries: Don’t you want to feel the dazzling and vibrant display of colors?
The handling of pure elation you employ has become fatal, more than the body of a living being can handle. Your Pleasure Thorns gain their final rank, as follows:

rows: VI
The target is joyfully distractible.
The target has difficulty paying attention on anything and everything, suffering Disadvantage on Investigation and Perception rolls.

entries: You’ve also learnt how to spread joy in a more effective manner, making it so every time you use your Poppin’ Elation feature on other creatures they also spread half their Thorn count to all creatures not suffering from the condition that would suffer damage.

subclassFeature.name: Time-Guarded Memory
entries: The knowledge of time and history are intrinsically linked, as awareness of one helps determine the state of the other. You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} skill. Whenever you take or receive the {@action Help} action, the creature making the aided roll gains an additional bonus equal to the helper's proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Tirer du Sens de l'Émotion Brute

entries: "Lorsque j'entendis pour la première fois la Voix murmurer à mes oreilles... lorsque l'Être Chéri accepta avec tant de grâce le mouchoir que j'avais confectionné... je crus que j'allais exploser de joie."

Red clings to your body like a tight hug, giving you warmth and purpose. You can tap into it as a source of inspiration and of hope, of faith that you can become something greater than a bottom-feeder if given the chance to do so: While Enraged, your ears ring with the most natural of voices beckoning you toward unseen light and your heart flutters with inspiration, with this growing feeling being represented by having at least 1 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} while in Rage. {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} grants you the following abilities:

entries.name: Griffe à Coudre
entries: As a Bonus Action you may spend 2 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count to turn one of your body's muscles into a mass of tissue that expands outward to form a skinless hand which you may instantly give a weapon to wield. You then make a melee weapon attack against a target within 15-ft. using that hand's wielded weapon, or if it isn't wielding any, using it's tendons as claws that count as a natural weapon that you are proficient with which have the Finesse property and deal {@dice 2d4} slashing damage and 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit. You may use this hand for regular weapon attacks until the end of your turn, where the hand dissolves into liquefied blood and you may use a Free Action to catch the weapon is was possibly wielding with a free hand. While Griffe à Coudre is active, your melee weapon attacks that wouldn't deal {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} now inflict half the count that would be caused by this abilities' natural weapon attack.

entries.name: Tissage Supplémentaire
entries: As a Free Action you may take once during your turn you may flay yourself bare so that you can drive inspiration from every single feeling that comes to grace you. You instantly suffer up to your proficiency bonus' worth of d12 damage that cannot be reduced through any means, then gaining 2 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count per damage die suffered. Additionally, you may choose to lose Resistance to all damage types to gain one {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count whenever you suffer damage from other sources for the same duration.

entries.name: Goûter à la Mode
entries: As an Action during your turn you may spend 6 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count to extend a number of hands from your body, having them trash and grab at all living ( and unliving ) beings within a 15-ft. cone of you. All creatures within that reach must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@dice 3d8} slashing damage and 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count plus an additional {@dice 1d8} slashing damage and 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count per 5-ft. square they occupy within that range, or half the damage and count on a success. You may then choose to devour whatever material is acquired, recovering an amount of d4 Hit Points equal to the number of creatures who fail this saving throw plus a value equal to half your current {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count.

The reach for Griffe à Coudre's extended attack extends by 5-ft. and {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} infliction increases by 2 whenever you reach 8th, ( 20-ft. , 4 count. ) 12th ( 25-ft., 6 count. ) and 16th level. ( 30-ft., 8 count. )
The amount of {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count gained per damage die suffered as per Tissage Supplémentaire increases to 3 when you reach 8th level and to 4 when you reach 16th level.

The range for Goûter à la Mode increases by 15-ft., its base damage increases by {@dice 2d8} and its base {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} infliction increases by 2 count when you reach 8th, ( 30-ft., {@dice 5d8}, 5 count. ) and 12th level. ( 45-ft., {@dice 7d8}, 7 count. )
Whenever an effect from this subclass asks for a saving throw, its Save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of your Strength or Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: To Be The Blade Sharpened in Violence
entries: Where your fellows may have perished, you lie there in remembrance of them. Where one would falter near death, you only grow stronger. At 17th level and onward, you only find your resolve boldened through the edge of death, as such, when you are below three fourths of your maximum hit points, rounded down, you gain a +1 to hit and a +1 to your damage rolls. This bonus increases for each additional fourth of missing hit points.
If you have only a single hit point left, you instead gain a +4 to hit and a +4 to your damage rolls, also delivering a critical hit on a dice result of 19 or 20.

subclassFeature.name: To Become a Canvas, Slowly Painted

entries: "Hah... the waves are rolling in."

The future is pre-ordained, and you are but a gear in a greater plan, slowly letting it shape you and in turn you shape the world around you. At the beginning of every long rest you draw a Prescript from the Crawling Prescripts Table at the end of this document. When you do so, you have up to a week or until you your next long rest to finish its objective, as per described in the Prescript itself.

Upon completing this Prescript, you gain a single count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD}. You may have a maximum of this effect equal to half your Proficiency Bonus at any given time, rounded down, and a minimum of -2.
You gain the following effects while you have negative or positive counts of this effect:

items: {@b Lesser than zero.} Your heart is beating at an unsteady rhythm, much like the crumbling road you feel like you walk upon. You cannot spend Hit Die to recover Hit Points during a short rest and only recover half your Maximum Hit Points on a long rest. You suffer a negative modifier to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws equal to the negative count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD}. You suffer Disadvantage on Death saving throws.

{@b Zero count.} You constantly feel uneasy, as if something bad will happen at any given time that you are not working towards your goal. You suffer a -1 negative modifier on Wisdom saving throws and gain a +1 bonus modifier on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Investigation} checks.

{@b Greater than one.} You can feel that all is going according to plan, and this confidence in the greater drives you on with a practiced ease. You gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to your current {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesFD} count. You deal additional damage equal to that value whenever you deal damage using your Cleric spells and your Spell Save DC increases by the same value.

entries: Additionally, whenever you fail a Prescript drawn from this feature, you suffer 3 {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesFD}. Whenever you complete one, you instead gain 2 {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD}, except you lose one at the end of your combats. You may only have up to 6 {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesFD} this way.

subclassFeature.name: To Become a Star
entries: You overclock your Star Luminary to a devastating effect making it grasp the power of constellations as if they were directly listening to your will and requests. It becomes a +3 Spellcasting Focus and as an Action during your turn you may overload the Star Luminary, making it so all Seven Marbles float behind your back, having all their effects active at once, with any Marble not on your inventory falling down from the sky to aid you. You may use a Celestial Burst as an part of this action, and Celestial Bursts do not deactivate an Astral Marble’s effects.
This can be used once per long rest and it remains active until you are {@condition Unconscious} or until the end of your next turn.

You gain an additional turn of having your Star Luminary Overloaded per Artificer Level above 15th, to a maximum of 5 Turns at 20th-level. You suffer one point of {@condition Exhaustion} per turn spent in this state after the second.

subclassFeature.name: To Behold Light Through a Gilded Keyhole (Key)

entries: "I'm sure you would like to know more about this... key. Hmm~ How do I put this? It's a medium...? A vessel for knowledge...? Kinda hard to explain to someone who hasn't used it before."

You are of a sect which makes use of special relics to glimpse newfound expertise directly, being one of the select number who learnt how to maximize learning in this way. You carry a gigantic Key of Knowledge, a magic item you are permanently attuned to that doesn't count toward your attunement limit. You gain the following benefits when you choose this feature:

items: Your Key of Knowledge counts as a monk weapon for you and you deal an additional 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on weapon attacks while wielding it. This increases by one upon reaching 8th level in this class.

Like the library of your mind, your Key may expand as needed to destroy things in your path. You may consume one {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} count at the end of your turn to expand the Key of Knowledge's size. Until the end of next turn, melee weapon attacks performed with the Key deal additional damage equal to the {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a target, to a maximum amount of damage equal to your proficiency bonus. It also gains the Reach weapon property, with that range being expanded by a further 5-ft. upon reaching 8th level in this class.

Quick attacks can be done with a quick palm, but you'd rather not dirty your hands when you can simply unlock a new way to attack. You may use your Bonus Action to perform an additional melee weapon attack with your Key by spending 1 Ki Point. Additionally, while you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} you may use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier for skill checks pertaining to the latter attribute, including the Condition's bonus. You may also spend one {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} to gain the same bonus to your {@skill Perception} checks for the next minute.

entries: If lost or destroyed, your Key of Knowledge can be re-made from a regular key over the course of a short or long rest.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: You may consider the Key of Knowledge as a magic item that can be given to an Artificer, Blacksmith or any other fitting craftsperson to work on and transform into a +1 monk weapon and so on for the sake of scaling until 11th level. Of course, gold cost may change harshly depending on campaign but we recommend having a base price 500 GP in materials for this +1 upgrade.

subclassFeature.name: To Embrace a Fleeting Moment in Life Toward Stillness of Death

entries: "Well do I understand your sentiment on death. Why not lay rest to the impulses in your heart for a moment and converse with me more?"

Even in a fight you've trained your thoughts to remain calm, to be a guiding light to all those around you. This training has also resulted in a demeanour that pacifies the pain in one's ailing mind to provide at least a moment's clarity. You gain a +2 bonus modifier on {@skill Insight} and Charisma skill checks regarding conversing with the Undead and while within 10-ft. of you, they regain at least the faintest hint of their memories and personality. - enough to enable conversation in the first place. Additionally you may use your Bonus Action to calm Undead creatures and similarly unliving beings. All Undead creatures within 60-ft. that can hear you must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC or become {@condition Charmed} by you and non-hostile toward creatures that haven't attacked them for the next minute, awakening some spark of sentience in them.

You do not gain this feature's skill check bonus modifier if the Undead are actively hostile to you or if you have dealt damage to them within the past hour. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

Whenever you calm Undead in this way, a butterfly perches upon the shoulder of the yet-to-be-departed, granting them a +1 bonus to Wisdom saving throws and they may choose to spend their Action to instantly die in peace. Upon reaching 20th level in this subclass, whenever a creature dies this way any curse or negative effect of your choice that would be caused, activated or maintained is instantly negated and lifted.

You may give these butterflies to friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you as a Bonus Action, spending an use of the feature. An ally remains with a butterfly for a minute before it flutters off, gaining the same Wisdom saving throw bonus and reducing any {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count they suffer by one. ( To a minimum of one. )
These bonus modifiers to your skill checks and Wisdom saving throws is increased by 1 upon you reaching 12th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: To Find That Which is Inside You

entries: "...May as well get used to it, right?"

As you reach 20th level, a split path is before you and you must make a choice based on the progression of your character thus far. These are split in polar opposites, either embracing the Will fully and having your being be indiscernible from it, or severing your ties to that which points your way and becoming your own being. Upon reaching 20th level, make a choice:

items: その時、下人は迷いを捨てた。 You gain the Unquestionable. Unquestionable. feature.
僕は幸福よりも真理を選ぶ。You gain the Truthful Procuration. feature.

entries.name: Unquestionable. Unquestionable.

entries: "Hear all. Hope all. With these hands, all will..."

Your heart beats when the Will wills it so, and it will cease beating only when the Will wills it so. The Prescripts that have led, fed and nourished you are all that your heart desires, and you in kind are part of the Will's wishes. Upon reaching the 20th level, you become the living instrument for the Will to enact itself upon the world, gaining the following benefits:

items: In addition to the random creature chosen randomly to become the The Prescript's Target, the first creature you hit during your turn also suffers from the effect. You may not choose another creature to become a Target until your chosen one is dead, and that creature does not count toward your Channel Divinity Feature's limit.
Your /UNLOCKED/ state now lasts for up to 10 minutes and you gain a +2 modifier to AC while in it.
You gain double the counts of Grace of the Prescript and Karmic Consequence whenever you gain either of the Conditions.

entries.name: Truthful Procuration

entries: "I have the talent to walk the path in front of me, if nothing else... Even if I don't have much happiness, I know where to go in the immediate future. And that's enough for me."

How long has it been since you've last tried to think for yourself, without the input of some magicked "thing" nebulously telling you what to do? Long. But not too long, as your path to healing from that programming has been set on its way, and you to find your own.

Upon reaching the 20th level, you may choose to break your Oath and sever your connection to the Will, but maintain everything that you have learnt while following this path and finally making it your own. You gain the following:

items: You lose your Channel Divinity features.

You may enter your /UNLOCKED/ state as a Bonus Action for one minute or until you are knocked Unconscious. You may do so up to three times per long rest. When you do so, the appearance of the manifestation around your body is that of your body, usually taking some form that represents you as your own person.

Instead of randomly deciding the creature who becomes the The Prescript's Target at the start of your turns, you instead decide to have any one creature you can see that is within 60-ft. of you to become the Target instead. Only you and friendly creatures benefit from the effects benefits.
While in your/UNLOCKED/ state you gain an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and may use your Charisma modifier in place of Dexterity for saving throws and against being Grappled.
Your Karmic Consequence count is reduced by an additional count whenever you finish a long rest.
You gain proficiency in the Insight skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient.

Whenever you draw a Prescript as per your Aura of Onus feature, you gain its benefits whenever you ensure that you and any other creature within 120-ft. of you fails to conclude that Prescript, and suffer its negative effects whenever a Prescript is concluded.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: Breaking a Paladin's Oath is never an easy feature, much less while using this subclass. However, the Will may not be an entirely (if even that) good presence in your campaign and your character's development might be to break away from it and have to start making their own choices through life.

Although it cannot be reflected in the subclass earlier as it is because of Paladin limitations, becoming an Oathbreaker in this subclass does not mean a full mechanical switch to another sub but instead gaining the Truthful Procuration feat. You and your DM may discuss implementing parts of Truthful Procuration's benefits at key moments of your character's development for a more gradual shift toward breaking apart from the Living Will.
Nevertheless, it's always a good idea to think of your character's now and their inevitable future at the creation of said character, so discuss with your DM to determine their best self!

subclassFeature.name: To Grasp Erudition With One's Own Hands (Fist)

entries: "Hold your gaze closer. We are not like the Keys; we are those who claim our knowledge through contact with our fists."

You are of a sect which prefers to shield the hand the least amount possible toward anything it can touch, becoming an expert in the written word as well as the ways of a pugilist. You gain the following benefits when you choose this feature:

items: You may be bearing no armor or weapon, yet you quickly prove that others shouldn't judge you by your surprisingly tough cover. Your Unarmored Defense Armor Class increases by half your proficiency bonus.

It isn't just the prowess gained from burning knowledge that drives you on, its also the raw emotion of having to sacrifice such important things in the first place. You deal one {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you hit a creature with an unarmed attack as part of your Attack Action. This increases by one upon reaching 8th level in this class.

You aren't just a brawler boasting intelligence, you are also a keeper and protector of the relics of the mind. You may spend your Bonus Action while having at least 2 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} count to grant yourself an amount of {@dice d6} Temporary Hit Points equal to your proficiency bonus by spending 2 Ki.

Defensive manoeuvres while being on the offense are still important, you have memorized that most efficiently. Whenever you perform a Flurry of Blows while having at least than 3 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} count you gain {@dice 1d6} Temporary Hit Points that last for up to one minute outside of combat. This increases to {@dice 2d6} upon reaching 8th level in Monk and to {@dice 3d6} upon reaching 12th level in this class. This value sums with other Temporary Hit Points you may already have.

entries: Additionally, while you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesCE} you may use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength modifier for skill checks pertaining to the latter attribute, including the Condition's bonus.

subclassFeature.name: To Heal the World’s Wounds

entries: Though the wailing hasn’t ceased,the weeping seems to have softened, just a little.

Your grasp of life and death has been synchronized with the Coffin you carry on your back, granting you further control of the ways of the beyond. Your maximum Lifeblood count becomes 15. While performing your Woundhealing Ritual you may spend your Action to spend 3 or more ( To a maximum of 15 ) Lifeblood to create a bloody ethereal arm that seeps out of the coffin, rippling with the screams and chittering of the damned.

This Death-Eating Hand is a magical melee weapon you are proficient with, having a reach of 30-ft. You use your Wisdom modifier for this weapon and it deals a number of d8 slashing damage and inflicting a number of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to the sum of each 3 Lifeblood spent this way. The Death-Eating Hand counts as a silvered weapon and makes it so Undead creatures it hits suffer its damage as if they were Vulnerable to it.

The Death-Eating Hand can be targetted for attacks, having an AC of 13 + ( 1 for each 3 Lifeblood ) and an amount of hit points equal to a number of d8+2 for each 3 Lifeblood spent to create it. It is Immune to all Conditions, psychic and acid damage and is Vulnerable to radiant damage. It cannot be healed by any means except your Ravenous Cycle of Bloodletting feature, also being healed by one hit point when you inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} with it.

Furthermore, when you hit a creature with below half their maximum hit points you may spend your Reaction to attempt to Grapple them, using your Spell Attack Modifier for this Grapple check. On a Success, the creature suffers one point of {@condition Exhaustion} for each time it starts its turn {@condition Grappled}, being able to attempt to break free by spending it’s Action to do so, rolling their {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} check against your Druid Spell Save DC. If this creature is suffering from four or more points of {@condition Exhaustion}, you may spend your Action to open the Wailing Coffin and suck the creature in, forcing them to pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or be instantly killed, with all but their magical belongings being eaten by that which lurks inside. When you do this, you gain a +1 to all rolls until the end of combat.

subclassFeature.name: To Sever Their Advent

entries: "With each smite I shall fracture thy life... - ... and in the end, shatter it!"

Your hammer has become imbued with the Obisidan God's grace, shimmering in golden light and pulsing with the power to put a stop to all false gods - A blessing granted only to the likes you, who have carried on HIS will with your bare, impudent hands thus far. Once per long rest you may use your Action to do the following, provided your Sanctum of Conservation Channel Divinity is active:

entries.name: Make Immaculate the Inner Sanctum
entries: You raise a great hammer of divine light which manifests in the palm of your hand, overtaking any weapon that may already exist, and then bring it down upon a rain of spectral nails which pierce all impudent of your Sanctum. All creatures of your choice within the Sanctum's area must pass a Wisdom saving throw or have their souls nailed down, suffering {@dice 2d8} piercing damage plus an additional {@dice d10} radiant damage per {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count they are currently suffering from, or half on a success. If they have counts of the condition, their movement speed is reduced by 10-ft. per count ( To a minimum of 0-ft. ), with them recovering 5-ft. of movement at the start of their subsequent turns. Creatures suffering from {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} suffer a -1 modifier to this saving throw per each 2 count of the Condition they are currently suffering from, and regardless of if they succeed or fail in this roll all count is removed after this effect passes. You and friendly creatures within the Sanctum's area gain a +1 modifier to your Armor Class for each non-summoned creature killed by this Action, lasting until the end of the Sanctum. If a creature who failed this Action's saving throws still lives, they suffer a negative modifier to their AC equal to half the {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count they had before you used this Action, with them restoring 1 AC at the start of their subsequent turns. If they had more than 10 {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count, they also have all damage Immunities be considered only Resistances and Resistances being rendered null until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Toll of Guardianship

entries: "I heard terrible things happen to any creature that enters the forest."

The Beast has long whispered in your ears to remember that all sacrifices are made in search of the greater good, and even if a little blood is spilled it will never compare to the death of all you hold dear.As a reaction to whenever a creature you can see or hear within 60-ft. of you would suffer damage, you may move towards the nearest empty space within 5-ft. of them and perform a weapon attack or spell attack against the source of that damage. On a hit, you don't deal damage to the source, instead parrying their attack with the side-effect of your own overwhelming force hurting the one you were trying to protect, having them instantly suffer {@damage 2d8} damage of your attacks damage type.This damage increases to {@damage 3d8} when you reach 14th level in Warlock.

subclassFeature.name: Tome of Grudges
entries: You carry a grand leather-bound Tome of Grudges granted by your family. It is a magic item and acts as an arcane focus for your warlock spells. You can summon or dismiss it as a free action. During a long rest, the Tome can break down and absorb another arcane focus as magical ink, destroying that item and gaining its properties. You can benefit only from the last arcane focus destroyed this way.
When a creature takes certain actions against you or your fellows, you become Offended and gain Offense Points, which can be spent in the following ways:

items: You can spend Offense Points to cast a warlock spell you know without expending a spell slot. You cannot upcast the spell, and its level cannot exceed your proficiency bonus. The cost equals the spell's level + 2 Offense Points. You can cast a spell this way a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

As an action, you can spend 5 Offense Points to Write 'Em All Down. Choose a number of creatures within 60 feet equal to your Charisma modifier and curse them with a {@b Vendetta Mark}. Whenever you hit a marked creature while it is within 60 feet, it takes an additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage. The number of additional d4s increases by one whenever the creature Offends you, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. The mark ends when you or the marked creature becomes {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}, or after four turns. A creature cannot gain another Vendetta Mark while it already has one.

When a creature within 30 feet hits you with an attack, you can spend 2 Offense Points to use the Payback With Interest reaction. Make a melee spell attack against the attacker. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d10} force damage plus a number of d6s of psychic damage equal to the number of damage dice rolled by the original attack.

entries: You gain Offense Points when you perceive one of the following acts within 60 feet through sight or hearing:

items: {@b Aggression Offense.} You gain 2 Offense Points the first time during a turn that a hostile creature damages you.
{@b Beatdown Offense.} You gain 2 Offense Points the first time during a combat that a friendly creature falls {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}.
{@b Grievous Offense.} You gain 5 Offense Points when you or an ally suffers a critical hit.
{@b Disrespect Offense.} You gain 2 Offense Points whenever you or an ally is forcibly moved, such as by being shoved or by the {@spell thunderwave|PHB|Thunderwave} spell.

entries: You can have a maximum number of Offense Points equal to twice your proficiency bonus. They are reduced to 0 when combat ends.

subclassFeature.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with {@item tinker's tools|PHB}. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of {@item artisan's tools|PHB} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Tools of a Detective
entries: Like any grand detective or keen-eyed activist from before, you've learnt how to perform a well conducted deduction as needed. You gain Proficiency in {@skill Investigation}, or Expertisein it if you were already proficient. Furthermore, you also share the thought that to know how others work, you've got to learn a thing or two from their trade; Choose one: (A) You gain proficiency in Thieves' Tools or (B) You learn how to speak Thieves' Cant.

subclassFeature.name: Traceless to Sight and Sound Alike
entries: At the start of your first turn in combat, or when you hit a creature using your Swiftfeet Protection reaction, you can make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check contested by each hostile creature's passive Perception. When you take the Attack action while hidden, you are not revealed and do not trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}'s extra damage until the last attack that hits during your turn. Each earlier attack that would have triggered {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead inflicts 1 additional stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Trained Under Moonlight
entries: You gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies and choose one of the following options:

items: {@b Amidst Shadows.} You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill.

{@b Under Moonlight.} You gain a cumulative +1 bonus to {@skill Perception} checks for each friendly creature within 10 feet of you, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. You gain the same bonus to your passive Perception, but its maximum equals twice your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: True Battle-Craze
entries: Upon going near your breaking point, you only feel more at ease for breaking other's. While at or below half your Hit Points, you gain the following effects:

items: You deal an additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on every attack.
You gain an additional {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesPR} when you would gain it.
You deal two additional weapon damage die on attacks.
You are considered Proficient on Wisdom, Intelligence and Charisma Saving Throws against spell effects.

subclassFeature.name: Twilight Bringer

entries: "Those who endure until the last moment shall reach an apocalypse for themselves..."

The Beast has become pleased with your devotion, pleased enough to grant you its direct help. Once per long rest when you take an action to summon from your Relicary of Lost Guardians you may instead summon three Eggs of the Black Forest each appearing at the closest unocupied space at the end of three 60-ft. lines spaced as a triangle centered from you.These eggs grant you their relics for the next minute until they are broken by another creature.They are as follows:

items: {@b Punishing Egg.} This chair-sized egg is small and has 40 hit points, with an AC of 8.Whenever it is hit, the egg has a fleshy maw appear from its cracks and perform a melee weapon attack using your spell attack modifier against the creature who hit it, dealing {@damage 2d12+4} piercing damage on a hit.

{@b Just Egg.} This barrel-sized egg is medium and has 80 hit points, with an AC of 12.Whenever it is hit, the egg rings out a hollow noise that surrounds a 30-ft. radius around it, forcing all creatures withinn reach or suffer 120 force damage divided between each creature who failed this saving throw.

{@b Watchful Egg.} This bear-sized egg is large and has 120 hit points, with an AC of 4.Whenever it is hit, the creature who hit it must pass a Charisma saving throw against your Spell Save DC or become Enchanted until the end of their next turn, being forced to spend all their movement speed moving away from the egg.

entries: If you break the eggs yourself, their relics do not vanish early. If you break all three eggs you may then spend your action to call upon a portal to the Black Forest as an action, making its doorframe appear within an unnocupied space of your DM's choice within 120-ft. of you.When you are within 5-ft. of this doorframe you may spend your action to open the door and let the beast appear for but a moment.

When you briefly open the doorframe, the sheer force emanating from the Beast covers a 160-ft. radius centered around the doorframe, causing every single creature within this reach to try a {@dc 20} ( Or your Spell Save DC, if it is higher ) Wisdom Saving Throw or have their minds raked by nightmares and visions of the Beast's inception, having them become {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} for the next minute, also suffering {@damage 18d8} psychic damage, or half on a success. Children and other pure-hearted beings are immune to these effects, instead becoming {@condition Blinded} until the end of your turn as bandages cover their eyes, a manifestation from the flicker of the Beast's original goal still being present.You can only do this once per long rest.

Otherwise, you may spend your action to fully open the door, causing the Beast of the Black Forest to appear, wishing to cleanse the world of sin. It works to destroy the nearest living creature or settlement that isn't you for as long as you don't attack it. If you defeat the Beast, you permanently gain its three Relics and are attuned to all of them, also recovering the sacrifice you have done as part of your Sacrifice to the Beast feature.The Beast uses the {@creature tarrasque|MM|Tarrasque} stat block.

subclassFeature.name: Under the Thumb of Greater People

entries: "I listen carefully to every order I'm given. I... just look to the ground to not risk staring at my superiors straight in their eyes."

There's a great organization you have joined, and you've been elected an acceptable enough cadet to be imparted with particular training toward attaining a certain role within the faction. Choose between the Ammunition Tributary and Warden of Respect features to gain one of them:

subclassFeature.name: Undying Persistence

entries: "Entrusting the exertion of physical force to a researcher, I must say, is a rather ill-considered arrangement."

Nights awake under blue lights are hardly an issue for you, and days spent weathering challenges are nothing but the regular state of your being - You, of course, have developed a process to turn your emotional and physical exertion into electricity for further usage in your endeavours. You gain {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus whenever you first attempt any Skill Check, before you roll. On a failure, you may call upon your own undying persistence to prove your superiority over matters - to do so, you instantly spend 4 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to re-roll this dice, taking the new result and possibly turning a failure into a success. This must be done after the dice's value is revealed, but before the DM announces its consequences.

You may have an amount of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} while out of combat equal to triple your proficiency bonus, with this value being halved on a short rest and reduced to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Unerring Undertaker, Unavoidable

entries: "A new Prescript has arrived: 'Behead seven dwellers of the Backstreets who resist when a blade touches their throat.' The tally aligns-seven of you stand before me. I shall commence."
While in your Blade Unlocked state, you gain additional effects, as per the following:

items: Once per short or long rest, when first entering theBlade Unlocked state you regain all your Warlock spell slots, except these may only be used to cast your Living Will Pact Spells and to fuel the following abilities:

items.name: Castigation
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to empower your weapon to its limits, punishing those who defy the Will's action through you. You instantly perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, dealing 4d12 piercing damage on a hit and dealing additional piercing damage equal to the sum of Sinking count on the target with your current Poise count times two. The target's AC is reduced by 5 for this attack.

items.name: Decapitation
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to momentarily sever another's soul from their body, shattering it with a force that governs the world around you. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, dealing 5d8 slashing damage on a hit and causing the target to suffer a further 4d6 force damage at the start of their next turn alongside having them deal only half of any damage they would deal in any attack, spell or otherwise until the end of their next turn.

items.name: Eradication
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to channel the Will directly, creating a number of mechanical arms that swing down from the heavens to crush any creature of a choice within 120-ft. of you. Any target within reach must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC, suffering 6d10 bludgeoning damage and being knocked Prone on a failure or only suffering half that damage on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Unforgiving, Unforgetting
entries: You perfectly recall information about any creature you have perceived bad-mouthing, obstructing, or otherwise slighting you or a friendly creature. While confronting such a creature, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks against it and can use Charisma instead of Wisdom for those checks. Furthermore, when you make a {@skill Perception}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@skill Survival} check to track a transgressor, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.

subclassFeature.name: Ungeziefer

entries: Those maggots squirmed harder than I expected.

Your body has become a nesting ground for the vermin that tear through the flesh of your opponents, and they can feel this with the slightest touch. You gain resistance to Necrotic damage, and, once per turn, as a reaction when you’re hit by a melee attack, the attacker must perform a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they suffer 2 counts of {@condition Maggots|TheUndertomesASV} and take {@dice 2d6} piercing damage.
If they succeed, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.
If the creature attacking you has eaten one of your fruits, you may use this ability twice per turn instead and as a reaction to any of their attack rolls targeting you.

subclassFeature.name: Ungezieferfaust

entries: Together… we are in rot.

{@condition Maggots|TheUndertomesASV} burst from the rotten fruits in your body, covering your arms and creating a gigantic fist of death and decay for you to strike your enemies with. As an action, you can extend your arm of maggots and strike a point in the ground you can see within 30 feet of you. Every creature of your choice within 30 feet of that point must roll a dexterity saving throw against your spell save dc. On a failure, they take {@dice 8d4} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Restrained}. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. A creature {@condition restrained} this way may reroll this saving throw at the end of their turns to try and break free, but if they’re unable to, they take {@dice 4d4} piercing damage and suffer 1 count of {@condition Maggots|TheUndertomesASV}.
Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Unrelenting Willpower
entries: By the time you reach 6th level you've learnt that despite any shortcomings of the moment that a lack of hesitation may bring, to truly hone your style you must face troubles head on. As such, when you would attempt an attack roll or a skill check, before rolling, you may declare that you are performing this action Without Relent. When doing so, you gain a bonus modifier equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die. If the roll is still failure, however, you suffer the side-effects of such relentlessness, hurting yourself in the process, you take an amount of d4 in damage equal to half the difference between the DC of the skill check or AC of the creature you tried to hit compared to your roll without the Martial Arts die bonus. This damage cannot be reduced in any way and is considered either slashing or psychic damage, whichever is most appropriate being determined by the DM.

entries.name: Designer's Note.
entries: When using this subclass, Flurry of Blows may be flavoured as weaker, quicker sword strikes, be it slashing at the blade or even with the hilt. The feature was not changed to directly involve attacking with a blade since the damage boost would simply become too much, too quick.

subclassFeature.name: Unrestrained Ripples of the Future to Come

entries: "Let me show you the singular teaching that has shaped my life."

The road to reach inner peace was or even still is hard and tenuous, however your efforts have come to bear fruit - your techniques flourishing into a knowledge of the world that only few can truly claim to have. As such, you may, once per long rest, coat your weapon in a manifestation of your very soul. You do so by spending your Bonus Action while you have at least 3 {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count. While encased this way, your weapon attack hits deal an additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and the effect lasts for up to a minute.

While benefitting from this, you may replace your True Decapitation Deathblow technique with a use of your Branches of Knowledge. When you do so, you perform a melee attack weapon against one target creature within reach, inflicting 12 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and an amount of {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count equal to your current count. All other hostile creatures within a 30-ft. radius of you must also pass a Wisdom saving throw or suffer the same amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count, or half on a success. You may choose to trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the main target instantly after performing this attack. Other effects of Deathblow apply to this attack.
Additionally, after attempting to hit a creature with your Branch of Knowledge, flip a coin:

items: {@b On a result of Heads,} you delve into the world of fears and insecurities, of secrets and all things that make you stronger toward peril. You suffer Vulnerability against psychic damage and deal an additional point of damage per {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count until the end of combat.

{@b On a result of Tails,} you delve into the world of order and strong morals, of comfort and authority that strengthen your resolve toward danger. You gain Immunity to psychic damage and reduce any damage you take by a value equal to your {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} count until the end of combat. Furthermore, after flipping this coin your maximum {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesAC} increases to 10 until your next long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Unseen Infatuation

entries: Composed entirely of pink slime, Melting Love is sliding around its Containment Unit.

You are an exceptionally charming person, with your mere presence tending to captivate those not used to the finer, most exotic or simply enticing figures of life. Whenever you grant a Bardic Inspiration die to another creature you may also use the simple scene of your inspiring of another to attempt to Charm a creature within the same range that can see or hear you. That creature must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, becoming {@condition Charmed} by you for the next minute on a failed saving throw.

A creature {@condition Charmed} by you suffers one count of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} each time it suffers damage while {@condition Charmed}, as they see you not move a muscle toward protecting them in spite of their devotion toward you. While the creature is still {@condition Charmed}, you may spend your action to utter words to break that creatures heart, having them instantly suffer {@dice 1d10} psychic damage, triggering {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on them and ending the Condition early. After this the formerly {@condition Charmed} creature has advantage against being {@condition Charmed} by you again for the next 24 hours. You may also spend a reaction when a friendly creature within reach deals damage to the {@condition Charmed} creature to do this.

The amount of Tremor inflicted whenever a {@condition Charmed} creature suffers damage increases to two counts when you reach 12th level in this class. The damage of this effect also increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach 6th level ({@dice 2d10}) and by a further {@dice 1d10} when you reach 12th level ({@dice 3d10}).
A {@condition Charmed} creature may re-attempt this saving throw at the end of its subsequent turns.

subclassFeature.name: Until the Last Drop
entries: When your Igniter Fuel is below half its maximum, it becomes Overheated Fuel. Spending Overheated Fuel on a Workshop Bathed in Fuel feature adds the corresponding effect below:

entries.name: Blazing Gasoline
entries: For every 4 Overheated Fuel spent, Pre-Heated Gasoline's Burn lasts 1 additional turn without being halved at the end of that turn.

entries.name: Complete Devastation
entries: When Fuel Detonation hits, each other creature within 10 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the same fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The original target then loses all Burn counts.

entries.name: Live Fire Zone
entries: A creature other than you that starts or ends its turn in Burning Grounds takes {@damage 1d8} fire damage and suffers 1 Burn count per 4 Overheated Fuel spent. The number of d8s is reduced by one at the start of each of your turns until the fire is extinguished.
If spending fuel takes you below half your maximum, only the fuel spent after crossing that threshold counts as Overheated Fuel.

subclassFeature.name: Unveil Information (Key)

entries: "Good thinking. Let my key be the guide to your enlightenment."

The way your Key processes light is unlike anything else you have seen, yet you have seen much through it and have learnt how to unveil the most through its vision. While wielding your Key you are considered to have Expertise in the {@skill Perception} skill and as a Free Action you may take once per turn or continuously out of combat you may use your Key as a looking glass, granting you Truesight toward a 30-ft. long cone in front of you. If you perceive any {@condition Invisible} or otherwise normally unseen creatures through this, you remember their location and they count as if they were not {@condition Invisible} to you until they move from that cone's reach.

subclassFeature.name: Vengeance Martial Archetype

entries: "Heh. Why work with your brains when you've got the brawn?"

The Vengeance Martial Archetype is selfish and unstoppable. You want personal vengeance against the world, and other people around you are just pawns for you to sacrifice in order to achieve that vengeance and the heights of greatness.

You belong to the Middle, a faction that treats all of their members like family, and mistreating one of theirs earns the ire of the entire group. Within, family forgives tiny missteps, but outsiders do not receive such mercy. However, you also believe thay a little sacrifice is nothing for the family, and will use your brothers and sisters to aid in your ascension, even if that costs them their lives.

Vengeance Fighters are very strong, but also uncaring. They trick you into believing you're a part of their inner circle, then use you for their own gains. You may play as a character that eventually comes to realize the wrong in their ways, but remember to always keep a desire for vengeance deep within your heart.

subclassFeature.name: Vestiaire du Rouge

entries: "Je me retire volontiers en moi-même."

Rebirth is done by going through a dark, messy and suffocating patch, by accepting and reinventing the death of your internal voice and even still rejecting giving up on what you are and what you are meant to become. While you are Enraged you may use your Action to spend 10 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count while below half your maximum Hit Points to enter your Changing Room, a cocoon of flesh and muscle formed around your person to clutch at something greater.

While within your Changing Room, you Resist all damage except for force and whenever you take damage, you gain one {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count. You cannot take Actions or Bonus Actions, but instead may use Reactions up to three times per turn, gaining the following uses as well:

items: You may spend your Reaction whenever a creature moves within 30-ft. of you to attack them with the natural weapons granted by your Griffe à Coudre ability. You do not need to spend {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} to do so, and this reach increases alongside the ability.

Once per turn you may spend your Reaction whenever a creature within 30-ft. attacks you to explode into a myriad hands that fling out and claw at all creatures of your choice within 15-ft. of you, forcing them to pass the Dexterity saving throw imposed by your Goûter à la Mode ability or suffer its consequences, as per your level. You do not need to spend {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} to do so.

You may spend your Reaction whenever you suffer damage to fold in on yourself for protection, disabling you from using any other Reactions until you leave the Changing Room, but granting you a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your proficiency bonus.

entries: You stay in your Changing Room until the start of your next turn, and after leaving it you gain {@condition Full Makeover|TheUndertomesCR} until one hour passes outside of combat, with this duration resetting upon another combat beginning. If you enter a short rest while in {@condition Full Makeover|TheUndertomesCR}, the Condition instantly ends and you instantly regain half your proficiency bonus' worth of spent Hit Die. You may instantly enter Rage without spending its use after leaving your Changing Room.
You can enter your Changing Room only once per long rest

subclassFeature.name: Violet~ Breaking Slam

entries: "Phew... Well, that takes care of the last of the 'Up-and-Coming Fixer Offices' featured in Fixers Monthly."
The power of the family's love and old, famous catchphrases from brave adventurers fill your heart with wonder and a burning desire to never stop fighting.

As a Reaction when a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} hits you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you, you may immediately perform a melee attack against them if you are within range, moving up to your remaining speed towards them if necessary. If the attack hits, choose one of the abilities below to trigger:

items: {@b I Do Not Forgive You. VIOLET SWORD!} This attack deals an additional amount of damage equal to half your Sneak Attack dice.

{@b The Show's Over. ALL-OUT ATTACK!} Immediately after you attack, you may choose a friendly creature within 30 feet of you to spend their Reaction and perform an attack against the same creature if within range.
{@b Siblings of the Family, I WILL LEND YOU MY ENERGY!} Choose a creature within 30 feet of you to recover 1 use of their Middle Tattoo feature.
{@b My Life Has No Regrets. FIRE BLADE!} Double all counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.
{@b Don't "What?" Me. YOU'RE ALREADY DEAD!} Double all counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries: You can use this ability twice, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Virescent Flame Soup

entries: "Thou should have imagined that there would be a hidden dragon lurking somewhere amongst the shadows, hm?"

Once per long rest, you can prepare a hot bowl of noodle soup. As a bonus action, you can drink it or have a willing creature within 5 feet drink it. The creature gains 4 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Until the end of its next turn, whenever it scores a Posture Critical Hit, it gains one additional bonus action, which must be used before the end of its next turn.

Alternatively, as a bonus action, you can spill the steaming soup on a creature within 5 feet. It must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, it suffers 6 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, 2 stacks of {@condition Nerve Strike|TheUndertomesBJ}, and damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die. On a successful save, it suffers half as many stacks of each condition and takes no damage.
