Once used in either way, the soup is expended and cannot be used again until you prepare another after finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Virescent Pyrojade
entries: You carry two round jade bracelets made from a magical material called pyrojade. If you lose them, you can procure a new set in any city or monastery that follows your way by spending a long rest doing so. While wearing these bracelets, the first attack you hit with on each of your turns inflicts 1 stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At 11th level, it inflicts 2 stacks instead. Additionally, you gain the following abilities:

items: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point to heat a weapon. Until the start of your next turn, it deals fire damage instead of its normal damage type and inflicts 1 stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever a creature hits with it.

As an action, you can spend 3 ki points to make a grapple check against a creature within your reach. On a success, you melt one nonmagical weapon, piece of equipment, or tool of your choice that the creature is holding or wearing, destroying it.
As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point to ignite a flammable object you can touch that is not being worn or carried.

As a bonus action, you can spend 2 ki points to make an attack roll against a creature within your reach. On a hit, roll a number of Martial Arts dice equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. The creature takes fire damage equal to the total and suffers a number of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to the number of dice rolled.

As an action, you can spend 3 ki points to melt a section of a nonmagical wall you are touching, creating a 5-foot-diameter hole. The wall must be made from a meltable material such as stone, wood, or metal.

subclassFeature.name: Volatile Manifestation
entries: There is a fire nestled deep within your soul, one that is let out when your emotions are flowing freely. As a bonus action, you can enter a Volatile State. It usually manifests as a blade and shield that reflect your personality and identity, but it can instead take the form of mystical appendages appearing from or around your body, such as wings. The state lasts for 1 minute. When you enter it, choose an Offensive Stance or Defensive Stance.

entries.name: Offensive Stance
entries: You produce a flame-wreathed weapon of your choice. Whenever you deal damage with a spell attack, add fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

items: {@b Sunset Blade.} When you cast {@spell Fleeting Emberblade|TheUndertomesWW}, you can expend a spell slot to empower it, applying 2 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts per level of the slot. If the slot is 2nd level or higher, the spell's reach increases by 5 feet for every 2 levels of the slot (10 feet with a 2nd-level slot, 15 feet with a 4th-level slot, and 20 feet with a 6th-level slot). At 6th level, if the cantrip has already hit during this turn, you can make one additional spell attack as part of the casting; that attack applies half the additional Burn counts. You can make one more additional attack this way at 14th level.

{@b Make the Future.} As an action, you can expend a spell slot and move up to 15 feet in a line toward the nearest unoccupied space. Each creature in your path must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 2d8} fire damage and suffering 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts per level of the slot on a failure.

{@b Rising Stigma.} As an action, you can expend a spell slot of up to 3rd level to gain a +2 bonus to AC for each level of the slot. This bonus lasts until the start of your next turn. For the same duration, you have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being moved or grappled. You then enter Defensive Stance.

entries.name: Defensive Stance
entries: You wrap magic around yourself like a cloak or shield. You gain a bonus to AC equal to your Charisma modifier, but your speed is halved.

items: {@b Brief Respite.} As a bonus action, you can expend a spell slot to summon translucent wings and move up to 15 feet directly backward without provoking opportunity attacks. The distance increases by 15 feet per slot level above 1st, to a maximum of 45 feet. If the slot is 3rd level or higher, a burst of flame fills the space you left. Each creature within 5 feet of that space must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts per slot level above 2nd.

{@b Face the Fear.} When you take damage, you can use your reaction and expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to reduce the damage by half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. If you expend a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you also gain resistance to all damage except force and psychic damage until the start of your next turn.

{@b Razing Wing.} As an action, each hostile creature within 5 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, a creature is pushed 15 feet away and suffers 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. You can expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to apply 2 additional Burn counts on a failed save, or half as many on a successful one. You then enter Offensive Stance.

entries: At the end of each of your turns in Volatile State, if you have not damaged a creature, affected a creature with one of your spells, hit with an attack, or taken a critical hit during that turn, the state wavers. Make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + your Charisma modifier + the number of times you have succeeded on this save during the current combat. On a failure, you take a number of d6s of psychic damage equal to the turns you have spent in Volatile State, and the state ends. The state also ends if you become unconscious or end it as a free action.

You learn the {@spell Fleeting Emberblade|TheUndertomesWW} cantrip. It does not count against your cantrips known. Once you enter Volatile State, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Volatile Passion
entries: At the end of each of your turns in Volatile State, you gain 1 Volatile Passion count. While you have Volatile Passion, you gain a bonus to attack rolls against creatures with Burn equal to half your Volatile Passion count, rounded down (minimum +1). When you hit such a creature, you also apply a number of Burn counts equal to this bonus.

If you have 3 or more Volatile Passion and apply {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} to a creature, each other hostile creature within 5 feet of it suffers half as many Burn counts, rounded down.

When your Volatile State ends without you ending it as a free action, you take {@damage 1d10} psychic damage per Volatile Passion count. If you had 3 or more counts, you can use your reaction when the state would end to extend it for 1 minute. You lose all Volatile Passion counts, still take the damage, and gain 1 level of exhaustion at the end of combat each time you extend the state this way.
While you are outside Volatile State, your Volatile Passion count is reduced by 1 at the end of each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Volatilized Rush

entries: "Thus, you sink into a bottomless slumber."

There is smoke in your lungs. You don't know when it got there, or when you failed to exhale it, but that haze has become a part of you. Whenever you would lose {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count from triggering a Posture Critical, only halve your current amount instead. Furthermore, whenever you trigger one while having a {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count of 10 or greater, you may choose to change the attack's damage type to force damage.

Additionally, you gain a new way to march on through your {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesFM|Torn Memories}. You may spend one count when you perform a ranged weapon attack during your turn. When you do so, you can see a series of blazing-red reticules in the air that guide your shot toward the targets heart, considering their AC to be lowered by your proficiency bonus for this attack. On a hit you always trigger a Posture Critical hit and this attack bypasses damage Resistances and considers Immunity to your dealt damage type as only Resistance instead.

subclassFeature.name: Wailing Coffin

entries: A wail fills the forest.

You have a large artifact you carry on your back, called a Wailing Coffin. It contains nothing and everything, being a gateway to a demi-plane of creatures who consume death itself, cleansing it from the material plane.
You must handle it with care, keeping it sealed and only peering it open when needed and under your supervision, respecting the object with the same reverence as you would the dead.

Whatever non-magical object you toss through it is devoured by clerids which crawl out of its depths, being permanently destroyed. You learn the {@spell Shrouded Hand|TheUndertomesASV} cantrip and may spend your Wildshape feature to enter a Woundhealing Ritual Chant, one where you unleash the clerids to from your coffin and act upon your full command. When you do this, the Clerids become a ravenous swarm that appears within an unnocupied space within 30-ft of you, suffering no damage and acting immediatedly after your turn, being controlled by you.
Your Clerid Swarm uses the Monster Sheet to the side while your Woundhealing Ritual Chant is active.

subclassFeature.name: Waiting for Vengeance
entries: You begin each combat with 3 Offense Points. When an enemy Offends you, you can inflict it with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}. When you target a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} with an attack, you gain a bonus to the attack roll equal to half your current Offense Points, to a maximum of +4, and deal additional psychic damage equal to your current Offense Points.

Additionally, your Grudge Points are no longer removed after combat. You can retain a maximum number equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, and they are reduced by 1 each hour. You can spend 1 Grudge Point to add +2 to a failed ability check, potentially turning it into a success as you push through to correct your grievance.

subclassFeature.name: Walking the Line of Death
entries: You've survived so many near-death experiences that you've learned to walk the edge between life and death with frightening ease. Starting at 13th level, whenever you would gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you gain an additional stack for each missing Chunk of hit points.

Additionally, at the start of your turn, if you are below half your maximum hit points, you may choose to heal yourself for a number of d6 hit points equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down). You can use this healing a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

You've also learned how to control your breath and adrenaline outside of combat. When you use the Take a Breath action, you also gain 4 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. While you have {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} outside of combat, you may get a Posture Critical with skill checks. When you trigger a Posture Critical on a skill check, you add a bonus modifier to up to half your current {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks (Rounded Down) to the result of the check. You may benefit from a bonus modifier of {@dice 3d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Wall Stitcher

entries: "We'd better hurry up, or surviving this long will have been for nothing."

You aren't the top dog and you know that, you don't have the greatest tools nor the greatest skills yet, so you've grown to rely on what you can get everywhere - making the most of what people would just let pass by without another glance. You gain proficiency in your choice of the {@skill Acrobatics} or {@skill Athletics} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient in the chosen skill.

Additionally you may cling surfaces to aid in staying still if something would move you, being able to spend your Bonus Action to wedge yourself as long as you are wielding a weapon that deals piercing damage. While wedged on walls and ceilings you do not fall at the end of your turn and once per turn you may spend a free action to attempt jumping 10-ft. upward or downward before wedging yourself in another surface within reach or jump down to the ground. You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would cause you to be moved or knocked {@condition Prone}, such as being Shoved or the {@spell thunderwave} spell. You may unlatch as a free action.

While out of combat you gain a base climbing speed equal to half your walking speed as long as you are wielding a weapon that deals piercing damage, as you can take your time to manoeuvre yourself. This increases by 5-ft. if you are wielding another piercing weapon in your other hand.

subclassFeature.name: Warden of Respect

entries: "... Anyone in The Thumb has to know how to wield bayonets. Nothing like the sharp blade and the hard stock of a rifle in situations when we can't use ammunition."

The way of the bayonet has been sliced into your memories, every movement and way to swing it - You know it. You also know how to best attach them to ranged weapons, requiring only a Dagger or similar light weapon to add onto a ranged weapon over a short or long rest.

When you attach a bayonet to a ranged weapon, you may also use it as a melee weapon you are proficient with. This weapon has gains the finesse property and retains the two-handed property if it had it, dealing a dice one step lower than the weapon's ranged damage dice (Such as a ranged weapon that deals {@damage 1d6} would deal {@damage 1d4}, an {@damage 1d8} would become an {@damage 1d6} and so on.) of a damage type of your choice between slashing or piercing damage.

You do not suffer Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls while a target is within 5-ft. of you when using a weapon with a bayonet and inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of damage die you would roll on a weapon attack hit.

Upon reaching 5th level your footwork has also improved to keep some distance between you and your target, increasing your AC by one until the start of your next turn whenever you hit a creature with melee weapon attacks. Your AC is increased by an additional point for the duration whenever you use your {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1}.

subclassFeature.name: Watch Your Back!

entries: "C'mon, don't get yourself written up in the Book for a few coins, yeah?"

Your body is a lethal weapon, and you don't need swords or lances when you have punches and kicks. Your unarmed attacks are considered Heavy Weapons and now deal {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier in damage. This number increases to {@damage 1d8} at level 5, {@damage 1d10} at level 11 and {@damage 1d12} at level 17.

When you would normally attune with a weapon, instead you etch a tattoo reminiscent of it in your body, being able to use its damage as unarmed attack damage and gaining all the benefits you would normally get from attacking with it. You can only have 1 weapon tattoo from this feature at a time. This is still considered as being attuned to the weapon.

Additionally, during combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall unconscious. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until the end of the first round of combat.

Whenever you hit an enemy with counts of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Watcher of Scorn
entries: Your ever watchful eyes are more than a weapon than whatever you may carry in your blood-soaked hands. Upon reaching 20th level, you may spend an action to become an embodiment of contempt at the world itself, gaining the following for one minute:

items: You gain immunity against being {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Blinded}.

Whenever a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw, misses an attack roll, or rolls a natural 1 on a skill check for the first time on a turn, you gain one Awesome Die (d8). You can have a maximum of 8 Awesome Dice at a time. All unused dice vanish only when you finish a long rest.
You can now spend Awesome Dice to add to an ability check you make, before you roll.

When a creature becomes {@condition Frightened} within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to attempt to Grasp them. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become {@condition Grasped|TheUndertomesRES} as per your {@i Golden Grasp} feature. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Waxen Wings Font of Magic
entries: {@i Pain has given me pain, but I will now bring pain. I have had enough. Pain.}

subclassFeature.name: Way of Crumbling Enlightenment

entries: "Remember not only to refill what you have burned out but also to add new knowledge into your repositories.""

Knowledge and the body are an organism when in combination, the brain's synapses leading to the fists clenching and bursting forward in a coordinated transfer of energy for devastating power. Monks who dwell in the sects of Enlightenment know this well, and cultivate their minds to accumulate as much intelligence as possible, then taking it apart crumb by crumb to fuel their arts.

Often cloistered with their fellows, these are also the keepers of vast reliquaries that do well in archival and retrieval of all manner of great item that was misplaced or forlorn to time, also holding out special holdings in the nourishing of young minds within their ranks, often acting as orphanages just as well.

entries.subclassFeature: Gathering of Knowledge as Kindling|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesCE|3

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Bright Star
entries: You have sworn yourself to a life of dedication. There are 108 Heroes that have earned the title of a Star, and your sole goal is to make the Dihui (地會) Star become the one true name people call you by. You utilize the power of Iaido to quickly unsheathe your sword to match your enemies' attacks with expertise and perfection.

In the Forgotten Realms, Monks of the Way of the Bright Star all train under a single roof, then travel to accomplish the tasks set forth by their master so that they can become the next Bright Star, ready to guide the next generation of Monks. In Ravenloft, the sect is much more violent, aiming to kill all other students so that the best and brightest star may stand victorious at the end of the night-it is a matter of hunt and be hunted across the mists. In the cyberpunk world of Genesis, no longer do stars shine in the sky, and Monks of this Monastery will only know they have ascended once they accomplish the impossible-a cut so vast and seamless that the light from the city will be erased, giving way to a beautiful, and naturally illuminated night sky.

Monks of the Way of the Bright Star are diligent students and unerring followers of their master. Consider making a serious character that focuses on nothing else but their goal to reach perfection. If you don't want to play a serious character, what they cannot differ from is their love for the blade and the way, and their desire to see it through, completed.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Burning Jade
entries: Monks of the Way of the Burning Jade train with a special tool called a Pyrojade, a round bracelet made from magical jade that ignites on command. Monks of this path train specifically to become immune to the magical fire this tool creates.

They are capable fighters in any situation, but especially in a pinch. Their fighting style revolves around never standing still, confusing their opponents through constant movement, and then striking with a fiery fist.

Monks of this path tend to be relaxed and friendly, even while fighting. They enjoy taking care of other people, especially if that means cooking for them. However, they also possess a burning, valiant soul that will not smolder until they see their dreams accomplished.
"Thy bladed instrument poseth little threat to me, amigo. Mine virescent pyrojade shall melt it to nothingness ere it doth me harm!"

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Homeward Blade
entries: Wield Blade and the will of your Homeland with one hand, determined to cut through any in your way.
Monks of the Way of the homeland usually follow a traditional style of swordplay where violence is as natural as breathing, being an encouraged force of power.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, they can be found through a mercenary band prowling the seas, the Azure Cloths, lending their blades to whatever combat is worthier, in others, such as Eberron, this fighting style was born on the battlefield by berserkers who had finally internalized their aggression, learning to let it go in violent outbursts aimed at others.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Sword
entries: At 3rd level, you've honed your swordplay enough that you feel confident in representing your homeland, creed or wherever you've gained your style in combat without the risk of disgracing it. As such, you gain proficiency with Longswords, also treating them as if they had the Finesse property, as you may choose to wield them with grace instead of sheer force.
You also may use your Flurry of Blows while wielding a slashing weapon, and you may choose to deal slashing damage instead of bludgeoning.
Additionally, you gain access to Swordplay Techniques, special abilities that you may employ at the cost of Ki Points as shown in the following:

items: Draw of the Sword. By spending your bonus action and one Ki point, you enter a stance with your sword sheathed. When you do so, when you take the Attack action, you forgo any additional attacks you might have, instead adding one roll of your Martial Arts die for each attack you have foregone on your next damage roll. Upon reaching 6th level, slashing damage caused while using this Technique surpasses resistance to slashing damage, instead being dealt normally, and if the target would be immune to slashing damage, it is considered resistant to it instead.

Remembrance of Blades. By spending a bonus action and one Ki point, you take a moment to briefly steel yourself, sinking your thoughts into the teachings of your homeland and poising yourself up. You gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to your proficiency bonus.

Acupuncture. When you would perform a Flurry of Blows, you may spend an additional Ki point to use the movement of your blade to better ready yourself for more magnanimous slashing. Whenever you land a hit during this Flurry of Blows, the effects of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} do not trigger, in addition, you gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each time you hit.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Vast Garden

entries: "Hm. Good eye. I'm a rare talent around here, you know?"

Study. Discipline. Evolution. The vast garden is a giant monastery that births new talents and prodigies every year. They fight amongst each other to decide who will stand at the top of the garden. You're one of those studious Monks trying to make a name for yourself, learn the deep teachings of the Vast Garden Monastery and either continue to embody them or change them for future generations.

In the Forgotten Realms, this monastery might focus on creating leaders for nations and estates, pitting them against each other so only the strongest survive. In Eberron, they study so that they can strengthen their psionic capabilities and earn control of cities as powerful and wise mayors. In the dark fantasy world of Alacritas, many monasteries train their students to overcome their masters with a lethal blow. Drenched in the blood of an unforgivable sin, they carry the souls of the departed with them on a wrathful journey of conquest, endlessly perfecting their style before starting the cycle anew.

If you want to play as a Monk of the Vast Garden, remember that you are a studious individual trying to become the best of your monastery. Vast Garden monks are usually diligent, listen to their superiors and are constantly trying to train and challenge themselves.

If you're using one as an NPC, they could be guiding the party through a city they have never visited before, or help them learn skills they have been wanting to study. If you want one as a BBEG, they could feel threatened by one of the party members and try to prove themselves by defeating them, or they might be trying to conquer a city or village that the players hold dear.

subclassFeature.name: Weapon Limit-Break
entries: You've become powerful enough to break away some of the limiters from your Issued Weaponry, unlocking devastating potential within. Starting at 10th level, you gain the ability corresponding to your chosen weapon.

entries.name: Daggers - Null Space Render.
entries: As a bonus action during your turn, you may spend 8 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to coat your blades in pure spatial disruption. Your next hit makes its target be infused with that disruption. Until the end of their next turn, the creature hit by your {@b N.S.R.} does not receive {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage, but gains an additional stack every time its attacked. Immediately after their turn ends, the {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} explodes as the disruption falls unto itself, dealing an amount of d4s in force damage equal to the Stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they have, then removing all of it.

entries.name: Axe - Crushing Current.
entries: By spending 8 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and your bonus action, you prime your axe's blade to reverberate almost like a chainsaw. Until the end of your turn, your attacks deal an additional weapon damage die and are particularly destructive, reducing the target creature's maximum Hit Points by the damage dealt. In addition, each attack reduces their AC by 1 for a minute.

entries.name: Spear - Overloaded Barrier Generator.
entries: During your turn, you may spend 8 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and an action to stomp your Spear into the ground, sending a shockwave of plasma that results in one of the following effects of your choice:
The Plasma solidifies into a tangible shield, as per the {@spell Wall of Force} spell, with it being cast targeting yourself and covering a radius of up to 15-feet instead of 10-ft.
Otherwise, you may target up to 6 creatures within a 30-foot radius of yourself, these creatures gain 40 temporary hit points until their next short or long rest.

entries.name: Longsword - Full Area Denial.
entries: Through spending 8 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and your action, you enclose a 15-feet sphere centered at any point within 60-feet of you by rapidly leaping from rift to rift around, ripping both space and coming in to slash at creatures within the area to shut them down. Every creature of your choice within the sphere must pass a Dexterity Saving throw or take {@dice 2d6} force damage and suffer 6 {@condition Charge-Bind|TheUndertomesCL}, also having their movement speed reduced to 0ft until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Gauntlets - Dosage of Wrecking.
entries: As an action, you clash your fists together, electricity overflowing and arcing between your fingers, by spending 8 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} you may deliver a particularly powerful punch to another creature. This attack deals an additional {@dice 4d4} lightning damage and is considered a Critical Hit on a roll of 15 or higher, before modifiers. A creature hit by this attack is flung back in a line of 30-feet, being hurled through space itself as the impact propels their body, or if this attack was a Critical Hit, they are propelled by 90-feet instead. If they would hit a wall, they would take an amount of additional d8 force damage equal to each 10 feet travelled, as space crashes in around their body from the gigatonic impact.

subclassFeature.name: What Remains

entries: My master had a very unfortunate life.

The aura coming from the Old Master’s paintings becomes more powerful and much harder to ignore. Creatures that fail the saving throw of your Portraits become {@condition Frightened} of them. They can repeat this saving throw at the end of their turns, ending the {@condition Frightened} condition on them on a success.

Additionally, as an action, you can see through the eyes in your Portrait’s painting and hear what creatures within 30 feet of it are saying until the start of your next turn. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses. Once per long rest, you can teleport yourself to its location. You can bring along objects as long as their weight doesn’t exceed what you can carry. You can also bring one willing creature of your size or smaller who is carrying gear up to its carrying capacity. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you use this ability.

subclassFeature.name: Where No One Can Hurt Another

entries: "Your magnificant city, Father - and you the brain of this city - and all of us in the city's light - - and where are the people, father, whose hands built your city - - - ?"

Whenever you target a hostile creature with a Sorcerer spell you may also attempt to throw them into internal disarray , disconnecting their heart from their head and forcing a panic in their system. That creature must attempt a Wisdom saving throw against your Sorcerer Spell Save DC, suffering half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} on a failure. If the spell's effect would already warrant a saving throw to be made, this Wisdom saving throw is ignored and they suffer this effect by failing the one they already would need to make.

A creature suffering from {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} that has been caused by you also suffers a negative modifier to attack rolls equal to half their {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} count, while their damage rolls suffer a negative modifier equal to double the Condition's count.

subclassFeature.name: Whispers of the Betrayed Knight

entries: "As with sorrow, perhaps sharing the burden will blunt the edge."

The injustices you have suffered do not end, and tears continue to flow from your face, bringing with them magic and a few blessings. Twice per turn, whenever you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you is hit by a hostile creature, you gain 1 count of Deep Tears. You can have a number of Deep Tears equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and you can use a bonus action to spend them according to the Deep Tears table. All counts of Deep Tears disappear when you finish a short or long rest.

entries.caption: Deep Tears
rows: Choose a creature within 30 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, its attacks apply 2 additional counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
You gain resistance to a damage type of your choice until the start of your next turn.
Choose a creature within 30 feet of you. It gains {@dice 2d6} temporary hit points until the start of your next turn.
Choose a creature within 30 feet of you. Whenever it rolls damage before the start of your next turn, it may change the result of one damage die to its maximum value.

subclassFeature.name: Will you Play?

entries: "Scissors beats rock. Teehee! That means you lose!"

Enough time has passed, and your companions no longer fear your creations, but embrace them as a part of who you are-certainly that is true. Whenever a friendly creature is within 5 feet of one of your toys, they gain the following benefits:

items: A bonus of +1 to their AC, to a maximum of +2 per toy.
If the toy is triggered or performs any sort of ability, they gain {@dice 1d10} temporary Hit Points once per turn.
The next time they hit an attack roll, they deal an additional {@damage 1d10} in Psychic damage.
Disadvantage on all saving throws that would give them the {@condition Frightened} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Wishmaker Domain
entries: The stroke of a pen, the birth of a line of paint, the death of a peccant - these are all intertwined in the wishes of people young and old, or that is the understanding of the ones who make use of paper talismans to manipulate sin through devouring and spewing alike: the Clergy of the Wishmaker Domain.

Devoted and spirited at their best, a cleric whom follows such a wishful way scours the land searching for evil to bear upon their own back instead of leaving such pains to the innocent people, and seal it away atop the very wellspring of all that is sinful. Yet these can often be led to a form of depersonalization, blind to their own sins and sense of self in lieu of always taking much more than they may even handle. Even the most devoted can tend to be forgetful of their own fragility.

In worlds such as those covered by the mists of Ravenloft, these clerics are better known as sin-eaters - fairytales of saviours and destroyers at the same time, which come to places beset by the cruelest of evils and leave turning it into a silent graveyard where no blood can be further shed, or in worlds such as Balefire, where they wax talismans to their bodies in a seeming captivation to bring penance for every single sin they absorb.

entries.name: So That No One Will Cry.

entries: "Heheh! Thou art quite full of wishes... Which of them dost thou desire to see come true?!"

It is of a singular desire that your order is born, to ensure that no other soul's tears will shed the earth. To do so, you have become as a doll to have ones pains to be placed upon, and although you are little more than a shabby creature for now, you have devoted yourself to become greater in the name of others. You have a number of Twisted Curse Talismans equal to your proficiency bonus, and may spend one of them for the following:

entries.name: Enfeebling Talisman.
entries: You produce a talisman meant to sap the strength from others. When you do so, you spend your Action to throw and attach it to a creature within 30-ft. with a ranged spell attack. On a hit, they suffer one {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} count. While suffering the Condition from this means, they suffer a negative modifier to their Strength modifier equal to half their Talisman count for the duration, to a minimum of one and rounded up. {@i "One dreamed of strength to see through the world's harshest labours, only to be crushed under it's weight."}

entries.name: Entrapping Talisman.
entries: You produce a talisman meant to lock up the muscles and joints of others. When you do so, you spend your Action to throw and attach it to a creature within 30-ft. with a ranged spell attack. On a hit, they suffer one {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} count. While suffering the Condition from this means, they suffer modifier to their Dexterity modifier equal to half their Talisman count for the duration, to a minimum of one and rounded up. {@i "One so wished to run away from their past, only for their legs to give in under the mounting pressure."}

entries.name: Engulfing Talisman.
entries: You produce a talisman meant to sink one's mind into the deepest of sorrows. When you do so, you spend your Action to throw and attach it to a creature within 30-ft. with a ranged spell attack. On a hit, they suffer one {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} count. While suffering the Condition from this means, they suffer modifier to their Wisdom modifier equal to half their Talisman count for the duration, to a minimum of one and rounded up. {@i "One desired the greatest of joys, yet all sweet smiles turned into sickening betrayals."}

entries.name: Encroaching Talisman.
entries: You produce a talisman meant to overtake every ill deed and malignant thought. You spend your Action to throw and attach it to a creature within 30-ft. with a ranged attack. On a hit, they suffer {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS} count up to a value equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded up. While suffering the Conditions from this means, they suffer an additional count at the end of their subsequent turns. {@i "And one poor soul shepherded away all sins, only to take them for itself."}

You may use your Bonus Action to spend one Twisted Curse Talisman to inflict yourself with up to your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Talisman|TheUndertomesOLS}. Alternatively, you may target yourself to attach one of the Talismans above. Alternatively, you can use your Bonus Action to spend your highest level spell slot available to regain an amount of Twisted Curse Talismans equal to half the level of the spell slot spent, rounded up.

entries.name: Domain Extended Spells.

entries: "When you detached one, - a candle in the room suddenly began to burn."
You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Wishmaker Domain Spells table.

entries.caption: Wishmaker Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell Bless}, {@spell Bane}
3rd
{@spell Aid}, {@spell Branding Smite}
5th
{@spell Bestow Curse}, {@spell Life Transference|XGE}
7th
{@spell Death Ward}, {@spell Otiluke's Resilient Sphere}
9th
{@spell Dispel Evil and Good}, {@spell Hallow}

entries.name: Thousand Red Sheets.

entries: "With another detached, - the fire burns even brighter."

Red ink constantly stains your fingertips as your training for talisman making has consumed your life, somewhat. Night, day, light or dark, rain or sunshine - It doesn't matter, you will master them for the sake of everyone else. You gain proficiency in Calligrapher's Tools. These may count as your Holy Symbol.

subclassFeature.name: Withstand the Snow

entries: "Survival was reserved only for those who learned to accept the Smoke as part of their daily lives."

For those who hail from the same homeland as you living long is a rarity, yet something that you somehow have managed to do, and in doing that your mental resistance has been sharpened to something unlike what most others possess. You gain Proficiency in Wisdom saving throws, Resistance to Psychic and Poison damage and any Disease or Poison you are suffering from ends after one minute.
Additionally, whenever you use your {@classFeature Indomitable|Fighter|PHB|9} Feature, you instantly recover half the damage taken during the previous turn, rounded up.

subclassFeature.name: Words of Power
entries: When you reach 15th level, you can infuse even simple words with bursting power to command your allies in a fight, as such you may spend two Order Die for the following:

entries.name: Continue the Slaughter!
entries: As a bonus action you may have a friendly creature attack with a weapon attack or cantrip attack targeting a creature within reach, as long as they're within your aura. When you do so, they add one roll of your Order Die to the attack roll, and two of them to the damage roll.

entries.name: Do Not Fear!
entries: As a bonus action you may instantly remove the {@condition Frightened} condition of up to two creatures within your Aura's reach.
Additionally, your Order Die increase to be d8s.

subclassFeature.name: World's My Stage
entries: Starting from 3rd level, you've really developed your skill of acting. You gain Expertise on performance and you may, as a free action, throw your voice so instead of sound coming off from you, it comes off from any spot within 30-ft of you, as long as you can speak.

subclassFeature.name: Woven Blessings

entries: "Hmm. Refraction of light through a polygonal mirror... This cannot be an appropriate interpretation of the Prescript to 'split the lights.'"

You are granted a special cloak to wear over your armor and garbs as a reward for your dutiful devotion to the Will. You have a piece of Prescript-Woven Fabric, which grants you an amount of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level times two plus your proficiency bonus. Whenever these Temporary Hit Points would be reduced, you may spend your Reaction to reduce the damage you would take by 1d8, and an additional 1d8 after reaching 16th level in Warlock.

While these Temporary Hit Points remain, you gain an additional two of them whenever you gain a count of Grace of the Prescript, but are instantly reduced by two whenever you gain a count of Karmic Consequences.
If lost or broken through your Temporary Hit Points reaching zero, you magically gain another piece of Prescript-Woven Fabric during a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: You're Gonna Burn Up

entries: "Teehee. You malding, bro? Whatchagonna do about it?"

You have learned how to keep your blades searing hot at will. With an Action, you can heat up your blade for 1 minute to cut through non-magical items and structures. You deal double damage to objects and structures with your weapon attacks. This feature has no effect on magical objects.

Additionally, while your sword is burning this way, you deal an additional 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when you hit a creature with an attack roll. Whenever an attack of yours would inflict a count of ({@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} this way, inflict the same amount of) {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: While this ability may appear simple at first, feel free to use it in creative ways. Carve a hole on the ground to create a trap for an enemy, destroy a wall to block the path and create difficult terrain, or even destroy walls to quickly get through locations. The world is the Middle's oyster!

subclassFeature.name: Zermürbender Würgegriff

entries: Metamorphosing into a hideous face.

The roots have overtaken most of your body by now, and are ready to sprout their blithes at your call. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your body for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point you spend, you can gain one of the following benefits of your choice, the effects of which last until the transformation ends:

items: Whenever you apply counts of {@condition Maggots|TheUndertomesASV} to a creature, you apply that plus 1 more.

You can sense a creature that has consumed one of your fruits even if they’re in a different plane of existence. You instinctively know where they are, or at least characteristics of where they are if you don’t know that plane of existence.

When you cast any spell where you have to roll to attack, you are able to grow and launch a rotten golden fruit with it. The target must make a constitution saving throw against your spell save dc or consume your fruit through your spell.

As an action, you can grow a golden fruit surrounded by barks on your arm and slam in on the ground. Every creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must roll a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.

entries: On a failure, they take {@dice 6d4} bludgeoning damage and suffer 2 counts of {@condition Maggots|TheUndertomesASV} as your rotten fruit’s contents explode on them. If they succeed, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

condition.name: Accumulated Past
entries: Accumulated Past is a counter representing the amount of compressed time a Crushbound wizard has collected.
It dissipates by 1 count per minute outside combat until it reaches 0, and it cannot normally be gained outside combat.

condition.name: Addicted
entries: An Addicted creature is considered {@condition Charmed} and will obey your commands, as long as the music does not stop. On their turns, they focus on attacking any other creature that isn't addicted until they are dead, doing their best to achieve such goal.

If a creature that is Addicted listens to the song until its end, the effect of Addicted does not fade until it is dispelled through the {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell or similar means, blindly following you in hopes of hearing the song again. Before that happens, though, an Addicted creature may attempt to retry the saving throw at the end of their turns.

condition.name: Battle Ready
entries: A Battle Ready creature is one who is focused on the fight around them, prepared to do their best as it comes. While Battle Ready, the threshold for your Hemorrhaging weapons is reduced by the amount of Battle Ready stacks you have. Additionally, you gain that same amount as a bonus to hit and to damage against the last creature who dealt damage to you or whichever creature caused a creature friendly to you to be knocked {@condition Unconscious}. When you score a Critical Hit, you deal an additional amount of d6 slashing damage equal to each stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} the target has, and then all stacks are removed from your target. These additional d6 are not multiplied by the Critical Hit.

condition.name: Bind
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Bind|TheUndertomesNW} is being slowed down in some form, reducing their movement speed by 5-ft. per count of the Condition they currently have. All count is lost at the end of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Bleed
entries: A Bleeding creature is well, bleeding! They take {@damage 1d4} damage when they perform any action ( Each attack is considered a different action, this also includes Bonus Actions, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ), and then Bleed is reduced by a count. They may have all Bleed count removed if any creature passes a successful {@skill Medicine} check on them as an Action. Otherwise, half their current Bleed count is removed upon receiving healing through an item or through a 4th level or lower spell. It is also fully removed upon the use of an item such as a {@item potion of greater healing|DMG|potion of Greater Healing} or a 5th level or greater spell.

On the case of casting a spell, they suffer an amount of {@damage d4} damage and lose an amount count equal to the spell's level plus one. ( Cantrips only deal {@damage 1d4} damage, 1st Level Spells deal {@damage 2d4} and so on. ) If a creature is suffering from lesser count than the spell slot level spent, they still suffer the maximum damage and remain at a single count.
The DC for this is 10 + their current Bleed count. If they have only one Bleed count, it may only be reduced through a {@skill Medicine} check.

condition.name: Bloodflame
entries: While you have Bloodflame, you may easily coat your swings into a pure blaze, causing you to deal an additional {@damage 1d6} fire damage per count of Bloodflame and also inflict two times your Bloodflame count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on melee weapon attacks. You may have up to three counts of Bloodflame at any given time, losing one whenever you deal damage to a creature and at the end of combat.

condition.name: Blooming
entries: A Blooming is slowly being overtaken by roots growing around their body and a constant haze clouding their mind. While suffering this Condition, they are under the following effects:

items: Whenever they suffer {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they suffer an additional count.
Their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count cannot be reduced under 3 times their Blooming count.

entries: Upon reaching 5 counts of Blooming, the creature must pass a Wisdom saving throw or become Fully Bloomed until the start of your next turn, also losing all Blooming count. On a success they lose half their count instead, rounded up. While under this Condition, they suffer from the following:

items: Their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count cannot be reduced.

Whenever they suffer damage, they suffer additional psychic damage equal to half their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, for a maximum value equal to double your proficiency bonus.
The creature is {@condition Stunned} for the duration. After becoming Fully Bloomed, that creature gains Advantage against the effect for the next three turns.

condition.name: Blubberbubble
entries: A creature with Blubberbubble has an amalgam of pulpy tears and gunk cling to them.

Despite their disgusting nature, they bring about a feeling of tears shed in solidarity with their situation. A creature under this Condition does not lose temporary Hit Points when gaining new temporary Hit Points.
A creature with counts of Blubberbubble loses 1 count at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Burn
entries: A Burning creature is set ablaze constantly, taking an amount of {@damage d4} fire damage equal to the number of Burn count on itself at the end of their turn, also halving its total count.
When at one Burn count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Butterfly

entries: "Long ago, people believed that they would become beautiful beings with small wings when they died."

A creature suffering from Butterfly is suffering two-fold, having a deep-seated lament cocoon around their heart and a grief for the departed flutter out as a pain that can hardly be avoided. For the sake of ease, the Butterfly Condition is also spread in two parts, starting out as Butterfly [The Living] when first applied to a creature and then turning into Butterfly [The Departed] at the end of the afflicted's turn.

entries.name: [ The Living ]
entries: Overflowing with lament for those yet to perish, a creature suffering from this Condition suffers an equal amount of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as it's current Butterfly [The Living] at the end of their turns, then turning any remaining Butterfly [The Living] into Butterfly [The Departed]. {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} gained at the end of a creature's turn this way is applied after being halved as usual.

entries.name: [ The Departed ]
entries: With grief unto death, any attack that inflicts Butterfly against the creatures deals an additional amount of psychic damage equal to half it's current Butterfly [The Departed]. count, to a maximum value equal to the attacker's proficiency bonus. Butterfly [The Departed]. count becomes 0 at the end of the afflicted's turn.

condition.name: Centipede Venom
entries: A creature suffering from Centipede Venom feels their muscles slowly constrict upon themselves, causing their body to grow stiff and pain to flare all around. They suffer from the following according to the sum of Centipede Venom count they are currently suffering from:

items: They suffer a number of d4 poison damage at the start of their turn equal to each 2 Centipede Venom count they are suffering from.
They suffer a negative modifier to Constitution and Dexterity Saving Throws equal to -1 per each 5 Centipede Venom count they are suffering from.

entries: Centipede Venom can only be applied to a Creature who is suffering from the {@condition Poisoned} Condition, ending as soon as {@condition Poisoned} ends.

A creature may only suffer up to 20 Centipede Venom count at any given time and if killed while still suffering the effect, all creatures within 5-ft of the dying creature must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or suffer from the {@condition Poisoned} Condition and inherit all the Centipede Venom count from the dying creature until the end of their next turn. The DC for this Constitution saving throw is equal to 12 + Half the Centipede Venom count.
( rounded down. )

condition.name: Charge
entries: A creature that is Charging is amassing an amount of energy - electrical, magical or otherwise, having jolts and arcs surround her body as the quantity intensifies.
Charge and its unique counterparts do not affect a character by itself, instead being a renewable resource to be spent for activating certain abilities and effects.

condition.name: Charge Barrier
entries: A creature benefititng from {@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH} has a coating of electrical signals that deter attacks made against them, taking the energy from such forces and dissipating them as much as possible.

A creature with {@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH} count gains an amount of Temporary Hit Points at the start of their turns equal to three times that count, or restores them to become that amount if they were any lower.
{@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH} count is reduced by 1 for each 3 points of damage taken while benefitting from these Temporary Hit Points.
Creatures who have {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Affinity have their count reduced by 1 for each 6 points of damage taken instead.

condition.name: Charge-Bind
entries: A creature suffering from Charge-Bind is one who's physically suffering moving their limbs and joints. Charge-Bind deducts an amount to the afflicted's initiative score equal to each stack of Charge-Bind is on a given creature. All stacks are destroyed on the end of the afflicted's turn.

condition.name: Charged Sting
entries: A creature suffering from a {@condition Charged Sting|TheUndertomesAED} has a wound that is particularly open to electricity, like turning their body into a portable lightning rod that is meant to attract and be ravaged by errant jolts. A creature under this Condition suffers an additional 3 points of lightning damage per count whenever they would suffer damage or fail a saving throw from an effect that would deal them lightning damage or that has spent {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, such as a {@spell Lightning Bolt} spell or the AEDD Tradition Wizard's {@condition Charged Sting|TheUndertomesAED} infliction skill. Wizards of the mentioned subclass always count as spending {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for the purpose of this Condition, and one count of it is lost at the end of the afflicted creature's turn.

condition.name: Coffin
entries: A creature with stacks of Coffin collects corpses they have killed inside a coffin taller than themselves that is wreathed in chains. You usually acquire points of Coffin after killing a creature, to a maximum of 10 points. A creature loses all stacks of Coffin after a long rest, as the bodies are completely absorbed by the coffin and turned into shadows.
During combat, at the start of their turn, any points of Coffin can be converted into several perks:

colLabels: Increase your speed by 5 feet for the next turn.
rows: Your attack rolls get an additional +1, to a maximum of +3, until the end of your turn.
You may add an additional dice to your damage rolls for each 4 points spent until the end of your turn.
Your AC increases by 2 until the end of your turn.
You may cast the {@spell Summon Shadowspawn} spell without requiring material components.
You may cast two Smite spells at once for a single spell slot whenever you attack until the end of your turn.

condition.name: Concussion
entries: A creature suffering form a Concussion has their senses flare up as if a worm was crawling and rattling the inside of their head, making any further breaks all the more painful. While suffering this Condition, they suffer the following:

items: Whenever the effects of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} are triggered, they count as if the triggering creature's Proficiency Bonus was its actual value plus one.
Whenever {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is triggered, the damage die dealt are one step greater, such as d4s instead being d6s.
The afflicted creature loses one count of Concussion at the end of their turns.

condition.name: Corpus Ingredients
entries: You, however, do not limit yourself to using your own body as material, also acquiring one Corpus Ingredients count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of Corpus Ingredients after such.

condition.name: Culprit!
entries: While being a Culprit!, a creature suffers an additional 2 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever it is hit and suffers a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20, before any modifiers. The Condition ends after one minute, after the Culprit! suffers a Critical Hit or after the Culprit! is knocked {@condition Unconscious}. When a Culprit! suffers a Critical Hit, they also suffer from {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Curse
entries: A creature inflicted with Curse rolls a {@dice 1d4} on the start of their turn, getting one of the following corresponding effects until the start of their next turn:

items: On a 1, the inflicted creature has a -1 on attack rolls and ability checks
On a 2, the inflicted creature has a -1 to their AC.
On a 3, the inflicted creature has a -2 on attack rolls and ability checks.
On a 4, the inflicted creature has a -2 to their AC.

entries: After gaining one of these effects, reduce your Curse count by 1.

condition.name: Dark Flame
entries: A creature ablaze with Dark Flame feels its soul weaken while the fire eats away at it. Its AC is reduced by 1 for every 3 counts of Dark Flame it has, to a maximum penalty of -3.
A creature afflicted with Dark Flame loses 1 count at the end of its turn. Dark Flame counts as {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Deathrite Fissure
entries: When {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is removed from a creature with points of Deathrite Fissure, its speed is reduced by 5 feet for each removed point. It recovers 5 feet of speed at the end of each subsequent turn. Its initiative is reduced by the same value and is restored by 1 at the end of each subsequent turn. After these effects are applied, the creature loses 1 point of Deathrite Fissure.

condition.name: Deathrite Haste
entries: When a creature with points of Deathrite Haste is hit by an attack, it takes one additional damage die for every 30 feet the attacker traveled during the current turn, to a maximum of four additional dice at 120 feet. It then suffers a number of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to the number of additional dice. After the attack hits, it loses all points of Deathrite Haste, ending the condition.

condition.name: Deathrite Venom
entries: A creature with stacks of Deathrite Venom suffers the following effects:

items: It has the {@condition Poisoned|PHB} condition even if it is immune to that condition.
Its AC is reduced by 1 for each stack of Deathrite Venom.
Its attack rolls and saving throws suffer a -1 penalty for each stack of Deathrite Venom.
Whenever it suffers a {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} critical or a critical hit, it takes an additional {@damage 2d8} poison damage and loses 1 stack of Deathrite Venom.

entries: A creature loses 1 stack of Deathrite Venom at the end of its turn. After losing all stacks, it is immune to Deathrite Venom for 24 hours.

condition.name: Deep Wound
entries: A creature suffering from Deep Wound has had a deep gash form in their body, great enough to assail them with pain constantly - And one that can be pushed to the edge with ease.

While suffering from the Condition, this creature has their movement speed reduced by 10-ft. and whenever they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they also suffer 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. A creature suffering from this Condition cannot gain {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesNA} counts.

condition.name: Defensive Stance
entries: You shift your whole body to be ready to protect first and foremost, cracking down on your foes while standing tall for your fellows. You gain the following effects:

items: Your movement speed is reduced by 10-ft. upon having a count of the Condition, and reduced by a further 5-ft. per additional count, to a minimum of 5-ft..
Their AC increases by 1 per count of the Condition.
All other creatures of your choice within 10-ft. of you have their AC increased by half the Condition's count.

Whenever you deal damage to a creature using your Divine Smite, you deal {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of damage die rolled for the attack, including other sources. ( Except for those granted by having another class, such as Sneak Attack die. )

entries: You can only have a maximum of amount of {@condition Defensive Stance|TheUndertomesPRT} equal to your proficiency bonus at any given time. You may choose to lose any amount of the Condition's count as a Free Action during your turn, also losing all remaining count at the end of combat.

Additionally, you may replace one of your attacks during your turn to slam your weapon in the ground and cause a shockwave, triggering {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} against all creatures within 15-ft. of you. If you have 3 or more {@condition Defensive Stance|TheUndertomesPRT}, you also inflict an amount of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to these creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus before triggering its Burst.

condition.name: Desperado
entries: A creature with Desperado knows that their resources are coming to an end and will not go down without a fight. You gain the following characteristics:

items: Any ranged attack that spends Ammunition deals an additional {@damage 1d10} Piercing damage.

You gain the Evasion ability. If you already have it, then when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Wisdom saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: A creature loses all counts of Desperado at the start of their next turn.

condition.name: Dimensional Rift
entries: A creature with points of Dimensional Rift is shown to have purplish lilac gashes cut across their body. At the end of their turn, the gashes disappear but sap away the creature's strength, giving them double the amount of points for the {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} condition equal to their points of Dimensional Rift.

condition.name: Drowsy
entries: A Drowsy creature is more succeptible to sleep, with any following rolls of the spell being considered double the result. In addition they suffer a -5 to their {@skill Perception} checks, as they are just too sleepy.

items: You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks, Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws and ranged attacks.
As a bonus action, you can yell at one of your allies to do better, granting them advantage on their next ability check, saving throw or attack roll, your choice

When you hit a creature that is {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremoring}, or Both, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} die of damage of equal damage to your weapon's damage type
You can substitute one of your attacks for a Sezionatura di Cervo.

condition.name: Enchanted
entries: A creature suffering from this condition takes an additional {@damage 1d6} of psychic damage whenever it takes damage, as it sees sights of a desired life it'll never have, degrading its mind. The condition lasts until the end of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Escalating Duel
entries: The rush of an Escalating Duel is that of a hunt going through its crescendo, building up for a magnificent climax. You gain the following effects according to your current count:

items: {@b 1 Escalating Duel.} You deal an additional 1 damage on melee weapon attacks.

{@b 2 Escalating Duel.} You gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit and deal an additional 2 damage on melee weapon attacks. Additionally, you inflict your choice of a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on hit.
{@b 3+ Escalating Duel.} You gain a +2 bonus modifier to hit and deal an additional 3 damage on melee weapon attacks.

entries: Additionally, you inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on hit and may choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the first melee weapon attack you hit during your turn.

condition.name: Eye of Precognition
entries: You have 15 counts of Eye of Precognition. While you have counts of this, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet
Your Armor Class increases by 3

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of Eye of Precognition. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature misses an attack against you due to your AC bonus, and 5 counts whenever you take no damage after succeeding on a Dexterity saving throw.
Once you lose all counts of Eye of Precognition, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesPP}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesPP} and gain up to 15 counts of Eye of Precognition, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

condition.name: Eye of Precognition - Overheat
entries: While you have counts of this, you gain the following characteristics:

items: You always roll an additional damage die of the weapon you are attacking with
Your Armor Class decreases by 3
Whenever taking Fire damage, take an additional damage die of the same value as your eye socket burns.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of Eye of Precognition - Overheat. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature hits an attack against you due to your AC decrease, and 3 counts whenever you take additional Fire damage from a hostile source. Once you lose all counts of Eye of Precognition - Overheat, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of Eye of Precognition - Overheat and gain up to 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesPP}, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

condition.name: Fanatic
entries: Whenever you enter your Rage you may choose to instead enter a state of sheer Fanaticism. While in that stage you have all the features you'd gain by being Raging, alongside the following:

items: Your faith burns brighter than anything, drawing holy wrath down the wounds poked into your foes. You deal an additional {@damage 1d6} radiant damage on and inflict {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesHF} count equal to the target's {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF} count on a melee weapon attack hit.

Your blind fanaticism may propel you to do grand things, but it also has you convinced of certain tribulations you simply must suffer entirely. Whenever you would be forced to make a saving throw or ability check, you may roll a {@dice d4}. On an odd result, you gain a bonus modifier equal to your proficiency bonus. On an even result, you get the same value as a negative modifier to the roll. If you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, you must always roll this {@dice d4}.

condition.name: Fatal Wound
entries: A creature suffering from Fatal Wound isn't long for this world, having a clear and brittle opening to the doorway that leads to their demise.

While suffering from the Condition, this creature has their movement speed reduced by 10-ft. and whenever they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they also suffer 6 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Furthermore, a creature has their minimum Critical Hit threshold increased by one, ex: They suffer a Critical Hit on an attack roll of 19-20. A Critical Hit against them triggers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and then removes their Fatal Wound Condition.
A creature suffering from this Condition cannot gain or have any Open or {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesNA} count, which is instantly removed if gained or sustained.

condition.name: Festive Fever
entries: Whenever a creature with points of Festive Fever attacks, it adds one extra die to all of their damage dice for each point of Festive Fever it has.
All points of Festive Fever are removed at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Focused Attack
entries: When a creature has a stack of Focused Attack, it gains advantage on attacks against you, and disadvantage on attacks against other creatures. It loses one stack of Focused Attack for each attack roll it makes.

condition.name: Fragile
entries: A Fragilized creature is suffering from having their defenses torn asunder or having difficulties in moving away from harm's way. While Fragilized, you have a cumulative penalty to your Armor Class equal to the stacks of Fragilized you are suffering. All stacks are removed when your turn ends.

condition.name: Fragility
entries: A Fragilized creature feels their interiors becoming brittle, and any blow could easily break them as the weakness sinks in, rendering attacks much more effective against them. A creature suffering from Fragility suffers from one of two effects depending on how many stacks they possess. From one to four, they suffer the equivalent value of stacks as penalty to their AC. On five or above the next damage type they take considered as if their resistance was one step down, with immunities becoming resistance, resistance becoming normal and normal becoming a vulnerability. After taking damage like this, one stack of Fragility is removed.

condition.name: Full Makeover
entries: You are simply glorious. A being that has taken the first step toward transcendence, and although that rush may be ephemeral in nature, you shall still remind all of your beauty while donning your Full Makeover. You gain the following while under this Condition:

items: Whenever you deal damage, you deal an additional amount of damage equal to a quarter of your current {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count, to a minimum of one additional point of damage.
You gain a bonus to your AC equal to half your proficiency bonus.
You inflict one additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you deal damage to another creature.

entries: Additionally, when first entering your Full Makeover, roll an amount of {@dice d12} equal to your proficiency bonus plus one additional {@dice d12} per 10 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count you have when entering the Condition. Your Maximum Hit Points increase by the result until the end of Full Makeover, where any excess Hit Points you have are turned into Temporary Hit Points. You regain these Hit Points when first extending your maximum.

condition.name: Game Target
entries: You may choose to make the last creature you attacked on your turn become your Game Target.

When you hit your Game Target with an attack roll, once per turn, you may choose to convert all of their counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremor Scorch}. Furthermore, whenever you apply counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to your Game Target, they suffer 1 additional count of each applied.

condition.name: Glimpse of Precognition
entries: At the end of your turns you gain a small peek into the future, gaining one count Glimpse of Precognition. You may have up to five counts of the Condition at any given time and lose all count at the end of combat. The source granting this Condition defines its remaining effects.

condition.name: Grace of the Prescript
entries: The blessings of the Living Will course through your veins like oxygen through your lungs, empowering your every movement and granting you a closer sense toward enlighten. You gain the following:

items: You gain a bonus modifier to your Attack Rolls and Saving Throws equal to half the count of Grace you currently have ( rounded down ).
You gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the count of this effect at the start of your turns, with this value remaining until the end of your turn.

entries: This effect ends whenever you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}. You lose one count of Grace of the Prescript whenever you suffer {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesFD}. You may have 9 maximum counts of Grace.

condition.name: Grasped
entries: A Grasped creature suffers the following effects:

items: A grasped creature's speed becomes 0, and they can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
The creature has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
The creature cannot restore hit points while grasped and suffers two of its hit die in bludgeoning damage at the start of their turns.

If the grasped creature is reduced to 0 hit points during the condition, their body is instantly crushed into paste by the hands holding it, rendering it impossible to revive through any means lesser than the {@spell Resurrection} spell or greater. Furthermore, you are magically healed by four of the creatures hit die's worth of hit points as their blood cascades down.

condition.name: Haste
entries: A creature that is going through Haste has a spring to their step, pushing themselves to move faster or are being carried through magical effects to become nimble as the breeze.

This creature gains 5-ft. of additional walking speed and, if already available flying speed for each Haste count they are benefitting from, to a maximum value of 5 times their proficiency bonus plus 5. All count of the Condition is lost at the start of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Haste
entries: A creature that is going through Haste has a spring to their step, pushing themselves to move faster or are being carried through magical effects to become nimble as the breeze.

This creature gains 5-ft. of additional walking speed and, if already available, flying speed for each Haste count they are benefitting from, to a maximum value of 5 times their proficiency bonus plus 5. All count of the Condition is lost at the start of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Headless Fowl [无头鸡]
entries: While in this state you have Disadvantage on any Saving Throws and Skill Checks, but may still move as your body acts upon its instincts looking for more fights. Whenever you inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on another creature, you deal one more count of the condition and you deal an additional damage die on every melee weapon attack, with its damage type being the same as your weapon's. You must roll a Death Saving Throws at the end of your turn and automatically regain half your Maximum Hit Points if you pass three Death Saving Throws, however instead of taking damage when a creature would deal any to you, you instead fail one Death Saving Throw per creature, per turn. You may benefit from Fuel My Rampage while like this.

condition.name: Heavy Blood
entries: Heavily Bleeding creatures are bleeding intensely, instead causing the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Condition and 2 count are removed every time it is triggered. The {@skill Medicine} Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

condition.name: Hexbind Curse
entries: A creature inflicted with the Curse condition feels their very veins constantly being pulled, twisted and nearly torn, making movement exceedingly painful. They suffer one Stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per time one of the following happens: The first time they are forcefully moved by another creature or use their movement speed during a round in initiative, every time they attempt to hit a creature and when they make Dexterity Saving Throws. The accursed creature loses one Stack of Curse at the end of their turn, or all stacks if the {@spell Remove Curse} spell is cast on them.

condition.name: High-Voltage Exoskeleton
entries: Your body crackles with lightning above the dermis, forming an armor-like structure that repels any incoming force. While under a {@condition High-Voltage Exoskeleton|TheUndertomesAED}, you gain an amount of Temporary Hit Points equal to 5 times the Condition's count. The Condition is lost at the start of your next turn and you gain twice it's amount in {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

condition.name: Hyped-Up
entries: A creature that is Hyped-Up is in a musical frenzy, hitting extremely hard, but being hit just as hard in return, You gain the following characteristics:

items: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, you deal an additional {@damage 2d4} psychic damage for each count of Hyped-Up you have.
Whenever you are hit by an attack, you must roll a {@dice d20}. On a roll of 5 or lower, you become {@condition Stunned} until the start of your next turn.

entries: You lose all counts of Hyped-Up at the start of your next turn. A creature cannot have more than 3 counts of Hyped-Up at once.

condition.name: Hysteria
entries: While raging, every time you miss an attack or take damage from a creature who is a Villain, you gain one stack of Hysteria, gaining double on any critical failures. You lose a stack whenever you land a hit against the Villain and lose them all when the Villain is knocked Unconscious or dies or your rage ends.
While under the effects of Hysteria, you progressively get more deranged in your pursuit of justice, your lofty goals propelling you forward like a hurricane of pain.

condition.name: Immobilized
entries: A creature suffering from Immobilized is one who's physically suffering moving their limbs and joints. While enduring Immobilized, they take a penalty equal to the number of Immobilized stacks they are afflicted with to all of their attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws. All Immobilized stacks are removed at the end of the afflicted's turn or after a minute has passed outside of combat.

condition.name: Immobilized
entries: A creature suffering from Immobilized is one who's suffering to move their stiffening limbs and joints. While enduring Immobilized, they take a penalty equal to the count of Immobilized they are currently afflicted with to all of their attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws.
