All Immobilized stacks are removed at the end of the creature's turn or after a minute has passed outside of combat.

condition.name: Immolation
entries: A creature beset by Immolation is suffering from the holiest of flames, taking an amount of {@dice d4} radiant damage equal to their current Immolation count at the end of their turns, also halving its total count. When at one Immolation count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Immolation
entries: A creature beset by Immolation is suffering from the holiest of flames, taking an amount of {@damage d4} radiant damage equal to their current Immolation count at the end of their turns, also halving its total count. When at one Immolation count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Impending Ruin
entries: Creatures with the Impending Ruin condition gain 3 stacks of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when their turn ends. Additionally, they have a -1 penalty to attack and damage rolls. If the creature becomes {@condition Frightened} while under this condition, the penalty becomes -2 instead, and they gain 5 stacks of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at end of turn instead.
This condition ends at the end of the turn, as long as the creature isn't {@condition Frightened}.

condition.name: Insight
entries: While you have Insight you gain a bonus modifier to unarmed attacks and Intelligence skill checks equal to half of your current count of the Condition. Additionally, you gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence saving throws and skill checks equal to your current count. You may have a maximum count of the Condition equal to your proficiency bonus.

If you spend Ki to perform an ability that requires you to have a minimum amount of Insight, you lose one count at the end of your turns. Otherwise, your count is reduced by one per minute spent outside of combat.

condition.name: Karmic Consequences
entries: As negative Karma builds up from your inaction and disregard for what must be done, a crippling force presses down on your soul, slowly bringing you to nothingness. You suffer the following effects according to how many Karmic Consequences you are suffering from:

rows: You have disadvantage on Ability Checks.
You have disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Saving Throws.
Your maximum hit points are halved.
You are instantly knocked {@condition Unconscious}. This Condition lasts until your next short rest.

entries: Your Karmic Consequences count is reduced by one upon a short or long rest, and is reduced by 3 whenever the {@spell lesser restoration} spell is cast upon you, or reduced by 6 whenever the {@spell greater restoration} is cast upon you.

condition.name: Larva
entries: A creature suffering from Larva have maggots crawling over and under their skin, little parasites spreading venom across their veins whenever they are disturbed. While suffering from Larva you take an additional point of poison damage per point of damage you would take from any other means while suffering from the condition, for a maximum value equal to your current Larva count and then reducing it’s count for as much damage as you have taken.
Furthermore, you suffer a -1 negative modifier to Constitution saving throws per 10 total count you have, to a maximum negative modifier of -4.

condition.name: Lodged Arrow
entries: A creature with counts of Lodged Arrows suffers the following effects:

items: When you suffer a count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, suffer 1 additional count per Lodged Arrows stack.
Lose 1 AC per stack, to a maximum of 2.
You take an additional {@damage 1d4} piercing damage whenever an attack hits you if you have 2 or more counts of Lodged Arrows.

entries: You can only have a maximum of 4 counts of Lodged Arrows.

A creature with counts of Lodged Arrows may use an action to remove the stuck arrows, taking {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and suffering 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each arrow removed in the process. Otherwise, they lose all stacks of Lodged Arrows on a short or long rest.

condition.name: Maggots
entries: At the start of your turn, you take {@dice 1d4} damage piercing damage for each count of Maggots that you currently have. If you are Bleeding while suffering counts of Maggots, you cannot stop the Bleeding with a {@skill Medicine} ability check, only being able to rely on healing magic or by waiting for the Condition to end.
A creature afflicted with Maggots loses 1 count at the end of their turns.

condition.name: Moonlit Azure Blade
entries: A creature with counts of Moonlit Azure Blade has honed their precision and instincts during the fight, connected as one with their blade. You gain the following effects:

items: At the start of your turn, you gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points. If you have 2 counts, you gain {@dice 1d6} instead, {@dice 1d10} if you have 3, {@dice 1d12} if you have 4, and {@dice 2d6} if you have 5.
If you score a Posture Critical hit or a Critical Hit, you add {@damage 1d8} force damage to the roll. If you have at least 3 counts, it becomes {@damage 2d8} instead.

entries: You lose 1 count of Moonlit Azure Blade at the end of your turn and all counts at the end of combat. You can only have a maximum of 5 counts of Moonlit Azure Blade at once.

condition.name: Naildle
entries: A creature suffering from Naildles piercing their skin is essentially being prepared, pinned down for soon-to-come cutting and sewing to come their way.

While under this Condition, whenever a creature pinned by Naildles suffers piercing damage, they lose one count and gain an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to the count lost.

A creature with a Dexterity score of 18 or greater can use their Bonus Action to pull off the pins without hurting themselves during a battle, rolling a Sleight of Hand skill check and losing an amount of {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} equal to the result divided by 4.
Otherwise, the pins are just too dangerous to remove without ripping skin, making it so they are only lost at the end of combat.

condition.name: Nails
entries: A creature suffering from Nails has a number of them embedded in their flesh, drawing out blood and the faith of certain individuals in equal measure. At the end of their turns, a Nailed creature halves their Nail count and gains the same value halved as {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.
{@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesHF|Fanatical} creatures gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls against Nailed creatures for each 15 Nails they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of +3.

condition.name: Nails
entries: A creature suffering from Nails has a number of them embedded in their flesh, drawing out blood and the faith of certain individuals in equal measure. At the end of their turns, a Nailed creature halves their Nail count and gains the same value halved as {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.
Fanatical creatures gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls against Nailed creatures for each 15 Nails* they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of +3.

condition.name: Needle
entries: A creature inflicted with counts of Needle suffers from a unique form of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. When you take slashing damage, gain 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and lose 1 count of Needle.
At the end of your turn, you lose 1 count of Needle and gain 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Nerve Strike
entries: Whenever a creature with points of Nerve Strike moves or is forcibly moved, it takes force damage equal to one roll of the Burning Jade monk's Martial Arts die. A creature can have a maximum of 3 points of Nerve Strike and loses 1 point whenever Nerve Strike causes it to take damage.

condition.name: Open Wound
entries: A creature suffering from Open Wound has a recent tear or puncture in their flesh that is still oozing with blood, and although they may not yet feel the pain from sheer adrenaline coursing through their body they already have difficulty in moving.

This creature has their movement speed reduced by 5-ft. per count of the Condition and upon reaching 2 counts, they lose that count and suffer from one count of {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesNA} instead.

Additionally, whenever a creature with Open, Deep or {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesNA} suffers {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, they are converted to {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesNA} count instead. If they were already suffering from any of the two Conditions, their sum is converted as well.

condition.name: Panicked
entries: A Panicked creature feels their heart nearly exploding constantly, as fears unimaginable crawl down their skin. As long as it is able to see the source of their panic must pass a Charisma saving throw on the start of their turn or have their movement reduced to 5-feet as they are nearly {@condition Paralyzed} from the horror. In addition to that, they suffer from a -2 penalty to their AC as long as they can see or hear the source of their Panic.

condition.name: Pheromone
entries: A creature affected by Pheromone lets out a citric smell that infuriates nearby creatures. They gain the following characteristics:

items: Any creature within 15 feet of you who targets a creature other than yourself with a melee attack must first make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or your Bee Save DC (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier), your choice. On a failed save, the creature chooses you as the target or loses the attack.
Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker suffers 3 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: A creature loses Pheromone at the end of combat or after 1 minute has passed while not in combat.

condition.name: Pheromone Mark
entries: A creature Marked by Pheromones is much more susceptible to being hurt by fire. For each 3 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} that they have, they take an additional {@damage 1d4} fire damage once per turn when attacked, to a maximum of {@damage 3d4}. They lose Pheromone Mark at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Photoelectricity
entries: A creature bedazzled by gathering {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} is having their body forcefully being used as an electrical conduit. Whenever they are hit with an attack or fail a saving throw, the originator of that attack gains an amount of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to this Condition's current count. {@condition Photoelectricity|TheUndertomesAED} fades and all count is lost at the end of the afflicted creature's turn. If a creature inflicts another with this Condition, they also gain the appropriate amount of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Piercing Sword
entries: A creature with Piercing Sword has a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls for every 2 counts of Piercing Sword it has. If the creature already benefits from a bonus to its attack and damage rolls, such as from a magic item, it instead adds {@damage 1d12} piercing damage to its damage rolls for every 2 counts of Piercing Sword.
A creature can have a maximum of 6 counts of Piercing Sword, and it loses all counts when combat ends.

condition.name: Pink Petals
entries: A creature affected by Pink Petals feels their body become covered in greenish roots feeding petals that weigh down on their soul. They gain the following downsides:

items: For every 5 counts, take 1 extra point of cold damage from attacks that either deal cold damage or inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
If you have 5 counts of this, gain an additional count of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you suffer it.
When suffering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, take additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage equal to half the proficiency bonus of the attacking creature.

entries: A creature can only have a maximum of 15 counts of Pink Petals. They lose 1 count of it at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Poise
entries: A creature benefitting from being Poised has their stance slowly being perfected to enter "the zone" while fighting, being able to perform a Posture Critical hit whenever they roll at least a 19 on attack, before adding any modifiers. This threshold is reduced by each additional count of Poise they have after the first, up to 4 ( Triggering a Posture Critical Hit on a roll of 16 or higher) and removing all Poise count from them when they land a Posture Critical hit.
When this effect is triggered, this creature deals an additional {@damage 2d6} damage on a hit of type equal to your attacks damage type.

If they have 6 or more stacks of Poise, they deal an extra {@damage d6} of damage for each two count above 6, to a maximum of {@damage 6d6} total. A Posture Critical Hit is not a regular Critical Hit.

condition.name: Preservation
entries: The amalgamation of all force compressed into the effort of having change be barred back, an arduous task as it often takes more to control such tides than to cause change itself. This Condition's count increases by 1 whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack or cast a spell of any level.

You gain a bonus modifier to Constitution saving throws and on Athletics or Acrobatics checks against being {@condition Grappled|PHB} for half of your {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} count, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. Additionally, you reduce damage taken by an amount equal to 1 point per 3 {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} you currently have, being able to do so at all times except when failing saving throws. You may spend your Reaction when you would suffer damage to actively spend {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} to change that conversion to 3 damage points reduced per {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} spent.

You may have up to 20 {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} count at any given time, and it is reduced by 1 per five minutes spent out of combat. This Condition counts as a form of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Procuration [Hermes]
entries: This Effect is granted and defined by the To Become a Canvas, Slowly Painted feature of the Fatalism Domain.

condition.name: Promised Nail
entries: "The promised hammer is bound by promise to drive in a nail. Therefore, whenever the hammer falls, a nail must exist there... even if there is none."

To be nailed down under the gaze of god is to be acknowledged as a noisy, uncouth bug to be squashed. Those suffering from {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} feel that in their heart - The ever-constant sense that the hammer will come down any second now. They suffer the following:

items: Whenever a creature suffers {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count, they also suffer the same value of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

For each 3 count of {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} the creature is suffering from they have their movement reduced by 5-ft.. Whenever a Paladin of the Obsidian God deals damage to a creature whose movement speed is currently 0-ft., their Divine Smite damage die become d10s instead of d8s.

Whenever a Paladin of the Obsidian God deals Divine Smite damage to creatures who are being pinned by Promised Nails they may choose to drive in the nails - Spending 3 {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count to deal an additional Divine Smite damage die and instantly gain 2 {@condition Preservation|TheUndertomesOBS} count per 3 Nail spent.

If the affected creature has 3 or more count of this Condition, their attacker may have {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} triggered whenever they suffer from an Attack that uses the Divine Smite feature. Whenever they are Burst in any way, they suffer an additional amount of magical piercing damage equal to their {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count.

entries: {@condition Promised Nail|TheUndertomesOBS} count is halved when the afflicted creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious|PHB} or fully removed when they die. They also phase out of existence after 1 hour out of combat.

condition.name: Protecting Sword
entries: A creature with Protecting Sword has a +1 bonus to its AC for every 2 counts of Protecting Sword it has.
A creature can have a maximum of 6 counts of Protecting Sword, and it loses all counts when combat ends.

condition.name: Pulsation
entries: Pulsation is sensation in its barest form, pure adrenaline coursing through you and the ever-growing will to do more and more using your body as the main tool to do so.
It's count increases in the following ways:

items: Increases by 1 whenever another creature deals damage to you through an attack or by a effect that results in you attempting a saving throw.

You may increase it by 2 whenever you would attack a creature with a weapon attack, wounding yourself in the process. You suffer an amount of damage equal to {@dice 2d6} plus your proficiency bonus whenever you do so.
You may increase it by 2 as a Bonus Action, suffering {@dice 2d10} damage that cannot be reduced in the process.

entries: You gain a bonus modifier to Athletics and Acrobatics checks equal to half your Pulsation count, to a maximum of +5. Additionally, whenever you would recover Hit Points by means that do not spend Pulsation, you recover an additional amount equal to half your current count.
You may have up to 20 Pulsation count at any given time, and it is reduced by 2 per minute spent out of combat.
This Condition counts as a form of {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Responsibility
entries: A creature with Responsibility takes one additional dice of damage whenever hit by an attack, but deals two aditional dice of damage when they hit a creature with an attack. The new damage is always equal to the original. This effect lasts until your next short or long rest.

condition.name: Rhythm
entries: A creature with this Condition has been enraptured by the god-rending melody of your carnage, and can't help but want to partake in it as musician and instrument, dealing and suffering an additional amount of damage equal to your Charisma modifier whenever they deal or suffer damage ( respectively ) equal to your 3 times your Rhythm count that they currently have. Whenever a creature declines receiving Rhythm, they halve the counts of the Condition they currently have, rounded up. Additionally, if a creature with this Condition benefits from your Bardic Inspiration rolls the minimum value rolled is always equal to their current Rhythm count, being increased if it was lower.

A creature with Rhythm gain an additional count whenever they first kill a creature during a round, except for summoned creatures. Additionally, a creature with 3 or more count may spend one count to perform an additional weapon attack or cast an additional spell of 3rd level or lower during their turn.

condition.name: Rupture
entries: A creature suffering from the Rupture Condition takes an amount of extra damage die equal to half their current Rupture count whenever they suffer an attack hit. The additional damage die depend on the attacking creature's Proficiency Bonus, being {@damage d4} at +2 Bonus, {@damage d6} at +3 Bonus, {@damage d8} at +4 Bonus, {@damage d10} at +5 Bonus, a {@damage d12} for +6 Bonus and finally {@damage 2d6} at +7 Bonus and greater.
Once an attack successfully hits and the condition is triggered, they lose all of their remaining Rupture count.
Ex: If a creature suffering from 5 Rupture would suffer a hit from a creature with a +4 Proficiency Bonus, they would take an additional {@damage 3d8} damage.

condition.name: Self-Charge
entries: {@condition Self-Charge|TheUndertomesAED} is a Condition that represents a mixture of sheer willpower and overwhelming energy keeping you from bursting at the seams. While you have count of the Condition, you are Immune to being knocked {@condition Unconscious} through any means. It counts as {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for the purposes of fuelling your skills and decays at a rate of 3 count at the end of your turns and 1 whenever you would suffer damage.

condition.name: Semi-Conscious
entries: While Semi-Conscious, you stay awake and may perform actions and so on as usual, with the penalties of having your movement speed reduced in half, your AC reduced by -4 and your rolls having a -4 penalty. The condition ends after you've been healed by a third of your maximum HP, rounded up.

condition.name: Serpent Arm
entries: A creature with Serpent Arm has 2 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for every stack of Serpent Arm it has.
Serpent Arm lasts until the end of the creature's next turn, when it loses all stacks. A creature can have a maximum of 3 stacks of Serpent Arm.
Serpent Arm usually manifests as violet scales on thin, fast arms, making them move like whips.

condition.name: Severed Tendons
entries: A creature suffering from Severed Tendons has had their movement options sliced clean through, reducing their movement speed by 5-ft. per count of the Condition. Furthermore, this debilitation hinders them further the worse it gets, having the creature suffer a cumulative negative modifier to Dexterity skill checks and saving throws for each 2 count.

One count is removed per hour spent without gaining more count or upon recovering any amount of Hit Points. All counts are removed upon being the target of the Restoration or {@spell Greater Restoration} spells.

condition.name: Sharpened by Tears
entries: A creature that is Tear-Sharpened has been pierced by a weapon that carries an enormous amount of despair and regret. It gains the following effects:

items: It is vulnerable to piercing damage.
Its AC increases by 2.
Whenever it hits an enemy with an attack, it rolls one additional damage die.
Whenever it or a friendly creature within 30 feet of it is hit by an attack, it can use its reaction to apply 6 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to the attacking creature.

entries: This effect lasts for 1 minute.

condition.name: Shimmering
entries: A creature with Shimmering generates 1 count of Bloodfeast whenever they are hit by an attack. Additionally, once per turn when they apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they may choose to gain temporary Hit Points equal to the amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the damaged creature, to a maximum of 10. This effect lasts until the end of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Sinking
entries: A creature that is Sinking has trouble focusing on anything as a deep unease washes over them, making way for pure leg-shaking terror or difficulty performing what they must. While suffering Sinking the afflicted creature has a negative modifier to Attack Rolls for each 3 Sinking afflicted to them, to a maximum of -5. Additionally, they have their Wisdom Saving Throws reduced by a negative modifier for each 10 Sinking, to a maximum of -3.
Sinking count is halved at the end of a creatures turn, rounded up. Upon having one count remaining it is removed entirely instead.

Ex: A creature with 12 stacks of Sinking suffers a -4 penalty to Hit. Additionally, that creature has their Wisdom Saving Throws reduced by a negative modifier for each 10 Sinking, to a maximum of -3.

condition.name: Sizzling Wound
entries: This state is granted and defined by the Masked Wounds feat.

condition.name: Smoke
entries: A creature suffering from Smoke has smog crawl and tear at their lungs, weakening their entire body horribly. They suffer an additional 2 damage per Smoke count they are suffering from whenever they would suffer any damage.

Smoke count is halved at the end of the afflicted's turns and fully removed upon ending a turn with a single count remaining, unless stated otherwise. There are few who can withstand this plume's effects, yet those who do can easily come to benefit from its vile use.

condition.name: Stigmatized
entries: At the start of your turns you may choose to have a creature become Stigmatized, the centre of your everlasting hatred. You may only do so provided there is no creature already Stigmatized, or you can use your Bonus Action to switch the victim of your Stigma.

condition.name: Strider Mao
entries: A creature with Strider Mao gains 5 feet of speed for each point it has and loses all points at the end of its turn.

As a bonus action, the creature can jump a number of feet equal to five times its proficiency bonus without provoking opportunity attacks. It can use this ability once, only while its speed is greater than 0, and regains the expended use when it finishes a long rest.
A creature with Strider Mao takes on rabbit-like features, usually morphing its feet into paws or developing a fluffy tail.

condition.name: Talisman
entries: Ill-Omens, disgraces and evil spirits - That is all these Talismans are to hold away, letting them find a new domain under the skin of whomever they are attached in. A creature from them has evil flood their everything, causing them to suffer an additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to their Talismans count whenever they first suffer damage during any creature's turns through an effect originating from another creature. ( Such as to have environmental hazards and traps not count. )

A creature may have up to 6 Talismans at any given time and the Condition is reduced to 0 when they fall {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}, die or over a long rest, as the Talismans quickly wither away.

condition.name: Target of the Prescript
entries: A creature who is the The Prescript's Target will soon feel the Living Will fall upon them.

Whenever a Target is dealt damage by a character that is aligned with the Will, such as a Living Will Warlock or Procuration Paladin, they suffer half their attacker's Proficiency Bonus in {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and the attacker may once per turn re-roll one of their damage die, taking the new result.
Other Conditions such as Will's Paper Slip also count as The Prescript's Target to any creature that isn't already benefiting from the equivalent Condition.

condition.name: Thermal Blades
entries: A creature inflicted with the Thermal Blades effect feels their blades have turned into searing hot weapons of burning incision. You gain the following effects:

items: If you hit a creature that has counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points. This becomes {@dice 1d6} at level 5, {@dice 1d8} at level 11 and {@dice 1d10} at level 17.
Whenever an attack of yours would inflict a count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, inflict the same amount of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries: You lose 1 count of Thermal Blades at the end of your turn and all counts at the end of combat.

condition.name: Torn Memory
entries: Whenever you kill a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} creature you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus and one Torn Memory count, as the already dissolving mental image of that which you have shattered lingers on in your aim. If you kill or knock a friendly creature {@condition unconscious} you gain one Torn Memory, yet you may only gain one count per creature per combat.
During your turn you may spend Torn Memory as a Free Action you may take once per turn for the following:

items: {@b Reload, Then Fire.} By spending one Torn Memory you may perform an additional attack as part of your Attack action during your next turn. This extra attack does not stack. Additionally, any ranged weapons you are wielding are instantly reloaded at the start of your next turn provided you have enough ammunition on your person.

{@b Designated Target Fire.} By spending at least three Torn Memory count you may spend your Action to perform a special attack, coating an 15-ft. radius within your weapon's range in a red haze that reeks of lingering sweat and charred hair. All creatures of your choice within that radius must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of d10 piercing damage and a sum of 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of Torn Memory spent. Creatures who succeed take half that damage and count instead. Afterward you gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each creature damaged through this, with an additional 8 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count if you have killed your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} creature through this attack. These 8 count do not count toward your turn limit. You cannot gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} in a single turn greater than double your proficiency bonus through this way.

condition.name: Tremor
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor is one suffering from immeasurable shaking and vibrations inside their body.

When a Tremoring creature suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage d4} thunder damage equal to their current Tremor count, then losing all remaining count.
The Condition is also lost after combat is over or at the end of the next short or long rest, if it was gained outside of combat.

condition.name: Tremor - Hemorrhage
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor - Hemorrhage is one that is currently bleeding out from countless cuts that rove and worsen inside their being.

A creature with Tremor - Hemorrhage counts suffers {@damage 1d4} damage whenever they perform any action ( Each Attack counts as a different Action, also including Bonus Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ) and then the Condition's count is reduced by one count. Creatures that have no blood are immune to this effect.

When a creature with Tremor - Hemorrhage suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage 1d6} damage equal to the total count of the Condition they are currently suffering from, then losing all remaining counts of the Condition. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition unconscious}. If they are healed to their Maximum Hit Points they instantly lose all counts of the Condition, also losing 2 counts whenever they are healed by any amount of Hit Points.

condition.name: Tremor - Hemorrhage
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor - Hemorrhage is one that is currently bleeding out from countless cuts that move and worsen inside their being.

A creature with Tremor - Hemorrhage counts suffers {@damage 1d4} damage whenever they perform any action ( Each Attack counts as a different Action, also including Bonus Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ) and then the Condition's count is reduced by one count. Creatures that have no blood are immune to this effect.

When a creature with Tremor - Hemorrhage suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage d6} damage equal to the total count of the Condition they are currently suffering from, then losing all remaining counts of the Condition. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious}, If they are healed to their Maximum Hit Points they instantly lose all counts of the Condition, also losing 2 counts whenever they are healed by any amount of Hit Points.

condition.name: Tremor - Scorch
entries: A creature suffering from Tremor - Scorch is one currently suffering from a blazing inferno that is eating them from inside out, with each flicker of flame reverberating across their entire being.
A creature with Tremor - Scorch counts suffers an amount of {@damage d4} fire damage equal to their current Tremor - Scorch count divided by 5, to a maximum of {@damage 8d4} per turn.

When a creature with Tremor - Scorch suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage d6} fire damage equal to the total count of Tremor - Scorch they currently have, then losing all counts of Tremor - Scorch. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious}, if they are fully submerged in non-flammable liquid or combat is over or on the next short rest, if it was gained outside of combat.

condition.name: Vengeance Mark
entries: During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a Vengeance Mark. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of Vengeance Mark is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of Vengeance Mark goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of Vengeance Mark until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains Vengeance Mark until the end of the first round of combat.

condition.name: Villain
entries: While you are wielding your Magic Wand, as long as no other creature is suffering from the Villain condition, the next creature you deal damage to suffers from being considered the Villain.

While you can see or hear the Villain, your near-sacred mission of protecting love takes hold of you. You gain a bonus to attack rolls equal to half your Proficiency Modifier against the creature and you deal your Strength modifier's worth of force damage instead of the usual damage type following your weapon on a hit.

condition.name: Volatile Passion
entries: A creature with Volatile Passion has a powerful will that can shatter if it falters.

While a creature has Volatile Passion, it gains a bonus to attack rolls against creatures affected by {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} equal to half its Volatile Passion count, rounded down. On a hit against such a creature, it also applies a number of Burn counts equal to that bonus.

condition.name: Well-Fed
entries: A creature remains Well-Fed until the next short or long rest. At 6th level, it has Resistance against Fire damage and at 12th level, Cold damage as well.

item.name: A Crow's Favorite Candy
entries: This little of dark candy tastes like licorice and most likely is licorice, with the odd fact that there is an intense kindness emanating from it. When consumed, you feel a warmth around you as if an angel's wing was curled over your shoulder, protecting you from wordly pains. You gain 7 temporary hit points and gain resistance to non-magical Slashing, Piercing and Bludgeoning damage for the next minute.

item.name: A Lovely Quarter
entries: This magical coin with one red and one blue, being both hot and cold to the touch at once. As a Bonus Action, you may propose a course of action for a bet against another creature or destiny itself, such as saying “You will land a big slash on that guy”, and choosing a face - Red or Blue. You then roll a d20 and toss the coin, with any roll of 10 or below landing on the Blue face and 11 or above being Red. After falling, the coin glows a bright light of the same color as the side up, and if you won the coin toss you gain your Proficiency Bonus as a bonus for the next time you take that course of action or suffering the same value as a negative modifier on a lost coin toss. If you do this while betting against another creature, you each choose one face and only one rolls the d20, with the winning creature gaining the bonus and the other suffering this negative modifier on the next time they attempt any roll related to the wager.
You may use this item for a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, regaining spent uses on a long rest.

item.name: Adaptable Extended Magazine
entries: Attachment, Martial Firearms (Tactical)
An exceedingly volatile magazine-set meant to attach and rebuild itself to fit the very specific bullet type of your weapon.
While Attached, the Reload value of your weapon is increased by half it's current amount.

item.name: Adhesive of Moral Reinforcement
entries: A small sheet of powerfully adorable stickers that can be glued to others to fill them with great happiness.
This sheet holds 5 Stickers that may be spent in the following ways:

items: You may spend a single Sticker to glue it to another creature within 5-ft. of you as a Bonus Action, giving them positive reinforcement and {@dice 1d6} temporary Hit Points. While these Hit Points remain they may once per turn add an additional {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to an ability check, attack roll or saving throw before or after rolling the die, but before the DM determines a result.

You may spend two Stickers at once as an Action to attempt to make another creature within 5-ft. of you find some happiness in their life, instantly causing them to be affected by the {@spell calm emotions} spell with a DC of 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier. Irrelevant to this effect's result, the creature feels a little less sad from being recognized in some way.

You may spend three Stickers at once as an Action to overwhelm another creature within 5-ft. of you with resolve, granting them the effects of the {@spell heroism} spell for the next minute. The temporary Hit Points gained through this are instead {@dice 3d4} temporary Hit Points plus your Charisma modifier.

entries: After its effects, any Stickers glued remain through fire and rain, clinging to belongings like memories. Memories are important, after all.

item.name: Advanced Bandolier
entries: A bandolier meant to be worn around the shoulder and across the chest, holding various ammunition pockets and a reliable set of hooks for heavier ranged weaponry.

While being worn, you can draw a weapon from the Holster as a Free Action you may take once during your turn, also stowing or discarding any currently wielded weapon as part of the same Free Action. You may also draw a pair of ranged weapons if they have the Light property.
Additionally, once per combat you may Reload a weapon as a Free Action by quickly reaching for back-up magazines stashed in the Bandolier.
This Bandolier takes the same time to don and doff as light armor, and you may benefit from only one Bandolier at any given time.

item.name: Advanced Holster
entries: A leather-bound holster that can be affixed on various places of the body to allow for tactical retrieval and stowing of light ranged weaponry.

While being worn, you can draw a weapon from the Holster as a Free Action you may take once during your turn, also stowing or discarding any currently wielded weapon as part of the same Free Action. To do so, the drawn weapon must not have the Heavy or Two-handed properties.
This Holster takes the same time to don and doff as light armor, and you may benefit for up to two Holsters at any given time.

item.name: Aiguille du Bonheur
entries: A pair of spear-sized hooked needles meant for crocheting live targets down to wearable size.

These weapons always come in a pair that shares the same characteristics, allowing you to comfortably use them for two- weapon fighting. If you wouldn't, you may add your Ability modifier to it's Bonus Action attacks.

You have a +3 modifier to attack and damage rolls while using these weapons and inflict 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you deal damage using them. Additionally, they count as Weaver's Tools.

entries.name: Exhilarating Craftsmanship
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with the Aiguilles you gain one {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count, and you gain an additional four count whenever you first knock another creature {@condition Unconscious|PHB} during combat or kill them.

entries.name: Fashionable Taste Test
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with the Aiguilles you may choose to weave their flesh into one of them, causing it to become slightly more unwieldy and have an accumulating -1 negative modifier to damage and attack rolls, for up to a -5. As a Bonus Action on your turn you may eat all of the meat gathered as if the needle was a kebab, instantly recovering an amount of d4+1 Hit Points equal to the negative modifier you currently have, then resetting it. (Made positive.)

entries.name: Matching Accessories
entries: While in {@condition Full Makeover|TheUndertomesCR}, these weapons deal {@dice 2d6} piercing damage instead of {@dice 1d10} and gain the Thrown (30/60-ft.) property, with you being able to use your Strength modifier for ranged attacks during it. When thrown in this way, you may use a lingering tendon-rope to pull back each Aiguille at the end of your turns as a Free Action, instantly returning them to your free hands. Whenever you hit a creature with a ranged attack using this weapon, you may spend your Bonus Action to attempt hooking them closer to you, attempting to Grapple them as per its usual rules. On a success, the target is instantly moved to the unoccupied 5-ft. space nearest of you. ( They are not Grappled. )

item.name: Aromatized Incense Burner
entries: An ornate box full to the brim with incense, in its metallic surface there are various etchings resembling holy symbols to preserve a veil of sanctity over it. As an action, a creature may start burning the incense, which lasts for a minute. It spreads a fine mist in a 60-feet area around itself, spreading to fit around corners and walls. This haze isn't enough to impair visibility, yet emits a strong herbal scent that is unpleasurable for Vampires, Bloodfiends and other blood-sucking creatures, having them feel nauseous and generally repulsed, granting advantage on any creatures insight checks to recognize their fiendish nature. This mist lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind or magical effect.

item.name: Atelier Logic Caliber Bullet
entries: {@i 5th-level Expanded Ammunition}
Have you wanted a smart, heat-seeking round? The Atelier Logic Caliber Bullet is laid in silver and expensive, extravagant technology to maximize its hit chance.

When used, you make a ranged weapon attack against a target within your range, you have a +3 to hit with this bullet. This attack's Critical Hit range is changed to a minimum of SL-20. On a Critical Hit, this attack instantly kills a creature with SL * 25 Hit Points or lower.

item.name: Band of Penance
entries: This leather sash contains various spikes on its inner fold, containing belts to be fastened to a creature's thigh or arm, feeding them a constant, righteous stream of pain. You may spend your Action to don or doff the Band of Penance, becoming Attuned to it. While Attuned, you suffer 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count at the end of your turns. This value increases by one for each day that you spend Attuned to the Band, also becoming Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} after reaching 6 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} per turn. While {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}, you gain Advantage on Wisdom Saving Throws, and while Heavily {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}, you gain a +4 bonus to Constitution and Wisdom Saving Throws. When you doff the Band and become Unattuned, you still suffer appropriate {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count at the end of your turns, reducing that value by 2 per day spent unattuned as your wounds slowly close.

item.name: Bandages of Inner Healing
entries: "Life can be hard, but thats okay." This looks like a completely normal roll of bandages, yet there's something about holding them that makes you feel calmer. A full roll has 3 uses, and the bandages may be applied to a creature within 5-feet reach as an action. When applied, the target creature is healed for {@damage 2d8+4} hit points and it feels weirdly soothed.

If the target creature is in a state of mental distress ( At the DMs discretion ) or has taken psychic damage in the last minute, the bandages can sense that hurt, healing an additional {@dice 2d8} damage and causing the creature to let out part of the weight on their shoulders, albeit momentarily. The creature gains resistance to psychic damage for one minute, and must pass a DC 15 Wisdom Saving throw or start crying, taking a -1 penalty to hit for the duration. As tears fall, they are magically soaked in by the bandages, which feed on the pained's tears and grow into more cloth for the roll, regaining one of its uses.

item.name: Basillisoup Ladle
entries: A large pole made by the clerics who follow the Lifestew, it dons a beak-like apparatus at its end that contains everflowing soup. It's scalding hot and exceedingly tough to handle by someone who knows not the ways of the stew.

entries.name: Stir the Stew.
entries: You may spend your bonus action to magically reheat the stew inside the ladle, having it become piping hot for this turn. When you do so, it deals an additional {@damage 1d8|d8} fire damage and inflicts a total of 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This lasts until the start of your next turn, where it becomes Warm, dealing regular damage and 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} only. After another turn, it becomes cold, dealing cold damage instead.

entries.name: Force-Feed.
entries: As an action during your turn, you may perform a melee weapon attack against a prone creature to force-feed it. On a hit, you deal an additional {@damage 1d8|d8} of fire damage and inflict 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on that creature.

item.name: Battle Gauntlet
entries: A mundane knight's gauntlet outfitted with blunt spheres on its knuckles, done so to elevate the sheer impact of a punch to the face.

item.name: Battle Torch
entries: A concealed torch that usually looks like a crude cudgel from its metallic casing. Its continual flame is hidden by a simple set of plates that can be opened up by holding a lever in its handle; it is done so since the flame is enchanted to quickly cover an area when blown on. While unlocked, the torch emits light like any normal torch.

item.name: Beak-Shaped Necklace
entries: A mysterious necklace made with small pellets reminiscent of gunpowder bullets and a sharp beak from an unknown bird at the center. Whenever you make a ranged attack that spends ammunition, you gain 5 feet of movement for ammunition spent this way until the start of your next turn. If all attacks you made hit, you gain advantage on ranged attack next turn.
Additionally, your attacks that inflict counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} piercing damage.

item.name: Beast Hunter Pistol
entries: This old, rickety handcannon holds many runes and magic circles inside so that any bullet will be blessed into tearing into monster's flesh. Any bullet fired by this gun is considered silvered and inflicts 1 Stack of {@condition Fragile|TheUndertomesASF} on a hit.

item.name: Beating Box
entries: An overwhelmingly sturdy boombox that has been attached to a set of golden chains. Its beats are solid, ground-breaking and positively skull-crushing.
Bards are considered Proficient with this weapon.

While used by a Bard, this weapon counts as a musical instrument that may be used for Spellcasting and {@skill Performance} checks. Additionally under the same condition this weapon gains the {@itemProperty SPL|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Splash} ({@damage 1d6}) property and may be used to deal thunder damage instead of bludgeoning, as a Bard best knows how to lay a beatdown with sound alone.

item.name: Bespoke Garments
entries: You stitch together a custom-made high quality weave for yourself or a target within reach. This uses the stats of a common-rarity mundane light armor of your choice, alternatively allowing you to spend an additional 2 {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count to make it be medium armor instead, or a further 2 count to make it be heavy armor instead.

Regardless of the weight class chosen, these garments are akin to any common or formal set of clothes, lacking plates and cushions yet showing all of the protective qualities armor should give, also making it so these do not incur Disadvantage on Stealth checks while worn.

A creature wearing this has a bonus modifier to their AC equal to half your proficiency bonus, and upon creation you may also accentuate one of their qualities - choosing one Skill they are proficient with to centre around. They gain a bonus {@dice d6} to checks using that skill while wearing the Garments.

You may toss the Garments to a willing creature within 30-ft. of yourself after finishing them at the start of your next turn. If you or the recipient of the Garments are being Clinged To by Needlekin they may use their Reaction to instantly change out of their current armor and put on the {@item Bespoke Garments|TheUndertomesNW} instead, making use of a quick wardrobe change montage to do so. The Needlekin provide folding screens for modesty.

If the creature complains about the work made ( as a Bonus Action ) you gain Advantage on attack rolls until the end of your next turn, yet suffer Disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws for the duration. What rude @$#@!&$.

item.name: Blind Judge's Scale
entries: This item cannot be attuned to by regular means, instead, during a period of 10 minutes you may drip a vial of blood extracted from a creature to fill its bowl, the creature becoming attuned to the Scale. This attunement lasts for one day. For the duration, a creature attuned to the Scale has their biases sharply weighted in directions they usually wouldn't.

The DM or Player (Whoever controls the character) may choose between having the creature do the inverse of what it usually would regarding its decisions, such as a politician who once plead for executing a person changing their mind and instead letting them free, or instead rolling dice to determine their choices, the die size being in accord to the number of options directly in their mind.

item.name: Bolt Rifle
entries: A powerful weapon made to take targets down from afar, possessing a bolt-action mechanism to fire rounds at unparalleled speed and force.

item.name: Bonecrusher Hammer
entries: This large hammer has its tip laid with spikes and a grip that facilitates both throwing and swapping it for a primary weapon. When you hit an attack with this weapon, the target suffers one stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture}.

item.name: BongBong Orange
entries: This slimy, yet delicious bubble dropped from a verminous creature is extremely healthy and, sadly, addictive. As a Bonus Action, any creature may eat this or feed it to a willing creature. The creature regains {@dice 6d4 + 6} hit points. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 14) or become addicted to the substance and unable to heal from anything else or eat anything else until their next Long Rest. This DC increases by 2 each time this item is consumed before a Long Rest.

item.name: Booster Shot
entries: {@i 3rd-level Expanded Ammunition}

Instead of the usual shell, this piece of ammunition is a syringe which will inject its contents upon piercing a target. When used, you may choose any creature within your Marksman Weapon's range, firing a healing round at them. They are healed by {@dice SLd6|SL d6} hit points and gain a +2 bonus to Constitution Saving Throws against being poisoned for the next hour, as the medicine strengthens their immune system temporarily.

item.name: Booze of Adoration
entries: A glass blown mug containing an endlessly self-replenishing pink-toned beer that goes down the throat like molasses.

Legends say it is made out of distilled, melted love, drawn from the many hearts of many people who only wished to have people to share a future with, a clinging desire that is left on the tongue after any swig.
You may drink from this mug as a bonus action to grant yourself the following bonuses until the start of your next turn:

items: You gain a supernatural courage and charisma, granting you advantage on your next Charisma skill check or saving throw.
A thin pink sheet of slime manifests around your exposed skin, beggining to grab onto anything it can. You gain advantage on grapple checks and a climbing speed equal to your movement speed.

You may spend your action to blow an Adoring Kiss toward a creature that can see you within 30-ft., forcing them to pass a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Charmed} by you for the next minute. They may retry this saving throw at the end of their following turns, and the DC for these is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

item.name: Botch Job Machine
entries: A small metallic backpack that can be affixed to the limbs of another creature. It’s insides contain an impossibly large and intricate amount of small surgical equipment it employs after being attached. As an Action while attuned you affix the Botch Job Machine to an {@condition Unconscious} creatures body, it uses an electrical shock to wake the target by restoring them to 1 hit point and then you may ask them a question: on an answer that is factually correct or that they believe to be correct, they are fully healed by the Botch Job Machine. If the answer is factually wrong or the creature is being untruthful, they suffer one of the following effects depending on where you have placed the Machine on their body:

rows: Head
The creature suffers grievous brain damage, losing their memory of the last week and a {@dice 1d4} value to their Intelligence Score.
Back
The creature suffers grievous muscle damage, losing proficiency in {@skill Acrobatics} if they had it and a {@dice 1d4} value to their Dexterity Score.
Chest
The creature suffers grievous body damage, losing proficiency in {@skill Athletics} if they had it and {@dice 1d4} value to their Constitution Score.
Arms
The creature suffers grievous nervous damage, losing the ability to use that arm and {@dice 1d4} value to their Strength Score.
Legs
The creature suffers grievous nervous damage, losing half of their walking speed.
Wings
The creature suffers grievous nervous damage, losing half of their flying speed.

entries: You may use this tool only once per body part and once per Long Rest. Furthermore, this machine does not work on creatures of Large size or greater. A body part that was damaged in this way can only be restored by means of a {@spell Greater Restoration} spell or greater.
Many of those who underwent an operation inside the machine have found themselves rested and healthy again.

item.name: Brainburst Bullet
entries: {@i 4th-level Expanded Ammunition}

Sometimes the best choice is to fully attempt to break a targets mind before their body. When used, you force a target creature within your range to attempt a Charisma Saving Throw, on a success they take {@dice 3d4} psychic damage. On a failure, they take {@dice 3d4} psychic damage upon failing and suffer an additional {@dice 2d4} psychic damage at the end of each of their subsequent turns, as the bullet pulses with psionic energy that causes massive aching. This lasts for up to one minute and the target may attempt the Charisma Saving Throw again after suffering the psychic damage at the end of their turn. On a success, the effect ends early but they suffer a parting echo of the psionic pain, taking {@dice 4d8} psychic damage.

item.name: Broken Signpost on the Way to Heaven

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: {@damage 1d4} radiant damage.
Versatile (1d10, 1d6)

This weapon wasn’t ever meant to be used as one, yet with dutiful faith it nevertheless concludes it’s purpose without question. Made out of pure gold and with a broken emerald signpost acting as it’s head, this Battleaxe emanates a purity aura like any other holy relic deespite the incomplete state it is in, immaculate even through it’s erosion.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a fiend or an undead with it, that creature takes an extra {@dice 2d10} radiant damage.

entries.name: As Is Written
entries: You may once per long rest cast the {@spell Augury} spell as an action without spending a spell slot, asking a course of action to the Deity who holds power above the Signpost and having a vague, cryptic answer being carved into the emerald tablet, only to vanish soon after as the material smoothens itself magically.

entries.name: Heaven-Sent Smite
entries: You may spend your bonus action to sprout wings made out of celestial light, which grant you a flying speed of 45-ft.. Whenever you would take fall damage while this ability is active, you may instead spend your Reaction to raise your axe and perform a melee weapon attack roll against a creature within reach, dealing whatever falling damage you would take to the target creature on a hit.

entries.name: Written Blessings
entries: You may cast the {@spell Guiding Bolt}, {@spell Find Traps}, {@spell Zone of Truth} and {@spell Spirit Guardians} each without spending a spell slot once per long rest.

item.name: Bum-Pick-Stitcher's Blade
entries: You create a weapon that is prim and proper. It is a +X Magic Weapon with the stat block of any common weapon you're proficient with, where X is replaced by a value equal to half your proficiency bonus.

This weapon also deals the same value as above in {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} count whenever you use it to deal damage to a creature. Whenever it is used to remove counts of the Condition from a creature you also gain an amount of Tiny and Sharp Nails. These Nails stick to and linger on your weapon as glorious decoration pieces, with you being able to stack up to 9 count at any given time.
Whenever you hit a creature using this Blade, you may remove an additional amount of {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} count from them equal to half your proficiency bonus.

You may use your Action to spend all Tiny and Sharp Nails you currently have to have them burst out as you let out some steam by swinging the weapon around wildly. All hostile creatures within a 15-ft. radius of you must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer {@dice 2d8} magical piercing damage and an amount of {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} equal to the damage die rolled, or half that damage and count on a success.

This radius is increased by 10-ft. per each 3 Tiny and Sharp Nails spent, and you deal an additional {@dice d8} damage per each 2 count spent. After using this Action, your weapon is stripped down to its barest materials, being broken and finding its only use as a non-magical Club.
If you are benefitting from the Pact of the Blade Boon you may choose to have the {@item Bum-Pick-Stitcher's Blade|TheUndertomesNW} count as a Pact Weapon for you while it still exists.

item.name: Butchered Knife
entries: A knife made out of pure, hardened meat and muscle. It will never rot or grow dull, as the cruelty in which it was shaped to become this way has forever seeped into the blade’s core, yearning for more blood to feel any sliver of life it might still be able to.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon and inflict 3 Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

entries.name: Butchering
entries: This dagger has its own desire for flesh, and it comes out violently whenever it has the chance to greatly wound a creature. Critical hits with this weapon deal triple the damage rolled instead of only doubling it, and you may spend your action during your turn to disfigure and dismember the corpse of a Large or smaller creature within 5-ft. of you, rendering it impossible to be revived by any means other than a True Ressurection or greater spell.

entries.name: Crawling From Nothing
entries: A deep dread is burrowed into this dagger, rendering it dependent on its wielder. While attuned you may spend a free action to recall it to one of your free hands no matter how far it is from you.

entries.name: Rush of Living
entries: While attuned to this dagger you feel a surge of adrenaline whenever this weapon senses the possibility of blood to be spilled, granting you 10-ft. of additional walking speed and making it so you may spend your reaction when you would be knocked below one hit point to have the blade bite into your hand, melding your flesh with its own. Your hit points cannot be knocked under 1 until the end of your next turn and you gain a further 10-ft. in walking speed, but are only able to take the attack action using this weapon. If you kill a creature like this, you are healed by {@dice 4d8+8} hit points, yet if you fail to do so you instantly fall {@condition Unconscious} at the end of your turn and suffer two failed Death saving throws as the knife takes from your blood directly.
…If I earned a name, will I get to receive love and hate from you? Will you remember me as that name, as someone whom you emotionally cared for?

item.name: Carmilla
entries: A whip made out of dry rosevines, holding it prickles your hands in its thorns, that although don't pierce through your skin, constantly reminds the weapon of its neverending hunger. At its tip, there is a wilting rosebud. This weapon is considered to have a +3 to your attack and damage modifiers, it also always inflicts one stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} on a hit. In addition to that, Carmilla deals additional piercing damage to the creature it hits equal to how many stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} the creature has. Hunger of Four-Hundred Roses. When you roll a 20 before any modifiers to attack while using Carmilla, the creature hit takes 20% of their maximum health in additional piercing damage, rounded down, as the rose in its tip starts blooming, and blood seeping down through the vine's length.

item.name: Chains of Loyalty
entries: A set of heavy, ostentatious golden chains that are usually rolled up around the wrists and forearms as a symbol of loyalty and the weight of family. To be used they are gripped in the hand and swung like a whip.
If you have any levels in a Middle subclass or the Sibling Background you are considered proficient in this weapon even if you normally wouldn't be.

item.name: Charred Mask
entries: This old metallic mask was owned by a man who lost everything, and in his desperation to eviscerate the mire of his mistakes, nothing remained except for it. While attuned, you have a -2 penalty to Wisdom Saving Throws and any Wisdom based Skill Checks. You also gain Immunity to Poison damage and Resistance to Fire damage. When you kill a non-summoned or magically created creature you gain {@dice 1d4+2} Temporary Hit Points as the Mask urges you onward until the purge is done. Furthermore, you are immune to the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} Conditions.

item.name: Cigarrette
entries: A cigarrete made out of a ground up and rolled herb that is infused with magical energy, aiding in focus and clearing one’s mind. You may spend your Bonus Action to smoke an entire cigarrete, gaining 1 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Count.
You suffer a point of {@condition Exhaustion} after triggering a Posture Critical hit if you have smoked more than four Cigarrettes before taking a Long Rest.

item.name: Coat of Evil Seeking
entries: This dark coat has a feathered collar and many golden, blazing eyes along its length. While attuned to this item, you have an AC of 14 +Your Dexterity Modifier ( Max. of 3 ) + Your {@skill Perception} Modifier ( Max. of 2 ). In addition, while donning it you cannot be surprised and have advantage on {@skill Insight} checks to detect evil intent from other creatures, with the addition of a faint dark aura appearing around the creature you made the check against, if its alignment is in fact evil.

On a critical failure in such an {@skill Insight} check, you determine they are evil no matter what, the armor activelly meddling with your thoughts to find any source of evil that could come from the creature, and the dark aura appearing all the same.

item.name: Collar of the Beast
entries: A collar made out of pure gold, its insides are full of intricate runes that lock up and slowly syphon the mana of the attuned, only to release it all back at a moment of true peril. This item can only be attuned by full casters. While attuned, this item is in sealed mode and latches itself to the attuneds neck, and while it isn't cursed it may only be removed by a spellcaster who knows at least fifth-level spells during a long rest.

Also while attuned, the wearer is rendered more fragile by the collars syphoning, taking their Proficiency Modifier's worth of additional force damage on each time they take damage. The attuned also gains a Release Counter, which starts at 0 every long rest and is increased by an equal value to the damage taken by the attuned. When the Release Counter reaches a value equal to your Proficiency Bonus times 50, the Collar enters its Released Beast state, which lasts for one minute.

The counter always resets to 0 on a long rest. Released State. After entering this state, you are granted your Proficiency Bonus times 20 temporary hit points and gain your Proficiency Bonus * 2 as a temporary increase to your Strength, Dexterity, Constitution scores and your Spellcasting score, to a maximum of 10.

Additionally, the overflowing mana releases can easily be manifested into Natural Weapons which take the shape of your choice, you may use your Spellcasting modifier to attack with this weapon and it has the Reach property, dealing {@damage 3d4} force damage on a hit. You also take your Proficiency Bonus times two less damage on each time you would take damage.

item.name: Composite Drawstring
entries: Attachment, String (Tactical)
This string is made of a agglomerate of materials interwoven and carefully enhanced to reach reliable draw strength and flexibility.
While Attached, you have a +1 to attack and damage rolls using this weapon. Additionally, your Short Range with this weapon is increased by half a value equal to its Short Range minus its Long Range.

item.name: Congealed Shot
entries: {@i 2nd-level Expanded Ammunition}

This bullet features a smooth gelatin congealed within its casing which explodes after hitting a target. When used, you may choose any point within your Marksman Weapon's range to shoot. When the bullet hits a surface, it detonates in the form of a 5-ft large sphere of gelatin.

If this gelatin hits a creature, they must perform a Strength Saving Throw or be pushed in the opposite direction of where they were hit for up to 10 * SL feet, with Large or greater creatures having advantage on this Saving Throw.

After being deployed, any creature within 5-feet of the gelatin may use their bonus action to hop onto the Gelatin, being flung in the air on a long jump for the same distance as if they would be hit in length and half that number, rounded down, of height, or the inverse if they choose to perform a high jump.

item.name: Corteous Garb
entries: A fancy piece of feywild clothing often used by the wealthiest of the fey to facilitate a flowing movement with absolutely no sacrifice to beauty or protection. It has light linen made from the vines of various magical flowers, boasting hanging ribbons that hang as adornments all over the arms of this outfit.

entries.name: A Most Gracious Bulwark
entries: As a bonus action during your turn you may focus on making sure not even the fastest arrow cuts through your marvelous body, granting you a bonus to AC equal to your Dexterity modifier, to a maximum of +3. This lasts until the start of your next turn and you may use this ability an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, recovering spent uses after a long rest.

entries.name: Dramatic Entrance!
entries: You may cast the {@spell Misty Step} spell without spending a spell slot for an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus ( rounded down ), recovering spent uses after a short rest. When you do so, you may choose to do a dramatic entrance or exit, granting you a +4 bonus modifier to your next Charisma skill check.

item.name: Courtesan’s Masquerade
entries: A porcelain mask whose origins are varied, with some saying it’s the physical manifestation of the fey courts having to force upon emotions to remain in their element, their faces forever stuck in certain emotions in this mask while others say this was the request of a king who went way out of his depth when he once asked to wear the face of a God. It is cold to the touch, as if it wreathed your face in a winter’s mist.

You gain a +1 bonus modifier to Charisma checks while attuned this mask, also being able to change it’s expression once per long rest or during it. You may don or doff the mask as a bonus action you may take during your turn. The expressions are as follows:

entries.name: Joy
entries: The mask’s lips curl up to a huge grin, granting you a false confidence that knows no end. While donning this face, you gain a further +1 bonus modifier to your Charisma checks and are healed by an additional {@dice 2d8} hit points whenever you recover hit poins, but suffer more from this supernatural sense of optimism, having your AC reduced by a -1 negative modifier and making you be Vulnerable to poison damage.

entries.name: Sorrow
entries: The mask’s frown nearly slips out of it’s cheeks alongside it’s tears, putting all the walls it can up from the world that wants to harm it so harshly. You gain a +1 bonus modifier to your AC and you always reduce damage taken by your proficiency bonus, but become Vulnerable to psychic damage and have disadvantage on all {@skill Perception} and {@skill Investigation} checks, also having your Passive {@skill Perception} score reduced by 5 while donning this mask.

entries.name: Wrath
entries: The mask nearly emits steam from its nose as it curls up in a mighty anger, granting you an additional 10-ft. of movement speed anda +1 to hit and to damage but making it so you cannot contain this destructive urge, both forcing you to pass a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw at the end of your turns or be forced to perform a melee weapon attack within reach of you, or automatically hit yourself if there are no others around, You are Vulnerable to any damage you deal to yourself while donning this mask.

While donning the mask you may use a free action to have it become {@condition invisible} or visible, revealing or hiding your face as it is locked into the same exaggerated expression as the one forced upon the mask.

item.name: Cowl of Nurturing Balance
entries: This flowing shawl meant to be worn over the shoulders is inlaid with silver resembling the scales of a carp. Touching its surface feels like caressing a cloud, yet it feels just as fragile. While attuned to this item, you feel a harmony come from the depths of your soul and resonate with the positiveness of whatever is around.

When you would use a hit die to heal yourself, you are instead healed by the full amount. Additionally, when you would cause or benefit from healing, you heal an cumulative +2 hit points per dice that would be rolled in the healing process.

item.name: Crimson Switchblade
entries: This weapon possesses an ingenous design with a retractable blade for ease of porting, possessing both a defensive and offensive mode. It usually sits in its defensive state, granting you a +1 bonus to your AC while wielding it with two hands.

entries.name: Switch.
entries: As a bonus action during your turn, you may switch this weapons mode, raising it to the air, unlocking its restraints and turning the blade outwardly, forming a great scythe. The weapon loses its original traits and gains the Two-Handed, Heavy and {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} (15) properties, dealing {@damage 2d8} slashing damage on a hit. In addition, you deal +2 weapon damage on hits against creatures below their hit point maximum.

item.name: Croaking Statue
entries: {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}. dc 16 Charisma | {@variantrule Active|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|active}, {@variantrule Primal|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Primal}
The statue of a tiny frog, bulbous in shape and with big, mushy eyes. It is made of a resin that makes it squishy and cool to the touch, being activated upon being squished.
An attuned creature may, once per turn, spend their Bonus Action ( In addition of an Action from the Active property )
to squeeze the Croaking Statue either in the back and stomach or in the head. When squeezed, the statue comes to life and performs an action depending on where it is squeezed:

entries.name: Back/Stomach: Gloomy Blubberubbles
entries: The frog spits out magical bubbles which float up to a number of creatures within 30-ft equal to your Proficiency Bonus, coating them in a magical wall of protection. They gain 1 count of {@condition Blubberbubble|TheUndertomesASV} and 5 + half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, temporary hit points.

entries.name: Head: Sorrowful Wail
entries: The frog’s eyes dart out of orbit before springing back, causing it to cry and wail so horribly that all creatures hostile to you within 30-ft must pass it’s Saving Throw or suffer 4 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

item.name: Crown of the Priest of Stars
entries: All the Lights in the Sky are Stars, and so are your friends. This crown is actually a visor that covers the eyes partially, yet its true magic lies in the fact that it can release a pleasant symphony that alleviates the troubles of the wearer's beoved. While attuned to this item and while you aren't {@condition Unconscious||unconscious}, you and all friendly creatures within a 15-foot radius of you restore a number of hit points equal to your proficiency modifier at the start of your turn as a magical wave emanates from the crown.

An {@condition Unconscious||unconscious} creature cannot benefit from this feature. If you take force damage while wearing this item, the crowns resonance is disrupted, causing the wave to instead deal force damage of an equal value of what would be healed. This lasts until the end of your second next turn.

item.name: Cursed Fireworks
entries: A modified lever-action rifle that acts as a shotgun. However, this modification is only the make-up for a much more devilish change that has been granted to this cursed creation.
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: A Pact With The Devil.
entries: This weapon's long range does not incur Disadvantage on attacks.

entries.name: The Power to Tear Open All Sides.
entries: Only one attack may be made using this weapon during your turn. When you do so, all creatures within 5-ft. of the original target are also targeted by the attack. You roll to hit only once and consider that result against the individual AC of each affected creature, also rolling damage only once for all.

entries.name: Iron sights on a Hazy Heart.
entries: This weapon is cursed to blow up the beloved persons in one's heart. If you are aware of two people who love each other platonically or romantically and deal damage to one while the other can see or hear, the other also suffers half the damage dealt as psychic damage. Whenever you Reload this weapon, if you have a beloved person yourself they suffer {@damage 3d8} piercing damage upon you firing the last bullet in this weapon's magazine. You may choose to otherwise suffer that damage yourself.

item.name: Cursewrought Blade
entries: This gigantic squared blade is engraved with runes that fester along its length. While attuned, potent ritual magic courses through your arms like a counterweight, allowing you to carry a weapon with the Heavy property in your other hand. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. A creature hit by it suffers 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If you hit a creature with this weapon after hitting the same creature with a weapon that has the Heavy property, the attack deals an additional {@damage 1d6} slashing damage.

item.name: Deck of Nothings
entries: This deck contains a number of cards made of solid shadow overlaid in a bright twinkling starlight to form its pictures. These decks also contain a great deal of nothing, which treathens to permeate the hearts of those desperate enough to draw from it.
To draw from this deck you may roll a d10, choosing as per the following tables.

You may draw only one card per day, and as soon as you draw a card from the deck, its magic takes effect. If you attempt to draw more than one card in a single day you must pass a DC 20 Constitution saving throw, on a success you suffer 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion} but manage to draw the card. On a failed saving throw you suffer 4 points of {@condition Exhaustion} and one of your fingers instantly disintegrates, making you lose part of yourself and consequently your choice of your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma score is reduced by two. This cannot be recovered from by any means other than the {@spell Wish} spell.

Once a card is drawn you must roll a d4 to determine if the card is drawn regularly ( on an even result ) or upside down ( on an odd result ), altering its effects. After being drawn, the card flies onto your chest and imprints its image above your heart as if it were a tattoo, becoming impossible to draw afterward.

rows: The Lover
A young lady frolicking through pink-tinted pastures with a defiant smile upon her face, having stars follow her unto the night as she waves a magical wand high.
You are cured of all Diseases, Curses and negative effects you are currently suffering from, also gaining advantage on any saving throw that would cause you to suffer any Disease or Curse.
The Knight
A lady knight holding her rapier high under the moonlight, shining with confidence and commanding floating swords that surround her in triumph

A legendary item of your choice vanishes from its rightful place or rightful owner, appearing suspended in the air in front of you and instantly becoming attuned to you until you die. This item can be ordered to float around you as a bonus action, requiring no hands to be used.
The Justiciar
A small child with gleaming, beautiful green eyes looking over a balance, mimicking it’s weights with open palms to be evenly matched.

A spiritual mediator appears in the nearest unnocupied space, taking the form of a small child who speaks politely and eloquently. That spirit offers to undo the strains between you and another target, teleporting you both to a demiplane of its own to discuss what wrongs each has done to the other, bringing back to reality any losses incurred by each of you, such as mending a broken item or magically reviving dead people. This cannot create what never existed, only undo what tragedy has already befallen both of you.
The King
A grand queen laying on an opulent golden throne, swirling wine as rows of subjects bow at their feet.
