You gain a magical, divine right to be the next in line of your choice of a major settlement that you know. This is proven by a marking burnt in gold around your wrist. All other direct competitors to the line of succession instantly crumble into dust as if they never existed in the first place, not being remembered by anyone that didn’t see you draw this card.
entries.caption: Upright Card

rows: The Hateful
A serpentine monster slithers through a village wreathed in purple moonlight, reaching out its scythe-like claws to grab at the heels of an unsuspecting child.

You are overcome with madness, believing the world has nothing to give you and it never will, being unable to feel any love that would be directed your way. You roll twice on the Long-Term madness table and suffer its effects until you die.
The Disgraced
A lady knight pierced by the blades she once controlled, with stars weeping sharp tears unto the earth.

entries: Three sharpened rapiers appear around you, with a copy also appearing atop the heads of your three most beloved people or creatures.

The DM gives you a quest you must complete until the end of the week, such as continuing the campaign’s story of stopping a powerful cult or something more specific, such as murdering the kind of a kingdom. If you do not complete this task within the given time, a rapier falls and pierces your heart and one of the creature’s heart, permanenly lowering your maximum hit points by 30% of your total hit points and instantly killing that creature. Another sword falls after each day spent without succeeding in your task.

rows: The Blind
A monster stands enraged atop a court room, hunting down every person that ever set foot inside.
A hulking monster using the Marut stat block appears in a settlement within an 100 mile radius of you, intent on destroying all who once called it a home.
The Tyrant
A monarch in a crumbling kingdom raises a gauntlet up high to swirl their golden wine, with golden cracks glowing through every broken pillar.

A lost civilization of the DM’s choice is instantly rebuilt in its peak, as if it were never destroyed in the first place. It’s leader(s) and people still remember how they fell and exactly how they died, yet blame the outside world for it. It’s leader(s) become influenced to pursue whatever will benefit their kingdom, uncaring of the expenses laid onto other nations or factions.
entries.caption: Reverse Card

entries: The following card cannot be pulled in inverse or regularly, having a form that misses any form of conventional definition.

rows: The Fool
A smiling masked fool wreathed in monochrome. It alone stands at the end of all things.

You may choose to delete one magical item ( and all its copies ), deity, important person ( such as the leader of a faction ) or kingdom from existance. If the target(s) had a physical form, it is turned to stone and is treated as if it always were a statue, with any memories related to this subject vanishing the next time anyone who remembers such blinks. The only creatures to remember this are those who saw you draw this card.
entries.caption: Immutable Card

item.name: Defender's Greatsword
entries: A high-tech, sleek machination of a blade, featuring a blunt- ended blade whose double-edged sides can extend into a greatshield while poised on the ground.

While wielding this Greatsword you may spend your Bonus Action to slam it on the ground, reducing your movement speed to 10-ft. and causing it to extend a luminous shield projection from its sides, granting a +2 bonus to your AC and that of friendly creatures within 5-ft. of you. You also suffer a - 2 to attack rolls while the sword's shield is active. You may return it to its standard form as a Free Action, lifting the limit to your movement speed at the start of your next turn.

item.name: Deluxe Prosthetic: "Silver Tongue"
entries: A prosthetic tongue for those who know they will need every linguistic trick and mannerism they can muster, and a famous sell amongst members of certain extremely punitive factions.

While having this Tongue be a part of your body, you can willingly turn off your taste buds, granting you Advantage against Constitution saving throws regarding being unable to consume something with horrible taste or enduring that process without throwing up. Additionally, you may have the sensory alteration to make any food you eat taste like any common-grade, store-bought meal.
Furthermore your Charisma score increases by 2, for a maximum of 22 and this Tongue aids your eloquence, granting you Proficiency to one Charisma skill of your choice.
You may have only an amount of tongues your race usually has at any given time.

item.name: Departure in the Shade
entries: An ebony colored pistol with fancy white engravings at its sides. Holding it gives a sense of determination to follow ones duty, yet when held alone you can sense a feeling of longing for its other wing. This Weapon has its own ammunition that is created magically when you reload, which you can do as a bonus action.
Reloading this way grants you 12 bullets for both Departure and Homecoming. You have a +2 to attack and damage rolls using this weapon, in addition to the following:

entries.name: TwinWings.
entries: This weapon's properties shown below are only active if you are attuned to both Departure in the Shade and Pale Homecoming.
In addition to those abilities, while attuned to both any damage you deal with this weapon also counts as radiant damage for the purposes of overcoming resistance and vulnerability.

entries.name: Absorbing the Light.
entries: The damage inflicted by this weapon fuels souls to keep on fighting for peace.

Every time you deal damage with it, this weapon and Pale Homecoming gain 1 collective charge. Upon delivering a critical hit against a hostile creature, you gain 2 charges instead. All charges dissipate at the end of combat or after one minute.
You start combat without charges.

entries.name: Calm in the Shade.
entries: When you spend your bonus action with this weapon, you may spend a number of charges to heal yourself.
You're healed by {@dice 1d8+1} per 2 charges spent, to a maximum of 8 charges spent.

entries.name: Gravekeeper's Duty.
entries: As part of your attack action, you may trade one of your attacks to cast the {@spell spare the dying|PHB|Spare the Dying} spell without expending a spell slot by using 2 charges.

item.name: Desperado
entries: A skull steel case filled with empty rounds of Ammunition that somehow empower you by their presence alone. You gain 10 feet of movement and a +1 to all Ranged attacks that spend Ammunition, as long as you already don't have a +3 from external sources.

At the start of your turn, if you only have 6 or less pieces of ammunition remaining, gain 1 count of {@condition Desperado|TheUndertomesDA}. At the end of your turn, you can spend a Bonus Action to make an additional Ranged attack against a creature within range as long as you have counts of Desperado Additionally, you always recover all spend Ammunition when searching for it after a fight as long as it wasn't destroyed.

entries.name: Not My First Rodeo
entries: As a Reaction to when a creature moves or uses an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction within reach of one of your ranged weapon attacks, you can immediately make a Ranged attack against them. If it hits, they must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity modifier) or become {@condition Stunned} until the end of their next turn. Once you use this ability, you can only do so again after the next dawn if the creature failed the saving throw.

item.name: Devouring Bloodstone
entries: A sphere of solidified blood that feels extremely rough to the touch, often rippling into small spikes while touching another surface. Inside it is a living hunger shivering to be sated.

As an Action you may toss the Bloodstone at an {@condition Unconscious} creature corpse within 30-ft of you, dealing {@damage 4d12} piercing damage to the creature if it is still living. If causing a creature to die or targeting a dead corpse, the Bloodstone quickly devours it until there is no trace left, generating Bloodfeast according to the creatures size, as follows:

entries.caption: Bloodfeast Generated
rows: Tiny
{@dice 1d4} - 1
Small
{@dice 1d4 + 1}
Medium
{@dice 1d6 + 2}
Large
{@dice 2d6 + 3}
Huge
{@dice 4d8 + 4}
Gargantuan
{@dice 8d8 + 6}

entries: A summoned creature or one with no blood cannot generate any Bloodfeast.

item.name: Disruptive Bullet
entries: {@i 1st-level Expanded Ammunition}
Also called thundershot, this bullet doesn't pack much of a punch but manages to disorient a person long enough to be helpful.

When used, you may choose a target within your Marksman Weapon's range and perform a ranged weapon attack against them, on a hit you deal {@dice SLd4} thunder damage and they suffer a penalty to Concentration checks and to any roll pertaining Interacting with an Object until the end of their next turn, as exceedingly loud ringing in their ears impedes them from doing so. This penalty's value is equal to half your PB times SL.

item.name: Divine Tears of Rage
entries: This round spherical object resembles an ornate egg with gold, platinum or silver bands wrapping around itself. In reality, it is the congealed wrathful tear of a divinty, whose rage may explode once more for even more destruction. As an action, you can prime this weapon and throw it in any space you can see within a 60-foot radius of yourself.

You prime this item by removing a latch that is an ornate symbol of its divinity atop the sphere. All creatures within a 15-foot radius of the sphere must pass a DC 22 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 10d8} radiant damage, or half on a success. On a failure whose final roll is 17 or below, the creature also has one of their limbs fully dissolved in light, roll a d10 to determine which.

A result of 1-2 is the right leg, 3-4 is the left leg, 5-6 is the right arm, 7-8 is the left arm, 9 is nothing lost and 10 the head or other relevant central organism, resulting in instant death. If a creature that failed that way has more than a limb or a completely different anatomy, the DM decides the roll and if a part can even be broken or not.

item.name: Double-Needled Needlekin Robe
entries: You make a nice little outfit for your naughty little $#!&$! You may give it to a {@creature Needlekin Servant|TheUndertomesNW} and order them to wear it as a Free Action at the start of your next turns.

While wearing this Robe, your {@creature Needlekin Servant|TheUndertomesNW} is invigorated by its beauty and the feeling of you actually caring about them! ( at least a little! ) You may choose to increase their Attribute Scores at a 1:1 rate when they first don the Robe, having a pool of points to spend equal to your proficiency bonus.
They also gain an Temporary Hit Points equal to an amount of {@dice d8} equal to your proficiency bonus, rolled when they first don the Robe.

You may spend your Reaction when the Needlekin would Buzz Off to have them flare out the Robes and ensure their safety first, having them retain one Hit Point until the start of your next turn. Additionally when you do so, the creature who last damaged your Needlekin must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC or have a thousand tiny needles explode near them at a trajectory starting from the robe and ending at their face. On a failure, they suffer an amount of {@dice d4} {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} equal to half your proficiency bonus.
After using this Reaction the Robe is torn to shreds, but your Needlekin isn't. It is grateful for that.

item.name: Emblazoned Hunting Shawl
entries: A Shawl fashioned for quick donning and practical movement while in a hunt. Its hem is lined with sharp emblems, either of holy symbols for protection or those resembling an old hunting order. This Shawl has six Vein Splitters spread around his hem, which you can spend to throw as part of your attack action. A Vein Splitter thrown this way is lost when thrown but inflicts {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} as per Hemorrhaging as long as it hits a creature who isn't immune to the condition. As an action while wearing this armor you may swiftly spin around, forcing all creatures within 5-ft of you to pass Dexterity Saving Throw whose DC 8 + Your Proficiency Modifier + Your Dexterity Modifier or suffer a number of d4 slashing damage plus the same number in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} stacks, or half on a success. This number is equal to half the amount of Vein Splitters still attached to it, rounded up. You may replace up to your Proficiency Modifier's worth of Vein Splitters to the hem of the shawl by using a separate Vein Splitter or by spending 20 gp per replaced part.

item.name: Emerald Elytra
entries: These small, insectile wings flutter enough to keep you afloat, no matter your weight and size. Once per long rest, as an action, you can cast the {@spell Fly} spell on yourself and gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Engulfing Wringer
entries: {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}. 14 dexterity | {@variantrule Adherent|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Adherent}, Arcana, Contract, Duration (2)
A small container of ooze that can easily be dug into the ground and burst out whenever a creature steps on it.
When triggered, a massive blob of slime bursts out and attempts to engulf and dissolve the triggering creature, causing them to be covered by slime on a failed saving throw.

A covered creature is {@condition Incapacitated}, has their movement speed become 0-ft. and they gain Resistance to all damage except acid, force and lightning damage. They instantly suffer {@dice 2d8} acid damage when they first are engulfed and at the start of their next turns. This creature may attempt to break free as a bonus action during their turn, performing an {@skill Athletics} check against a DC of 14 which lessens by 1 per turn spent engulfed, to a minimum DC of 10.

item.name: Evening Twilight’s Chains
entries: Set (2)

A pair of clear ivory chains that you may wrap around your wrists. They pulse with a faint light, promising to hold back the means to fight against the undending night ahead. You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
You gain Advantage on {@skill Athletics} checks to Grapple creatures while attuned to Evening Twilight’s Chains.

entries.name: Binding Lights
entries: As an Action within your turn you may throw both chains toward a creature within 30-ft, forcing them to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@dice 5d8} Radiant Damage, being pulled to be within 5-ft of you or to the closest space available and then being {@condition Grappled}, or only taking half that damage on a Sucess. A creature who fails this Saving Throw by a value greater than 5 points from the DC is instead {@condition Paralyzed} until the end of your next turn. The DC for this Saving Throw is 11 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency modifier and increases by 1 for each 25% of your missing max hit points, to a maximum of +4 when you are at 1 hit point remaining.
You may use the Binding Lights ability a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, per Long Rest.

item.name: Evening Twilight’s Hammer
entries: A small hammer made of silver and ivory. Despite it’s intricate craftsmanship, it carries no other outward features to impress. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon.

entries.name: Evening Twilight’s Shine
entries: While attuned, if you are to be knocked {@condition Unconscious} you briefly have your vision flash in white, with an echoing chorus of voices booming around your brain in a way only you perceive. They ask if you wish to “Become a true hero”, if you answer in negative, nothing happens. On a positive response you are bathed in a bright light, with the hammer in your hands growing to become a Warhammer that you are proficient with. You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon and it has the heavy and two-handed properties, dealing {@dice 4d12} radiant damage on a hit. You are also fully healed of any missing hit points and gain Resistance to all damage types until the end of combat, with your aligntment changing to become Lawful Good if it wasn’t before.

In addition to that, two spiritual warriors who share your character sheet form from pure light at the nearest empty spaces around you, donning pure-white armors and a copy of the same warhammer. They are friendly to you and hostile to creatures hostile to you, taking their own turn in Initiative.
You or the DM may control them, as per the DM’s discretion.
Their personality is also under the Dm’s discretion.

After there are no more hostile creatures that you can see within a 300-ft radius, your soul is taken into the hammer as you become one of it’s spirits. You instantly die from this and cannot be brought back by any means short of a {@spell Wish} spell.

item.name: Executioner's Greatsword
entries: A blunt-tipped greatsword with a two-handed grip that could be used to keep danger at bay as much as it can be swung to slice down threats.

entries.name: Assist
entries: A weapon with the Assist property is one that was designed to aid in defending the wielder, yet it’s usage makes it cumbersome to wield anything too big at the same time. While wielding an Assist weapon you gain a +1 bonus modifier to your Armor Class, but you cannot benefit from wielding Heavy weapons or a Shield.

item.name: Eye of an Archfey
entries: This eyeball has an unusual green tint with a misshapen pink pupil that still seems to tremble with life. It once belonged to an Archfey, yet it’s connection has been severed and made to serve a new master.

As part of the process of attuning to this item you may press the Eye into your own eyeball, having it absorb this magic item and become one with it. You cannot break this attunement unless you rip out the eye used. You gain a you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells. Furthermore, you gain Truesight with the same reach as your normal vision.

entries.name: Blooming Ethereality
entries: As a reaction to whenever a creature dies within 120-ft. of you, you may cause many flowers to germinate from the body, quickly overtaking it for nutrients.

The creature cannot be revived by any means other than a {@spell True Resurrection} spell as you drain their body dry of any lingering arcane energy and you may spend a bonus action while within 5-ft. of the newly formed flower bed to extract that energy, recovering any spent spell slot of 5th level or lower.

entries.name: Fairy Signet
entries: You may cast the {@spell Fae Wedding|TheUndertomesASV} spell as a ritual, and you may cast your choice of the {@spell Sylvan Mark of Extirpation|TheUndertomesASV}, Flower Field, {@spell Sprouting Lights|TheUndertomesASV} and {@spell Pixie Finders|TheUndertomesASV} spells as if you were spending a 7th level spell slot to do so without spending a spell slot for up to three times per long rest.

entries.name: False Attunement
entries: After first attuning to this item it does not count to your total attuned items as it becomes part of you. You also become Vulnerable to Cold Iron weapons and Immune to the {@condition Charmed} condition for as long as you are attuned.

entries.name: Perfect Vision of Unnatural Nature
entries: You may cast the {@spell Plant Growth} spell as an action without spending a spell slot at will. You also learn the {@spell Druidcraft} cantrip.

item.name: Fairy Feast
entries: A bundle of green-ish meat from an unsuspecting fairy. It smells of a mixture of herbs, with more pronounced hints of mint and ginger. It tastes heavenly and pops on your tongue.

A creature may spend a Bonus Action to consume the meat, being healed by {@dice 8d8+8} hit points and gaining {@dice 4d8+4} temporary hit points, then being forced to pass a DC 18 Wisdom Saving Throw or become addicted to Fairy Feast on a failure.

An addicted creature must pass a DC 14 Constitution Saving Throw at the start of all Long Rests, with this DC increasing by 2 on a success or the creature failing to benefit from the Long Rest on a failure.
A creature loses this addiction after succeeding three of these Constitution Saving Throws.

item.name: Feather of the Plagued
entries: People often mistake the dark coloration of this long raven feather and its namesake as some sort of ill-omen bringing filth and pestilence, yet the reality is that the feather itself seems to seek the broken and sickly to grant them respite. Upon attuning to this item, you can almost feel a welcoming presence comforting you whenever you take a long rest, one that you could only describe as gentle. When taking a short rest, you may instead of rolling your Hit Die to restore hit points, you may simply choose to restore your hit points as if you had rolled the maximum value for half of your total Hit Die.

In addition, when taking a long rest you heal double the amount of Exhaustion points you have, you also have advantage on any checks to resist disease and sickness that you might have contracted. In addition to this, you gain resistance to any damage taken whose origin is magical and have advantage on spell Saving Throws. The feather's black coloring slowly turns paler as it is attuned to.

On the twelfth time it is attuned to, counting only attunements from different cretures, it turns fully white, not granting any benefit on further attunements. In addition, all creatures who once have benefitted from its effects start seeing life itself as a disease to be cured, becoming hostile to nearly all creatures. If they were dead, they are revived and dug out of the earth if buried, filled with that one notion to flock around the feather and destroy all in their path so the world may begin anew.

All of the once-attuned gain a +3 bonus to all of their rolls, resistance to all damage types except Radiant damage, of which they gain immunity. Their alignment is also changed to Lawful Evil and will do anything in their power to protect the feather. This occurs for all of the previously attuned except for the 12th creature to have attuned to this item, who instead retains their alignment and any damage they would deal to the other previously-attuned is instead considered as if they had vulnerability, disregarding the damage type inflicted.
In addition, the 12th gains the ability of destroying the feather through cremation in sanctified incense.

item.name: Feather of Three Saints
entries: This greatsword weights more than the skeleton of a dragon, slices like the teeth of a Hydra and has been through conflict that would put beings from the Astral Sea to shame. To attune to this weapon, you must have the will of a true monster, not a simple warg hunting its food nor the malice of those that would rather take entire settlements, instead you require a will strong enough to bend the entire world and make it into something new. To attune to this item, you must have at least a Strength or Dexterity score of 20 and an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma score of 20.

Otherwise, attuning to this weapon fails and you suffer a level of exhaustion from the futile attempt. This item holds 20 charges, which you may use to fuel the abilities described below. It restores {@dice 1d8+3} expended charges at twilight.

You also have a +4 bonus to hit and for damage rolls while using this magic weapon. ShimmeringWings. As part of your attack action, you may spend 1 charge per attack hit to change the attacks damage type to what the target has vulnerability against.

Ordeal ofTwilight. As a bonus action on your turn, you spend 4 charges to slam the greatsword onto the ground and unleash a wave of magic covering a 60-feet radius around you. All creatures of your choice must pass a DC 20 Wisdom Saving Throw or suffer disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you.

Creatures that fail this check by a difference of 5 or more also become Panicked for one minute. The Futility of Humanity. As a reaction to when you take over 30 hit points of damage, you may spend 6 charges to give this weapon theVorpal trait until the end of your next turn, also lowering your critical hit treshold by two.

Final Judgement. As an action on your turn, you may spend 12 charges to invoke a giant stone scale behind you. All creatures of your choice in a 120-foot radius must pass a Charisma Saving Throw or take {@damage 6d8} force damage per each creature they have killed in the last week, or half the damage on a success.

item.name: Firing Gauntlet
entries: A gauntlet made out of various heat-resistant metals. While worn, you can use it for unarmed attacks. Fire Breathing Hand. Once per Long Rest you may extend your hand in place of one of your attacks (as part of the Attack Action) and emit a 15-ft cone of flame from it, causing any creature within reach to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take {@damage 3d6} fire damage and suffer 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count. The DC for this Saving Throw is 8 + Your Dexterity Modifier + Your Proficiency Bonus.

item.name: First Seal Removed: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: The first time you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, your choice.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 10-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Looks Like I Gotta Unbox the Second Layer, too.
entries: Upon reaching level 10 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item Second Seal Removed: Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Flesh Pipe
entries: This flute reeks of the smell of damp blood. Its appearence is rather common, made from some silverish metal and with intricate details of musical notes littering all of its surface. When played, its instinctual for you to play a hauntingly beautiful tune.

Song from the Heart. As an action, once per day you may start playing a melody that makes the body curl inside itself, unraveling minds from its sheer beauty. This song lasts for up to one minute, with concentration rules applying to it.

At the start of your turn, all creatures within 60-feet of you that can hear must pass a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or be afflicted by the melody, becoming {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} to it. An {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} creature is considered {@condition Charmed||charmed} and will obey your commands, as long as the music does not stop. On their turns, they focus on attacking any other creature that isn't addicted until they are dead, doing their best to achieve such goal.

If a creature that is {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} listens to the song until its end, the effect of {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} does not fade until it is dispelled through the {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell or similar means, blindly following you in hopes of hearing the song again. Before that happens, though, an {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} creature may attempt to retry the saving throw at the end of their turns. Feed the Machine!

As a bonus action during your turn while playing Song from the Heart, you may start casting a spell through the flute, any corpses within 30-feet of yourself start convulsing and caving into themselves, adding unto the bloody melody. {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} creatures gain a cumulative +1 to their attack and damage rolls, alongside gaining 5 temporary hit points per corpse that joins the melody, losing all these bonuses on the song's end. Additionally, the Saving throw for breaking free from {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesASF} increases by 1 per corpse that has been forced into the song.

item.name: Forestkeeper's Bell
entries: A massive silver bell held at the end of a quarterstaff. Its sound, when played near a creature can be made to reverberade so loud it hurts.

Rumours say that this bell was crafted by a lone druid who'd tend to the animals every single day, playing the bell twice when the critters grew old and perished. After centuries of this, the souls of the animals laid to rest grew to miss their old friend, and the ringing of that peaceful bell, still holding on for the chance another creature could come and play it for them.

entries.name: Don't Leave Us.
entries: When you become attuned to this weapon, the spirits of various critters hold onto you for their comfort. If you attempt to unattune from this weapon, you must pass a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you take 2 points of exhaustion as you feel a shortness of breath overtake you, as if you were being clung to tightly.

entries.name: We'll Help.
entries: If you would be reduced below one hit point, you instead mantain one hit point until the end of your next turn, as the spirits of wildlife keep you wide awake for a last chance of success, lest they are left alone because of the claws of death once more.

item.name: Forget-me-please
entries: A piece of parchment painted black through various substances alongside its own quill of white ink. You may write any passage containing a piece of information, name of a person you know or an event that happened. You then may fold the paper and eat it, instantly forgetting any memories associated with the subject held within the paper’s confines.

item.name: Forgotten Saint's Spear
entries: This spear is still warm to the touch, despite being made of what seems to be congealed blood and dry sinew. When it pierces another creature, it drinks blood as if that would bring back the Old God it used to be wielded in service of. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and when you hit a creature using this weapon and its roll before modifiers is within the range of 17-20, the target suffers a stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} that cannot be removed unless the creature takes fire damage, as the Spear grows sharp thorns inside their flesh, those being torn off and stuck inside when you reel the spear back.

item.name: Galaxy Egostone
entries: A waystone, guiding one heart to another in their connected galaxy. This twinkling, dark-colored geode is finely engraved to nearly look like a coin, its center exposing the shining white core of the outer-space mineral. This Egostone, when attuned, also absorbs a little of the attuned creature's mana to fully connect to them, and the attuned must speak aloud a new command word for it.

This attunement does not break save for the creature who attuned unattuning or the spell {@spell dispel magic|PHB|Dispel Magic} be cast unto it. An Egostone is meant to be exchanged with another, so two souls may always be able to see eachother. With an action, you may speak the stone's command word, when you do soo a magical illusion showing its attuned creatures whole body and 20-foot area around them or from their shoulders up appears, and you can hear everything around 30-feet of them clearly.

When you speak, you may choose to let the creature hear you and consequently everything else within a 10-foot radius of the stone, where the creature will telepathically hear everything inside their head.

item.name: Gecko of Disconnection
entries: Wondrous Pet
This tiny little lizard usually sports a dull, marble-like colouring with it’s spine protruding like a jigsaw puzzle.
Whenever aggravated or sensing another creature is feeling strong emotions near it, it might flash it’s skin into a bright golden or dim blue-ish glow.
While Attuned to the Gecko, you gain a +2 on {@skill Insight} checks to discern another creature’s feelings.

entries.name: Jinx & Luck Up
entries: You may spend your Reaction whenever a creature within 30-ft is about to roll a d20 to tell your Gecko to perform a small manipulation of fate against them.

When you do so, the Gecko acts upon it’s own whim as to how they perceive the targets wishes against yours, favouring the one who has the least willpower. You roll a d4, on an even result the target gains a bonus modifier to their next roll equal to half your proficiency bonus. On an odd result, they suffer a negative modifier of the same value.

item.name: Generic Acceleration Round
entries: This bullet is a marvel at providing a surge of speed to any weapon its spent on, commonly used to gain immense acceleration and throw opponents off or give way for more openings in rapid succession. These will leave higher-ups in life feel like they've been given leftovers, but they suffice for most jobs.
These can only be used in a Weapon that has the {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} property for melee weapon attacks.
Whenever you attack with a weapon that spent one such round, you gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

item.name: Generic Armor-Piercing Round
entries: It works like a double jab, one punch to scrape off the armor, the second one to punch through. What can you say? Its the old reliable.

Whenever you spend one such round to fire, the target for this attack is considered to have a -1 negative modifier to their AC if they are benefiting from any kind of armor. These bullets consider the {@itemProperty IPN|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Impenetrable} armor property's benefit to AC as if it were halved, rounded down.

item.name: Generic Flame Round
entries: A bullet filled with combustible fluid that's ready to detonate. For the love of the Wings, please don't think these are protected enough not to violently explode if you leave them near a lighter.
Whenever you spend one such round to fire, you deal fire damage for the attack and it inflicts 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

item.name: Generic Frost Round
entries: A bullet filled with cryogenic fluid. Don't expect to put super-soldiers in icebergs with these.

Whenever you spend one such round to fire, you deal cold damage for the attack and the target suffers a -1 to their next attack roll, as ice crystals form wherever they were hit. This negative modifier does not stack.

item.name: Generic Heat Conversion Round
entries: Fit with disposable micro-engines that intake heat to provide an increasingly rapid counter-weighted rotation inside the bullets chamber that allows it to keep its flight path while also delivering a chaotic vector of energy dispersal upon landing, these things are miracles of technology that were patented and watered down to the point where you can get them cheap for what they truly are.

Whenever you spend this ammunition, any {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} you would inflict on your attack is converted to {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead. If you would inflict none or lower, inflict 2 Tremor instead.

item.name: Generic Heavy Blast Round
entries: Also known as big blast sonic rounds, these forearm-sized bullets are meant only for the weapons that nearly escape the head's jurisdiction from their heavy calibre to their ludicrous stopping power. Because of heavy regulation and high selling prices, suppliers will sell an extremely limited stock of this type of bullet, enough to cover a single magazine of a fitting weapon.
Whenever you spend this ammunition, you inflict 5 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit and deal an additional {@damage d12} piercing damage.

item.name: Generic Propulsion Round
entries: A bullet not meant only to fire its load, but instead designed with the purpose of causing a continuous heat blast to supercharge the weapon's usage momentarily through a devastating shot or blazing swipe. These aren't the standard issue certain great organization use, but it fits the bill for a replacement.
These can only be used in a Weapon that has the {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} property.
Whenever you deal damage with a weapon that spent one such round, you also inflict an additional 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

item.name: Giant Pearl
entries: A giant shiny pearl extracted from a gigantic clam monster, being white, pink or green in colors. It is highly sought after despite its fragility.

item.name: Glasses of Restored Sight
entries: A pair of vintage round-lensed glasses with a silvered frame.
It seems well-worn but also well cared, a small artifact that has endured through the ages in a respectful manner.

While attuned, you cannot be {@condition Blinded} and if your ability to see is harmed in any way, it is restored while wearing the glasses, but lost upon their removal. Furthermore, you gain a +2 bonus modifier to {@skill Perception} skill checks and gain the ability to, as a Bonus Action, tap twice at the frame of the glasses and cause runes on the lens to light up and create a magical lens that you can see the world through with. These lenses show any ruins as they were once in their prime, such as a fallen castle standing tall or the corpse of a giant as if it were the creature laying down in a deep slumber. You may use your Bonus Action to turn these runic lenses off.

item.name: Goblet of the First Kindred
entries: A goblet of pure gold, emblazoned with rubies and other red jewels and intricately detailed with the figures of the first Bloodfiends to ever exist. An endless amount of crystalline blood sprouts from the cup, yet it never seems to spill, with the liquid defying gravity when turned upside down. Spilling Blood, Sharing Familial Bonds. Whenever a creature consumes from the Goblet, their eyes turn a deep red and their canines sharpen to the point of easily cutting flesh. The creature is turned into a Bloodfiend and cannot be restored by any means except the destruction of the Goblet. Destroying the Goblet of the First Kindred. To destroy the Goblet, you must burn the current First Kindred of a family to ashes and sink the Goblet inside them, then fixating it to the blades of a windmill using silvered stakes. After doing so, you must have the windmill for twenty four hours, to where the Goblet will have melted and its contents irrevocably spewed.

item.name: Golden HHair Coupon
entries: This is a golden ticket to utmost lusciousness, separating those with bristly hair from gods in humanoid form. This ticket is glistening gold, resembling the quality of shininess provided to follicles upon its use and has ancient engravings to allow use for any reputable and/or irreputable hair salon, filling the stylist with vigour and granting them the capability to cultivate the mane of dreams even if they wouldn't be able to cut a shrub with their fingers.

This item may be given to any hair stylist over the course of downtime or a long-rest for you to receive a luscious hair cut, consuming the item in the process. Any stylist must pass a DC 30 Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to give you the hair cut for free, as per the ticket demands. This process takes approximately 30 minutes, and afterward your Charisma score increases by 4, to a maximum of 24. Additionally, you permanently gain Proficiency in one Charisma skill of your choice and Expertise in another Charisma skill of your choice.

If you have not the access to a hair stylist at the given moment, you may read upon the faint engraving at this hair coupon's title, which at first seemed like a misprint doubling the "H" is actually fine print for "Haunted", indicating the capability of invoking a stylish poltergeist that will give you the hair cut instead of a living being in exchange for the ticket when it is folded neatly and then cut in two, as part of the phantom's ghastly ritual of utter lavishness.

entries.name: Cursed: Smells Like Chocolate.
entries: This item is a magnet to be stolen by lowly street dogs, as such any other creature has Advantage on {@skill Stealth} and {@skill Sleight of Hand|Sleight of Hands} to steal this item. When stolen, the thief permanently gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, even if they die and are revived. You deal an additional {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage on Unarmed Strikes against that creature.

item.name: Goldengrasp Hand Prosthesis

entries: "Don't be too bitter over it. Indeed, class is earned, not given for free; it's only right to give it the respect it deserves."

As if ripped from the Golden King Midas, the Goldengrasp Hand Prosthesis is inlaid with the beautiful material and finely carved to truly befit the moniker of leadership that all who wield it should have.
You have a +2 bonus modifier to attack and damage rolls while using this Prosthesis as a natural weapon.

entries.name: Accendino Molto Elegante.
entries: Although it is still little more than a secondary option, this prosthesis' beautiful fingers can act as a reliable lighter if your main one is missing. When you light a Cigar or Cigarette this way, you automatically pass their Constitution saving throws.

entries.name: Insegne del Pollice.
entries: This gilded hand is a heavy weight. Not for you, the bearer, but if you ever need to remind someone else of their place. While attached, it counts as a natural melee weapon you are proficient with, deals {@damage 2d4} bludgeoning damage plus two {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit and has the ammunition, finesse, light, range (30/45-ft.) and {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} (3) properties.

You may fold one of its fingers to reveal a series of revolver-like firing chambers as well, allowing it to reliably act akin to a magnum on a short-hand. While used as a ranged weapon, it deals {@damage 2d6} piercing damage and 4 Burn count on a hit.

entries.name: Giudizio Sommario.
entries: Whenever you would kill a creature, you may spend your Reaction to Enact Judgement on them instead. When Enacting Judgement, choose:

entries.name: Approvazione.
entries: You are merciful, allowing the creature to live. It isn't killed by your attack and instead is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}, instantly suffering 3 points of Exhaustion as well.

entries.name: Disapprovazione.
entries: The rat bastard simply deserved their judgement. The creature is killed outright. All creatures within 60-ft. that could see and were friendly to the dead must pass a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened||Frightened} of your for the next minute, being able to re-attempt this save at the end of their subsequent turns.

item.name: Good Intent
entries: An old, ornate walking cane carved out of an ancient tree, dark purple in its color. When held close to ones chest, a burning desire is felt. It sports the head of a crow at its top and a razor-sharp talon at its bottom.

When attuned, this weapon counts as a +1 arcane focus and any spells cast through it that deal necrotic damage also have that damage count as radiant damage for the purposes of overcoming resistence, vulnerability and immunity. Additionally, if your roll on a spell attack is equal to 20 before any modifiers, the target creature(s) cannot recover a value of hit points equal to the damage dealt for the next week, as they feel an overwhelming dread looming over them.

item.name: Grappling Dart
entries: A long rope with a weighted hook at its end, meant to be thrown and pulled afterward. When you hit a creature with this weapon you may spend your Bonus Action to attempt Shoving them 5-ft closer to you. When you do so you gain your Proficiency Bonus' worth as a bonus to your {@skill Athletics} check to do so and the creature takes an additional {@damage 1d4} piercing damage if successfully pulled. After being thrown you may spend a Free Action to instantly pull the Dart back into your hands.

item.name: Greatshield of Hollow Screams
entries: A huge shield that requires significant to wield, with it’s rectangular shape and multiple plates resembling a granite casket lid. It emmits a low rumble when wielded, as if it were a throat preparing to lash out and scream to the skies.
You must have a Strength score of at least 17 to wield this shield. While holding this shield, you have a +1 bonus to AC.
This bonus is in addition to the shield’s normal bonus to AC.

entries.name: Wailing Shield
entries: As a Reaction to when a creature within your melee range would deal damage to you, after taking damage you may make the shield lash out with it’s languished screeching, forcing your attacker to attempt a Wisdom Saving Throw or become the target of the shield. The shield manifest red ghastly hands that grasp and claw at it’s target, dealing {@dice 6d8} psychic damage and causing the target to become {@condition Frightened} of you until the end of their next turn.
Creatures {@condition frightened} this way have a -2 negative modifier to hit you.

The DC for this ability is 8 + Your Proficiency Modifier + Either your Strength or Constitution modifier. You may use this ability a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, regaining spent uses on a long rest.

item.name: Greatsword of Justice
entries: This sword's blade is a great rectangle of a darkened metal. Its wrapped in several bandages that somehow never shred as its swung around, and can't be dislodged by any means. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, additioanlly when you hit a creature they gain one stack of Sin until the end of combat.

When you hit a creature with Sin you gain an additional +1 to your attack and damage modifiers for each 2 stacks of Sin on the creature, to a maximum bonus of +3. If a Creature has 5 or more stacks of Sin, you may, as an action, perform Justice, you perform an attack with advantage against the target, and they take an additional d8 radiant damage per stack of Sin on them, then removing every stack of Sin they had.

item.name: Green Stiletto
entries: volatile
A blade made out of the flesh of a green fairy. It is soft to the touch yet surprisingly durable, with a velvetine texture that will never peel off and a sharpened point that will never go dull.
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon and you inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit.

entries.name: The Roots Deepen
entries: As a Bonus Action you may take during your turn you can swipe at the air and cause the Green Stiletto to grow elongated and reach far, gaining a reach of 15-ft. until the start of your next turn. However, this unwieldy nature makes it so you lose half your movement speed until the end of your next turn when you do this.

entries.name: To Support a Ravenous Nature
entries: The Stiletto holds a hungry {@skill nature}, being able to absorb the flesh of the living to heal it’s wielder. As a Reaction to when you would damage a non-undead creature with it you may make the Stiletto carve out the targets flesh and absorb it in a flourish, replenishing your hit points by half the damage dealt. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, regaining spent uses on a short or long rest.

item.name: Grim Grinning Visage
entries: A mask made out of solid stone and bearing the engravings of a sharpened grin, tear streaks running down it’s cheeks and half-circle eyes. It also has pierced ears and a crown affixed to it’s warm stone.

While attuned to this mask, you gain resistance against fire damage and inflict one {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when you hit a creature with an attack, or 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count if you land a Critical Hit against a creature. This manifests as flames flicker out of the mask’s mouth and spin around your weapon, ammunition or spell attack.

Furthermore, you may cast the {@spell Belch Flame|TheUndertomesASV} spell for an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, without spending a spell slot. You regain spent uses during a long rest by letting the mask sit inside an open flame, such as a campfire, oven or brazier.

item.name: Grinder Mk4
entries: This polearm ending in a circular shape with a smiling face drawn on it has spikes protuding from its head, as a saw lays concealed inside. As a reaction taken when you deal damage to a creature using this weapon, you may turn on the grinder, forcing the creature to pass a Constitution Saving Throw whose DC is equal to your 8 + Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus or take an addiitonal {@damage 4d4} slashing damage.

item.name: Harmonics
entries: A strange, bloodied instrument infused with dark magic and put together with scraps of a dark machine. Whenever a creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or suffers a Critical Hit, every creature that is not {@condition Deafened} within 30 feet of you suffers 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesMG}.

If you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you applies counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} while there are Fragility creatures within 30 feet of you because of this effect, all friendly creatures within 30 feet of you lose 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesMG}, and the attacked creature suffers an additional 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Hatchling of Justice
entries: While this little bird is quite lanky for its size category, it can still be carried over the shoulder with ease, as most of its length comes from its crane-like neck. Its body is covered by dark feathers, and its head by bandages of a gift long given. It gives tips on how to be impartial and fair always and yearns for justice.

While attuned to a Hatchling of Justice, you gain a +1 bonus to your {@skill Insight} checks, as the Hatchling aids in guiding your judgements. As an action, once per day, you may perform a Peacekeeping Gift. Choose up to four willing creatures beside yourself.

A spectral white pinion falls and lodges itself in any place that it can addorn, such as on one's hair or pauldron, and you become linked for a quick moment. In this quick moment, the health values of all creatures in this ritual is summed up and then divided equally for each creature, becoming the result of that. If this value would exceed one's maximum hit points, they gain the excess as temporary hit points.

This cannot affect creatures who are {@condition Unconscious}. Woundrous Pets & Friends A "Wondrous Pet" is the mechanical term this document uses to refer to, well, pets! A Pet in this way is a magical being that while attuned, will always remain within a 60-feet radius of its perceived owner.

They do not require food nor sleep, but will gladly partake in either joy. A Pet does not partake in combat initiative, instead it is treated like any other magic item when called upon for an active or passive ability it grants. Additionally, it has no stat block of its own, instead only providing static benefits to its master.

Much like the {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiar} spell, a pet may be commanded with a free action to move and to enter or exit an extradimensional space where it is kept safe. It automatically enters that space if it would be immediately in harms way, instead remaining safe. If the {@spell dispel magic|PHB|Dispel Magic} spell is cast on the Pet, it vanishes for one minute, and then rematerializes after this time.
During its vanishing, you cannot benefit from its abilities.

item.name: Hatchling of Protection
entries: This tiny, fist-sized bird is a big ball of dark feathers that still fail to cover the various golden. slightly incandescent eyes across its body. Those, of course, only being rivaled in quantity by the sharp teeth in this bird's mouth. It cannot fly, but will gladly use its big wings to climb up and hoist a ride on its owner's shoulders.

It really wishes to keep all safe and sound. While attuned to a Hatchling of Protection, you gain a +1 bonus to {@skill Perception} skill checks and your passive {@skill Perception}, as the Hatchling's watchful gaze always helps you find your way. Also, while attuned you may spend your reaction when an ally would be targeted by an attack to Draw in Interlopers.

Draw in Interlopers. You ready yourself for a fight as the Hatchlings eyes and yours glow in a golden light. The attacking creature must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or be compelled to attack you instead until the end of their next turn.

The DC for this is whichever your class would have for their features or Spellcasting. If there is none, the DC is 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. You must be in range of the attacker's attack to use Draw in Interlopers.

item.name: Hatchling of Punishment
entries: A small, round little bird that resembles a little dove. It has a penchant for pecking people and perching on peoples heads. While attuned to a Hatchling of Punishment, you gain a +1 to Wisdom Saving Throws, as the Hatchling's incessant pecking keeps you annoyed, but focused with whatever task at hand.

As a reaction you may forgo this bonus on yourself and give it to a friendly creature within 15-feet of you. Also while attuned, once per day you may use your action to Enact Punishment. Enact Punishment.

Some people have pushed things too far and they need to get their due. You perform an attack against a creature within melee attack reach, gaining advantage if this creature dealt damage to you on the last turn. On a hit, you deal an additional {@damage 4d8} piercing damage as a force compels you to use the beak of your weapon to stab the culprit a few additional times.
This action may only be used when you are below half your maximum hit points.

item.name: Heaven's Thorn
entries: This seems like the torn off branch of a tree, yet on closer inspection, its made of muscle tissue and sinew. It never rots, and when attuned to, you feel a need to be gazed back upon whenever you look another creature in their eyes. You hear echoes from time to time coming from the Thorn, echoes saying that it came from Paradise.

While attuned to Heaven's Thorn, it always crawls up to your shoulders by itself during combat, as if it were alive. Whenever a creature that was engaged with you disengages or suffers from blindness, the Thorn performs an attack against it. This attack has a reach of 10-ft., a +8 to hit and deals {@damage 2d10} piercing damage plus {@damage 4d8} radiant damage as it pierces the target with its thorns, absorbing any blood spilled.

item.name: Heavy Gauntlet
entries: A metallic glove made specially to allow for heavy punches instead of the usual defense a gauntlet provides.

entries.name: Special
entries: Heavy Gauntlets are meant to facilitate the use of your hands while being donned, yet still have their limitations. While donning a Heavy Gauntlet, you can still use that hand to cast Somatic components or interact with objects, but the metal makes it impossible to wield another weapon over it.

item.name: Heavy Revolver
entries: A steel-made revolver capable of causing heavy damage, but remaining unwieldy due to it's unwieldy kickback.

item.name: Helmet of Mambrino
entries: A golden crown and visor meant to be worn as a helmet, covering the eyes in many jingling parts. It is finely crafted and rumoured to grant invulnerability to its wearer. Might Before the Tall Things. Not even a living mountain could get past you! While attuned to the Helmet, you think you are invulnerable to damage and that you automatically pass all Saving Throws. You also become immune to the {@condition Charmed||Charmed} and {@condition Frightened||Frightened} Conditions. Cursed. The Helmet of Mambrino digs teeth-like appendages onto its wearer's face after being attuned with an imperceptible pain. If not through a {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell or greater, a forced attempt to remove the helmet will cause you to suffer {@damage 6d8} slashing damage and become permanently {@condition Blinded||Blinded} as you lose your eyes.

item.name: Hemobar
entries: A bar of compressed and dried blood meant to quench the thirst of Bloodfiends and Vampires alike. It is textureless and tasteless, functioning as a Ration yet barely palatable. You may spend an Action to consume a Hemobar and gain one Bloodfeast, yet must pass a DC 13 + Times you've consumed a Hemobar until your next Short or Long Rest Constitution Saving Throw to benefit from another one, suffering one point of Exhaustion on a failure.

item.name: Hoarfrost Chick
entries: Wondrous Pet

A small chick covered in icy-blue feathers and actual ice crystals that define its beak and eyes. It appears to have taken a liking to you, perhaps guided by the only warmth it has ever felt in its life.

entries.name: And Now, the Snowy Weather
entries: The Hoarfrost Chick always knows when it’s going to snow in the next 7 days, and will let you know by gently pecking your feet or shoulders.

entries.name: Happy Trail
entries: Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of the Hoarfrost Chick do not consider snowy and icy terrains as Difficult Terrain.

entries.name: Chilling Peck
entries: As a bonus action, you can command the Hoarfrost Chick to make a melee attack roll against a creature within 5 feet of it. If the Hoarfrost Chick hits, the creature takes {@dice 1d6} cold damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (save DC 14) or suffer 3 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Hollow Mirror
entries: A small hand-mirror that seems nigh unbreakable, having a handle made out of an unrecognizable pink material that smells vaguely of meat and is sticky to the touch, having the texture of soft fur and being oddly warm to the touch. It holds a piece of you, but you might have not come to learn that yet. Neither has it.

When you attune to this item, a reflection of you appears constantly on it’s surface, speaking telepathically to you at all times. This version of you is its own being, having all memories you do until this point yet striving to aid in your tasks with the best advice it can, criticizing and guiding you at all times without ever vanishing. The only difference between you and the You in the mirror is that it has no filters, constraints or inhibitions, always leaning onto being direct and plain in it’s thoughts, unpleasant and overly critical as they may be.

entries.name: Helpful Advice, Shameless Criticism
entries: You gain advantage on all skill checks you are proficient in as the You in the mirror always aids you, however its contant criticism has you suffer one point of {@condition Exhaustion} whenever you fail a skill check you are proficient in.

entries.name: The Better You
entries: If you die while attuned to this item, the mirror breaks, slowly inching closer to your corpse with a movement speed of 5-ft. if separated from you. When it arrives within the same space as you, its glass shards dig into your body and possess it, fully healing you and reviving you, except you are now the one in the mirror, while the False You takes over your body, inheriting all your characteristics and stats.

entries.name: You Cannot Escape You
entries: If you go further than 120-ft. away from the mirror, the You in the mirror finds its way back to you unless you are the target of a {@spell Remove Curse} or greater spell. The You in the mirror can appear in any and all reflective surfaces that can see you, and the surface’s size directly commands how loud and imposing the other You may be, becoming louder the greater the size of such a reflection. If another creature holds the mirror while you are attuned, they may speak with the you inside the mirror.

item.name: Hundred-Tailed Whip

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage.

A long, black whip made out of chitin and hundreds of vertebrae, boasting various fibers of growing length as they get closer to its end. These fibers seem to ricket and twitch when the whip is being gripped tightly, coming to a point where after spending enough time with the whip, they safely coil against your arm in what seems like a centipede showing affection. Despite that, each fiber still has a chance to inflict a deadly poison if mishandled.

You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon and when you hit a creature with it, roll a d100, inflicting the {@condition Poisoned} Condition on the target until the end of your next turn and inflicting a Centipede Poison count for each sum of 20 rolled.

item.name: Hungry Hand Puppets
entries: The child always loved playing the dragon, it was in their blood afterall. It was a shame when they decided that their chivalrous friends would no longer touch their hoard, and they didn't know how much of a dragon lied beneath their skin. A pair of fluffy mittens that almost look like little cotton balls if not for the chattering teeth at its sides.

It fully covers the fingers, forcing it so a puppet-like mouth is the only type of shape your hand can take as you wear this. While attuned to the pair of mittens, the palms protude sharp teeth that gash and gnaw, and you always feel a tinge of elation to all you do, as if a filter were placed upon your perception of the world, making it all feel more chivalric. This weapon is considered to have a +1 to your attack and damage modifiers, in addition, it can hold up to 5 charges.

It regains one charge each time you deal damage to an enemy. You may spend charges to perform one of the following actions: Feast for the Chivalrous. As part of your action, you may spend 5 charges to indulge in a great feast.

Until the end of your turn, this weapon's damage die is changed to a d12, and you heal for half the damage dealt, as the mouthes in your gloves grow to gnaw away at your foes. Whirlwind of Om-Nom-Nom. By spending 5 charges and your action, you may perform an attack on each creature of your choice within a 5-feet radius of yourself.
You heal 2 hit points for each hit creature.

item.name: Imperfect Eye of Precognition

entries: "Enlightening...? What are you, fuckin' blind? You don't have shit to learn from these amateur-hour failures, Lucio. Or you wouldn't have, had you stuck to my instructions like I told you to."

Its hard to determine if this is a fake or if this legendary relic has been tarnished just like the reputation of its most famous wielder, its sights failing at times as the uncertain future closes in like a blazing room - soon to be consumed to leave only ashes behind.
While implanted, you gain a +2 bonus modifier to your Armor Class.

entries.name: Glimpse of Precognition.
entries: At the end of your turns you gain a small peek into the future, gaining one count {@condition Glimpse of Precognition|TheUndertomesTT}. You may have up to five counts of the Condition at any given time and lose all count at the end of combat. You gain a bonus modifier to weapon attacks equal to your current count, but whenever you suffer damage for the first time in any creature's turn you must pass a Wisdom saving throw or lose that bonus until the end of your next turn, where you also lose all count gained. While you lose this bonus, your AC is decreased by an amount equal to your current count. The DC for this saving throw is equal to 16 plus your current count.

entries.name: Opportunistic View.
entries: You've grown accustomed to looking for opportunities to strike while using this unreliable thing, so when you get a freebie you can't help yourself but to draw everything you can out of that opportunity. Whenever you would deal damage to a creature that is Immobilized, Paralyzed or Stunned you may re-roll each damage die you would roll once, taking the higher value of each. The same applies if you have a Critical Hit.

entries.name: Misplaced Opening.
entries: It is tiring because of the odd synapses that the eye causes, but you can manage to tap into the short insights you get into the future to draw out openings on your targets. Once per turn, whenever you would hit a creature with a weapon attack you may instantly spend one {@condition Glimpse of Precognition|TheUndertomesTT} count to perform an additional weapon attack against them.

item.name: Innard Gazer
entries: A polearm containing a spinning buzzsaw instead of a bladed end. When activated, the saw spins willdly, causing it to become harder to control if not activelly cutting through a target.

entries.name: Gaze Guts
entries: This weapon has a certain rythm to be used, sinking deeper into a target’s flesh if well applied yet flailing wildly on a miss. When hitting a creature with this weapon, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to your next attack and damage roll against it, but when you miss an attack you suffer a -1 negative modifier to hit and to damage rolls.

Furthermore, the final attack you could perform during your turn is enhanced by this potence, dealing double the bonus or negative modifier’s worth of damage, such as having a +2 dealing 4 additional slashing damage or a -1 causing you to deal 2 less slashing damage. This effect is reset at the start of your turns. If you hit a creature {@condition Grappled} by you, you deal an additional d4 slashing damage die per bonus modifier you have from this effect.

item.name: Insignia For The Capo
entries: A simple set of a well-cared for burgundy hat and the golden insignia of the Thumb. Despite having no incredible enchantment or even some sort of technology, these carry the weight of being given to many souls who gave their all only to be crushed under the Thumb of the Capo.

entries.name: Shoot When Asked to Shoot.
entries: Your head hangs heavy with the weight of each bullet spent. Whenever you spend non-standard ammunition ( Such as Generic Acceleration Rounds, Flame Rounds, etc ) for a ranged weapon attack you deal an additional damage dice on a hit and inflict your choice of one additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

entries.name: Kill When Asked to Kill.
entries: Your heart skips a beat whenever you make another stop forever. Whenever you kill a creature that was suffering from {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count all creatures of your choice within 10-ft. of the killed suffer half the Tremor count they had when they died.

entries.name: Die if You're Told to Die.
entries: Your whole being lives and dies upon the orders of another, upon the benefits of another. Whenever you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} for the first time in combat or be killed, all friendly creatures within 60-ft. of you gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls and inflict their choice of 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever they hit a creature with an attack or have a target fail on their saving throws. This bonus lasts until the end of combat, as your dutiful sacrifices demand respect even beyond the grave.

item.name: Karkosa Workshop Minelets
entries: {@i "Supplant, suffuse, subjugate."} is one of the motto's presented by the workshop that modelled these bullets after the bursting pustules that certain mermaids form. Disgusting inspiration aside, these bullets pack a punch once installed.

Whenever you spend this ammunition you may target an empty space within range to deploy the mine, firing it rapidly to cause it to drill into the ground. If you hit a creature with this, the minelet burrows inside them. In both cases, the minelet is inert until the start of your next turn and after becoming active, it explodes the next time a creature moves out of the space it was fired upon or the creature it was burrowed in suffers damage, forcing all creatures within a 10-ft. radius of the mine to make a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 3d8} piercing damage and your choice between 4 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count or triggering {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

The DC for this save is 8 + your attack modifier with the weapon used to shoot. The same value is used as a DC on Investigation or Perception checks to locate a minelet on the ground. While Inactive, a minelet may be safely removed by a creature within 5-ft. of it spending their Bonus Action to make a Sleight of Hand check against a DC equal to the Dexterity save.

item.name: Knuckles of Loyalty
entries: A set of heavy golden knuckledusters, housing enough weight to break a face and still retain their luscious shine.
If you have any levels in a Middle subclass or the Sibling Background you are considered proficient in this weapon even if you normally wouldn't be.

item.name: Lead Bullet
entries: {@i 3rd-level Expanded Ammunition}

Simple, effective. This bullet is made of solid lead, containing only a handful of poisons and acids applied. When used, you make a ranged weapon attack with your Marksman Weapon. On hit, in addition to its normal damage inflicted, the target must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or suffer from the {@condition Poisoned} Condition for the next minute, repeating this Constitution Saving Throw at the end of their turns. On the first failure of this Saving Throw and on subsequent Saving Throws at the end of their turn, regardless of their outcome, the {@condition Poisoned} creature also suffers {@dice SLd8|SL d8} poison damage. Creatures immune to poison damage instead treat this damage as if they only had resistance.

item.name: Liar's Apple
entries: An apple painted golden until it began shimmering. Inside it holds a cruel poison, concentrated as the sheer evil in its maker’s heart.
Upon ingestion, the creature who ingests it must pass a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or suffer {@dice 18d8} poison damage.

If they are knocked {@condition Unconscious} by this, they continue being {@condition Unconscious} until a {@spell Remove Curse} or greater spell is cast upon them or a specific course of action specified by the apple’s creator comes to pass, such as being kissed by the creature’s true love. While {@condition Unconscious}, the creature is in a deep slumber and if they wake up their memories are foggy enough that they cannot clearly remember how they came to fall asleep.

item.name: Litograph of an Unknown Prophecy
entries: This is a sizeable emerald tablet carved out to contain what most believe to be a prophecy of an apparent Deity, yet it’s contents are nearly unreadable. It appears suddenly when gifted to another creature whenever it is tossed away, being a burden to be passed along and only by doing so can you ever get rid of it.

You are automatically Attuned to this item when picking it up if there was no previous creature who was attuned to it or when it is gifted to you by another creature, an unease washing over you as the object always teleports within 5-ft of you if further than that as soon as it is out of your view, appearing as a sudden weight in your bags, clothes or upon your feet. It emanates a sense of unease, with the thoughts of a predetermined destiny washing over you, making you suffer a -1 negative modifier to Wisdom saving throws and skill checks, but having a spell encroach on your body to make sure you will carry out it’s uncertain words, making it so you always heal by an additional die when you would recover hit points, or an additional {@dice 1d8} if you wouldn’t need to roll a dice to do so.

item.name: Little Book of Vengeance
entries: Prerequisites: Be part of the Middle through a Subclass, Background or Feat.

This Book of Vengeance is awarded to all Little Brothers and Sisters of the Middle, and is connected to all other Books of Vengeance of the organization. Anything that is written in the book is shared among all Books of Vengeance, and no matter its size, it manages to magically contain every single page of vengeance. You can read its contents as a free action, and your DM will let you know whether there is any mission currently available for you to undertake and exact vengeance for the Middle.

Additionally, you can write down someone's name on the Book of Vengeance, and any other person that carries a Book of Vengeance will be able to read it and hunt that creature to earn the rewards below.
When you complete a quest from the Little Book of Vengeance, you gain the following benefits:

items: Until the next long rest, with every attack that you hit, you deal {@damage 1d4} extra damage of the same type as the attack.
Until the next long rest, you gain advantage on an ability check of your choice.

item.name: Little Harbinger Bird

entries: "The bird fights its way out of the egg. The egg is the world. Whoever will be born must destroy a world."

A tiny round bird that could fit in your hand. Its feathers are umbral in pigmentation, devouring light as if the world itself was temporarily erased in its space - Despite that, it has bright white dots for eyes that calmly peer into others' souls. This bird will herald the dawn of change wherever it goes.

entries.name: Canary in the Coalmine
entries: The Bird acts a Familiar linked to you as per the {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiar} spell, using the {@creature eagle|MM|Eagle} stat block, except it is Tiny and has an amount of Hit Points equal to 10 times your level. You also cannot see or hear through its senses, but it is able to reliably use a bunch of chirps, cute gestures and a psychic connection to perfectly convey what it saw to you when necessary. If killed or if it has missing hit points, the Bird can be brought back or be healed through a ritual you may perform over the course of 10 minutes or a short or long rest; Once hatched, a fledgling of apocalypse can hardly be forever stopped.

entries.name: The First Trumpet
entries: The Harbinger Bird is attentive, realizing details as small as itself with ease, and its makes use of its shockingly strident singing to echo out alarm when danger approaches. The Bird always knows whenever a creature with hostile intent enters a 120-ft. area of yourself or prepares to deliver a particularly powerful attack on their next turn, such as a Dragon's Breath weapon. It does so by chirping a song that can be heard by creatures within 30-ft. of you or, if you order it to be sneaky about it, by pecking you softly at a rhythm.

entries.name: Wade Through the Worlds
entries: Once per long rest you may order the bird to step through the worlds of darkness and light as a Bonus Action. When you do so, choose between Dark and Light:

items: {@b Wade to Darkness.} The bird distorts a 60-ft. radius around you, extending the pure blackness of its body to cover it as per the effects of the {@spell darkness|PHB|Darkness} spell, except it does not require Concentration and you may end it as a Free Action and you plus a number of creatures of your choice can see through this magical darkness.

{@b Wade to Light.} The bird's eyes flash and dispels all illusions, reveals all {@condition Invisible} creatures and repels all magical darkness within a 30-ft. radius around you, establishing order once again for you to benefit from.

item.name: Little Wings
entries: A cloth patch of a pair of small wings with a pale blue color that can easily be sewn into clothes. Rumours say it was made by a small child with sorcerous abilities who simply wanted to rid the world of evil, so they ran as much as they could to work on that dream, despite their little legs. To attune to this item, you must sew it into a piece of clothing you are wearing.

Fluttering Wings Once per long rest, you may tap the patch as a bonus action to activate it. While active, tiny spectral wings hover over your shoulder and you gain a fly speed equal to your walking speed for one minute. You cannot, however, stay afloat in air, as your wings are to weak to fully carry you.
You fall 10-feet per round spent in the air. Additionally, if the Wings are inactive and you would take fall damage, they activate by themselves to negate that damage, even if they were used before.

item.name: Lockdown Solution
entries: A small leather sack thats been treated to specially hold a liquid that sticks exceptionally well against any surface pressed against it, acting as a superglue of untold proportions. You may spend an action to apply it to an opening or surface you can see, such as a door, chest or even the floor, covering at maximum a 10-ft by 10-ft opening or being able to be spluttered atop 5-ft. of empty space. This solution dries quickly, making it so a DC 18 Strength Saving Throw is needed to pry anything open from the Lockdown Solution, such as breaking down a door or even lifting your boots out of ground covered in the liquid. If it was used to reinforce an already enclosed opening that would require a DC to open, that DC increases by +5.
A sack of Lockdown Solution can only withstand one use, as any leftover glue quickly hardens when first exposed to air.
Additionally it instantly is dissolved by Universal Solvent.

item.name: Logging Axe
entries: An ancient and bloody axe that belonged to a berserking woodsman. When it used to fell trees, everyone nearby was able to hear it and run from the mad man.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While attuned to this weapon, you have the Siege Monster ability. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 6 counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} if they don’t have any. If you hit a creature suffering from counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you may cause a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Objectified Destruction
entries: Once per turn, when you hit an object or a structure with this weapon, every creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or either suffer 6 counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, your choice.

item.name: Love Cannon
entries: This cannon is made out of a dark pink glass-like material, a melted down collection of oozes that have solidified into a seethrough barrel capable of congealing any feelings of affection and passion around its vicinity into gruesome slime bombs.
