You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you would deal a Critical Hit while using this Cannon, the explosion’s impact splashes over and instantly hits all creatures within 5-ft of the original target, dealing the weapons damage without doubling it.

entries.name: Alternative Love Languages
entries: You may cast the {@spell Charm Person}, {@spell Calm Emotions}, {@spell Tongues} and {@spell Dominate Person} spells each without spending a spell slot once per long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for these spells.

entries.name: Lovely Little Clumps
entries: Whenever a creature suffers damage from this Cannon, they also suffer one count of Adoration. A creature with Adoration suffers a reduction to their movement speed equal to 5-ft. per count and a -1 negative modifier imposed to their Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to their Adoration count. Upon reaching 4 Adoration count the creature must pass a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition Charmed}, or have all Adoration counts removed instantly on a success, becoming immune to gaining any until the end of their next turn. Adoration count is otherwise reduced to zero when a creature suffering from it is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or when combat ends. The maximum Adoration count a creature may have is equal to your proficient bonus.

entries.name: Overtaking Consumption
entries: If a creature suffers damage caused by the Love Cannon and they are immune to the {@condition Charmed} condition, they lose that Immunity until the start of their next turn. Furthermore you deal an additional d6 of acid damage per Adoration count the target is suffering, also dealing d8s instead of d6 against a target suffering from 4 or greater Adoration count.

item.name: Lucky Umbrella
entries: An unique umbrella that resembles a four leaf clover.

Legends say that this item was blessed by the fae themselves, passed hand to hand to weather through all kinds of bad weather with sheer luck, always finding a sunny spot no matter what thunderstorm might befall those underneath.

This item grants you a +3 bonus modifier to Wisdom and Charisma Saving Throws, alongside providing immunity to any Wilderness Hazard effects with any harm that might befall you magically being turned away, such as an avalanche hitting a rock and sliding away from the precise spot you are in.

While attuned, you may chose to add or remove 20 from any d100 roll. Additionally, whenever you would roll a Critical Failure on a skill check or attack roll, you may choose to make your next attack roll or skill check be considered a Critical Success as if you had rolled a 20. For these effects to be active you must hold the umbrella in one hand.

item.name: Lureberries
entries: A green berry that always emits a vibrant light when its squeezed. Seems incredibly appetizing and its hard to control the urge to simply eat it. These berries can have many uses depending on who gets their hands on them, even more-so for adventurers.

As such, it may be sold for 100 GP per berry, or used for one of the following concotions: Lureblade Oil. By grinding a berry to a fine paste, you may coat the liquid on a weapon as a bonus action. For the next ten minutes, you may use your bonus action to raise the blade and shake it, causing the liquid to shine in a bright light.

Any creature besides you must pass a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Blinded||blinded} and {@condition Deafened||deafened} until the end of their next turn, as they can only focus on the bright light. Creatures who have resisted against or suffered the effects from Lureberries have advantage against this check. Lying Flytrap Phial.

During a long rest, you may use a Lureberry and 20 GP in other ingredients to brew them into a potion called the Lying Flytrap Phial. To do so, you must be proficient in Alchemist's Supplies and have a set for use. When consumed, this potion grants its consumer the effects of heightened resistance to any sort of enchantment, for the next ten minutes they have advantage against any Charisma saving throws and to resist Enchantment spells.

item.name: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as an extra {@damage 2d6} Fire damage. You also gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Scorching Hot
entries: You gain Immunity to Fire damage.

entries.name: Armor of the Fire Giant
entries: As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. Additionally, whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll, they take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Melt Away and Die
entries: On a Critical Hit with this weapon, the target creature's skin blackens like charcoal, their veins glowing orange like lava. For the next minute, they suffer a {@dice 1d8} penalty on all ability checks and saving throws. If you score another Critical hit against the same creature, no matter when, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be immediately killed, their body melting away into nothing.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 20-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain filled with molten lava. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 8d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects. Any creature other than you that enters the area for the first time on their turn or starts their turn within the area immediately takes {@damage 1d6} Fire damage.

entries.name: Burn Through Any Opposition
entries: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical flammable object with this sword and cause it to ignite. If the object isn't being worn or carried, it is reduced to ash at the end of your turn. Additionally, as an action, you can touch a nonmagical wall, floor, or similar structure and melt a 5-foot cube of it, provided the material can be melted by heat.

item.name: Machine Coil

entries: "You will one day remember us and miss us. You will miss our world where no one can hurt or be hurt by anyone."

The coil is a wondrous machine created for the sake of maintaining the power of the world, granting electricity to its veins so it could live on. That goal, however, has been warped by the idea of a head who decided this power needed to be fed through any means necessary.
Whenever you attack using this weapon a powerful wave of electromagnetic static is emitted from the Coil, causing bursts of lightning to form around your targets.

entries.name: Repudiation
entries: Whenever you target a creature to attack using the Coil you may spend 3 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to ensure the repression of those who would dare defy order. When you do so, the target suffers an additional damage die on a hit and they have Disadvantage on their next attack roll. This effect can stack into multiple attack rolls.

entries.name: Float
entries: While you are Attuned to this weapon you may make use of it without the need of your hands, having it float idly around the height of your shoulders, being kept within your peripheral view and moving alongside you. You cannot benefit from this while you are {@condition Blinded|PHB}.
Catalyst (Artificer, Bard).

entries.name: Catalyst
entries: A weapon with the Catalyst Property was specially made for the purpose of channelling spells, often bearing their own engraved forms of spell craft. A weapon with this property does not use Strength for its attack modifier, instead making use of the spellcasting ability of the Class(es) shown in parenthesis next to this property. It also uses that classes Spell Save DC if required. The displayed classes automatically have Proficiency with the weapon, even if they wouldn't usually. These also count as spell foci for them.

item.name: Magical Maestro's Baton
entries: An ivory baton emblazoned with onyx engravings that resemble various partitions. Its base presents an opal which functions as a conduit for bardic magic, guiding and shaping it along in many unsuspected forms of play.

While attuned to this magic item, if you do not have any other increase to your Spell Attack modifier or Spell Save DC that comes from another magic item, such as a +3 focus, you gain a +3 to your Spell Attack Modifier and Spell Save DC. The Magical Maestro's Baton can hold up to 6 charges, restoring 1 spent charge after a short rest and 2 spent charges after a long rest. You may spend charges to shape your Bard spells as if you were spending Sorcery Points toward {@classFeature Metamagic|Sorcerer|PHB|3} known, as follows:

rows: {@optfeature Careful Spell|PHB}
{@optfeature Distant Spell|PHB}
{@optfeature Empowered Spell|PHB}
{@optfeature Extended Spell|PHB}
{@optfeature Quickened Spell|PHB}
{@optfeature Seeking Spell|TCE}

item.name: Manatek Charger
entries: A round contraption thats painted in a smooth white finishing. It passively has lightning arch around it when fully charged, and may be used for a boost on ranged weapons by simply attaching it near the ammunition's shooting method. During a long rest, you may attach the Charger onto a ranged weapon, while attached, the weapon ignores the loading condition and needs no ammunition, as the Charger generates ammunition made of pure arcana.

Once per day you may spend your action to do have the Charger create copies of the ammunition fired from your weapon, acting as a volley. When you take this action, you may choose to target up to three creatures on your next attack and then attack with your attached weapon. If special ammunition was used for this, it retains its properties.

item.name: Mask of Teething Maws
entries: This black, metalic facemask covers the bottom of nose, the mouth and both cheeks in a giant row of teeth that when attuned, fuses to the wearer's face, leading to their stomach when opened. While attuned to this item, you feel a constant peckishness about you, and you may actively indulge in that desire for food with a natural Bite attack you gain. You are proficient with this bite attack, it is considered a melee attack which deals {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and you are healed by half the damage dealt after a hit using it, as you tear off and consume part of a targets flesh.

You do not heal from undead and construct creatures. As an action during your turn, you may gorge yourself on a dead body of a creature of Medium or Large size within 5- feet of yourself. When you do so, you rapidly consume it as a whole, recovering {@damage 3d8+4} hit points, with a bonus {@damage 2d8+2} hit points if it was a large creature.

This item has 3 stages of power, and it is natively in its 1st stage. It evolves or dissolves into another stage as the value of SMILE reaches certain numbers. SMILE is a counter for each dead body consumed using the Mask of Teething Maws, of which you gain 1 point when you consume a dead body, and lose 1 point for each week you go without consuming a dead body.

STAGE I. You feel a ravenous hunger at most times, yet can barely push back from the urge to bite down the first thing you can see. If suffer from a negative modifier to all your rolls equal to the amount of negative SMILE points you have, if you haven't eaten.
STAGE II. Hunger's need turns to desire, gluttonous joy. Your Bite natural attack grows in strength, gaining a +1 to hit and for its damage roll, also now dealing {@damage 2d8} piercing damage.
Additionally, your movement speed is increased by 10-feet. You reach STAGE II with 4 SMILE points. STAGE III.

The elation from consumption of another's being is unbearable. Your Bite attack changes once more, becoming disjointed and destructive, you have a +2 to hit and a +3 to damage rolls using it, alongside dealing {@damage 3d8} piercing damage. Aditionally, your movement speed is increased by 20- feet, and once per day you may cast the Sickening Sludge spell without spending a spell slot.

You can cast it more times by spending 2 SMILE points. You also may spend 1 SMILE point to gain an additional 5-feet to your movement speed until the end of your turn or spend the same value for a +1 for your attacks hit and damage modifier, also for the same duration. You reach STAGE III with 10 SMILE points.

item.name: Mask of the Parade's Prince/Princess
entries: A simple carnival mask made out of linens and metals. It has a deep fragrance of fresh blood when close to the face, and is said to have belonged to the single most beautiful vampire in the world. While Attuned, your Charisma becomes 23 if it was lower and you have Advantage on {@skill Persuasion} Saving Throws as the Mask's allure hides any undesirable traits of your body and makes all other beauty make itself known.

item.name: Masterless Polterportrait
entries: Wondrous Pet

A portrait of someone or something else that has taken a life of it’s own in living memory of someone who once cherished it. It cannot speak, but the image etched upon its frame moves and expresses outward emotion with ease, with perople depicted changing their faces in unison and even houses coming to have the effect of it’s windows becoming eyes and a door a mouth.
While attuned to the Polterportrait, it aids your recollection of previous events, granting you Advantage in any skill checks to remember something you might have forgotten.
Furthermore, its attentive manners have it so you have Advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Investigation} checks to find traps.

While in combat, the Polterportrait hovers around you in a haunting manner, and at the start of your turn you may direct it to face a creature as a free action, instantly inflicting 2 Sinking on that target.

item.name: Mediocre Bayonet
entries: Attachment, Simple Firearms (Under-Barrel)
You might as well have grabbed a chunk of sharpened scrap metal and called it a day.

While Attached, your weapon may also be used for melee weapon attacks at a reach of 5-ft. It deals {@damage 1d4} slashing damage on a hit and you may choose to use half your Dexterity modifier for rolls pertaining to this weapon instead of Strength.
You may Attach a Dagger to a weapon and have the same benefits as a Mediocre Bayonet.

item.name: Melted Eyeball
entries: A blue-tinted eyeball that was preserved not only in it’s freshness, but also in a deep sadness inside. You may spend a Free Action on your turn to consume the Melted Eyeball, popping it within your teeth to cause a distinct taste of a home you have never known yet still abandoned you to wash over your tongue, emanating through your body and soul.

After consumption, you deal an additional 3 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on your next hit, triggering {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instantly afterward. When you trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} from this effect, the deep sadness within you is tranfered to the target, causing them to suffer a negative modifier to attack rolls equal to your Proficiency Modifier until the start of your next turn. Furthermore, whenever a creature suffers damage for the duration they suffer 1 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

item.name: Mounted Flamethrower
entries: Attachment, Martial Firearms (Under-Barrel)
A machination holding a fairly well secured gas canister with a spewing mechanism and lighter, serving well as a live-target-lighter in bursts.

While attached, you may replace one of your attacks as per part of the Attack Action with a spouting of flame. When you do so, the fire covers a 15-ft. cone in a direction of your choice, forcing all creatures inside to pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@damage 3d4} fire damage and 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, or half of both on a success.
You may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per long rest, also being able to restore one use over a short rest.

item.name: Nebulizer of Endless Smoke
entries: A small device that is meant to have breath drawn from, yet instead of oxygen all it contains is an endless amount of smoke, easily filling one’s lungs when using it.

As a Bonus Action during your turn to spend a charge and inhale from the Nebulizer, being forced to pass a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or suffering disadvantage on Dexterity and Constitution saving throws until the start of your next turn, as you have a coughing fit. On a success you gain 6 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and this smoke spreads around you, granting 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to all creatures of your choice within 10-ft. of you. This item holds 3 charges that are restored during a long rest.
While attuned to this item, you have Advantage on its Constitution saving throw, or automatically succeed it if you have at Constitution score of at least 22.
Something is breathing heavily. The source of it, its form strange, lay there.
It appears to be an Abnormality. The thing is struggling to even breathe—its every breath is laborious and irregular.
Is it... crying?

item.name: Necklace of a Headless Portrait
entries: An iron chain holoding up a small oval portrait of someone whose face has been eroded and scratched away as if it never was. It is nearly always cold and when opened usually sends a chill upon those who peer into its contents.

While Attuned, whenever you Critically Hit a creature with an attack you cause that creature to become {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, with them being able to attempt a Wisdom saving throw to end the Condition early at the end of their turns. The DC for this is 10 + Your Melee or Spell Attack Modifier. You may also spend your Reaction when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points to flash the Necklace to another creature who can see within 60-ft, forcing the creature to attempt the same Saving Throw.
Furthermore, whenever you would start your turn all hostile {@condition Frightened} creatures within a 60-ft of you suffer 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

item.name: Nettleburst Joint
entries: A deceptively thin bundle of special herbs and narcotic spikes that were crushed and rolled up into thin paper, resembling a long spike. When consumed, you feel a burst of flavours hitting your mouth constantly and gain an natural charisma to bolster, becoming more joyful and relaxing to better act in any social situation. You gain a +1 bonus to Charisma rolls for the next minute, also gaining {@dice 2d4} temporary hit points from the ephemeral courage that washes over you.

If you inhale more than one Nettleburst Joint before a long rest, you must pass a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or become increasingly addicted to it, suffering one point of {@condition Exhaustion} after each long rest you spend without taking a Nettleburst Joint, for an amount of long rests equal to the amount of times you had to roll this Wisdom saving throw.
This DC increases by 2 every time you succeed a saving throw until you become addicted, resetting to 14 afterward.

item.name: Orb of Tired Hopes
entries: A large marble that could be clutched in one’s hand and cold to the touch. It is adorned with stattuetes of twin geckos whose spine juts out like a puzzle piece, their eyes hollowed and unthinking. It controls fate while refusing to be controlled itself, abhorring those who want and welcoming those who simply get by with no hope.
You can use this orb as an Arcane Focus for any spells, and you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your wizard spells.

entries.name: Austere Request
entries: As a Reaction when you would cast a spell, you may chose to raise the Orb of Tired Hopes and channel it’s power to embolden your spell at the risk of the orb rejecting you. When you do so, roll a d100 with the following effects varying on the result:

rows: Your spell is upcast as if you were using a 9th-level spell slot. If you were already casting a 9th level spell, you do not spend it’s spell slot.
Your spell is greatly heightened, being cast as if you had spent two spell slot levels higher.
Your spell is heightened, being cast as if you had spent one spell slot level higher, such as a 1st-level spell being upcast as if you spent a 2nd-level spell.
Your spell is unaltered.

Your spell is weakened or otherwise dispersed, causing it to be cast at one level lower than you did, if possible, or otherwise causing the spell to be cancelled yet you do not consume the spell slot spent to do so.
The spell flickers out of existence like a star turning to dust. You still lose the spell slot spent for casting this spell.

entries: You must know at least one spell of the level you upcast to with this effect, with nothing changing if you do not. The only exception to this is the effect for rolling a 1. If you have succesfully passed a Wisdom, Intelligence or Charisma saving throw a flicker of hope and intent is lit in your heart, having you suffer Disadvantage on this d100 until the end of your next turn.

item.name: Pale Dagger
entries: This pale dagger seems meek and brittle, yet it will never break. When it senses its wielder taking particularly grievous wounds, its blade turns a deep red and seeks punishment.

When a creature scores a critical hit against you, you can use your reaction to make an attack against that creature with advantage. If the attack hits, it is considered a critical hit and deals an additional {@damage 4d4} piercing damage.

item.name: Pale Homecoming
entries: An ivory colored pistol with ornate black engravings at its sides. Holding it makes you feel at peace with yourself, yet when held alone the weapon also emits a sense of loneliness.

This Weapon has its own ammunition that is created magically when you reload, which you can do as a bonus action. Reloading this way grants you 12 bullets for both Homecoming and Departrure. You have a +2 to attack and damage rolls using this weapon, in addition to the following:

entries.name: TwinWings.
entries: This weapon's properties shown below are only active if you are attuned to both Pale Homecoming and Departure in the Shade. In addition to those abilities, while attuned to both any damage you deal with this weapon also counts as necrotic damage for the purposes of overcoming resistance and vulnerability.

entries.name: Shimmering Light.
entries: As part of your Attack action, you may spend charges to switch one of your attacks to instead shoot a friendly creature within reach.
This shot does not deal damage, instead healing them for an amount of {@dice 1d6+1} for each 2 charges spent.

entries.name: Fear Not Death.
entries: As a reaction to when a creature within 30-feet of you becomes {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed}, you may spend 4 charges and 6 ammunition to offload a hail of magical bullets that restore their mental state, ending the condition instantly.

item.name: Paradise Lost
entries: A ceptre made from materials unfathomable to mere mortals. It resembles a limb carved out from an angels wing, entwined with the intestines of divinity itself. A red orb stands at its end, radiating holy power.

While attuned to this item, your spells gain a +3 modifier to hit and your Spell Saving Throw DC is increased by 3, in addition, this item can hold up to 20 charges. You gain one charge each time you deal a cumulative 20 points of damage through spells cast using Paradise Lost, also gaining one charge when healing {@condition Unconscious||unconscious} creatures and 3 charges when reviving dead creatures. You may spend your charges to perform the following miracles: Minor Miracle of Life.

As an action, you point Paradise Lost at a creature within 60-feet of yourself and spend any number of charges to heal them for an amount of d4+1 hit points per charge spent. Minor Miracle of Pain. As an action, you point Paradise Lost at a hostile creature within 60-feet of yourself and spend any number of charges to deal an amount of d6+1 necrotic damage per charge spent.

Miracle of Semi-Omnipresence. You may spend 5 charges to cast the {@spell Step Through Heaven's Door|TheUndertomesASF} spell without spending a spell slot. When cast like this, if you do so within the next minute, spend 2 charges to cast the spell again and being teleported to your original space, or the nearest unnocupied space.
Punishment of the Bad Apple. You may spend 15 charges to cast the {@spell Paradisiac Rapture|TheUndertomesASF} spell without spending spell slots. Punishment of Debauchery.

You spend 15 charges to cast the {@spell Fear of God [Cleric Only]|TheUndertomesASF|Fear of God} spell without spending a spell slot. When cast this way, all sources of damage caused by this spell deal an additional two dice of damage. Greater Miracle of God's Love.

As a bonus action during your turn, you may spend a number of charges to restore a spell slot whose level equals half the charges spent, to a maximum of spending 10 charges to regain a 5th level spell slot. When you do this, you may choose to regain multiple uses of the same level of spell slot, such as spending 12 charges to regain three 3rd level spell slots. Whenever you do this, you feel your devotion deepen greatly.

item.name: Pendant of the First Drop
entries: This golden necklace contains the rumoured first drop of blood ever shed by a First Kindred, crystalized and engraved in their grand visage. While Attuned, you gain a bonus +1 modifier to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws for every 5 Bloodfeast you have consumed to fuel an ability until the start of your next turn, to a maximum bonus modifier of +4.

item.name: Phantom of Present Time
entries: Wondrous Pet

A dark, shadowy figure that’s vaguely humanoid and wields a distinct scythe made of the same shadow. It has large, expressive emerald eyes that try to contain themselves into only serious expressions.

While attuned to the Phantom, it floats around your shoulders and enters into walls whenever there is combat, silently watching over you. It does not speak, only going through grumbling whispers and has the mannerisms of a cranky old man. It grasps to the passage of your time, making it so you don’t willingly age ever since attuning to it and have Advantage against any effects that would cause you to be aged or de-aged.

entries.name: Whispers of Time
entries: The Phantom whispers the secrets of foregone times into your ears, although you might not always grasp them. You have advantage and a +2 bonus modifier to all History rolls, gaining the same bonus to any rolls pertaining to the past of a subject, such as Religion, Arcana or Nature. Furthermore, it can embody the essence of another creature’s past after a long rest spent with them, allowing to choose one of their Attribute Scores to store after that long rest. You may spend your Bonus Action to switch your Attribute Score with the stored one, such as storing a Bard’s Charisma and gaining it for the next minute, where it reverts afterward. The other creature is unnafected besides having dreams of their past if they were sleeping while the Phantom was learning of their story.

item.name: Pincushion of Exploding
entries: An unassuming pincushion of a red, velvety color. It is packed to the brim with various used pins, often being used as makeshift weapons by barbers. You may prime the Charge as an Action, throwing it to a point within 30-ft of you, exploding in a hail of pins when it hits a surface and forcing all creatures within 10-ft of it to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@damage 4d4} piercing damage and 4 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count, or half of both on a success. The DC for this Saving Throw is 14 + your Dexterity Modifier, or your Artificer Spell Save DC if applicable.

item.name: Pink Bouquet
entries: A magical bouquet of flowers empowered by the energy of a Domain of Pleasure's Spring season. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a ranged attack, you deal an additional 5 ({@damage 1d10}) piercing damage until the end of your next turn. Whenever you knock a hostile creature unconscious with a ranged attack, you gain an additional 10 feet of movement for 1 minute.

Additionally, whenever a friendly creature within 30 feet of you inflicts counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature, that creature also suffers 1 count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesDA} the creature is already Sinking they suffer an additional count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesDA} and 1 count of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
At the start of your turn, choose a creature within 30 feet of you that is Sinking, they lose 10 feet of movement until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Spring's Genesis
entries: As an Action, all terrain within a 100-foot radius centered on you becomes fertile, and immediately grows patches of grass and pink flowers. If there were already seeds planted on the ground, they germinate immediately and yield fruits.

If you do this in an area already taken over by nature, the plants grow beyond their natural abilities and the area becomes thick and overgrown with plant life, turning into difficult terrain. Any ice or snow present within the area immediately thaws and melts, and any fire burning outside of a container is extinguished.
Once you use this ability, you can only do so again after the next dawn.

item.name: Pink Petals
entries: A vine covered in a bundle of pink petals that produce an aroma which brings with it feelings of melancholy and nostalgia. Whenever you would inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} inflict 1 count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesDA} as well. Inflict 1 additional count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesDA} if the creature already has 5 or more counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Pistol
entries: A simple firing mechanism that is easy to handle and to hide, if needed.

item.name: Plate Armor of Breathlessness
entries: This skeletal armor grants you theair you need to accomplish your tasks, but it is gone as soon as you believe yourself to be accomplishing anything on your own. At the start of your turn, if you have no counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you gain 4 counts of it.
Whenever you successfully perform a Posture Critical hit, however, your AC becomes your base AC, as if you were not wearing any armor.
The wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks.
If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 15, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

item.name: Plate Armor of Breathlessness (p. 54)
entries: A plate armor made out of the hardened shells of a gigantic mollusk, altough its joints don’t move too well because of a special glue the monster once produced. It fully protects against poisons, but makes moving inside it surprisingly difficult.
You gain Immunity to poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned} condition while attuned to this armor, also gianing Resistance against acid, and non-magical piercing and slashing damage.

Whenver you suffer damage from a melee attack you may spend your reaction to jut out the armor and let one of its plates burst into a horrible infected water, forcing the creature who damaged you to pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@condition Larva|TheUndertomesASV} count equal to the damage you’ve taken, to a maximum of 20. The DC for this saving throw is equal to 8 + your proficiency modifier + your Constitution modifier and you may use this reaction an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

item.name: Plate Armor of Unfeeling Steel
entries: An armor made out of thick, darkened metal plates.

Although cumbersome to wear, It is said that the one to wield it will never have any pain come to their heart ever again, not physical nor emotional, the plates too thick to allow anything to pass through.

While wearing and attuned to this armor, your movement speed is reduced by 10-ft. and you gain Immunity to the {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Frightened} Conditions, alongside gaining Resistance against psychic damage. If you do not take off this armor after donning for a month, you must pass a DC 18 Charisma saving throw or develop an {@spell Iron-Hearted Curse|TheUndertomesASV}, as per the eponymous spell. On a success you remain the same and feel a gnawing weight at your heart, reminding you to doff the armor as soon as possible. If another month passes without doffing the armor and becoming unnatuned, you must retry this saving throw.

item.name: Pleasure Bat
entries: This is a flowery green bat with red petals and thorns covering one end of it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon, and it deals an additional {@dice 2d8} radiant damage when it hits.
When you hit a creature with this weapon, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (save DC 14 + your charisma modifier or your own prefered spell/ability save dc)

or become {@condition charmed} for a minute and delight in being hit repeatedly, giving you advantage on attack rolls against them while they’re {@condition charmed} this way. They can reroll the saving throw at the end of their turns, ending the effect on a success. If they’re successful on the saving throw, they become immune to this effect for an hour.

item.name: Poet's Everbeating Heart
entries: A still beating heart of a prominent poet whose real name has blurred within the passing of time. It has been mutated through various arcane processes, growing a mouth and teeth that bite and latch onto you when Attuned. While Attuned, you become immune to the effects of a Vorpal weapon and gain Resistance to Psychic damage, as the heart constantly whispers tales to you. Whenever you start your turn within 15-ft of a {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creature, the heart beats faster, causing your blood to rush violently. When this happens, you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage of your weapon's damage type per {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creature within reach whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack, to a maximum bonus of {@dice 6d4}.

item.name: Potion of Lost Personhood
entries: A diamond-shaped vial of rose-tinted glass containing a nearly unseen liquid that does not permeate any non-living organic tissues it touches, sharing most properties closer to quicksilver than water. It smells of longing and tastes like the question that you will never have the chance to answer.

When consumed, all the hair in your body falls out, thick skin grows to cover your mouth, eyes and any other orifices and your whole body smoothes over until you become a featureless humanoid being of a pink-ish skin that tastes like plastic. Whenever you speak or project your voice through any means it is overlaid in a myriad of other voices and tones, making your own be lost and indistiguishable to any listener.

You retain your memories and can both see and speak despite the newfound growths on your body. yet cannot be transformed back to normal by any means other than the {@spell Wish} spell. Shape-changing effects like the {@spell True Polymorph} spell instantly fail against you, and so do any kind of location spells such {@spell Locate Creature}. Any wounds caused on you become obscured in a pure umbral tissue with clear water pouring out instead of blood. Your Charisma score becomes 2 and cannot be increased by any means.

item.name: Potion of Venomous Skin
entries: Brewing: 1.000 gp

This vial is full of a dark blue liquid that smells like sadness waiting to burst out and that causes one’s eyes to water. You may consume this vial with a Bonus Action, causing your skin to quickly grow blue bubbles in that store vibrations inside, bursting inside like a pop of air whenever you perform a quick movement, sending all that energy to your fingertips.
For the next minute you deal an additional 2 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack.
After this duration, your skin turns back to normal, with the bumps smoothing out quickly, yet the blue dots remaining for the next {@dice 2d12} hours.

item.name: Premium Brand Top Sib's Hair Gel
entries: A premium brand of hair gel that leaves you cool to the touch.

Whenever you hit a friendly creature using this item, you may choose to instead of chucking the bottle full force at their head, having it be a glorious splatter of gel onto their hair. When you do so, you deal no damage and the creature gain a +1 to their Charisma modifier until the end of their next turn.

item.name: Primal Claws of Scarring
entries: A pair of gauntlets made out of cobalt, their blue hue gleams against moonglight, and the fingertips end in claws sharp enough to rival most greatswords. You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and additionally you gain the following bonus action: Cobalt Scar. After spending your bonus action during your turn, you may choose to pounce on any creature that is below its maximum hit points as long as it is within a 30-foot radius of yourself.

item.name: Prolific Pauldrons Potion
entries: A round bottle containing a dirty, grimy solution. It’s cork is marked with the letter “P” that’s been crossed out. This potion used to be consumed often by soldiers who tried to modify their bodies for an advantage at war and has nearly never seen the light of day again after such fateful days.
When consumed as an action you can naturally extend your arms to reach much further than usually possible, gaining a reach of 20-ft. to all melee weapon attacks for one minute.

item.name: Prosthetic Tongue
entries: A replacement tongue with functional taste buds. Hopefully this replacement will keep you from speaking out of line.

While having this Tongue be a part of your body, you can willingly turn off your taste buds, granting you Advantage against Constitution saving throws regarding being unable to consume something with horrible taste or enduring that process without throwing up.
You may have only an amount of tongues your race usually has at any given time. To install it you go through the same process as Attuning to a magic item, but it does not count toward your total.

item.name: Ravenous Clipped Wings
entries: A pair of bladed tonfas that curve inwards, resembling wings in the middle of beating. Both of them emit the constant smell of iron, and its wielders often report feeling a greater appetite. The weight of each tonfa belies their sleek design.

This weapon is considered to have a +1 to your attack and damage modifiers, in addition, whenever you score a critical hit against a creature while using the Ravenous Clipped Wings, you heal for half the damage dealt. Additionally, when you take the attack action, you may spend one charge to perform a Ravenous Wingbeat attack. Ravenous Wingbeat.

You deliver a violent attack onto a victim, draining them of their nutrients and absorbing all of them into yourself. Perform a melee weapon attack against any target within your reach, on a hit, you heal for half of the damage dealt. You may then spend any further attacks you would have had to automatically hit the same target, shering into their flesh with the Wings toothed blades, dealing a further {@damage 1d4} slashing damage and healing for that damage dealt.
This weapon has 3 charges, and you regain all uses on a long rest, additionally it recovers one charge every time you'd gain a point of exhaustion because of starvation.

item.name: Reasonable Decanter of (Near) Endless Joe
entries: A marvel of technology and the arcane , this thermal bottle can produce and hold endless coffee of at least reasonable quality. It also comes with a detachable cap that works as a mug and with a set of coffee brewing tools - a grain grinder, a scale, kettle and a timer. Its bottom compartment also works as a concealable storage for coffee grains with easy-use separators.

This item needs some time to recharge since it disallows one from drinking stale coffee, having 6 charges that are recovered during a long rest. A creature holding the Decanter may spend a Bonus Action to pour and drink from the Decanter or a nearby container they have poured into, granting the effects of the Blend contained within. By default, this is only black coffee that aids in reinvigorating the body - having the imbiber ignore one of their Exhaustion Points until the start of their next long rest, counting as if they had one Exhaustion point less for the duration.

Over a long rest you may brew a new blend of coffee while the Decanter is emptied, then fill it with this fresh batch. It gains the properties from the Blend made, being able to have up to three Beans to benefit from at any given time. After a Bean is first used to make a Blend in the Decanter, it does not need to be supplied again to use that specific Bean in another Blend or refill.
The available Grains may vary, yet a baseline are:

items.name: Goodberry Beans
items.entry: Made from fusing the arcane components of the {@spell Goodberry} spell with Arabica grains, these make the Blend feel hearthy and wholesome, having the creature who imbibes it be considered as if they just had a full meal after drinking from the Decanter.

items.name: Heal-Heal Beans
items.entry: Created from a secret mix of specific coffee beans, unicorn tears and love from a pixie, these Beans make any Blend have a minty aftertaste and causes the creature who imbibes it restore {@dice 2d6+2} Hit Points.

items.name: Neversleep Beans
items.entry: These are the blackest grain possible, tasting like a forbidden night of sleep. After drinking from the Decanter while these are added to the Blend, the creature cannot gain Exhaustion Points and has Advantage on saving throws against falling asleep for the next hour. If you drink from a Blend using this more than once before taking a short or long rest, you must attempt a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or have your body fall out of whack. You do not benefit from any restorative properties or positive effects of your next long rest, or any short rest until you take a long rest.

entries: These are usually available in packs at most magic item shops for a price ranging from 300-600 GP .

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: Feel free to talk to your DM about adding new Bean types for you to blend away, as these are only a sample selection! As for DMs, the availability of Beans depends on you, so if there are any you'd rather not deal with or that you'd like to make available through other means, feel free to get creative with it! Merry Blending!

item.name: Recollection of a Certain Day
entries: This is a small portrait depicting a scene that has happened some time ago, infused with everything from then - It bears the same smell as the ambient, when pressed close to an ear it’s chatter is revealed and when gazed at the very surroundings seem to morph into what once was.
The Portrait holds 3 Charges, which are restored during a Long Rest. This magic item may be used by spending your Action and a charge to do one of the following:

entries.name: Draw In Recollection
entries: You gaze into the portrait, letting yourself be embraced by the scenery and gaining a certain focus because of it, easily distinguishing all that is going on around you as if they were interlopers inside your household. You gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Furthermore, you gain a bonus to your Dexterity saving throws equal to half your {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, rounded down, to a maximum of +3. This effect lasts until you run out of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Entrap In Past
entries: You hold the portrait outward, showing it to a creature and forcing them to pass a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition Charmed} by you for the next minute, being able to retry this saving throw at the end of their subsequent turns. A creature {@condition Charmed} this way believes they are inside a room or scenery of your choice ( provided you have seen that scenery within your own eyes ), also suffering a -2 modifier to attack rolls for the effect’s duration.

item.name: Red Hunter's Hood
entries: A pair of a flowing crimson hood, blood-red in its color, and a metalic facemask with grafitti resembling the toothy grin of a predator. When attuned to this item, you feel constantly reminded of your grudges and the monsters that lurk around the world, unpunished. Once per long rest, you may declare a creature your quarry, your thoughts scarcely being able to leave the thought of the creature for the rest of the day.

You gain disadvantage to Intelligence skill checks unrelated to the creature, their place or region of residence and anything that wouldn't be pertinent to hunting this quarry. This lasts until your next long rest, yet you also gain a +2 to {@skill Perception}, {@skill Investigation} and {@skill Survival} rolls to locate or perceive your quarry, additionally can always know their location if you have inflicted the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} condition on them, as you see a red outline of their body if you are within a 300- feet radius of them. You also gain a +2 to hit this creature with weapon attacks, and gain the following bonus action, which you can also take as part of your attack action: Hunter's Advance.

You lunge at your target with eviscerating strikes, aimed right at their arteries. Until the end of your turn, your attacks deal 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on hit. You may use this bonus action a number of times equal to half your proficiency modifier, regaining expended uses on a long rest.

item.name: Red Spider Fang
entries: A ornate rapier that seems to be made from some sort of ebony metal. Its guard is like webbing held by six spider legs curling inwards toward the hand. Whenever a particularly vicious strike is dealt, its wielder can swear the legs move, and they feel the fleshy, wet feeling of a bright red eye opening on the hilt against their palm.

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, or a +2 instead against creatures that are below you on the initiative order by a difference of 3 or higher. In addition, whenever your roll to hit's result is a 16- 20 before any modifiers, you inflict one Paralyze on the target. Paralyze deducts an amount to the afflicted's initiative score equal to each stack of Paralyze is on a given creature.
All stacks are destroyed on the end of the afflicted's turn.

item.name: Requiem
entries: This is a magical weapon that adds +1 to your attack and damage rolls for each 3 points of {@condition Coffin|TheUndertomesOA} you have. Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with this weapon, you deal {@dice 1d6} additional psychic damage.

You can summon Requiem with a bonus action, and you automatically wield it. If you were already wielding a weapon, you stow it as a part of the same bonus action. Whenever Requiem is summoned or as an action on your turn, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition Frightened} of you for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to Requiem's {@condition Frightened} condition for the next 24 hours. Requiem may be wielded by its summoner as if ignoring the Heavy property, and only one of it may be summoned at any given time.

entries.name: Lament, Mourn and Despair.
entries: As an action, you may open Requiem and attempt to lock a creature inside it. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become stuck inside Requiem for 1 minute, being able to reroll the saving throw at the end of their turn. Whenever you attack a target, the creature inside Requiem takes {@dice 3d6} piercing damage as it's punctured by the spikes inside it. If it's killed that way, you gain 3 stacks of {@condition Coffin|TheUndertomesOA} instead of one. You may only attempt to lock a creature of Large size or smaller with this feature and Large creatures have advantage on this saving throw.

item.name: Respectable Bayonet
entries: Attachment, Martial Firearms (Under-Barrel)
Designed with a sleek "snap-on" mechanism that remains affixed no matter how fast the weapon is swung, this is a decent blade for anyone who wishes to be a fighter at any range.

While Attached, your weapon may also be used for melee weapon attacks at a reach of 5-ft. It deals {@damage 1d6} slashing damage on a hit and has the Finesse property. Whenever you hit a creature with this weapon you may spend your Reaction to move up to 10-ft. backward. Attack rolls provoked by this movement are made at Disadvantage.

item.name: Robes of a Priest who Wished to Cure Sin
entries: These robes smell like a long forgotten summer dream. They are of a dark color, embroidered in the imagery of wings and feathers. If an evil-aligned creature attempts to attune to this item, the attunement fails as the Robes reject it.

While wearing this armor, your AC is 12 + your Dexterity modifier + 2. Additionally, you have the following traits: To Don Penance. Whenever you take 12 or more points of damage in one attack, you gain a +5 bonus to your Concentration checks as the pain keeps you even more focused on your goals.

Sticks and Stones. If you would take less than 10 damage in a single attack, lower that damage to 1 instead. This value is increased to reducing any damage below 24 if you are also attuned to Paradise Lost. ..

item.name: Robes of Entropic Balance
entries: This flowing open robe is inlaid with a refined bronze mixed with ruby dust to form the pattern of fish scales, with its cloth being soft to the touch yet surprisingly resistant, painted in a dark brown color. While wearing this item, your AC is 12 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier ( Max. 3 ). This item has 6 charges, and regains all expended ones at dawn.

As a reaction to when you would take damage or be targeted with a damaging spell effect, you may spend 2 charges to activate the latent ki powers embedded in the cloth. Redirect Despair. You suffer no damage nor effects from the source of this reaction, instead it is redirected into the flow of the universe.
You may choose to redirect the damage or spell to target one creature within 60-feet of yourself instead.

item.name: Ropes of Sentimentality
entries: A coil of dark-red ropes that smells like old blood, made from drenching it after a short period of extracting this material and letting it soak for hours on end. Just holding the ropes makes one feel a tug of pain in their heart.

You may spend your Action to tie these ropes onto an object or willing ( or {@condition Unconscious} ) creature, causing them to be {@condition Incapacitated} until freed through attempting to break free as a free action at the end of their turn, rolling an {@skill Athletics} Check at Disadvantage. The DC of this check is 20 minus the bound creature’s Wisdom Modifier minus the amount of rounds it has spent bound. Escaping this way makes it so the rope isn’t destoyed.

A creature bound this way is assaulted by feelings of loneliness no matter how many people they may be surrounded by and a gnawing desperation similar to that of sinking down a puddle and becoming unable to swim upward.

While bound, they suffer disadvantage on all Charisma, Intelligence and Wisdom Saving Throws as the deep sadness overtakes them at all waking hours. A bound creature also suffers a point of {@condition Exhaustion} per day bound, being unable to benefit from a Long Rest until freed.
The bonded creature may also be broken free through cutting the rope, which has 1 Hit Point and an AC of 8.

If this rope is cut or otherwise destroyed, all of its soaked blood sprays out in a screeching mist, forcing all creatures within 15-ft of it to attempt a Wisdom Saving Throw of the same DC as breaking free from it. On a failure, they take {@dice 6d8} psychic damage and suffer 2 points of {@condition Exhaustion} instantly, or half that damage and {@condition Exhaustion} on a success.

item.name: Royal Binds
entries: A piece of velvet ribbon that follows your every whim and command, created by drenching it in a rune-engraved basin holding it’s dye it flies and cracks around upon feeling it’s masters will.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. You may have the Vestigial Killer fly out of your hand and attempt to Grapple a hit creature as a Reaction to when you would damage it using the Killer, using your weapon attack or spell attack modifier instead of your strength modifier for this check. On a succesful Grapple check, the Vestigial Killer starts choking out the target. If it requires to breathe, it is knocked {@condition Unconscious} after it ends its turn while being {@condition Grappled} for an amount of turns equal to its Constitution modifier, to a minimum of 3, with the Vestigial Killer unlatching from the targets neck afterward.
You may spend a free action during your turn to call back the Killer, having it fly back and wrap around your wrist.

item.name: Royal Jelly Perfume
entries: A strange bottle of perfume made from an extract of monstrous bees. As a Bonus Action, you can spray yourself with the perfume bottle to gain {@condition Pheromone|TheUndertomesDA}, which lasts for 1 minute or until the end of combat if you enter one while it is still active. Whenever a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} enemy hits you, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d8}.

Additionally, at the end of your turn, the creature that dealt most damage to you during the last round suffers from {@condition Pheromone Mark|TheUndertomesDA} If no creature dealt damage to you, choose 1 hostile creature at random.

item.name: Ruins of a Fragmented Doomsday
entries: A small shard of a ruined temple that once was meant to hold the beacon to bring forth the end of all things. It still flickers with a tiny, nearly imperceivable flicker of that overwhelming power that could burn all that ever existed.

Many intricate runes are etched into the tiny pebble that is this item, and you may ativate them with an action, then throwing them to any space within 80-ft. When it hits a surface within that range, it raises into the air, shaking violently before emitting a great explosion of whirling flame and destruction, covering a 60-ft radius around the point where it landed. All creatures within range must pass a Constitution saving throw or suffer 8 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@dice 8d12} fire damage, or half that count and amount on a success.

Creatures on the 5-ft border of that radius may attempt to pass a Dexterity saving throw to jump off of the way altogether, taking no damage on a success but suffering 4 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and an additional {@dice 4d12} fire damage on a failure.

This saving throw DC is equal to 16 plus your Proficiency Bonus when you threw the stone and it’s damage ignores it’s targets resistance to fire damage and treats immunity to it as if it were only resistance. Any structure within range suffers double the damage rolled instead.
The shard is destroyed after it is used.

item.name: Rusty Iron Stake
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} property (16-20).
A grimy iron needle that has rusted over with dried blood over its length. It is unusually large, reaching the size of a rapier.

entries.name: Special: Pinned.
entries: When you hit a creature with this item, you may choose to stick it to their body. While stuck, any melee weapon attacks against the creature are considered to have the Hemorrhaging(16-20) weapon property and it may only be removed by the creature spending their Bonus Action to do so, also causing them to suffer {@damage 1d6} piercing damage and suffering 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count.

item.name: Sac à Main Joyeux
entries: A small handbag with a beautiful woven finish and a stomach that could swallow a kraken. Whenever you attack with this weapon, it supplies its own tendrils from the bag's mouth, spikes and teeth included!
This item counts as and has all the abilities of a {@item Bag of Holding|DMG} in addition of being a natural weapon you are proficient with.
You have a +3 modifier to attack and damage rolls while using this weapon and inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you deal damage using it.

Anything stored in the Sac à Main remain inside its extradimensional storage even if you swap it for another item, having the same continuous access thorough iterations of your work. Additionally, you may always be Attuned to items stashed inside it as to instantly benefit from their Attunement when they are pulled out, for up to an amount of items equal to half your proficiency bonus. These do not count toward your Attunement total.

entries.name: Noveau Mode
entries: Whenever you take a long rest you may unleash the inspiration gained from items you've devoured as per your Foi Affamée feature, creating a new magical item of your design that inherits all the traits of what you've absorbed. You must use a weapon, armor or item as a base, then losing any stored magical item properties and storing the newly made magic item into the Sac à Main. You may have up to half your proficiency bonus' worth of items stored in this way, needing to scrap one of them to make more upon reaching the limit. These items retain their properties for an hour after being pulled out of the bag, and must be stored during a long rest to regain them after falling inert.

entries.name: Revisiting Trends
entries: You may use a Free Action to stash and wield weapons or items stored in the Sac à Main. You may use this Free Action once to stash and once to wield something for each hand you have.

item.name: Salazen Atelier "Royal's Regalia" Tongue

entries: "Ah, yes! A favourite amongst our esteemed Thumb clientele! All of the Consigliere and Sottocapo's that actually manage to amass the reasonable dowry for such a marvellant prosthetic do declare that this invention is indubitably valuable to their person!"

Featuring inlaid golden details to sweeten the taste of your very own words, this esteemed product from Salazen Atelier's S-Class catalogue is sure to take you up and above all heights of the greater echelon no matter which region you carry your frabjous presence toward.

While having this Tongue be a part of your body, you can willingly turn off your taste buds, granting you Advantage against Constitution saving throws regarding being unable to consume something with horrible taste or enduring that process without throwing up. Additionally, you may have the sensory alteration to make any food you consume taste like the beamish gourmet meals that you so perfectly deserve. Whenever you do so over the course of a short or long rest and consume a Ration or similar food, you gain {@dice 1d8} Temporary Hit Points until your next long rest.

Furthermore your Charisma score increases by 6, for a maximum of 26 and this Tongue makes you exceptional at wordplay, diction and overall aids in being a better conversationalist, granting you Expertise in one Charisma skill of your choice and Proficiency in two others.

Finally, this Tongue is designed in such a way that it ingrains you with the instinctive itch to avoid overly offending others by accident, granting you advantage on Insight checks to perceive if saying something to another creature would provoke any sort of emotional outburst such as rage, panic or a bout of extreme depression.
You may have only an amount of tongues your race usually has at any given time.

item.name: Sanctified Canister
entries: A vial of holy water that has been primed and pressured to explode on hard contact with a surface. Instead of performing an attack with this weapon, you instead throw it to a space you can see within its thrown range, causing any creatures within a 10-ft radius of that point to perform a DC 15 + Your Dexterity Modifier Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer its damage. If thrown at a long range, this Saving Throw is performed at advantage.

item.name: Saw Guitar
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} property (18-20).

A fully metallic guitar featuring a buzzsaw as its base, rendering it useful in the act of both shredding a chord or shredding another creature to bits. Despite being in its lonesome, this guitar always sounds as if it were plugged to an amplifier.

While attuned, if you are proficient with any string instruments, you are considered proficient with the Saw Guitar. Additionally, you may choose for Charisma to be your main modifier using this weapon instead of Strength, it also counts as a bardic focus. You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it may hold up to 8 charges. You may spend them to use the abilities described below.

Charges are restored by {@dice 1d4+1} at dawn, or by 1 whenever your bardic inspiration is used by another creature. The abilities below have a range of a 30-feet radius with you as its center, and only willing creatures of your choice may be affected unless described as otherwise.

entries.name: Please work harder!
entries: You may spend your action and 3 charges to turn your playing into a resolute, low-tone solo, droning in the background of the fight.

Until the end of your next turn, all willing creatures listening to you feel an urge to push themselves to no end. They suffer a penalty of -2 AC, yet gain a +2 to hit with their attacks. Additionally, you gain a +1 bonus to your own AC per creature affected by this.

entries.name: Lets make music!
entries: As an action, you may spend 4 charge and start playing a frenetic solo, contagiating any willing creature so they give their maximum. Until the start of your next turn, all creatures affected by this deal a critical hit on one value less, such as a roll of 19 before any modifiers being considered a critical hit.
Additionally, affected all creatures deal an additional {@dice 1d8} dice of slashing damage.

entries.name: Harmony of Despair.
entries: When a friendly creature reduces a creature below one hit point within this weapons range, you may spend 6 charge and use your reaction to start harmonizing the sounds of tearing flesh with your guitar.

The creature downed automatically takes a hit as its flesh begins to be cut, as if the buzzsaw were on them, and all hostile creatures within reach must pass a Charisma Saving throw against your Spell Save DC or take {@dice 3d8} + your Charisma modifier in psychic damage, as the harmony cuts through their mind. If any creature would be knocked below one hit point by Harmony of Despair, the same creatures must repeat the Saving Throw, taking the same damage on failure. This repeats for a maximum of two times.

item.name: Scroll of Red Order
entries: A mysterious scroll blessed by a religious order that is yet to be uncovered, it seems to have been written with bloodied tears and empowers those that fight against the weak and the cowardly. The scroll of Red Order has 6 charges, and you can spend them with the following effects:

As a bonus action by spending 2 charges, you and all creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you deal an additional {@dice 1d8} dice of cold damage whenever you roll damage against a creature with {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If that creature dies, another creature of your choice within 10 feet of it must roll a Wisdom saving throw (save DC 15) or gain 3 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

As an action by spending 4 charges, you can summon a Swarm of Insects (Monster Manual 2014) on a space next to you. It is friendly to you and your allies and obeys all your commands to the best of its abilities. In combat, the swarm rolls its own initiative and acts on its own turn. When the swarm drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. While it is 100 feet of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. Additionally, as an action, you can see through the swarm’s eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of its Blindsight. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses.
The scroll of Red Order regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Sealed Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.
While attuned to it, you gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 10-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Time to Unpack!
entries: Upon reaching level 7 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item First Seal Removed: Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Second Seal Removed: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as {@damage 1d6} additional Fire damage. You also gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Armor of the Fire Giant
entries: As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. Additionally, whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll, they take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: The first time you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 20-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Burn Through Any Opposition
entries: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical flammable object with this sword and cause it to ignite. If the object isn't being worn or carried, it is reduced to ash at the end of your turn. Additionally, as an action, you can touch a nonmagical wall, floor, or similar structure and melt a 5-foot cube of it, provided the material can be melted by heat.

entries.name: Unsealed Phenomenon: Lævateinn
entries: Upon reaching level 15 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesVM}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Serrated Hand-axe
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} property (15-20).
A crude lead-made hand-axe with sharp points sawed off of its edge. These nearly pierce skin on simple touch.

item.name: Seven Bullets
entries: This rifle inlaid with blue accents reeks of faint traces of contractual magic. When you would be about to attune to this weapon, it speaks to you inside your head as if possessed, explaining its curse and asking if you do want to use its bullets.

If you say no, you become unable to attune to it for the next 24 hours, if you say yes, you become attuned to it. It does not ever speak again, yet those who plead for it to go away say that they can hear the rifle laughing. You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it also has the following effects:

entries.name: Magic Bullets.
entries: When you shoot with this weapon, a magic portal opens at its barrels end, turning a bullet into a line of destruction. When you target a creature, all other creatures in a line from it to you are caught in the bullets wake. When you roll to hit, your roll counts as if you were attacking all creatures in this path, dealing the weapons damage if it would hit their AC.

entries.name: Devil's Six.
entries: When you hit another creature with this weapon, its critical hit threshold is reduced by 5.

entries.name: Number of Divine Deliverance.
entries: Every time you shoot with this weapon, wether you hit or miss, add a +1 to a counter. After this counter reaches 7, the counter resets and Seven Bullets binds your fingers and arms in tight chains, spectral in their appearence and freezing to the touch. They manipulate you to take a shot aimed at your closest loved one, such as a spouse, best friend and so on.

This shot ignores range, instead automatically hitting any creature fitting that criteria as long as they are within a 3-mile radius. If there would be no creature that counts for this available in the area or otherwise, Seven Bullets targets you instead. The damage for this attack is doubled.

item.name: Shard from Beyond
entries: This spear seems to always change its shape slightly when looked at for a second time, as it still seeks its form much after it's left a forge. When attuned to, its wielder can feel the spear always trying to explore the back of its thoughts, so it may finally find what it wants to be.
While unformed, its black surface nearly seems like a child's scribbles, with crude little drawings detailing it. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Moment of Clarity.
entries: While attuned, if either your Intelligence or Wisdom scores are higher than 14, you may sometimes reach a special synchrony with the spear. Whenever you roll an 18 or higher to hit, before any modifiers, the spear coalesces into a more tangible form, becoming smoother and more well finished. It remains like that for a minute, and for the duration it deals {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and gives a +2 bonus to hit and to damage rolls instead of a +1.

item.name: Shard of Crystalized Blood
entries: A shard of crystalized blood, easily shatterable within one's hand. You may spend your Bonus Action to shatter the Shard under your palm, causing it to melt and meld into your body, instantly causing you to recover up to your {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count's worth of d4 + 1 hit points, to a maximum of {@dice 10d4 + 10} hit points. After doing so, your wounds close and heal, ending the Condition automatically.

item.name: Sharpshooter's Smoking Pipe
entries: An ornate smoking pipe made out of dark wood and blue engravings, it never seems to need any tabbacco, instead puffing out clouds of celestial smoke when puffed on, resembling the stars in the sky. When an attuned creature uses their bonus action to smoke from this pipe, they feel their heart feel colder, as if hugged by frost. They also learn instinctively the exact location of a creature of your choice that you have seen in your life.

You only know where they are at that given moment, yet if within your attack range, you gain advantage to hit this creature until the end of your turn after smoking. If you use this while attuned to Seven Bullets, its loses its range property, instead being able to be aimed at any target discovered from the pipe ignoring cover, as a magic portal appears near the target to fire at them.

item.name: Shelter of All Future Days
entries: This bronze greatshield might be the finest piece of work that has ever been made to protect another, despite it’s commonly found material every beating of a hammer on it’s surface was laced with the fear of more suffering come to pass, a desperation to create one last truly safe place on the world. What resulted was a masterwork of craftsmanship laced with a potent magic that came out of the very smith’s heart, uniting to and protecting it’s wielder until their last breath.
You gain a +3 bonus modifier to your Armor Class while attuned to this shield and unless your Strength score is 17 or greater you lose 10-ft. of movement while wielding it.

entries.name: Shelter
entries: While wielding the shield you may spend your bonus action to Hunker Down, dropping lower into the ground while hoisting your shield up high. While Hunkered Down your Movement Speed is halved and you cannot take the Dash action until you spend another bonus action to get back up, but you gain a further +2 bonus modifier to your Armor Class and may add the total (+5) bonus to AC gained from this Shield for Constitution and Dexterity saving throws. Because of your focus on holding the shield up attacking becomes much more cumbersome, causing you to suffer a -3 negative modifier to your attack rolls.

entries.name: Relief
entries: This Shield has 3 charges, restoring one per long rest.

You may spend one charge when Hunkering Down to grant yourself {@dice 3d8} temporary hit points while in that state, losing them when you go back to normal. You may also spend one charge to cast the {@spell Sanctuary} spell at a target within reach, or all three charges at once to cast the {@spell Perfected Sanctuary|TheUndertomesASV} spell instead.

entries.name: Respite
entries: While attuned to the shield the first half of hit die spent on a short rest to heal yourself are considered to be their maximum value, despite what was actually rolled. This value is rounded up.

item.name: Shimmering Star
entries: A large mace fashioned out of roots and a particularly hard apple that appears to be made out of pure gold. While pressing your hand against the cold head of the mace you can feel a warm wriggling inside.
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon.

entries.name: Beautiful Exterior, Harmful Interior
entries: You gain 2 Golden Sheen after taking a short rest while attuned to the Star, or 4 Golden Sheen after a long rest, to a maximum count of 5. Furthermore, when you run out of counts of this Condition, the apple atop the Shimmering Star breaks onto a mess of maggots and thorny roots, inflicting 2 Rotting Flesh on a hit with it until you regain the condition or become unnatuned to the Star.

item.name: Shotgun
entries: Tough and sturdy, this shotgun delivers a nasty blow to anything stupid enough to remain near it.

entries.name: Special.
entries: When fired, any creatures 5-feet around your target suffers half the damage dealt on a shot if the dice rolled to hit is higher than their AC, as the spread catches them.

item.name: Shrapnel Shot
entries: {@i 2nd-level Expanded Ammunition}

Various steel pellets are found within this bullet's shell, having a second ignition trigger after hitting a target and exploding to expand its field of effect. When used, you may choose a point within your Marksman Weapon's range, all creatures within a 5 * SL radius of the point must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer SL die of damage plus your Charisma Modifier, with the type of die and damage matches the Marksman Weapon's. On a success, creatures take half the damage rolled

item.name: Sigil of the Flame Scion

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: {@damage 2d4} fire damage.

A gigantic stone disc etched with various runes regarding the end of the world and burning all living and unliving things to nothingness. It burns bright when held and cackling can nearly be heard when attuned to it.
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon, but lose 10-ft of movement speed while wielding it.

entries.name: Special
entries: If you have a Strength score of 18 or greater you may ignore the Two-Handed property, instead gaining the ability to wield the Sigil as a Shield, gaining +2 to your AC when you do so.

entries.name: Crackling Soul-Link
entries: If are a spellcaster you may use your Spell Attack Modifier instead of Strength for weapon attacks using the Sigil. Furthermore, it counts as a +2 spellcasting focus for your spells and causes you to be able to make it so whenever you roll to deal damage with a fire damage dealing spell you may change the result of up to half your proficiency bonus’ worth of die to become their maximum value instead. This amount is rounded down.

Furthermore, while attuned you may have the Sigil float softly around a 10-ft space of you, removing the need to carry it and having it so it’s Thrown property is instead considered to have a reach of 30-ft.

item.name: Simple Laser Emitter
