entries: Attachment, Simple Firearms (Tactical)
A simple laser point emitter, an unremarkable way to find your way or bring down metal birds.
While Attached, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls and Perception checks, but suffer a -2 modifier to Stealth checks.
You may toggle this effect On and Off as a Free Action you may take once per turn.

item.name: Simple Reflex Sights
entries: Attachment, Simple Firearms (Optics)
A mountable attachment relying on an LED display to aid in pin-point accuracy. It'll help in pointing and shooting at things, but expecting for much more is unadvisable.
While Attached, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls.

item.name: Single-Stroke Katana
entries: A sleek sword meant to end fights quickly after it's drawn from its sheath.

item.name: Slimeheart Gown
entries: A reddish-pink colored gown made of a fine velvet fabric and addorned with crystallized ooze from Valentin’s Oozes, providing a slightly sticky and gleaming shine on its borders.
It is a perfected model of a fashionable, resistant and most important of all alluring piece of clothing. It holds a heart-shapped addornment at its neck.
Your Charisma score increases by 2 while attuned to this Gown, to a maximum value of 24.

entries.name: Pink-Gel Nails
entries: While donning this Gown you may, as a free action, coat your nails with a thin gel sheet that acts as a fashionable polish that also grants you a climbing speed equal to your movement speed, and an additional 10-ft. of walking speed if you are also attuned to a {@item Booze of Adoration|TheUndertomesASV}.

entries.name: Melting Make-Up
entries: As a reaction to when you would fall below a quarter of your maximum hit points, rounded down, you expand the crystal lining of your dress to fortify your defenses, turning them into powerful plates of congealed slime. You gain {@dice 4d8+8} temporary hit points and a +1 bonus to your Armor Class until your hit points are recovered to at least half their total or u ntil you lose these temporary hit points.

entries.name: Swooning Heartbeat
entries: If you would become {@condition Frightened} while attuned to this Gown, you may spend your reaction to instantly end the Condition as it soothes your muddied brain.

Furthermore, your marvelous style allows you to bring the most out of any sort of inspiration - Making it so that if you add a Bardic Inspiration die to your rolls, it is considered to be at least half its maximum value, if the result would be lower.

item.name: Sniper Rifle
entries: Because of its heavy weight and hefty recoil, this weapon is best used while stationary. Despite the drawbacks, it is a master of the battlefield when used right.

entries.name: Special.
entries: If you have not moved within the last Initiative round, you manage to focus more before taking any shots. You gain a +1 to hit and to damage rolls for your next attack. Your Critical Hit Threshold is also lowered by one. (Triggering on a 19-20.)

item.name: Solitude
entries: A weapon left behind by a specter that no longer wishes to tell their stories.

When you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer a number of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts equal to the number of times they were hit by this weapon in the last minute (If it’s the first time they’re hit, they suffer 1 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. If it was the second time, they suffer two, and so on).
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon.

item.name: Spada dei Bognatelli
entries: {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} ({@damage 1d6})
Featuring a segmented blade, this sword can be unlocked to act as a whip just as well as hold its ground on close quarter combats - its flexibility making creating openings a much easier ordeal.
Whenever you hit a target with this weapon, gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. This value cannot be increased through any means.

This weapon's {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} ability can only be activated by expending Acceleration Rounds. When you do so, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to the attack roll and also receive 2 Poise count before the attack is rolled.

You may use your Bonus Action and spend a bullet as per the Blast-Cartridge property to immediately perform an additional melee weapon attack against a target you've hit with a melee attack using this weapon. Attacks from this weapon that would benefit form the Blast-Cartridge property are considered to have the Reach property.

item.name: Spike Bomb
entries: A spherical object that resembles a pinecone with some protrusions of sharp yellow spikes that make your skin flutter upon a touch. You may use your action to shake the Bomb violently, causing the volatile seeds inside to become agitated and soon explode. As part of that same action you also toss the bomb to any point you can see within 60-ft. of yourself, causing it to detonate and engulf a 15-ft. radius around the point it hits in a thousand poisonous needles, forcing all creatures within reach to pass a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or suffer {@dice 4d6} piercing damage and the {@condition Charmed} condition for the next minute. A creature {@condition Charmed} this way considers every other creature they can see or hear to be the source of their {@condition Charmed} condition, also having a -1 attack modifier for the duration. A creature {@condition Charmed} this way may retry this Constitution saving throw once per turn when they suffer damage, only being able to attempt another one after the end of their next turn. On a successful save, the creature only suffers half the damage rolled.

item.name: Sporestalker
entries: A stalk of blue mushroom with a sharpened end. Despite it’s elongated and misshapen form, this spear functions as a dangerous weapon in the hands of any creature as it contains a horrible infection that easily spreads through a targets body, weakening them in the process.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Unavoidable Taming
entries: Upon hitting a target with the Sporestalker, that target loses Resistance to poison and acid damage for the next minute, or only become Resistant against those damage types if they were Immune.

entries.name: Little Sting
entries: As a reaction to when you would perform an atack with the Sporestalker you may ready your lunge or throw to be exceptionally powerful, strong enough to sink in and become stuck to the target creature on a hit. On a succesful hit against the target, the spear becomes lodged into the creature’s flesh until it is ripped out by you or through a creature spending either an action or bonus action to pry it off with a succesful DC 14 Strength check. While stuck, the spear may be targetted for attacks to drive it further into the pinned creature, with the spear itself having an AC equal to the AC of the creature it is stuck in plus 2, and a hit dealing the damage of the weapon used to attack plus {@dice 1d8} acid damage, also reducing the pinned creature’s movement speed by 5-ft. until the end of their next turn.

item.name: Spreading Spore
entries: {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}. 13 Constitution | {@variantrule Adherent|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Adherent}, {@variantrule Contact|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Contact}, {@variantrule Far-Mount|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Far-Mount} (15-ft.), {@variantrule Multiple|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Multiple}(4), {@variantrule Primal|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Primal}
A bundle of spores that when planted into ground will sprout a clump of blue shrooms that desire nothing more than to captivate others and spread as much as they can.

When triggered, the mushrooms explode in a blue spore cloud that covers a 15-ft. radius around the triggering creature, forcing them to pass a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or suffer from a much heavier version of the same mushrooms to grow on their body, weighing them down massively. On a failure the creature suffers a 30-ft. reduction to their movement speed, to a minimum value of 0-ft. This reduction is lessened by 5-ft. times the creature’s Strength modifier, as they manage to carry their bodies despite the horrible growths.

The mushrooms grown on a creature’s body remain for one minute before they dry into dust, but can also be cut off, having an AC of 7 and 30 hit points, with Immunity to psychic and poison damage and Vulnerability to acid, fire and necrotic damage.

item.name: Stake
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} property (14-20).
A simple wooden stake that was carved until deep wounds could be punctured with its use.

item.name: Stake Crossbow
entries: A more complex heavy crossbow with a mechanism for firing stakes, forgoing any kind of arrows in the process. When a stake is fired using this weapon, it always inflicts one stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}.

item.name: Staticky Two-Way Radio
entries: A strange communication device that never seems to reach anyone, it only transmits a buzzing static sound. Whenever you make a ranged attack that spends ammunition, you gain 5 feet of movement for each ammunition spent this way until the start of your next turn. If all attacks you made hit, you gain advantage on your first ranged attack next turn.
Additionally, your attacks that inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} cold damage.

item.name: Still-Warm Coffee
entries: A cup of coffee that never loses its warmth, no matter how many days it spends out in the cold. This item holds no nutritional value, but drinking from it brings a powerful boost. As a bonus action, you can drink from this beverage to give yourself {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points. If you have all of your Hit Points, you also gain advantage on your first attack each turn for 1 minute.
If you drink more than 1 Still-warm Coffee before a Long rest, you suffer 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion} when its effects wear off.

item.name: Stitchwrap Bomb
entries: A carefully built bomb wrapped by various spools of red thread that was drenched in blood, forming sharp crystals all around to be used as pins. When triggered, the triggering creature must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@damage 3d4} piercing damage and 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count, or half on a success as the pins go off and latch onto the target's face. On a failure, if the triggering creature is of Large or smaller size it must roll a d4. On an even roll they have their eyes stitched, becoming {@condition Blinded||Blinded} until they suffer slashing damage. On an odd roll, they have their mouth stitched, becoming unable to speak until they suffer slashing damage.

item.name: Striscia dell'Accelerazione
entries: {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} ({@damage 1d8})

This rapier's blade is divided into many segments that won't break easily, unlike its most famous wielder. Would you believe it if you were told that even those that can soar as high as monsters in the night can fall in such an ugly manner?

Whenever you hit a target with this weapon, gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. If you score a Critical Hit, gain 4 Poise instead. These values cannot be increased through any means. Whenever you trigger a Posture Critical, you may also choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
You may use this weapon as a ranged weapon. When you do so, it deals {@damage 2d4} piercing damage.

You have a +2 bonus modifier to attack and damage rolls while using this weapon. Whenever you use it's {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} ability you bypass Piercing damage Resistance, consider Piercing Immunity as Resistance and ignore the target's {@itemProperty IPN|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Impenetrable} armor property, if applicable.

This weapon's Blast-Cartridge ability can only be activated by expending Acceleration Rounds. When you do so, you gain a +1 bonus modifier to the attack roll and also receive 2 Poise count before the attack is rolled. Attacks from this weapon that would benefit form the Blast-Cartridge property are considered to have the Reach property.

You may use your Bonus Action and spend a bullet as per the Blast-Cartridge property to immediately perform am additional melee weapon attack with each weapon you are wielding against a target within hit. If you kill the target using this, you instantly gain 6 Poise count.

entries.name: Colpi Devastanti.
entries: Once per turn, you may extend your melee weapon reach by 15-ft. while wielding this weapon. Whenever you attack a creature further than 5-ft. away from you using this, you are instantly moved to be within 5-ft. of the target and deal additional piercing damage equal to half your {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

item.name: Styptics Bag
entries: A grab bag of healing herbs laid out and pressed against bandages for easy use to stop bleeding. You may consume this item to instantly end the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} Condition.

item.name: Sugar Cloud
entries: A small vial of crystalline glass containing a swirling green and pink liquid that glows in the dark. It smells like mint and arsenic, also tasting like sugar. This taste never goes away, no matter how hard you try.

When consumed, you become permanently {@condition Blinded}, except that you can still vaguely see your surroundings around a 60- ft. radius of yourself as if they were put through rose-tinted lens, with blood being replaced by rainbows and all creatures and acts seeming as friendly gestures to you. You automatically fail on any {@skill Insight} checks and to perceive Illusion spells, seeing everything as absolute reality despite any aparent flaws.

item.name: Sunglasses of Surmountable Style
entries: A pair of golden trimmed and purple lensed sunglasses that radiates stylishness, being one of the few that most people can and should accept to be worn even during night. It is a symbol of class and power within certain families.

entries.name: Advanced Lusciousness
entries: Your Charisma score becomes 23 while Attuned to this item as long as it was lower than this value. Additionally, if you weren't proficient in the Persuasion or {@skill Intimidation} skills you still add half your proficiency bonus to skill checks of either.

entries.name: Curricular in Castigation.
entries: Let your heart beat and be beaten in the name of the family. At the start of your turn you may spend a Bonus Action to adjust your sunglasses and let them shine with a challenge to all - kill you or die trying. You gain Vulnerability to all damage types until the start of your next turn. At the start of your next turn and until its end any damage you deal to others has them be considered Vulnerable to that damage type. If you or a creature made Vulnerable this way would have Resistance to a damage type, they only take an amount of damage equal to the normal damage they would take plus half that same damage. If either were Immune to a damage type, they suffer that damage as if they were not Immune instead.

entries.name: Quality Eye Protection.
entries: You gain Advantage on rolls against effects that would cause you to be blinded. These glasses are just that good.

item.name: Suppressive Fire
entries: {@i 1st-level Expanded Ammunition}

Although not very practical for inflicting great damage, this magazine contains a series of compact bullets useful to effectively pin down a target. When used, you may choose a target within your Marksman Weapon's range, it must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer immense hardship to leave its position, having their movement speed reduced by 5 * SL, to a minimum of 5-feet. In addition, if the target does move during this duration, the next attack aimed against them has your SL as a bonus modifier to hit.

item.name: Talisman of Enwrapping Dissonance
entries: As a bonus action, make a ranged weapon attack against a creature you can see within 60 feet. The talisman disintegrates when used. On a hit, it triggers the target's {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and distributes the amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it had as evenly as possible among creatures of your choice within 5 feet of it. You choose which creatures receive any remainder. If the original target had no {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, it instead suffers 3 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Talisman of Quick-Wits
entries: This talisman is worn around the wrist or attached directly to skin or bone. When you roll initiative, you can allow it to burn away and add {@dice 1d4} to the roll as revitalizing energy sharpens your focus.

item.name: Tattoo Set of Confidence
entries: A set of intricate tattoos that make use of their wearer's confidence to harden muscles to protect the flesh from any damage the user would suffer. These are usually worn with leather or pelt-based clothing onto to further bolster their wearer's confidence in themselves.

This armor is a set of tattoos that glow whenever active, as such it cannot be doffed without specialized means yet may be covered by other clothing or even armor. While wearing armor over a Tattoo Set, you must choose to benefit from the effects of only one of the armors.

Due to the glow of these tattoos you have Disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks unless you are proficient in the {@skill Deception} skill or have expertise in the {@skill Stealth} skill, as you are more knowledgeable on how to mask such unnatural lights as a common part of the scenery or obfuscate that glow altogether.

item.name: Tears of a Lost Child

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: {@damage 2d4} cold damage.

An old, rusty pickaxe which has had ice grown on it’s surface as if it were moss. Legend says this ice was once the tears of the various children lost to the elements in the streets, with their cries coming to dry upon the famine imposed upon them.

You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon and you inflict 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit with it. Furthermore, the ice that gnaws on this old pickaxe only grows as it senses the lousy feelings lingering in the hearts of those around, causing it to deal an additional d4 cold damage and inflict 1 additional {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count per 5 total {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count of the sum of all creatures within 15-ft.
of you.

entries.name: Stagnant Heel
entries: You may, as part of an attack you could take as part of the Attack action, bring the pickaxe down on a target creatures legs on a hit, robbing them of their near future and reducing their movement speed by 5-ft per {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on them, to a minimum value of 5-ft. That target recovers 5-ft of movement speed at the end of their turns or 10-ft when suffering fire damage. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to your Proficiency Modifier, regaining spent uses on a long rest.

item.name: Teeth of Perseverance
entries: A simple looking necklace sporting sharp teeth as its main piece. When attuned to it, you feel your determination towards your goals being slightly amplified, as if it were easier to focus on such. Once per day, when you would fail a roll, you may spend your reaction to re-roll the dice, possibly turning a failure into a success, as you feel the necklace feel almost alive, it's sharp tooth pecking at your chest to motivate you onward.

item.name: Tendrils Connecting to Nothing
entries: Dried flesh and sinew woven into a number of red cords hanging off an etched-bone handle, with leather that always feels warm to the touch. In fact, touching it reveals this magic items slow, steady heartbeat. Its tendrils exhibit a life of its own, extending to cling onto another’s life and take it for its own, curring through both flesh and soul as if such concepts were one.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The Tendrils have a reach of 30-ft. while you are attuned, and inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit also being unable to recover hit points for as long as they are Bleeding. Creatures who receive the Condition this way must instead pass an {@skill Arcana} check instead of {@skill Medicine} to heal the condition, as their gashes are covered in a thin, mushy membrane that pulsates in tandem with this weapon’s heartbeat.

entries.name: Take for the self
entries: Whenever you first deal damage to a creature during your turn, you may choose to have the tendrils latch onto and bring back a fragment of their soul - a small copy of a memory of your choice, allowing you to learn from them as if you were told that piece of information directly. You may choose between the following pieces of information or roll for them, having the DM tell you as if the target creature was telling it themselves, if able to speak:

rows: You learn about their parents, their names and a brief insight of who they are or were.
You learn about their most beloved person.
You learn their most precious memory.
You learn their most despised memory.
You learn their greatest passion.
You learn what they hate the most about themselves.
You learn their greatest fear.
You learn what they want most in life.

entries.name: Living Finger Puppet
entries: As a reaction to whenever you damage a creature with this Weapon, you may attempt to let them sink to the back of the targets neck, forcing the target to pass a Dexterity saving throw ( Whose DC is 11 + your Attack modifier ) or suffer {@dice 3d8} piercing damage and become controlled by you until they spend an action to pull it out by performing a succesful {@skill Athletics} check ( Whose DC is 15 ).

While controlled, you may take control of the targets mouth to speak whatever you want. Furthermore, while controlling its tendrils you may spend your reaction at the start or end of their turn to force them to perform a weapon attack against a creature within their reach. When unlatched, the target suffers 4 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

entries.name: Yearning to be
entries: You may cast the {@spell Alter Self} spell at will without spending a spell slot.

item.name: The Clock Says
entries: A delicate pocket watch made from silver and diamonds. It is ornate in its design and could easily be found as the heirloom of a mighty noble family. It’s clock hands are made out of pure diamond and can conduct the flow of time in an area, demanding more from those around like a contract made long, long ago. Refusing the Watch is impossible, as the debts of time are always collected, no matter whose.

entries.name: It Wasn’t Enough
entries: As an Action you may take during your turn you may open the pocket watch and wind back its hands to empower it, causing all damage dealt within a radius centered on you whose size equal to 5 times your proficiency bonus to be doubled, as the afterimages of any damage sources appear and glitch in and out of the zone’s timestream. After using this you cannot do so again until after a long rest. If any sort of antimagic enters this zone, such as an {@spell Antimagic Field} spell is cast and overlaps it or a Counter Spell at 7th level of greater is cast targeting the watch the entire zone collapses, making it so all creatures within range must pass a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or suffer {@dice 6d12} force damage and {@dice 1d4} points of {@condition Exhaustion}, rolled individually, or one point of {@condition Exhaustion} on a success.

item.name: The Harper

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: {@damage 1d4} piercing damage.

A grandiose bow made out of impossible materials resembling ivory and marble, sporting black etchings that remind of musical notes. It has four white strings, each becoming a darker shade of black when plucked and releasing sound made solid instead of an arrow, always in the performance of it’s next symphony.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. You fully ignore cover when attacking with this weapon, except for Full cover, which is considered only half cover for your weapon attacks. You are considered proficient with this weapon if you have levels in Bard.

entries.name: Arco per Arpa
entries: The Harper also counts as a Harp of which you have Expertise in and a +3 Bardic focus.

entries.name: Attacco Accelerato
entries: You may spend your action to quickly nock four arrows into The Harper’s strings, all taking the same shape and color. You then perform four ranged weapon attacks with this weapon to any target within reach, instead dealing only {@dice 1d8} thunder damage per hit and not increasing Symphony, instead gaining a +1 bonus modifier to hit the same target creature you have hit with these ranged attacks, to a maximum modifier of +3. This bonus resets to zero at the end of your turn.

entries.name: Melodia a Tre Stadi
entries: Each time you hit an attack against a creature, you gain one Symphony count, being able to channel the pure power of The Harper going from it’s shorter strings to it’s longest ones - Performing a crescendo of attacks with a devastating finale. You deal an additional {@dice 1d8} thunder damage per Symphony count you currently have, and after reaching 3 Symphony count it is reset to zero, causing your next attack to be infused with the powerful energy of a Finale, dealing a total of {@dice 6d8} thunder damage plus {@dice 1d4} piercing damage on a hit. A target hit by a Finale also must pass a Constitution saving throw or be knocked {@condition Prone} and have all objects that aren’t being worn or wielded burst into pieces as the sheer melodic force forces them to scream out loud. You lose one count of Symphony when you miss an attack.

entries.name: Melodie Magiche
entries: You may cast the {@spell Charm Person}, {@spell Silence}, {@spell Phantasmal Killer} and {@spell Legend Lore} spells each without spending a spell slot once per long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for these spells.

item.name: The Helmet of Begon
entries: The crown of an ancient king, known for granting invulnerability to its wearer. It is made of pure gold and hangs various ornaments in its visor, ostentating its might. Might Before Giants. While attuned, you gain Resistance against all types of damage except for Force damage. You also become Immune to all non-magical damage and magical piercing, bludgeoning and slashing damage.

item.name: The Last Drop
entries: This silver laden goblet has no discernible features on its surface, with no special engraving apart from lattice-like scratches resembling a wine racket. Its contents are a nearly overflowing amount of deep red wine, which never seems to overflow, not even when the cup is fully turned does the liquid fall. When consumed, you become instantly attuned to The Last Drop as the overly sweet taste overtakes your senses and you feel an emptiness in your heart slowly form.

While attuned, you have a constant longing for more wine, as you feel it is the only thing you may do to acknowledge that your life had any successes. At the beginning of a long rest, you must pass a DC 14 ( Plus however many times you've already consumed from the Last Drop ) or consume more of the liquid, which never empties. For each time you drink, you feel a heavier weight placed upon your heart, until you can't handle it anymore, eventually wasting away.

For each time you've consumed, you lose one hit die until this condition is cured. If you have no hit die left to lose, you start taking an amount of typeless damage equal to your hit die, for an amount equal to however many "negative" hit die you have. This condition may only be cured with the {@spell greater restoration|PHB|Greater Restoration} or {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spells, or similar means.
Upon curing, you restore one of your destroyed Hit Die, and regain one more on each further long rest.

item.name: The Life Story of a Gravekeeper
entries: This is a hefty and worn logbook of a nameless gravekeeper who had been collecting the stories of theri graveyards inhabitants for years now. When attuned, you feel the amalgamated spirit of so many tales swerve around in the book. Once per day, you may peer into the book to get a gleamse of its wisdom, granting you a d8 bonus to one skill check until your next long rest.

item.name: The One Stone Dagger
entries: A single hand-held dagger carved out of pure granite, feeling freezing cold to the touch and bearing not many exquisite details apart from marks of wearing and tearing and a single onyx teardrop at the base of its hilt. When attuned and active, the dagger takes the form of a longer dirk, its handle coated in a repeating black and white diamond pattern that feels as comfortable as a king’s bed and it’s granite blade darkens to contain starlight through its edge, cutting through anything as if it were butter.

When you first attune to this item, you see yourself fall through a sudden cliff at the end of everything, having a glimpse of the creation of your universe, but never being able to gaze into the future. You cannot break attunement from this item, becoming its wielder until your final death, maintaining attunement if you would be revived. You cannot benefit from any sort of Divination spells or effects and when active this dagger also produces a sun-shaped porcelain mask in front of your face, with hollow holes replacing any windows to your eyes, with dark tears streaming down the cheeks and covering parts of a long, shameless smirk.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Applaud for a Foolish Man
entries: Whenever you help another creature or another creature takes the Aid action helping each other, the target of this action also gains a d6 bonus modifier to their next roll.

entries.name: Crumbling Kingdoms, Stone-Hearted Men
entries: Whenever you would knock a creature {@condition unconscious} while using this dagger you may spend your reaction to extend it’s stone blade to touch their soul, causing the creature to become {@condition Petrified} until the ends of time or until the statue is broken, causing the creatures soul to also be destroyed. This statue has an AC of 12, Resistance to acid, fire, lightning, necrotic and radiant damage, Immunity to poison and psychic damage and Vulnerability to magical bludgeoning and thunder damage.
This Petrification cannot be undone unless you spend your action to do so or through the effects of a {@spell Wish} spell.

entries.name: Void
entries: As an action during your turn you may choose to have the knife’s instincts overtake your own, giving up control for a number of turns of your choice, chosen when taking this action and to a maximum of 5 turns. For the chosen amount of turns your body moves on its own will, having you move towards the nearest living hostile creature and spending your action to perform the maximum amount of attacks you can against that creature until it dies. You gain a bonus modifier to your attack and damage rolls equal to the amount of turns chosen, but cannot do anything else of your own free will, losing your bonus actions and being unable to benefit from spell effects that would give you additional options, such as the {@spell Haste} spell. You remain cognizant during this state. For this duration this dagger also deals force damage instead of piercing.

item.name: The Path of Freedom
entries: The Path of Freedom is a lantern held with a dark metallic cage, and its light is constantly covered by a black cloth. Whenever it is revealed, the light comes from a shimmering golden orb that swirls inside itself as if liquid was present inside, and the distorted sounds of a forest may be heard. While attuned and while holding the lantern in one hand, you may spend your bonus action to raise it toward a creature that can see within 60-feet of you.

They must pass a DC 18 Charisma Saving Throw or be enthralled by its swirling light, using their reaction to immediatedly move double their movement speed up to the closest empty space close to you, as if they used the Sprint action. If they are within reach when their reaction ends, your next attack is done with advantage and is considered a critical hit on a roll of 15 or higher before adding any modifiers.

item.name: The Red Axe
entries: {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} (15-20)

A true lumberjack doesn't mind how tired he is, nor what kind of wood he cuts into. There will never be greater elation than feeling the warmth of freshly cut sap dig into their fingernails as they once again fell another, nor when they hear the logs roll over. This handaxe reeks of blood yet it looks incredibly well preserved, almost hypnotic.
When you attune to this weapon, you cannot unattune from it, save for the effects of the {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell.

entries.name: Sanguine Desire.
entries: While attuned to this weapon, all your senses feel heightened, mere passing moments of joy turn into elation, small annoyances into heavy grievances and so on.

As such, you gain advantage on any {@skill Performance} checks, as they become much more genuine, yet your clouded judgement has you suffer disadvantage on any {@skill Insight} checks. Additionally, there is a bloodlust that instills in you, feeling completely natural. When you reduce a creature below 1 hit point during combat, this weapon gains a cumulative +1 bonus to hit and to its damage rolls, to a maximum of +3.

You cannot deal non-lethal damage with this weapon, nor use any other weapon to attack while attuned to the Red Axe. Additionally, in the same turn when you kill a creature, you must spend all your remaining attacks to slash at the body, all to satiate your bloodlust.

item.name: The Road Back
entries: This magical tattoo was made out of crushed dreams and a bundle of the most resilient hope in a broken heart, melded black and into the a Magical Symbol that feeds upon failure.

entries.name: Magical Symbol
entries: Every time you fail a roll, you gain one count of Magical Symbol, to a maximum of 4. After reaching 4 Magic Symbol count, you gain Resistance to all damage types except force and psychic until the end of your next turn, also making it so any creature that damages you suffers a +2 additional damage modifier whenever they receive damage until the end of of their next turn. This additional damage matches any that would be dealt and this bonus stacks for each time they have hit you while Magical Symbol was in effect. When this effect ends your Magical Symbol count is reset to 0.

item.name: The Thumb's Capo Uniform
entries: {@itemProperty IMP|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Imposing} (4), {@itemProperty IPN|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Impenetrable} (1)

Meant for the distinguished members of the Thumb, this set of clothes might not seem to have as much variation from the Capo's underlings beside the ability to have its golden inlays customized to show a variety of images, but it actually boasts a considerable upgrade in the form of nueovo fabric. To eyes who aren't to be removed, this uniform is a sign to pay respect.

item.name: The Thumb's Heavy Triggerblade
entries: {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} ({@damage 2d8})

The north of the City's cold has a need to be quickly cut through to maintain an orderly schedule, and through the ingenuity of certain workshop masters a heavy-duty weapon design has been created to reflect that very need. Boasting a mounted with high calibre gun parts and an even heavier blade, the Heavy Triggerblade is a weapon that demands respect to itself, rather than only representing something to the wielder.

entries.name: Bulky Reload.
entries: Due to the insane calibre this weapon boasts, you may only spend your Action to fully reload it, or load a single bullet in as a Bonus Action. This weapon uses the Reload property for both regular ranged attacks and to benefit from {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge}, accepting only Heavy Blast Rounds for any kind of fire.

entries.name: Heavy-Duty Fire.
entries: Whenever you use this weapon for ranged weapon attacks, you inflict {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you'd inflict. You may also choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you hit a creature in such way or deal a Critical Hit with any type of weapon attack.

entries.name: Unrelenting Punishment.
entries: Whenever you would use this ammunition's Blast-Cartridge property you may sweep your weapon, causing its range to become an area reaching any other creature of your choice within 5-ft. of the original target. You roll your melee weapon attack once, hitting any creature whose AC is equal to or lower than the result.

item.name: The Thumb's Rifle
entries: A bolt-action rifle with a burgundy stock and several intricate mechanisms to accept both regular and propulsion bullets that is commonly used by the Thumb. Its sleek design make it so a propulsion round can be placed on the side and have its momentum used for an exceptionally fast flurry of slashes at one given time.
Attacks made with this weapon inflict one additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

If attached with any kind of Bayonet or you would otherwise be able to make melee weapon attacks with this weapon, it gains the {@itemProperty BLC|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Blast Cartridge} (2d4) property and you may use either Acceleration or Propulsion Rounds with it. This weapon is considered to have the Reload (2) property when pertaining to Blast-Cartridge uses.

Additionally, you may target creatures up to 15-ft. away from you while using this property, instantly repositioning yourself to be standing atop an unoccupied space within 5-ft. of them and then attacking.

You may use your Bonus Action and spend a bullet as per the Blast-Cartridge property to immediately perform an additional melee weapon attack against a target you've hit with a melee attack using this weapon.

item.name: The Thumb's Soldato Uniform
entries: {@itemProperty IMP|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Imposing} (1)

A set of formal clothes and hat emblazoned in the signature burgundy coloured fabrics of the Thumb and stricken with dusty golden inlays. Even the lowest of the organization demand respect, as they are still representative of the whole.

entries.name: Imposing.
entries: An Imposing armor set is the kind of clothing that demands some level of respect, no matter from whom. You benefit from having your Intimidation skill modifier be at least the value displayed in Parenthesis, if it was any lower.

item.name: The Thumb's SottoCapo Uniform
entries: {@itemProperty IMP|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Imposing} (8), {@itemProperty IPN|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Impenetrable} (3)

An outfit that was assembled with a single goal in mind: to be gazed up upon and have the viewer feel ashamed of their own lack of station. Fitted with the finest nueovo fabric to boast comfort, style and resistance as to allow the wearer to take bullets without flinching, this uniform is meant only for those who have already managed to raise their hands to pass judgement and bear the weight of hierarchy upon their backs.

entries.name: Impenetrable.
entries: An armor seat with the Impenetrable property has remarkably good stopping power against piercing forces and other kinds of missiles. Your AC against attacks that would deal piercing damage or that are otherwise missiles ( such as arrows, bullets or certain ranged spells ) is considered to be higher by a value presented in parenthesis near this property. Additionally, whenever you would suffer damage through one such attack it is reduced by an amount equal to double the value presented in parenthesis.

item.name: Thieves’ Unsuspecting Overcoat
entries: A completely normal-looking overcoat whose style can range from a prim and fancy piece of clothing to essentially a rag with pockets. Nevertheless, these pockets are actually made using the same techniques and magic required to create a Bag of Holding, containing a demi-plane where you can store up to 150 pounds of objects, provided that these don’t exceed a volume of 32 cubic feet.

The Overcoat’s pockets share any other similar aspects to a Bag of Holding, except the entire Overcoat’s inner layering also provides a thin coat of a Lead metal blend that protects it from any 4th-level or lower spell that could detect it’s magic while still being remarkably easy to move in.

item.name: Thorns Of Regret
entries: A warhammer bearing an immeasurable weight not in the physical sense, but to its wielders mind. Its malformed head bears spikes that tear into its target's flesh, yet so does its handle, so that its wielder may quickly learn the weight of their own actions. You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, but you take half the damage dealt on each hit, in addition, you gain the Regret condition until the end of your next turn.

Metallic Ringing. While afflicted with Regret, your attacks become more unhinged. On a roll of 18-20 before modifiers, your attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} thunder damage as the metal makes sounds reverberate inside the targets head in an unbearable droning.

Regret. A creature with Regret feels the weight of their sins on their mind, yet it must be beared, lest the mind break fully. For the duration of Regret, the creature has disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws, but the dulling of its mind renders more focus to the body, gaining advantage on Constitution saving throws.

item.name: Time, The Killer

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: {@damage 1d8} force damage.

A deceptively easy to wield scythe of obsidian black. Its shadow wreathe and dance around the wielder’s fingers, with a clockhead etched to its top as if an eye overlooking the lives of all its blade will meet without a hint of shame, ill-intent or anticipation - only looking forward to the inevitability of time. Whenever swung with the intent to harm, its blade leaves a green trail in the air as its blade cuts through space itself, robbing its target of what holds them together.
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon and it counts as a +3 spellcasting focus.
Whenever you would deal damage through a spell attack you deal an additional d8 force damage.

entries.name: Inhale, Drink, Take
entries: To consume time is the destiny of all living and dying creatures, yet while wielding this scythe you manage to do so actively. When you would deal damage to a creature it is robbed of the very time it possesses left, having their maximum hit die reduced by the value of force damage dealt by the hit. This cannot be restored by any means except a {@spell Remove Curse} spell cast at 8th or greater level or the {@spell Wish} spell. Furthermore, you gain one count of Provision for the first time you deal damage to an individual creature during your turn, with you being able to gain another count from that creature only after the end of your turn.

entries.name: Relentless, Finite
entries: You may consume up to three Provision count as a Bonus Action during your turn to wind up the clockhead of your scythe. Your next attack deals an additional d8 force damage per count spent.

entries.name: Winding, Endless
entries: You may consume up to three Provision count as a Bonus Action to have time flow into you. You are healed by an amount of d8+1 equal to the amount of count spent.

item.name: Timed Detonation Bullet
entries: {@i 4th-level Expanded Ammunition}

Waiting for the second time to press the trigger is often harder than landing the shot. This bullet contains a small incendiary explosive capable of causing a big wreck. When used, you make a ranged weapon attack against a target within your range. On a hit, a Detonation Bullet is lodged inside them.

You may, as a free action taken whenever there is no ongoing roll, pull a trigger to have the explosive perform its role. The creature containing the bullet must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or take SL * d12 fire damage as if they were Vulnerable to fire damage, or half this damage on a success. In the case of a failure, all creatures within a 15-feet radius of the detonation must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take SL * d8 fire damage, or half on a success.

item.name: Tinker Bell
entries: An ornate bell made out of gold and mysterious metals that give the item a marble-like smoothness and sheen, bearing profoundly intricate engravings that remind you of a tapestry depicting the many faces of a long lost fairy queen and her court, lost to time and to her own ailing mind. This bell has been blessed by all fey courts, containing an innate magic that cannot compare to anything near it.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon and may use your Spell attack modifier for attack rolls made with it. The bell has an innate connection to magic, reaching out to connect with any caster to fulfil its true potential. While being wielded by a creature who cannot cast any spells, this item is instead only a +3 light hammer mechanically, but to casters it also counts as a +3 spellcasting focus.

entries.name: Blessed by All-Courts
entries: While attuned to this magical item you have an intrinsic authority over all fey creatures, gaining advantage on any Charisma check against them. Furthermore, you can cast the {@spell Command} spell at will as long as your target is a Fey creature. The creature knows when this spell is being cast upon it whenever you use the bell in this way.

entries.name: Courtly Guardianship
entries: As a reaction to when another creature would deal damage to you, you may have them hit the bell and resonate with it - causing all the magic inside it to burst in an incredibly loud noise that disperses all the damage that would be dealt to you and any other creatures targeted by the attack. All the damage for this attack is reduced to 1 of the same damage type that would be dealt.
You may use this feature once per long rest, as the bell needs to reassemble all its dispersed energy.

entries.name: Twinkling Noises
entries: You may cast the {@spell Faerie Fire}, {@spell Shatter}, {@spell Summon Fey|TCE} and {@spell Conjure Fey} spells each without spending a spell slot once per long rest. You also learn the {@spell Toll the Dead|XGE} cantrip, which deals an additional die of necrotic damage when cast using this bell as a spellcasting focus.

item.name: Tomorrow’s Fortune
entries: A small snow-globe containing the entire cosmos in miniature. Inside it, unimaginable power swirls, contracts and expands as if the breathing of a living organism. You may tap into this power whenever you clutch on tight to its base, causing the stars inside to align and shape your spells in a way most wouldn’t even be able to dream of.

You gain a +4 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells. Furthermore, while attuned you gain an additional 9th level spell slot which is replenished only after a month has passed since spending it.

entries.name: Multi-Colored Starlight
entries: While using the Globe to cast spells you may change any spell’s damage type dealt to another damage type of your choice. You may also change any physical saving throw ( Strength, Dexterity, Constitution )

or mental saving throw ( Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma ) to require another attribute within the same group. You may do this an amount of times equal to your proficiency modifier, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

entries.name: Pocket Universe
entries: While attuned to this item you may cast the {@spell Plant Growth}, {@spell Animate Objects}, {@spell Awaken} and {@spell Creation} spells at will. When attuning to this item you choose between Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma to be the spell casting modifier for these spells.

entries.name: Universe in the Palm of your Hand
entries: As an action during your turn you may place your hand ontop of the Globe, kindly asking it to “Be silent and clear”. Upon doing so, up to a 600-ft. radius around you has the following effects of your choice:

items: That area is devoid of any darkness, as if all were illuminated through moonlight. No spaces can be Obscured through any means and any magical darkness is dispelled. Any {@condition Invisible} creature inside the area becomes visible.

That area is engulfed by a swirling dark mist ecloding from bright stars. This area counts as Heavily Obscured to all creatures other than you and creatures of your choice, who can see through it normally.

All creatures except those of your choice must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC or be unable to speak for the duration. Furthermore, any words written down are blurred out as if ink were turned to water, dripping off of its surface and any carvings only crack and destroy the surface its on, rendering it impossible to read.

entries: These effects last for the next minute or until you choose to remove your hand. To do this, you must maintain Concentration on holding your hand over the Globe as if you were maintaining a spell. You may do this only once per long rest.

item.name: Tonfas
entries: A pair of matching beating sticks with grips on the sides, commonly used in tandem with one another rather than on their lonesome.

item.name: Toxic Goop Canister
entries: A vial containing a dense amount of a toxic green goop that expands in contact to air, emitting a foul gas that poisons all in its vicinity. You may spend your action to toss a Canister toward a space within 30-ft of you, forcing all creatures within a 15-ft. radius of that point to pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@dice 2d6} acid damage, or half on a success.

A mess of green slime is left on the space the canister exploded, it is of medium size and it’s space is considered as Difficult Terrain, instantly covering its space in a Poisonous Gas that expands to cover a 5-ft. further radius at Initiative count 1, to a maximum of covering 30-ft.

The DC for both the explosion and Poisonous Gas saving throws is 14. The Poisonous Gas cloud is dissolved after the green slime is destroyed, it has 30 hit points, an AC of 8 and all it’s Ability scores are considered to be 2.

item.name: Training Dummy Rabbit
entries: wondrous pet
You have either encountered or created a small machine that looks like some sort of training dummy shaped like a rabbit.
It seems to enjoy your company, and follows you around by either rolling or bouncing. It wants to help you achieve a good training routine!

entries.name: Practice Makes Perfect
entries: Once per long rest, you may train with your training dummy rabbit any topic you wish. Until the next long rest, you may choose to gain proficiency in a skill of your choice. If you choose one you already have proficiency with, you gain expertise instead.

item.name: Tremor-Locking Plate Armor
entries: The standard armor set used by the Zwei West knights, made out of various plates that easily lock in place to impede being moved back from their target zones.
Properties: {@itemProperty IMV|TheUndertomesPRT|Immovable} (5), {@itemProperty DSP|TheUndertomesPRT|Dispersing} (2).

entries.name: Immovable
entries: An armor set with the Immovable property is too heavy or too stubborn to be tossed around. Whenever you would be moved forcefully, you may choose to be moved an amount of feet less equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property, such as a 5 meaning that you can resist being moved 5-ft. per time you would be forcefully moved.

entries.name: Dispersing
entries: An armor set who boasts the Dispersing property evenly spreads any sort of vibrations and possible cracks it could receive, making it shrug off lingering blows much easier. Whenever you would receive {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count that amount is reduced by the value between parenthesis to the side of this Property, to a minimum of 1.

item.name: Tributary Cigar Carton
entries: Count yourself lucky if you get to feel the heat of one of these, be it while tasting its smoke or by being some object to have it put off. These cigars are expensive, luxurious and the best fit to be given by lower-ranking Thumb members to their superiors as tribute.
This Box contains 6 Cigars that can be cut and lit as a Bonus Action during your turn, lasting for one minute while being smoked. For that duration you receive the following:

items: Whenever you deal damage to a creature, you deal an additional fire damage equal to the targets current {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

Whenever you trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} you deal 3 additional {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you would apply the Condition until the end of your next turn.
You are considered to have Expertise in the Investigation and Perception skills for the duration.
You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws for the duration.

item.name: Trivia Trapper
entries: {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}. Repair: 100 GP; Varies | {@variantrule Contact|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Contact}, {@variantrule Durability|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Durability} ( 6 )
A small oval device resembling a plate, with a large lamp at it’s top that becomes alight when a creature steps close.

You may prepare a list of 6 trivia with your Dungeon Master, with the DM choosing their level of difficulty in general knowledge, dealing more damage the easier the piece of trivia would be, as follows:

rows: Trivial
{@dice 6d4} psychic
Easy
{@dice 4d4} psychic
Medium
{@dice 2d4} psychic
Hard
{@dice 1d4} psychic
Impossible
1 psychic

entries: You organize the trivia on a table as you’d like and may replace this trivia on a long rest. When triggered, you may roll a d6 on that table, resulting in the Trivia Trapper emanating a robotic voice asking about that tidbit of trivia to the triggering creature, who suffers its damage if it answers incorrectly, or nothing on a success.

item.name: Twinshield Projector Device
entries: Deployable Tool, Rare. Repair: 200 GP. Non-hitting; {@variantrule Adherent|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, {@variantrule Arcane|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, {@variantrule Instant|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, {@variantrule Sturdy|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} (14, 80).
A metallic disc which, when activated emits various energy projections which shield determined creatures in its area of activation.

When Deployed, a 40-ft. wide and long square area around the Projector has its edges project warning lines. All creatures of your choice ( when first deploying it ) gain a +1 bonus to their AC until the start of their next turn while they are within the area. They lose this bonus prematurely if they leave this area.
This bonus is considered to be a +2 against ranged weapon and spell attacks, and may be added on saving throw against missile-based effects, such as that of the {@spell Fireball|PHB} spell.

item.name: Vampiric Noblesse Clothes
entries: Finely crafted clothes that help you hide your bloodthirsty nature with an otherworldly sense of style. While wearing these clothes, other creatures have Disadvantage on {@skill Insight} checks for perceiving you as a Vampire, Bloodfiend, Shapechanger and otherwise, instead usually assuming you are only a flamboyant noble.

item.name: Vein Splitter
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty HEM|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Hemorrhaging} property (15-20).

This easily concealed blade can be worn as a brooch and easily be mistaken as one, having a mechanism to fully unsheathe its sharpened blade quickly when needed. You have advantage on {@skill Stealth} Checks to keep this weapon concealed.

item.name: Vial of Centipede Venom
entries: You can use the venom in this vial to coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition.
Applying the venom takes an Action.

A creature hit by the {@condition poisoned} weapon or ammunition must make a DC 15 Constitution Saving Throw or suffer {@dice 1d4} Centipede Poison count and becoming {@condition Poisoned} until the end of their next turn. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute before drying.

item.name: Vial of Pristine Blood
entries: A glass vial of certain blood collections mixed with a number of special reagents to make it pure. When consumed with a Bonus Action, you are healed and gain Bloodfeast according to the Vial's rarity, as presented below:

entries.caption: Vial of Pristine Blood
rows: Common
50 gp
Rabble
{@dice 1d4 + 1}
Uncommon
200 gp
Adventurers
{@dice 2d4 + 2}
Rare
Aristocrats
{@dice 3d4 + 3}
Very Rare
Future Kings
{@dice 4d4 + 4}
Legendary
Priceless
Gods

item.name: Vial of Silver Water
entries: A charm of holy water mixed with silver dust for an even stronger purifying effect. It can be worn around your body, having its own AC that equals yours + your Dexterity Modifier and 10 hit points. While worn, creatures with a weakness to radiant damage, silvered weapons or that are bloodfiends suffer a -1 modifier to all Saving Throws as long as they are within 60-ft of you.

item.name: Vial of Unicorn Tears
entries: One always must think to themselves how a product was taken from nature, yet this one? This one will bring tears to yourself. When consumed, you are healed for {@damage 8d8+8} hit points as the unicorns purity washes over all of your body, a sense of innocence and care swealling in your heart.

After you are healed by this, you must pass a DC 18 Charisma saving throw or start crying uncontrollably as the memories of what caused such a creature to cry flood your mind's eye. While crying, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and to maintain concentration. Evil-aligned creatures have advantage against this saving throw.

item.name: Void Glyph
entries: Produced by a special needle, this magic tattoo features a symbol of oblivion.

entries.name: Tattoo Attunement
entries: To attune to this item, you hold the needle to your skin where you want the tattoo to appear, pressing the needle there throughout the attunement process. When the attunement is complete, the needle turns into the ink that becomes the tattoo, which appears on the skin. If your attunement to the tattoo ends, the tattoo vanishes, and the needle reappears in your space.

entries.name: All Returns to the Void
entries: As an action, you may target a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see. Wisps of darkness cover you both, and, if they’re unwilling, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 18 or your spell save DC) or become unable to take any sort of actions until the end of their next turn. While in this state, their AC increases by 2 and they gain {@dice 4d6} temporary hit points. Once this ability is successful, you can only use it again after you complete a long rest.

item.name: Walking Bass
entries: A serrated instrument infused with dark magic and put together with scraps of a dark machine. At the start of your turn in combat, you may choose to gain 1 count of {@condition Hyped-Up|TheUndertomesDA} as a free action. Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, but before you apply damage, roll a {@dice d20}.

On a roll of 16 or higher, you and 1 random friendly creature within 30 feet of you that isn't {@condition Deafened} gains 1 count of {@condition Hyped-Up|TheUndertomesDA} If it was an attack that inflicts counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it happens on a roll of 11 or higher instead.

entries.name: Curse
entries: You love the sound of your own music too much, so you can't go without listening to it during the chaos of combat. If you spend more than 2 turns without Hyping yourself up, you hear discordant notes inside your mind, taking {@damage 2d6} psychic damage that cannot be reduced in any way.

item.name: Waykeeper's Ledger
entries: This ledger is bound by a dark leather that feels like a tree's bark when you run your fingers across. A pen made out of obsidian and inlaid with silver is chained to it. This item does not attune to a person, instead, its attunement process during a long rest is made through marking down an area for up to a 25-ft. cube using the Ledger's pen.
Any creature that passes through this area has its given name, a near-photographic sketch of its face, if it has one, and the time they passed magically etched on the Ledger.

item.name: Weighted Glove
entries: Not too heavy, not too light. This glove is made not to deliver the most powerful blows at once, but to make sure blows are constantly delivered while the wearer can focus on their agility as well.

item.name: Wound Clerid
entries: An enchanted object composed of blood and made to look like a small beetle. Once per day, as a Reaction after you apply {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} with an attack, you can immediately bring out the clerid to tear deeper into the creature’s flesh, dealing an additional 4 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If this ability has already been used, this item regains the ability to use it daily at dawn.

item.name: Yang's Blessing
entries: This light-colored earring of a teardrop represents all the positivity in the world. While attuned, when you or another friendly creature you can see would take damage, you may choose to, as a free action, share of your blessing so the pain is highly diminished, making it so the damage taken is reduced to a mere 1, instead of whatever else it would be. This feature may be used a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, regaining uses at dawn.

If this item is attuned at the same time asYin's Blessing, its feature may be used an amount of times equal to your proficiency modifier instead, additionally, you may spend one of its uses to make use of Impose Balance, as described below Yin's Blessing.

item.name: Yearning Desire
entries: heavy This greatsword yearns for humanity, to become akin to a humanoid. This desire shall never be granted, forever remaining just a desire. Instead of metal, it seems to be made of bone, muscle and sinew, yet it is sharper than anything else you've ever seen.

You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it holds 5 charges, which you can spend to: Yearning, Calling. The sword absorbs and funnels a victims blood on hit in hopes that will make it feel more alive, yet ends up only funneling the life force into you. After dealing damage to a creature withYearning Desire, you may spend 1 charge to heal yourself for half the damage dealt.

Learn of Inner Humanity. You raise the sword with a clamour, bringing it down to cut a creature in two. Before you attack, you may spend 2 charges to cause your next attack to be considered a critical hit on a roll of 14-20, before modifiers.

Broken Speech. It likes to speak, although its false murmuring could never make it be considered truly sentient. By spending 1 charge, you may have the sword mimic the speech of any person you've heard within the last week.

This gives advantage to any checks to see through the lie that is this fake voice. Its intonation at parts is fully wrong, though, enough for close people to notice. If a creature tries to see through the lie and is closely familiar with the fake voice's origin, it has advantage on checks to discern the truth.
You gain one charge every time you kill a creature whose CR is equal to or higher than your level.

item.name: Yin's Blessing
entries: This dark-colored earring of a teardrop represents the entropy in the world. While attuned, when you take damage you may roll {@dice 1d8} as a free action. On a roll of 8 instead of taking the damage you would take, you instead are healed by the exact amount, as the energies of destruction and creation are swapped at the last moment.

You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, regaining expended uses at a long rest. If this item is attuned at the same time asYang's Blessing, the effect of this item activates on a roll of 4 or higher instead of just 8. Additionally, you may spend 2 charges to make use of Impose Balance, as described below.

item.name: Young Book of Vengeance
entries: Prerequisites: Be part of the Middle through a Subclass, Background or Feat.

This Book of Vengeance is awarded to all Young Brothers and Sisters of the Middle, and is connected to all other Books of Vengeance of the organization. Anything that is written in the book is shared among all Books of Vengeance, and no matter its size, it manages to magically contain every single page of vengeance. You can read its contents as a free action, and your DM will let you know whether there is any mission currently available for you to undertake and exact vengeance for the Middle.

Additionally, you can write down someone's name on the Book of Vengeance, and any other person that carries a Book of Vengeance will be able to read it and hunt that creature to earn the rewards below.
When you complete a quest from the Young Book of Vengeance, you gain the following benefits:

items: Until the next long rest, with every attack that you hit, you deal {@damage 1d6} extra damage of the same type as the attack.
Until the next long rest, you gain advantage on two ability checks of your choice.
You gain a single point of Inspiration that can be used until your next Long Rest.

entries: {@note Little siblings usually take easier quests, suited for players from levels 1 - 5. Young siblings take quests from levels 6 - 10, Big siblings take levels 11 - 17 and Great siblings take quests from levels 18 and above.}

item.name: Zone Clearance Mechanism
entries: {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}. price: 125 gp; 14 Dexterity - {@variantrule Adherent|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Adherent}, {@variantrule Durability|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|durability} (14), {@variantrule Sensor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Sensor} (30-ft.)

A steel box with keyholes centered around it’s faces. A disturbingly realistic eye can be seen from the inside, with faint breathing being heard when close. Inside it holds a complex set of retractable buzzsaws which jut out when activated, sweeping inside an entire area to clear it of any trespassers it can see.

When activated, all creatures within a 25-ft radius must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@dice 3d8} slashing damage and 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, or half that damage on a success.

feat.name: Adorable
entries: You are absolutely, irrevocably adorable when you wish to be! You gain the following:

items: Your Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain a +2 bonus modifier to {@skill Persuasion} Checks.

You may spend your Bonus Action during your turn to attempt to Charm a creature, forcing them to pass a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Charmed} for a minute. A creature {@condition charmed} this way suffers a -2 modifier to attack you or creatures friendly to you that are within 10-ft of you for the duration. The DC for this saving throw is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier. You may use this ability for an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per long rest, rounded down. A creature that has passed this saving throw has advantage against it for the next 24 hours.

feat.name: All Returns to Nihil
entries: This feature may be taken multiple times.

You have touched the primal essence of a deity, a powerful patron or one of the many Planes teeming with magic, and, sometimes, that magic changes you. During the first long rest after you have taken this feat, you can change your Class and Subclass to another one of your choice. All of your stats and your level remain, but all of your abilities will be swapped with the abilities of the newly chosen class and subclass. As such a massive change takes its toll on you, you gain 2 points of {@condition Exhaustion}.

feat.name: All-Devouring Maw
entries: Guts of iron, razor sharp teeth... You've got them all. You may eat anything and everything without a hassle, you gain a +5 to Constitution Saving Throws when ingesting poison, alcohol or any similar sort of effect inducing substances.

Additionally, you may use your action to consume even unnusual objects for a meal, such as swords and other kinds of weapons. Each consumed weapon counts as a full ration eaten. Additionally, once per day you may bite down a magic item to temporarily disrupt its energies, nearly leaving a dent in both it and your teeth.

For the next ten minutes, as long as the magic item is a tiny object, it loses all magical properties. Any ongoing effects coming from the item are immediately stopped, and they don't resume when the magic returns.

feat.name: Awe-Inducing
entries: Some have called you a terrific presence to be around, yet others are able to truly acknowledge your grandiosity, that feeling that makes one's heart stop and beat at your beck and call. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 22.

When your presence would cause a creature to become {@condition Frightened||frightened}, it instead becomes Reverent for the original duration. At the start of each of its turns while it can see you, a Reverent creature must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or have its speed reduced to 0 for that turn. It also has disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws while it can see you, and the DC of its concentration checks increases by 7.

prerequisite.other: Be able to cause the Frightened Condition, 16th level.

feat.name: Bayonet Combatant

entries: "The Thumb's chain of command is simple: Obey the orders issued by your superior unconditionally, and do not question the intentions of your superior."

The first shot should always be the best, then close in for close-quarters combat, impede their momentum, create openings for the superiors. Those are the orders of action that have been ingrained on you as a respectful warrior, and that is what you will act upon whenever the need arises. You gain the following:

items: You gain 6 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count before the first ranged weapon attack of your turn, losing that count afterward.

While wielding a ranged weapon that you can perform melee weapon attacks with you may spend your Reaction whenever you are targeted by a weapon attack to attempt to reflect it away with a clean swipe of your own. To do so you roll an attack roll against a DC equal to the attack against you, increasing your AC by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus on a success and potentially turning a hit into a miss.

entries: You may use this Reaction without spending your Reaction for an amount of times equal to however many leftover attacks you may have since the start of your last turn.

feat.name: Bloodarts Master
entries: You have become learned in the manipulation of blood. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Blood Arts
entries: You learn two Blood Arts from the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} ancestry:

entries.optionalfeature: In the Dark of the Night|TheUndertomesTO

entries: You can take this feat more than once.

prerequisite.other: You know at least one Blood Art; 4th level

feat.name: Body Sculpted in War
entries: After adventuring for a while, you've gained a great many deal of scars from your various encounters. Your skin is most likely hoarse to the touch after receiving so much damage, yet knowing your body is etched in the history of your exploits gives some pride, respite or an acknowledgement that you were there.
You receive the following benefits:

Your scars ache from time to time, yet you endure it. As a free action during your turn, you may choose to take 1 bludgeoning damage from them. You may do this a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, restoring expended uses on a short or long rest.

So much fighting has allowed you to better resist getting wounded once more. You may spend your reaction when taking any damage type besides force and psychic to gain resistance to that damage type until the start of your next turn. You may do this a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier, regaining expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Break and Enter
entries: Sometimes your targets cower beneath some shoddy door, box or wall; They really don't know what's coming. You can use your action to attempt to topple and destroy a non-wieldable nor worn object or wall by performing an {@skill Athletics} check against a base DC of 14 plus the modifier shown in the table below according to its material:

entries.caption: Material DC Modifier
rows: Wood
Stone
Metal

entries: You cannot break a wall that is thicker than 10-ft, and objects made of a material that is not listed above may have its modifier assigned as the one closest, as per the DM's discretion.
When you break a cover, you may spend your reaction to move to 5-ft around a creature who was benefitting from it and perform a melee weapon attack against them.

feat.name: Caffeinated

entries: "Alright, let me welcome you to our humble research team. Take this—I lost a bet today, so I've got to buy everyone a cup of joe."

Maybe you've lost a bet a few too many times or maybe you just love the stuff, it doesn't matter how you came to be like this, but you've become somewhat of a coffee lover, always being able to supply the stuff. You gain the following:

items: Your Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would put you to sleep or being knocked {@condition Unconscious} by means that aren't your Hit Points reaching 0, such as the {@spell Sleep} spell.
Your Passive Perception score increases by a value equal to your proficiency bonus.

During a long rest you can always provide your comrades with a fresh cup of joe, granting yourself and them a bonus to their Passive Perception score equal to half your proficiency bonus. This bonus modifier also applies to saving throws against being forced to sleep, as per described above. These last until each individual creature's turn end in combat after the long rest, or after 3 hours.

feat.name: Cardiae
entries: As a reaction that you take when you kill a non-undead, non-construct creature, you reach into their chest, grip their heart and remove it, replacing the emptiness of your chest with it. You can choose between substituting one of their stats with yours or acquire one of their traits or attacks.
After you finish a long rest, the heart will spoil and you will lose the ability, skill or substituted stat.
You can only have 1 stolen heart with this ability. If you steal a different one, the previous one immediately decays.

Designer's Note It’s recommended DM’s discretion when substituting a creature’s ability or skill. DMs will know best when an ability might break a campaign or when one of them is simply impossible to copy.

feat.name: Caving Mole
entries: The instincts and will of worms have gotten to you, and you have decided to join the moles in the dirt for their eternal dig, be it through frivolous use of your magic or the repeated stomping of your fists against even rock. You gain a burrowing speed of 25-feet, additionally, you may choose to leave a 5-foot by 5-foot tunnel in the wake of your digging. If you stay too long underneath the earth, you start losing track of what might be happening outside, as such you suffer from the {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} conditions if you finish your turn fully burrowed, losing these conditions upon re-emerging.

prerequisite.other: Strength or Spellcasting score equal or greater than 16, 4th level.

feat.name: Chained Wrath
entries: Your anger and rage only festers as you wait to unleash it, nearly bursting as any fight breaks out. Upon the start of a combat, you may choose to have your initiative be considered one for the rest of combat. If you do so, your first melee attack always has a bonus to hit damage equal to the number of creatures who acted before you, and double that number for its damage modifier.

prerequisite.other: Proficiency in martial melee weapons or unarmed attack, or Barbarian

feat.name: Courtly Poisoner
entries: You are a master poisoner, enjoying an uncanny ability to make incredibly potent substances. You gain the following effects:

items: Your choice of your Constitution, Intelligence or Wisdom Attribute Scores increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Any DC for your poisons is increased by a +2 bonus modifier.

You may create one Basic Poison (vial) per long rest, provided you have an Alchemist’s Kit. This Basic Poison has a base DC of 15 instead, and due to making it with more affordable materials it becomes inert and therefore unfit for sale after a long rest.

entries: The centipede-like thing donned a rotten sheet of cloth.
The cloth reeks of rotting bodies, like it was used to dress a corpse.
There are strange booklets hanging all over its body.“ “Looking closely, those are prayer books.
What does it believe in, and what does it pray for?

feat.name: Cunning Mockery Dangerous Musician
entries: You’ve learnt how to use the very instruments of your craft to produce melodies that not only entice but channel magic directly, making powerful soundwaves that can harm as easily as a bow being fired. You are considered proficient with any instrument of the same category as one you already are proficient in, such as being proficient in a Lute allowing you to use any other String Instrument as if you were proficient for the purposes of this feat. While wielding these following instrument categories, they have the following weapon properties, counting as ranged weapons:

Any area effects from Instruments start centered at you, and to use them you only perform one attack roll compared to the AC of every creature within reach, determining if you hit them using only your roll, such as if you roll a 15 on your attack roll you hit any creature with an AC of 15 or lesser, but miss any of those whose AC is higher than that value. You also roll the attack’s damage die only once.
{@condition Deafened} creatures are resistant to any damage from these weapons. You use Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity to use these weapons.
Brass {@dice 1d10} thunder damage Two-Handed, Loading Brass instruments fire a blast of music towards a 30-ft. long cone in any direction.
Bowed Strings {@dice 1d8} thunder damage Two-Handed, Range (60/80-ft.)

Bowed Instruments have a cadence to them, having their damage die increase by one step for each consecutive hit against a target, with {@dice 1d8} becoming {@dice 1d10} and so on. This is reset when you miss an attack or target another creature.
Percussion {@dice 1d10} thunder damage Two-Handed, Range (30/45-ft.)
Percussion instruments cause a quake around their target, making it so attacks made with it also target any creatures within a 5-ft radius of the initial target.
Plucked Strings {@dice 1d6} thunder damage Versatile({@dice 1d8})
Range (30/60-ft.) This weapon has no special properties.
