components.m: The Death sound of a star

entries: You clasp your hands together before slowly spreading them apart, causing giant claws of dust to appear above you and tear open the fabric of space all around, creating a gash into the cosmos and revealing a myriad of small stars which become stretched until they burst into an infernal flame that overtakes the entire area in blazing explosions and sheer destruction.

All other creatures within reach must pass a Constitution saving throw or suffer {@dice 18d8} fire damage and 8 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, or half that fire damage and count on a success. Disregarding if a creature passed or failed in this saving throw, for the next three rounds their {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count is not halved at the end of their turns after suffering the conditions damage, instead being doubled instantly as the flames take on an overwhelming {@skill nature}, also dealing d8s of fire damage instead of d4s.
All creatures that fail this saving throw cannot benefit from resistance or immunity to fire damage.

spell.name: Unpromised Faith

components.m: A weapon to be the spell's target and a marble

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: If you cast this spell by spending a 3rd Level Spell slot or higher, the bonus granted and it’s limit are increased by one and the value for breaking the weapon is increased by 20 for each second Spell Slot Level spent above 1st. ( Ex: Casting this spell at 3rd Level would grant it’s target gains a +2 bonus to a maximum of +3, but breaks on a roll of 61 or greater on it’s d100. )

You hold up the marble and think of the targets weapon, causing the marble to flicker quickly between a bright golden light and a shallow blue glow. You point to a weapon within reach and roll a d100. On a roll of 80 or lower, the weapon becomes a magic weapon if it wasn’t before and gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls. If you roll an 81 or above, the weapon is shattered into pieces and broken, or loses all it’s magical properties for the duration of the spell if it is a magical weapon.
A weapon enchanted in this way may have a maximum modifier of +2, with the spell fizzling out and doing nothing if the target weapon already is at that limit or greater.

entries.name: Duration
entries: Until your next short or long rest

spell.name: Unwinding Pain
entries: You reach out to a creature within reach that you can see and envelop them in a green glow, forcing their body to retrace their recent steps, rewinding in real time. That creature must pass a Wisdom saving throw if unwilling or suffer the spells effects on a failure, those being having their hit point count reversed to what they were at the start of the target’s previous turns, with wounds being mended as if rewinding from when they were formed or any form of healing received just bursts off as a painful attack repeats without a blade.

If a target creature that was healed from becoming {@condition Unconscious} would lose their recovered hit points, they remain at a minimum of one hit point instead of becoming {@condition Unconscious} again. If a target creature that was knocked {@condition Unconscious} has their hit points restored to a point where they become conscious again they become dazed until the end of their next turn, suffering the whiplash from healing.
For the duration the creature suffers a -3 negative modifier to all their rolls.

spell.name: Varmin Tide

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, this spell’s poison damage and additional {@condition Larva|TheUndertomesASV} count infliction increase by {@dice 1d8} per spell level used above 2nd.

You cause a wave of dirty water to appear form the ground and crash over a 10-ft. long and 30-ft. wide line starting from a point within reach, having all the vermin and venom within spread to the targets. Any creature within that line must make a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@dice 2d8} poison damage and an amount of {@condition Larva|TheUndertomesASV} count equal to the damage taken by the creature, or half that damage on a succesful save.
If a target creature is already suffering from {@condition Larva|TheUndertomesASV}, they take {@dice 1d8} additional count of {@condition Larva|TheUndertomesASV} on a failed saving throw.

spell.name: Waves in Adagio

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you deal an additional {@dice 1d8} thunder damage for each slot level above 2nd.
You perform a drawn out melody, creating a wave of pure sound that washes over the ground in a slow movement.

When you do this, you create a 15-ft. long and 10-ft. wide cone that moves 10-ft. in a direction you choose as part of casting this spell. This movement happens at the end of your turns, lasting for up to three turns and becoming 5-ft. wider yet losing 5-ft. of its length per turn, until it vanishes.

Any creature who comes to share the same space as the wave must pass a Constitution saving throw or suffer {@dice 2d8} thunder damage and be knocked {@condition Prone}, or only suffer half that damage on a success.

spell.name: Weaver's Wright
entries: You fold the piece of cloth and consume it, then point to up to six creatures within reach. Each of those creatures is wreathed by a woven mantle of white that protects them from whatever is to come, granting them {@dice 2d10} + your Spellcasting modifier's worth of Temporary Hit Points.

While these Temporary Hit Points remain, any damage taken that exceeds their value is reduced instead to become however many Temporary Hit Points remain, as the mantle takes the brunt of any attack before it can be directed at its wearer.
Ex: If a cloth-wearing creature is dealt 26 damage and they have 15 Temporary Hit Points, they instead only take 15 damage from that source.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the amount of Temporary Hit Points granted increases by {@dice 2d10} for each other slot level above 4th.

spell.name: Weight of Binding
entries: Choose a creature within range. It must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, golden chains burst from the air and bind it. The creature is {@condition Grappled||Grappled} for 1 minute and takes {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage at the end of each of its turns while grappled. After taking this damage, it can make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against your spell save DC, ending the spell on a success.

spell.name: Weight of the Crown
entries: Much like what befalls a ruined kingdom, the weight of a crown is one that can make one sink to the ground with ease. You summon a giant spectral crown above a target creature within reach, which slowly comes to crush them after a certain amount of time. This happens upon your choice that you may take as a free action on the end of your target’s turn for the next minute, forcing them to make a Strength saving throw or be crushed alive by the dangling crown, having on eof the following effects:

If the target is standing atop hard ground such as bricks or metal, it is simply crushed, suffering {@dice 8d8} bludgeoning damage and having their movement speed reduced to 0-ft. until the start of their next turn, or only suffering half that damage on a success.

If the target is standing atop soft ground such as sand or dirt, it is sunk into the ground and blocked by the crown, becoming {@condition Restrained} for the next minute or until another creature spends their Action while within 5-ft of the crown to pry it off by passing a Strength check against your Spell Save DC.

spell.name: Wickerman's Brambles

components.m: A living leech you must swallow

entries: Not only skin can be turned into bark, nor will only it be bitten into by flame. Choose one creature within range, they are forced to pass a Constitution Saving Throw or have their veins slowly start to turn into wood. The searing pain from such causes them to be unable to focus well on anything, taking a -3 penalty to their attack rolls and Saving Throws.

This effect ends early if they take fire or lightning damage, as the wood inside their body rapidly catches onto a blazing inferno, causing the creature to take damage from that source as if it were vulnerable to it, or resistance if it was immune to these damage types, also taking an additional {@dice 3d8} damage of the respective type. At Higher Levels: When this spell is cast at a level higher than 5th, it deducts an additional -1 to the total penalty and deals an additional {@dice 2d8} damage by each second spell slot above 5th. ( 7th level and 9th level ).

spell.name: Will of Nihil

components.m: a Stone Statue that fits in your fist

entries: You produce a small stone statuette to contain all the willpower of hostile creatures within 120-ft. of you, forcing them to pass a Wisdom saving throw or suffer the following effects:

items: They lose Immunity against the {@condition Frightened} Condition if they were Immune to it. If they didn’t, they also have disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would cause them to be {@condition Frightened}. Any creature who suffers this Condition while under Will of Nihil’s effects also has their movement speed reduced to 5-ft.
They suffer a -3 negative modifier to their attack rolls and saving throws, which grows to become a further -1 negative modifier at the start of your subsequent turns, to a maximum value of -7.

They suffer Vulnerability against one damage type of your choice, declared when you first cast this spell. You may declare an additional damage type at the start of your subsequent turns, to a maximum of seven vulnerabilities.

entries: These effects last for the next minute or until the statuette is destroyed. It has an AC of 15 and 100 hit points, being Resistant to all but force damage, which it is Vulnerable to.

spell.name: Wind-Up Clock of Damocles

components.m: the minute hand of a pocketwatch

entries: The sounds of a clock ticking down can become infernal, and you're here to bring hell, after all. You point to a creature that you can see within range, it must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or suffer from perceiving a giant, sharpened clock hand dangling above their head, nearly dropping. This clock hand cannot be broken and will fall if the target creature fails to wind up the clock.

For the duration, whenever this creature is hit by an attack, it must perform a Concentration Check, and on a failure the clock hand falls as they miss their chance to wind-up the clock. The clock hand deals {@damage 6d10} piercing damage and inflicts the effects of the Slow spell to the target creature automatically, lasting for a minute. The clock hand may be dispelled through the {@spell dispel magic|PHB|Dispel Magic} spell or through breaking your concentration, and if the creature does not trigger the hand to fall during your spell's duration, it simply cracks and explodes into harmless golden dust.

spell.name: Woundwalking
entries: The eyes are the window to the soul, while you know the wounds are the doorways to the flesh. You point to a creature you can see within reach that is below half their maximum hit points, having your body unravel from your fingertip to your feet as if you were unspooling your flesh into thin air. You then instantly reappear from inside the target creatures open wounds and may choose to come out of their gashes as a full, re-structured body or safely reform your body in a looser form, being able to slip out without harming the creature. You reappear at an unnocupied space within 5-ft of the target.

If you chose to re-appear with your whole body formed, the creature must pass a Constitution saving throw or suffer {@dice 8d8} bludgeoning damage as your regrowing body violently erupts from their open wound, also having the next weapon attack performed against the target being done at advantage. On a succesful save, both you and the target take half this spells damage.

optionalfeature.name: Acceleration Chamber Maintenance
entries: You've scrounged up a set of bluepints to fit an Acceleration Chamber Mechanism and attach it to most weapons over the course of a long rest. You can have an amount of such Mechanisms created and installed equal to half your proficiency bonus at any given time, before you are required to scrap an existing one for pieces to make new prototypes.

A weapon that you modify to hold an Acceleration Chamber can spend Generic Acceleration Rounds to be activated. You also manage to create enough Rounds equal to twice the Reload value of Chambered weapons per long rest, provided you have the modified weapon in hand to be sure of its specifications. Attacks made with these weapons while activated grant 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and a +1 bonus modifier on the attack roll to the wielder. This count is gained before the attack roll itself.

The amount of Poise gained by Acceleration round spenditure increases to 3 when you reach 8th level in Artificer, then 4 at 12th and finally 5 at 16th. Additionally, when activated the wielder gains a +2 bonus modifier to hit instead of a +1 after you reach 12th level.
Due to the ever-rising price of ammunition and bullet regulations, these Rounds become inert and rendered useless on the next long rest after their creation.

optionalfeature.name: Aiding Scissors
entries: After you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors, the next attack that targets them has advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Alluminum Defender
entries: Instead of using the Steel Defender statblock for your metallic companion, you can use the {@creature All-Around Helper|TheUndertomesASF|All-Around Helper} statblock below. The same rules apply to it, except it gains an additional Hit Die and additional maximum hit points whenever you gain a level. The Hit Die has the size shown in its statblock. Additionally, it gains one additional attack when you reach 8th level and another when you reach 12th level.
At 10th level, you can order the {@creature All-Around Helper|TheUndertomesASF|All-Around Helper} to use its Thorough Cleaning action.

optionalfeature.name: Aura of United Guardians
entries: You not only exude the best you can give in a fierce aura, but also can bring forth the best in the allies near you. You, as a bonus action during your turn, may consume one use of your Channel Divinity to initiate an Aura of Union between you and any friendly creature within a 10-feet raius of you. You and those creatures gain a bonus to damage rolls equal to +2 for each friendly creature within that area.
This area increases following the Paladin's usual area increase.

optionalfeature.name: Avenger Fighting Style
entries: You would never let any harm brought upon your dear companions go unpunished. After a friendly creature within 30-feet of you takes damage, you gain a +2 to the first attack roll against its source. This bonus is not added to damage rolls.

optionalfeature.name: Bio-Venom Vial
entries: A vial of highly venomous cells that reproduce rapidly into small maggots that wriggle away and dig into a creature’s flesh when disturbed. You can use the venom in this vial to coat one slashing or piercing weapon ( lasting for three attacks ) or up to three pieces of ammunition. Applying the poison takes a bonus action. A creature hit by the {@condition poisoned} weapon or ammunition must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or take {@dice 4d4} acid damage and suffer {@condition Larva|TheUndertomesASV} count equal to the damage suffered, or only take half of that damage on a success. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute before drying.

optionalfeature.name: Bleeding Scissors
entries: Whenever you apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} with your Scrap Scissors, you apply that many counts + 2 instead. Additionally, friendly creatures within 5 feet of you apply 1 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when they hit a creature with a melee attack.

optionalfeature.name: Bleeding Spell
entries: Cost: (1 Point)

When a creature is hit or fails a saving throw against one of your damaging spells, you can spend 1 sorcery point to additionally make them suffer counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to half the spell’s level, rounded down.

optionalfeature.name: Blood Is Fuel

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As an action, you can spend 4 Blood Charges to cast {@spell enhance ability|PHB|Enhance Ability} on yourself. You can also spend an equal number of Blood Charges and Hit Dice to gain temporary hit points equal to the total rolled on the expended Hit Dice. Hit Dice spent this way are regained only when you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Bloody Coating

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As a bonus action, you can spend a number of Blood Charges up to your proficiency bonus to coat the weapon you are holding in Hardblood. For a number of turns equal to the charges spent, the weapon deals additional piercing damage equal to the charges spent and inflicts 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count on a hit. A coated ranged weapon produces its own Hardblood ammunition.

optionalfeature.name: Channel Divinity: Salinify The Improper
entries: Alternate feature to Channel Divinity:Turn the dead As an action, you present your holy symbol and utter a string of prayers to weaken the wicked. Up to six creatures of your choice that can see or hear you within 60-ft of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If they fail they become saltbound for 1 minute or until it is knocked {@condition Unconscious}.
A saltbound creature has their skin crack in spouting salt, weakening their body and spirit alike in a purifying burn.
Their Immunities are considered only Resistances for the duration and any Resistances are ignored.

optionalfeature.name: Chef-d'Œuvre Vorace

entries: "Je me déleste des mensonges dont on m'a affublé... et j'embrasse mon véritable moi!"

Your body wasn't all that emerged from your flesh cocoon, and it wasn't inert - You worked. Your bones and your mind, filled and fuelled by ecstasy as to make an accessory to cap your outfit no matter which shape it takes, a relic that would be fit to grant a god as a birthday gift. Choose one of the following items to emerge with, they are all Artefacts that you are always Attuned to, count as having the Mesmerizing property while being you wield them and you ultimately choose their appearance. These also become +4 Weapons while you are in {@condition Full Makeover|TheUndertomesCR} and you may switch your chosen item to another one when emerging from your Changing Room, automatically Attuning to them.

items: {@item Sac à Main Joyeux|TheUndertomesCR}
{@item Aiguille du Bonheur|TheUndertomesCR}

optionalfeature.name: Chokehold Fighting Style
entries: Grappling a creature is only half the job to one such as you, one must still deprive them of the very air to weather them down! When you grapple a creature, you may forgo any number of attacks to automatically deal {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage + your Strength modifier per attack spent like this, as you squeeze down the creature.

optionalfeature.name: Citizenship Unto the Masses

entries: "Come, let us build us a tower whose top may reach unto the stars! And the top of the tower we will write the words: Great is the world and its Creator! And great is Man!"

The City is good. The world is good. You are doing good by maintaining that order, and that is your responsibility that you have burdened with pride since the moment you were born, is it not? You may now assign Molds to other creatures as an Action by spending a Sorcerer spell slot to do so, choosing up to a number of creatures equal to one plus the spell slot level spent divided by three, also gaining the same effects you would as per your Inner Disharmony feature when spending such spell slots.

The order of your world benefits you the most, as it should, as is good. With each building block set in place for your society , a spectral force starts emanating from behind you. You are under the following effects:

items: At the start of your turns you gain {@condition Charge Barrier|TheUndertomesPH} equal to the amount of Bricks of the Tower. within 120-ft. of you. You may use a Free Action at the start of your turn to reduce your count of the Condition by any number and transfer the same value to another creature you can see within the same range.

After having at least three Bricks of the Tower. present within 120-ft. of you, you gain an additional Turn at Initiative Count 1. ( Always acting last. ) You cannot move during this turn and may instead only use it to cast a spell as an Action or Bonus Action.

Upon having nine Bricks of the Tower. within 360-ft. of you a manifestation of the society you envision appears around the same area, as per your design. While within it, you and friendly creatures gain a +2 bonus to their AC and you may cast any sorcerer spell of your choice that you know as if you were spending a 9th level spell slot without spending any spell slots. This spell automatically hits any creature that it targets ( or forces them to fail their saving throw. ) and it's effects automatically succeed. A creature may spend three uses of Legendary Resistance to still resist this effect.

entries: After casting a spell in this way the 120-ft. area around you is permanently shaped in your image at Initiative count 0, with structures rising from the ground as per your view. Creatures may be moved in the moment where all changes. You are always considered to have nine Bricks of the Tower. while within this range, also gaining 3 {@condition Charge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns and having your {@item Machine Coil|TheUndertomesPH} always be considered a +4 magic weapon and focus for your spells.

When first taking this feature you may choose to have your creature type become Construct as well as Humanoid, with you growing metallic features, such as your limbs becoming robotic in nature or your voice losing the capability to display emotion fully , instead becoming a harmonized amalgam of various synthesized noises.

optionalfeature.name: Collective's Pocket Watch
entries: This pair of magic pocket watches is inscribed with a particular series of runes to track any who match its own. Once per long rest a creature may spend their action to use their Pocket Watch as an Arcane Focus to cast the {@spell Locate Object} spell targeting all other Watches who match its inscription.
You may take this Infusion repeatedly, creating another pair of Collective's Pocket Watches that may also be linked to the first ones.

optionalfeature.name: Combination Tactician
entries: Upon choosing this boon, you gain access to Combo Tactics, special melee weapon attacks that you can use as a free reaction ( A reaction that doesn't spend your reaction ) to perform after a friendly creature hits a target within your melee range, to do this you must consume one Ammo.

entries.name: Steadying Combo.
entries: You aim to throw the target back and forth between you and an ally, using the enemy's momentum to build up a stance, granting you and the friendly creature your Proficiency Bonus {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks.

entries.name: Bedazzling Combo.
entries: With a swift swipe of your hands, you nab right in the eyes when an opening is made, having them suffer a penalty equal to your Proficiency Bonus to hit until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Piledriver Combo.
entries: You direct your ally to use full force alongside you, pushing the enemy back for up to 5 * your Proficiency Bonus feet on a failed Strength Save, also causing the target to fall {@condition Prone}. If the target hits a wall during this reaction, they take {@dice 3d8} bludgeoning damage.

In addition to this, any Marksman Weapons you use are considered to have a Special property which causes them to be considered Martial Melee weapons that you are proficient with, in addition to being Marksman Weapons. You do not suffer disadvantage from firing at close-range with these weapons, yet cannot spend Ammo to increase your damage dealt.

optionalfeature.name: Contractual Enactment
entries: Instead of entering a blind rage, your barbaric enactments of violence come elsewhere, from a contract or pact with someone or something from far away, far from what you'd initially think at least. By using a bonus action to start your contractual enactment, you unleash your given power like a congealed tempest, for the next minute you gain the following benefits: You have advantage on Charisma checks and Charisma saving throws. You may use Charisma for your attack and damage rolls.
When you make a melee weapon attack using Charisma, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll. This bonus increases as you level. You have your tongue and magical, chiding words as a natural weapon.

It has a range of 30 feet and deals {@damage 1d8} psychic damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while enacting. Your contractual enactment lasts for 1 minute.

It ends early if you are knocked {@condition Unconscious||unconscious} or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your enactment on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have enacted your contract the maximum number of times for your barbarian level, you must finish a long rest before you can enact it again.
You may rage 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.

optionalfeature.name: Copying Spell
entries: cost varies By spending Sorcery Points, you can use an action to cast a spell you witnessed another creature within 30 feet of you cast within the last turn, as long as it doesn’t have Material components. You can spend Sorcery Points equal to the Spell Level table below instead of a spell slot to cast it:

optionalfeature.name: Cornering Fighting Style
entries: Instead of using your weaponry only to tear apart, you've also come to use it as a pin to stop your targets dead in their tracks. Whenever you attempt to Grapple a creature, you may use a melee weapon you are wielding instead of a free hand. Whenever you do so, you may also choose to roll an attack roll for the Grapple's contested check instead of an Athletics check.
Additionally, if the target willingly breaks free you may spend your Reaction to make a melee weapon attack against them. You do not add your ability modifier to this attack's damage on a hit.

optionalfeature.name: Critical Goggles
entries: A pair of goggles that analyze moments of incredible failure for others to turn them into moments of incredible success for you. Whenever a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you scores a Critical Failure, you can add 1 charge to the glasses, to a maximum of 3. You can spend 1 charge of the glasses to give yourself advantage on your next roll, or 3 charges to treat your next d20 roll as a 20.

optionalfeature.name: Critical Scissors
entries: Your attack rolls with your Scrap Scissors can score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

optionalfeature.name: Cross Stitch Explosives
entries: You managed to create a densely packed mess of strings and needles that explode when pressed in the wrong way. Once per Long Rest you may create one {@item Stitchwrap Bomb|TheUndertomesTO|Stitchwrap Bomb}, and a second one upon reaching 12th Level in Artificer. You cannot create more than what your Level permits at any given time, yet repair them at no additional cost.
See {@item Stitchwrap Bomb|TheUndertomesTO} for the deployable tool created by this infusion.

optionalfeature.name: Cunning Mockery
entries: Alternate Arcane Trickster Rogue feature, Replaces {@spell Mage Hand} Legerdemain 3rd-level feature.

While most others who dabble in your less than savoury arts and the arcane traditions at the same time, they tend to have it so they can best employ sticky fingers unseen to the eye. You’ve grown to be just the contrary, preferring to be the main attraction and still take the chance to hit in the silent moments between laughter and screaming. You learn the Vicious Mockery cantrip instead of {@spell Mage Hand} as part of your Arcane Trickster Spellcasting Feature and your Vicious Mockery cantrip gains the following traits:

items: When you use Vicious Mockery, the target creature has disadvantage on a number of their next attack rolls and {@skill Perception} checks equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
The spell’s damage becomes {@dice 1d6} instead of {@dice 1d4}.

You may choose to target an additional target creature within reach per damage die this cantrip would deal, but dealing one less damage die on a hit, to a maximum of 4 separate targets and {@dice 1d6} psychic damage.

optionalfeature.name: Cursed Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 1 count of {@condition Curse|TheUndertomesHT}. This count increases to 2 upon reaching level 9.

optionalfeature.name: Depraved Consumption

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: While you have fewer than half your maximum Blood Charges, you can use your action to consume a corpse within 5 feet. You regain hit points and Blood Charges based on the size of the creature:

entries.caption: Depraved Consumption
rows: Tiny
Small
{@dice 1d4 + 1}
Medium
{@dice 2d6 + 2}
Large
{@dice 3d6 + 4}

entries: You gain these benefits only if the corpse belonged to a creature that had blood and was not summoned, such as a rat produced by a Bag of Tricks.

optionalfeature.name: Discard Self
entries: Ki Cost: 1 There are teachings of which it is said that to fully be free from the influences of the world, you must cut yourself from it, embracing the thoughts of becoming nothing and thus learning how to be your own person. You may apply that thought process as an action during your turn by spending 3 Ki Points, gaining the following bonuses for the next minute:

items: You instantly end the {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Frightened} conditions if you were suffering from either and gain advantage against being afflicted by them for this effects duration.
You gain advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Investigation} checks to perceive the presence illusions and to discern that another creature is suffering from an enchantment.

entries: You may also use your Wisdom modifier in place of Intelligence for {@skill Investigation} checks.

optionalfeature.name: Disruptive Attack
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike swiftly and cause a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can reduce a value of damage you would take by {@dice 1d6} for a creature's opportunity attack after you provoke it. The next attack against the creature has advantage, in addition, if you have advantage granted by another creature to attack a hostile creature, for the first attack during your turn you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage.
The amount of the extra damage reduced and dealt increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table. The die size remains the same.

optionalfeature.name: Divided Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors can now be split into two separate blades for each hand. When separate, they each count as a {@item handaxe|PHB} you are proficient with, with the exception that they also have the finesse property. You may unite or separate them as a free action.

optionalfeature.name: Dulling Strike
entries: Ki Cost: 2 Emptying your own mind isn’t nearly enough anymore, what you have learnt to perform is a strike to fully have all senses vanish from your target, so they too may attempt to reach some type of enlightenment. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, the target must pass a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Deafened} and unable to Concentrate on spells. These effects last for a minute, with the creature being able to attempt another Constitution saving throw at the end of their following turns, choosing to recover from one of these effects on each successful save.

optionalfeature.name: Emergency Exit Cutter
entries: You have created a small backpack packed with a foldable sawblade that extends to sink to the ground and cut your way out on a whim. You may spend your action to use the saw to either attack a creature, cut a hole or make a breakaway as follows:

Buzzcut Attack. You swipe the riveting sawblade down toward a creature within 15-ft. of you must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Artificer spell save DC or suffer your proficiency modifier’s worth of d8 slashing damage and half that amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, rounded down. On a success they only suffer half that d8 slashing damage.
Diamond Cutter. You use your saw to loudly cut open a doorway for you and your fellows. That doorway must be at least a 5-ft. by 5-ft. cube and at maximum a 15-ft.
by 15-ft. cube, with the saw being able to penetrate up to 5- ft. times your proficiency bonus of material. This is exceptionally loud, being easily heard by any creature within 600-ft.

Cut a Getaway. You sink your saw into the ground and have it hoist you up through a mechanical arm, moving in a line against the surface you attach to for up to 20-ft. times your Proficiency Bonus’ worth, being able to latch onto walls and ceilings with ease. If you would end your movement near a square that you could stand upright, such as climbing a cliffside and stop atop of it you may simply slow down the saw to do so safely.

optionalfeature.name: Enchanting Words
entries: Alternate Arcane Trickster Rogue feature, Replaces Versatile Trickster 13th-level feature.

Your way with words your continued use of Vicious Mockery has opened a way for many more means of taking advantage of any creature who falls for your irritation or adoration. You may spend a spell slot and attempt to infuse your words with a magical charisma, performing a {@skill Persuasion} check against a number of creatures that can hear and understand you within a 60-ft. radius equal to the spell slot level spent. Each target creature must pass an {@skill Insight} check against your {@skill Persuasion}, becoming {@condition Charmed} for the next minute on a failure.

A creature {@condition charmed} this way suffers a negative modifier to attack rolls against you and creatures friendly to you equal to half the spell slot level spent, with a minimum of a -1 negative modifier. Furthermore, you have advantage on weapon attacks against any creature {@condition Charmed} in this way.

optionalfeature.name: Encroaching Fighting Style
entries: You arrive like a disease, silently waiting for your target to slip up and take their eyes away from a second, and then deliver your terrifying blows. You have a +2 to damage rolls against creatures that are {@condition Blinded||blinded} or otherwise can't see you, such as if they can't see through darkness.

optionalfeature.name: Eyes on the Prize

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As an action, you can spend 3 Blood Charges to focus your senses. You instantly detect the location of any creature with blood within 120 feet of you, seeing a faint afterimage as if it had been pinged by a submarine's radar. This sense is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.
If you extract blood from a creature you've downed within the next minute, you gain 2 Blood Charges instead of 1.

optionalfeature.name: Fading Memories Pact Boon
entries: There are some moments during your day where foreign yet eerily beloved memories flash into your head, just when you're in the moment they seem all that much clearer, yet that has anything else you don't perceive pass by as if it were never there. During combat, you have a +1 to your rolls against or related to creatures directly engaged to you in combat, or those within 5-feet of you. In contrast, you suffer a -1 penalty to your rolls against or related to creatures who are not engaged to you during combat.

optionalfeature.name: Faker's Grenade
entries: This adorably adorned bomb resembles a hedgehog, but packs a horrible punch. Once per Long Rest you may produce one of these items and use them to cast the {@spell Metalboom|TheUndertomesDX} spell as an Action.
Due to the nature of this bomb, you have a +5 bonus to Rolls pertaining to hiding it within your person as if it were a toy.
Upon reaching 10th level you may use this feature twice per long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Family Heirloom

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You create a relic small enough to hold in one or both hands. While it is on your person, you can store excess Bloodfeast in it during a long rest, up to an amount equal to your level + your proficiency bonus. As a bonus action, you can retrieve any amount of that stored Bloodfeast.
If the heirloom is lost or destroyed, you can rebuild it during a long rest using 50 gp of fine materials.

optionalfeature.name: Favored Bullet
entries: You name one of your Magic Bullets as your favorite, exacerbating its effects when you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesMK}, as shown in the Favored Bullet table.

entries.caption: Favored Bullet
rows: The 1st Magic Bullet
A creature hit by this bullet always takes force damage equal to your warlock level, regardless of whether it succeeded on or failed the saving throw.
The 2nd Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw becomes {@condition Paralyzed|PHB} until the start of your next turn, except attacks made within 5 feet of it are not automatically critical hits.
The 3rd Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw deals only half the damage it rolls for the effect's duration.
The 4th Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw also suffers 4 counts of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesMK}.
The 5th Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw has its AC reduced by your proficiency bonus until the end of your next turn.
The 6th Magic Bullet

All creatures within range suffer an additional {@damage 1d6} fire damage for every combined 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count among the targets, to a maximum of {@damage 8d6} additional fire damage.
The 7th Magic Bullet
Whenever you or a creature you hit with an attack suffers a critical hit, or rolls a 1 on a saving throw you impose, that creature is beheaded as though by a {@item vorpal sword|DMG|Vorpal Sword}.

entries: The Seventh Magic Bullet is the only exception: its favored effect is always active. If you are beheaded, you instantly die.

optionalfeature.name: Fighting Style: Sacrifice
entries: As a Reaction when you see a friendly creature within 30 feet of you miss an attack roll, you may immediately use your remaining movement speed to jump towards them and make an attack roll against the creature they tried to hit if it is within reach. If you're successful, you deal damage to both creatures, but an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage to the creature you hit. This damage cannot be diminished or prevented in any way, and they suffer any statuses as normal.

optionalfeature.name: Foi Inébranlable

entries: "Arrgh... La Voix, je... la Voix a disparu...! Pourquoi m'as-tu abandonné?! Non, non, non...!"

The cocoon and you are one of the same, the only real change is that you accepted it - ripped off the roots which clung to your heart to create a void and filled it with whatever your stomach desires. Whenever you enter your *Changing Room*, you leave its doors open - expanding your body in an amalgam of flesh that lashes and tears at the world with little pause to give. It has the following changes:

items: You stay in your Changing Room for one minute and are considered to be Raging for its duration, with you being able to leave only after being killed or instantly leaving it by suffering the effects of the {@spell Calm Emotions|PHB} spell.
You may still use your Action and Bonus Action as normal.

You retain two additional Reactions which may be used the uses of Griffe à Coudre and Goûter à la Mode abilities, as previously described. These still cost {@condition Pulsation|TheUndertomesCR} count, but those costs are halved.
Your Armor Class increases by a value equal to half your proficiency bonus.
You inflict 2 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on attack rolls against creatures that damaged you since the end of your last turn.

You gain two additional arms that sprout from your back. Both count toward wielding weapons you are proficient with and they may be used to benefit from Two-Handed or Versatile weapons. Additionally, all of your hands count as natural weapons that you are proficient with which have the Finesse and Mesmerizing property and deal {@dice 2d4} slashing damage and 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.
All your natural weapons are considered to be +2 weapons, becoming +3 weapons upon you reaching 16th level.
You cannot gain the {@condition Full Makeover|TheUndertomesCR} Condition anymore.

entries: Additionally, your maximum Hit Points permanently increase by {@dice 2d12} plus double your Constitution modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Friendly Warning
entries: This magic item is a magical flare who functions by spending an Action to cast the {@spell Skywrite|XGE} spell with the changes that it may only vanish after one minute passes and you may choose which creatures are able to see the message as long as you know how they look like. Furthermore, any creature within a mile that can see this gains a bonus to {@skill Perception} checks equal to half your Intelligence Modifier (rounded down) and cannot be Surprised.
After casting the spell like this, this Infusion desintegrates into dust and you may take a new Artificer Infusion during a Long Rest.

optionalfeature.name: Frightening Scissors
entries: After hitting a creature with your Scrap Scissors, you can force them to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 turn. A creature affected by this can repeat their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Gluttonous Attack
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you've gained a knack for performing particularly violent gashes and being filled with vitality from the motivation of each blow struck. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll, and you regain hit points equal to half the additional damage dealt. The attack must use a melee weapon with either the finesse or heavy property.

You don't need advantage on the attack roll if the target is below half its hit point maximum, isn't {@condition Incapacitated||incapacitated}, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. The extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

optionalfeature.name: Grappling Blast
entries: When you hit a creature with eldritch blast, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition Grappled} until the end of its next turn. After a creature fails this saving throw, they become immune to it for the next 10 minutes.

optionalfeature.name: Green Slime Brewing
entries: You have learnt how to produce a substance that can act both as an extremely powerful glue at the same time that in right dosages it can be downright toxic, being able to apply a few uses of the substance on your hands. You may create an amount of objects using this glue equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. These objects are your choice between Toxic Goop Canisters and Lockdown Solutions, but after a long rest the substance hardens and can’t be used anymore.
You may use your Artificer spell save DC instead of these items when you use them.

optionalfeature.name: Hard to Kill
entries: No one will be allowed to put you down, not until your body finally gives out. You gain the following benefits: Your Constitution or Wisdom score is increased by 1, to a maximum of 20. If you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious} by being reduced below one hit point, you instead stay half-awake in the {@condition Semi-Conscious|TheUndertomesASF} condition, which only ends after you've been healed by a third of your maximum HP, rounded up.

While {@condition Semi-Conscious|TheUndertomesASF}, you stay awake and may perform actions and so on as usual, with the penalties of having your movement speed reduced in half, your AC reduced by -4 and your rolls having a -4 penalty.

optionalfeature.name: Hardblood Armaments

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 Blood Charge to coalesce your blood into a Hardblood Armament. Choose whether it deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, then choose one of the following configurations:

entries.name: Brutality
entries: The armament deals {@damage 1d12} damage and has the heavy and two-handed properties.

entries.name: Swift Execution
entries: The armament deals {@damage 1d6} damage and has the finesse and light properties. You can create a secondary Hardblood Armament for two-weapon fighting; the secondary armament deals {@damage 1d4} damage.

entries.name: Rain Death
entries: The armament deals {@damage 1d6} damage and has the finesse and thrown (30/60) properties. It dissolves into mist after it hits or misses, and you can resummon it to your hand as a free action.
You must use a bonus action and spend 1 Blood Charge to change your Hardblood Armament's configuration. You are proficient with your Hardblood Armament.

During a long rest, you can bathe a magic weapon in the blood used for your Hardblood Armament. At the end of the rest, the armament gains that weapon's magical properties. The consumed magic item loses all its magical power, which flows into your Hardblood Armament. The armament is magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance to nonmagical attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Harmonize Spell
entries: For a two Sorcery points, you may better make use of your blood lineage through literally supplying that source onto your spells for better damage. When you cast a damage- inflicting spell, you may choose to take a number of your hit die in damage to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus, after doing so the cast spell deals the same amount of additional die in damage, the die size and damage is equal to the spell's. If the spell has multiple die listed, you choose which to add onto.

optionalfeature.name: Headshot Focus Fighting Style
entries: You are particular with where you aim your weaponry, focusing for a quick and clean kill whenever able. Whenever you target a creature that has a head with a ranged weapon attack, you may choose to Aim For the Head. When you do so, the following applies:

items: The Target's Armor Class is increased by their proficiency bonus.
You cannot hit the target unless you beat their AC, regardless of scoring a Critical Hit.
If you would Critically Hit yet miss the targets AC, you still roll damage, dealing half that amount as your shot grazes them.
You Critically Hit on this attack with a Critical Threshold reduced by 2, such as rolling an 18-20 on your dice, before any modifiers.

optionalfeature.name: Hemomancy

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You're particularly adept at controlling your own blood, and soon that of other creatures. You learn Sanguine Authority when you select this Blood Art, Hemorrhaging Gashes at 3rd level, and Exsanguinate at 5th level. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells. You can cast them by spending Blood Charges equal to the spell's level; Sanguine Authority costs no Blood Charges.

optionalfeature.name: Higher Presence

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You gain proficiency in Persuasion if you aren't already proficient, and you can spend 2 Blood Charges to cast {@spell command|PHB|Command}.

A Bloodfiend of lesser rank, or a creature whose level or CR is no greater than half your level rounded up, has disadvantage on the saving throw. A Bloodfiend of greater rank automatically succeeds. A creature whose level or CR is greater than half your level rounded up has advantage on the saving throw.

optionalfeature.name: Hit Like a Train
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to put everything you have in a single blow. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to hit like a train. Doing so makes you forgo any extra attacks you would have during your turn, including opportunity attacks, but you gain advantage on this attack roll and deal {@dice 2d8} additional damage equal to your weapons damage type, as well as additional d8 for each attack you forewent for this.
However, attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Homely Porta-Home
entries: You have managed to make a piece of minimizing technology able to contain an entire house, albeit small, onto a single briefcase for safe and portable solution to your problems.
You create a Homely Porta-Home, which can be deployed remotely as an action provided no creatures are within the briefcase’s reach as a full house, which is a 60-ft. wide, 20-ft.

long and 10-ft. tall rectangle. When in its house mode the Porta-Home holds no furniture except for lights and bedding for you and your companions if you so choose, but can be furnished however you want. You may use any Artisan’s Tools as a material to create workstations inside the Porta-Home which function as the supplied Artisan’s Kit, except a creature using it also has a +2 on any check using that Kit.

The Porta-Home automatically has the Alarm spell cast around a 20-ft radius of it’s extremities and may be retrieved as an action provided that no creature is inside it, using a complex magic to shrink down and compartmentalize all furniture inside while holding it in place, becoming a simple briefcase of your design which weighs 2 lb. and may be used as a weapon ( light hammer ) if needed. While being a full house the Porta-Home also has wheels which makes it function like a wagon if needed.

optionalfeature.name: Hungry for More

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: When you would be reduced below 1 hit point, you can spend 2 Blood Charges to remain at 1 hit point until the end of your next turn. This cost increases by 1 each time you use it during the same combat and returns to its original cost after a long rest. You also gain 1 level of exhaustion each time you use this feature.

optionalfeature.name: Impose Balance
entries: Sometimes, your will falls in place with that of the very universe. As a reaction to when another creature would roll a dice within a 60-feet radius of yourself, after the result is shown, you may change it to become the inverse of what it should be, such as a 15 becoming a 5 or vice versa. A roll of 10 does not change.

optionalfeature.name: In the Dark of the Night

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of red and black. You can spend 2 Blood Charges to touch a willing creature and grant it the same darkvision for 1 hour.

optionalfeature.name: Judgmental
entries: During combat, whenever you witness a creature within 30 feet of you scoring a Critical Failure on an attack roll or a saving throw, you gain advantage on your next attack roll or saving throw.

optionalfeature.name: Junk Surprise
entries: You create one of the following traps during a long rest: (A) a {@trap Jawgrind Trap|TheUndertomesDX}, (B) an {@trap Explosive Trap|TheUndertomesDX} or (C) an {@trap Detector Trap|TheUndertomesDX}.

You set them down by spending an Action to do so, and may spend an Action to retrieve them after they have been used. You may re-prime them during a Long Rest. Upon reaching 10th level you may create two traps.
You may refer to the Traps section for each of the Traps.

optionalfeature.name: Little Fun Guy
entries: This little blue guy is just the best, it is sometimes sporting a vaguely humanoid shape despite being the size of a human fist and a mushroom-cap that’s way too big sprouting out of it’s head, or manifesting as other type of fungi. It is sentient and can speak in words that don’t exist, often sounding like a bunch of noise that somehow conveys its intention and needs. Little Fun Guys tend to have an easy going and fun-loving personality, and that grants you a +1 bonus modifier to {@skill Persuasion} and {@skill Nature} skill checks, as it aids both in the sense of being adorable and recognizing plant life.

During a long rest, the Little Fun Guy also brings you a gift that it made by itself, that being your choice from a Potion of Healing (Common) or a Potion of Poison, except it deals {@dice 1d4+1} poison damage instead of {@dice 3d6}. Both of these lose their potency after 24 hours, turning into a mildly tasty beverage with no additional effect.

Once per long rest you may spend your bonus action to hoist the Fun Guy over your shoulder, having them breathe out a nasty spore cloud on a target creature within 15-ft., that target creature must pass a DC 13 saving throw or become incredibly itchy until the start of your next turn, making them suffer a -1 negative modifier to attack rolls for the duration. These mild spores are strong enough that even constructs and undead are affected.

optionalfeature.name: Manor Master
entries: You gain a +1 modifier to attack and damage rolls the following objects as improvised weapons:

items: Any form of cutlery, such as knifes, forks or spoons.
Any type of plates, mugs and cups.

Chairs and small pieces of furniture, such as stools, pillows and candlestick holders. While wielding any of these, they the first two listed items gain the Thrown (30/60ft.) property and the third gains the Thrown (15/30ft.) property. You deal {@dice 1d4} damage of slashing type for knifes, piercing for forks and bludgeoning for spoons.

entries: You deal {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage for plates, mugs and cups and you deal {@dice 1d8} damage with Chairs and other Small Furnitures, which also have the Versatile ({@dice 1d10})
property. When thrown, these deal {@dice 1d12} damage and break instead.
Furthermore, while wearing light gloves ( such as leather or linen ) they count as unarmed weapons you are proficient in, dealing {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage and having the Finesse property.

optionalfeature.name: Manufacturing Armorer
entries: You've come to take comfort in the repetitive process of creating bullets to fit all sizes and needs. Over the course of a long rest you create up to your double your proficiency modifier's worth of specialized ammunition. These bullets can be any combination of "Generic" Ammunition such as Acceleration Rounds, Armor-Piercing Rounds and etc. You may only create bullets of Uncommon rarity until 12th level, where you can then create up to Rare rarity and finally creating Very Rare ammunition upon reaching 16th level.
The quality of your bullets also increases accordingly, being considered +1 ammunition upon you reaching 6th level, +2 ammunition after 12th level and then +3 ammunition upon reaching 16th.
These bullets are powerful at the cost of wringing everything their materials have out, rendering them useless if not used until your next long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Marksman's Repositioning
entries: Sometimes what you need is not the perfect shot, but something to distract opponents while you make a getaway. You learn the {@spell eldritch blast|PHB|Eldritch Blast} cantrip, and it does not count against your warlock cantrips known. When you cast {@spell eldritch blast|PHB|Eldritch Blast}, you can have each bolt deal {@damage 1d4} force damage instead. A target's attack and damage rolls are reduced by 1 for each bolt that hits it. Furthermore, your speed increases by 5 feet until the end of your turn for each bolt fired.

optionalfeature.name: Master of Training
entries: After reaching the apex of your craft, there is nothing else to do but teach it forward. You have decided that everything you’ve learned will not be eroded by the sands of time.

items: If you are a Fighter, Barbarian, Ranger or a Paladin, you can train a willing creature for a year. After that, they gain the Warrior Sidekick Class.
If you are a Rogue, Monk, Artificer, Bard or Ranger, you can train a willing creature for a year. After that, they gain the Expert Sidekick class.
If you are a Wizard, Warlock, Sorcerer, Bard, Druid or Cleric, you can train a willing creature for a year. After that, they gain the Spellcaster Sidekick class.

entries: “Rumor has it this Abnormality was chosen to be used for training as it is the most docile and tame of any that we have extracted. It’s called a training dummy “rabbit”, but it doesn’t seem to enjoy carrots. It likes people.
If it escapes, it is merely following the employee as they leave its Containment Unit.”

optionalfeature.name: Mind-Clearing Clap
entries: Sometimes, a clear head is all it takes to achieve peace, be it for yourself or a friend in need. As a bonus action during your turn, you may spend 2 Ki points to clap your hands and let the sound wash away your worries for a moment, or those of a friendly creature within 15-feet of yourself. After doing so, the target has advantage on their next Wisdom Saving Throw for the next minute.

optionalfeature.name: Mirrorwalk Blast
entries: You can cast {@spell Eldritch Blast} through any small or larger object that has a reflective surface within 30 feet of you, using that surface as the starting point for the spell's range.

optionalfeature.name: Molar Scissors
entries: Instead of attacking a creature, you may choose to grapple them with your Scrap Scissors instead. You may choose to perform an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) ability check instead of a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) ability check for the grapple, and you may perform the ability check with advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Monocle of Breaking Down
entries: This magic item is some form of eyewear that was enchanting to better understand the properties of other objects. You can spend an Action with it to cast the {@spell Identify} Spell at will, also being able to spend an Action to determine the main material of an object you can see, such as a barrel being made majoritarily of wood or a fine suit being made of linen.

optionalfeature.name: Nailing Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 2 counts of {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesHF}. This count increases to 3 upon reaching level 9.

optionalfeature.name: Naturalist Master Fighting Style

prerequisite.other: {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} or Druid, Fighter, Ranger, or Sorcerer

entries: While you wield no weapon or shield in either hand, your natural weapons gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls against targets below half their hit point maximum.
You deal 2 additional damage of your natural weapon's damage type.

optionalfeature.name: Needled Lacing

prerequisite.other: A suit of armor or set of clothes; requires attunement

entries: With a lining of spikes or other jagged points, this piece of wear has become something that should be handled with care or have someone incur dire consequences.

When an attuned creature suffers damage from another creature within 5-ft, they may spend their reaction to have the item's pointy ends flare out as they are coated by spilled blood. The attacking creature must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer {@damage 2d4} piercing damage and 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count. On a success, they suffer half the damage and half that {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count, rounded down.

This damage increases by {@dice 1d4} and you deal an additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count when you reach 6th Level in Artificer ({@dice 2d4}, 3 Count) and once more when you reach 12th Level in Artificer ({@dice 3d4}, 4 Count).

optionalfeature.name: Neverending Pain
entries: You won't be boggled down by what lowlifes such as your enemies attempt to afflict you with. By spending a Superiority Die and a bonus action, you may instantly end one condition afflicting you and you may, as a reaction to when you do so. you may perform a weapon attack against any target within your reach, dealing your Superiority Die in additional damage thats equal to the weapon's damage.

optionalfeature.name: Nihilation Blast
entries: You can cast {@spell Eldritch Blast} through infusing it with a severe energy conjured from the vast nothing of the astral sea, imbuing it with a voiding property. Creatures hit by your {@spell Eldritch Blast} suffer a cummulative -1 negative modifier to perform the last action they performed, to a maximum modifier equal to your proficiency bonus. This action can be attempting an melee attack roll, a ranged attack roll, casting a spell or any differently named actions in a Stat Block. This lasts until the end of their turn, ending early if they take a different action during their turn.

optionalfeature.name: One Day Now, One Day Less
entries: You can't die, not yet, not now. There is more to be done. When you would suffer a failed Death Saving Throw, you may instead choose to have it become a success.

Whenever you do this, your Hit Points are permanently reduced by a value equal to half your hit die plus your Consittution modifier. This reduction cannot be lowered or restored by any means short of the Wish spell, as some scars will never heal, no matter how hard you try.

optionalfeature.name: Overheated Fueling Mechanism
entries: You create a gadget you can attached to a melee or ranged weapon to have it coat its edges with a dosage of overheated fuel, which starts blazing when exposed to air. You may spend your Bonus Action to ignite, causing your weapon attacks to inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count on hit until the end of your turn. You can use this an amount of times equal to Intelligence Modifier per Long Rest. This Infusion can also be used as an item, that being Uncommon and can be annexed to a weapon by Attuning to it. Instead of the users Intelligence Modifier, it uses their Proficiency Bonus to determine its maximum uses per Long Rest.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Broodmother
entries: Your patron grants you one of its dear children to protect and aid you in your ordeals. You gain the {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiar} spell and may cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.

As an action, once per short rest, you may summon handfuls of tiny creatures resembling the visage of your patrons brood and scatter them around all 5-foot squares surrounding yourself. A creature besides yourself moving into the a space with these creatures must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or step onto one of the tiny creatures, squashing them. Upon sensing harm come to even a vestige of its brood, your patron manifests a great spider leg or otherwise fitting weapon that automatically hits the transgressing creature, dealing {@damage 3d8} piercing damage to them.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} at 6th, 12th, 15th and 18th level. Any given space containing these creatures lasts for up to one minute after being created or until they are squished.

optionalfeature.name: Penitent Fighting Style
entries: For Fighter, Ranger & Paladin. The pain adorns your body like the hilt of a blade, wield it to its fullest. Whenever you take one tenth of your maximum hit points of damage in a single turn, you gain a +1 to hit for your next attack and damage rolls.
This effect does not stack.

optionalfeature.name: Perfected Marksman's Weapon
entries: You have a near-perfect connection with the Marksman, allowing you to make full use of its Marksman's Weapon. When you first summon it, you can choose its appearance, such as a rifle or longbow, although it functions as a longbow that accepts any kind of ammunition. You are considered attuned to your Marksman's Weapon at all times, and this counts against your attunement limit.

The Marksman's Weapon becomes a +1 weapon when you reach 5th level in the warlock class, a +2 weapon at 11th level, and a +3 weapon at 16th level. It also counts as an arcane focus for your warlock spells, granting the same bonus to your spell attack rolls and spell save DC. This bonus does not stack with other magic items.

During a long rest, you can perform a ritual to feed another magic item to your Marksman's Weapon. The consumed item is destroyed, and the Marksman's Weapon inherits its properties. It can consume only wondrous items and other magic weapons, and it can retain the properties of a maximum of three consumed items at a time. If it consumes another, you must choose one of the previous three sets of properties to be destroyed. Once per turn as a free action, you can change your Marksman's Weapon into any previously consumed weapon, inheriting its properties and damage. If it has consumed a total of three +3 weapons, it permanently has a +4 bonus instead and is considered a legendary magic item.

optionalfeature.name: Pinstack Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 2 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesHT}.

optionalfeature.name: Poisoned Spell
entries: {@b Cost:} 2 Sorcery Points
When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast, you can spend 2 sorcery points to give it the {@condition Poisoned|PHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Polished Needles
entries: Much like the wings of a butterfly, sometimes your projects should be pinned down to truly be observed. This has led to you creating specialized pins that you may craft so you have two at hand at any given time.

You create up to two {@item Rusty Iron Stake|TheUndertomesTO|Rusty Iron Stakes} during a Long Rest if any are missing, and you gain a +1 bonus modifier to Attack and Damage Rolls using them upon reaching 5th level in Artificer, a +2 upon reaching 12th Level and a +3 upon reaching 18th Level.

optionalfeature.name: Powerful Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

optionalfeature.name: Preserving Scissors
entries: Your attack rolls with your Scrap Scissors do not remove counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesHT} from affected creatures.

optionalfeature.name: Pressure Offload Point
entries: You take a swift palm or finger to a creature's pressure points, having them feel their tense body near instantly cool off. By spending 2 ki points you can target one creature within 5-feet of you with a jab to their pressure points, if the target is willing they fall under one of the effects of {@spell calm emotions|PHB|Calm Emotions} spell, ignoring its original saving throw. If the target is hostile, it must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw to dodge your apparent attack.
You choose which effect takes place.

optionalfeature.name: Primeval Howling
entries: Upon reaching 3rd level, you can at times let all of the savage energy within you swell up in a guttural howl to strike the fear of nature into your foes' hearts. As an action, you may bellow out a mighty howl, all hostile creatures within 15-feet of you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw whose DC is 8 +Your strength Modifier + your proficiency modifier or take {@damage 2d8} thunder damage and suffer a negative modifier to their Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma based rolls equal to half your proficiency modifier, rounded down. This lasts until the end of their next turn and they take only half the damage on a success.
After this Howl, you become winded, suffering the same negative modifier to your Strength, Dexterity and Constitution based rolls until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Propulsion Chamber Maintenance
entries: You've come up with blueprints to create your very own Propulsion Chamber Mechanism and attach it to virtually any weapon over the course of a long rest. You can have an amount of such Mechanisms created and installed equal to half your proficiency bonus at any given time, before you are required to scrap an existing one for pieces to make new prototypes.

A weapon that you modify to hold a Propulsion Chamber gains the {@itemProperty Blast Cartridge|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} (1d6) property, accepting Generic Propulsion Rounds to be fired. You also manage to create enough Rounds equal to twice the Reload value of Chambered weapons per long rest, provided you have the modified weapon in hand to be sure of its specifications. Attacks made with these weapons inflict one {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.
The damage from the Blast-Cartridge property created by you increases to {@damage 1d8} when you reach 8th level in Artificer, then {@damage 1d10} at 12th and finally {@damage 2d6} at 16th.
Due to the ever-rising price of ammunition and bullet regulations, these Rounds become inert and rendered useless on the next long rest after their creation.

optionalfeature.name: Pushing Scissors
entries: After you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be pushed 5 feet back. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Quasi-Formed Bloodbag

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You can spend 4 Blood Charges to afflict a creature within 30 feet with your blood. It must make a Charisma saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a failure, it becomes a Quasi-Bloodbag for up to 1 minute while you maintain concentration.

You can issue simple commands that don't cause the creature to harm itself directly. On its turn, it acts on instinct and bloodlust and attacks the closest creature. It retains its other abilities and repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature immune to being {@condition Charmed||charmed} automatically succeeds.

optionalfeature.name: Quick Learner
entries: You’ve learnt how to read your opponent’s moves only after suffering them once, so that pain may never be repeated upon you again. Whenever you are hit by another creatures attack you may choose gain a +1 bonus modifier to your AC against that specific attack until the end of combat. You may only learn a number of attacks per combat equal to your Wisdom modifier. This bonus does not stack.

optionalfeature.name: Random Targeting
entries: Sometimes an ability or feature may ask you to choose a random creature. To do so, refer to an order of the possible creatures to be chosen ( Such as groupings of hostile or friendly creatures, also making preferential use of the Initiative order if in combat ) and rolling an appropriate die for the number of creatures.

For a two or three creatures, simply roll a d4 or d6 respectively, with each creature having a "weight" of 2 on the roll, such as when rolling a d6 on a result of 1-2 creature A gets picked, while 3-4 would be creature B and a 5-6 results in creature C.

For creatures greater than that in an even number, simply roll an appropriate die, such as a d4 for 4 creatures, d6 for 6 and so on. In the case of odd creatures, roll the closest die rounded up, such as rolling a d8 if there are 7 creatures to be chosen. If the result is an unassigned number, simply re-roll until the result is a listed creature, or pick the last creature in order if this is repeated more than twice.

optionalfeature.name: Relocator Fighting Style
entries: Wielding certain weapons that are a menace from afar has become second nature to you, and you have learnt how to better grip and shove all on your way to shape the battlefield to your liking. Whenever you hit with a weapon that has the Reach property, you may move the target up to 5-ft. closer to you if they were within 10-ft. of you or push them away if they were within 5-ft. of you.

optionalfeature.name: Repudiation of the Tower

entries: "I wanted to look into the faces of the people whose little children are my brothers, my sisters..."

It's all wrong. The incessant feeling has been stemming from inside your own neglected heart for all this time, this accursed world was no more than a flimsy construct of your mind that disregarded all else. Upon coming to this realization and finally accepting to try anew, you have the following:

items: You lose your Expertise on subjects of law as per your Inner Disharmony feature and instead gain Expertise on Insight. If you were already an Expert in Insight, you have Advantage on all Insight checks.
You may spend three Metamagic points to assign two additional creatures a Mold whenever you do so.

You may now use your Action to Repudiate other creatures, rolling a ranged spell attack using your {@item Machine Coil|TheUndertomesPH} against them. On a hit, you deal an amount of {@dice d10} lightning damage equal to 1 plus the amount of Bricks of the Tower around 120-ft. of you.

Your rage against the machines of mankind still burns on, causing you to be able to spend a Reaction whenever a Brick of the Tower performs certain acts to Repudiate them with additional effects. These may only be done after the triggering creature's effect is resolved and all their die are rolled for the act, with the following triggers in accord to their Mold:

entries.caption: Repudiation Effects
rows: Heads
Whenever the Head casts a Spell or adds their Intelligence modifier to a roll.

The Head must attempt a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failure, roll a {@dice d4}. On an even result, they are {@condition Deafened|PHB} until the start of their next turn. On an odd result, they are {@condition Blinded|PHB} for the same duration.
Hands
Whenever the Hand deal more than 10 damage to another creature through any means. Alternatively, whenever they attempt an Athletics or Artisan's Tools check.
The Hand has a -3 to their next attack roll. Alternatively, this negative modifier is applied to their Save DC when they next have another creature attempt a saving throw.
Hearts
Whenever the Heart is the cause for a creature recovering Hit Points or monologues.
The Heart is forced to bite their tongue, suffering 1 piercing damage. If they caused the recovery of Hit Points, that recovery is halved.

items: You gain an additional Reaction per turn for each 2 Brick of the Tower within 120-ft. of you.

As an Action during your turn that you may take once per week and provided there are at least 6 Brick of the Tower within 360-ft. of you, you may Bring Down the Tower. ( As per described in the next page. )

entries.name: Bring Down the Tower
entries: You manifest the agglomerate of all laws, bonds and contracts perceived by you and those within 360-ft. of you into a colossal spire that would dare pierce the heavens, only to pull it down and fall to the ground like shooting stars to ravage all who built it. Ask the following questions around the table:

items: Were the actions of your foes meant for a greater cause?
Is your foe in a leadership position? If so, are their followers willing to die for their leader?
Has your foe already had some success in their goals?
Will your foe's actions or goal change the lives of many people? ( Such as a settlement, a kingdom or the entire world. )
Do you agree or empathize with your foe's actions or the reasons for their actions?

entries: For each question ( Except the last. ) whose answer was an unanimous "Yes." from the table as a whole, including the DM, ( Who has final say ) choose one of the following effects to add to the tower's collapse:

items: The fall brings newfound hope for a future that is less maculate. Targets of your choice may choose to automatically fail this saving throw and suffer no adverse effects, instead recovering an amount of Hit Points equal to half the damage that would be dealt. They also become Immune of the {@condition Frightened|PHB} Condition for one hour.

The Tower isn't the only one to fall, with all the lingering resentment from the world also being manifested as a fierce thunder fall to punish the insolent. The Tower's collapse deals d12s instead of d8s.
Pain is the only thing you could believe this world deserves. The Tower's collapse deals an additional 4 damage die.

The ground shall be scarred by the destruction wrought upon this day , and so will those who survive. All spaces within this range become Difficult Terrain that you and creatures of your choice may ignore. On a failed saving throw against the Tower's collapse, creatures who survive it gain a permanent scar upon their person. This scar may only be removed by a use of the Wish spell.

Nothing shall last, not a ruin, not a thought nor a memory. All faeric, demonic and holy contracts of your choice within the area immediately end. Area-based spells of your choice instantly end. Any desecrated or consecrated areas that come into contact with that range are instantly neutralized and any traces of lead become silver instead.

entries: The Tower then collapses, raining destruction over all creatures of your choice within reach. They must pass a Charisma saving throw or have their bodies broken by the debris of that which dared the Heavens, suffering {@dice 8d8} radiant damage and being knocked {@condition Prone|PHB} on a failure, or suffer half that damage on a success.
The fifth question is individual and only meant for you.
For the week after using this you cannot assign Brick of the Tower. Your Heart wouldn't be able to deal with such regiments again so soon.
"The mediator between the head and the hands must be the heart."

optionalfeature.name: Resist and Bite Fighting Style
entries: What is one more scar for a body so used to carrying them? They'll only fuel the punishment delivered onto your enemies. As an action during your turn, you may forgo attacking to instead enter an enduring stance.

You release all the pain you've taken in a free action attack at one creature within reach on the start of your next turn, dealing an amount of additional damage die equal to the number of times you've taken damage during your enduring stance. If you would have additional attacks, also add one additional weapon damage dice for each of that you have foregone.

optionalfeature.name: Rhythmic Cadence
