entries: You have created a method to use the momentum from your swings synced to your growing heartbeat to better deliver your blows - At the risk of missing the mark and miss more often. You gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit when you hit an attack and a -1 negative modifier to hit when you miss an attack, to a maximum positive or negative modifier of 3.

Furthermore, the last attack you would hit during your turn deals an amount of additional damage equal to twice the positive bonus modifier you have gotten, or deals less damage equal to triple the negative modifier you’ve gotten.
This modifier resets to 0 at the start of your turns.

optionalfeature.name: Round Cleanup Fighting Style
entries: Its nice and all to deal with duels one on one, but you haven't ever been afraid of taking on an entire crowd at once. When you hit a creature, you gain a +1 to hit a different creature with an attack.

optionalfeature.name: Royal Practice Fighting Style

prerequisite.other: {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} or Cleric, Fighter, or Paladin

entries: Few can truly call swordplay an art form in the way that you and your kindred can, evolving a single slash onto a bloody manifesto of your being.

Once per turn you may replace one of the attacks you'd perform from the Attack Action to a Flourishing Attack, of which you perform a Melee Weapon Attack against a target within reach. On a hit, you deal an additional 1 damage die that matches your weapon's and inflict 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count. On a miss, you whiff and embarrass yourself, suffering a -2 negative modifier to your Armor Class and Charisma related rolls until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Running Stream's Rush
entries: As your action during your turn, you may spend 3 ki points to enter a state of constant flow and movement. You may move up to your movement speed's worth in any direction, not provoking opportunity attacks until the end of your turn. Additionally, the first time you leave a creature's reach you may perform an unnarmed strike against them.

optionalfeature.name: Saint's Touch
entries: Your mere touch is enough to take another creatures pain away, as you are one to be able to shoulder your fellows suffering. As an action on your turn, you may touch another creature within 5-feet of you and restore their hitpoints for a value equal to your Paladin level times five. When you do so, you take the same value in damage.
Starting at 11th level, you may also choose to remove one condition or non-magical disease from your target and suffer it yourself.

optionalfeature.name: Scattering Aroma
entries: {@b Cost: 2 Sorcery Points.} As a Reaction to when you would be targeted for an attack, you may use your own magic to momentarily disperse the thoughts of your attacker, imposing Disadvantage on the attack. You may so after the creature rolls to hit but before the DM determines the result.

optionalfeature.name: Seeker of Warm Hearts
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can force them to roll a constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. If they fail, they fall {@condition Prone}.
Whenever you kill a {@condition Prone} creature with your pact weapon, you gain a number of temporary hit points based on its size:

{@dice 1d4} for Tiny, {@dice 1d6} for Small, {@dice 1d8} for Medium, {@dice 1d10} for Large, {@dice 1d12} for Huge and {@dice 2d12} for Gargantuan. Temporary points gained this way can stack, and do not disappear when you gain additional temporary hit points.

optionalfeature.name: Sharpened Weapon
entries: The weapon gains the Hemorrhaging (17-20) property. If it already has that property, choose one of the following benefits:

items: The weapon's Hemorrhaging threshold is reduced by your proficiency bonus.
The weapon's Hemorrhaging threshold is reduced by 1, and the property inflicts 1 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count when triggered.

optionalfeature.name: Sharper Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors deal an additional {@damage 1d8} slashing damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d8} upon reaching level 9. If the Scrap Scissors are being held with two hands, the d8 becomes a d10 instead.

optionalfeature.name: Singing Spells
entries: As a free action when you cast a spell, you may spend one Sorcery point to start an oddly harmonious string of noises that form a sligthly off key melody as you go from slinging spell to spell. Choose one creature as the focus of your song, it takes an additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage whenever it would take damage, as for it the song sounds much more distorted, as if a horrible droning had settled in their eardrum. You may spend an additional Sorcery point on the start of each of your subsequent turns to maintain the effect on the target or switch to another one.

optionalfeature.name: Single Minded Fighting Style
entries: You focus only on what is ahead of you during a battle, disregarding the world at your own peril but being able to become a much fearsome foe to whoever has the unluck of having you as a target. While in combat, the first creature you deal damage to becomes your Target until you or the Target is knocked {@condition Unconscious}. All creatures that aren’t your target gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit you and to damage rolls against you. You, however, gain the same bonus modifier to hit your Target and deal an additional 2 damage equal to your weapon’s damage type against your Target on melee weapon hits.

optionalfeature.name: Singleton
entries: A spell may have a part of its text contain the "Singleton." keyword. This signifies that the spell has a special benefit to the first time it is cast until your next long rest, with this effect being written following the "Singleton." keyword itself If you cast multiple "Singleton." spells within the same long rest, their special effects trigger once per each individual spell.

optionalfeature.name: Sniper's Concentration
entries: Upon choosing this Pact Boon, every turn you don't deal damage directly through your melee or ranged weapons attacks or spell effects, you gain one level of Sniper's Concentration, as shown in the level below. Upon dealing or taking damage, your Sniper's Concentration level returns to zero. You can only trigger Sniper's Concentration effects when causing damage with a Marksman Weapon.

rows: You gain a +1 bonus to hit for your next attack and deal an additional damage die of same type and size as your weapon's damage dice.
Your bonus to hit becomes a +2 plus your attack is considered a Critical Hit on a 19 or 20.
Your bonus to hit becomes a +3, you now deal two additional damage die and your attack is considered a Critical Hit on a roll of 18 to 20.
entries.caption: Sniper's Concentration

entries: The effects of each Sniper's Concentration level remain even if not mentioned directly, such as the additional damage die from level I in level II.

If you deal damage to a creature while in Sniper's Concentration and a friendly creature has dealt damage to your target creature while in your turn, you may spend your reaction to enter a perfect timing state, easily aiming for a creature's weak spot. You gain 8 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for that attack, which are reduced to zero when your turn ends.

optionalfeature.name: Solemn Focus
entries: You cannot be deterred by anything when you are completing a arduous task in a fight, making it so you gain the following effects until the end of your next turn when you deal damage to a creature:
You gain advantage on Saving Throws that would result in you being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}.

For the duration if a creature who attempted to hit you with an attack that would deal psychic damage, regardless of if they hit or not, or attempted to target you with an ability that would result in you becoming {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}, regardless of your success or failure, you gain a +1 bonus on attack rolls targetting them and deal an additional 2 damage on hits against them. This additional damage matches your attack’s damage type.

optionalfeature.name: Song of the Black Forest
entries: You can subtly deploy an enchatment through your song to better allow another to reach their end. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature suffers from {@condition Enchanted|TheUndertomesASF}. {@condition Enchanted|TheUndertomesASF}. until the end of their next turn.

A creature suffering from this condition takes an additional {@dice 1d6} of psychic damage whenever it takes damage, as it sees sights of a desired life it'll never have, degrading its mind. Your Song of the Black Forest die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.

optionalfeature.name: Spreading Floral Breeze
entries: {@b Cost: 1-4 Points.} As a Free Action during your turn you may have your magic solidify roots sprouting from your shoulders or around your back that mimic your hands, acting in unison to deliver more at once. Your next weapon attack or cantrip spell attack until the end of your turn may target an additional different target for each Sorcery Point spent, provided the targets are still within reach.
If the cantrip you would cast can already target multiple targets, you just choose one more target for each Sorcery Point spent.

If you would deal additional damage with sources such as Divine Smite, that additional damage is divided evenly toward all targets, rounded down and with a minimum of one die or value of extra damage.
{@b Ex:} If you would deal an additional {@damage 5d8} fire damage from a magic weapon against four creatures, each suffers only an additional {@damage 2d8} fire damage.

optionalfeature.name: Stalker in the Night Fighting Style
entries: The shadows are an appropriate prowling ground for one such as you, who prefers to attack while unseen. If you deal damage from a weapon attack to a creature while you are hidden from it, you also inflict one {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count per damage die you deal.
In the case of inflicting more than 4 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count at once, you instead inflict Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}.

optionalfeature.name: Statue of Provations
entries: A statue that can be found in many forms, containing a special challenge and consequence if it is not met. It usually takes one of the following forms and challenges:

The statue is triggered by perceiving any creature within 60 ft, of it. It has 60 ft. of darksight and a Passive Perception of 16. When triggered, a Wall of Force spell is cast centered around it, forcing one of the creatures inside to take up its task, which is explains out loud, or instantly have all creatures it can see within 60 ft. suffer the effects of failure. These statues appear in a low/medium/high hazard division as shown in the table above, and are usually fit for each of the first three tiers of play respectively.
The Warrior A creature must deal 40/80/150 damage of any kind to the statue.
The statue becomes alive and delivers a series of punches before vanishing into dust, dealing {@dice 3d8}/{@dice 8d8}/{@dice 14d12} bludgeoning damage to the one who failed this task.
A +1/+2/+3 weapon.
The Sage A creature must pass a DC 14/18/22 {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Nature} or {@skill Religion} skill check as the statue asks for specific knowledge.
The statue saps the intelligence and knowledge from the one who failed this task, reducing the attribute associated with it’s skill check by 1/2/3 until the next Long Rest A +1/+2/+3 arcane focus.
The Berserker A creature must suffer {@dice 5d8}/{@dice 10d8}/{@dice 14d12} force damage and not be knocked {@condition Unconscious}.
The creature is healed by one hit point and cannot recover hit points until the third round of it’s next combat or until the next Long Rest.
A +1/+2/+3 armor.
Statue Challenge Failure Success

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of an Thunderstorm
entries: Whenever you would be forced to attempt a Dexterity saving throw to resist the effects of a spell or attack that affects a radius, line or sphere that has a physical form ( Such as a {@spell fireball|PHB|Fireball}, {@spell lightning bolt|PHB|Lightning Bolt}, Ballista Bolt or Cannonball ) and pass, you may spend your Reaction to suffer no damage if you would take half and punch through the attack, redirecting it to instead hit another point of your choice within 60-ft. of you. When you do so, all creatures within this new area must attempt the same saving throw against the original DC. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Arcana
entries: As an action, you can make your tattoos glow with a magical aura. For 1 minute, or until you dismiss it as an action, you shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like. You can take this as a reaction instead of an action when you enter your Rage. While you are glowing, you can spend a bonus action, or do this as part of your reaction when you rage, to force all creatures of your choice within 20 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or become {@condition Frightened} of you until the start of your next turn. Creatures {@condition Frightened} this way take an additional dice of damage from your Unarmed Strikes whenever you hit them. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until your next long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Binding
entries: You can use a bonus action to force an enemy creature to make a Constitution saving throw against your tattoo save DC as magical shackles extend from your tattoos to hold them. If they pass, they take {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage as they break off the chains (this damage increases to {@dice 2d6} on 6th level, {@dice 3d6} on 10th level and {@dice 4d6} on 14th level). If they fail, both you and the creature can only use one action per turn until the start of your next turn. Extra attacks cannot be used as part of the same Attack action. This ability can only be used a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you recover all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Bloody Knuckles
entries: When you cause a creature to suffer {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, it instead suffers {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} until cured. Heavily Bleeding deals {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as Bleed and loses 2 stacks whenever triggered. The {@skill Medicine} check DC to remove it increases by 5.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Dominance
entries: A bright light shines from your tattoos, and zaps of electricity signify to all creatures around you the build up of strength you're about to commence when activating this tattoo. As a bonus action, which you may take together with your Rage bonus action, you begin for yourself a Test of the Big Brother. Until the start of your next turn, all enemies have advantage on attacks against you, and you gain vulnerability to all damage types. Once your second turn starts, if you're still alive, you pass the test, removing all the previous conditions. For two rounds, until the end of your second turn after this, you gain advantage on all of your ability checks, attack rolls and saving throws. Additionally, all creatures you attack gain vulnerability to your Unarmed Strikes for the duration.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Entrenched Ankles
entries: You gain 10-ft. move speed. Whenever you attempt to climb a surface, you can spend up to 10-ft. of walking speed at a time to successfully climb the same amount of feet spent by kicking and locking your feet into the surface, remaining there without falling at the end of your turns.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Family
entries: If an ally within 30 feet of you also has active magical tattoos on their body, you may spend a bonus action to gain temporary hit points equal to your Unarmed Strike dice + your rage damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Fists
entries: When you hit a creature with an unarmed attack, you may perform another attack as a bonus action if the creature has a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}. Additionally, you can add your rage bonus to {@skill Intimidation} checks.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Goading Scowls
entries: While engaged in combat with a creature, when it attacks another creature, you can use your reaction to make your tattoos flash and goad it. It has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you until the end of its turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Kicking
entries: You can use an action to kick down an enemy's weak spot, leaving them vulnerable for further attacks. As a part of this action, roll an Unarmed Strike against the enemy. If it hits, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or become {@condition Paralyzed} for a minute. The creature can reroll the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you successfully use this ability, you can only use it again after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Lockdown
entries: In place of one attack during the {@action Attack} action, you cause purple chains to burst from your tattoo toward a target within 20 feet. Make a grapple check against it. On a success, both your speed and the target's speed become 0 until the end of its next turn. If the target has {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, your speed is halved instead. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Loyalty
entries: When you hit a creature that has a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} with an Unarmed Strike, other creatures will gain advantage on their first attack roll against it until the end of the affected creature's turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Mutual Discombobulation
entries: Once per turn you may choose to change one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action with a Headbutt. To do so you perform a melee Unarmed Strike that you are proficient in against a creature within 5-ft. of you. On a hit, you deal {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage and inflict half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, then suffering half the damage dealt yourself and the same amount of the Condition's count. When you gain it this way, you only lose this count at the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Needle Fractures
entries: You can sink the ink in this tattoo to create binding points in your muscles that take out the force of whatever hits you as a Reaction you may take whenever you suffer damage. When you do so, reduce the damage taken by your choice between your current amount of tattoos or proficiency bonus. You cannot reduce force damage this way and may use this tattoo an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Passion
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you inflict 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Additionally, you gain advantage on {@skill Performance} checks whenever performing with ( or to impress ) other friendly creatures or against a hostile creature.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Payback
entries: When a creature hits you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you with an attack, you may, as a reaction, immediately move up to that creature without provoking opportunity attacks and hit them with a fortress-breaking punch, leaving a small crater on the floor. They must roll a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or take {@dice 10d8} bludgeoning damage and gain one stack of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesCL}. Additionally, you may add {@dice 1d4} to the next attack roll you make, and if it hits, add {@dice 1d4} force damage to the damage roll. On a successful save, they only take half the damage, but you still gain the attack and damage bonus. Once you use this feature, you can only use it again after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Punching
entries: When you make an attack action on your turn using an unarmed melee attack and successfully hit a creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or gain one stack of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesCL}. If you managed to hit all of your unarmed attacks made with your attack action this turn and they failed all of your saving throws, they gain 2 stacks of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesCL} per attack instead. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Remembrance
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you inflict 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, you gain advantage on {@skill History} checks made to remember events you participated in. You may inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} this way up to two times per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Scary Faces
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Intimidation}, or expertise if already proficient. When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}), Charisma ({@skill Deception}), or Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check, you can use {@skill Intimidation} instead. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a short or long rest. When making an Intimidation check against a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, you can use Strength instead of Charisma.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Skull Bursting
entries: Whenever you hit a Grappled creature you may choose to suplex them and cause them to become {@condition Prone}. When you do so, for the remainder of the duration this creature remains {@condition Prone} you may choose to re-roll any damage die against them, taking the greater result. You may do so once per die.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Starburst
entries: Whenever you deal a Critical Hit against a target creature, you deal an additional 2 damage die equal to the attack's current damage. Additionally, you inflict an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count against the hit creature equal to the amount of damage die rolled and when you perform this your fists burst into bright-light that covers an 30-ft. area around you. All hostile creatures within that reach must then pass a Constitution saving throw or be Blinded until the end of their next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Stitches
entries: When a creature within 30 feet targets you with a spell, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, purple chains wrap around its mouth, preventing it from speaking for 1 minute. It repeats the saving throw at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. A creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} has disadvantage on this saving throw. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Ten Thousand Vendettas
entries: As a bonus action, you etch the names of a number of creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, onto your body. Each suffers {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} until it is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} or dies.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of the Great Wielder
entries: After grappling a Large or smaller creature, you can wield it as a martial weapon with which you are proficient. Such a weapon is two-handed, and it is Heavy unless the creature is Tiny. A Tiny creature deals {@damage 2d4} bludgeoning damage, a Small creature deals {@damage 2d6}, a Medium creature deals {@damage 2d8}, and a Large creature deals {@damage 2d12}. Whenever an attack using the creature hits, the wielded creature takes half the damage dealt. Your speed is reduced by 10 feet while wielding a Medium creature and 20 feet while wielding a Large creature. A creature at 0 hit points instead deals only 1 bludgeoning damage.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Threadmarks
entries: As an Action during your turn you may brace yourself for a violent sprint. When you do so, you gain 30-ft. of walking speed until the end of your turn and any damage dealt to you through Opportunity Attacks is halved. Whenever you move through another creature's space they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be caught in your wild trample, being knocked {@condition Prone} on a failure and suffering an amount of d10 bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half that value on a success. The DC for this is 8 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus. When you do so you may choose to Grapple up to your Strength modifier's worth of creatures instead of Knocking them {@condition Prone}, then knocking them {@condition Prone} in a pile onto of any unoccupied space within 5-ft. of you at the end of your turn. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Turtle Skin
entries: You may spend your Bonus Action to have the ink from this tattoo spread out and flow over your skin, creating a protective layer over it. As long as you aren't wearing armor or are wearing a Tattoo Set armor, you gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your current magical Tattoo count until the start of your next turn. For each attack performed against you in that duration this modifier is reduced by one. You may use this tattoo an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Twisting
entries: As an action, you speak a command word and make your body rubbery for up to 1 hour or until you dismiss the effect. You can twist and bend through any opening greater than 1 foot in diameter, gain a +5 bonus to checks made to escape a grapple, and take only half damage from falling.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Vengeance
entries: As an action, you get to dash in a straight line of up to 60 feet towards a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG}, leaving behind a purple trail of light and energy. This action does not provoke opportunity attacks. All other creatures of your choice in this line must roll a Dexterity saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or take {@dice 2d10} force damage, taking only half that damage on a success. Once you reach the target, you may roll an attack roll against it for each attack roll it has made in its last turn, with a minimum of two. After beating the creature to a pulp, it must make a Constitution saving throw, becoming {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} until the end of its next turn on a failure due to your thunderous pummeling. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Vicious Burns
entries: You learn the {@spell vicious mockery} spell. Whenever you causa damage to another creature using it, you may choose to fire damage instead of psychic and one {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each damage die rolled. If you are not a spellcaster your DC for this spell's saving throw is 10 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus + any bonuses gained from being Attuned to a magical weapon.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Wrath
entries: As an action, you accumulate powerful magical energy from your tattoos on your fists, charging up a devastating attack. You punch the ground, immediately shattering it like a crater as long as the material is non-magical. All creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you must roll a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC. On a failure, they take a number of {@dice d6} of force damage equal to the number of Magical Tattoos you have and are {@condition Stunned} until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. You can use this ability twice, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: The Caring Hand

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You can spend Blood Charges to generate twice as much Bloodfeast, to a maximum amount of Bloodfeast equal to your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: The Custodian

entries: "Listen. We live in a binary world. The world that is luscious... and the world that is bristly. Are you aware of their differences?"

Style, force and loyalty are words that radiate through your gait wherever you walk, exhaling a powerful aura that booms through the hearts of others, either shaking them to the core or having them fall under the protection of your beat.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters who are great leaders and bolster both courage and imperativeness toward their fellows, taking care of any under them like a grand family that extends far beyond the bonds of blood. These are driven by and for their groups and factions as the first thing in their world, going to great lengths just to make sure they are happy and safe, also being reasonably vengeful at whoever wrongs them and their kin.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, the following apply:

items: Describe how your presence extends like a bursting melody that has others quake in their boots. When first triggering this Burst, all hostile creatures that can see or hear you within a 360-ft. radius must pass a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, also being able to retry this saving throw to end the Condition early at the end of their subsequent turns. While Frightened, a creature under this Condition suffers 2 {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the start of their turns, losing one count after each ability check, saving throw or attack roll.

You feel a surge of power at your fingertips - Confidence made manifest in pure, raw bravado. You gain unarmed weapons that you are proficient with in the shape of your fists and legs for the duration. These have the Finesse and Mesmerizing properties, dealing {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage on a hit. If you already had an Unarmed Strike option, you instead deal an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on your Unarmed Strike hits.

Your feet are stepping on air when it comes to being near those you care about. As a Bonus Action during your turns you may instantly move upwards to 30-ft. in a single leap, having to end your movement within 5-ft. of a friendly creature within that reach. If you are to occupy the same space as a hostile creature you may attempt a Shove attempt against them as part of the same Bonus Action, pushing them 5-ft. toward any direction and taking their space on a success or being forced to land within 5-ft. of that creature on a failure.

Whenever you hit a creature that has {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesMBG} with an Unarmed Strike, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage against them and may choose to instantly push them back 5-ft.

optionalfeature.name: The Disgrace

entries: "I'll be damned before I let you ruin this! Not after toiling like a goddamn dog for decades, climbing up the ranks...!"

What have you done? You should already know the answer to that question, after all it has been repeated in your head as often as you can recall. There's something you did, of your fault and folly, that has rendered you a complete and utter disgrace to those around you, a shame that would be best left erased. Yet still, your exhausted, spiteful fingers grip onto your remaining life like a starving animal does to its last meal.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters who have screwed up phenomenally and even more-so as that failure being of their on fault. That single event is something that has defined them more than anything else in the past, even more-so if they were someone important before their horrid fall from grace. These are often seem as bitter and arrogant people.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, you gain the following effects:

items: Hatred, spite and bitterness overtake your emotions to create a rage-fueled drive towards all your actions, granting you Immunity to becoming {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed}.

You gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the start of your turns. Whenever you deal damage, you deal an additional amount of damage equal to half your current {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, to a maximum value equal to your proficiency bonus.
Whenever you would inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you inflict an additional count.

Additionally, the anxiety to re-instate your greatness has you become even quicker on your feet as it grows. Each time an attack hits you, your AC increases by a +1 bonus modifier. You lose this bonus whenever you are missed with an attack.

optionalfeature.name: The Fatebound

entries: "It must've been fate that brought us together. To think that I'd ever meet a husband like you..."
Your heart beats to the tune of the fates, scattered to the waves until it stops. Even though volatile, you always make sure that when you crash, it will be glorious.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who are marked by a certain detachment with everything else, those with a turbulent attitude toward their goals or characters who are ultimately fatalists.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following in accordance to your current missing Hit Points:

items: While you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, deal an additional d6 damage whenever you damage a creature. This damage is of the same type as your original attack.
While below half of your Maximum Hit Points currently missing, gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit on your attack rolls. While below a quarter, gain a +2 instead.
Whenever you would gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, gain two additional counts of the effect.
Once per turn per creature, whenever you deal damage to a creature suffering from being {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed} and you aren't, deal an additional 2d4 psychic damage as well.

optionalfeature.name: The Shackled

prerequisite.other: A Wisdom score of 18 or lesser

entries: "I... I have to move forward... F-follow the shadow...!"

You have a profound dependency or love for a particular subject, be that an object or a person. That is what keeps you going through anything so you can keep its safety and possible happiness guaranteed at any cost.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters that have developed a deep and ( although not always ) unhealthy obsession with something or someone, those who would split the word in two to complete what is requested for them or characters who are ultimately seeking some form of validation or to have others be proud of them.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: Name a creature or object as your Desire when first activating your Burst. Whenever they suffer damage or are grabbed by another creature ( respectively ), you gain a cumulative +1 bonus modifier to hit and to damage on your next attack against the creature who harmed your Desire. This bonus is reset after dealing damage to them.

While your Desire is {@condition Unconscious} ( if it is a creature ) or is within a hostile creature's possession ( if it is an object ), you deal an additional 1d8 damage when dealing any damage while being within 15-ft of your Desire.
You gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your proficiency bonus while within 15-ft. of your Desire.

You are permanently under the effects of the {@spell guidance} cantrip when tasked by your Desire ( if they are a creature ) to attempt something that would require a Skill Check or while using your Desire. ( if they are an object. )

entries: If your Desire is an object, you and your DM must agree that it is important enough for you to value it greatly. That item can be a weapon that has accompanied you through your journey and that has the possibility of being pried away from you, or a memento that keeps you steady through the hardest of times, such as a carved totem that reminds you of home or something of the sort.

optionalfeature.name: The Truthseeker

entries: "Even if I don't have much happiness, I know where to go in the immediate future. And that's enough for me."

You have always bene ticked off by the small rips at the seams of the world and the thoughts of what might move in the shadows. You may not always know how or why, but your heart yearns to understand the world and its many meanings.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who just can't stand still when they've got the feeling that something is off, those with great intuition and those inclined to try to face the truth even if they may not be able to withstand it fully.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain Advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Insight} checks.
You gain Advantage against resisting and perceiving Illusions of any kind, you also gain Advantage against Enchantment spells.
While you are above half your Maximum Hit Points, all damage you suffer is reduced by 1d4 as you feel like you can handle any erosion from seeing what you shouldn't.

While you are at or below half your Maximum Hit Points you feel the weight in your mind start to become heavy, yet a supernatural focus has been unlocked in your being. You suffer a -2 negative modifier on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws, but gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns and whenever you trigger a Posture Critical, that damage cannot be reduced through any means.

optionalfeature.name: The Veteran

entries: "Thanks to that, I'm free to point the barrel at anyone I want. No matter where I fire it, this shotgun can blast anyone into fireworks like it hit them point blank, how wonderful is that?"

Your life has been a warpath going from battle to battle, conflict to conflict. This might not be in the case of a literal war, but instead of various minor conflicts that have led you along to be hardened by them, granting you an askew view of your surroundings and the people that walk near you.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who have been put through conflict for most of their lives be that by their own volition or otherwise. They are often found lurking over memories of their own path or attempting not to overlap their sights with something that isn't really there, but vary wildly in how they cope with their experiences.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain Resistance to psychic damage and the Frightened Condition.
You gain {@dice 1d4+1} Poise count at the start of your turns.
You gain Advantage on ability checks and saving throws against being Grappled or Blinded.
You are considered Proficient in the {@skill Athletics} skill if you weren't, and to have Expertise in said skill if you were.

entries: Additionally, choose one of the following to determine which feature you gain based on your own personality traits. If you see people still as a precious thing and value life greatly, gain this:

items: Whenever a friendly creature that you can see within 120-ft. of you is healed or protected by another creature, such as per the Protection Fighting Style, you gain Hope For Your Fellows until the end of your next turn. While clinging onto this Hope, you may reduce any damage you suffer by two die that equal double your proficiency bonus. ( Such as a +2 being 2d4, +3 being 2d6 and so on. ) Additionally you may, as a Free Action at the start of your turns, pass this Hope and its effects to a friendly creature within the same reach as first described.

entries: If you see people as resources to be spent toward your goal, gain this:

items: Whenever a friendly creature that you can see within 120-ft. of you suffers damage for the first time in the round, you gain one Poise count. Whenever a friendly creature within that same reach dies or first falls Unconscious during this combat, you gain Woe For Your Foes until the end of your next turn. While clinging into this Despair you may choose to re-roll once any individual damage die you roll on weapon attacks after first rolling them, having to take that result.

entries: And finally, if apathy towards life is all that fills you, gain this:

items: You may spend your Reaction when suffering damage to reduce your damage taken by a value equal to your current Poise count plus your proficiency bonus, as you only try to thread forward in the never-stopping march of life.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: For more information on Core Bursts, see the Fatalist Domain cleric.

optionalfeature.name: The Ward

entries: "Anyhoo, has anyone here actually read 'The Cloudburst Blade?' If ya did, well... if I may have but 3-no, 4 hours of your time, good sir..."

To be a ward is to be a waif in your life, you might still be under the graces of your master - your captor - your guardian, whatever they may be to you, and you may still somewhat believe in them but your heart, so carefully forged, has already seen through cracks that you might not be so keen to accept.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters that are living a dichotomy of being attached to a reality that they hold immense fervour toward, but also having that reality being no more than a farce that could break under their feet at any moment. They are those who possess immense knowledge of specific topics but may seem sheltered to the outside world or have trouble accepting certain truths no matter how hard they stare them in the eye.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, you gain the following:

items: The sheer energy pent up in you bursts out like a fire, granting you an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and having all your weapon or spell attacks inflict an additional 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

Your fervour is a dual-edged blade, both blinding you to what would leave most quaking but also obfuscating certain alluring dangers. You are Immune to being Frightened but suffer Disadvantage on saving throws against being Charmed.

You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient. You and your DM may discuss a topic of particular interest to your character when first taking this Core Burst, then gaining Advantage on {@skill History} skill checks related to this interest after it is agreed by you and the DM. Additionally, you gain one of the following depending on your current relation to your guardian or symbol of affection:

{@b House of Glass Dreams.} If your relationship is of admiration or an otherwise positive outlook to this false idol, whenever you perform a Critical Hit or have success in a skill check or saving throw within sight of your idol, they may spend their Reaction to Praise you. When they do so, you may add a {@dice 1d8} bonus modifier to one roll of your choice until the end of your next turn and may only do so before you roll.

{@b House of Scattered Hopes.} If your relationship has been broken or is otherwise negative to this false idol, you suffer a {@dice 1d6} negative modifier to all rolls while you can see them within 160-ft. of you as a powerful heartache easily overtakes you. However, after this pain your broken hopes can still be picked up and become stronger through your turmoil. Whenever you have a Critical Success or have success in a skill check or saving throw you gain Confidence. You may spend one Confidence after you roll any of the aforementioned rolls to add an additional {@dice 1d6} to the final result, and may hold up to three Confidence count, which is only reset after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Transfusion

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As an action, you can spend a number of Blood Charges up to your proficiency bonus to heal a creature within 5 feet of you, including yourself. The creature regains {@dice 1d4} hit points per Blood Charge spent.

optionalfeature.name: Unloved Gift Surprise
entries: Artificer Infusion Prerequisite:A gift box. Once per long rest, you long to feel unloved by someone. As such, you grab a perfectly good looking and ordinary gift box and tinker away with its insides to make a compact explosive device that triggers either when the box is opened, or at your merry whim, also letting some rocks slip inside to make it truly believable.

When you attempt to gift this item to another person, you have advantage on persuasion checks to do so. Additionally, as an action on your turn, you may toss the Gift to a space within 30-feet of yourself, and spend your bonus action to trigger the explosives inside. When triggered, all creatures within a 5-feet radius of the Gift must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take {@damage 5d8} fire damage, or half on a success, also being covered in soot for good measure.
If a creature was surprised by this, it has disadvantage on this saving throw.

optionalfeature.name: Unrelenting Fighting Style
entries: After sinking your teeth in, it becomes only easier for you to lay waste to your targets. After hitting with an attack, you gain a +1 bonus to your next attack roll against the same target.

optionalfeature.name: Vibroweld Morph-Combat Cane

prerequisite.other: A Weapon with the Finesse Property

entries: You break down a weapon to become a metallic cane that can extend blades to be ready for combat as needed. This magic weapon becomes a simple weapon with the Finesse and Light property which deals {@dice 1d6} piercing damage and inflicts one {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. When you hit with this weapon, you may choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Furthermore, this item is made to be concealed from any and all authority - Or any onlookers. As such, you gain a +5 to skill checks pertaining to disguising this weapon as a plain object.
If you use a magic weapon to make this Infusion, it inherits its magic properties.

optionalfeature.name: Vital Engine
entries: You create an engine that runs on life for the sake of bolstering stronger magic, burning through any vital energy of a creatures remains to do so. The Vital Engine is a metallic furnace that is carried on the back or strapped to your side, having a hatch to shovel any remains in, filling vials at it’s sides with a red glowing liquid to tap into. You may shovel a creature’s heart into the Vital Engine with an Action, gaining an amount of Heartbeat corresponding to their size, as follows:
You cannot extract any Heartbeat from Undead, (Non-Organical) Construct or creatures that do not have a heart, and may spend that Heartbeat as follows:

items: You may spend 4 Heartbeat to heal a creature of your choice within 15-ft for {@dice 2d8+4} Hit Points.

You may spend 3 Heartbeat and your Reaction when you cast a spell to upcast it as one level higher, such as if you were casting a 3rd-level {@spell Fireball} it counts as if it were cast with a 4th-level spell slot instead.
You may spend a number of Heartbeat to restore one of your spent spell slots, which costs a number of Heartbeat equal to twice the Spell Slot’s Level + 1.

entries: You may do this once per short rest, with any subsequent use before another short or long rest causing you to tire from the supernatural exchange, having you suffer 2 {@condition Exhaustion} per time used after the first.
You must be attuned to the Vital Engine to actually activate the Vital Engine.
Tiny 1 Small 2 Medium 3 Large 5 Huge 8 Gargantuan {@dice 1d12+6} Creature Size Heartbeat Generated

optionalfeature.name: Wind-up Spanner

prerequisite.other: A Martial Weapon that does not have the Two-Handed property (requires attunement)

entries: This magic item must be attached to a suitable weapon to work, gathering vibrations to then unleash them in a flurry of attacks. Once per combat you may spend your bonus action to Prime it, having the weapon gain one Wind Up counter per each turn you end without taking the Attack action.

At a further turn you may spend your action to take the Attack action and gain an Extra Attack for each Wind Up counter you have collected, except these attacks do not add your ability modifier to their damage rolls. You may up to four extra attack this way.

optionalfeature.name: Wounding Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors and the attack deals more than half their hit points in damage, or was a critical hit, you may roll on the Lingering Injuries table to cause a wound on them.

trap.name: Detector Trap
entries: All of the following traps are triggered when a creature walks into their space or ends their turn within, which is any 5-ft by 5-ft square. Any Saving Throw required by these is equal to your Artificer Spell Save DC.

A simple tripwire that unlike others, may be set up to cover a 5-ft wide line that goes up to 20-ft in length. A creature who comes into its space must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw, triggering it on a failure, or having it remain inactive on a Success. Upon triggering, one of the following effects that you must choose when you set it down happen:

items: It blares a loud noise that can be heard around a 120-ft area. This noise may be a simple sound or a short recording of a voice.
You link it to psychically alert you that a creature has passed, having only you know that it was triggered.

trap.name: Explosive Trap
entries: All of the following traps are triggered when a creature walks into their space or ends their turn within, which is any 5-ft by 5-ft square. Any Saving Throw required by these is equal to your Artificer Spell Save DC.

The clasic, a payload that goes boom the second a creature triggers it - But you've put a twist in it, first loading it up with a vibration trigger that shakes up the area before detonating it all. A creature that triggers this trap and all other creatures within 5-ft of them must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer taking {@dice 4d8} piercing damage plus 4 stacks of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and then suffer {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a Success, they suffer only half that damage and status infliction.

trap.name: Jawgrind Trap
entries: All of the following traps are triggered when a creature walks into their space or ends their turn within, which is any 5-ft by 5-ft square. Any Saving Throw required by these is equal to your Artificer Spell Save DC.

This bear-trap seming trap is fitted with additional gears to latch onto and grind down a creature. The creature who triggers this trap must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or be {@condition Grappled} by the trap, taking {@dice 3d4} slashing damage and 2 points of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, or half the damage and stacks on a success.

While {@condition Grappled}, the creature must spend their Bonus Action to re-attempt the Dexterity Saving Throw, although they may choose to use Strength to do so. While {@condition Grappled}, they automatically suffer the damage and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the end of their turns, up to 3 turns, where the trap then breaks and the creature is freed.

trap.name: Lureberry Bush
entries: This lush bush of white colored leaves tends to grow on the underbrush of forests and other more covered areas, preferring to bask in the shade of other trees so its shine makes itself more proeminent. The Lureberry bush produces vibrant green fruit that have a hypnotizing glow about them, with an enchanting effect that the actually carnivorous plant uses to lure in prey and then strangle them with a myriad of roots. The Bush usually covers a 10-feet area, with any creature that comes within a 30-feet radius of it noticing its light.

It must pass a DC 16 Wisdom Saving Throw or spend its movement to reach the bush, all thoughts and instincts in their head replaced by the single desire to consume the berry. A creature that comes into 5-feet of the Bush must pass a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition Grappled||grappled} by a mass of spiked vines, a creature that was enchanted by the bush has disadvantage on this check. On the start of each of their turns, a creature {@condition Grappled||grappled} by this automatically takes {@damage 2d6} poison damage as its nutrients are absorbed by the bush, they then may retry their initial Wisdom Saving Throw, breaking free from an enchantment on a success.

The DC to break free from the vines is the same as the Dexterity saving throw, and any slashing damage dealt to the Bush's vines will make them retract. After doing so, one may extract {@dice 1d4} Lureberries from the bush.

trap.name: Rocking Chair of Ages
entries: Haunt bonus: +8 Detection: passive Wisdom (Perception) score equals or exceeds 18 or passive Intelligence (History) score equals or exceeds 16.

entries.name: Trap Type
entries: Haunted Trap

This haunted trap is a finely carved rocking chair that seems like it had centuries of wood, made out of mahogany, It seems comfortable to sit on and watching it causes a creature to feel a certain fatigue that will only come to pass after resting ontop of it. Any non-undead creature within 60- ft who can see it must pass a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or spend their movement to come and sit down on the rocking chair, becoming unable to truly focus on anything else but rocking on it. Creatures with a Constitution score of 15 or greater have Advantage on this saving throw.

While sat down, the creature is {@condition Charmed} and cannot willingly get off the chair on their own unless the {@condition Charmed} Condition ends or another creature spends their Action to attempt to Grapple the {@condition Charmed} creature out, pulling them off on a succesful Grapple check. While sat down, the creature ages five years per minute spent sat down and has an uncontrollable will to share stories about their past, no matter how personal or odd. If the creature would reach elderly age while sat down, they quickly rot into a skeleton that falls to dust as they die. A creature revived from this death is revived with the age they had before sitting down on the rocking chair.
This haunted trap manifests as the result of a ghastly influence. Casting {@spell gentle repose} on the statue permanently disarms the haunted trap.

_.special: A set of common clothes handcrafted by the people of your hometown

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill History}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Languages & Tool proficiencies
entries: One Language of your choice and either Cartographer’s Tools or a Vehicle of your choice.

items.name: Equipment
entries: A set of common clothes handcrafted by the people of your hometown, a ceremonial shortsword, a purse containing 15 gp and a backpack with your choice of a holy symbol, emblem of your people or a trinket of your choosing.

entries.name: Feature: GLORIOUS FATE
entries: Your birth was a sign of change, you were henceforth trained and raised to be a monumental hero for all others, but fated to die an early and dangerous death at the first slip. You gain a permanent +1 modifier to any attacks you perform and they always count as magical. Furthermore, you may spend your Reaction once per day to perform a heroic act of throwing yourself in front of an attack that would hit another creature within 5-ft of yourself, with you suffering it’s damage instead but reducing it by your Proficiency Bonus’ worth of d8.
Your fate, however, cannot be changed and you instantly die when you are reduced to 0 hit points, being unable to be revived by anything below a True Ressurection or {@spell Wish} spells.
Otherwise you may take the Rustic Hospitality feat.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You have always been raised to know what your life will lead to, an unavoidable death admist a great deal of heroism. You may have been part of a prophecy that began long ago before you were born, or be part of an old family of heroes that have all met their demise in odd and glorious ways. Anyhow, you are aware and prepared for what will happen.

rows: I am overly cautious - Every step might be my last!
I have a hard time listening to anyone who tries to order me, if my life is pre-ordained all I have left are the small choices I can make for myself.
I tend to go along with whatever anyone asks of me. It’s been like this my whole life.
I love every single bit of attention that I draw.
I believe that heroes should be stalward examples for people and strive to be just like that.
I don’t believe in something as silly as destiny no matter how many time “fate” seems to rear it’s ugly head in my life.
I know I will die, but I shall make sure it is the most well-remembered death in history!
I am the only one who can do what I was born to do, and anyone who tries to help will only get in my way.
I have an old mentor that was a retired adventurer known far and wide around the land, yet they never told me why they retired.
My parents said I magically appeared out of a cabbage one day out of their house. What are they hiding about my origin?
My existance is a lie, my whole life was. I was created artificially with only one purpose in mind, and I must know who created me.
All I know from my quest actually comes from an old scroll that has been near me since I can remember. It speaks of my own future.
I am the seal of an elder evil and my death will serve to finally put an end to it.
A great chaos engulfed me and I don’t know my way home anymore, thinking my people have been left without a hero for as long as I am lost. I don’t even know the full extent of my quest.
A true hero must believe in the others around themselves and I wish to be no different, embodying law and respect for the good of all. (Lawful)
I actually don’t know what my quest is and am only going through my life holistically. (Any)
Although I may perish at the end, my journey for the good of all will be a gift onto itself - With me spreading my heroic touch every step of the way! (Good)
All I wish for is to conclude my quest, and will deal with all obstacles in accord. (Neutral)
Those who have chosen my life for me deserve to pay as much as destiny itself, and I will make sure to be their end myself. (Evil)
Those who have chosen my life for me don’t deserve a drop of my thoughts, my life is mine and mine alone and I will live it how I wish to! (Chaotic)
I will die, so I live every day like it will be the last, damned be the consequences.
I will die, so I live my life devoid of people and close relations, they only would get in my way.
My demise is what scares me most, and I am always looking at my shoulder for when it will creep up on me.
Every single person and thing around me might be a piece in the grand tapestry of my life, so I am over analytical of every single thing.
To me good and evil are clearly defied, and as such there cannot exist anything in the middle.
I never agreed to this, as such I am only looking for a raplecement hero before I can run away from this horrible fate.

entries: So [Hammer of Light] is such a simple abnormality. It takes as much it gave to you. What price did you pay to it?

_.special: all the items of the background you are faking
a crumpled paper that reminds you of what you wish to become (or what was chosen for you to become)

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of your choice

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: All the items of the background you are faking, and a crumpled paper that reminds you of what you wish to become (or what was chosen for you to become)

entries.name: Feature: Facsimile
entries: You've trained yourself to become something that you are not. Your walk, your manner of speech, even the abilities you openly display have been trained to craft a delicate persona that you perfectly maintain. When you choose this Background, choose another Background.

You gain a +1 bonus modifier on rolls using the Skill Proficiencies of the other Background. If this background would give you a bonus to rolls, you gain half the value you would add to those rolls, to a minimum of +1. This is always rounded down.

If it gives you protection or information of some sort, you cannot get it for sure, but have enough knowledge on the topic and an ability to weasel your way inside, gaining Advantage on checks related to that goal.
You add double your {@skill Deception} modifier to checks regarding maintaining your persona.

entries.name: Persona.
entries: Fakers can come in all shapes and sizes, and they'll convince you that they are something else. They aren't just liars or schemers, instead they are someone pretending to be what they ultimately are not at all given moments. To aid with a choice of who to become, you may roll on the following table or make up a Persona of your own:

rows: I was born poor and alone, always wanting to protect others, and so I used my strength to do just that, no matter if some betrayed me or not. (Folk Hero Background)
I am no one, but I have a dream. A dream to reach the highest- reaching factions and stand shoulder to shoulder to them all. (Urchin Background)
I have lost what once was my heart, yet its ghastly beat remains reverberating in my chest. I'll take my time to grow back into strength and take my dazzling revenge. (Soldier Background)
My friends, I always thought I'd protect them, that I'm a hero, but I'm not so sure anymore. I can't help but to run away from where I should be, like any weeping coward would. (Charlatan Background)
I am looking for my lost child, as I have been for so long and will keep doing so even if I need to tear the world apart to reach them. ( Far Traveler)
I have beckoned people towards a just cause, to a brighter future. I truly believe what I preach, even if most around me don't feel the same yet. (Sage Background)
My family is dead, my road thus far has been that of blood-shed, pain and suffering to those left in my wake. I will never go back to what once was. (Criminal Background)

I followed someone who I truly believed in to the bitter end, and my place in the world was lost in the process. Nevertheless, I am one who has earned and embodied my position even as I look toward the future. (Acolyte Background)

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Now, one such as you has varied characteristics that even you might forget at times, as your Persona's have been superimposed onto you. Roll in your chosen background's Tables.

background.name: Fanghunter

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@skill Survival}, plus one from among {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Acrobatics}, {@skill Stealth}, {@skill Sleight of Hand}, {@skill Investigation}, and {@skill Intimidation}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@item Woodcarver's Tools|PHB|Woodcarver's tools} and one type of artisan's tools

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of your choice

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Two wooden stakes, a {@item Dagger|PHB|dagger}, a set of {@item Traveler's Clothes|PHB|traveler's clothes}, a necklace of garlic, and a pouch containing 14 gp

entries: You were either raised in a tradition of vampire hunters, taught never to sleep without a stake beneath your pillow-or you became one the hard way, when something with fangs nearly stole your life. Whatever your path, you've made it your mission to eliminate {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} and their ilk from the world.

Fanghunters are dedicated, relentless, and superstitious. They study their prey, learn their patterns, and ensure that no creature of the night sleeps soundly. Some belong to secretive orders with ancient rites, while others work alone, driven by personal vendettas. How did you take up the fanghunt? What rituals do you follow before a kill? What do you fear more-the monsters, or what you've become to fight them?

entries.name: Feature: Hunter's Knowhow
entries: You know how to prepare for a hunt. During a long rest, if you have access to wood (such as from a forest or broken furniture) and woodcarver's tools, you can craft up to six wooden stakes as part of your light activity. Additionally, you have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) and Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to locate merchants, black markets, or craftsmen who sell vampire-hunting gear.

When you take this background, choose one of the following weapons: {@item Stake Crossbow|TheUndertomesTO|Stake Crossbow} or {@item Serrated Hand-axe|TheUndertomesTO|Serrated Axe}. You gain proficiency with the chosen weapon.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I always knock on wood three times before doing anything.
Cleaning my weapons is how I relax.
Secrets are meant to be kept, lest the entire world panic.
I barely take anything seriously anymore, just so I can weather through the horrible things.
I adore telling tales of my hunts more than anything.
I hate staying still in one place, it's sickening.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Protection. I will protect those that can't protect themselves, making sure no village is unsafe to walk at night. (Good)
Obedience. I receive orders from my superiors, and eliminate the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} I am told to. No more, no less. (Lawful)
Self. I don't care about {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} or Humans. I get rid of those that bother my personal life, and that's that. (Chaotic)
Dominance. I will subjugate all {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends} I meet. They will become weapons for my own schemes (Evil)
Patience. I do not hunt {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiends}, for I might mistakenly wound innocents. I wait until I am the one hunted, for it to learn it was never the predator. (Neutral)
Tradition. I was told since a young age that this was what I needed to do. Every day, I toil in blood, both theirs and my own, and wonder whether that continues to be true. (Any)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: My family has done this for generations.
I run with a whole enclave, no one can escape our hunt.
There is a village that I'll never allow fiends in.
There was the one bastard that got away, but not for long.
All of my loved ones were murdered by a fiend.
I nearly got turned, yet in the wake of that I have gotten a taste for {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesTO|Bloodfiend} blood instead.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: When I start something, I won't focus on anything else until it's done.
People call me paranoid. I say I'm well protected.
I can't stand the sight of gluttonous people or feasts.
Whispers tell me when something's wrong, it's my sixth sense.
No matter how much I clean my hands, I will never be clean.
There are particular beliefs and rituals to be done, and those who do not perform them are fools.

background.name: Flickering Hope

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@skill Survival}, plus one from among {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Acrobatics}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Stealth}, and {@skill Intimidation}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of artisan's tools

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A keepsake from your old home or group, a set of worn {@item Traveler's Clothes|PHB|traveler's clothes}, a canteen of whiskey, a rusty {@item Dagger|PHB|dagger}, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries: You might've been an adventurer or just a commoner, either way there's one thing that connects both: a full wipe-out of life. You've suffered great losses in a critical moment of your life, your family, your friends, comrades and faces who once smiled with your own. They might be hard to remember now, as they were taken in some horrible event that has left your heart struggling to beat ever since. What took everything away from me? Was it a reckless decision of your own? Do you wish for revenge? Is there still any going back to what once were?

entries.name: Feature: Light at the End of the Tunnel
entries: Death's embrace is one that you won't take lightly, as it has taken too much from you. You've braved through many a storm, and by now it only motivates you to keep living on, as such when you are below half your hit points you may add an {@dice 1d6} bonus to a roll. You must do this before rolling and you can only do this once per short rest.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: Sometimes when I look away I see the faces of my fallen comrades.
I can never relax unless I write my days in a diary meant for someone who will never read it.
Sometimes I might focus too much on one thing and tune the world out.
There's always an itching feeling in my chest, like everything will happen again.
I should've died with everyone else.
All I want is to show others what I once had, so it's memory might never be forgotten.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Prevention. I'll make sure that what happened to me happens to no one else. (Good)
Oath. Carelessness costs us everything. I've developed a code of morals so I will never stray from the right path again. (Lawful)
Self. People call me obsessive, that I can't give a piece of mind to anyone else -- I'm simply focused on enacting my revenge. (Chaotic)
Revenge. Nothing will get in my way to burning every single thing that reminds me of my past. (Evil)
Abandon. There is nothing else for me to lose nor to gain. I'll just keep living on until I flicker out, that's all I wish for. (Neutral)
Perseverance. The past is ashes in the wind, but the ones I lost would want me to keep on, so that is what I will do. I will move past the ashes to become someone new. (Any)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: I keep a vial of the fuel used to burn down my home.
My comrade's weapons are all that remained, and sharpened they remain as well.
My old kingdom was raised to the ground, yet its echoes linger on in me.
I am haunted by those gone.
The bastard. That one bastard was the one who caused all this, I will find them and I will have my revenge.
A faction did this to me. It will cease existing and never be remembered when I've burned it all down.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: I never let go of what I have. What if I lose it?!
Getting close to people just burns, and I'm done being scorched.
The fire in my chest is intense and easily lashes out at those close to me.
Everytime I close my eyes I see what happened.
All I think about is vengeance.
It was all my fault. No one else's. Everything is.

_.special: a keepsake from your old home or group
a set of worn traveler's clothes
The trinket of a necklace showing two lizards hugging a sphere that is said to represent faith and promise
a sharp glass shard of the first mirror you broke

items.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: {@skill Insight}, {@skill Survival}

items.name: Languages & Tool proficiencies
entries: Two of your choice

items.name: Equipment
entries: The trinket of a necklace showing two lizards hugging a sphere that is said to represent faith and promise, a sharp glass shard of the first mirror you broke, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch containing 3 gp

entries.name: Feature: USED TO DESPAIR
entries: Life never went your way at all, and that has made you keep your expectations low and to remain unfazed in the face of imminent danger. You gain a +1 bonus to your saving throws against being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}, and if a creature scores a Critical Hit against you, you can diminish the damage by 1 roll of your Hit Dice.
Additionally, many religious people wish to rid you of your misfortune. They will shelter you and give you food, unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them.
Otherwise you may take the Alert feat.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: You’ve never had a shred of luck ever since you were born. Perhaps that is because you were born during a terrible bad omen.

Perhaps your family has long been cursed by a powerful entity. Or, perhaps, your family has used up all of the luck before you were born, leaving you without any good fate. Whatever the reason, your life has been constantly mired in a series of unfortunate events.

rows: I am constantly excited, I just can’t help but to wait for the next time everything will turn into a hectic mess, I live for it.
I always know when something will go wrong and if my intuition say sso, I’ll trust it more than anything else.
I have illusions that all the bad that happens to me is a provation to show my own greatness, afterall, the mightiest must face the greatest challenges.
I belive anyone else might be my next jinx, a person might just be the next cyclone to sweep my life to pieces.
I just can’t stop gambling, the thrill is all that I have now.
I gave up trying to fight it, becoming apathetic to all the horrid things.
I have a grievous obsession with the occult and supersticious.
I have a subconscious habit of always knocking on wood, no matter what.
Life has many downs, but I might as well minimize them. I have constructed my own code of conduct to keep myself safe. (Lawful)
There is a reason for my ill-fate and I must find it by any means. (Any)
My shortcomings have given me a level-headed look on the world and the suffering of others, suffering of which I wish to help alleviate. (Good)
I gave up long ago, only allowing life to take me by the hand. (Neutral)
Befriending and beguiling people just to see them fall with me is my calling in life. (Evil)
I actively tempt fate by doing every bad luck ritual I can find. (Chaotic)
It all began in a great town that has been wiped from the map. I still don’t know what happened.
I’ve been estranged from my peers ever since I was born, but adventurers took me in as one of theirs as I was left to wander.
There is a magical artifact that I believe keeps me safe despite all the bad luck.
Someone that I once loved has been taken from me because of my destructive fate. I can still see them.
I have met many people while being a vagabond, leaving a trail of unintended destruction like a force of nature.
I have fully lost all hope in the world, and that has served me well. But there are people who still care for me that have yet to give up.
I keep far away from any relationships nowadays.
Something will go wrong, and if it hasn’t already it’s only a matter of time.
I enjoy seeing the reactions to when people are swept up in my wave of misfortune.
Survival of the fittest is specially true when in a situation like mine, so the fittest thing to do is lighten the pockets of people who don’t need as much as me.
I have seen so many absurd things that distinguishing truth from unreality is simply too hard for my cognition nowadays.
When anything good happens to me, I can’t feel any positive feeling about it. It’s bound to go sour soon.

_.special: a set of fancy clothes bearing purple all over them
at least two sets of golden chains
another 5 gp's worth of beer and other party drinks

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@skill History}, {@skill Intimidation}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of gaming set and one musical instrument

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of fancy clothes bearing purple all over them, a Family-gifted boombox, at least two sets of golden chains, a wallet containing 10 gp, and another 5 gp's worth of beer and other party drinks

entries.name: Feature: Middle Finger to the World
entries: Your family has gotten your back no matter what happens, but that can hardly matter when you are adventuring nigh and high with other folk, so they provide you the best they can when you're away from them. You have a 25% discount on any magical tattoos you'd purchase for yourself or trusted creatures.

Additionally, whenever you are within Middle controlled territory you have advantage on {@skill Intimidation} rolls and other siblings will easily provide food and shelter for you and any friends you bring along.
Alternatively, with your DM's permission ( or if you are playing with '24 Backgrounds in general ) gain the {@feat Ink Thicker Than Blood|TheUndertomesOL} Feat.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The vast majority of those adopted into the Middle are colourful figures who are a living party unto themselves, with many was to show that. Despite the seeming union of the faction as a whole, there are those who are around for power rather than just the ones who are looking for true loyalty and camaraderie. Nevertheless, a great knowledge for their extensive grudges is a must for any of them.
The Middle is defined by some form of relation to the rest of the gang, be that a quirk toward them or a way you particularly enjoy being part of the whole thing.

entries.caption: Familial Quirk
rows: I spend an embarrassingly massive amount of gold on cute stickers to award to others.
I look up to others easily and feel afraid of disappointing them.
Blasting loud music is the same as breathing to you, screw what others say.
I write every. Single. Little. Slight. In the book. No exceptions.
I spend excessive time every single day taking care of your luscious mane of hair.
I tend to butt heads with your siblings often in good humour, making sure everyone has enough strength to carry their chains.
I are a collector of trivia and information about each persons tattoos, usually recognizing people by their ink before their faces.
I always look cool to your younger siblings and you don't know why. After all, its simply your job to take care of them.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I meet any slight with immediate retribution in the form of violence.
I tend to give others a second chance, even if it is after giving them a well-deserved punch.
If my neck-line isn't invisible from the sheer weight of my chains, I am not stylish enough.
I can't calm down without a good beat in the background.
I live my life by the book, both in vengeance and in my lifestyle, preferring to have my routines be sacred and unchanging.
I can't deal with technicalities and hedge-cases that are complex, so I just always default to the worst case scenario on the basis of a single coin flip.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: The reason I joined the family is freedom, I want to do whatever the hell I want whenever I want! (Chaotic)
Loyalty to your fellow is the most important thing in life. Breaking away from that is unforgivable. (Lawful)
I enjoy loud music. Environments with clear regulation are also favorable. (Neutral)
