While swallowed, the creature is {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Restrained}, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange], and it takes 21 ({@damage 6d6}) acid damage at the start of each of the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange]'s turns.

If the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall {@condition Prone} in a space within 10 feet of the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange].
If the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone.

footer.name: Loot
entries: Once killed, BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] will always drop 4 {@item BongBong Orange|TheUndertomesDA|BongBong Oranges}.

footer.name: Bestiary
entries: A mysterious insect-like creature with acidic insides that, when in contact with air or diluted enough, turns into a sweet beverage. This creature seems to prefer easier prey and prioritizes attacking targets that are slow, usually going for those with less movement or that are lower in the initiative count.

monster.name: Clerid Swarm (Familiar)

trait.name: Death Eater
entries: The swarm can instantly perceive any Undead creature within 30-ft as if they has blindsight.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can’t regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

action.name: Bites
entries: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 ({@dice 1d4 + 3} ) piercing damage plus inflicts 1 Bleed on a hit.

action.name: Devour Mind Wound
entries: The swarm climbs onto a willing creature within 5-ft, emitting a loud wailing as it devours any psychic energy affecting it. If the creature is suffering from the {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened} Condition or suffering from an Enchantment spell effect, that Condition or Effect ends early. This ability may be used for an amount of times equal to half your PB, rounded down, recovering spent uses on a short or long rest.

languages: understands any you speak, but cannot communicate through any means other than cacophonous buzzing.

monster.name: Clerid Swarm (Ravenous)

hp.special: Your Druid Level + proficiency bonus + Half your Wisdom Modifier

trait.name: Passive Perception
entries: 12 + PB

trait.name: Death Eater
entries: The swarm can instantly perceive any Undead creature within 30-ft as if they has blindsight.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can’t regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

action.name: Ravenous Bites
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: Your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 ({@dice 3d4} + PB ) piercing damage plus inflicts 2 Bleed on a hit. If the Swarm is below half its maximum hit points, it deals only {@dice 1d4} + PB piercing damage but inflicts 4 Bleed.

action.name: Consume Body
entries: (Requires 6th-Level) The Swarm devours the body of a dead creature within 5-ft of it, being healed by {@dice 2d8}+PB hit points and generating 3 Lifeblood. A Small or lesser creature only heals and generates half those amounts, rounded down, and Large creatures may be eaten from twice before the body is gone.

action.name: Devour Mind Wound
entries: The swarm climbs onto a willing creature within 5-ft, emitting a loud wailing as it devours any psychic energy affecting it. If the creature is suffering from the {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened} Condition or suffering from an Enchantment spell effect, that Condition or Effect ends early. This ability may be used for an amount of times equal to half your PB, rounded down, recovering spent uses on a short or long rest.

languages: understands any you speak, but cannot communicate through any means other than cacophonous buzzing.

monster.name: Dullahan

hp.special: 19 + your Charisma modifier + five times your paladin level (the Dullahan has d8 Hit Dice equal to your Paladin level)

languages: Understands the languages you speak, but can't speak

action.name: O, Dullahan...!
entries: {@atk mw} +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d12 + 4}) psychic damage. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, If the target has {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they take an additional {@damage 1d6} psychic damage for each stack of Sinking. Otherwise, they gain 2 stacks of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

monster.name: Festival Fairy
languages: Fae, any its summoner can speak

trait.name: Flutterby
entries: While the creature remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal chicken.

trait.name: Fly Around
entries: The Festival Fairy may begin orbiting around a non-hostile creature within 5-feet of itself on the end of its turns. Until the start of its next turn, its AC is considered the same as the creature it is orbiting.

action.name: Wingbeat
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. {@h}3 (1 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Care
entries: The lone Fairy can't restore as much as when with its brethren, but it still tries its best. One friendly creature within 5 feet of the Fairy restores one hit point to it. This does not work if the creature is downed.

monster.name: Gift Friend
languages: Any its host spoke, can only immitate basic words with no coherence

trait.name: Claiming Friendship
entries: If the Gift Friend deals damage to a creature suffering from the effects of the {@optfeature Unloved Gift Surprise|TheUndertomesASF} feature, it instantly triggers that feature's Heartbreak effect.

trait.name: Disturbing Appearence
entries: Any creature that can see the Gift Friend has a -1 to Saving Throws to resist becoming frightened.

trait.name: Enlarged Heart
entries: The Gift Friend may use its action to fully devour a dead creature's corpse that is medium in size. For each 2 corpses it eats, it gains an additional action.

action.name: Stab
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 10ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) piercing damage.

action.name: Consume
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) piercing damage, the Gift Friend Heals by half the damage dealt this way.

monster.name: Needlekin Servant

hp.special: (4 + half your proficiency bonus) times your Warlock Level (Uses d6s for Hit Die.)

languages: Any you are able to speak

trait.name: Bindstitch - Cling
entries: The Needlekin may Cling to other willing creatures within 5-ft. of them, provided they aren't other Needlekin. While Clinging to them, they move alongside that creature and they cannot be targeted for attacks until the creature that they are Clinging to stops protecting them as a Bonus Action or are {@condition Incapacitated|PHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|PHB}, {@condition Unconscious|PHB} or die. Additionally, this creature may choose to take the brunt of any damage the Needlekin would've suffered from area-of-effect attacks such as Fireball.

trait.name: Weaver's Aide
entries: The Needlekin may willingly provide help to creatures within 5-ft. whenever they attempt an Artisan's T ools check, granting a {@dice d4} bonus modifier for each Needlekin present. If they are aiding a Needleworks Warlock they also have that creature count as if they had Expertise in said Artisan's T ools.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The may use its Tacking Stitch attack up to an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus.

action.name: Tacking Stitch
entries: uses your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target(S). Hit: 1 piercing damage and inflicts one count of {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} and one count of {@condition Bind|TheUndertomesNW}. If the target has {@condition Naildle|TheUndertomesNW} count already, the Needlekin inflicts an additional count.

monster.name: Punishing Bird
languages: Can understand common but can't speak

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The Punishing Bird doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Punish the Wicked
entries: When the Punishing Bird or a creature it is friendly to takes damage, it may perform a Punishment attack against the source of that damage, if within reach.

action.name: Beak
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Punishment
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. {@h}12 ({@damage 4d4 + 4}) piercing damage.

monster.name: Stigmatized Memory

ac.special: 12 + your PB, chosen when summoning this creature

hp.special: 4 times your Ranger level plus your PB

languages: understands any you know, but can't speak other than unintelligible murmurs

trait.name: Designated Execution
entries: Whenever killed by a Fell Memoir Ranger or a creature who similarly clutches memories to use as fuel, the killer deals an additional {@damage 1d8} damage until the end of their next turn. This extra damage is of the same type of the creature's attacks.

action.name: Shambling Jab
entries: {@atk mw} {@hitYourSpellAttack} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d6} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Re-Enactment of the War
entries: {@atk rw} {@hitYourSpellAttack} to hit, range 60/90 ft., one target. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Obey Firing Order
entries: When ordered by their summoner, the {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} Memory performs a Shambling Jab attack or a Re-Enactment of the War attack against a target creature of the summoner's choice.

reaction.name: Obey Repositioning Order
entries: When ordered by their summoner, the {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesFM} Memory spends their Reaction to move up to 20-ft. in any direction of the summoner's choice.

trait.name: The Blessing of Life
entries: Whenever the Pumpkinhead would take radiant damage, it instead recovers an amount of Hit Points equal to the damage it would take.

trait.name: Who’s The Real Deal?
entries: The Pumpkinhead is naturally elusive, playing tricks on those unaware. When a creature first sees the a Pumpkinhead they must pass a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be {@condition Charmed} by all Pumpkinheads, perceiving them as if they were a random present creature of the DM’s choice, such as another party member or NPC currently in the scene. On a success, the creature becomes immune to this ability regardless of which

trait.name: Pumpkinhead it originates from
entries: This lasts for 24 hours.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Pumpkinhead makes up to two attacks during its turn.

action.name: Rake to Oblivion
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: one target. Hit: 8 ({@dice 2d4+4}) slashing damage. This attack deals an additional 6 ({@dice 2d6}) necrotic damage to {@condition Charmed} creatures.

reaction.name: Steal or be Stolen
entries: Whenever the Pumpkinhead deals damage to a creature, it steals part of their abilities at random, being able to use them as if it were its own until it is killed or until combat ends. The creature stolen from cannot use these abilities until recovered. To determine which ability is stolen, roll a d4 and then the DM chooses a specific one. For a roll of 1, an Offensive ability is stolen, for 2 a Healing ability, for 3 a Skill Proficiency and on a 4 the Pumpkinhead swaps an Attribute score of its own with the targets. To determine the Attribute score roll a d6, following the order of Attributes displayed in Player Character Sheets. The Pumpkinhead may use any of the target creature’s modifiers to use these abilities. An Offensive ability is any type of attack such as a Greatsword attack or a Monk’s Flurry of Blows, while a Healing ability may be a Fighter’s

reaction.name: Second Wind or a Cure Wounds spell
entries: If a spell is stolen, the Pumpkinhead may cast it only once, with it then being recovered by it’s original owner.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The valentine’s ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Loving Abomination
entries: Another creature may gift the ooze a magical item to make it non-hostile. If the item is rare or greater, that creature is granted a cartoon-heart shaped blob of slime that can be squeezed to grant a Saint Valentin’s Blessing. A rare item being given grants a minor blessing while a Very Rare one or greater grants a major blessing.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The valentine’s ooze can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The valentine’s ooze makes two pseudopod attacks. It can use engulf in place of one of these attacks.

action.name: Rake to Oblivion
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: one target. Hit: 13 ({@dice 2d8+4}) bludgeoning damage and 7 ({@dice 2d6}) psychic damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is {@condition Grappled} (escape DC 14). Until this grapple ends, the target is {@condition Restrained}. The blood ooze can grapple up to two creatures at a time.

action.name: Rake to Oblivion
entries: One creature {@condition grappled} by the blood ooze must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be pulled into the ooze’s body. An engulfed target is {@condition blinded}, {@condition restrained}, unable to breathe, and has total cover from effects that originate outside the ooze. At the start of each of the ooze’s turns, the engulfed creature takes 18 ({@dice 4d8}) psychic damage. The ooze can have only one creature engulfed at a time. An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make its choice of a DC 14 Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. On a success, the creature escapes and uses 5 ft. of movement to enter a space of its choice within 5 ft. of the ooze. If the ooze dies, an engulfed creature is no longer {@condition restrained} by it and can escape from the corpse by using 10 feet of movement. If the engulfed creature dies, it becomes another valentine’s ooze that is expelled to the nearest vacant space. It can only be restored to it’s former self with a True Polymorph, {@spell Greater Restoration} or greater spell, having all their memories as an ooze being a breezy blur. Melting Love

itemProperty.name: Arcana Shot
entries: A weapon with the Arcana-Shot property has a specialized magazine that allows the use of magic-infused bullets. They may be limited in which bullets the magazine accepts, denominated by a string of letters as per the following table:

entries.caption: Arcana Shot Ammunition
rows: Acidic
A
Flaming
F
Gravital
GR
Icebound
I
Lightning
L
Necrotic
N
Pure
P
Radiant
R
Thundering
T

entries: If no letters are named, that weapon accepts all type of Arcana Shot.

itemProperty.name: Assist
entries: {@b Assist.} A weapon with the Assist property is one that was designed to aid in defending the wielder, yet it's usage makes it cumbersome to wield anything too big at the same time. While wielding an Assist weapon you gain a +1 bonus modifier to your Armor Class, but you cannot benefit from wielding Heavy weapons or a {@item Shield|PHB}.

itemProperty.name: Blast Cartridge
entries: {@b Blast Cartridge.} A weapon that boasts the {@i Blast Cartridge} property is inlaid with a firing mechanism that can be triggered whenever you hit a creature with it, spending one appropriate piece of ammunition to do so. ( Usually a bullet. ) Whenever you do, you inflict additional damage equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property.

itemProperty.name: Blazing
entries: {@b Blazing.} With the right angle, a weapon with the {@i Blazing} property ignites the air in a furious blaze., Whenever your base dice roll is equal to or greater than the first value displayed in parenthesis besides this property, you apply an amount of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the second value presented.

itemProperty.name: Burst
entries: {@b Burst.} Weapons with the Burst property are ones that can be fired or used in a quick burst of attacks that compromise accuracy for the chance of more damage. You may benefit from Burst weapons whenever you take the {@action Attack} action, choosing to replace a singular attack you would be able to make with a number of attacks displayed in parenthesis next to this property. You may choose only one target for each burst of attacks, being able to switch between targets with each differing attack replaced to do so.

You may do so for each attack you would usually be able to make, but suffer a negative modifier starting at a value equal to your Dexterity modifier minus the first number in parenthesis (Minimum of 1), further subtracting one for each individual attack made after the first. This negative modifier is reduced by 2 if you are wielding your weapon with two hands and fully reset at the end of your turns.

You do not add your ability modifier to damage dealt by this Property's feature, and the damage dealt by a burst shot may differ from the original damage that would be dealt by the weapon. If so, this value is displayed after the number of attacks made in a burst.

Ex: As a level 5 Fighter you have two attacks as per the {@action Attack} Action. You may perform one normal attack and then choose to use the feature from a Burst (3) weapon, performing three attacks against the same target. You have a Dexterity modifier of 3, thus having no negative modifier for the first roll in your burst, then a -1 for the second and a -2 for the third.

itemProperty.name: Catalyst
entries: A weapon with the Catalyst Property was specially made for the purpose of channelling spells, often bearing their own engraved forms of spell craft. A weapon with this property does not use Strength for its attack modifier, instead making use of the spellcasting ability of the Class(es) shown in parenthesis next to this property. It also uses that classes Spell Save DC if required. The displayed classes automatically have Proficiency with the weapon, even if they wouldn't usually. These also count as spell foci for them.

itemProperty.name: Chain-Through
entries: {@b Chain-Through.} A weapon with the Chain-through property has an easy way of cutting into targets after initially being lodged onto them. These are saws, barbed axes and even barbed spears which can be wedged, pushed and pulled for a nasty amount of damage even if the target tries to dodge away. While dealing damage with a Chain-Through weapon, provided you haven't missed your previous attack, you deal at least half the value of damage die you'd roll if you had rolled lower than that.

Ex: If you, a Paladin, deal {@damage 2d8} slashing damage + {@damage 2d8} radiant damage with a Chainsword, if you roll a total of 2 slashing and 2 radiant damage, you instead deal 8 slashing and 8 radiant damage on that hit.

itemProperty.name: Concealed
entries: {@b Concealed.} A weapon with the Concealed property is perfect for hiding in-between clothes or other belongings, seeming like a harmless trinket until it is drawn. While not being held, you may use your Bonus Action to suddenly draw it with a free hand and perform a weapon attack roll against a creature within reach. If you had no free hands, you instantly swap one of your held items with the Concealed weapon. You also gain a +5 bonus modifier on {@skill Stealth} checks to hide a Concealed weapon.

itemProperty.name: Dispersing
entries: An armor set who boasts the Dispersing property evenly spreads any sort of vibrations and possible cracks it could receive, making it shrug off lingering blows much easier. Whenever you would receive {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count that amount is reduced by the value between parenthesis to the side of this Property, to a minimum of 1.

itemProperty.name: Draw
entries: {@b Draw.} A weapon with the Draw property is one meant to deliver its full force when unsheathed instead of over various strikes. While sheathed, your next unsheathed attack made with a Draw weapon gains a bonus modifier to hit equal to half it's wielder's proficiency bonus, rounded down, and deals an additional damage die on a hit. After being unsheathed, it's wielder may spend one of their attacks as part of the {@action Attack} action to sheathe it.

itemProperty.name: Ennervate
entries: {@b Ennervate.} A weapon with the {@i Ennervate} property is usually a living, breathing thing - Feeding on that very same life to fuel a diverse spectrum of effects. These are found under their own section of the {@i Ennervating} weapon and may be activated by sacrificing an amount of Hit Points equal to the number listed within parenthesis beside this property.

itemProperty.name: Entrench
entries: {@b Entrench.} A weapon with the Entrench property carries an enormous punch but also a considerable amount of blowback whenever it is fired or swung. Whenever you perform an attack with it, your remaining movement speed is reduced by the value in parenthesis beside this property. If two numbers are shown, these are in order the amount of movement speed reduced by one handed attacks and two handed attacks.

itemProperty.name: Hemorrhaging
entries: {@b Hemorrhaging.} Meant to cause deep gashes and cuts, a {@i Hemorrhaging} weapon excels at drawing out blood. Whenever your base dice roll to hit a creature is equal or greater to than the first number presented in parenthesis beside this property, you inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the second value presented.

itemProperty.name: Immovable
entries: An armor set with the Immovable property is too heavy or too stubborn to be tossed around. Whenever you would be moved forcefully, you may choose to be moved an amount of feet less equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property, such as a 5 meaning that you can resist being moved 5-ft. per time you would be forcefully moved.

itemProperty.name: Impenetrable
entries: {@b Impenetrable.} An armor seat with the {@i Impenetrable} property has remarkably good stopping power against piercing forces and other kinds of missiles. Your AC against attacks that would deal piercing damage or that are otherwise missiles ( such as arrows, bullets or certain ranged spells ) is considered to be higher by a value presented in parenthesis near this property. Additionally, whenever you would suffer damage through one such attack it is reduced by an amount equal to double the value presented in parenthesis.

itemProperty.name: Imposing
entries: {@b Imposing.} An {@i Imposing} armor set is the kind of clothing that demands some level of respect, no matter from whom. You benefit from having your {@skill Intimidation} skill modifier be at least the value displayed in Parenthesis, if it was any lower.

itemProperty.name: Lobbing
entries: {@b Lobbing.} A lobbing weapon isn't just thrown straight ahead, instead aiming up to strike down from afar. Lobbing weapons ignore cover if that cover isn't at least as tall as their short range, as per the Range or thrown properties.

itemProperty.name: Mesmerizing
entries: {@b Mesmerizing.} ( Also known as Funny ) Mesmerizing weapons aren't made just to be used with the usual strength of technique that a swordmaster or a great archer would have, no. They instead rely on another technique: that of the spectacle! You may use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength while using these weapons.

itemProperty.name: Reload
entries: {@b Reload.} Weapons with the Reload property have a limited amount of rounds that can be shot before needing to be reloaded. A Reload weapon needs to be reloaded after a certain amount of attacks, with this value being found in parenthesis following the property. To do so, you must spend your Action or Bonus Action to do so - Nevertheless, you cannot take the {@action Attack} action using the reloaded weapon on the same turn you reload it.

itemProperty.name: Set
entries: {@b Set.} A weapon with the Set property is instead multiple weapons that can be used together or a stock that is easily replenished in the heat of battle, whether they are thrown and lost or easily breakable upon impact. The maximum amount of uses these weapons have is shown in parenthesis after the weapon property, with you having the ability to easily produce or procure more at the end of a short or long rest. A lack of a number instead indicates that the weapons may be used infinitely.

itemProperty.name: Splash
entries: {@b Splash.} A weapon with the splash property has a tendency to cover an area of effect in its strikes or have a small splash zone where hits go off to. While you wield a Splash weapon to hit a target, all other hostile creatures within 5-ft. of the target take damage equal to the value in parenthesis beside this property. By default the damage type is the same as the weapon's first presented damage type, or denoted if otherwise.

itemProperty.name: SteelHack
entries: {@b SteelHack.} A weapon with the SteelHack property is designed to have sliding or otherwise transmutative mechanisms to allow it to exist in multiple forms at once. The base weapon is described in the initial weapon text, with a secondary one being presented below it for each alternative form, which may change its properties, damage and so on. Ammunition stashed in a SteelHack weapon remains inside it even if its current form wouldn't use it, requiring a form-change to rip it out. Additionally, changing a weapon's form this way usually takes a Bonus Action, with any deviations of that rule being specified in parenthesis beside the property as A for Action and FA for a Free Action that may be taken at any time.

itemProperty.name: Unarmed
entries: A weapon with the Unarmed property is usually light enough to be worn over the hands as more of an accessory than a tool. While wielding those, you count any attacks done with them as unarmed weapon attacks.

variantrule.name: Active
entries: An Active {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} requires active usage from a creature who must spend their Action while within 5-ft of the Tool to trigger it.

variantrule.name: Adherent
entries: An Adherent {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one that can easily cling to any even surface, being able to be placed on unoccupied ceilings or walls.

variantrule.name: Arcane
entries: An Arcane {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one commonly used by scholars and people attuned to the arcane, such as Wizards and Sorcerers. Characters with levels in these classes may repair up to their Proficiency Bonus' worth of Relicary Tools during a Long Rest as if they were an Artificer, also being able to choose using their own Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Modifier for these Tools.

variantrule.name: Bulky
entries: A Bulky {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} requires more space than usual for its operation. This space is listed in parentheses after this property is listed.

variantrule.name: Concealed
entries: A Concealed Tool is made hard to perceive. All Creatures have Disadvantage on {@skill Perception} Checks to find it, with the tool having a Passive {@skill Stealth} Score displayed in parenthesis following this property.

variantrule.name: Construct
entries: A Construct {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} has the same Resistances as most of its kind, being a mechanical mess of machinery in its operation. It has Resistance to acid damage, Immunity to poison and psychic damage and the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Poisoned}, {@condition Prone} and {@condition Incapacitated} Conditions.

variantrule.name: Contact
entries: A Contact {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} triggers whenever a creature moves into the area it occupies.

variantrule.name: Core Bursts
entries: "…In order to use Shin, one must clear their mind of all emotions and then tap into their most intense memories…"

Upon reaching a certain level of awareness and strength, certain people may come to develop a manifestation of their inner self, coming not only to understand what they are but to push that understanding outwards like an expanding force unique to them alone. This is a force composed of a mastery and understanding of your emotions and how you wish to impose that will on the world.

Upon reaching 10th level, you may choose to gain a Core Burst as per what best fits your person, activating it with a Bonus Action during your turn. This effect may come to manifest as a small effect surrounding you like an aura, such as crackling lightning forming whenever you move or smoke raising from your feet. This lasts for up to one minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

This process is exhausting to the mind, being able to be used once per long rest. You may instead use your Core Burst twice per long rest upon reaching 20th level. You may choose to push yourself particularly hard and activate your Core Burst after all uses have been expended, but you gain a point of {@condition Exhaustion} when it ends.

variantrule.name: Cumbersome
entries: A Cumbersome {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is particularly harder to deploy. You must instead spend an Action to deploy this {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}.

variantrule.name: Deployable Tools
entries: Deployable tools are traps or other mechanisms that a character may employ in dire times. They are placed down within an unnocupied 5-ft reach by spending your Bonus Action during your turn and have a trigger according to its properties, as shown below their name, much like weapon properties. If a Tool requires a Saving Throw to be passed, it will be displayed before it's properties, with the DC's associated Ability Score being placed in parentheses, and below that it's effect(s) when trigger. Tools usually occupy a 5-ft by 5-ft square. You may also spend your Bonus Action to retrieve a Tool.
Unless specified, all Deployable Tools only trigger against creatures hostile to who deployed it.

All Tools have a Durability Property, which denominates how many times they may be activated until they break down and require repairs. A broken down Tool may be repaired by a blacksmith for half of it's buying price or during a Long Rest spending one use of a Repair Kit during a Long Rest, where at least one Character must spend their time repairing or re-stocking the Tool. Otherwise, a Player Character with a number of levels in the Artificer Class may fix up to their Proficiency Modifier's worth of Tools during a Long Rest. To do so, they must meet a minimum level requirement according to the Tool's rarity, as follows:

rows: Common
Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary

entries: Furthermore, Artificers may choose to use their Spell Save DC instead of the Deployable Tool's when it is triggered, instead of the Tool's original Saving Throw required. This also applies to the Artificer's Spell Attack Modifier in the case the Deployable Tool performs attacks.

variantrule.name: Durability
entries: A {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}'s Durability measures how many activations a Tool can handle before needing repairs or re-stocking. This value displayed in parenthesis after this property.

variantrule.name: Far-Mount
entries: A Far-Mount {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} can be easily tossed and assemble itself. You may deploy a Far-Mountable Tool on any unoccupied space within a radius of yourself as shown by the number of feet within parentheses following this property's listing.

variantrule.name: Installing and Uninstalling Prosthetics
entries: In a Setting or table where downtime should matter more, you may have the process of acquiring any given Prosthesis for part replacement and upkeep be only the first step in benefitting from such. There are two means of installing Prosthesis, either with the aid of a professional in a specialized clinic/workshop or trying to do so by yourself.

When relying on a Professional such as a surgeon, ripperdoc or meister to do so, you have the limb successfully installed or removed after 8 hours spent in surgery. These are the usual costs for such operations:

entries.caption: Professional Installation and Removal Costs
rows: Common
45 GP.
Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary
Artifact

entries: When relying on yourself or attempting to install a Prosthetic on another creature, you must spend 8 hours of uninterrupted work to do so, also requiring to pass a {@skill Sleight of Hand} check of which you may choose to use either your Dexterity or Intelligence modifier to do so. The base DC for this check is 10, with the following modifiers:

entries.caption: Prosthesis Installation DC Modifiers
rows: Common Rarity
Uncommon Rarity
Rare Rarity
Very Rare Rarity
Legendary Rarity
Artifact Rarity
Unstable Work Environment
Specialized Work Environment
Artificer Levels
Negative modifier equal to Artificer level.
Proficiency in Tinker's Tools

entries: For further clarification, an {@i Unstable Work Environment} might consist as a specially dirty or unsanitary place or an active war zone where the surgeon simply cannot focus properly. On the other hand, an {@i Specialized Work Environment} is a clinic, workshop or anything of the sort. This is ultimately up to the DM's clarification of the current environment. On a failed check, the item is not spent but you must roll on the {@i Surgery Accidents} table:

entries.caption: Surgery Accidents
rows: Nothing too egregious happens and any damage caused to the patient is negligible.

There are some mild wounds that will last for a while, causing the patient's Maximum Hit Points to be reduced by an amount equal to double the Rarity Modifier of the Prosthetic as per the above table. ( To a minimum of 2. ) These Maximum Hit Points are recovered at a rate of 1 per short rest and 5 per long rest.
What have you done. The patient must roll on the {@table Lingering Injuries|DMG} table and suffer its consequences.

entries: If you are attempting to remove a limb, the DC is increased by twice the patient's proficiency bonus instead.

variantrule.name: Instant
entries: An Instant {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one that does not keep functioning in the field as long as it still has Durability, instead having it's Durability consumed whenever it is placed down, usually because this {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} comes in sets or may be used repeatedly. After a placed Instant Tool is triggered, it is destroyed, with only it's pieces remaining for posterior repairs or resupply.

variantrule.name: Mount
entries: A Mount {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} may be mounted by a creature standing in the same space as it by them spending their Action or Bonus Action to do so. While mounted their movement speed is 0 and the Bonus Modifier gained from their Dexterity Modifier on Dexterity saving throws can only be a maximum of 2. A creature may spend a Free Action to dismount. Mount {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool}s usually require a mounted creature's Action to be used.

variantrule.name: Multiple
entries: A Multiple {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is actually a set of Tools that may be placed down multiple times while it still has Durability, such as {@item Caltrops|PHB} being thrown from a bag.

variantrule.name: Primal
entries: A Primal {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one commonly used by those who are surrounded with nature, such as Druids and Rangers. Characters with levels in these classes may repair up to their Proficiency Bonus' worth of Reliquary Tools during a Long Rest as if they were an Artificer, also being able to choose using their own Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Modifier for these Tools.

variantrule.name: Reliquary
entries: A Relicary {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is one commonly used by churches, such as Clerics and Paladins. Characters with levels in these classes may repair up to their Proficiency Bonus' worth of Reliquary Tools during a Long Rest as if they were an Artificer, also being able to choose using their own Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Modifier for these Tools.

variantrule.name: Reloading and Ammunition Swapping
entries: A creature may Reload their weapon as usual even if they still have bullets left to spend, recuperating any ammunition they haven't shot. They may also use different Ammunition Types, such as {@i Arcana Shot} or {@i Propulsion Rounds} when Reloading their weapon, consuming an amount of the chosen ammunition equal to the weapon's Reload value. If unloaded, any un-shot ammunition is recovered.

variantrule.name: Sensor
entries: A Sensor {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} triggers whenever a creature of your choice moves in or outside of the range that follows this property in parenthesis.

variantrule.name: Sturdy
entries: A Sturdy {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} is unlike others, having no Durability and instead possessing it's own AC and Maximum Hit Points, displayed respectively in parenthesis following this property. They are usually Immune to psychic and poison damage, Vulnerable to Acid damage and are Immune to the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Grappled}, {@condition Poisoned} and {@condition Prone} Conditions, unless stated otherwise.

variantrule.name: Timed
entries: A Timed {@variantrule Deployable Tools|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Deployable Tool} triggers on a timer, usually at Initiative Count 1 or at whatever count that is lower than yours when it has been set. If you have none, you may choose from 15 below. The Trap only triggers after any other creature with the same Initiative Count has acted.

variantrule.name: Tremor Burst
entries: Tremor Burst is not a Condition, but instead a trigger for the {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} Condition which is caused by some feats, spells or other abilities.

variantrule.name: Wondrous Pets & Friends
entries: A “Wondrous Pet“ is the mechanical term this document uses to refer to, well, pets! A Pet in this way is a magical being that while attuned, will always remain within a 60-feet radius of its perceived owner. They do not require food nor sleep, but will gladly partake in either joy.
A Pet does not partake in combat initiative, instead it is treated like any other magic item when called upon for an active or passive ability it grants.

Additionally, it has no stat block of its own, instead only providing static benefits to its master. Much like the {@spell Find Familiar} spell, a pet may be commanded with a free action to move and to enter or exit an extradimensional space where it is kept safe. It automatically enters that space if it would be immediately be put in harms way, instead remaining safe.
If the {@spell Dispel Magic} spell is cast on the Pet, it vanishes for one minute, and then rematerializes after this time. During its vanishing, you cannot benefit from its abilities.

In the case that the “Pet” is instead a Friend or otherwise similarly sentient and possibly humanoid creature with their own will and volitions, they still try to stick close to you and keep out of harms way, but cannot ( if they aren't inherently magical ) enter the aforementioned extradimensional space.

Otherwise, in the case that the setting calls for the destructability or otherwise harm of a Wondrous Pet or Friend, they have a pool of Hit Points that matches their attuned master's level and their rarity, as per the following table:

rows: {@dice 1d4} per Player Level + Level
Common
{@dice 1d6} per Player Level + Level
Uncommon
{@dice 1d8} per Player Level + Level
Rare
{@dice 1d10} per Player Level + Level
Very Rare
{@dice 1d12} per Player Level + Level
Legendary

entries: You may roll on this table when first attuning to them.

Upon reaching 0 Hit Points, various things may happen depending on the Setting's intended tone and should be discussed between the Players and Dungeon Master when including Wondrous Pets & Friends into their setting. These are as follows:

items: The Pet is knocked {@condition Unconscious} until the end of battle and loses its effects until the next short rest.
The Pet initiates Death Saving Throws like a Player Character would, dying upon three failures. While {@condition Unconscious}, it does not provide any benefits.

If a Pet or Friend dies, you may choose to either have them be able to be brought back through a {@spell Revivify} or similar spell, through a ritual similar in cost to the {@spell Find Familiar} spell that any Spellcaster may perform or have them permanently die.

disease.name: Promise
entries: In lands watched over by gods of justice, or with the powerful presence of Celestials, there might be the presence of Promise in the air.
When you betray someone or succeed on a {@skill Deception} ability check, you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 13) or be stricken with Promise.

While stricken with Promise, the guilt of your lies and betrayal weighs heavy on your back. For a week, your intentions will always be the best, no matter who you interact with, and you must attempt to do whatever is requested of you as if you were under the {@condition Charmed} condition.
Promise can be cured by a {@spell Greater Restoration} spell or any other magical method for curing disease or insanity.

cult.name: Cult of Astu
entries: Astu is the Lawful Good deity of Society and all its laws.

entries.name: Cult Type
entries: Celestial

Certain groups of cultists reject the notion that change is a constant and necessary part of Astu’s teachings, and are aiming to preserve their societies in a single, specific, and perfect way in their eyes. Those that do not love the way their city is have no place in society as a whole.
Hushed Conversion. This creature can cast Silence and Suggestion once per day without the need for components. If they do not have a spell save DC, it becomes 10 plus their CR (Maximum of 19).

Those Who Love Their City. Once per day, as a bonus action, this creature can be instilled by an overflowing and powerful aura of devotion. They heal {@dice 4d4 + 4} Hit Points and, for a minute, deal additional radiant damage whenever they deal damage equal to their Wisdom modifier.

race.name: Blight

entries.name: Age
entries: Blights have the same age they had when they were killed. They usually live for as long as it takes for the magic to run out of their body, making it finally rot. Without a new ritual, you live around 100 - 150 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Blights have the same alignment they used to have when they were alive, as their personality, memories and soul usually remain. If any of these change, or if the ritual spell used to bring them back was especially charged with negative or positive energy, feel free to choose any different alignment that best fits their predicament.

entries.name: Blighted Instrument
entries: You can infuse your weapon with your poisonous blood. As a bonus action, for a minute or until you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (save DC 8 + your Constitution modifier + your Strength or Dexterity modifier) or become {@condition Poisoned} for a minute. A creature {@condition poisoned} this way can reroll this saving throw at the end of their turn. If you hit an already {@condition Poisoned} creature with this ability, you deal an additional {@dice 1d8} poison damage. This damage increases to {@dice 2d8} at level 5, {@dice 3d8} at level 11 and {@dice 4d8} at level 17.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language that you and your DM agree is appropriate for your character.

entries.name: Poison Identification
entries: You can identify if any substance contains poison (DC 14) without the need of an Alchemist’s kit.

entries.name: Thick Skin
entries: You have resistance to Poison damage.

Blights were once a creature killed with a powerful, magical poison. A ritual spell of revivification was used on them, but the poison reached deep into their soul, and they return as an intoxicated undead. Blights usually retain their memories and personality, but know they aren’t exactly the same person they left this world as. Their appearance is usually that of their previous race, but with pale skin, black veind and completely blackened fingertips with sharp nails.

entries.name: Age
entries: Bloodfiends do not age naturally and can live indefinitely, provided they are properly nourished. Once they reach physical maturity, they remain in that prime state indefinitely.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Most Bloodfiend families adhere to strict internal codes, often enforced under threat of death or worse. This rigid structure lends them toward lawful alignments. Despite their dependence on the blood of others, they are far from mindless predators; their ability to engage diplomatically often pulls them toward neutrality. However, some reject restraint entirely, leaning into a more openly evil nature.

entries.name: Blood Arts
entries: When you choose this ancestry or are turned into a Bloodfiend, you gain access to unique abilities known as Blood Arts. These represent how you've learned to control your Bloodfiend powers. Choose one Blood Art:

entries.optionalfeature: In the Dark of the Night|TheUndertomesTO

entries: At 12th level, choose one additional Blood Art:

entries.optionalfeature: In the Dark of the Night|TheUndertomesTO

entries: A Bloodfiend performs Blood Arts by spending Blood Charges. These arts are usually passed from parent to child, although a Kindred can develop one independently.

entries.name: Fear of Water
entries: Your kin hold an unbelievable fear of water, running or still. While you are within 5 feet of a body of water, you have disadvantage on attack rolls, Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws, and concentration checks.

When a creature tries to splash you with water, make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by its Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. On a failure, you take {@damage 2d6} psychic damage. On a success, you dodge and can leap 5 feet in a direction of your choice.

entries.name: It's in the Blood
entries: When a creature with blood drops below 1 hit point because of your actions, you gain 1 Blood Charge. You can also use an action to extract blood from a corpse that has been dead for less than 1 day. You can store up to 10 Blood Charges. This maximum increases to 15 at 6th level and 20 at 12th level.

entries.name: Sanguinary Tools
entries: You can manifest a partial demonic form, usually overtaking one limb and half your face in shadowy blood. You have a claw natural weapon with which you are proficient. It deals {@damage 1d8} slashing damage. You can treat it as a finesse weapon; if you do, it deals {@damage 1d6} slashing damage instead.

entries.name: Size
entries: Bloodfiends vary in height and build and often resemble the race from which they originated. Your size is Medium or Small.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice, appropriate to your background and approved by your DM.

entries.name: Fear of Water Modifiers
entries: The Fear of Water trait can take many forms. With your DM, you can replace its usual effects with one of the following optional modifiers:

entries.name: Bloody Trance
entries: While you are within 5 feet of a body of water, you take a penalty to your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores equal to your proficiency bonus and gain an equal bonus to your Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores. At the end of each of your turns, you take {@damage 1d8} psychic damage, plus one additional d8 for each previous turn during which you took this damage. The effect ends when you move more than 15 feet from the water.

entries.name: Fearful Headache
entries: When you come into contact with water, you take {@damage 2d8} psychic damage instead of {@damage 2d6}. This damage increases by {@damage 1d8} whenever you gain an Ability Score Improvement from gaining a level.

entries.name: Cornered Prey
entries: When you come into contact with water, you take no damage. Instead, you move 15 feet in a direction of your choice and fall {@condition Prone||prone}. If you remain in water after moving, repeat this movement and gain 1 level of exhaustion for each additional 15 feet traveled this way.

entries.name: Absolute Terror
entries: When you come into contact with water or stand within 5 feet of it, you become {@condition Frightened||frightened} of the space containing the water. As a bonus action, you can make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 19 - your Wisdom modifier, ending the effect on a success. The effect ends automatically when you move at least 60 feet from the source.

entries.name: Weakening Poison
entries: When water touches you directly, you take a penalty to attack rolls and saving throws equal to your proficiency bonus until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Mild Discomfort at Water
entries: Instead of the usual effects, you take a -1 penalty to all rolls while near water.
The DM and players should agree on one option that affects all Bloodfiends in the party equally. The Fear of Water trait and these modifiers can be ignored entirely if the group prefers.

entries.name: Optional Rules
entries: The following drawbacks can be used when the default ancestry is too strong for a particular campaign:

entries.name: Bloody Flow
entries: Whenever you take damage, you lose 1 Blood Charge.

entries.name: Low Reserves
entries: While you have fewer than 3 Blood Charges, you suffer the effects of 1 level of exhaustion. While you have 0 Blood Charges, you suffer the effects of 2 levels of exhaustion.

entries.name: Thirst for Blood
entries: When you finish a long rest, you must spend 4 Blood Charges. If you can't, you regain no hit points during that rest and gain 1 level of exhaustion. If you complete another long rest without paying the cost, you gain no benefits from the rest and gain another level of exhaustion. You can't recover from exhaustion until you spend the required Blood Charges.

entries.name: Red Banquet
entries: When you deal more than 20 damage with one attack, you gain 1 Blood Charge, to a maximum of 2 Blood Charges gained per attack.

entries.name: Age
entries: You were created resembling a humanoid creature of any given age and will never age further than that. Fired doll’s can live for great amounts of centuries before their fire expires and they slowly become stiff and dormant until a ritual is undergone to awaken them again.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Most Dolls are created with a specific purpose etched into the material that they were made, usually on the neck, back or chest - a list of tenets that they should never break, having them in their majority lean towards some form of Lawfulness, but others might let their effervescent nature guide them instead with little regard for any man-made conceptions, having them go towards the contrary way of Chaos.

entries.name: Gnawing Blazes
entries: When you kill a sentient, non-summoned, non-undead and non-construct creature or one is killed within 30-ft of you, you may spend your Reaction to rip out and consume part of their vital energy, empowering yourself as a result. For the next minute you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} fire damage on a hit and inflict 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit. You cannot consume more while you are already empowered.

entries.name: Living Flame
entries: You are granted life through an endless flame that is your soul, usually residing in your head, protected behind a stone mask. You can tap into this Flame to imbibe vital energy into others. You have a pool of Life Embers equal to the maximum value of half your proficiency bonus’ worth of Hit Die, rounded down. You may, as a bonus action, spend Life Embers and take damage equal to that value spent to heal another creature within 5-ft. of you by double the amount spent.

entries.name: Knowledge Etched In Stone
entries: Since before your creation a purpose was chosen for you, granting you your choice of proficiency in one Artisan’s tools and proficiency in {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language that you and your DM agree is appropriate for your character.

entries.name: Age
entries: Faefolk in Green have their childhoods pass in the blink of an eye, rapidly growing into adulthood in usually less than a year alive, with a lifespan known to reach the thousands easily.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Most Faefolk follow only the laws of the Feywild, often disregarding anything else as a mere suggestion as of how to maintain a mask. This makes them lean toward a chaotic nature, acting upon their wills and whims as if it were as natural as drawing breath,

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of yourself as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You discern colors in that darkness only as shades of blues, greens and purples.

entries.name: Fae Trickery
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Deception}. You may attempt to deceive a creature you can hear and understand you that is within 60-ft as a Bonus Action to believe that you mean no harm and that there is no reason to fight. You roll a {@skill Deception} check contested against the target’s passive {@skill Insight} score, with the target becoming {@condition Charmed} by you on a success, being forced to use their available movement speed to approach you during their next turn. You have Advantage on attacks against {@condition Charmed} creatures and deal an additional 2 damage die equal to the attack’s original damage die against them. You may attempt to charm a creature this way for an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, restoring spent uses during a Long Rest. A creature who has become {@condition Charmed} has advantage against being {@condition Charmed} in this way for the next hour.

entries.name: Green and Goopy
entries: You can squeeze through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide, provided you are wearing and carrying nothing. You have advantage on ability checks you make to initiate or escape a grapple.

entries.name: Man Eater
entries: As a Reaction to where you would deal damage to a creature within your melee reach you may carve out a chunk of their flesh to nourish yourself, being healed by half the damage you have dealt to the target creature.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

entries.name: Age
entries: Jiangshi can unlive their existance without the presence of aging, rather having their body dry up and be in a permanent state somewhere near rigor mortis if they do not consume vital energy often enough. A sign of a well-fed Jiangshi is them looking closer to a living being, being able to even look like what they once were by the time they were alive, yet never moving quite right.

entries.name: Absorb Life
entries: You subside on the very essence of life to exist, and can draw it out to absorb like inhaling mist. You may spend your Bonus Action to absorb the Vital Energy from an {@condition Unconscious} or Dead creature, causing you to be healed by half your proficiency bonus’ worth of d8 hit points, rounded down, and granting you a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls for the next minute, for a maximum modifier of +2. You may do this once per Short or Long Rest, gaining a second use upon reaching 8th level and a third when reaching 16th level.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: The Jiangshi are not an unified race in the common sense, and vary a lot in the beliefs and wants they have carried after death, depending on who they were before they were alive, Something that is common between some of them, though, is a newfound perspective of their lives that might have them leaning towards neutrality.

entries.name: Keen Senses, Dull Eyes
entries: Your nearly decayed body has returned to life with enhanced senses, excluding your poor eyesight.
You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks to perceive visually, but have advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that involve hearing.
Your vision is restored for the duration of Absorb Life's effects when used, negating the negative effects of this ability.

entries.name: Slashing Nails
entries: You can channel destructive energy to your nails, extending them to be gigantic razor-sharp claws when you need to. You do so as a Free Action during your turn, extending the fingernails of a hand of which you aren’t wielding any weapon or shield in. These Claws count as natural weapons you are proficient in, dealing {@dice 1d6} slashing damage and {@dice 1d4} additional slashing damage while your Absorb Life's ability is active. These Claws have the Finesse, Reach and Versatile ({@dice 1d8}) weapon properties. You may retract your Claws as a free action during your turn.

entries.name: Inflexible Mobility
entries: You’ve got a rigid body that doesn’t need food, drink or to breathe oxygen. You have disadvantage on {@skill Acrobatics} checks and Dexterity Saving Throws because of your stiff joints, but as you become revitalized through your Absorb Life ability that becomes advantage on both for it’s duration when active. Furthermore, you may spend your Reaction when a creature would move outside of your melee range to hop a 30 ft. line towards the empty space closest to them. You may use your Reaction in this way for a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per Long Rest.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language that you and your DM agree is appropriate for your character.

hazard.name: Heaving Rain
entries: A Heaving Rain is an abnormal climate pattern that causes raindrops to fall with greater weight and density than usual, pelting creatures below in a painful immobilizing storm. All uncovered spaces where heaving rain is falling in are considered lightly obscured and hard terrain.

Furthermore, if any creature stands for longer than a turn below heaving rain suffer form the raindrops starting to harm them as the pelting builds up, having them take {@dice 2d4} bludgeoning damage at the start of their turn after the first spent in an uncovered space.

hazard.name: Poisonous Gas
entries: A thick colored cloud of gas thats noxious to living creatures, making it so any creature that needs to breathe suffer from a terrible poison while within a {@condition Poisoned} Gas area. A creature that starts or ends their turn inside must pass a saving throw shown near the mention of Poisonous Gas or suffer the following effects:

items: The creature becomes {@condition Poisoned} until they end their turn outside of the Poisonous Gas.
The creature takes an amount of d6 poison damage equal to the amount of turns it spent inside the gas, or half on a success. This damage can go up to {@dice 4d6} poison damage per turn.

A {@condition Poisoned} creature has disadvantage on this saving throw. Poisonous Gas cannot be removed by a gust of wind, instead being moved to cover a different area depending on the wind’s strength, such as a Gust of Wind spell being able to move the entirety of Poisonous Gas toward a 60-ft line of the caster’s choice. An area covered by Poisonous Gas is considered Difficult Terrain.

entries: It’ll sting~ It won’t come off once you’re cut.

reward.name: Blessing of the Summer Court
entries: Your Charisma score increases by 2, to a maximum value of 22. You gain the following ability: Summertongue. As a reaction to when you fail a Charisma check, you may attempt to roll again, potentialy turning a horrible failure into a success as you tap into either a warm personality to aid in your pursuits or even add scorching remarks to your previous statements to reinforce your points.

reward.name: Blessing of the Winter Court
entries: Your Constitution score increases by 2, to a maximum value of 22. You gain the following ability: Consume Warmth. As a reaction to when a creature within 30-ft. of you dies you may draw in any remaining ounce of life from their body, absorbing it to ensure your own survival. You are healed by {@dice 2d8} hit points and remove one point of {@condition Exhaustion} if you had any.

reward.name: Saint Valentin's Blessing
entries: This blessing grants you a bonus modifier to {@skill Persuasion} and {@skill Performance} checks as you are filled with constant confidence, as if you had comforting whispers at the back of your mind constantly. Furthermore, you gain the same bonus to Charisma and Wisdom saving throws for the same reason.
The value of this bonus depends on the blessing’s tier, as per the following table:
